Title: OéRIX – AI Resource Intelligence for Sustainable Industry
Subtitle: A plug-and-play IoT + AI platform helping industrial SMEs, utilities and public operators in Africa and the Arab region cut energy, water and cold-chain losses in real time.
Problem Statement: In developing and middle-income economies, industrial SMEs, utilities and public facilities waste a large share of their energy and water. Losses come from inefficient equipment, undetected leaks, poor load management and broken cold chains. Most of these organizations have no metering beyond the monthly utility bill. They have no data infrastructure and no in-house energy or data expertise. Existing industrial monitoring and AI solutions are designed for large corporations in high-income markets: they are expensive, hard to integrate with legacy equipment and poorly adapted to local constraints (intermittent connectivity, mixed equipment brands, French/Arabic-speaking users). As a result, operating costs remain high, climate commitments are hard to measure, and SMEs are excluded from the productivity gains that digitalization and AI offer.
Solution Overview: OéRIX is a cloud and edge IoT + AI platform developed by Be Wireless Solutions (BWS), a Tunisian company founded in 2016 with 10 years of IoT expertise and 4 years of applied AI development. How it works: Sensing layer. Non-intrusive sensors and gateways (energy meters, water meters, temperature/humidity probes, Modbus/KNX/DALI gateways, GPS trackers) are retrofitted onto existing installations, regardless of brand. Connectivity and data layer. Data is transmitted via LoRaWAN, GSM/4G or Ethernet, buffered at the edge in case of connectivity loss, then normalized and stored in a unified data model. AI layer. Machine-learning models detect anomalies (leaks, consumption drifts, equipment malfunctions, temperature excursions), forecast consumption and benchmark sites against each other. They then generate prioritized, actionable recommendations. Decision layer. Multilingual dashboards (French, English, Arabic), real-time alerts, automated reports and ROI tracking are delivered to operators, managers and energy auditors. Modules: energy efficiency, water loss control, cold chain monitoring, fleet tracking and resource management, deployed separately or combined. Partnerships and collaboration models: BWS partners with public energy agencies (e.g., ANME in Tunisia, within the TEEP energy-efficiency program), local integrators and distributors in new markets (e.g., Saudi AI in Saudi Arabia under a signed MOU), and market-access partners (Betawaves). BWS operates a South–South replication model through its offices in Tunis, Strasbourg, Bahrain and Nouakchott, transferring know-how and training local technicians in each country.

Implementation location(s): Deployed in 10 countries across 4 continents. BWS operates from Tunisia (head office, Tunis) and its subsidiaries in France (Strasbourg), Bahrain and Mauritania (Nouakchott). Deployments also cover the United States, Morocco, Senegal, Switzerland, Qatar and Côte d’Ivoire. Market entry in Saudi Arabia is underway through a local entity and integrator partner. Sites include industrial plants, utilities, banking networks, hotels, healthcare facilities, public buildings and vehicle fleets.
Implementation timeline(s): 2016 – ongoing: IoT resource monitoring deployments (BWS Platform). 2022 – ongoing: AI modules (anomaly detection, forecasting, recommendations). 2026 – ongoing: OÉRIX engine with root cause analysis, quantified action plans and the Ask OÉRIX assistant.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 2 to 6 weeks. This covers site assessment, sensor and gateway installation (or connection to existing meters), platform configuration, AI baseline learning, and operator training in the local language. Deployment relies on local integrator partners and a hardware-agnostic, cloud or on-premises architecture.
Desired impact: Objectives: Make resource performance visible, actionable and measurable for industries, utilities and public operators in emerging economies. Turn fragmented operational data into prioritized, quantified decisions that cut costs and carbon emissions. Build local digital and AI capabilities among operators, technicians and engineers. Demonstrated impact (BWS customer base): 2,844 tonnes of CO₂ emissions avoided per year. 50,000+ sensors and GPS trackers deployed. 2.5 billion data points collected. 188+ active customers in 10 countries across 4 continents. Observed gains of up to −25% in operating costs, up to +20% in energy efficiency, up to −30% in CO₂ emissions and up to −50% in decision-making time. 50+ engineers employed, most of them in Tunisia and Mauritania, creating skilled digital jobs in the region. Illustrative case: OÉRIX detected an energy anomaly 5 times above baseline on an industrial site. It identified the root cause (abnormal base-load activation) and recommended a corrective plan with an estimated cost of €1,500 and savings of about €400 per month. That is a 3.8-month payback and a 320% ROI. The plan was executed and closed within 48 hours of detection.
Key technologies: IoT: smart energy, water, gas and fuel meters, temperature and environmental sensors, GPS trackers, and industrial gateways (Modbus, KNX, DALI); connectivity via LoRa, 4G/5G and Wi-Fi. Artificial intelligence: machine learning for baseline modeling and anomaly detection, automated root cause analysis, consumption forecasting, and recommendation ranking by cost, savings and ROI. Generative AI: Ask OÉRIX, a conversational assistant that explains anomalies, builds action plans and answers operators’ questions in natural language. Data platform: a unified, governed data model with real-time dashboards, energy performance and network quality indices, bill simulation and multi-site benchmarking. Deployment and integration: cloud or on-premises deployment and open APIs for ERP, CRM and building management systems. Security and quality: an ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certified information security management system.
Unique Characteristics: From data to decisions, not just dashboards. Most monitoring tools stop at alerts. OÉRIX closes the full loop (detect, understand, recommend, plan, measure) and attaches a quantified cost, savings, ROI and payback to every recommended action. Explainable, human-in-the-loop AI. Operators qualify each anomaly, validate or reject recommendations, and can question the system through Ask OÉRIX. This builds trust and transfers skills rather than creating a black box. One platform for all resources. Electricity, water, gas and fuel are managed in a single unified view across multiple sites, instead of siloed tools. Built in and for emerging markets. Retrofit on existing equipment of any brand, resilience to connectivity constraints, multilingual interfaces (French, English, Arabic), and pricing adapted to SMEs and public operators. Certified and proven. BWS holds ISO 9001 (quality), ISO 14001 (environment) and ISO 27001 (information security) certifications, and the solution is already deployed with 188+ customers and 50,000+ connected assets. South–South delivery model. An African company develops the technology, deploys it through local partners and trains local technicians, keeping value and skills within the region.
Sustainable Change: OÉRIX creates value beyond individual sites by generating reliable, granular resource data where none existed. At the national level, this data can strengthen energy-efficiency programs, utility network management and the measurement, reporting and verification (MRV) of climate commitments, as BWS’s collaboration with Tunisia’s national water utility and energy agency illustrates. Because each recommendation carries a measured ROI, the solution also helps financial institutions and public funders de-risk green investments and design results-based financing for SMEs. The model is built for replication. The platform is hardware-agnostic and modular, and it is deployed through local integrator partnerships, which already allowed expansion from Tunisia to 10 countries, with Saudi Arabia underway. Every new deployment trains local technicians and engineers, building a regional workforce skilled in IoT and AI. In the long term, aggregated and anonymized benchmarks across sectors and countries can inform industrial and energy policy. This creates a lasting effect: more SMEs gain access to AI, more decisions are based on evidence, and resources are used more efficiently across the industrial base of emerging economies.

Title: Driverless Fleets, Cleaner Mines: Embodied AI for Sustainable Autonomous Haulage
Subtitle: A production-proven L4 autonomous haulage system that removes operators from hazardous open-pit mines, lifts haulage efficiency above human benchmarks, and cuts energy use and emissions per tonne.
Problem Statement: Mining is a high-stakes, high-cost industry defined by harsh conditions and remote geographies. Operations sit at high altitude or in rugged terrain where workers face extreme weather, shifting ground and long hours of repetitive labour on rough roads — producing chronic labour shortages, high turnover, safety incidents and escalating operating costs. Autonomous mining trucks average over 21 hours of daily operation against manned shift patterns, and haulage remains one of the highest-risk activities on site. Building for mining autonomy demands a full-stack capability from hardware to perception to control, plus deep domain expertise. Most autonomous driving companies lack the robustness, adaptability and platform-level integration to succeed there; most traditional mining equipment manufacturers are not software-native and struggle to deliver intelligent automation at scale. Very few players globally can deliver autonomy for mining at scale, and penetration reflects it: autonomous mining trucks were around 12% of sales in China in 2025. The environmental stakes are structural. Diesel haulage fleets are among the largest sources of operational emissions on a mine site, and electrification alone does not close the gap — without autonomy, electric trucks remain bound to human shift cycles and inefficient driving behaviour. Users affected: large mining companies and their contractors who operate haul trucks, plus the drivers themselves. If unsolved: continued safety exposure and turnover, constrained capacity in remote and high-altitude regions, and a decarbonisation pathway that stays uneconomic.
Solution Overview: How it works: Two integrated suites. ORCASTRA — autonomous mining trucks plus the proprietary Autonomous Fleet Management System (AFMS), combining the on-vehicle Autonomous Driving System, a modular drive-by-wire electronic controlling chassis platform, proprietary vehicle E/E architecture, and a cloud-connected dispatch and coordination layer. Conductor Plus — mining digitalisation covering excavation, haulage and dumping, plus production, safety and asset management, usable on autonomy and non-autonomy sites alike, launched 2023. A typical deployment has three layers: on-vehicle real-time perception, localisation, prediction and control; a roadside/infrastructure layer for automated parking, dispatch, obstacle avoidance and loading-zone coordination, with retrofit instrumentation so conventional equipment can work alongside autonomous fleets; and a cloud and control layer for fleet monitoring, scheduling, production management, 5G connectivity and remote driver assistance for edge cases. Autonomy spans the full load–haul–dump cycle. Methodologies and technologies: - Vehicle-cloud collaborative architecture: real-time functions execute on the vehicle, the cloud handles high-level task scheduling, fleet coordination and long-horizon planning — higher resilience and fault tolerance in low-connectivity pits than cloud-dependent legacy designs. - Multimodal perception: LiDAR, camera and other sensors fused through a deep-learning framework using BEV LiDAR fusion and occupancy-grid reasoning; differentiates uneven ground from safe paths and distinguishes similarly shaped machinery, holding accuracy in dust, rain, snow, low light and vibration. - Predictive planning with multimodal trajectory forecasting: the engine anticipates motion and intent of 20+ dynamic agents across intersections, merging zones and unstructured roads, with conflict resolution, blind-spot avoidance and energy-aware path planning. - Hybrid localisation: fuses LiDAR, vision and inertial data with learned trajectories, reducing reliance on prior maps and RTK in high-altitude or low-connectivity zones. - Vehicle stability control: anti-slip control with adaptive drive-force distribution, monitoring grip, gradient and load. - AI toolchain: agent-based simulation where virtual vehicles make independent decisions, AIGC-generated test cases, self-reinforced models trained on six million+ autonomous trips across three software generations and 100+ releases, plus a CI/CD pipeline running automated simulation and hardware-in-the-loop tests. - Universal Safety Framework: four-layer sensing redundancy, six-level braking protection, dual-path redundancy across perception, decision-making, control and computing; ISO 26262 ASIL D, ISO 27001, ASPICE-aligned; 30+ equipment-level safety protocols, eight SOPs and 11 safety programmes codified into site execution. - Hosting: on-board inference at the edge; cloud training. Partnerships and collaboration models: The company sits at the centre of the value chain as systems integrator — contracted OEMs upstream supply non-powered chassis platforms and assemble to its integration specification against a contract manufacturing fee; mining companies and contractors downstream operate the trucks. Around 13 OEM partners, including Tonly, LGMG, Yutong and NHL, co-develop vehicle platforms: the EL100 with LGMG, the ET100/ET90/ET70M with Tonly, and the world's first fully electric autonomous fleet (YTK90E) with Yutong. Commercially there are two delivery models — customer-provided fleet (customer owns or leases trucks; EACON provide the autonomy stack, remote driving assistance, autonomous dispatch, remote technical support and OTA updates, priced per cubic metre at RMB0.44–2.65/m³) and company-provided fleet (EACON own or lease and manage the fleet including daily maintenance, priced per m³ or tonne). Contract mining companies are the principal channel and fleet owner in most deployments; third-party leasing companies finance acquisition.
Solution Provider(s): OEMs -- co-developers: Tonly (China's leading manufacturer of off-road wide-body mining dump trucks with roughly 40% domestic market share), XCMG (one of the world's largest construction and mining machinery manufacturers), Sinotruck (China's largest heavy-duty truck manufacturer and exporter), Shantui, etc. Mining companies -- users: CHN Energy (the world's largest coal producer and one of China's largest power generation groups), SPIC (one of China's five major state-owned energy groups with integrated coal, aluminium and power assets), Shougang Mining, Zijin Mining (one of the world's largest gold and copper producers), etc. Mining service companies -- users: Thiess (the world's largest mining services provider), Mingyang Group
Implementation location(s): Over 40 mine sites in China: Northwest (17 sites), North China (17), East China (2), Southwest China (3), South China (1). Mines sites cover terrains such as desert and plateau. Outside of China, the solution is deployed in Australia: Kalgoorlie, Western Australia (Norton Gold Fields, retrofit project in trial deployment)
Implementation timeline(s): China: field testing from May 2019; commercial deployment from 2020 to present. Australia: 2023 office established, trial deployment 2024 to present. 0 injurious accident record during the whole implementation period (2200+ days).
Duration to pilot in a new geography: In China: As short as 3-14 days to 24/7 autonomous haulage operation. International: 3–6 months from site agreement to autonomous production pilot, considering site survey and map build, fleet retrofitting or factory-fit lead time, local regulatory and safety approval, and workforce training. In a jurisdiction with no existing autonomous mining vehicle framework, allow up to 12 months to reach 24/7 autonomous operation with regulatory concurrence.
Desired impact: Objectives: (1) Remove human operators from the highest-risk task in open-pit mining while maintaining or exceeding manned productivity. (2) Make autonomous haulage economically accessible to ordinary mines — not only mega greenfield projects — by collapsing deployment time and cost. (3) Decouple industrial output growth from diesel consumption and per-tonne emissions by making autonomy electrification-ready, enhancing the electrification of mining trucks. (4) Rebuild the mining workforce around supervision, dispatch and data-driven operations rather than manual driving. Demonstrated impact of the whole fleet as of October 2026: - Scale: 4000 active autonomous mining trucks in 40 mine sites — the largest fleet globally; 42 mines equipped across 30 active sites; 22 million+ completed commercial autonomous trips; six consecutive years of field deployment without a major safety incident; 37.6% of China's mining autonomy market by revenue. - Deployment: three days from vehicle commissioning to safety-operator-free operation, against a 6–12 week domestic industry norm. - Productivity: 21+ hours of daily operation, roughly 10% above human benchmarks; 108% of human-level transport efficiency in commercial deployment. - Energy and carbon: EL100 extended-range trucks deliver 25–30% better fuel efficiency than conventional diesel models. The solution avoids 3,978.5 kg CO₂ per vehicle per year. The Yushi drive-by-wire platform has delivered fuel savings above 20% with fleet fault rates below 5%; several vehicles have passed 100,000 km of fully autonomous operation. - Commercial validation: 100% retention across all end-customer groups for three consecutive years; 91.3% of new customers acquired through referral. Demonstrated impact measured on the commercial fleet of its flagship partner, over one year post-deployment: - Deployment time: 9 weeks → 3 days, a –95% reduction against the 6–12 week industry benchmark. - Hourly transport efficiency: +13%, reaching 107% of human-driven benchmarks; autonomous trucks operate 21+ hours per day versus manned shift patterns. - Energy: 3,296,000 kWh saved per year, –13.3% energy consumption, including energy recovered from downhill regenerative braking. - Emissions: on the flagship battery-electric iron ore fleet, 386,000 kWh of regenerative recovery equates to roughly 185 t CO₂ avoided, alongside US$2.2M+ annual fuel and labour savings; mechanical braking usage down 70%, brake-pad life up 300%+. - Safety: 2,000+ consecutive days of safe operation with no major safety incident across the deployed fleet; –50% reduction in human workload in dangerous haulage tasks. - Scale: 2,400+ autonomous trucks in daily operation across 25 large-scale open-pit mines; 100 million+ km cumulative driverless haulage and 500 million+ m³ of material moved. - Fleet growth at the flagship site: +330% in the number of trucks equipped within one year of deployment.
Key technologies: L4 autonomous driving stack; multi-modal sensor fusion (camera + LiDAR) with BEV + Occupancy-Network perception; HD-map + RTK + LiDAR SLAM localisation; Transformer-class trajectory prediction models with self-supervised pre-training; diffusion-based motion planning and reinforcement learning; proprietary drive-by-wire control platform and vehicle E/E architecture; edge inference with cloud training; cloud-connected intelligent dispatch and fleet coordination platform; digital twin and end-to-end closed-loop simulation with synthetic data generation; IoT telemetry for dispatch and maintenance.
Unique Characteristics: - Full-stack ownership. Algorithms, the Yushi drive-by-wire platform, vehicle E/E architecture and AFMS are built in-house as one architecture, spanning 120+ vehicle models — the precondition for a coherent ASIL D safety case and for cross-OEM scale. - Edge-first distributed architecture. Localisation and control run on the vehicle with minimal truck-to-cloud communication, so operations survive weak or intermittent networks and the operator's infrastructure investment drops — the opposite of cloud-dependent legacy designs. - Only proven mixed-fleet operator. Mixed traffic, mixed loading and mixed dumping in live production; prediction models ranked No.1 on the Argoverse 2 Multi-World Forecasting leaderboard since September 2024 — external verification, not self-reported. - Yushi is the moat. The industry's first scalable drive-by-wire electronic controlling platform purpose-built for autonomous mining, adopted by around 13 OEMs including Tonly, LGMG, Yutong and NHL across 120+ models. It decouples hardware from software and abstracts OEM-specific protocols, breaking the custom-fit cycle that has historically kept autonomy unscalable. - Deployment speed as the product. 2 weeks instead of 6–12 weeks, delivered through a standardised modular platform and a scenario library built from commercial operations — this converts autonomy from a capex mega-project into a repeatable operational upgrade. - Business-model innovation. Turnkey seeding followed by migration to asset-light, usage-based delivery, with per-cubic-metre, one-time-fee and per-truck pricing options tested in live projects. Mines of very different financial capacity can adopt the same technology, and 70-model compatibility protects existing capital stock. - Data flywheel. Six million+ autonomous trips across three software generations and 100+ releases feed continuous retraining, compressing adaptation time per new mine type. - Safety record as evidence. Six-plus years of deployment without a major safety incident, four-layer sensing redundancy, six-level braking protection, ISO 26262 ASIL D, ISO 27001, ASPICE-aligned development, 30+ equipment-level protocols and eight operating SOPs.
Sustainable Change: - Rule-making, not just product-making. With the strong experience in the field, the company is actively participating in establishing national, industrial and association standards. It is designated lead unit of the Open-Pit Mine Autonomous Driving Standardization Working Group under China's mine safety standardisation committee, and is a founding partner of the National Mine Safety Administration's Key Laboratory for Intelligent and Safe Non-coal Open-pit Mining. Autonomy becomes an institutionalised norm rather than a vendor feature — the mechanism by which the change outlasts any single deployment. - Workforce restructuring with a skills floor. A whole autonomous fleet runs with a handful to roughly 100 on-site personnel, mostly coordinators, operational engineers and maintenance technicians, with R&D and monitoring centralised remotely. Drivers move into remote operation, dispatch and intelligent maintenance — automation raises the skill floor instead of merely subtracting headcount. - Lowering the entry threshold. Retrofit capability, 120-model compatibility and usage-based pricing open autonomous haulage to mid-tier miners, contract miners and quarry operators who cannot fund a greenfield autonomous fleet — a market-access effect, not just an efficiency effect. - Decarbonisation coupling. Autonomy is deliberately paired with electric and extended-range powertrains, making electrification economically viable at the mine and exporting China's new-energy supply chain into global mining. - Replicable playbook. The solution is proved to be replicable with the 7/24 operation in 40 mine sites. The company leads a clear scale-up model: Flagship deployment → proven economics → fleet scale-up → footprint expansion. With Australia as the first international beachhead and Canada, Chile, Mongolia, Kazakhstan, the Middle East and Africa mapped next, it follows a concrete route for cross-region technology transfer, including to emerging and developing mining economies. - Adjacent industry spillover. The same stack — infrastructure-light localisation, mixed manned/unmanned traffic, dust- and low-light-tolerant perception — transfers to quarrying, aggregates, construction earthworks, ports and large-scale material handling.
Funding Sources: The company is listed on HKEX main board since July 2026. Besides the stock market, financial resources come from the following sources: - Equity financing. Eleven pre-IPO rounds from Series Pre-A (2020) to Series D++ (2026), raising roughly RMB2.1 billion in aggregate, from a mix of financial investors (Eight Roads, Shenwan Chuangtou, Zhengzhou Hi-Tech Fund, among others) and strategic industrial investors including Zijin Mining, CATL and Tonly. - Capital-market financing. A public listing of H shares on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, with proceeds earmarked for software R&D, hardware R&D, IT development, global business expansion, customer acquisition, talent development, strategic alliances and working capital. - Asset-backed and lease financing. Sale-and-leaseback transactions on self-owned trucks under the turnkey model to recycle capital, plus direct truck leasing from third-party leasing companies in selected cases. - Customer-funded deployment. Under the asset-light model the customer finances truck procurement (average selling price RMB1.4–2.4 million per truck), so a growing share of deployment capex sits with the operator while recurring usage fees fund ongoing operations — the mechanism behind the shift of the asset-light model to 56.8% of 2025 revenue. - Operating cash flow and bank facilities, supplemented by government-recognised R&D programmes and industry research collaboration with universities and national laboratories.

Title: AI-Powered Industrial Energy & Resource Optimization Platform
Subtitle: A hardware-agnostic AI and IoT platform that cuts industrial energy waste by 20-30% and ensures ESG compliance.
Problem Statement: Industrial facilities and commercial buildings in developing economies waste up to 30% of their energy due to undetected equipment inefficiencies, lack of real-time data, and outdated infrastructure. Most SMEs cannot afford expensive closed-loop industrial EMS or the dense sub-metering required to find waste. Furthermore, with the rise of EU CBAM regulations, industries must provide verified carbon data, which they currently lack the tools to generate. This leads to increased operational costs, reduced competitiveness, and higher GHG emissions. Title: Infrared City: Hyperlocal AI Microclimate Simulation in Seconds
Subtitle: AI-powered microclimate simulation for cities and buildings at meter resolution: heat, wind, sun and daylight in seconds, through web app, API and plugins, for climate-informed design decisions.
Problem Statement: Cities are getting hotter and weather more extreme, yet decisions about streets, buildings and public spaces are still made largely blind. A full CFD study takes days and covers one plot per design option. Satellite and city-wide weather data stop at the district, so cooling budgets are spent by averages and operators work from one weather number for the whole city. And because every consultant uses their own tool and KPIs, results cannot be compared or reproduced. Climate is rarely built into design and operational decisions at the speed and resolution they need.
Solution Overview: How it works Infrared City is a headless climate engine. It shows designers, planners and operators how a place will feel and perform, before it is built or as conditions change. A user brings a site from Rhino/Grasshopper, QGIS or ArcGIS, a city's 3D Tiles, or a direct API call, chooses an analysis, and gets results at 1 m resolution on the ground, roofs and facades. A run typically takes 1 to 4 seconds. Twelve models cover thermal comfort (UTCI), wind and pedestrian wind comfort, solar radiation, direct sun hours, sky view factor and daylight. Large areas are split into tiles that run in parallel, so 100 km² of Hamburg runs end to end in 37 seconds. Every design option runs against the same baseline and KPIs, so results can be compared side by side. The live climate layer prepares a city once and then updates hour by hour for the coming days from weather forecasts. Users can add trees, shade or materials anywhere in the twin and get a new site variant in about 20 seconds. Results can be queried by place and hour, and are exported as 3D Tiles and 2D map tiles for digital twins. Methodologies and technologies AI surrogate models, trained on physics simulations, run on elastic serverless cloud compute that scales from zero to about 10,000 cores in minutes. Together they make 1 m resolution in seconds possible. Sun hours, sky view and daylight use deterministic raytracing. The engine runs in our EU cloud or on a customer's own servers, and is delivered through a REST API (OGC API compliant), Python and TypeScript SDKs, an AI agent skill, Grasshopper, QGIS and ArcGIS plugins, and a web platform. We test each model against reference data: • Radiant heat (UTCI) against field measurements at four sites, where it was more accurate than SOLWEIG at all four. • Wind against high-fidelity CFD (index of agreement 0.988). • Solar radiation within 2-5% of Radiance. • Sky view within 1 point of Radiance. • Direct sun hours identical to Radiance, hour by hour. Outputs are screening-grade decision support. Comparing design options is more reliable than reading absolute values. Teams decide fast with Infrared City and validate the critical few with full-physics CFD. Partnerships and collaboration models Infrared.city is a spin-off of the Austrian Institute of Technology (AIT) and has recently opened an office in Abu Dhabi under Hub71. It is supported by NVIDIA Inception, Microsoft for Startups, AWS, FFG, Austria Wirtschaftsservice, EIT Urban Mobility, the EIC (D2XCEL) and Leading Cities. We work in four models: 1. Subscriptions through the web platform and plugins. 2. Pay-as-you-go API and enterprise licences for embedding in third-party software. One of the top five AEC software platforms is integrating our API. 3. City live layer as a custom setup per city or operator. The City of Luleå is a paying client. 4. Planning assessments and project work. HafenCity University Hamburg pays for assessments that replace consultant studies. SvN and LAND work with us, and a paid marathon route project ran in Kobe, Japan.
Solution Provider(s): Austrian Institute of Technology GmbH (AIT) – Austrian research and technology organisation; research partner and origin of Infrared City (spun out of its City Intelligence Lab); sector: research and technology, City of Luleå (Luleå kommun) – Swedish municipality; paying client running our live climate layer including a winter risk indicator; sector: public sector and local government, HafenCity University Hamburg – German university for architecture and urban planning; paying client using our simulations for planning assessments; sector: academia and urban planning, SvN Architects + Planners – Canadian architecture and planning practice; design partner that optimised wind comfort of a mixed-use towers scheme with our AI models; sector: architecture and urban planning, Hub71 – Abu Dhabi's global tech ecosystem for startups; our base in Abu Dhabi; sector: innovation ecosystem, Amazon Web Services (AWS) – cloud computing provider; hosts our simulation infrastructure; sector: cloud technology, NVIDIA Inception – NVIDIA's programme for AI startups; member since 2023; sector: AI and technology
Implementation location(s): Live climate layers: Vienna (Austria), Stuttgart (Germany), London (UK). Paying clients: City of Luleå (Sweden), HafenCity University Hamburg (Germany). Project work: Kobe (Japan). Platform and API available globally.
Implementation timeline(s): December 2024 to present (ongoing). New platform launched 13 July 2026.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 2-4 weeks for setup per city.
Desired impact: Main objectives 1. Make climate a standard input to every design and planning decision, by giving architects, planners and developers results at 1 m resolution in seconds instead of days, so that testing every option becomes practical. 2. Replace one-off consultant studies with one comparable baseline. Every design option runs through the same engine and KPIs, so results can be compared and rerun. 3. Keep cities current with a live climate layer for heat, wind, shade and ice, updated hour by hour for the coming days, for operations, routing and events. 4. Put climate intelligence inside other software and AI agents through an API and SDKs. Demonstrated impact • Speed and scale: One run takes 1 to 4 seconds, against days for a consultant study per option. 100 km² of Hamburg ran in 37 seconds and 400 km² of Berlin in 44 seconds. • Adoption: More than 3.2 million simulations have been run on our engine. • Better designs: SvN Architects + Planners used our AI models in a genetic optimization of a mixed-use towers scheme in Mississauga, Canada. It found 11.6% less uncomfortable wind (above 5 m/s) and 9.6% less very uncomfortable wind (above 8 m/s). • Paying clients: The City of Luleå runs our live layer (outcome numbers not yet published). HafenCity University Hamburg pays for planning assessments that replace consultant studies. One of the top five AEC software platforms is integrating our API. Expected impact In hot cities the opportunity is large. In Abu Dhabi, air conditioning accounts for about 60% of annual electricity use, and the urban heat island is responsible for up to 15% of the emirate's yearly cooling load, according to Masdar Institute and MIT research. Climate-informed choices on shade, vegetation, materials and building form at design stage target that load. Our outputs are decision support, so savings depend on the design changes clients make.
Key technologies: • Artificial intelligence: AI surrogate models, trained on physics simulations, predict thermal comfort (UTCI), wind and pedestrian wind comfort at 1 m resolution in 1 to 4 seconds. Results are tested against field measurements, high-fidelity CFD and Radiance. The platform also includes an AI assistant and AI-generated reports. • Physics-based simulation: Direct sun hours, sky view, solar radiation and daylight use deterministic raytracing, on the ground, roofs and facades. • Cloud computing: Serverless, elastic compute scales from zero to about 10,000 cores in minutes, with a capacity of about 1,500 simulations per second today. It runs in our EU cloud or on a customer's own servers. • Digital twins: The live climate layer prepares a city once and updates hour by hour for the coming days from weather forecasts. Users can test changes such as trees, shade or materials. It works with a city's own twin through 3D Tiles (Cesium), exports 3D Tiles and 2D map tiles, and can be queried by place and hour. • APIs, SDKs and agent integration: A REST API (OGC API compliant), Python and TypeScript SDKs, an AI agent skill, Grasshopper, QGIS and ArcGIS plugins, and a web platform. The engine can run inside other software and AI agent workflows. Not used: blockchain and robotic
Unique Characteristics: • One engine for the whole outdoor climate picture. Heat (UTCI), sun and shade, wind, solar radiation and daylight run in a single engine instead of separate tools. To our knowledge, nobody else combines all of these in one engine built for AI agents and integrators. Solar radiation, sky view and daylight also resolve on facades, not just the ground. A 1,800-building district with facades and roofs runs in about 15 seconds. • Physics-trained AI at 1 m in seconds. AI surrogate models trained on physics simulations replace days of CFD setup and compute per design option with a 1 to 4 second run at 1 m resolution. Radiant heat is tested against field measurements at four sites, where it was more accurate than SOLWEIG at all four. • Comparable and reproducible by design. Every option runs against the same baseline and KPIs, so results from different teams and consultants can be compared side by side and rerun. Consultant studies each use their own tool and KPIs. • Headless, portable delivery. The engine needs no interface. It is available as a REST API, Python and TypeScript SDKs, an AI agent skill, Grasshopper, QGIS and ArcGIS plugins, and a web platform. It runs in our EU cloud or on a customer's own servers. • Live layer for digital twins. A city is prepared once and then updated hour by hour for the coming days. It works on a city's own twin through 3D Tiles: users edit, simulate and bring results back. A new site variant takes about 20 seconds. • Business model that scales with use. One usage-based model applies across the platform, Grasshopper and the API: subscriptions, pay-as-you-go API access and enterprise licences. Live layers for cities are custom setups. • Partnership model through embedding. Our engine runs inside one of the top five AEC software platforms, so professionals reach it inside the tools they already use. We also work directly with cities and universities, such as the City of Luleå and HafenCity University Hamburg.
Sustainable Change: • Replication city by city. A city is prepared once and then stays current, with hourly updates for the coming days. The same setup repeats in each new city. The live layer already runs in Vienna, Stuttgart and London, and the City of Luleå is a paying client. It deploys in our EU cloud or on a city's own servers, so cities with data-sovereignty requirements can adopt it. • Scale-up without redesign. The serverless engine scales from zero to about 10,000 cores in minutes, and today handles about 1,500 simulations per second. A run covers anything from a single block to a metropolis: 400 km² of Berlin took 44 seconds. • From one-off studies to a shared baseline. A city can keep one baseline, and every submitted design runs against it with the same KPIs. Planning evidence becomes comparable and reproducible instead of depending on each consultant's tool. HafenCity University Hamburg already pays for planning assessments that replace consultant studies. • Climate checks inside everyday tools. Our engine runs inside one of the top five AEC software platforms. Open interfaces (REST API, SDKs, 3D Tiles and an AI agent skill) let other software and AI agents call it too. Climate analysis can then become a routine step for design professionals, well beyond our direct customers. • Follow-on uses of city-wide data. Street-level, hour-by-hour heat, wind, shade and ice data can feed shade- and heat-aware routing, ambulance placement and event planning, and can be reused by a city's digital twin. • Regulation is moving towards this evidence. In Abu Dhabi, the Estidama Pearl rating is required for a building permit. Its Pearl Building rating system includes a mandatory outdoor thermal comfort strategy credit. Rules like this need fast, comparable evidence at scale, and our screening-grade results support that kind of decision. • Credibility to scale. Per-model validation studies are underway, with a consolidated overview being prepared for publication.

A EUR 1.025M pre-seed round in October 2023, led by xista science ventures with 2bX, Heartfelt Capital, Antler and P3A Ventures. It funded the first commercial release of the platform. 2. Public grants and programme support. Non-dilutive grants of EUR 0.8M and EUR 1.2M, with support from FFG, Austria Wirtschaftsservice (aws), EIT Urban Mobility and the European Innovation Council (D2XCEL). Programme support has also come from AWS, NVIDIA Inception, Microsoft for Startups, Hub71 and Leading Cities. 3. Customer revenue. Client implementations are paid for by the clients: the City of Luleå (live climate layer), HafenCity University Hamburg (planning assessments), an AEC software platform integrating our API, and a paid marathon route project in Kobe, Japan. In total, EUR 3.025M has been raised across equity and grants.

Title: Low-Carbon Intelligent Production Planning for Recycled Plastics
Subtitle: Intelligent production planning through mathematical optimization at two recycling facilities in Shandong and Vietnam raises efficiency and enables rapid re-planning in recycled-plastics production.
Problem Statement: INTCO Recycling is a manufacturer that created a full supply chain with recirculated plastics to make a variety of consumer products. As operations scaled, the planning system faced three pressures that made the current approach no longer sustainable. Plan efficiency degraded as complexity grew. Planning was done manually, and expertise sat with a small number of senior planners with the necessary experience. And re-planning after order changes or disruptions was slow. The company’s production planning was done manually using Excel spreadsheets, and the process depended heavily on a small number of senior planners. Data had to be collected, aggregated, analyzed, and verified across different systems before a correct plan could be produced. This made the workload large and the communication cumbersome, and the result heavily dependent on each planner’s level of experience. The scheduling logic was not written down anywhere, so when personnel changed or the scenario changed, the planning approach would fluctuate noticeably. Manual planning was also limited in its quality. Because a person is constrained by their own attention, the plans were executable but might forgo globally better trade-offs, such as inventory turnover and capacity utilization. A single master plan took several hours to one or two days to compile, and when temporary events such as rush orders, equipment failures, or material delays came up, the planner could only adjust the plan by hand, leaving outcomes hard to guarantee. These limitations carry real costs. Inefficient plans mean higher energy consumption per tonne, greater material loss, and a higher carbon intensity for recycled output. As circular manufacturing capacity grows, increasingly in developing economies, production planning benefits from shifting towards digital and AI-driven solutions so that recycled material is turned efficiently into product.
Solution Overview: Cardinal Operations designed a two-tier rolling planning system, integrating optimization modeling and high-performance mathematical solving with its proprietary commercial solver Cardinal Optimizer, commonly known as COPT. The deployment covers two of INTCO Recycling’s production sites, in Shandong and Vietnam, spanning 90 production lines and 12 product categories. The system splits the planning problem into two coordinated layers, a Master Production Plan that sets the weekly schedule across sites and a Line Plan that sequences daily work on each line. The Master Production Plan operates over a forward four-week horizon and uses a rolling T+3 lock to stabilize near-term decisions, which are then covered by the Line Plan. It solves a large-scale mixed-integer program that optimizes multiple weighted objectives, namely maximizing on-time delivery, minimizing unscheduled volume, minimizing delay, minimizing inventory overhang, minimizing category line-open volatility, minimizing production span, minimizing plan-change rate, and minimizing overtime and idle capacity. The solution accounts for all hard constraints and soft rules covering material availability, vessel and ship dates, customs clearance status, bill-of-materials release, capacity attainment, line-open caps, bottleneck processes, inspection requirements, and order priority, and outputs the master schedule, the total line-open plan, the category line-open plan, and the review ship dates. It also supports order splitting by treating each order number and batch number combination as a unique scheduling entity. The Line Plan considers order, style, line, and day over a three-day horizon from T+1 to T+3. It uses a two-stage algorithm in which COPT first solves a mixed-integer program for line allocation and daily scheduling under hard constraints such as line eligibility, earliest and latest time windows, minimum batch sizes, co-production ratios, line-open caps, inspection rules, and plan stability. An Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search metaheuristic then searches a set of destruction and reconstruction neighborhoods covering violation and inspection risk, cross-category hotspots, order fragmentation, rolling windows, and co-production pairing, in order to minimize changeover cost and maximize continuity by category, frame, and size, ultimately outputting per-line, per-day job sequences with start and end times. A data-integration and governance layer ties together five heterogeneous business systems, including MRP, bill-of-materials, transport management, and production reporting, to form a closed loop of data input, rule configuration, model computation, and result display. The methodology is a co-development in which Cardinal Operations provides the optimization modeling and the COPT solver, built on INTCO Recycling’s industrial scenario, operational data, and subject-matter expertise across its Shandong and Vietnam plants. Because the system encodes scheduling logic as explicit models and configurable rules rather than personal experience, it runs identically at the Shandong and Vietnam sites and can be directly replicated at new facilities.
Solution Provider(s): INTCO Recycling (Intco Recycling Resources Co., Ltd.), a publicly listed manufacturer operating a full supply chain around recovered plastics, converting recycled polystyrene into finished consumer products. Sector: recycling and circular-economy manufacturing.
Implementation location(s): The algorithmic planning took place for two of INTCO Recycling's manufacturing facilities in Shandong, China and Vietnam.
Implementation timeline(s): The project kicked off on September 2nd, 2025 and finalized on July 3rd, 2026, for an end-to-end implementation period of 10 months.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: The estimated time for deployment at a new location is 3 months, covering data integration, local rule configuration, and parallel running before cutover. The scheduling logic is model-based and configurable, so replication requires adaptation rather than redevelopment.
Desired impact: The solution pursues three main objectives. First, to stabilize operations and reduce errors by raising on-time delivery rates, reducing inventory overhang, and accelerating inventory turnover. Second, to build a durable planning system that reacts efficiently to changes, generating new plans quickly and internalizing resource efficiency into the scheduling objective. Third, to minimize plan generation time, with a maximum of thirty minutes for the master plan and ten minutes for the line plan, and best-effort targets of ten and three minutes respectively. The program completed six master-plan trial runs, four in Shandong and two in Vietnam, several of which were compared directly against the manual plan produced for the same batch of orders. On delivery performance, the Shandong batch of May 8 saw the share of delayed orders fall to 4.6 percent against 11.3 percent for the manual benchmark, a reduction of 6.7 percentage points, while average delay fell from 2.51 days to 1.58 days. The Vietnam batch of May 11 reduced average delay from 2.33 days to 1.80 days. The Vietnam batch of May 18 reduced the delayed-order share to 1.5 percent against 2.0 percent while cutting average delay from 2.80 days to 1.45 days, and steady-state on-time delivery was stabilized at 93 to 95 percent once abnormal orders were excluded. Inventory turnover improved in parallel. The number of days between production start and ship date fell by between 1.4 and 4.8 days across batches, most strikingly in the Vietnam batch of May 11, where it dropped from 14.97 days to 10.15 days, a saving of 4.82 days, bringing overall turnover to roughly ten days. Constraint compliance showed the largest shift. The number of orders violating the earliest-start rule fell from more than two hundred under manual planning to single digits or zero under the algorithm, with the count on the Shandong batch of May 8 falling from 392 to 3 and on the Vietnam batch of May 18 from 120 to zero, and with baseline and line-addition rules never broken. Inspection attainment under the algorithm was roughly equal to or better than manual planning, reaching 100 percent on the Vietnam batch of May 18 against 98 percent manually, after earlier batches had been tuned to parity. Planning efficiency gains changed the operating rhythm. A single master-plan computation takes fifteen to twenty-five minutes and a line-plan computation ten minutes, compared with a manual master-plan cycle that previously took several hours to one to two days, and the planning frequency can be raised from weekly updates to a one-to-two-day rhythm, enabling faster response to changes in orders, materials, and capacity. The stage report summarizes the aggregate effect as stable delivery with fewer late days, faster inventory turnover, an overall balance across multiple business objectives, strict respect for scheduling constraints with reduced reliance on individual experience, and significantly better stability, together with direct benefits in planning efficiency, delivery fulfillment, daily line balance, daily inventory turnover, and production cost savings, and indirect benefits from structured data governance.
Key technologies: The solution uses the Cardinal Optimizer (COPT), a high-performance mathematical optimization solver developed by Cardinal Operations. COPT belongs to the decision-making branch of artificial intelligence: rather than predicting or generating content, it computes the best feasible plan from millions of possible combinations under hard physical and business constraints. In this deployment, COPT solves the large-scale mixed-integer programs at the core of both planning tiers, allocating orders to sites, lines, and days while jointly optimizing delivery, inventory, capacity utilization, and plan stability. Because the output is a mathematically verified solution, every plan is guaranteed to respect all encoded constraints, which is the property that allows the system to replace experience-based judgment in a production environment. COPT supports the full range of problem classes relevant to industrial planning, including linear, mixed-integer, and conic programming, and ranks first in multiple problem classes in the independent Mittelmann benchmarks (https://plato.asu.edu/bench.html), the standard public reference for solver performance.
Unique Characteristics: The innovation of this solution lies in how industrial optimization technology is applied. Production planning at INTCO Recycling ran predominantly on spreadsheets and individual experience, and this solution is built specifically for recycled-plastics production. Three differentiating features are specific to this case. The first is the codification of tacit expertise, whereby forty-two expert scheduling rules were structured into twenty master-plan and twenty-two line-plan algorithmic constraints, moving planning knowledge into a configurable and transferable system. The second is a data-governance foundation built for the sector’s realities, with seventeen governance items and more than one hundred tagged lines creating a durable substrate for matching orders to line capabilities. The third is a carbon-ready objective function, designed to incorporate unit energy consumption, time-of-use electricity tariffs, carbon factors, and recycled-batch ratios, providing a direct path from efficiency-first scheduling to efficiency-and-carbon co-optimization. The solution also brings to this sector capabilities that its incumbent practice lacks: plans that balance delivery, inventory turnover, line balance, continuity, and resource efficiency jointly rather than sequentially; hard constraints guaranteed by the solver, with earliest-start violations falling from hundreds of orders to single digits or zero; and re-planning on a one-to-two-day rhythm, supported by a T+3 lock and plan-change-rate control, so rush orders, breakdowns, and material delays are absorbed without destabilizing the near-term schedule. This distinctiveness has been recognized: the case was selected by the China Association of Circular Economy for showcase at its COP31 China Pavilion side event on digital and intelligent circular-economy solutions in Antalya, Türkiye.
Sustainable Change: The solution is designed to be transferred and re-applied efficiently. The scheduling logic is encoded in the optimization models, so deployment at a new site only requires adapting parameters. The two-tier architecture extends across the recycling industry, to recycled metals and paper, and beyond it, to remanufacturing and to discrete and export-oriented manufacturing. The approach can go further through industry-themed model templates. The constraints and objectives common to a sector are built once, and each new adopter configures them to its own lines, products, and rules, which lowers the cost and time of every subsequent deployment. The solution also changes the planner’s job. Instead of building schedules by hand, planners handle exceptions, confirm parameters, and review results, so planning knowledge moves into the system and the roles around it are strengthened. At scale, replacing virgin material with recycled material is itself carbon reduction, and the solution aligns with circular-economy policy and the dual green and digital transition agendas. The manual-to-digital transition in production planning also addresses a wider imbalance. Investment in AI is concentrated in a small number of economies and sectors, and its benefits do not reach every economy equally. In manufacturing, and in recycling in particular, planning decisions that shape energy use, material loss, and delivery are still made by hand. This deployment shows that the transition can be made within months, and it offers a template wherever recycling capacity is built.
Funding Sources: The implementation has been fully funded by INTCO Recycling whereas the development of the underlying solver technology is funded by Cardinal Operations through private venture investment.
Testimonials and Endorsements: The INTCO Recycling production-planning case has been selected by the China Association of Circular Economy (CACE) for showcase at its COP31 China Pavilion side event on digital and intelligent circular-economy solutions in Antalya, Türkiye this November 9-20, 2026. A certificate of selection is being issued by CACE and can be forwarded to the evaluation committee once received, but no public links are available at the time of submission. Formal testimonials from stakeholders and beneficiaries have not yet been collected, though reference contacts at INTCO Recycling can be made available on request.

Title: AEN Circular Intelligence: AI for Second-Life Batteries
Subtitle: NEMA-licensed AI platform that grades end-of-life lithium cells in 90 seconds and repurposes them into PAYG LED bulbs & 5kWh storage for off-grid communities facing 8-hour blackouts.
Problem Statement: Uganda faces a dual energy and waste crisis. 65% of households in Wakiso and peri-urban areas experience 8+ hour blackouts daily or are off-grid, spending 30% of income ($18/month) on kerosene and diesel, causing respiratory illness and loss of income for women-led micro-businesses. Simultaneously, Uganda imports ∼10,000 tons/year of lithium batteries from telecom towers, boda boda e-bikes, and laptops with zero formal recycling infrastructure. These batteries are dumped or burned, leaching lithium/cobalt, while informal waste collectors (143 in our network) earn <$2/day without safety gear or formalization. New lithium storage costs $450/kWh unaffordable. No local AI-based grading or battery passport system exists to safely certify second-life cells, blocking UNBS approval and EU Critical Raw Materials compliance.
Solution Overview: HOW IT WORKS (3-Step Circular Loop): 1. COLLECT: 143 NEMA-registered informal waste collectors + 15 women agents collect end-of-life lithium batteries from E-charging stations, solar systems, laptops and other electronic consumables boda boda e-bikes, and corporate e-waste. Core Technology and Process 1. Battery Collection and Sorting Source Identification : partner with e-waste collection agencies, manufacturers, and individuals to source used or defective lithium-ion batteries. Sorting Mechanism : A proprietary sorting system evaluates battery health based on parameters such as capacity, voltage, internal resistance, and physical integrity. This ensures only viable cells are selected for reuse. 2. Cell Testing and Refurbishment Diagnostic Testing : Each cell undergoes rigorous testing using AI BMS automated equipment to assess its remaining charge capacity and overall performance. Refurbishment Process : Damaged terminals, degraded casings, or minor faults are repaired through manual and robotic processes. Cells with sufficient capacity are marked for integration into final products. 3. Product Design and Assembly Rechargeable LED Bulbs : Design : The bulbs integrate refurbished lithium-ion cells with high-efficiency LED modules, ensuring long-lasting illumination. Applications : Ideal for emergency lighting during blackouts and outdoor activities.
Solution Provider(s): Uganda Industrial Research Institute (UIRI), Public Research & Industrial Development Institution (Government), Sector: Industrial Research & Manufacturing, National Environment Management Authority (NEMA), Government Environmental Regulatory Agency, Sector: Environment & E-Waste Compliance, Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (MoSTI) Uganda, Government Ministry for Science Policy, Sector: Innovation Policy & Public Sector, Savant Analytics Build Cohort 4, Private Technology Company specializing in AI, Business Development Systems, Sector: AI & Digital Infrastructure
Implementation location(s): Kampala, Uganda — Hub in Kamwokya Town, operations across Wakiso & Kampala Districts
Implementation timeline(s): Pilot implementation: January 2024 – Ongoing (current operations) Formal company registration (AEN Holdings): June 2023 – Present NEMA e-waste license obtained: October 2024 Full pilot hub operational with AI grading rig: March 2025 – Present
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3 to 4 months to deploy and pilot in a new geographyBreakdown for UNIDO (if form allows details):Month 1: Site identification, NEMA-equivalent licensing, recruitment of 25 waste collectors & 5 women agents, telecom/e-bike partner MoUMonth 2: Setup of containerized grading hub (AI rig + safety equipment), USSD/MoMo localization, import of 5,000 seed cellsMonth 3: Grading & assembly of 300 BESS units, PAYG onboarding of 200 pilot households, IoT monitoring activationMonth 4: Performance validation (uptime, repayment, diversion metrics) & UNBS-equivalent certification pathway
Desired impact: Main Objectives: To decarbonize and circularize Africa's battery value chain by diverting end-of-life lithium batteries from informal burning/dumping into certified second-life energy storage. To democratize affordable, reliable energy access for peri-urban and off-grid women-led households and micro-businesses facing 8-hour blackouts, using AI to make storage 70% cheaper than new. To advance inclusive digital industrial transformation (Global Digital Compact Objective 2) by formalizing informal waste collectors and women agents into the digital economy via USSD, MoMo PAYG, and digital battery passports. Demonstrated Impact (Pilot: Wakiso, Uganda - Jan 2024 to Present):Environmental: 40 tons of e-waste lithium diverted from landfill/burning; 12,500+ cells tested; 50,000+ cells graded with AI (90-sec grading); Estimated 85 tCO2e emissions avoided from prevented burning and displaced kerosene/diesel. Energy Access & Resilience: 1,200 low-income families connected via PAYG LED, 5kWh BESS; 96.2% uptime vs. 60% grid reliability; Average $18/month energy cost saving per household (70% cheaper than new battery).Inclusive Jobs & Skills: 143 informal e-waste collectors formalized (38% women), income increased 2.5x to $5/day; 15 women agents own last-mile distribution micro-franchises; 8 full-time green jobs created at hub. Digital Inclusion: 100% transactions via MTN MoMo USSD (no smartphone needed); Digital battery passport with QR code launched for traceability aligned to EU Battery Regulation; AI model reduces cell testing time by 95%.Health & Safety: Zero battery fires in graded packs; 100% of collectors trained in safe handling and provided PPE. Expected Impact at Scale (4 Ugandan hubs + 1 regional hub by 2028):500 tons e-waste diverted, 10,000 households powered, 500 green jobs, 1,200 tCO2e avoided, $2.1M saved by low-income users.
Key technologies: 1. Artificial Intelligence (AI) / Machine Learning - Core Innovation: Proprietary AI-powered grading platform ( in house AI BMS) using Computer Vision + Time-series ML trained on 50,000+ lithium cells. Predicts State-of-Health (SoH), Remaining Useful Life (RUL), and safe second-life application (LED vs. 5kWh BESS) in 90 seconds vs. 8 hours manual. Accuracy: 94.3% vs. lab test. Custom BMS (Battery Management System) with IoT sensors for real-time monitoring of voltage, temperature, SoC. GSM module transmits performance data every 6 hours. Enables 96.2% uptime tracking, predictive failure alerts, and PAYG remote lock/unlock. Edge computing on ESP32 for low-connectivity operation. 3. Digital Infrastructure & Data Ecosystems: USSD + MTN MoMo API integration for offline-first PAYG collections ($0.22/day), collector payments, and inventory tracking no smartphone required. Cloud dashboard (AWS) for hub management. Digital Battery Passport: QR code system storing cell origin, chemistry (NMC/LFP), SoH, safety certification, and chain-of-custody aligned to EU Battery Regulation 2023/1542 and UNBS standards. 4. Circular Manufacturing & Green Tech: Low-tech containerized remanufacturing hub design (low capex $15k) for cell disassembly, grading, re-assembly into certified packs with fire-retardant casings. Reuse of telecom tower and e-bike battery waste streams. Not used: Blockchain (too costly for low-income users), Robotics (manual disassembly safer for second-life).Short version if character limit: AI/ML grading (94.3% acc), IoT BMS with GSM, USSD/MoMo PAYG digital infra, Digital Battery Passport QR, Containerized circular manufacturing.
Unique Characteristics: 1. Technology Innovation - AI makes waste bankable: Everyone tests batteries manually. We are the first in East Africa to deploy AI that grades a cell in 90 seconds with 94.3% accuracy, turning hazardous e-waste into a certified financial asset. This reduces grading cost by 95% and unlocks telecom tower & e-bike waste — a $2.4B untapped feedstock in Africa that no one else can process safely at scale. 2. Business Model Innovation - Formalizing the informal via PAYG micro-franchise: We don't compete with 143 informal collectors we formalize them. Collectors' income 2.5x ($5/day) via MoMo, with PPE + training. 15 women agents own last-mile distribution (not employees). This is inclusive platform economics, not extractive recycling. 100% USSD, zero smartphone barrier. 3. Financing Mechanism Innovation - $0.22/day energy = fintech meets circular economy: New BESS costs $800 impossible. Our second-life BESS at 70% discount + PAYG micro-lease ($0.22/day) matches kerosene spend, enabling 1,200 low-income families to own assets. Remote IoT lock de-risks default (repayment rate 92%). This unlocks carbon credits + battery-as-a-service revenue. 4. Delivery & Partnership Model - Containerized + Telco waste stream: $15k containerized hub (vs. $250k factory), deployable in 3-4 months anywhere. Exclusive MoUs with telecom tower operators for battery waste (predictable supply) + e-bike companies — creates circular loop where their waste powers communities near their towers. Digital Battery Passport (QR) creates trust for regulators (NEMA, UNBS) and future EU export. 5. Systemic Differentiation: We solve 3 crises with 1 product: e-waste pollution + energy poverty + informal worker exclusion. Aligned to Global Digital Compact Objective 2: inclusive digital industrial transformation where women waste workers become digital economy participants.In one line for judges: AEN is not a battery company — it is an AI-powered circular industrial platform that turns Africa's fastest-growing waste stream into affordable, certified energy for the people most affected by blackouts.
Sustainable Change: Potential for Systemic Change — Beyond Immediate Implementation:1. Industrial System Change: Creating Africa's Second-Life Battery Standard 1. Today, Uganda has NO certification pathway for second-life batteries — so all reuse is informal and dangerous. Our NEMA license + UNBS certification pathway + Digital Battery Passport (QR: origin, SoH, safety) will become the national standard. This formalizes an entire informal sector (estimated 5,000+ collectors in Uganda alone), shifting from burning/dumping to safe circular manufacturing. Follow-on effect: Unlocks EU Battery Regulation-compliant exports, making Uganda a hub for circular batteries, not just a dumping ground. 2. Economic System Change: Waste Collectors to Green Industrial Workforce Our model proves informal waste work can be dignified digital work. 143 collectors now earn 2.5x via MoMo, with PPE and data history. This creates a replicable workforce formalization model for all e-waste streams (phones, solar). By 2028, 500 jobs — by 2030, 10,000+ across East Africa via telco partnership replication. Women agents (15 now) become energy entrepreneurs, shifting gender norms in energy distribution. Systemic effect: From linear take-make-dump to circular industrial jobs that youth want. 3. Energy System Change: Decentralized Resilience Grid reliability in peri-urban Uganda is 60%. Each 5kWh BESS is a mini-resilience node. 1,200 units = 6MWh distributed storage that prevents diesel use during 8-hour blackouts. At 10,000 units, this is a Virtual Power Plant for low-income communities — a model for climate adaptation where storage is owned by users, not utilities. Replicable in any country with blackout + e-waste (Nigeria, Kenya, India). 4. Digital System Change: Inclusive Digital Transformation (GDC Objective 2) 100% USSD, no smartphone needed — yet every transaction creates digital footprint for unbanked women and collectors. This is how Global Digital Compact becomes real: waste workers enter digital economy via MoMo, energy data builds credit history. Our containerized hub + AI model can be licensed to 14 countries in 3-4 months per geography, using same telecom waste stream MoU template. 5. Replication & Scale-Up Pathway: Uganda: 1 hub → 4 hubs by 2027 (Wakiso, Kampala, Mbarara, Gulu) = 10k families Regional: Kenya, Rwanda via tower partner replication (same battery chemistry, same MoUs) — $15k capex per hub, 3-4 month deployment Global South: Licensing of AI grading rig to e-waste cooperatives in Nigeria, South Africa, Philippines Policy: Digital Battery Passport data informs NEMA/UNBS to create Extended Producer Responsibility policy for lithium. Sustained Change: Once AI grading exists and certification exists, the market can never go back to informal burning. We are building irreversible industrial infrastructure.

Title: African Investments Dashboard: AI Matching Capital to African Industry
Subtitle: An AI-powered platform matching 33,000+ institutional investors with African enterprises and industrial projects seeking capital, across all 54 African countries.
Problem Statement: African manufacturers, agro-processors, industrial SMEs and energy and infrastructure projects face a financing gap widely estimated in the hundreds of billions of dollars. The core failure is often not a lack of capital but of discovery and matching: international and African institutional investors cannot efficiently find, screen and compare investable industrial opportunities across 54 fragmented markets, while promoters - particularly those outside the main financial hubs, and many women- and youth-led businesses - lack the networks, data and visibility to reach the right investors. Deal origination remains relationship-driven, expensive and slow; information is unstructured (pitch decks, PDFs, emails); and there is no common taxonomy linking what a company produces to what an investor, buyer or partner is looking for. The result is under-capitalised industry, missed trade linkages and slower inclusive industrialisation.
Solution Overview: The African Investments Dashboard (AIDB, www.africaninvestments.ai) is an AI-powered digital marketplace, built on Salesforce, that matches African companies and projects seeking capital with institutional investors. HOW IT WORKS 1. Intake - any company can list a capital raise free of charge, via an online profile or simply by emailing a pitch deck; AI tools extract structured data (sector, country, transaction type, amount sought, stage) from unstructured documents. 2. Classification - opportunities, companies and investors are coded against a standard taxonomy (60+ sectors, 12 transaction types, all 54 African countries) and UNSPSC product/service codes using text-embedding similarity models - a product-coding module developed under the USAID Prosper Africa programme. 3. Matching - each opportunity is scored against the stated mandates of 33,000+ institutional investors (sector, geography, ticket size, asset class) and pushed to matched investors through personalised alerts. The companion Africa Business Opportunities Dashboard (80,000+ registered users) sends up to 2.2 million personalised matched-opportunity emails a year. 4. Engagement and closing - engagement data (opens, clicks, enquiries) informs follow-up; a premium, success-fee-only capital-raising service manages investor introductions through to closing. Opportunities are also profiled in sector and country Digital Deal Books and presented at AFSIC - Investing in Africa, our annual London summit (1,500+ attendees; 350+ deals worth US$10bn+ presented in 2025). METHODOLOGIES AND TECHNOLOGIES Salesforce Enterprise CRM and Account Engagement (Pardot) marketing automation; AI/large-language-model document extraction and data enrichment; vector embeddings and nearest-neighbour search for product-code matching; cloud APIs (AWS); automated workflows and match scoring. PARTNERSHIPS AND COLLABORATION MODEL AIDB works through 130+ pan-African partners - investment promotion agencies, chambers of commerce, stock exchanges, law firms and corporate advisers - who source and verify deal flow, and with governments, DFIs and UN/development agencies that use the platform and Deal Books to promote country and sector pipelines (e.g. Deal Books for the UK Government's Manufacturing Africa and GET.invest programmes; USAID Prosper Africa via DAI; the Tanzania Investment Growth Facility with ESRF and UNDP Tanzania). The model is free to list, funded by success fees and sponsorship, keeping it accessible to MSMEs.
Solution Provider(s): Africa Events Limited (AFSIC - Investing in Africa; sister company; organiser of a leading annual Africa investment summit in London and country investment summits; events and investor engagement), Salesforce (technology platform provider - Enterprise CRM and Account Engagement; AIDB won the 2022 Salesforce Partner Innovation Award for Financial Services; technology), Pan-African partner network of 130+ investment promotion agencies, chambers of commerce, stock exchanges, law firms and corporate advisers (deal-flow sourcing and verification; investment promotion and financial services), DAI Global (prime contractor for USAID Prosper Africa; implementation partner for platform enhancements 2022-2024; international development), Economic and Social Research Foundation (ESRF) with UNDP Tanzania (Tanzania Investment Growth Facility - investor mobilisation for the Tanzania Investor Summit 2026; research and development)
Implementation location(s): Pan-African - all 54 African countries, delivered digitally; operated from Jersey and London (UK) with team members in Botswana, South Africa and Ethiopia; in-person deal-making at AFSIC (London) and country investor summits (e.g. Tanzania Investor Summit, Arusha, June 2026)
Implementation timeline(s): Ongoing - in continuous operation (African Investments Limited est. 2014); USAID Prosper Africa-funded platform enhancements Oct 2022 - mid-2024; Tanzania Investment Growth Facility (ESRF/UNDP) Jan - Jun 2026
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3-6 months (the platform is cloud-based and already covers all 54 African countries; a new-country pilot mainly requires onboarding local partners, a pipeline call for opportunities, a country Deal Book and matched investor outreach)
Desired impact: OBJECTIVES 1. Close the information and matching gap that keeps capital from African industrial, manufacturing, agro-processing, energy and infrastructure enterprises. 2. Give MSMEs - wherever they are located - free, digital access to a global institutional investor base. 3. Generate structured, comparable pipeline data that governments, investment promotion agencies and DFIs can use to promote investment. DEMONSTRATED IMPACT - Network: 33,000+ institutional investors, 200,000+ mailable business contacts and 80,000+ registered users on the Africa Business Opportunities Dashboard; 11m+ digital impressions a year. - Pipeline: US$50bn+ of live deals profiled; 1,000+ companies profiled for investor matching in 2024-25; c. 3,900 formal deal submissions; 350+ deals worth US$10bn+ presented at AFSIC 2025. - Capital mobilised: US$113m+ in closed transactions attributed to platform and AFSIC introductions, including US$103m (debt/equity) for Husk Power Systems, a clean-energy minigrid provider in West Africa; US$10m for BURN Manufacturing, a Kenyan clean-cookstove manufacturer; and US$10m debt for a West African aviation company. - Trade: US$1bn+ of trade opportunities originated; US$100m of export trade executed following USAID Prosper Africa-funded platform enhancements. - Climate co-benefits: closed deals include clean-energy and clean-cooking manufacturers, supporting energy access and reduced emissions.
Key technologies: - Artificial intelligence: large language models to extract structured deal data from pitch decks, teasers and PDFs and to enrich company and investor records; text-embedding models with vector nearest-neighbour search to assign UNSPSC product/service codes to companies and opportunities; algorithmic investor-opportunity match scoring. - Cloud CRM and data platform: Salesforce Enterprise with custom data model for opportunities, investors, partners and scoring, automated with Flows and Apex. - Marketing automation: Salesforce Account Engagement (Pardot) for personalised, matched opportunity distribution at scale (up to 2.2m emails a year) and engagement tracking. - Cloud infrastructure and APIs: AWS-hosted matching service (API Gateway, Python/FastAPI). - Web platforms: africaninvestments.ai, businessopportunities.ai and digital sector/country Deal Books.
Unique Characteristics: - Africa-wide scope and scale: one platform covering all 54 African countries, 60+ sectors and 12 transaction types, built on an institutional investor network of 33,000+. - Push, not pull: instead of waiting for investors to search, AI matching proactively pushes each opportunity to the investors whose mandates fit - turning a static listing into active deal distribution. - Frictionless MSME onboarding: companies list free of charge, simply by emailing a pitch deck; AI converts unstructured documents into structured, comparable investor-ready profiles. - Common product taxonomy: UNSPSC coding links what a company produces to what investors, buyers and trade partners seek, enabling both investment and buyer-supplier/trade matching. - Aligned business model: free to list; the premium capital-raising service is success-fee only (no upfront fee), so companies pay only when capital is raised. - Digital plus in-person: AI matching is combined with face-to-face deal-making at the AFSIC summit in London, country investment summits and 32 in-country investor road-trips, increasing conversion. - Recognised innovation: winner of the 2022 Salesforce Partner Innovation Award for Financial Services.
Sustainable Change: - Market infrastructure, not a one-off project: the platform builds a persistent, structured dataset of African industrial pipeline and investor mandates that improves matching with every deal and can inform policy, DFI programming and investment promotion. - Replication through partners: investment promotion agencies, chambers and governments can plug in their own pipelines - country and sector Digital Deal Books have already been produced for the UK Government's Manufacturing Africa and GET.invest programmes and for the Tanzania Investment Growth Facility (ESRF/UNDP) - so the model can be replicated country by country at low marginal cost. - Crowding in private capital: by cutting search and transaction costs, it makes smaller-ticket industrial deals and frontier markets viable for international investors, mobilising private finance alongside DFI and UN programmes. - Inclusion: free, digital access widens participation to MSMEs outside the main financial hubs. - Scale-up pathway: integration with UNIDO and other UN programmes (e.g. investment promotion and supplier-development initiatives) could deliver dedicated industrial deal pipelines, matched investor outreach and investor forums for target countries, and extend the model to other developing regions.
Funding Sources: - Self-funded by African Investments Limited and its sister company Africa Events Limited, from commercial revenues (success fees on capital raised, AFSIC event sponsorship and delegate revenues, bespoke Deal Book and investment promotion services) - no equity or grant funding required for core operations. - USAID Prosper Africa (via prime contractor DAI): two subcontracts that funded platform enhancements and network development - ATI-013 Digital Trade Services (US$179,382.50; product-coding module, Dashboard UX/UI, US network development, trade helpdesk) and ATI-005 Buyer-Supplier Advisory and Support Services (US$152,820; African network outreach, buyer identification, trade intermediary linkages), 2022-2024. - Client-funded deployments: e.g. ESRF/UNDP Tanzania Investment Growth Facility (2026) - investor segmentation and mobilisation and Deal Book dissemination for the Tanzania Investor Summit; Deal Books for the UK Government's Manufacturing Africa and GET.invest programmes.
