Title: AGIBOT G2 Humanoid Robot for Production Line Loading and Unloading
Subtitle: Industrial embodied AI humanoid robot with visual-force perception, real-robot RL, and fleet scheduling for precise, flexible, 24/7 loading/unloading in 3C and chip testing lines.
Problem Statement: Legacy automation faces high changeover costs, poor compatibility across machines/workstations, idle fixed assets when capacity fluctuates, and low reliability of repetitive manual loading/unloading, where fatigue can cause tray mishandling, material mixing, pressing, drops, and damage to high-value materials.
Solution Overview: AGIBOT G2 is an industrial-grade humanoid embodied AI robot integrated with Genie Studio. It uses multi-angle/head-mounted cameras, 360° fisheye, LiDAR and ultrasonic perception, high-DOF force-controlled dual arms, and visual-force perception to locate materials, grasp single items, identify loading area coordinates and pose, perform adaptive precision loading, and complete closed-loop unloading and return. Real-robot reinforcement learning and end-to-end embodied algorithms enable hour-level task migration, sub-millimeter closed-loop control, and adaptation to tray/port tolerances. The solution supports multi-robot fleet scheduling, autonomous charging, hot-swappable batteries, AGV docking, and MES/EAP integration.Deployment with Longcheer Technology in a 3C precision manufacturing line validated >99.9% success rate, 19–20s task cycle time, and >99.9% yield.
Solution Provider(s): Shanghai Longcheer Technology Co., Ltd. (Longcheer Technology)——leading global smart product ODM; 3C electronics manufacturing; provides 3C precision manufacturing line scenarios and validation
Implementation location(s): Nanchang, Jiangxi Province ——Longcheer Technology 3C precision manufacturing production line, located in Nanchang High-tech Industrial Development Zone
Implementation timeline(s): Longcheer Technology: 2026.3–present.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 2–6 weeks
Desired impact: Main objectives: reduce changeover costs, overcome legacy robot compatibility limits, improve asset utilization, replace unreliable repetitive manual loading/unloading, and enable flexible 24/7 precision manufacturing. Demonstrated impact: Longcheer Technology Nanchang production line: G2 completed 2,283 precision loading/unloading tasks in an 8-hour live broadcast with 100% success rate and zero failures; adapted to a 20-second cycle high-speed production line, with a single process taking only 18–20 seconds, zero major anomalies in 8 hours of continuous operation, overall operational success rate above 99.5%, a single robot completing 310 products per hour, peaking at 316. In the 64-hour tablet mass-production quality inspection live broadcast, total robot operations reached 64,828 pieces, task success rate 99.99%, operational precision fluctuation 2mm, cycle time 22 seconds.
Key technologies: AI、robotics
Unique Characteristics: Humanoid embodied AI robot instead of fixed automation; positioned as an industrial-grade interactive embodied operation robot, working as a "formal employee" on the production line; hour-level real-robot RL task migration, learning precision flexible operations in one hour; plug-and-play across different machines; sub-millimeter visual-force closed-loop control and micron-level contact flexible assembly; world's first cross-wrist force-controlled arm; 5-DOF waist simulating human bending and twisting motions; multi-robot collaborative scheduling and data sharing; 24/7 operation via battery hot-swap and autonomous charging; 360° surround perception safety system; full closed-loop operation from loading to finished product return.
Sustainable Change: The solution drives industrial embodied intelligence from R&D demonstration to scaled deployment. Through the joint laboratory and low-code toolchain, robots can quickly adapt to new tasks, improving equipment utilization and shortening debugging cycles, forming a sustainable closed loop of "toolchain development – scenario validation – commercial deployment." It can be replicated across 3C electronics, automotive parts, and other precision manufacturing sectors, alleviating labor shortages and fatigue-induced quality variability, enhancing supply chain resilience, and leveraging an open platform to export toolchain and data capabilities to customers and partners for broader scaled adoption.
Primary thematic focus area: Embodied AI, Industrial Robotics and Smart Manufacturing
Summary: AGIBOT's G2 is a humanoid robot for loading and unloading on 3C and chip-testing lines, demonstrated at Longcheer Nanchang with 2,283 tasks and no failures. Its strength is a measured, filmed result on a real line; its weakness is a single-site footprint and a blank funding answer, which caps application at band 4 and removes finance from the assessment.

Name of your organization: Yalong River Hydropower Development Company, Ltd. ("Yalong Hydro")
Title: AI-Powered Green Energy Solution: Building Resilience in Harsh Scenarios
Subtitle: Huawei and Yalong Hydro build smart plants at the world’s largest hydro-wind-solar base, moving staff off 4,000 m sites to remote control: 92%+ forecast accuracy, power loss halved, safer plateau O&M.
Problem Statement: The growth rate of renewable energy installed capacity has already outpaced that of operational capacity. According to the IEA's Renewables 2025 report, global renewable energy installed capacity is expected to increase by approximately 4600 GW from 2025 to 2030, with PV accounting for about 80% of this addition. More and more PV power plants are being built in harsh environments and remote areas, such as river basins, plateaus, deserts, and islands, as well as in emerging economies with a shortage of professional O&M personnel. From the Andes in South America to the Himalayas and the East African Plateau, high-altitude regions often have the best solar resources, but power plants in these areas are also the most difficult to maintain and operate. The bottleneck of energy transition is shifting from "installation" to "safe, efficient, and large-scale operation." The Yalong River Basin is the most extreme example of this challenge. Located in southwest China, the Yalong River Basin Hydro-Wind-Solar Energy Base is the world's largest energy base integrating hydro, wind, and solar power. It is also one of the four major hydro- wind-solar energy bases that China has planned to build from 2026 to 2030. The total installed capacity will reach 78 million kW by 2035, including 39 million kW of wind and solar power, distributed across multiple plants each with a capacity of over 1 million kW. So far, about 3.3 million kW of wind and solar power installations has been put into operation. Among them, the Kela PV Plant is the world's first GW-level energy complex built on permafrost at an altitude of 4600 meters. Most of the plants are located across the western Sichuan plateau at altitudes of over 4,000 meters, featuring low oxygen levels, extreme cold, intense ultraviolet radiation, and harsh volatile weather. Utility-scale renewable energy plants have long been facing the O&M challenges of large area, low efficiency, and lack of safety warning. 1. Harsh high-altitude conditions endanger workers’ health and safety: Large PV and storage plants are typically built in deserts, plateaus and mountains. Plants on the western Sichuan plateau sit above 4,000 m, where oxygen is only about 60% of sea-level levels, snow lasts eight to nine months and temperatures can fall below -30°C. Gales, blizzards and intense UV radiation are frequent. In extreme weather, roads ice over and signals fail, making travel difficult and site work hazardous. 2. High labor costs and talent shortages: A single PV plant can span dozens of square kilometers with widely dispersed devices, requiring many staff stationed at remote sites for manual inspection. Recruiting O&M personnel is increasingly difficult, versatile experts in power electronics and energy storage are scarce, and the cost of keeping staff at remote sites rises every year. 3. Low manual O&M efficiency: Engineers must walk row by row past PV modules, inverters and battery cabins, so inspection cycles are long, blind spots are common and responses are slow. One engineer can cover only a limited area per day, so frequent full-site coverage is impossible. Fault diagnosis depends on individual experience, with no systematic decision support; different staff may reach different conclusions on the same fault, newcomers take years to become proficient, and veterans’ know-how is rarely captured. Without early warning, faults are found only after energy yield has been lost. 4. High risks in abnormal conditions: Battery cabin overheating, DC arcing and grounding faults must be detected and handled on site, which is slow and difficult at high altitude. Delayed handling can lead to equipment damage and even safety accidents. 5. Unpredictable generation: Complex terrain and local microclimates such as gales, blizzards, hail and sudden cloud cover lower power forecasting accuracy, disrupting grid dispatch, hydro-wind-solar coordination and power trading, and raising curtailment risk.
Solution Overview: Used by the Yalong River Hydro-Wind-Solar Base, the world’s largest of its kind, the solution covers wind and PV plants totaling over 3.3 GW above 4,000 m, including the 1 GW Kela PV Plant, the world’s first energy complex built on permafrost at 4,600 m. Architecture: A three-layer system links plants, regional maintenance centers and a headquarters control center, enabling “device-side sensing, regional collaboration and central control”. Staff move from high-altitude sites to remote control. 1. Plant layer (sensing and execution): Drones and robots collect equipment, environmental and safety data. Huawei inverters and ESSs carry built-in AI chips, so devices sense and diagnose themselves, with data from millions of devices. 2. Regional layer (collaboration): Shared drone systems inspect PV modules, wind turbines and power lines and identify defects automatically. Centers coordinate repairs and emergency response across plants. 3. Headquarters layer (decision-making): An AI-agent-based smart O&M platform unifies monitoring, diagnosis, scheduling, energy efficiency management and AI applications, assessing device health, issuing fault warnings and recommending optimizations, shifting O&M from reactive to proactive. Key capabilities: 1. Robot-based inspection: The inverter’s smart I-V curve diagnosis locates faulty strings plant-wide, then drones fly auto-planned routes to confirm module-level faults. Routine inspection needs no site visits, raising O&M efficiency by 80%. Wheeled robots patrol ESS and substation areas 24/7, and rail robots read relay-room meters with over 90% accuracy, keeping staff out of electrical hazard zones. 2. Fault warning: The PV health guard uses fault-mechanism models to warn of inverter component faults (recall over 85%, precision over 90%), cutting unplanned downtime by 75%. The ESS health guard runs 10+ AI mechanism models on hundreds of millions of data points daily, warning of risks seven days ahead (cell-level recall over 97%, precision over 95%) and reducing ESS energy loss by 87%. 3. O&M cockpit: Digital twin maps faults and staff to exact locations; cost-benefit evaluation ranks faults by recoverable energy; route planning and offline GPS navigation guide staff across vast, weak-signal plateau sites. O&M efficiency rises by 50%, and Kela’s annual yield is expected to grow by 2% (about CNY 1 million). 4. Knowledge assistant: Senior experts make up only about 20% of the team. An LLM-based Q&A system turns their experience, troubleshooting guides and case history into a knowledge base, so newcomers get diagnosis advice in natural language and train faster. 5. Power forecasting: Huawei Cloud’s Yunxi weather model shortens update intervals from 10 hours to 1 hour and refines resolution from 30x30 km to 3x3 km, improving weather forecast accuracy by 20%. Inverter MPP estimation filters out curtailment data, and a mixture-of-experts model converts weather into power. Kela reaches 92.54% ultra-short-term and 92.36% short-term accuracy, 3.5% above conventional methods, reducing grid penalty risk. 6. PV+ESS scheduling: A 106 MWh ESS paired with Kela’s 1 GW PV, controlled by a millisecond-level smart power plant controller, turns volatile output into a smooth, predictable curve and shifts low-price energy to peak hours for spot-market arbitrage. Scheduled-curve pass rate exceeds 96%, with grid-point deviation below 1%.
Solution Provider(s): Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd. is a global leading ICT and digital power solutions provider. As a key technology partner, Huawei provides the cloud-edge synergy AI platform, Yunxi weather model, power forecasting and precise power allocation algorithm authorization, and high-altitude Smart PV/ESS equipment. Huawei also works with the joint innovation center to carry out 11 R&D programs. Industry: ICT/renewable power
Implementation location(s): The locations of the projects that have been implemented are as follows: Yalong River Basin, Sichuan Province, China (western Sichuan plateau, more than 4000 meters above sea level): Kela PV Plant phase 1 (Yajiang County, Garzê Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture); Suorong PV Plant (Litang County, Garzê Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture); Chabulang PV Plant (Muli County, Liangshan Yi Autonomous Prefecture); and Labashan Wind Farm (Liangshan Prefecture) . This solution will be launched globally, including key regions such as Asia Pacific, Middle East, Africa, and Latin America.
Implementation timeline(s): In September 2023, Huawei and Yalong Hydro jointly established a joint innovation lab to carry out joint R&D on the entire lifecycle of power plants. In 2024, plant-level programs on topics such as intelligent O&M and fault warning were first implemented and delivered in the first phase of the Kela PV Plant. According to the promotion plan, the regional maintenance center and group's centralized control AI agents will be deployed in Q1 2027, and then be promoted to all power plants across the entire energy base in Q2.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: The solution adopts a modular design and can be deployed in three levels based on local conditions. Regions with limited funds and infrastructure can start from the first level. Level 1: Rapid deployment of AI software (about 3 to 6 months). Directly integrate inverter and SCADA data for the existing power plants. Implement AI-based power forecasting, precise power allocation, and inverter predictive maintenance. No additional hardware is required. The investment is the lowest and the effect is the fastest. Level 2: Intelligent inspection deployment (about 6 to 9 months). Add drones and other physical sensing devices to replace manual daily inspection. Level 3: Unattended operation (about 12 to 18 months). Deploy the multi-agent O&M, centralized control center, and regional maintenance system to implement remote centralized control and onsite less-staffed operation. Each level includes three steps: onsite evaluation and data ingestion, model calibration based on the local climate and terrain, and pilot operation and KPI verification. Edge inference ensures that the plants can continue to operate when the communication is interrupted, reducing the requirements for network conditions in remote areas.
Desired impact: Objectives: 1. Use end-to-end AI to manage wind and PV plants above 4,000 m remotely, ensuring safe operation and freeing workers from high-risk plateau environments. 2. Replace reactive response with predictive maintenance and unmanned inspection, reducing downtime and O&M costs while minimizing disturbance to fragile meadow and permafrost ecosystems on the cold plateau. 3. Improve power forecasting and generation control so that more stable clean electricity from the plateau can be fed into the grid. Verified impact of the pilot project: 1. Environment: clean electricity and carbon reduction (1) Carbon reduction: Based on its designed annual output of 2 billion kWh, the Kela PV Plant displaces coal-fired power equivalent to about 650,000 tons of standard coal, avoiding over 1.6 million tons of CO2 a year. (2) Grid integration: More accurate forecasting reduces the risk of scheduling deviation and PV curtailment, maximizing the value of existing clean energy assets. (3) Ecosystem protection: Drones and robots perform inspections, reducing how often vehicles and personnel enter the site and minimizing damage to high-altitude meadows and permafrost. Early fire detection protects the meadows. 2. Worker health and safety (1) Machines replace manual work: Routine inspection, temperature measurement, meter reading and post-operation confirmation are performed by drones, robots and one-click sequential control, greatly reducing outdoor work in conditions of oxygen deficiency, extreme cold and intense UV radiation. (2) From plateau to plain: Operations are monitored remotely from the centralized control center in Chengdu, at an altitude of about 500 m, instead of on site, significantly reducing the time workers spend above 4,000 m. (3) Fewer emergency repairs: In December 2025, all 5,236 inverters at Kela PV Plant Phase I were diagnosed, and four devices with abnormal insulation resistance were identified before failure, allowing planned maintenance instead of emergency repairs in harsh weather. 3. Grid resilience and economic value (1) Power forecasting: Short-term forecasting accuracy reaches 92.36% and ultra-short-term accuracy 92.54%, about 3.5 percentage points higher than existing service providers (88.90% and 88.92%, respectively). (2) Generation control: PV+ESS coordination raises the tracking precision of generation control to 98%, reducing deviations from generation plans. (3) Cost advantages from technological innovation: a) Visualized construction supervision based on high-precision 3D modeling avoids 40% of construction quality issues. b) The intelligent O&M cockpit built on Huawei’s digital foundation improves O&M efficiency by 50% compared with traditional methods, saving US$0.85 million a year. c) A PR (performance ratio) indicator system that uses data to guide O&M increases annual energy yield by 3%, generating additional revenue of CNY 1.51 million a year. d) The intelligent self-cleaning function of Huawei’s 300KTL inverters (330KTL outside China) saves about US$2.5 million in labor costs over the project lifecycle. e) Huawei Cloud’s Yunxi weather model significantly improves weather forecast accuracy, further enhancing PV power and generation forecasting and enabling more precise generation schedules to better fulfil power supply obligations. 4. Full-scale rollout targets (industry benchmarking based on similar smart plants) (1) Improve O&M efficiency by 100%. (2) Achieve zero safety accidents at plateau sites. (3) Monitor wind and PV plants in real time and perform equipment status analysis, routine operations and troubleshooting remotely, ending 24-hour on-site attendance. Staff will be relocated from plateau plants to regional maintenance centers, significantly improving their working conditions. (4) Expand coverage from about 3.3 GW in operation to about 17 GW by 2030, and eventually to all 39 GW of wind and solar capacity across the base.
Key technologies: AI-based weather and energy forecasting: 1. Yunxi weather model: This model uses parameter identification based on recurrent neural networks and generative spatiotemporal prediction technology based on LLMs. It integrates satellite remote sensing, weather reanalysis data, and onsite weather data, and corrects numerical weather forecasts for the complex terrain and local microclimate of the western Sichuan plateau. The corrected data is used as the weather data input for power forecasting. 2. Plant-level power forecasting model family: The strategy of "plant-specific solutions, zonal modeling, and multi-mode optimal selection" is used. Time series submodels (LSTM/Transformer) are dynamically selected based on weather types to produce short-term and ultra-short-term power forecasts. 3. Differentiated power allocation algorithm based on MPPT capability estimation: Power is accurately allocated to each inverter based on its real-time MPPT capability, replacing the traditional equal power allocation strategy. 4. Device degradation forecasting model: Based on key parameters such as inverter capacitance attenuation, insulation resistance, IGBT junction temperature, and relay degradation, the time series forecasting and anomaly detection algorithms (Isolation Forest and Autoencoder) are used to output the fault risk level and maintenance suggestions. AI diagnosis and visual recognition: 1. IV & CV co-diagnosis: This function integrates I-V scanning and AI image recognition, and supports two integrated modes: "ultra-fast mode (I-V full scan → CV precise screening)" and "refined mode (concurrent I-V + CV full inspection)". This enables precise fault locating from the string level to the module level. 2. CV defect identification: Based on the object detection and image segmentation algorithms, more than 10 types of defects can be identified from visible light and infrared images, such as hot spots, cracks, zero-current strings, diode faults, blade leading edge corrosion, gel coat peeling, meter reading, and meadow fire. The model is trained based on the images of hundreds of power plant scenarios in China. 3. String-level diagnosis based on the integration of I-V curves and mechanistic models: String-level diagnosis is performed based on the string I-V data reported by inverters and mechanistic models are used to screen out low-efficiency or zero-output strings. Large models and multiple AI agents: 1. Multi-agent technology: The multi-agent framework based on cloud-edge-device synergy is used, and the orchestrator-subagent mode and agent team mode can optimize accurate task breakdown and serial/parallel flow control, supporting autonomous operations of O&M agents. 2. Knowledge ontology and RAG: The domain knowledge base covers the electric power industry standards and regulations, grid assessment rules, maintenance manuals, historical high-quality reports and cases, and plant O&M knowledge ontology. Semantic search and keyword search are used together to automatically generate structured documents such as inspection reports, maintenance policies, and assessment appeal materials. IoT and digital twin: 1. Multi-source sensing devices: Visible light/infrared drones, inspection robots, electronic fences, smart locks, and power and environment monitoring devices. 2. Digital twin: The orthographic image (DOM) of a power plant is segmented based on photogrammetry and aerial triangulation calculation. The geographical coordinates of each PV string are automatically identified and automatically matched with the site construction CAD drawing to support automatic planning of inspection routes and accurate defect locating. 3. High-altitude power electronics: The smart inverters designed for high-altitude environments feature the IP66 rating and triple DC safety protection, and can run stably in permafrost environments at an altitude of 4600 m. The inverters' MPPT capability is estimated to implement intelligent power distribution.
Unique Characteristics: 1. Closed loop vs. single-point automation: One of the few harsh-environment solutions with full-chain collaboration among multiple AI agents Most smart-plant pilots deploy single-point modules such as drone inspection, intelligent monitoring or fault diagnosis, which are still connected manually. This solution uses a workflow engine and six AI agents to streamline the entire process, from inspection and defect detection to scheduling, work permits, maintenance and operations. Key decisions are confirmed by people, and O&M shifts from AI-assisted to AI-driven. Rather than “separate systems linked by hand”, it achieves collaboration at the system level. 2. Plateau-specific vs. general-purpose models: Verified on site in permafrost at 4,600 m Most solutions apply general-purpose models trained for plains without recalibrating them for plateau microclimates. The weather and power forecasting models in this solution are trained on plateau terrain and weather data, and selected dynamically on the principle of “plant-specific solutions, zonal modeling and multi-mode optimal selection”. It is one of the few AI forecasting capabilities verified on site in permafrost at 4,600 m. The difference lies not in model parameters but in remodeling for extreme geographic conditions. 3. Software deployment vs. heavy-asset retrofit: Unlocking value from existing assets Conventional smart retrofits require large amounts of new hardware such as drones and robots, meaning high upfront investment and a high entry barrier for remote high-altitude sites, especially in developing countries. This solution delivers precise power allocation and AI power forecasting using existing inverter and SCADA data, with no additional hardware investment. Operators can progress in three phases: software deployment, intelligent inspection and unattended operation. Instead of the heavy-asset “hardware + platform” model, it offers a lightweight, pay-per-use approach. 4. Local capability building vs. vendor-retained expertise Under the common one-off “product delivery + training” model, expertise stays with external vendors and owners cannot build their own capabilities. This solution uses a plant O&M knowledge ontology and a RAG knowledge base to turn scattered O&M experience, maintenance records and operating rules into structured, searchable and reusable local knowledge assets. AI tools also lower the skill threshold for frontline staff. Capabilities accumulate with local operators rather than external experts, which is the essential difference from the product delivery model. 5. Edge autonomy + knowledge outreach: Built for remote areas with weak connectivity and few staff Remote high-altitude plants in developing countries typically face two constraints: unstable communication and a shortage of skilled personnel. Edge inference keeps plants running when communication is interrupted, and the knowledge ontology turns scarce expert experience into reusable handling guidance, making the solution viable where infrastructure and skills are limited. This contrasts with models that depend on centralized cloud services and expert availability. 6. New evaluation metrics: Redefining smart-plant criteria at high altitude with “reduced plateau person-days” and “share of planned maintenance” The industry usually measures smart-plant effectiveness by installed capacity and the number of connected plants, paying little attention to human factors at high altitude. This solution adopts reduced person-days on the plateau, fewer emergency repairs and the share of planned maintenance as core KPIs, turning “replacing humans with machines” into a measurable occupational health indicator. It offers a new reference framework for evaluating high-altitude renewable plants and validating AI models in the power sector.
Sustainable Change: This solution has four distinct features: large scale, harsh scenario, intelligent collaboration of wind, solar, and storage, and digital innovation to improve end-to-end efficiency and ecological benefits. First, the solution makes full use of the abundant sunlight resources in the local region, especially in combination with local hydropower, to provide stable power supply. Second, the project uses digital and intelligent technologies to improve the intelligence level across the entire lifecycle of power plants, and build the world's first digital benchmark for utility-scale clean energy bases on drainage basin and plateau areas. This is expected to trigger a series of far-reaching chain effects: (1) Large-scale deployment within the Yalong River energy base: The standard architecture enables new power plants to be connected through configuration. The platform can be expanded from about 3 million kW to about 17 million kW of PV and wind power installations in 40 power plants across the entire base. (2) Replication to global utility-scale energy bases and harsh-scenario areas: Many of the world's best solar resources are located in high-altitude regions, such as the Andes in South America, the Himalayas, and the East African Plateau. These regions are mostly in developing countries, which also face challenges such as oxygen deficiency, extreme cold, inconvenient transportation, and a shortage of professionals. The AI O&M capabilities of this solution can be deployed for these power plants by deploying software only, and then expanded to intelligent inspection and unattended operation on demand. (3) Changing the industry practices: The project proves that remote centralized control and minimal staffing can be achieved in large-scale remote renewable energy plants. It provides a reference for intelligent plant evaluation, high-altitude O&M, and AI model verification in the electric power industry, and lowers the threshold for small- and medium-sized operators who are unable to build such capabilities. (4) Policy validation: This solution corresponds to two high-value scenarios of AI and Energy domain: high-precision hydro, wind, and solar power forecasting, and intelligent O&M and unattended/less-staffed operation for power plants in developing countries. The actual test results provide evidence for renewable energy integration, occupational health protection, and digital infrastructure investment. (5) Decent work and local capabilities: AI has shifted the work from dangerous high-altitude sites to control rooms and regional teams in plains, making the working environment safer and more skill-intensive. Knowledge graphs and AI-assisted tools convert scarce experience into training materials, helping build a stable local O&M team in the project area. (6) Global cooperation: All parties involved in the cooperation are willing to share experience through AIM Global, for example, by holding knowledge sharing sessions or carrying out pilot cooperation with partners in developing countries that have high-altitude and remote renewable energy plants.

Name of your organization: China Oil & Gas Pipeline Network Corporation (commonly referred as PipeChina)
Title: AI-Ontology Driven Intelligent O&M Paradigm for Critical Compressor Units of PipeChina
Subtitle: Integrating large models, industrial ontologies, and agents to achieve 10 min early precise warning and full-link O&M automation for pipeline compressors, setting a global benchmark for energy digitalization.
Problem Statement: Long-distance natural gas pipelines serve as the "arterial lifelines" of a country's energy transmission, while compressor units act as the "heart" or "booster engines" of the pipeline system. Their core mission is to pressurize natural gas, and their secure, stable, and highly efficient continuous operation directly determines the lifeline of national energy supply and the transmission efficiency of the network. With the interconnectivity of the PipeChina’s "National One Network" strategy—which integrates previously dispersed oil and gas pipelines and infrastructure across China through interconnection mechanisms, building a modernized, national-level energy super-transportation network stretching from Heihe in Heilongjiang in the east to Tarim in Xinjiang in the west, Inner Mongolia in the north, and Guangdong and Hainan in the south, spanning dozens of provincial-level administrative regions nationwide and achieving the comprehensive integration of "West-East Gas Pipeline, North-to-South Gas Transport, and Offshore Gas Landing"—critical pipeline equipment is facing severe geographical and operational challenges. Compressor units are typically deployed in stations located in high-latitude, extremely cold regions (where severe winter temperatures plunge below minus tens of degrees Celsius in the northeast, posing extreme tests on equipment heat tracing, lubricant viscosity, and metal materials), or shoulder the heavy responsibilities of cross-regional, high-drop, high-pressure, and long-distance supply hubs. Clean energy transmission and long-distance pipeline operations and maintenance (O&M) have long faced severe challenges characterized by "harsh environments, intertwined pain points, and failure of traditional methods": 1. Threats of Extreme Environmental Overlays and High-Intensity Operation: Pipeline stations are often distributed across vast northern cold regions or remote areas, where severe winter cold, gales, and freezing weather occur frequently. Low-temperature environments impose severe disturbances on the lubrication systems, dry gas seal systems, and cold startup and thermal balance of high-power motors. Outdoor inspections and high-risk troubleshooting by O&M personnel in severe weather are extremely difficult, posing severe tests to personal safety and operational health. 2. Outdated Warning and Response Modes, Missing Best Intervention Windows: Traditional O&M relies excessively on manual monitoring and static, fixed alarm thresholds, lacking intelligent insights into multi-dimensional, high-frequency operating data. Facing complex internal vibration waveform spectra and auxiliary system process parameter changes, sites often fall into a "reactive repair" cycle ("alarm equals accident") due to the lack of early warning capabilities, leading to severe unplanned shutdowns and economic losses. 3. Knowledge Fragmentation and Difficulty in Retaining Expert Experience: Compressor troubleshooting involves multi-disciplinary coordination across mechanics, electrical engineering, instrumentation and control, and fluid dynamics. It is time-consuming and heavily relies on the "individual experience" of senior experts. Such expertise is lost during personnel turnover, and massive unexpected fault cases fail to transform into systematic, standardized digital assets, leaving tacit knowledge difficult to solidify and reuse. 4. The "Black Box" Trust Dilemma in AI: Frontline O&M engineers find it difficult to verify the accuracy of AI recommendations online, resulting in reluctance to adopt the technology ("not daring to use, unwilling to use"), which severely hinders the deep trust and deployment of intelligent technologies in critical industrial fields. This solution empowers operations through the synergy of AI technology and O&M ontological knowledge, tackling these challenges at the root, transforming reactive emergency repairs into proactive predictions, and rendering AI decision-making transparent and trustworthy.
Solution Overview: Starting from October 2024, China Oil & Gas Pipeline Network Corporation (PipeChina) and Huawei have jointly innovated and implemented this project with a total cumulative investment of RMB 3.5 million (524K USD), including RMB 2.4 million (340K USD) for data governance, RMB 1 million (140K USD) for data product service development, and RMB 100,000 (14,000 USD) for data compliance costs. It builds a 5-in-1 intelligent O&M system integrating a "Data Foundation + Foundation Model + Ontological Knowledge + Agent + Business Application." By significantly expanding the monitoring points of a single compressor from over 20 to more than 1,000, and aggregating tens of millions of high-quality industrial datasets, the system leverages time-series and anomaly detection foundation models to predict potential faults 10 minutes in advance. Meanwhile, by introducing an exclusive ontological knowledge graph for the oil and gas industry, AI is empowered with logical reasoning capabilities, achieving an alert traceability accuracy of over 90%. Through WeACT digital employees and seamless integration with the IMS management system, a full-process automated closed-loop of "early warning – diagnosis – work order dispatch – handling" is achieved. 1. Anomaly Detection Foundation Model: Focuses on comprehensive diagnosis and precise identification of current states. Targeting high-frequency, multi-dimensional complex data (especially vibration waveform spectra and various auxiliary system process parameters), multi-working-condition fusion analysis breaks away from traditional single, rigid fixed-threshold alarms, enabling dynamic threshold alarms based on actual operating conditions. This transforms the traditional "manual screen monitoring" mode—which heavily relied on human labor and was prone to visual fatigue—into a capability that keenly and accurately captures instantaneous or composite anomalies. 2. Time-Series Forecasting Foundation Model: Focuses on extrapolating future development trends and proactive early warnings. By deeply fusing multi-source process variables such as vibration, temperature, pressure, and lubricating oil, a trend forecasting model capable of capturing data evolution patterns is constructed. Concurrently, combined with incremental learning mechanisms, the model continuously adapts, iterates, and self-optimizes with routine operational data accumulation, achieving precise early warnings 10 to 30 minutes in advance and successfully shifting the traditional mode from reactive emergency repairs to proactive prevention. 3. Industrial Ontological Knowledge Engineering: Expert experiences from FMEA (Failure Mode and Effects Analysis), technical bulletins, and failure reports are subjected to ontological construction. Ontologies define "what the equipment is, how equipment elements relate to each other, and the basis for association rules". Building upon this, an intelligent maintenance ontology and an intelligent O&M decision-making agent are constructed, enabling the agent—guided by ontological knowledge—to "understand business, think like a human, and provide reasonable explanations and accurate judgments". 4. For example, when triggered by a "low lubrication oil header pressure" shutdown alarm, the agent leverages the ontological knowledge base to cross-validate multi-sensor readings, ruling out true pressure drops. By verifying that all bearing temperatures and flows remain normal while filter differential pressure hits the threshold, it accurately pinpoints an "impulse line blockage." Backed by a transparent reasoning chain with >90% traceability accuracy, the agent seamlessly connects with WeACT and the IMS system to drive an automated "warning – diagnosis – dispatch – handling" closed-loop, completely resolving the AI trust dilemma.
Solution Provider(s): 1. China Oil & Gas Pipeline Network Corporation (PipeChina) —— A key state-owned backbone energy enterprise in China, responsible for the investment, construction, operation, and management of national oil and gas trunk pipelines and storage facilities. As the leader in business scenarios and industry standards for this project, PipeChina provides real-world, complex long-distance pipeline operation scenarios and massive industrial measurement data (expanding single compressor monitoring points from over 20 to 1,000+), accumulates tens of millions of high-quality industrial sample datasets, takes the lead in defining industry intelligent O&M standards and ontology knowledge specifications, and contributes frontline expert operational experience; Sector: Energy / Oil and Gas Storage and Transportation. 2. Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd. — A global leading provider of ICT (Information and Communications Technology) and digital energy infrastructure. As a key technology and computing power partner, Huawei provides robust AI computing infrastructure and foundation model support, and collaborates with PipeChina on joint innovations across various applications, including: enabling potential equipment faults to be warned 10 minutes in advance through the integration of time-series forecasting and anomaly detection foundation models; constructing an exclusive ontology knowledge base for the oil and gas industry to achieve explainable AI decision-making (with an alert traceability accuracy of over 90%); and co-developing an intelligent compressor O&M agent to achieve a full-chain automated closed-loop from fault warning and root-cause diagnosis to work order dispatch and handling feedback. Sector: ICT / Digital Intelligence.
Implementation location(s): The application has been successfully deployed across 31 units along the China-Russia East-Route Natural Gas Pipeline, including 31 compressor units at stations in Tai'an, Tangshan, Heihe, Mingshu, Jinzhou, Wudalianchi, Zhaoyuan, Yongqing, Shenyang, and Anping cities in China.
Implementation timeline(s): PipeChina and Huawei officially launched this joint innovation project in March 2024, focusing on the intelligent operation and maintenance of core compressor units along long-distance natural gas pipelines. Adopting a phased and regional rolling implementation strategy, the project successfully deployed 31 compressor units across 10 core stations operated by Northern Pipeline, Beijing Pipeline, Northeast Company, and Shandong Company in four distinct phases between March 2025 and March 2026, with all station-level acceptances successfully completed.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: It is expected to be scaled up and deployed across all 461 units within China Oil & Gas Pipeline Network Corporation (PipeChina) Group by the end of 2027. The 1-year rollout plan for all 461 compressor units across the pipeline network is structured as follows: Phase 1 (Nov 2026 – Feb 2027): Select 30 typical compressor units as pilot carriers to conduct on-site adaptation, measurement point integration, and localization tuning of models and knowledge bases. Output unified deployment specifications, complete O&M personnel training, verify multi-site adaptability, and establish reusable templates to support subsequent large-scale replication. Phase 2 (Mar 2027 – Sep 2027): Roll out the solution across 310 units in batches, completing platform access, measurement point retrofitting, and system joint debugging. Establish a regional O&M support system and a rapid-response mechanism for issues. Use early warning accuracy and event closure rates as monthly observation indicators to drive continuous model iteration and ensure batch deployment quality. Phase 3 (Oct 2027 – Dec 2027): Implement the solution on the remaining 121 units, achieving 100% coverage of all 461 compressor units. Launch a unified O&M dashboard to enable cross-site data sharing. Conduct a comprehensive review of project outcomes, and output cross-pipeline reusable solutions as well as benchmark indicators for large-scale operations.
Desired impact: The application is designed to establish a "smart health intelligence brain" and operational decision-making hub for long-distance pipeline compressor units, the solution transforms traditional passive emergency repairs into AI-enabled proactive prevention. It constructs a novel intelligent management model characterized by "centralized monitoring, hierarchical disposal, collaborative optimization, and feedback iteration," ensuring the secure, stable, and highly efficient operation of national energy lifelines. Actual Results: 1. Data Governance & High-Quality Dataset Formation: The monitoring points per compressor have expanded dramatically from over 20 to 1,000+, accumulating tens of millions of high-quality industrial sample data points. 2. Advanced Early Warning Capability: Leveraging the multi-parameter correlation and learning capabilities of time-series large models, precise early warnings for potential equipment anomalies are achieved 10 minutes in advance. 3. Fault Traceability & Reliability: Driven by the industry-exclusive ontology knowledge base, the traceability accuracy exceeds 90%, effectively resolving the trust challenges of AI "black boxes". 4. Smart O&M Capability: The O&M intelligent agent autonomously conducts root-cause analysis and operational guidance, boosting routine maintenance efficiency by over 30%. 5. Significant Optimization in O&M Response: In 2026, a total of 182 early warning issues have been successfully processed, achieving minute-level diagnostic response, 100% knowledge retention and closed-loop management, and maintaining an average Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF) of over 13,000 hours for the compressor units. 6. Energy Saving & Carbon Reduction: Relying on smart early warnings and refined O&M, unintended load fluctuations and inefficient operations of units were reduced, resulting in a cumulative reduction of over 20,000 tons of carbon emissions in 2025, alongside reduced self-use gas consumption and enhanced energy efficiency for core pipeline energy-consuming equipment. 7. Safety Prevention & Control: By identifying abnormal risks in vibration, temperature, and pressure in advance to eliminate equipment failure hazards, the frequency of high-risk outdoor inspections and emergency repairs by personnel was reduced, avoiding safety risks such as media leakage and mechanical injuries caused by sudden unit failures, thereby solidifying the safety defense line for unit operations and operational personnel. 8. Economic Benefits: Following project implementation, maintenance strategies were optimized from scheduled overhauls to predictive maintenance, saving RMB 61.2 million (approx. 8.74 million USD) in maintenance costs in 2025 and effectively reducing expenses on spare parts and outsourced repairs.
Key technologies: Targeting the O&M challenges of core compressor units in cross-regional long-distance natural gas pipelines, the solution deeply integrates core technologies such as time-series foundation models, industrial ontological knowledge engineering, multi-agent systems, and the IoT: 1. Time-Series Foundation Models & Anomaly Detection Technology: Powered by the robust anomaly identification and multi-parameter trend prediction capabilities of time-series foundation models, traditional single and rigid fixed-threshold alarms are replaced. Targeting high-frequency and multi-dimensional complex data (such as vibration waveform spectra and auxiliary system process parameters), multi-working-condition fusion analysis enables dynamic threshold alarming to precisely capture transient or composite anomalies, achieving proactive early warnings 10 to 30 minutes in advance. 2. Industrial Ontological Knowledge Engineering (Ontology-based Engineering): An exclusive compressor maintenance ontology knowledge base for the oil and gas industry has been constructed, deeply integrating FMEA (Failure Mode and Effects Analysis), technical bulletins, and expert O&M experience. This endows AI with powerful logical reasoning and "white-box" explainability, utilizing ontologies to define equipment association rules and achieving an alert traceability accuracy of over 90%, fundamentally resolving the AI trust dilemma. 3. Collaboration between AI Agents and the Internet of Things (IoT): Backed by a massive industrial measurement point data collection foundation—expanding monitoring points per compressor from over 20 to 1,000+—an intelligent compressor O&M agent is established. Through a multi-agent framework for autonomous analysis and decision-making, seamlessly linked with WeACT digital employees and the IMS management system, a full-chain automated closed-loop of "fault warning – root-cause diagnosis – work order dispatch – handling feedback" is realized.
Unique Characteristics: 1. Technological Innovation (Constructing "White-Box" Explainable AI to Resolve Trust Dilemmas): Pioneered a multi-driver architecture of "Large Models + Industrial Ontology Knowledge Base + Intelligent Agent." Unlike traditional AI "black boxes" that lack logical explanation, the project introduces an exclusive compressor maintenance ontology knowledge base for the oil and gas industry, endowing AI with logical reasoning and "white-box" explainability. This achieves an alert traceability accuracy of over 90%, ensuring that conclusions are verifiable and explainable, and enabling frontline O&M personnel to genuinely dare to use and trust the system. 2. Model Innovation (Full-Chain Automated Closed-Loop & Transitioning from "Visibility" to "Manageability"): Breaking the bottleneck of slow traditional multi-professional coordination and difficult experience transfer. Adhering to the philosophy of "governing data first, then refining models," the monitoring points per compressor were expanded from over 20 to 1,000+, accumulating tens of millions of high-quality datasets. Powered by time-series foundation models for 10-minute early warnings, and seamlessly linked with WeACT digital employees and the IMS system, the solution achieves a full-chain automated closed-loop of "early warning - diagnosis - dispatch - handling," setting a new paradigm for AI-native applications in the energy industry. 3. Partnership Innovation (Deep Integration of Industry and Research in Business Scenarios and Technical Foundations): Through joint innovation between China Oil & Gas Pipeline Network Corporation (PipeChina) (leading real-world business scenarios and industry standards) and Huawei (providing robust computing infrastructure and foundation model support), the partnership achieves complementary strengths, making a leap from co-creating business pain points focused on core equipment monitoring to leading industry standards in intelligent O&M for long-distance pipelines.
Sustainable Change: The solution has not only been successfully implemented on core compressor units within PipeChina, but also drives profound systemic change across the energy industry through three major strategic dimensions: "technological evolution, business scale replication, and standards-and-paradigm leadership": 1. Business Scale Replication (Expanding from Compressors to All Equipment Types and Scenarios): The solution can be rapidly replicated and promoted from compressor units to all types of rotating and storage-transportation equipment (such as oil pumps, instrumentation, and electrical systems) within PipeChina, achieving comprehensive asset O&M coverage. Furthermore, it can be horizontally scaled to the entire oil and gas sector and broader process industries (such as chemical engineering and power generation), possessing exceptional industry-wide applicability and replication value. 2. Technological Evolution (Reshaping AI-Native O&M Production Models via "Digital Employees"): Driven by multi-agent collaboration and 24/7 duty of WeACT digital employees, traditional passive and fragmented manual screen monitoring and troubleshooting are reconstructed into automated, intelligent collaborative workflows. Meanwhile, leveraging low-code application development and knowledge base accumulation, the initiative fosters a versatile workforce adept in both equipment and AI, forging an AI-native productivity paradigm for traditional energy enterprises. 3. Leadership in Standards and Paradigms (Translating Pipeline Practices into Industry Assets): Grounded in PipeChina's real-world business scenarios, the project takes the lead in establishing intelligent O&M standards and ontology knowledge specifications for oil and gas equipment, delivering a replicable and scalable "PipeChina solution" for intelligent O&M. By continuously accumulating ontology knowledge bases and fault case libraries, it builds shared industry knowledge assets, comprehensively serving and driving the high-quality digital, intelligent, and standardized transformation of global energy infrastructure. 4. Environmental & Climate Systemic Change (Quantified Carbon Reduction & Energy Efficiency): By leveraging time-series foundation models to optimize unit operating conditions, eliminate inefficient operations, and provide early warnings for seal and valve anomalies to prevent leakage, the solution achieved a cumulative reduction of over 20,000 tons of carbon emissions in 2025. It simultaneously lowers self-use gas and power consumption, providing a quantifiable empirical benchmark for efficient and low-carbon operations in global long-distance pipeline networks. 5. Occupational Safety & HSE Upgrade (Solidifying the Defense Line for Personnel Safety): Addressing the challenges of dispersed station locations and complex inspection environments, the solution replaces frequent manual site visits with AI forecasting and intelligent inspections. This significantly reduces the frequency of high-risk outdoor troubleshooting and emergency repairs by personnel in harsh weather, effectively mitigating safety hazards such as mechanical injuries, frostbite, and media leakage, thereby comprehensively upgrading industry occupational health and safety (HSE) standards. 6. Economic Sustainability & High ROI Demonstration: Empowering existing assets with a lightweight "software + foundation model" architecture at a total investment of only RMB 3.5 million (approx. 0.5 million USD), the project optimized maintenance strategies through predictive maintenance in 2025, saving RMB 61.2 million (approx. 9.2 million USD), in maintenance costs and drastically reducing expenses on spare parts and outsourced repairs. This demonstrates an exceptional return on investment (ROI) and robust commercial scalability.

Title: Chery AI Materials Scientist: Scaling Sustainable Materials Innovation
Subtitle: Chery applies industrial AI to screen and validate sustainable materials. Its recycled-aluminum solution is in production, while carbon capture and battery recycling are in development.
Problem Statement: A key challenge for sustainable industry is not simply identifying low-carbon materials, but enabling complex and variable secondary resources to consistently meet the stringent requirements of advanced manufacturing. Material composition, microstructure, performance, cost and processing conditions are closely interdependent. Traditional R&D relies heavily on expert experience and repeated trial-and-error testing, making it difficult to efficiently optimise multiple performance objectives simultaneously. Three major challenges remain: • Limited discovery efficiency: The potential combinations of material compositions are vast, while conventional, experience-based approaches cannot explore a sufficiently broad design space. • The gap between scientific discovery and industrial application: Laboratory predictions must still be validated against variations in raw materials, manufacturing processes, equipment constraints, product safety and mass-production quality requirements. • Limited transferability of innovation: Without systematic data feedback and engineering validation, individual technological breakthroughs are difficult to replicate across projects, companies and regions. To address these challenges, Chery has developed an integrated solution connecting real industrial applications, AI-driven optimisation, experimental validation and engineering deployment. Its effectiveness is measured against tangible improvements in R&D efficiency, engineering quality and environmental performance.
Solution Overview: I. Solution: A Five-Step Industrial AI Workflow Chery AI Materials Scientist integrates materials data, knowledge graphs, machine learning, multi-agent systems, scientific computing and high-throughput experimentation into a reusable R&D workflow. Field Deployment Engineering (FDE) connects AI research with manufacturing. AI handles prediction and screening, while experts retain responsibility for scientific judgement, validation and final engineering decisions. The workflow comprises five steps: 1. Scenario Identification: Define industrial requirements for recycled aluminium, carbon capture and battery recycling. 2. Data Integration: Leverage approximately 3 TB of materials data, over 200,000 adsorption-material records and knowledge graphs. 3. AI Optimisation: Combine machine learning, multi-objective optimisation and expert rules, integrating 1,214 research skills. Platform testing shows 10-fold higher prediction efficiency, 50% improved accuracy and 90% lower computational costs. 4. Experimental Validation: Verify AI recommendations through scientific computing, high-throughput experiments and material performance testing. 5. Engineering Deployment: FDE teams translate validated formulations into production parameters and quality specifications through cross-functional collaboration. II. Flagship Application: 100% Recycled Aluminium To meet automotive structural requirements, AI analysed 36 elements, screened over 1,000 formulations and selected 21 for melting trials. Validation established an integrated solution combining 100% recycled aluminium, heat-treatment-free processing and integrated die casting. Now in mass production, it is applied to structural components in the EXEED Sterra ES, Sterra ET and Fulwin A9L, with qualification rates exceeding 95%. Melting cycles decreased by over 50%, material development time by approximately 50%, and evaluation efficiency increased tenfold. Material-stage CO₂e emissions fell by approximately 80%, delivering an estimated 3.27 tonnes of CO₂e savings per vehicle. At 150,000 vehicles, annual economic benefits are estimated at USD 3 million. III. Extended Applications 1. Onboard Carbon Capture: AI screened over 500 candidate materials, achieving 85% recommendation accuracy, 300% higher daily experimental throughput and 90% fewer errors. Laboratory validation is complete. WLTC tests achieved over 90% capture efficiency and approximately 12 g CO₂/km. 2. Battery Recycling: AI-assisted material identification and process optimisation support selective lithium recovery. Laboratory results achieved ≥97% lithium leaching, ≤10% iron-phosphorus co-leaching and ≥99.5% battery-grade lithium carbonate purity. IV. Engineering Deployment and Global Replicability The methodology extends to magnesium alloys, high-strength steel, recycled plastics and battery materials. It can support cross-industry applications in transport, aerospace, construction and energy equipment. Through modular deployment and adaptation to local materials, data and industrial conditions, pilot projects in new regions can potentially launch within 2–3 months. Ultimately, the solution turns AI-driven materials discovery into validated engineering solutions and scalable green manufacturing applications.
Solution Provider(s): 1. Lead Implementer: Chery Automobile is responsible for defining industrial requirements, developing AI-driven R&D capabilities, engineering materials solutions and integrating them into automotive applications. Internal participating teams include materials R&D, AI, metallurgy, die casting, computer-aided engineering (CAE), testing and validation, component development and whole-vehicle R&D. 2.External Collaboration: Chery engages with universities, research institutes, material suppliers, recycled resource providers and component manufacturing partners. These partners contribute to fundamental research, raw material supply, process development, testing and industrialisation. Looking ahead, Chery plans to explore demonstration-platform partnerships with international organisations, including UNIDO, to facilitate the cross-industry and cross-regional adaptation and application of AI-enabled green materials R&D technologies.
Implementation location(s): China: Chery's materials R&D facilities, melting and experimental facilities, die-casting manufacturing operations, materials testing and validation facilities, component development operations and whole-vehicle R&D environments. The recycled aluminium solution has been applied to relevant automotive structural components in the EXEED Sterra ES, EXEED Sterra ET and Fulwin A9L models.
Implementation timeline(s): The solution is under continuous implementation as of November 2026: 1.Recycled aluminium: The materials solution has entered mass production and is being applied in automotive structural components. 2.Onboard exhaust carbon capture: Laboratory validation has been completed, and the project has progressed to vehicle demonstration and engineering adaptation. 3.Power battery recycling: Laboratory-scale testing has been completed, with development progressing towards pilot-scale validation at the 100 kg level.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Subject to the availability of local industrial partners, relevant material data, basic testing facilities and necessary regulatory approvals, the solution is expected to complete initial technical adaptation and launch a pilot within 2–3 months in a new geographical location. This timeline does not imply that mass-production certification will be achieved within the same period. Month 1 – Requirements Definition and Data Preparation Assess local industrial requirements, material sources, process constraints and data availability. Deliverable: an agreed definition of the pilot application and its technical requirements. Month 2 – AI Model and Process Adaptation Adapt AI models, knowledge graphs and multi-objective optimisation methods to local material systems and manufacturing conditions. Deliverable: candidate material formulations and process solutions. Month 3 – Joint Experimentation and Initial Validation Conduct collaborative experiments and preliminary performance and process validation. Deliverable: a pilot validation report and an engineering roadmap for the next development stage.
Desired impact: Core Objective The primary objective of Chery AI Materials Scientist is to bridge artificial intelligence, materials science and industrial manufacturing, enabling AI to accelerate the transition of sustainable materials from laboratory research to production-line applications. The solution aims to advance circular resource utilisation, industrial decarbonisation and the large-scale deployment of green manufacturing technologies. Through a closed-loop workflow of scenario identification, performance definition, AI-driven optimisation, experimental validation and engineering deployment, the system develops green technologies that are applicable, verifiable and scalable. It transforms previously underutilised waste resources into high-value industrial materials, generating tangible environmental and economic benefits. Key Impacts 1. Climate Impact •By replacing primary aluminium with 100% recycled aluminium, material-stage emissions are reduced from approximately 16.38 kg CO₂e/kg to 3.0 kg CO₂e/kg, an approximately 80% reduction. This translates into an estimated reduction of 3.27 tonnes of CO₂e per vehicle. If deployed across Chery's annual production and sales volume of nearly 3 million vehicles, the theoretical annual reduction potential would be approximately 9.9 million tonnes of CO₂e. At a global adoption rate of approximately 20% of new vehicles, the theoretical reduction potential could exceed 53 million tonnes of CO₂e annually. •Under WLTC testing conditions, the onboard exhaust carbon capture system achieved a CO₂ capture efficiency of at least 90%, capturing approximately 12 g/km. Based on annual mileage of 15,000 km, the estimated capture volume is approximately 180 kg of CO₂ per vehicle per year, offering a potential new emissions-reduction pathway for the global fleet of existing internal combustion engine vehicles. 2. Resource Efficiency and Circularity •The mass-production application of 100% recycled aluminium in critical automotive structural components enables waste aluminium to be transformed into high-performance automotive materials, supporting higher-value resource circularity. •The power battery recycling process has achieved a lithium leaching rate of at least 97%, an iron-phosphorus co-leaching rate of no more than 10%, and battery-grade lithium carbonate purity of at least 99.5%, providing technical support for the efficient recovery and reuse of critical materials from end-of-life batteries. 3. Industrial and Economic Benefits •The AI materials R&D platform has shortened screening cycles by up to 90%, improved prediction efficiency by approximately 10 times and reduced computational costs by 90%, accelerating sustainable materials development and engineering deployment. •In the recycled aluminium project, melting furnace cycles have been reduced by more than 50%, material development cycles shortened by approximately 50%, and die-cast component qualification rates increased to over 95%. By reducing R&D trial-and-error and optimising material solutions, the project has improved overall costs by approximately USD 20 per vehicle. At an application volume of 150,000 vehicles, the estimated annual economic benefit is approximately USD 3 million. 4. Inclusive and Globally Scalable Industrial Development •The system has expanded from mass-produced recycled aluminium applications in the automotive sector to carbon capture and power battery recycling, establishing a transferable methodology covering material design, experimental validation and engineering deployment. •Through modular deployment, adaptation to local data and collaboration with industrial partners, the solution is expected to enable pilot projects in new countries or regions within 2–3 months. This can help regions with different resource endowments and levels of industrial development strengthen their materials innovation capabilities through AI, promoting knowledge sharing, access to green technologies and collaborative industrial development
Key technologies: • Materials Data and Knowledge Graphs: Approximately 3 TB of materials databases and more than 200,000 adsorption-material records, establishing relationships between material composition, structure, properties and processing conditions. • Industrial AI and Multi-Agent Systems: Machine learning, multi-objective constrained optimisation, OpenJiuwen, Agent Team Engine and 1,214 scientific research skills. • Scientific Computing: MindSpore Science, AtomBit, VASP, Gaussian and other tools supporting multiscale simulation and material performance prediction. • High-Throughput Experimentation and Characterisation: Material melting, experimental testing, XRF, ICP-MS, XRD, FTIR and intelligent visual analysis. • Engineering Deployment and Responsible AI: FDE-based on-site adaptation, human review, experimental verification, engineering approval, and data and intellectual property governance.
Unique Characteristics: 1.Defining AI Tasks Through Real Industrial Scenarios Rather than applying AI as a standalone research tool, Chery works backwards from the safety, manufacturing, cost and environmental requirements of automotive structural components to define material development tasks and design the corresponding AI workflow. 2.Establishing an Evidence-Based R&D Chain The solution connects AI recommendations, scientific computing, melting trials, die-casting validation and data feedback into a continuous evidence-based workflow. Model outputs are never treated as established industrial facts without experimental and engineering verification. 3.Validating Circular Materials for Mass Production For the recycled aluminium application, the system evaluated 36 relevant elements, screened more than 1,000 candidate formulations and selected 21 for melting trials. This process ultimately supported the large-scale application of 100% recycled aluminium in automotive structural components. 4.Reusability Across Different Material Systems The same underlying methodology has been extended from recycled aluminium to carbon capture materials and power battery recycling, while clearly distinguishing the different technology maturity levels of each application. 5.Modular FDE-Based Deployment Data models, experimental workflows and engineering expertise can be adapted to different industrial environments and local requirements through modular Field Deployment Engineering, supporting international industrial collaboration. 6.Human-AI Collaboration and Clear Accountability AI enhances scientific exploration and decision support, while critical scientific judgements, production safety assessments and final engineering approvals remain the responsibility of qualified human experts.
Sustainable Change: The systemic value of this solution lies in its ability to progressively transform capabilities traditionally dependent on a limited number of materials experts and extensive R&D infrastructure into a digital materials innovation methodology that can be accumulated, shared and replicated across industrial scenarios. • R&D Transformation: Materials data, scientific knowledge, experimental results and engineering experience are consolidated into reusable digital assets, enabling continuous learning and more efficient innovation. • Industrial Collaboration: The solution connects resource recovery, materials R&D, component manufacturing and vehicle production, enabling circular resources to be upgraded and processed to meet high-performance industrial requirements. • SMEs and Developing Economies: Modular tools, joint laboratories and engineering training can support local capability development, reduce duplicated infrastructure investment and broaden access to advanced materials innovation. • Talent Development and Inclusion: The methodology can be integrated into professional training and collaborative programmes involving universities, young researchers and women engineers, expanding opportunities to participate in industrial innovation.
Funding Sources: The solution has primarily been funded through Chery Automobile's internal R&D investment, covering materials databases, algorithm development, scientific computing, multi-agent collaboration, experimentation and characterisation, recycled aluminium engineering deployment, and R&D on carbon capture and battery recycling. For future international pilot projects, joint validation can be supported through collaboration with industrial partners, research institutions and local testing facilities. Chery also plans to explore phased investment arrangements and technology service models to support deployment in different regions.
Testimonials and Endorsements: While direct stakeholder testimonials and beneficiary quotations are not currently included, the solution and its key recycled aluminium application have received the following external recognition: • 2025 Altair Enlighten Award: Chery's Answering Earth with Low-Carbon Recycled Aluminum received the Global Runner-Up distinction in the Sustainable Product category. • UNIDO Global Call 2025: Chery's recycled aluminium project was recognised as the China Regional Champion in the Sustainable Materials category. • Outstanding Corporate Climate Action Case: Chery's case, Recycled Aluminium Alloys: A Scalable Solution for Global Emissions Reduction, was selected as an outstanding corporate climate action case and featured at COP30-related events.

It is the strongest combination of artificial intelligence, industrial application and measured environmental outcome in this batch; the single-country footprint is what keeps it out of the top three.
