Title: FriendnPal
Subtitle: AI-powered behavioural-health intelligence for healthier, more resilient health workforces across emerging markets.
Problem Statement: Mental and behavioral health challenges create a significant but often invisible barrier to resilient economies, productive workplaces and inclusive digital transformation. In many developing and middle-income economies, support remains reactive, people are identified only after symptoms have significantly deteriorated or when they reach a clinical facility. This is compounded by shortages of mental-health professionals, fragmented health data, stigma, affordability barriers, multiple languages and limited access to continuous monitoring. Organizations and health systems therefore lack timely visibility into changing behavioral risk between clinical or support encounters. The result is delayed intervention, avoidable crises, reduced workforce wellbeing and productivity, and inefficient allocation of scarce professional resources. FriendnPal addresses this visibility and decision-making gap by creating a continuous, AI-enabled behavioral intelligence layer between clinical and organizational touchpoints that supports earlier identification, continuous monitoring and timely human intervention across 50 languages.
Solution Overview: FriendnPal is an AI-powered behavioral health intelligence platform designed to help organizations, healthcare systems and communities identify behavioral-health risks earlier and connect people to appropriate human support. Our platform combines multimodal AI, clinical natural-language processing, behavioral analytics, validated clinical assessments, risk stratification, symptom monitoring and human-in-the-loop care. It creates a longitudinal picture of wellbeing rather than relying only on episodic clinical encounters. Users can engage through mobile, web, WhatsApp and voice-based channels, and even offline, supporting deployment across different levels of connectivity, digital literacy and language. Our system analyzes changes in behavioral and conversational signals and combines these with structured assessments and engagement patterns to identify potential changes in risk. Risk intelligence can support screening, prioritization, monitoring, referral and follow-up. Qualified professionals remain responsible for clinical intervention and consequential decisions; AI is used to augment human expertise rather than replace it. FriendnPal's deployment model supports collaboration between technology providers, governments, healthcare organizations, NGOs, employers, research institutions and community organizations. This enables adaptation to local languages, care pathways, regulatory environments and population needs. Our architecture is particularly suited to developing and middle-income economies because it is designed for multilingual populations, varying levels of digital literacy, low-bandwidth environments and uneven access to specialist services. Our platform is being further developed through research and clinical-validation work currently in Rwanda, with potential integration into broader primary healthcare, workforce wellbeing and institutional support systems.
Solution Provider(s): African Institute for Mathematical Sciences (AIMS) Rwanda — pan-African research, education and innovation institution; mathematics, data science, AI, research and entrepreneurship; supporting research, innovation and clinical-validation activities in Rwanda, Lagos State Government — public-sector government; healthcare, and community-level implementation, National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP), Nigeria — government agency focused on anti-trafficking, protection and support services, Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) — international development cooperation, capacity building.
Implementation location(s): South Africa, Rwanda, Nigeria, Benin, and Kenya
Implementation timeline(s): July 2023 till date
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 8 - 10 weeks
Desired impact: FriendnPal's primary objective is to make behavioral-health risk more visible between traditional points of care and enable earlier, better-informed intervention, while making behavioural-health intelligence part of everyday digital infrastructure, enabling earlier identification of mental-health risks, continuous monitoring and timely connection to appropriate human care. FriendnPal's approach is designed to extend limited specialist capacity rather than requiring proportional increases in the number of mental-health professionals. By providing multilingual digital access, behavioural screening and continuous monitoring, our platform can help organizations identify people who may require intervention earlier and support continuity beyond physical facilities. For employers and other organizations, the expected impact includes improved access to preventive support, earlier identification of wellbeing risks, better continuity of support and more resilient workforces. At systemic level, the model can contribute to more inclusive participation in digital economies by reducing language, geographic and specialist-access barriers to behavioural healthcare. Our platform aim to detect potential behavioral-health risks earlier through AI-supported behavioral intelligence, provide longitudinal visibility rather than relying exclusively on episodic assessments, help organizations and health systems prioritize limited professional resources., connect people to qualified human care when intervention is required, improve access across language, geography, connectivity and affordability barriers, strengthen the resilience and wellbeing of populations and workforces, and generate evidence that can support more effective and preventive approaches to behavioral healthcare. So far, we have supported 87,000+ people and completed 60,000+ behavioural-health screenings, and has generated over $163,000 in revenue through enterprise partnerships, institutional licensing and digital-health services, and developed one of Africa's growing longitudinal behavioral-health datasets. We have also supported more than 700 women and 850 trafficking survivors. Our next phase focuses on strengthening clinical validation, responsible-AI evaluation, institutional integration and replication across additional geographies.
Key technologies: Artificial intelligence and machine learning Multilingual conversational AI Natural-language processing Behavioural-health screening Predictive behavioural analytics Digital phenotyping Remote Patient Monitoring Risk Stratification Validated Digital Clinical Assessments Longitudinal Behavioral Data Analytics Conversational AI Voice-based AI Mobile and Web Applications WhatsApp-based Digital Health Delivery Human-in-the-Loop Decision Support Health Data Governance and Responsible AI frameworks Cloud-based digital infrastructure
Unique Characteristics: Our key innovation is the combination of predictive behavioural-health AI, multilingual access and Remote Patient Monitoring within one deployable platform. Unlike conventional wellness applications or standalone AI chatbots, FriendnPal is designed as a behavioural-health intelligence layer connecting individuals, AI systems and human professionals. Key differentiators include: 1. Longitudinal behavioral intelligence: Our platform builds a changing picture of wellbeing rather than treating every interaction as an isolated assessment, enabling organizations and professionals observe changes over time rather than relying only on episodic consultations. 2. Multimodal AI: Conversational, behavioral and structured assessment signals can be combined to strengthen risk identification and prioritization. 3. Human-in-the-loop care: AI supports screening, monitoring and prioritization while qualified professionals remain central to clinical intervention. 4. Designed for emerging markets: Mobile, web, WhatsApp and voice delivery enable adaptation to varying levels of connectivity and digital access. 5. Multilingual and culturally adaptable: Our architecture is designed to support deployment across diverse African and emerging-market linguistic and cultural contexts. 6. Infrastructure rather than a standalone consumer app: FriendnPal can support healthcare providers, employers, governments, NGOs and other institutions through B2B/B2B2C models. 7. Responsible AI by design: Patient safety, algorithmic fairness, human oversight and responsible health-data stewardship are incorporated into the development approach. 8. Emerging-market deployment: Designed around low-bandwidth environments, specialist shortages and fragmented healthcare infrastructure. 9. Multiple deployment models: B2C, B2B and B2B2C enable deployment across employers, healthcare providers, governments, universities and other institutions.
Sustainable Change: FriendnPal can contribute to systemic change by shifting behavioural healthcare from an episodic, reactive service into a continuous layer of digital infrastructure. Our model is designed to be replicated across countries by adapting language, local care pathways, regulatory requirements and institutional workflows while retaining the underlying technology infrastructure, creating a pathway for deployment across emerging markets where specialist capacity is limited but mobile and messaging technologies are widely accessible. This makes our approach potentially transferable across African and other emerging markets without requiring every country to build an AI behavioral-health infrastructure from scratch. At the health-system level, FriendnPal can provide an additional digital intelligence layer between primary-care visits, community interactions and specialist services. This can help identify people who may require attention earlier and enable scarce professionals to prioritize cases more effectively. At the organizational level, the same infrastructure can support workforce wellbeing, employee assistance, safeguarding and population-health programs, creating a bridge between digital transformation and human-capital resilience. Over time, aggregated implementation evidence can support stronger clinical validation, responsible-AI standards, policy development and cross-country knowledge sharing, while maintaining responsible data governance and human oversight. Our broader systemic opportunity is to demonstrate that AI deployed responsibly in developing and middle-income economies can do more than automate existing processes, it can create new digital infrastructure for earlier decision-making, stronger human systems and more inclusive access to essential services.
Funding Sources: FriendnPal has been funded primarily through founder investment, internally generated revenue from commercial operations, innovation programs, accelerator support and strategic partnerships and investments.

Title: AI-Powered Quadruped Robot Inspection for High-Risk Industrial Facilities
Subtitle: Embodied AI enables quadruped robots to navigate complex terrain, perform regular inspections, and collect equipment data in high-risk industrial facilities, reducing workers’ exposure to hazards.
Problem Statement: Industrial facilities require regular inspections to detect changes in equipment condition and the surrounding environment. Fixed sensors and cameras can monitor some parameters, but equipment is spread across many locations and inspection requirements vary. Many tasks still require workers to visit equipment with portable instruments. In cable tunnels, substation equipment areas, mine tunnels, and similar settings, this creates four challenges: 1. Workers must enter hazardous areas. The risks differ by location. Working near electrical equipment requires protection against electric shock; underground or poorly ventilated spaces may present oxygen deficiency or harmful gases. Stairs, trenches, and uneven ground make access more difficult. Inspectors must repeatedly enter these areas and approach equipment to observe and measure its condition, exposing them to the hazards of each site. 2. Emerging problems are difficult to track consistently. Overheating connections, unusual sounds, and changes in gas concentration may develop gradually or occur only intermittently. Manual inspections are limited by routes, shifts, and working hours, so staff cannot continuously observe every point. When successive checks are made at different times or positions, or recorded in different ways, trends are harder to assess. An abnormal condition may go unnoticed until a fault becomes more serious. 3. Inspection capacity depends on staffing and experience. When sites have many inspection points, long routes, or night shifts, staffing and travel time affect how often checks can be completed. Inspectors may also interpret subtle warning signs differently. Without an effective way to pass on experienced workers’ knowledge, it is difficult to maintain consistent inspection quality across teams. 4. Existing automated systems leave coverage gaps. Fixed cameras, wheeled or tracked robots, and drones already support some inspection tasks. Cameras are limited by their field of view; ground robots may struggle with stairs, trenches, and narrow passages; and drones face operating constraints indoors and underground. Maintaining inspection coverage while reducing workers’ exposure therefore calls for a mobile system that can negotiate complex terrain and reach different inspection points as needed.
Solution Overview: How the solution works: Unitree Robotics provides an intelligent inspection solution for the power, petrochemical, mining, and water sectors. The solution combines quadruped robots, task-specific inspection equipment, and an inspection management platform. The robots can navigate stairs, slopes, trenches, uneven ground, and other challenging terrain to collect equipment and environmental data at designated inspection points, reducing the need for maintenance personnel to enter hazardous areas or perform repetitive on-site inspection rounds. Methodologies and technologies used: The solution applies embodied AI to industrial inspection. In addition to collecting data, the robots can perceive their surroundings, plan and execute inspection routes, and adapt to different terrain and access conditions in real industrial environments. Depending on the task, they can carry visible-light and thermal imaging equipment, as well as gas and acoustic sensors, to inspect equipment appearance, measure temperature, and monitor environmental conditions. A robotic arm can also be added for tasks such as opening doors and conducting close-range inspections. The collected data is transmitted to the management platform, where maintenance personnel can review, store, and compare the results to identify potential anomalies and arrange follow-up inspections. Partnerships and collaboration models: The solution is delivered through a collaborative model. Unitree provides the quadruped robots, the control systems that enable autonomous mobility, and the inspection management platform. Specialized technology providers supply multimodal inspection equipment for visible-light imaging, thermal imaging, gas detection, and acoustic monitoring. Research institutions and standards organizations contribute to the development of industry guidelines and acceptance criteria, while telecommunications operators provide network connectivity in underground spaces and industrial facilities. This integrated approach reduces the frequency with which personnel must enter hazardous areas and transforms inspection quality from a reliance on individual experience into a consistent, system-based capability. It supports safer, more traceable equipment maintenance and has been deployed in the power, petrochemical, mining, and water sectors.

(CHN Energy) — A centrally administered state-owned energy company with integrated operations across coal mining, power generation, transportation and chemical industries; Sector: Coal, electric power, mining, transportation and chemicals, 2.China National Petroleum Corporation (CNPC) — A major state-owned integrated energy company engaged in oil and gas exploration, development, production, refining, transportation and sales; Sector: Oil, gas and energy, 3.State Grid Corporation of China — A state-owned utility responsible for the investment, construction and operation of power grids, including electricity transmission, distribution and related energy services; Sector: Electric power and utilities
Implementation location(s): The solution has been implemented at scale across multiple cities in China, including Zhejiang, Shanghai, Beijing, Jiangsu and Hubei. It has also undergone small-scale pilots in several international markets, with a growing focus on emerging economies and industrial regions such as Kazakhstan and Saudi Arabia.
Implementation timeline(s): The solution was implemented in 2020 and has since been scaled in successive phases across the power, petrochemical, mining and water sectors.

Desired impact: The primary objective of the solution is to use the complex-terrain mobility of quadruped robots and multimodal inspection equipment to undertake repetitive and hazardous on-site inspection tasks, thereby reducing the need for personnel to enter high-risk areas. By standardizing inspection points, data collection requirements, and inspection management, the solution also improves the continuity and consistency of inspections and provides more reliable information for equipment condition tracking and maintenance decision-making. The expected impacts include reducing inspectors’ exposure to high-risk environments, such as areas near high-voltage equipment and underground or poorly ventilated spaces; extending inspection coverage to locations that are difficult for fixed monitoring systems or conventional mobile robots to reach; and enabling inspection results to be centrally reviewed, stored, and compared so that maintenance teams can promptly verify anomalies and arrange follow-up actions. Under continuous operation, robots can increase daily inspection frequency to four to six times that of manual inspection. In some deployments, the time required for a single inspection has been reduced by approximately 75%, while the average time to detect and address faults has been reduced by approximately 60%. Project experience has also shown operating-cost reductions of approximately 45% and a reduction of approximately 90% in assessed operational safety risk in certain settings. By automating routine data collection and reducing personnel entry into designated high-risk areas, the solution helps lower occupational hazard exposure and the likelihood of incidents.
Key technologies: Quadruped Robotics, Embodied AI, Autonomous Navigation, Multimodal Sensing, Industrial Inspection Platform
Unique Characteristics: The solution is distinguished by combining the complex-terrain mobility of quadruped robots with industrial inspection, enabling them to reach areas that are difficult for fixed cameras and wheeled robots to cover and to collect equipment and environmental data at designated inspection points. By integrating different inspection devices, the same robotic platform can be adapted to applications in the power, petrochemical, mining, and water sectors. Inspection data is consolidated on a management platform for continuous recording, comparison, and review. The solution follows a human–robot collaboration model: robots undertake repetitive and hazardous on-site data collection, while maintenance personnel supervise operations, assess the findings, and determine the appropriate response. This enables the solution to be piloted and gradually scaled within existing maintenance workflows.
Sustainable Change: The solution can be scaled from an initial pilot site to similar substations, power cable tunnels, mines, and water facilities. Reusing established inspection workflows, sensor configurations, and data management methods can reduce the repeated effort and cost associated with deployment and personnel training in new locations. As adoption expands, robots can undertake more frequent, repetitive, and high-risk on-site data collection, allowing maintenance teams to focus on verifying anomalies, assessing risks, and making maintenance decisions. Over time, standardized inspection data can also support equipment condition tracking and the optimization of maintenance plans, helping industrial inspection evolve from reliance on manual site visits and individual experience toward a human–robot collaborative, data-supported maintenance model.

Title: Hexing Partner Agent Collaboration Platform——A Unified Agent Collaboration Portal for Railway Production Environments
Subtitle: Using the complex heavy-haul transportation environment of the Shuohuang Railway as a typical application scenario, this solution precisely addresses the pain points in railway production, such as fragmented system entry points, severe data silos, lengthy operational workflows, heavy reliance on domain expertise, and highly repetitive document preparation. We have built a unified agent collaboration portal that, supported by agent orchestration, Skills encapsulation, and a knowledge base, seamlessly integrates existing professional systems and office tools into a single workspace. Through natural language interaction alone, users can break down system barriers and significantly reduce operational thresholds and switching costs, thereby completing daily production, management, and administrative tasks with higher efficiency and quality, realizing an intelligent transformation from a "human-searching-for-systems" model to a "task-driven" approach.
Problem Statement: This solution addresses the following challenges:1.Fragmented Systems and Data: Multiple system entry points and scattered data make collaborative data management difficult. 2.Complex Operations & Maintenance (O&M): Increasingly complex operating environments for equipment and facilities lead to low O&M efficiency and insufficient precision. 3.Variable Safety Risks: The high-speed, high-density, and large-volume characteristics of railway transportation create highly variable safety risks.
Solution Overview: This solution does not replace existing production systems. Instead, through agent orchestration, skills encapsulation, knowledge base support, and a unified interactive interface, it integrates production systems, professional analysis tools, office tools, and management workflows into a single workspace. This enables users to complete daily production, management, and administrative tasks via natural language interaction, task lists, workspaces, and skill invocation. The project is built upon the overarching concept of "a single entry point, multiple systems, capability encapsulation, and closed-loop task management." The initial phase targets production, technical, and management personnel at high-speed railway infrastructure maintenance divisions, covering 15 job categories and 200 users. It focuses on integrating three representative production systems: the track circuit system, the centralized signal monitoring system, and the ATP wireless download system. Core functions developed include task management, workspace management, historical conversations, knowledge base, skill library, component library, and agent dialogue. In the future, it can be scaled to more railway stations/depots, job roles, and existing production systems based on application performance.
Solution Provider(s): The key application partner for this solution is China Energy Shuohuang Railway Development Co., Ltd. (Transportation Sector). As a key subsidiary of CHN Energy, the company operates three heavy-haul freight railways with a total mileage of 889 km. Through rigorous validation in such complex large-scale industrial scenarios, the platform has demonstrated high reliability and flexibility. This also lays a solid foundation for promoting this technology in a cost-effective and lightweight manner to Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) in the industrial supply chain in the future.
Implementation location(s): The implementation location for this solution is Suning County, Cangzhou City, Hebei Province.
Implementation timeline(s): The "Research and Construction of Autonomous and Controllable Heavy-Haul Transportation Large Model System" project signed with China Energy Shuohuang Railway Development Co., Ltd. has an implementation period from February 2025 to October 2026.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: In the next step, based on the production and administrative needs of railway owners, we will continuously improve the standardized Skills capability library and the railway professional knowledge base, and gradually expand the pilot units, user scale, and business coverage to develop a replicable and scalable one-stop intelligent agent for rail transit production management and control. Meanwhile, leveraging its dual hubs in Singapore and Hong Kong, HollySys continues to expand its overseas business. With a global service network covering multiple key markets, the company continuously leads the internationalization of China's digital product manufacturing industry. Backed by this global service network and the international cooperation corridors of our existing partners, we plan to expand this solution into Southern countries and regions, particularly Southeast Asia. Targeting the limited network infrastructure in these regions, we will introduce a lightweight version that supports offline operation to empower the digital transformation of rail transit in more developing economies.
Desired impact: Using the Shuohuang Railway as a typical application scenario, the proven impacts of the Hexing Partner Agent Collaboration Platform include: 1. Efficiency Improvement: The time required for a single fault analysis report has been reduced from 240 minutes to 5 minutes; frontline operations and maintenance (O&M) efficiency has increased by ≥30%; system response time is ≤60 seconds. 2. Quality Enhancement: Fault identification accuracy is ≥90%; professional Q&A accuracy is ≥90%; over 100 typical fault cases have been accumulated. 3. Security and Controllability: 100% of operations are traceable and auditable; 100% manual confirmation is required in high-risk scenarios; private deployment ensures data remains strictly within controlled boundaries. 4. Experience Transfer: The onboarding period for new employees is shortened by 40%; the reuse rate of senior experts' experience is increased by 60%; knowledge assets are continuously iterated with version control.
Key technologies: The key technology used in this solution is Artificial Intelligence (AI). The Hexing Partner Agent Collaboration Platform is centered on Large Language Models (LLMs) and Multi-Agent Orchestration, and integrates Natural Language Processing (NLP) technologies to provide a unified intelligent dialogue and task interaction portal. Furthermore, it innovatively integrates Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with "Skills encapsulation" technology. This enables the AI to securely and precisely invoke existing production systems and internal knowledge bases, achieving automated closed-loop execution of complex industrial tasks.
Unique Characteristics: The application of the Hexing Partner Agent Collaboration Platform in the heavy-haul transportation scenario of the Shuohuang Railway demonstrates the following key innovations: 1. Innovation in Unified Entry Point: Shifting from isolated point tools to a unified intelligent agent portal, enabling cross-system, cross-task, and cross-document collaboration to reduce multi-system switching costs. 2. Innovation in Skills Encapsulation: Encapsulating existing system capabilities into standardized, callable, composable, and extensible "Skills," enabling the agent to organize capabilities around specific tasks rather than relying on isolated Q&A. 3. Innovation in Task Context: Utilizing workspaces, historical conversations, and knowledge bases to achieve document reuse, process traceability, and the accumulation of professional experience. 4. Innovation in Human-AI Collaboration: Positioning the AI agent as an assistant responsible for retrieval, organization, summarization, generation, and prompting, while critical production judgments and important operations are confirmed by human professionals. 5.Innovation in Security and Controllability: Ensuring strict permission boundaries, controlled interfaces, audit trails, verifiable outputs, and traceable operations, thereby providing a reliable foundation for deploying AI agents in industrial production environments.
Sustainable Change: Potential for Systemic Change: The platform has the potential to drive systemic change beyond its immediate implementation through four key dimensions: 1. Paradigm Shift in Industrial Workflows: It transforms the traditional "human-searching-for-systems" model into a "task-driven AI collaboration" model. By breaking down data silos, it establishes a new standard for human-AI collaboration in complex industrial environments, shifting workers' roles from manual operators to high-level decision-makers. 2. Knowledge Democratization and Skill Equity: By capturing and structuring tacit expert knowledge into a reusable knowledge base, the platform bridges the skills gap. It significantly lowers the entry barrier for new employees and underserved groups, democratizing access to advanced AI tools and fostering an inclusive digital workforce (aligning with GDC Objective 2). 3. Ecosystem Standardization and Replication: The standardized "Skills encapsulation" architecture allows the platform to be easily replicated across different railway bureaus, and seamlessly adapted to other critical infrastructure sectors (e.g., power, manufacturing). This creates a scalable, plug-and-play ecosystem for industrial AI. 4. Global Scalability for Developing Economies: Designed with private deployment and offline capabilities, this solution is highly adaptable to developing countries with limited network infrastructure. It offers a low-cost, highly efficient, and secure pathway for developing economies to leapfrog in digital industrialization, ensuring that AI benefits are shared globally.
Funding Sources: The funding for this solution is structured in two phases. During the R&D phase, the project was primarily self-funded through the company's internal research and development budget. During the implementation phase, financial sustainability is achieved through commercial revenue generated from collaborative projects and service agreements with our industry partners.
Primary thematic focus area: Embodied AI, Industrial Robotics and Smart Manufacturing
Summary: The Hexing Partner Agent Collaboration Platform gives railway staff one agent-based entry point across otherwise separate production systems, deployed on the Shuohuang Railway. Its strength is a named industrial deployment with sharp time savings; its weaknesses are unmeasured model quality, descriptive rather than demonstrative media, and a single-country footprint.

Title: The Intelligent Island Model: Leading a Revolution in Automotive Manufacturing
Subtitle: Replacing the rigid assembly line with AI- and digital-twin-driven decoupled, reconfigurable, adaptive production: 8 models per line, +30% efficiency, +80% logistics, -33% cycle; replicable globally.
Problem Statement: Automotive manufacturing currently faces three pressing challenges. First, the hot-selling window of a new vehicle model has been compressed from 36 months to 12 months, whereas the investment payback period of a conventional rigid production line is as long as 19 months and cannot keep pace with rapid model iteration. Second, personalized customer orders keep increasing and multiple models must be built on a single line, yet traditional assembly lines are slow to change over and inefficient in mixed-model production. Third, market demand fluctuates sharply, with a marked mismatch between production and sales peaks and troughs, making it difficult to align capacity planning. The root cause is the rigid serial assembly-line structure, which cannot reconcile mass production with customized production. SAIC-GM-Wuling pioneered the Intelligent Island Manufacturing System (I2MS), using artificial intelligence and digital twin technology to decouple processes and reconfigure production lines: the fixed serial assembly line is broken down into plug-and-play, scalable modular intelligent-island units, while AI dynamically schedules the mobile handling equipment and sequences the processes. This delivers threefold flexibility—of products, lines and capacity—and fundamentally reconstructs the automotive manufacturing model. The solution can further extend from complete vehicles to electric drive systems, battery PACKs, chassis, and interior and exterior trim components, providing a basis for cross-category replication.
Solution Overview: 1. How the solution works Following the transformation path of “process decoupling – line reconfiguration – island-based smart manufacturing”, the conventional serial assembly line is dismantled into 78 independently operating intelligent assembly islands: main-line islands undertake base-configuration assembly with streamlined processes, while branch-line islands serve individualized customer customization. Fixed conveyors are replaced by IGVs (Intelligent Guided Vehicles) that carry vehicle bodies and materials with autonomous navigation. Through the industrial internet, digital twins and smart logistics, “dynamic workstations” and “static islands” are linked in real time, enabling adaptive scheduling in which “the vehicle finds its workstation and materials find the vehicle”, with precise tooling docking. Islands can be plugged in or removed, the manufacturing-island topology can be rapidly reconfigured, and process paths can be dynamically planned, so that changes in models and capacity are accommodated without interrupting production. Vehicle-body model changeover time has been shortened from 45 minutes to 15 minutes. 2. Methodologies and technologies used The solution comprehensively applies the EOAI AI-based production-scheduling system, digital twins (a full-3D factory and a five-dimensional digital twin model), the industrial internet of things, 5G, cloud–edge–device collaborative computing, IGVs and collaborative robots, machine vision with AI in-line quality inspection, big-data real-time adaptive scheduling algorithms, flexible reconfigurable manufacturing cells, and PLC and industrial control software. Self-developed equipment includes unmanned forklifts, unmanned logistics vehicles, welding robots, collaborative robots, controllers and an intelligent fleet-control and scheduling system, breaking through the “black box” of equipment control to achieve end-to-end digital and intelligent connectivity of all production equipment. The five-dimensional digital twin model and a global intelligent scheduling methodology underpin intelligent process rehearsal, predictive maintenance and continuous optimization. 3. Partnerships and collaboration models An industry–academia–research–application collaborative innovation model is adopted. A consortium of 39 leading universities, research institutes and industry-chain enterprises has joined forces to upgrade I2MS 2.0, rapidly connecting technology R&D with industrial application and fostering a virtuous cycle between the innovation chain and the industrial chain. A mutually empowering “OEM–supplier” ecosystem has been built.
Solution Provider(s): China Automotive Industry Engineering Co., Ltd. (automotive industrial engineering and manufacturing-system integration); BZS (Beijing) Technology Development Co., Ltd. (intelligent logistics systems and industrial automation); Zhejiang Humanoid Robot Innovation Center Co., Ltd. (embodied intelligence and humanoid robotics R&D).
Implementation location(s): •  Liuzhou, China – SAIC-GM-Wuling Automobile Co., Ltd. •  Liuzhou, China – Saike Ruipu Power Battery System Co., Ltd. •  Liuzhou, China – Liuzhou Saike Technology Development Co., Ltd. •  Liuzhou, China – Liuzhou Huizhong Automotive Manufacturing Co., Ltd. •  Cikarang, Bekasi Regency, West Java, Indonesia – PT SGMW Motor Indonesia The Intelligent Island model has been extended from complete vehicles to electric drive, battery PACK and chassis enterprises, forming a replicable flexible manufacturing solution for components. SAIC-GM-Wuling Automobile Co., Ltd. – Baojun Base (first line commissioned in 2023): Production efficiency of the final-assembly shop increased by 30%, and the body-shop changeover cycle was shortened by 66.7%. The coordination of flexible smart manufacturing with intelligent quality inspection safeguards high-quality multi-model production, lifting overall operations to a new level. Saike Ruipu Power Battery System Co., Ltd. (commissioned January 2025): The PACK island line adopts a modular architecture, supports rapid switching among multiple CTP battery packs, and achieves fault isolation and elastic capacity expansion. Liuzhou Saike Technology Development Co., Ltd. (commissioned June 2025): The electric-drive island line decouples processes into independent units scheduled and transported by IGVs; a single island accommodates 36 electric-drive products, model changeover is shortened to 15 minutes, and the new-product introduction cycle is halved. Liuzhou Huizhong Automotive Manufacturing Co., Ltd. (commissioned August 2026): Huizhong transplanted the island model to chassis assembly; relying on flexible IGV flows, PCS scheduling and digital twins, the new-product introduction cycle is shortened by 30% and retrofit costs are reduced by about 30%. PT SGMW Motor Indonesia line (commissioned January 2025): The PACK island line adopts a modular architecture supporting fast switching between multiple CTP battery packs for both hybrid and battery-electric vehicles, achieving 100% traceability of process data and a 99% first-pass yield, with a lean and flexible layout. The Indonesia power-battery intelligent island is the flagship overseas deployment of the Intelligent Island system. The line solution is customized to the investment budget and deploys core battery-island modules including a cell-integration island and a laser-welding island, full-dimension in-line inspection and an MES. AI plus vision supports welding guidance (recognition of complex features), AI pre-judgment of all quality parameters of cells and complete packs (including prediction of cell and pack performance degradation), and predictive equipment maintenance (such as alerts on parameter drift of key welding equipment), while adapting to local operating conditions and regulatory requirements in both countries. The intelligent islands enable flexible co-line production of multiple battery models with controlled consistency and stably compliant yields, verifying that the entire modular intelligent-island system can be transplanted and reused across regions and providing a standardized blueprint for subsequent overseas replication.
Implementation timeline(s): The first line at SAIC-GM-Wuling’s Baojun Base was commissioned in 2023 and has remained in continuous operation since then; multi-model mixed-line expansion and replication across multiple bases were completed in 2024–2025. Saike Ruipu Power Battery System Co., Ltd. was commissioned in January 2025; Liuzhou Saike Technology Development Co., Ltd. in June 2025; Liuzhou Huizhong Automotive Manufacturing Co., Ltd. in August 2026; and the PT SGMW Motor Indonesia line in January 2025.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: With a completed factory building and sound site infrastructure in place (road access and connections for water, power, gas and telecommunications, plus leveled ground), deployment can be achieved in as little as two months, followed by one month of production ramp-up. Experience from existing projects: Saike Ruipu Power Battery System Co., Ltd.: •  Equipment procurement: September 2024 •  Equipment arrival on site: November 2024 •  Installation and commissioning: December 2024 •  Trial production: December 2024 •  SOP (Start of Production): January 2025 Liuzhou Saike Technology Development Co., Ltd.: •  Equipment procurement: February 2025 •  Equipment arrival on site: April 2025 •  Installation and commissioning: May 2025 •  Trial production: May 2025 •  SOP (Start of Production): June 2025
Desired impact: Main objective: to replace the traditional rigid assembly line with the AI- and digital-twin-driven Intelligent Island Manufacturing System (I2MS), achieving decoupled processes, reconfigurable lines, adaptive capacity, value-adding data, an evolvable system and an extensible model; supporting highly efficient mixed-model production of multiple vehicle models; and enabling replication and promotion across global discrete manufacturing. Verified impact at SAIC-GM-Wuling’s Baojun Base since the deployment of the Intelligent Island system in 2023 (large-scale operating data): 1. Product flexibility: a single line simultaneously supports mixed-model production of eight vehicle models, with a total designed capacity of no less than 300,000 units per year per line. 2. Efficiency gains: mixed-model manufacturing efficiency up 30%; logistics efficiency up 80%; final-assembly manufacturing cycle shortened by 33%. 3. Quality and traceability: quality-detection accuracy of 99.5%; first-pass yield of 99.3%; 100% traceability of data from key manufacturing-process steps. 4. Green and low-carbon: an energy-and-carbon benchmark factory has been built around the intelligent islands, with per-vehicle production energy consumption of approximately 0.10 tce (tonnes of coal equivalent) in 2026, a global industry-leading level. A multi-dimensional energy-consumption model built with AI dynamically generates optimal control schemes for best-in-class system energy efficiency: under identical operating conditions, the energy-saving rate is 19%, and 1.9 million kWh of electricity was saved in 2025. 5. Innovation and social value: 110 granted invention patents and 67 software copyrights accumulated; participation in developing and revising six Chinese national and industry standards; a smart-manufacturing workforce of more than 10,000 professionals cultivated; smart-factory construction guidance provided to five industry-chain enterprises.
Key technologies: Artificial intelligence (the EOAI industrial large model), digital twins, the internet of things (IoT), IGVs (Intelligent Guided Vehicles), big data and real-time adaptive scheduling algorithms, machine vision and AI in-line quality inspection, cloud–edge–device collaborative computing, the Excellence Operation Digital Platform (EODP), flexible reconfigurable manufacturing cells, PLC and industrial control software, and 5G.
Unique Characteristics: 1. Technological innovation: six disruptive breakthroughs •  Decoupled processes: the serial assembly line is split into independent intelligent assembly islands, with hundreds of intelligent IGVs shuttling for precision delivery, allowing multiple process flows to run in parallel. •  Reconfigurable lines: a workstation layout combining dynamic and static stations enables minute-level vehicle-model switching. •  Adaptive capacity: workstations and assembly islands can be added or removed without interrupting production, supporting “the vehicle finds its workstation” and “materials find the vehicle”. •  Value-adding data: the self-developed EODP platform connects the entire R&D–supply–manufacturing–marketing chain. •  Evolvable system: the self-developed EOAI operational excellence large model establishes a new data-driven, real-time-responding, self-evolving paradigm. •  Extensible model: successfully applied to body manufacturing, battery manufacturing and knock-down (KD) exports, with the potential to migrate to discrete-manufacturing sectors such as home appliances and medical equipment. 2. Innovation in partnership and delivery models Joint development under the industry–academia–research–application model, bringing together 39 leading universities, research institutes and industry-chain enterprises, rapidly connects technology R&D with industrial application and fuels a fast cycle between the innovation chain and the industrial chain.

Title: AI-Driven Precision AgTech Platform for Sustainable Crop & Climate Management
Subtitle: An integrated ecosystem combining satellite intelligence, IoT weather sensors, and AI to optimize resource efficiency and mitigate climate risks for regional agribusinesses.
Problem Statement: Agribusinesses face severe climate volatility, water scarcity, and inefficient resource allocation. Traditional farming lacks real-time, data-driven field visibility, leading to excessive chemical and fertilizer usage, crop losses, and high operational costs. This solution addresses these challenges by transforming raw agronomic, satellite, and climate data into actionable, AI-powered insights to ensure food security, minimize inputs, and foster sustainable industrial agricultural operations.
Solution Overview: Our solution integrates satellite remote sensing, localized IoT hardware, and predictive AI models to optimize large-scale farming and agribusiness value chains. We deploy the Cropwise Operations platform alongside METOS precision weather stations to stream field telemetry, including vegetation indices (NDVI) and real-time soil-moisture levels. By applying machine learning models to this data, the platform generates automated, actionable insights for crop planning, operational task management, and precise input deployment (water and fertilizer). The collaboration model operates as an integrated commercial platform linking global tech providers with regional agribusinesses to drive local agronomic validation and scalable digital deployment.
Solution Provider(s): Syngenta Cropwise Operations (Switzerland, Digital Agriculture Platform Provider), METOS / Pessl Instruments (Austria, Precision Climate and IoT Sensor Manufacturer), Velcourt (United Kingdom, Farm-Management and Technical Advisory)
Implementation location(s): Egypt (Multiple agricultural sites including Giza, Beheira, Minya, and El Farafra Oasis).
Implementation timeline(s): Implemented from January 2024 to Ongoing.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3 to 6 months (including IoT hardware deployment, satellite calibration, and local team training).
Desired impact: The main objective is to empower agribusinesses with actionable intelligence to counter climate uncertainty and maximize resource efficiency. Our demonstrated impact includes an average 15-20% reduction in water consumption through precision soil-moisture tracking, and a 10-15% optimization in fertilizer and agrochemical application rates, directly lowering agricultural input costs and chemical runoff. Furthermore, the solution improves crop yield forecasting accuracy by up to 90%, strengthening regional food supply resilience and securing higher profit margins for local farmers.
Key technologies: Our solution leverages a robust blend of advanced technologies: 1) Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning models for predictive crop analytics and disease detection; 2) Internet of Things (IoT) via localized smart weather and soil sensors for real-time telemetry; 3) Satellite Remote Sensing and Geospatial Data Analytics (NDVI) for extensive canopy monitoring; and 4) Big Data Architecture to ingest, process, and synchronize multiple environmental and agronomic data streams seamlessly.
Unique Characteristics: What differentiates our solution is its hybrid delivery approach that links global digital frameworks with local field execution. Unlike static software, we merge satellite analytics with localized IoT sensory data to deliver hyper-local, field-specific insights rather than regional generalizations. Additionally, our business model stands out by integrating technology with a trusted agronomic distribution network, ensuring seamless adoption, active local training, and ongoing hands-on technical support for agribusinesses in emerging markets.
Sustainable Change: Our solution drives systemic change by shifting traditional agriculture from reactive practices to proactive, data-driven frameworks. By proving the commercial and environmental viability of AI-powered farming, we inspire market-wide digital adoption. The follow-on effects include standardizing resource conservation, reducing chemical footprints in national agricultural outputs, and training a new generation of tech-savvy agronomists. Built on a flexible and cloud-based architecture, our digital model is highly replicable and easily scaled across diverse geographies, facilitating broad-scale agricultural resilience and systemic food security throughout emerging markets.
Funding Sources: The solution has been entirely self-funded through private corporate investments by DOTRA Group, alongside commercial technology partnerships and joint deployments with global agricultural developers.

Title: AI for Cotton-to-Yarn: From Fiber Intelligence to Smart Spinning
Subtitle: Enabling AI for fiber measurement, intelligent analytics, optimized cotton blending and smart spinning technologies to improve productivity, quality and industrial competitiveness
Problem Statement: Cotton is a major source of livelihoods, export earnings, job opportunities, and industrial potential in many developing countries. However, gaps in fibre-quality information and manufacturing capabilities limit opportunities to improve competitiveness and capture greater value across the cotton-to-yarn chain. First, cotton market systems do not adequately capture or communicate the full range of fibre characteristics that determine industrial performance and end-use value, including fibre length distribution, short-fibre content, colour variation, maturity and impurities. Existing testing and classification systems provide useful technical information, but this is not consistently translated into actionable intelligence for pricing, sourcing, cotton blending and spinning decisions. These information gaps can prevent producers and ginners from obtaining appropriate quality premiums, while manufacturers face repeated testing costs and uncertainty about raw-material suitability. Limited capacities for advanced fibre analytics and market-oriented interpretation further constrain quality-based value upgrading. Second, spinning manufacturers face challenges in both standalone automation and process continuity. At the individual-machine level, labour-intensive operations and repetitive manual tasks limit production consistency and increase dependence on operator availability and experience. At the production-line level, even automated machines may remain disconnected: manual material transfers, poorly coordinated processing stages and limited integration between equipment, material handling and production-management systems create bottlenecks, excessive work-in-progress inventory and delays. Third, end-to-end production intelligence remains limited. Conventional automation typically operates on preset parameters and cannot readily adapt to variations in raw-material quality, environmental conditions or equipment performance. Fragmented data and limited real-time analysis make it difficult to connect fibre characteristics with optimized cotton blending and spinning settings, trace quality problems across the production chain, and detect emerging equipment faults before they cause downtime. Together, these challenges create a need for an integrated cotton-to-yarn approach that connects AI-enabled fibre measurement and intelligent analytics with machine automation, continuous material flows and adaptive spinning operations. Such integration can support quality-driven markets, more efficient manufacturing and greater local value addition, particularly where shortages of specialized expertise constrain industrial development.
Solution Overview: The integrated cotton-to-yarn solution brings together its AI-enabled fibre testing and intelligent analytics with spinning equipment, automated material handling and digital production-management capabilities. Working with research and quality institutions through the proposed UNIDO project “Transforming Cotton Value Chains through Intelligent Fiber Analytics for Competitive and Transparent Markets” (Smart Cotton Value Chain), Jingwei contributes to the development and industrial application of fibre-analysis technologies and their connection with downstream manufacturing. The package creates a pathway from cotton-quality information to informed sourcing, optimized blending and smart spinning. How the solution works The package comprises four interconnected components: • Intelligent cotton-fibre testing and analytics: Planned next-generation testing equipment would measure fibre length distribution, short-fibre content, three-dimensional colour, maturity and impurities, while integrating other High-Volume Instrument (HVI) parameters covered by current standards. Automated sample preparation, imaging and AI-enabled analytics would translate measurements into insights for cotton selection, blending, spinning and transparent, quality-based trading. • Automated spinning equipment: Machinery automates individual processing stages, reducing repetitive manual tasks and supporting consistent production. The proposed connection with fibre analytics would help inform raw-material selection and spinning parameters. • Integrated material handling: Linking systems connect carding–drawing, drawing–roving, roving–spinning, spinning–winding and winding–packing, coordinating material movement to reduce manual transfers, bottlenecks and work-in-progress accumulation. • Intelligent production management: Connected equipment and sensors support monitoring, quality traceability and remote operations. AI-enabled analysis supports process-setting optimization and early fault identification. Integration with upstream fibre analytics would allow cotton characteristics and operational data to jointly inform manufacturing decisions. Methodologies and technologies used The fibre-testing machine component combines automated sample preparation, measurement and imaging technologies, multi-dimensional fibre analytics and AI-integrated control systems. Its development methodology would include laboratory validation, comparative testing, model calibration and prototype refinement, followed by validation of industrial applications. The AI methodology follows a “sense, decide and predict” approach: sensors and imaging capture fibre characteristics and operating conditions; analytical models support cotton selection, blending and process settings; and machine-condition analysis identifies emerging faults to inform maintenance. The intelligent material-handling system integrates closely with manufacturing execution systems (MES), enterprise resource planning (ERP) and warehouse management systems (WMS). Using Internet of Things (IoT) and radio-frequency identification (RFID) technologies, it automatically collects data on incoming and outgoing materials, delivery to production lines and work-in-progress movements, enabling coordinated production across the full process. Partnerships and collaboration models Jingwei works with Donghua University (DHU) and the University of Science and Technology of China (USTC) on technology innovation, research, testing and validation, connecting academic expertise with industrial requirements for intelligent fibre analysis and automation. For international delivery, Jingwei collaborates with CTMTC, the international engineering and business unit of China Hi-Tech Group Corporation. Equipment and engineering capabilities are combined with local partnerships, knowledge sharing and adaptation to host-country market conditions, resources and regulatory requirements.
Solution Provider(s): China Texmatech Co., Ltd (CTMTC) — the international engineering and business unit of China Hi-Tech Group Corporation (CHTC), operating in textile engineering, machinery and international industrial cooperation; Donghua University (DHU) — academic and research institution specializing in textile and fibre science, partner for fibre measurement and intelligent analytics research and testing; University of Science and Technology of China (USTC) — academic and research institution with expertise in automation and intelligent technologies, partner for automated sample preparation and control-system integration.
Implementation location(s): Burkina Faso, Pakistan, Vietnam, India, Türkiye, Mexico, Nicaragua
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 1 year
Desired impact: The solution aims to improve productivity, yarn quality and resource efficiency by connecting intelligent cotton-fibre analysis with optimized blending, automated spinning and integrated production management. Its objectives are to: • Improve understanding of cotton characteristics and processing suitability, supporting informed raw-material selection, optimized blending and more transparent, quality-based trading. • Increase production consistency and continuity through automated equipment and coordinated material flows. • Reduce avoidable material waste, energy use and downtime through data-driven process optimization and early fault detection. • Support industrial competitiveness and local value addition through technology transfer, knowledge sharing and the development of technical capabilities. For the spinning component, Jingwei reports demonstrated results at the 45,000-spindle Dasheng mill in Nantong, China, which has been in full production since 2025 and is equipped largely with Jingwei machinery. The reported indicators are a 40% increase in production efficiency, a 30% reduction in energy consumption per unit of output, fewer than eight workers per 10,000 spindles, and 100% quality-data traceability. These are mill-level results from integrated equipment, automation and digital management. The planned intelligent cotton-fibre testing component would extend these benefits upstream by translating fibre measurements into practical information for cotton selection, blending and spinning. It is expected to help producers and ginners communicate quality more effectively and enable manufacturers to better match cotton inputs to production requirements. These upstream benefits have not yet been quantified.
Key technologies: The solution combines the following technologies: • Intelligent fibre testing and imaging: Planned next-generation machine would measure fibre length distribution, short-fibre content, three-dimensional colour, maturity and impurities, while integrating additional High-Volume Instrument (HVI) parameters covered by current standards. Automated sample preparation, imaging and control systems would support consistent measurement. • AI-enabled analytics: Fibre and production data would inform cotton selection, blending and process-setting optimization. Jingwei’s spinning approach follows a “sense, decide and predict” methodology: vision and sensors capture fibre and operating conditions; analytical models support suitable process settings; and predictive analysis identifies early signs of equipment faults. • Automated spinning and material handling: Equipment and linking systems coordinate successive stages from carding and drawing through roving, spinning, winding and packing, reducing manual transfers and supporting continuous production. • Industrial Internet of Things (IoT) and radio-frequency identification (RFID): Connected sensors and identification technologies collect equipment and material-flow data, including incoming and outgoing materials, line-side delivery and work-in-progress movements. • Integrated digital management: Manufacturing execution systems (MES), enterprise resource planning (ERP) and warehouse management systems (WMS) connect production, logistics and business information, supporting monitoring, quality traceability and remote operations.
Unique Characteristics: AI marks a shift from “Automation” to “Intelligence”. Jingwei’s solution brings this shift to cotton-to-yarn production by connecting fibre analysis with smart spinning. Conventional automated equipment typically runs on preset parameters, with adjustments relying heavily on operator experience. AI-enabled analytics use fibre and operational data to support more informed responses to changes in raw materials, environmental conditions and equipment performance through three interconnected functions: SENSE: Vision systems and sensors capture fibre characteristics, foreign matter and operating conditions, providing detailed information beyond what routine visual inspection can reliably assess. The planned intelligent fibre-testing component would extend this capability through more comprehensive cotton-quality measurements. • DECIDE: AI-enabled analytics translate fibre and production data into decision support for cotton selection, optimized blending and suitable spinning settings. This connects raw-material characteristics with yarn-quality requirements and helps reduce reliance on trial-and-error adjustments. • PREDICT: Analysis of machine data helps identify early signs of equipment faults, supporting timely maintenance and reducing the risk of unplanned downtime. By linking fibre intelligence with spinning decisions, the solution makes cotton-quality data actionable for both manufacturing and transparent, quality-based trading. Embedded analytical support also reduces reliance on specialist experience for routine adjustments, helping address skills shortages that can constrain the establishment or upgrading of spinning industries.
Sustainable Change: The solution could support a broader transition towards cotton value chains in which quality information guides trading, processing and investment decisions. More detailed fibre analysis could help producers and ginners demonstrate the value of their cotton, support fairer and more transparent trading, and strengthen incentives for quality improvement. Manufacturers could use the same information to select suitable cotton, optimize blends and produce yarn that meets market requirements. For cotton-producing developing countries, connecting fibre intelligence with smart spinning could support greater local processing and value addition. More consistent production, efficient resource use and better quality control could strengthen industrial competitiveness and create opportunities for local technical services, equipment maintenance and skilled employment. The solution also offers a pathway for progressive upgrading. Existing mills could introduce relevant components according to their needs, while new factories could adopt an integrated cotton-to-yarn approach. Replication would require adaptation to local cotton characteristics, infrastructure, workforce capabilities and market demand. Collaboration between Jingwei, academic institutions, CTMTC and local partners could support this expansion through technology development, testing, training and knowledge transfer. Building local capabilities to operate, maintain and adapt the technologies would help sustain improvements beyond individual installations and support wider industrial development.
Funding Sources: Previous implementations have been primarily private-sector driven, through commercial investment in equipment and industrial deployment.

Title: EDITH - Education Digital Interactive Tool Helper - WhatsApp-native AI that turns government records into decisions
Subtitle: A WhatsApp assistant that gives education ministry staff one fast, cited answer on schools, teachers and policy, built on 13,444 school records and 19 official documents in Sierra Leone.
Problem Statement: Sierra Leone’s education ministry oversees 13,444 schools across 16 districts, but its information was hard to reach and hard to trust. Policy and data queries took 48 to 96 hours through traditional channels. Nineteen official documents and years of census data sat in separate files. False claims about policy spread on WhatsApp with no way to check them. Field staff who work only on smartphones were shut out of desktop systems. Slow, fragmented, unverified data leads to slow decisions, and AI that answers without a source can’t be trusted in government. Inclusive transformation of any sector, industry included, starts with this base layer: reliable public data and institutions able to run AI themselves.
Solution Overview: EDITH is live with the Ministry of Basic and Senior Secondary Education (MBSSE) since March 2026. Source: https://edtechhub.org/case-study/the-graduate-who-brought-ai-to-sierra-leones-ministry-of-education/ How it works: a staff member sends a question on WhatsApp. EDITH checks an access code, matches the question against a curated knowledge base, and answers with a citation to the source it used. If the base has no answer, it searches approved news sources live. It also checks false claims against the law (confirmed, false or unverified). Knowledge base: 13,444 school records, 2,144 teacher records (looked up by PIN) and 19 official policy and legal documents, covering all 16 districts. Technology: retrieval-augmented generation with GPT-4o, a WhatsApp interface with no app to install, and a five-layer zero-trust security design. Partnership model: built with the ministry’s Delivery Unit under EdTech Hub’s Ministries of Education AI Challenge, with R4D and UK-funded support. Eight members of the ministry’s delivery team were trained.
Solution Provider(s): EdTech Hub (education research and technical assistance organisation), Results for Development (R4D, global development non-profit), Ministry of Basic and Senior Secondary Education, Sierra Leone (public sector; Delivery Unit).
Implementation location(s): Sierra Leone: knowledge base covers all 16 districts; used by ministry staff with access codes, including a rural teacher pilot.
Implementation timeline(s): October 2025 (embedded build began) to present; live with MBSSE since March 2026.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: About 3 to 4 months, if the host institution provides its records and approved documents. This is my estimate. The first build took 7 months, so change it to what you can deliver.
Desired impact: Objective: give government staff one fast, trusted, cited answer on WhatsApp, and show that a ministry can run AI on its own approved data, with security built in. Demonstrated: Answers in under 3 seconds, against 48 to 96 hours through traditional channels (reported baseline). Week one (March 2026): 132 queries in 87 conversations. 70.1% of rated answers were helpful (61 of 87), 20.7% partly helpful, and 9.2% not helpful. Usage reached about 1,000 conversations a month by September 2026. 120 individual staff access codes, a weekly human review of “not helpful” answers, 14 prompt versions and 7 rounds of user testing. Chosen from 30+ applications across 16 countries for EdTech Hub’s expert support package. The published case study notes that building such a tool from scratch would have cost upwards of $100,000. “Foundation Before Tool” was selected for AUDA-NEPAD’s AYEF 2026 series. Expected: phone-number whitelisting, an audit dashboard and district expansion, which your roadmap marks as dependent on resources.
Key technologies: AI (retrieval-augmented generation with GPT-4o), WhatsApp Business API, live web search, zero-trust access control (access codes, canary codes, session gate, retry limit, human review).
Unique Characteristics: 1.Every answer cites an approved source, and a false-claim checker tests rumours against the law. 2. It runs on WhatsApp, so there is no app, desktop or IT skills needed. 3. Zero-trust design: individual access codes, honeypot “canary” codes that log probes, and weekly human review. 4. It was built inside the ministry by an embedded expert, with a method of repeated testing (14 prompt versions, 7 rounds) and “no data, no AI” discipline.
Sustainable Change: The method (curate the approved data first, then add cited retrieval over WhatsApp) can be adapted to other ministries and to agencies that support industry and MSMEs. It is low-cost, with no new devices needed. Your own lessons point to what sustains it: a named technical owner, and regular refreshes of the knowledge base. The next step is a pilot in a new country or sector.
Funding Sources: Built in 2025 to 2026 with a £50,000 expert support package awarded to the Ministry of Basic and Senior Secondary Education (through its Delivery Unit) by EdTech Hub’s AI Observatory and Action Lab. It was selected from over 30 applications across 16 countries for the Ministry of Education AI Challenge. The AI Observatory is supported by UK International Development (FCDO), and EdTech Hub is supported by UK International Development and the World Bank Group. The platform runs on a one-year licence (source: EdTech Hub case study). Next-phase funding is being sought.
Testimonials and Endorsements: From Conrad Sackey, Minister of Basic and Senior Secondary Education, Sierra Leone, in a LinkedIn post about EDITH (link: https://lnkd.in/p/e556MMjd): “EDITH is a digital aid for our ministry officials in the field, simplifying access to critical education information and reducing tasks that once took days or weeks down to minutes.” “Seeing Deputy Directors move from ‘what is AI?’ to actively exploring how it can solve real administrative challenges and watching their excitement during EDITH’s presentation and installation was the most rewarding part of this journey.” “Sierra Leone built something real. And we are just getting started.”
Primary thematic focus area: Industrial Ecosystem Enablers: Finance, Skills and Market Access

Its strength is a live government deployment with measured response times and a zero-trust design; its weaknesses are unmeasured retrieval performance and a single-country footprint, which hold technical capability at band 3 and geography at band 1.

Title: Uravu Clausius: AI-Powered IoT Cooling for Water-Positive Industry
Subtitle: AI-powered closed-loop platform that utilizes real-time IoT data and industrial waste heat to deliver autonomous, water-positive cooling, eliminating groundwater reliance in heavy industries.
Problem Statement: Global heavy industries, pharmaceutical complexes, and rapidly expanding data centers face a critical, compounding three-fold challenge: 1. Severe Water Depletion: Industrial manufacturing relies heavily on traditional evaporative cooling towers. These loops consume billions of liters of high-purity freshwater daily, directly depleting local groundwater tables and putting operations at risk from strict environmental regulations and intense water scarcity. 2. Massive Energy and Thermal Waste: Industrial processes reject immense amounts of low-grade thermal waste (35°C to 85°C) directly into the atmosphere. This unused energy represents a massive loss of resource efficiency and drives up operational Scope 1 emissions. 3. Inefficient, Static Infrastructure: Conventional industrial cooling and water systems operate on static, hard-coded parameters. They are completely unable to adapt in real time to fluctuating ambient microclimates or variable facility thermal loads, resulting in highly inefficient energy use and frequent operational downtime. Our solution turns these compounding challenges into a synchronized, circular utility loop.
Solution Overview: Solution Overview How it Works: The Uravu Clausius platform is a cyber-physical system that transforms industrial thermal waste into a water-positive utility loop. A proprietary liquid desiccant absorbs ambient atmospheric moisture, which is then released as ultra-pure, zero-TDS water using low-grade industrial waste heat (35°C–85°C). Integrated directly into data center or factory cooling systems, it replaces water-intensive evaporative cooling towers, delivering zero-groundwater cooling and a negative Water Usage Effectiveness (WUE). Methodologies & Technologies: 1. Physics & Thermodynamics: Proprietary liquid-desiccant chemistry and high-efficiency low-grade waste heat recovery (WHR) loops. 2. Industrial IoT & Telemetry: Secure edge gateways streaming live sensor data (ambient climate, fluid flow, thermal loads) via MQTT/Modbus protocols. 3. Edge-AI Optimization: An AI engine that cross-references live IoT telemetry with external meteorological APIs to predict micro-climate shifts and dynamically adjust desiccant regeneration cycles. This active data loop boosts moisture-extraction efficiency by 35% over static hardware. Partnerships & Collaboration Models: 1. Utility-as-a-Service: Deployed via Water-as-a-Service (WaaS) and Cooling-as-a-Service (CaaS) models, eliminating client CAPEX through transparent, AI-monitored, performance-based monthly SLAs. 2. Industrial Integration: Collaboration with global EPC firms and Building Management System (BMS) providers for rapid plug-and-play scaling. 3. Validation Networks: Backed by clean-tech acceleration frameworks (such as the UNIDO-linked FLCTD) to fast-track deployments in water-stressed industrial clusters globally.
Solution Provider(s): Facility for Low Carbon Technology Deployment (FLCTD) / Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) (Sector: Multilateral & Government Clean Energy Acceleration; Profile: A project implemented jointly by UNIDO, the Global Environment Facility, and the Government of India that selected Uravu Labs as a winner, providing funding and validated pathways for industrial waste-heat recovery), Anheuser-Busch InBev (AB InBev) (Sector: Global Beverage & FMCG Manufacturing; Profile: A multinational beverage corporation that partnered with Uravu Labs through its 100+ Accelerator program to pilot and validate sustainable atmospheric water loops within commercial production), Hub71 Abu Dhabi (Sector: Global Tech Ecosystem & Venture Acceleration; Profile: Abu Dhabi’s global tech ecosystem that selected Uravu Labs into its incentive program, providing strategic corporate access, market expansion scaling, and regional validation for deploying water-positive cooling in hyper-arid environments), Qatar Science & Technology Park (QSTP) (Sector: Deep-Tech Research & Development Ecosystem; Profile: A premier incubator and free zone within Qatar Foundation that accelerated Uravu Labs, validating their proprietary liquid-desiccant thermodynamics and supporting regional R&D for rainfall-independent industrial utility platforms), Radisson Hotels / Luxury Hospitality Chains (Sector: Commercial Hospitality & Real Estate; Profile: Premium hospitality groups serving as commercial off-take partners, utilizing Uravu Labs' 100% renewable, zero-groundwater atmospheric water systems to fulfill corporate net-zero water mandates).
Implementation location(s): India (Bengaluru), United Arab Emirates (Abu Dhabi), Qatar (Doha).
Implementation timeline(s): 2019 – Present (Continuous Multi-Phase Deployment) India (Bengaluru), 2026 - United Arab Emirates (Abu Dhabi), 2027 - Qatar (Doha).
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3 to 6 Months
Desired impact: 1. Core Objectives of the Solution Eliminate Industrial Groundwater Consumption: To replace water-intensive evaporative cooling towers in heavy industries and data centers with a closed-loop, water-positive liquid-desiccant framework, driving the facility’s Water Usage Effectiveness (WUE) down to a zero or negative value. Unlock Zero-Cost Resource Circularity: To harvest low-grade, unutilized industrial waste heat (35°C–85°C) that facilities typically vent into the environment, converting it into a valuable thermal power source for atmospheric water generation. Deploy Autonomous Data-Driven Utilities: To transition traditional, rigid mechanical industrial cooling infrastructure into an intelligent, self-optimizing system using real-time IoT networks and localized Edge-AI predictive modeling. 2. Demonstrated and Expected Impact (Quantified Metrics) Water Savings & Conservation: By eliminating evaporative cooling losses, a single standard commercial installation saves up to 90% of freshwater consumption compared to traditional cooling configurations. For a medium-scale data center facility, this preserves millions of liters of local groundwater tables annually.
