Title: AI, Can!: Sovereign AI Infrastructure That Gets Industry Past the Pilot
Subtitle: Deploys secure, governed AI infrastructure into an organisation’s own Azure tenant in under 15 minutes, with Zero Trust and governance enforced from installation. No data leaves the tenant.
Problem Statement: Industrial firms and public bodies can build AI pilots. Few reach production. Four barriers stop them. Time and cost. A secure, production-grade AI environment typically takes 3–9 months and $50,000–$100,000+ of specialist engineering to build, and it is rebuilt for each project. Skills. The engineers who can build it are scarce, and hiring takes 12–18 months. Security and regulation. Security and compliance are usually retrofitted after deployment. NIS2, which now covers many manufacturers, and the EU AI Act make that too late. Sovereignty. Data, models and logs must stay under the organisation’s control, not a vendor’s.
Solution Overview: How it works. AI, Can! is an Azure Managed Application, bought on the Microsoft Azure Marketplace for $799 a month. In under 15 minutes it deploys a complete production AI environment into the customer’s own Azure tenant. The environment is defined as code: hub-and-spoke networking, Azure Firewall, API Management, and Azure AI Foundry behind private endpoints. Zero Trust identity controls and governance policies are enforced from installation. All customer data stays in the customer’s tenant. A central governance layer keeps AI behaviour consistent and version-controlled across development, testing and production. The runtime is MCP-native, so AI agents reach tools and data through the open Model Context Protocol inside a secured boundary. In development for V2: automated compliance evidence for NIS2 and the EU AI Act, infrastructure drift detection, automated secret rotation, and a cost dashboard showing cost per agent and per conversation. Methodology. We engineer production AI for governments and regulated organisations. Every pattern proven in the field ships back into AI, Can!, so each deployment makes the next faster and safer. We then train the customer’s own team through accredited programmes delivered with CYENS, ATI, UCLan and COMCY. One programme is approved by Cyprus’s Human Resource Development Authority (HRDA). Live deployments. Artemis has built and runs 3 live systems: - CySKILLS-AI, a national skills-intelligence platform for the Republic of Cyprus, funded by the Research and Innovation Foundation and delivered with CYENS and the Ministry of Education - TideMRV, a blue-carbon monitoring, reporting and verification (MRV) pilot - PromoGoat, an AI ad-planning SaaS for small businesses Separately, two customers pay for AI, Can! on the Marketplace, with zero churn since January 2026. Artemis’s founders co-founded TideMRV and PromoGoat. Partnerships and collaboration model. Artemis is a Microsoft Cloud & AI Partner, with co-sell active in Cyprus and in activation in Poland and Malaysia. KPMG Cyprus IT Advisory is testing AI, Can! and co-developing an offer for its enterprise clients. CYENS is our research and delivery partner. Partners bring the client and the domain expertise. We bring the platform, the engineering and the training. Customers buy through the Marketplace, so the purchase counts toward their existing Azure spending commitments. Because each environment is a code template, a solution proven in one country can be redeployed in another country’s Azure region, under its own data rules.
Solution Provider(s): Microsoft Corporation – global cloud provider; Artemis is a Microsoft Cloud & AI Partner, AI, Can! is sold through the Azure Marketplace, and co-sell is active in Cyprus; sector: cloud computing, KPMG Cyprus – professional services firm, IT Advisory practice; testing AI, Can! and co-developing an enterprise offer; sector: professional services and advisory, CYENS Centre of Excellence – Cyprus research and innovation centre in interactive media, smart systems and emerging technologies; research and delivery partner on CySKILLS-AI; sector: research and innovation
Implementation location(s): Republic of Cyprus (nationwide)
Implementation timeline(s): AI, Can! in production since January, 2026, listed on the Azure Marketplace since April 2026. Implemented on CySKILLS-AI: since August 2026 (36-month programme, ongoing). TideMRV pilot: September 2026. PromoGoat: live since August 2026, ongoing.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Platform deployment into a new country’s Azure region: under one day. Working pilot, with one use case live, data connected, governance controls configured and the local team trained: 6–8 weeks. The estimate depends on Azure being available in that country or a nearby region.
Desired impact: Objectives. First, get mid-sized manufacturers, regulated firms and public bodies from AI pilots to secure, governed production systems. Second, replace months of custom engineering with a repeatable deployment. Third, leave local teams able to run and extend their AI systems without us. Demonstrated impact (self-reported, 2026): Time and cost. Infrastructure set-up falls from an estimated 3–9 months and $50,000–$100,000+ of specialist engineering to under 15 minutes and $799 a month. Adoption. Three paying Marketplace subscribers, $2,397 in monthly recurring revenue and zero churn since January 2026, all acquired at $0 direct acquisition cost. Public sector. One sovereign government deployment. Products built on the platform. PromoGoat has 150+ small-business beta users, who have created 3,000+ campaign plans. Skills. Two executive AI programmes delivered, one HRDA-approved, and five more in development. 67 people trained to date. Jobs. 11 people in engineering and business development: 4 employees and 8 contracted specialists. Expected impact by end 2027: 50 organisations running AI in production on AI, Can!; 150+ people trained to operate it; deployment in at least one new country through a development or advisory partner.
Key technologies: AI. Large language models and AI agents, run on Azure AI Foundry inside the customer’s own tenant. Model Context Protocol (MCP). An open standard connecting agents to tools and data through one governed runtime. Infrastructure as code. [Tool: Bicep, Terraform or ARM], packaged as an Azure Managed Application and deployed from the Azure Marketplace. Zero Trust architecture. Hub-and-spoke virtual networks, Azure Firewall, API Management, private endpoints and identity-based access controls. Governance layer. Version-controlled AI behaviour across development, testing and production. A natural-language interface for compliance evidence, built on Microsoft Copilot Studio, is in development. TideMRV, built on the platform, also processes satellite Earth-observation data. No IoT, blockchain or robotics.
Unique Characteristics: 1. Production AI as a subscription. A secure environment that normally takes months of engineering deploys in under 15 minutes, for $799 a month. 2. Sovereign by design. Everything runs in the customer’s own tenant and region. No data leaves it. 3. Governance enforced from installation. Security and governance controls are part of the template, so a project starts governed rather than being audited into compliance at the end. 4. Built from real deployments. The platform’s patterns come from five live systems, including two sovereign government deployments. Three patentable innovations have been identified, and patent filing is planned. 5. Open agent standard. An MCP-native runtime lets agents and tools from different providers work inside one secured boundary. 6. Procurement without friction. Customers buy through the Azure Marketplace, including private offers, and the spend counts toward their existing Azure commitments. All three current subscribers came at $0 direct acquisition cost. 7. A delivery model that compounds. We engineer, ship each proven pattern into the platform, then train the customer’s team. Partners bring clients and domain expertise. Accredited training lets eligible companies in Cyprus have the skills side publicly co-funded.
Sustainable Change: AI, Can! turns secure, governed AI from a bespoke engineering project into a template anyone can deploy. That changes three things beyond any single deployment. Replication across countries. A solution proven in one country can be redeployed in another country’s Azure region, under its own data rules, in weeks. The Embassy platform already serves three countries from one deployment. CySKILLS-AI shows a national pattern any government with education and labour-market data could run. Microsoft co-sell is in activation in Poland and Malaysia, which gives a route into Central Europe and Asia and the Pacific without building a local sales team. A higher baseline for mid-sized industry. Mid-sized manufacturers and suppliers in regulated supply chains get the same security and governance controls that large enterprises build with platform teams. That lowers the cost of meeting NIS2 and the EU AI Act, and lets smaller firms supply regulated customers. Lasting local capability. Every deployment comes with training, so the skills stay in the country. Advisory firms, distributors and research centres can take the platform to their own clients, so adoption grows through partners, not through our headcount.
Funding Sources: AI, Can! was built with Artemis’s own funds and is sold on the Azure Marketplace at $799 a month, so today’s implementations are paid for by customer subscriptions. Microsoft partner cloud credits supported development. Each implementation on the platform was funded differently: - CySKILLS-AI: public R&D funding from the Research and Innovation Foundation of the Republic of Cyprus, under the AI in Government programme (Grant Agreement AI IN GOV’T/0725 – Contracts – Phase A/004). - TideMRV pilot: funded by FIERCE, with further EU and Microsoft Azure grant awards. - PromoGoat was built with founders own funds. Now revenue earning.
Primary thematic focus area: Industrial Digital Infrastructure and Data Ecosystems
Summary: AI, Can! deploys a governed Azure AI environment into a customer's own tenant in under 15 minutes for 799 dollars a month. Its strength is a specified, sovereignty-preserving architecture sold through a commercial channel; its weakness is the absence of a named deployment with a verified result, which holds application at band 3 and geography at band 1.
Thematic focus areas (as submitted): Industrial Digital Infrastructure and Data Ecosystems; Industrial Ecosystem Enablers: Finance, Skills and Market Access

Title: PLASMA lets plant teams run maintenance by talking to ChatGPT or Claude
Subtitle: Built inside a Colombian sugar mill. 77 technicians, 7,400+ work orders and 37,000+ field reports later, maintenance runs on data, voice and AI, with every record sealed on blockchain.
Problem Statement: Most mid-sized plants in Latin America, like sugar mills, still run maintenance on paper, Excel and WhatsApp. Tools like SAP or Maximo are too expensive and complex for them. So they lose hours to unplanned stops, waste spare parts and lubricants, lose know-how when senior technicians leave, and have no data to make decisions.
Solution Overview: PLASMA is a web platform for maintenance and operations. Technicians and supervisors log work orders, inspection routes, daily reports, warehouse transfers and lubricant use from any device. We built our own MCP server, so the plant team can use PLASMA directly from ChatGPT, Claude or even ChatGPT's voice mode. A supervisor walking the plant can just ask out loud "which machines failed most this month?" or "who didn't report today?" and get the answer from live plant data. The AI can also prepare work orders and reports, but it only sees and does what that person's role allows, and nothing is saved until a human approves it. Every record is sealed on Basis Network, our own blockchain, so the maintenance history can't be altered. We built it together with the maintenance team of Ingenio Sancarlos, a sugar mill in Tuluá, Colombia. We sell it as an annual subscription with setup and training included.
Solution Provider(s): Ingenio Sancarlos S.A. (sugar mill and agro-industrial company in Tuluá, Colombia, anchor client and co-development partner), Ruta N Medellín (innovation agency of the District of Medellín, support through the Gen N program)
Implementation location(s): Ingenio Sancarlos, Tuluá, Valle del Cauca, Colombia
Implementation timeline(s): March 2025 to present
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6 to 12 weeks
Desired impact: Keep mid-sized plants running with data and AI, while people stay in charge. Real numbers at Ingenio Sancarlos since March 2025: 77 technicians on the platform, 7,400+ work orders worth about COP 21.7 billion (around USD 5M) in maintenance managed, 37,900+ field reports, 111,000+ technician hours logged and 6,600+ tasks closed. The client verified a 91% gain in operational efficiency and COP 300 million (around USD 75K) in direct savings in the first 6 months. Why it matters for sustainability: Colombian sugar mills are also renewable power plants. They burn cane bagasse to make electricity, and the sector delivers around 180 MW to the national grid. When a mill breaks down, that clean power stops too, and cut cane waiting in the yard starts losing sugar within hours, wasting the land, water and diesel used to grow and haul it. Fewer breakdowns mean less crop waste and steadier renewable energy. Tracking every lubricant application also cuts overuse and hazardous used oil.
Key technologies: Generative AI through our own MCP server, so PLASMA works inside ChatGPT, Claude and ChatGPT voice mode. Blockchain (Basis Network, our own Layer 1), where every record is stored and can't be tampered with. Cloud web app for desktop and mobile.
Unique Characteristics: Nobody on the plant floor has to learn new software. They talk to PLASMA from ChatGPT or Claude, even by voice, in Spanish. It was built inside a working sugar mill, not in a lab, and it's priced and deployed for mid-sized plants in weeks, not months. We designed the AI to be responsible from day one. It only sees and does what each person's role allows, everything it creates is a draft until a human approves it, the plant owns its data, and every action is sealed on our own blockchain so anyone can audit it later.
Sustainable Change: Colombia's sugar mills all share this problem, and so do palm oil, coffee, food processing and utility subsidiaries across Latin America. A single mill already runs about 4,500 work orders and 24,000 field reports a year through PLASMA, so the sugar sector alone means tens of thousands of maintenance decisions a year that AI can make faster and with less waste. Each new plant adds data that moves us toward predictive maintenance and benchmarks between plants. The bigger goal is to bring mid-sized industry, and the rural workers behind it, into the AI economy instead of leaving them out.
Funding Sources: Self-funded with revenue from Base Computing's client work, starting with the original development contract with Ingenio Sancarlos. Non-dilutive support from Ruta N Medellín (Gen N program). Our blockchain layer, Basis Network, received a USD 15,000 grant from Avalanche Build Games. No equity raised.
Testimonials and Endorsements: "Before PLASMA, we ran maintenance on spreadsheets and on the memory of our veteran operators." Jeison Rentería Díaz, Head of Maintenance and Projects, Ingenio Sancarlos (https://plasmaindustrial.com) Recognition: 1st place, Gen N "Next" category, Ruta N Medellín, and Gen N Ambassador 2026 Joven Referente 2026, District of Medellín Top 50 and USD 15K grant, Avalanche Build Games Winners, Área Metropolitana Innovation Award Winners, Blockchain Summit LATAM 2025 (Protección S.A. track) Top 50 nationwide out of 1,300+ companies, Jóvenes Nestlé Colombia 3rd place, AI Hackathon Our founding team has won 20+ hackathons
Primary thematic focus area: Industrial Digital Infrastructure and Data Ecosystems
Summary: PLASMA records work orders, inspection routes, daily reports and lubricant use in a web platform, exposes itself to ChatGPT and Claude through a company-built MCP server, and seals every record on its own blockchain. Ingenio Sancarlos, a Colombian sugar mill that also supplies renewable power to the grid, has run it since March 2025.
Thematic focus areas (as submitted): Industrial AI Models and Intelligent Decision-Making

Title: DIGBA: AI compliance intelligence for sustainable agro-industrial trade
Subtitle: AI that helps West African agro-exporters prove sustainable, compliant supply chains through regulatory intelligence, document verification, geospatial traceability and risk detection.
Problem Statement: West African agro-exporters and cooperatives face growing pressure to prove compliance with international regulations, certification standards and buyer requirements. EUDR requires geolocation data and deforestation-free proof for covered commodities, while Rainforest Alliance, Fairtrade and buyers impose additional sustainability requirements. Yet many SMEs manage evidence across scattered spreadsheets, PDF certificates, producer registries, GIS files and emails, relying on manual checks to identify missing documents, geospatial risks and data inconsistencies. In more than 20 recorded conversations with organizations across Côte d'Ivoire, Ghana, Cameroon and Togo, we heard recurring challenges: last-minute audit preparation, manual forest-map checks, duplicate producer registrations and deliveries exceeding plots' expected yields. These issues can lead to shipment delays, payment disruptions, certification problems and lost contracts. As requirements tighten, smaller businesses risk losing access to premium markets not necessarily because they are non-compliant, but because they struggle to produce reliable, verifiable evidence.
Solution Overview: DIGBA is an AI-powered compliance intelligence platform that helps West African agro-exporters and cooperatives demonstrate compliance with international market requirements and build more transparent, sustainable supply chains. Its three core capabilities (supported by AI) are: 1. Regulatory compliance intelligence: Converts requirements from EUDR, Rainforest Alliance, Fairtrade and relevant buyer requirements into actionable compliance checks. 2. Traceability and production plausibility: Cross-checks producer registries, plot data and delivery records to flag anomalies, including duplicate registrations, deliveries exceeding expected yields and potential forest overlap. 3. AI-assisted document and risk analysis: Processes certificates, audit reports, spreadsheets, images and geospatial files to identify missing documents, inconsistencies, expired certificates and potential compliance risks. The DIGBA Compliance Co-Pilot/AI organizes the available evidence, evaluates it against applicable requirements, and presents findings by requirement, with a compliance readiness score and prioritized corrective actions. It supports internal compliance preparation and pre-audit reviews; it does not replace independent certification or regulatory authorities. Methodologies and technologies DIGBA combines a rule-based verification engine, AI-assisted document analysis and regulatory intelligence. Human-validated rules provide consistent checks, while large language models help interpret documents and identify additional potential risks for review. Geospatial analysis supports plot-level traceability and deforestation-related checks. A regulatory intelligence workflow monitors official sources, identifies potential regulatory changes and prepares candidate rules for human validation before deployment. This approach combines automation with human oversight to improve reliability and keep compliance checks current. Client data is not used to train models. Partnerships and collaboration model DIGBA follows an exporter-first model, working with exporters and cooperatives to improve compliance across their supply chains. Compliance consultants and audit firms can use the platform to support clients' audit preparation and identify corrective actions earlier. DIGBA is discussing collaboration with an audit firm in Côte d'Ivoire and benefits from industry advice from the cocoa sector. An annual software licence provides a scalable B2B model designed to make compliance intelligence more accessible to small and medium-sized agricultural businesses.
Solution Provider(s): MEST Africa (Meltwater Entrepreneurial School of Technology), Accra, Ghana, pan-African technology entrepreneurship school and incubator, sector: technology and venture support (DIGBA is in its AI Startup Program incubation, Class of 2026), Youssouf Diaby, industry advisor, senior cocoa supply-chain and sustainability professional in West Africa, sector: cocoa and agro-export (signed advisory agreement, September 2026), NVIDIA Inception, AWS Activate and Claude for Startups (Anthropic), technology startup programs, sector: AI and cloud computing (program support and credits)
Implementation location(s): Côte d'Ivoire (Abidjan) and Ghana (Accra). The MVP has been demonstrated to exporters, a cooperative, certification and sustainability staff and a compliance consultant in Côte d'Ivoire (June-August 2026), and has been used by one compliance consultant since September 2026. No paid deployment yet.
Implementation timeline(s): Customer discovery and prototype: March-August 2026. MVP (V1) in production and V2 in testing with users: since September 2026, ongoing.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: About 4-6 weeks in a new country for the same commodities and standards (EUDR, Rainforest Alliance, Fairtrade), mainly to encode national rules, adapt document templates and onboard a local partner; longer where a national regulator must approve tools first.
Desired impact: Objectives: (1) Help West African agro-exporters and cooperatives maintain access to international markets by making regulatory compliance and supply-chain evidence easier to verify continuously. (2) Reduce the time and cost of compliance and audit preparation. (3) Detect documentation gaps, traceability inconsistencies, production anomalies and potential deforestation risks before they lead to shipment disruptions or certification problems. Expected impact and measurement: DIGBA is at MVP stage, and its impact has not yet been quantified. During pilots, we will measure compliance assessment time (target: under 5 minutes per company), agreement between automated findings and expert review (target: at least 85%), non-conformities identified and corrected before audits, producer and delivery anomalies flagged, and the share of relevant plots checked against the applicable forest baseline. Expected longer-term outcomes include fewer preventable compliance-related shipment disruptions, lower audit-preparation costs, improved traceability across agricultural supply chains and more inclusive access to regulated markets for SMEs and cooperatives. Systematic geospatial checks can also help identify potential deforestation risks earlier and support more responsible sourcing.
Key technologies: Large language models (Claude models through AWS Bedrock) for document understanding, data extraction and risk reasoning; a deterministic rule engine with human-validated compliance rules; geospatial analysis of farm GPS points and polygons against the EU JRC Global Forest Cover 2020 map; an AI-assisted regulatory monitoring pipeline with human validation; secure cloud hosting on AWS.
Unique Characteristics: DIGBA differentiates itself through: - Requirement-level evidence verification: Rather than simply collecting traceability data, DIGBA checks whether available evidence satisfies each applicable requirement and cross-checks producer registers, deliveries, documents and plot data to flag inconsistencies and potential fraud. - Transparent, actionable AI: DIGBA combines validated regulatory rules with AI-assisted risk detection, distinguishes between their findings and provides prioritized corrective actions. It supports audit readiness without claiming to replace independent certification. - Designed to integrate with existing workflows: Rather than replacing the tools exporters and cooperatives already use, DIGBA aims to connect with their existing systems and fragmented data sources. Its Compliance Co-Pilot brings together information from spreadsheets, document repositories, producer registries and geospatial tools to perform cross-source compliance checks, minimizing workflow disruption and reducing the need for duplicate data entry. - Designed for West African supply chains: The platform accommodates French and English workflows, commonly used document formats and cooperative records, bringing national requirements together with international regulations and certification standards.
Sustainable Change: As EUDR, due-diligence and sustainability requirements increasingly determine market access, DIGBA can help shift agricultural supply chains from reactive audits to continuous, evidence-based compliance. Each validated regulatory rule can be reused across exporters, reducing the cost of demonstrating compliance as adoption grows. Starting with cocoa, coffee and cashew in Côte d'Ivoire, DIGBA can scale across commodities, West African markets and other export sectors, working with existing tools rather than replacing them. By connecting exporters, cooperatives, consultants and auditors around more structured, comparable evidence, DIGBA can help identify compliance gaps and sourcing risks earlier. Ultimately, it aims to help small producers and exporters remain competitive in global value chains as requirements tighten, rather than being excluded because they lack the resources of larger companies.

Problem Statement: Small-scale farmers in North-Eastern Nigeria are confronted with significant productivity challenges owing to a combination of recurring droughts, soil degradation, and weather-related shocks. Existing agricultural extension services do not integrate data in a timely manner, and local farmers are not able to access the necessary information required to understand precisely when to plant crops or how to mitigate agricultural stress by using climate-resilient crops. As a result, the food supply chain suffers from instability and exclusion.

The platform employs machine learning for processing this data and generating planting schedules and input optimization models for smallholder farmers. Quantified Impact: Deployed across pilot networks in Gombe State, mobilizing over 1,000 youth and smallholder farmers, optimizing input efficiency by up to 25%, and establishing scalable frameworks for drought-resilient sorghum cultivation in conflict-affected terrain.

Title: Credit for digital tree, digital tree for credit access
Subtitle: e-Busytree helps smallholder farm forestry farmers turn trees into verifiable, bankable digital assets using AI mobile app that tracks and records live tree planting, live tree growth, monitor tree survival, track and record live carbon sequestration and tree value, allowing access to credit and carbon credit market for smallholder farmers
Problem Statement:
Smallholder farmers in Uganda face three interconnected barriers that undermine sustainable tree growing, environmental restoration, and climate-resilient livelihoods. First, over 40% of planted trees die within the first 12 months, largely due to inadequate financing for quality seedlings, labour, water-retention inputs, technical knowledge, and post-planting management. This results in wasted investments, failed tree-growing initiatives, and continued environmental degradation.

Second, approximately 90% of smallholder farmers lack access to financing for tree growing. Traditional financial institutions consider tree-growing investments risky because trees take years to mature, generate returns, and are rarely recognised as acceptable collateral. Consequently, farmers cannot afford the upfront costs required to establish and maintain productive trees.

Third, approximately 90% of smallholder farmers lack access to carbon credit markets, despite their significant potential to contribute to carbon sequestration through agroforestry and farm forestry. Limited access to carbon measurement, verification, certification, market information, and aggregation systems prevents farmers from monetising the environmental value of their trees.

These challenges reinforce one another: inadequate financing contributes to tree mortality, while the absence of digital monitoring, reliable tree valuation, and accessible carbon markets limits the financial incentives for farmers to invest in long-term tree growing.

e-Busytree seeks to break this cycle by integrating tree-growing finance, digital tree tracking, AI-powered monitoring and valuation, and carbon market access into one scalable solution. Our goal is to transform trees into surviving, measurable, and financeable assets while improving smallholder farmers' livelihoods and restoring the environment.
Solution Overview:
e-Busytree offers an integrated, technology-driven solution built around "Credit for Digital Tree and Digital Tree for Credit Access." The model combines affordable financing, tree-growing services, digital monitoring, AI, and carbon market linkages to address high tree mortality, limited access to finance, and smallholder farmers' exclusion from carbon markets.

Through the AI Tree App, farmers are registered, their farms mapped, and every planted tree digitally recorded and geotagged. Farmers access seedlings, labour, organic water-retention inputs, and technical knowledge on credit, with repayments structured around agreed tree-growing cycles. The platform monitors tree growth, health, and survival using farmer reporting, field inspections, GPS, GIS, satellite imagery, and Earth Observation technologies.

AI and farm-level data supports tree growth analysis, carbon sequestration estimation, and tree valuation, creating verifiable digital tree records that can support farmer credit assessment and future carbon market participation.

We use participatory farmer engagement, climate-smart agroforestry, results-based financing, digital monitoring, reporting and verification (MRV), GPS/GIS mapping, Artificial Intelligence, remote sensing, Copernicus Sentinel satellite data, and cloud-based data management.

We collaborate with farmer organizations, tree nurseries, financial institutions, government agencies, technology developers, GIS and research institutions, carbon project developers, buyers, and development partners. These partnerships support service delivery, financing, technology development, scientific validation, and market access.

e-Busytree aims to create a scalable digital ecosystem connecting farmers, trees, finance, technology, and carbon markets, making tree growing a sustainable economic opportunity while restoring ecosystems and improving rural livelihoods.
Solution Provider(s): African Center for Digital Transformation promotes digital transformation in Africa
Implementation location(s): Uganda
Duration to pilot in a new geography: two months
Desired impact:
The overall objective of e-Busytree is to transform smallholder tree growing into a sustainable, financeable, and digitally verifiable economic activity through its "Credit for Digital Tree and Digital Tree for Credit Access" model.

The specific objectives includes;

1. Reduce tree mortality: Improve tree survival beyond the current identified 60% baseline through access to quality seedlings, appropriate planting practices, maintenance inputs, technical support, and continuous digital monitoring.

2. Improve access to finance: Enable smallholder farmers to access affordable credit for tree planting and management, using digitally recorded and growing trees as potential economic assets to support credit assessment.

3. Expand carbon market access: Digitally register, monitor, and aggregate smallholder trees to support carbon sequestration estimation, carbon project development, and farmers' participation in carbon markets.

4. Develop digital tree assets: Use the AI Tree App, GPS, GIS, AI, and Earth Observation technologies to track tree locations, growth, survival, estimated carbon sequestration, and economic value.

5. Improve rural livelihoods and climate resilience: Promote productive agroforestry, diversify farmers' income sources, restore degraded landscapes, and strengthen climate-resilient farming systems.

e-Busytree has already worked with 26 smallholder farmers, achieving 99% tree survival and 90% loan repayment in its initial implementation. A team commission incentive model has also increased client acquisition and the number of trees planted by over 50%.

Building on these results, our flagship Tree Crop Forest Village initiative targets 250,000 tree crops across 625 acres in northern Uganda villages, with an estimated investment of USD 250,000.

Expected short and long term impacts include;
- 250,000 tree crops planted, creating productive and environmentally beneficial farming landscapes.
- Improved tree survival, targeting at least 90% survival through continuous monitoring and management.
- Increased financial inclusion, enabling more smallholder farmers to access tree-growing credit.
- Carbon sequestration: Increased carbon storage through growing trees, with quantities established through appropriate field measurements and verified carbon accounting methodologies.
- Improved livelihoods: Increased opportunities for income generation through productive tree crops, improved farm productivity, and potential carbon revenues.
- Employment creation: Opportunities for youth and community members in nurseries, tree planting, maintenance, digital monitoring, and agroforestry services.
- Environmental restoration: Improved tree cover, biodiversity, soil protection, and climate resilience across participating farming communities.
Key technologies:
e-Busytree integrates digital technologies, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Geographic Information Systems (GIS), and Earth Observation (EO) to transform tree growing into a measurable, traceable, and financeable activity.

1. Artificial Intelligence (AI): Used to analyse farm and tree data, monitor growth patterns, predict tree survival risks, estimate tree value, and support farmer credit assessment.

2. Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and GPS: Used to map farmers' land, geotag individual trees or tree plots, record planting locations, and track the geographical distribution of tree-growing activities.

3. Earth Observation and Remote Sensing: Satellite data, particularly from the Copernicus Sentinel programme, will support vegetation monitoring, land-use change detection, assessment of tree-growing areas, and estimation of biomass and carbon sequestration.

4. Mobile and Cloud Computing: The AI Tree App will provide a digital platform for farmer registration, tree records, field data collection, real-time reporting, notifications, and secure data management.

5. Data Analytics and Predictive Modelling: Integrates tree species, age, growth, survival, farm characteristics, and satellite observations to estimate carbon capture, tree development, and potential economic value.

6. Digital Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV): Combines geotagged records, field observations, and satellite imagery to provide traceability and evidence of tree planting, growth, survival, and environmental impact.

These technologies work together to create a digital ecosystem connecting farmers, trees, financial institutions, and carbon markets. Our focus is to make every tree digitally traceable, environmentally measurable, and potentially valuable as a financial asset.
The AI application is already in google play store but the advanced form as describe above is still under development and upgrades will continues as the work progress
Unique Characteristics:
e-Busytree's innovation lies in transforming tree growing from a traditional environmental activity into a digitally verifiable, financeable, and income-generating economic asset. Our distinctive model, "Credit for Digital Tree and Digital Tree for Credit Access," integrates climate action, agricultural finance, AI, and carbon market opportunities into one solution.

1. Trees as digital financial assets: Unlike conventional tree-planting initiatives, we digitally register, geotag, and track individual trees or tree plots, creating traceable records that can support tree valuation, farmer credit assessment, and potential use of trees as collateral, subject to financial agreements.

2. Pay-as-trees-grow financing: We provide seedlings, labour, organic water-retention inputs, and technical support on credit, with repayment structured around agreed tree-growing cycles. This reduces upfront financial barriers and creates a revolving financing model.

3. AI-powered tree monitoring and valuation: Our AI Tree App integrates farm data, GPS/GIS, satellite imagery, and Earth Observation to monitor tree growth and survival, estimate carbon sequestration, and assess the potential economic value of trees.

4. Smallholder carbon market aggregation: We digitally aggregate trees belonging to individual farmers and farmer groups, creating opportunities to develop larger carbon projects and reduce barriers to accessing carbon markets.

5. Integrated service delivery: We connect farmers with nurseries, farm-forestry service providers, financial institutions, and carbon market actors through a coordinated digital ecosystem.

6. Performance-driven environmental financing: Our model links financing with tree establishment, survival, growth, and management, encouraging long-term tree protection rather than simply counting seedlings distributed.

By combining innovative financing, digital traceability, AI, and partnerships, we aim to make tree growing commercially attractive, environmentally sustainable, and scalable across Uganda and Africa.
Sustainable Change:
e-Busytree has the potential to transform how tree growing is financed, managed, valued, and rewarded across Uganda and Africa. By combining digital technology, AI, innovative financing, and carbon market linkages, we aim to shift tree growing from short-term planting campaigns to sustainable, commercially viable, and measurable investment systems.

Our "Credit for Digital Tree and Digital Tree for Credit Access" model can influence the financial sector by demonstrating how digitally registered and monitored trees can become measurable productive assets that support smallholder farmers' access to finance. This could encourage banks, microfinance institutions, and impact investors to develop new financial products for agroforestry and climate-smart agriculture.

The AI Tree App will create a scalable digital infrastructure connecting farmers, tree nurseries, financial institutions, service providers, and carbon market actors. Aggregating smallholder trees will also create opportunities for collective participation in carbon markets, allowing farmers previously excluded from these markets to benefit from environmental finance.

Our flagship initiative targeting 250,000 tree crops across 625 acres in northern Uganda will provide a practical model for replication. Lessons, data, and results will inform expansion to other districts, farmer cooperatives, and eventually other African countries.

Beyond direct beneficiaries, the solution can stimulate rural employment in nurseries, tree planting, maintenance, digital monitoring, and agroforestry services. Increased tree cover can also contribute to biodiversity conservation, soil protection, carbon sequestration, and climate resilience.

e-Busytree seeks to create a systemic shift where trees are recognized not only as environmental resources but also as measurable economic assets, farmers become active participants in climate finance, and environmental restoration becomes a sustainable engine of rural economic development

Title: Earthwise SmartBrood AI: Intelligent Poultry Production Infrastructure
Subtitle: SmartBrood embeds computer vision and predictive AI into solar powered poultry infrastructure to detect chick health risks, optimize brooding and refrigeration, and reduce production losses.
Problem Statement: Africa's poultry industry continues to expand day old chick production, but the traditional model of selling fragile chicks directly to smallholder farmers fails to deliver profitable and sustainable poultry businesses. In Rwanda alone, annual demand reached 25 million day old chicks in 2025, against domestic production capacity of 18 million. Yet many farmers receiving improved commercial breeds such as Sasso lack the infrastructure and technical capacity to raise them successfully, relying on charcoal heating, inadequate ventilation and manual disease detection during the critical first 14 days. Poor temperature control, inadequate ventilation and delayed detection of disease outbreaks drive chick mortality above 35% in poorly managed systems, resulting in 3,500 birds lost for every 10,000 chicks. Brooding 20,000 chicks in small batches consumes approximately 30 tonnes of charcoal, further increasing production costs. High mortality and disease outbreaks wipe out farmers' investments in chicks and feed, making repeated production cycles financially unsustainable while undermining commercial hatcheries' customer retention and market growth. Even when farmers successfully raise their chickens to maturity, inadequate refrigeration exposes up to 40% of poultry production to postharvest losses, reducing profits for farmers, processors and retailers. The industry continues investing in producing and distributing more day old chicks while farmers struggle to keep them alive, control disease outbreaks and recover production costs. Without reliable brooding, continuous health monitoring and cold storage, increasing chick production does not translate into more market-ready chickens or profitable poultry businesses.
Solution Overview: Earthwise is transforming Africa's poultry industry through SmartBrood, our AI-powered industrial poultry infrastructure that integrates commercial hatching, intelligent brooding, smallholder production and refrigerated distribution. Instead of distributing fragile day old chicks directly to farmers, we centralize the critical first 14 days in solar hybrid facilities, where computer vision continuously assesses chick health and behaviour to detect early signs of disease, temperature stress and abnormal development. Predictive AI combines these observations with temperature, humidity and ventilation data to optimize brooding conditions, reduce mortality and improve energy efficiency without charcoal-dependent heating. Farmers digitally order healthy, vaccinated 14-day-old starter birds, each linked to a traceable production record containing its origin, health assessments and vaccination history. Through our ContractGrow platform, we monitor flock growth, feed consumption and mortality, using predictive AI to identify production risks, forecast harvest dates and align production with market demand. We also provide feed financing and guaranteed offtake, enabling farmers to raise poultry profitably without investing in expensive brooding infrastructure. At maturity, Earthwise purchases qualifying birds from participating farmers, currently offtaking 30 tons of poultry weekly, and processes, preserves and distributes the meat through our decentralized solar-hybrid cold hubs. AI-powered temperature monitoring, energy optimization and demand forecasting connect refrigeration and distribution with farmer production, reducing spoilage, operating costs and market uncertainty. Title: AXION: On-Device AI Wearables for Industrial Workflows
Subtitle: A wearable platform bringing local AI, task verification and worker communication to logistics and manufacturing, with a roadmap to reduce process errors and material waste.
Problem Statement: Frontline workers in warehouses and factories often have to switch between physical tasks, handheld terminals, paper instructions and manual checks. This creates interruptions, duplicate entries and avoidable picking, assembly and returns-processing errors. New employees need accessible task guidance, while managers need reliable information linking the physical task to enterprise records. In developing and middle-income economies, uneven connectivity and limited integration resources can make cloud-dependent tools harder to adopt. AXION addresses this gap at the point of work, with selected checks performed on the wearable and worker communication integrated into the same platform. The sustainability opportunity is to prevent errors, rework and unnecessary material use; these environmental benefits still require measurement.
Solution Overview: AXION is an industrial wearable platform developed by Thread In Motion (TIM). It combines wearable hardware, embedded software, barcode capture, camera-based text recognition, motion sensing and worker-to-worker push-to-talk. Management confirms that basic OCR and motion detection operated on the device in the v5 prototype tested with ten customers after June 2026. Series production has not started. The approach links information captured at the point of work to a defined industrial task and worker feedback, with integration into customer enterprise workflows. Running selected processing locally reduces dependence on a continuous cloud round trip for those functions; enterprise synchronisation and communication still require suitable connectivity. The next development stage will extend the baseline towards visual quality checks, voice-based task guidance and onboarding, inertial-sensor emergency notifications, and exploratory 3D-camera capture for robot-training data. These advanced capabilities are planned rather than completed. TIM proposes joint pilots with industrial operators and local integration partners, using agreed task baselines, configuration records and measurements of errors, completion time and reliability before wider deployment.
Solution Provider(s): Lead developer and solution provider: Thread In Motion (TIM), industrial wearable hardware and software. Management-reported customer trial references include Netlog Logistics (logistics), Şok Market (retail), Renault (automotive manufacturing), AISIN (automotive components) and DEEMAH (food manufacturing/returns processes). These are industry trial references, not confirmed consortium partners for this UNIDO call. Local pilot hosts and integration partners for new geographies would be agreed during deployment planning.
Implementation location(s): TIM is based in Istanbul, Türkiye. Management reports customer trials in logistics, retail and manufacturing environments, including Netlog Logistics, Şok Market, Renault, AISIN and DEEMAH. Exact country/city and site mapping for the individual trials is being consolidated.
Implementation timeline(s): AXION v5 customer trials took place after June 2026, according to management. Individual trial start and end dates are being consolidated. Series production has not started.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Indicative planning estimate: 8–12 weeks to configure and launch a limited pilot of the existing v5 baseline once a host site, devices and integration requirements are agreed. This is a proposed deployment estimate, subject to local requirements and hardware availability, not a committed delivery date. The advanced AI functions require a separate development and validation programme.
Desired impact: AXION aims to help factory and warehouse workers complete physical tasks with fewer interruptions, errors and repeated entries. Initial applications are barcode-led picking, returns verification and task confirmation. TIM reports v5 trials with ten customer organisations after June 2026; series production has not started. Company-reported trial results include 45% higher picking productivity at Netlog Logistics, 28% operational-efficiency improvement at Şok Market, 18% improvement in assembly speed at Renault and 35% efficiency improvement in parts-sequencing at AISIN. These are management-reported outcomes: sample sizes, baseline definitions and measurement records are being consolidated and the figures have not been independently verified. The next phase will develop voice-guided onboarding, visual quality checks, motion-based emergency notifications and exploratory 3D capture for robot training. For users in Türkiye and other developing and middle-income economies, intended benefits include easier onboarding, operational reliability and less avoidable rework and material waste. Future pilots will compare defined workflows with baseline performance and measure operational and material outcomes. No quantified carbon saving has yet been established.
Key technologies: AXION combines a modular wearable computer with barcode capture, a camera, audio communication and motion sensing. Its existing v5 baseline comprises barcode reading, worker-to-worker push-to-talk, wearable ergonomics, basic optical character recognition (OCR) and basic motion detection. Management confirms that OCR and motion detection ran on the device in reported customer trials. TIM develops the electronics, mechanical design, device software and workflow integration in-house; available application builds also include third-party Google ML Kit OCR libraries and models. The proposed architecture associates captured information with an expected item and task, applies defined checks, gives worker feedback and transfers agreed transaction results to enterprise systems. Future work will extend this baseline to voice guidance, visual quality control, IMU-based emergency-event classification and exploratory 3D capture. Integration will be evaluated for recognition quality, response time, battery use, heat and workflow correctness.
Unique Characteristics: AXION brings local recognition, task context and worker communication together in a wearable platform. Its intended differentiation is to keep task capture and feedback at the point of physical work, reducing repeated interactions with separate terminals. The architecture is designed to associate barcode, text and image information with an expected task, apply workflow rules and route uncertain or conflicting results for human review. TIM controls the integration of electronics, mechanical design, device software and enterprise workflows, combining its own engineering with standard components and third-party recognition libraries. Selected processing runs locally, while enterprise synchronisation and communication use connectivity when needed. The key engineering challenge is to combine these functions within wearable limits for energy, heat, reliability and ergonomics. Existing v5 trials provide the practical baseline. Advanced visual checks, AI voice guidance, emergency-event recognition and robot-training capture remain development objectives whose value will be tested through task-specific comparisons.
Sustainable Change: AXION proposes a shift from separate scanning, checking and later data entry towards feedback and traceability within the worker’s physical task. If validated and commercially adopted, this approach could help industrial sites improve how operational knowledge is transferred, exceptions are handled and quality issues are identified. In developing and middle-income economies, we aim to support modernisation of existing factories and warehouses through defined workflows and enterprise-system integration. Planned voice guidance could support onboarding, while planned visual checks could identify errors earlier and reduce rework and avoidable material waste. Workers would remain involved in reviewing uncertain results. Wider adoption will depend on measurable value, affordability, integration effort, training and ongoing support. We will evaluate operational and material outcomes alongside device energy use. Replication would use agreed pilot procedures, local integration support and lessons from each site, with adaptation to local workflows and worker needs.
Funding Sources: AXION development has been financed through TIM’s company resources. Related earlier industrial-wearable R&D received TÜBİTAK support: TEYDEB 1501 project 3231260, an AI-based warehouse orchestrator using wearable technology (contractual support period January 2024–June 2025), and TEYDEB 1507 project 7220218, an industrial quality-control system using wearable technology (support period July 2022–December 2023). These are prior R&D projects, rather than confirmed funding for the proposed new-geography AXION pilot.
Primary thematic focus area: Industrial AI Models and Intelligent Decision-Making
Summary: Thread In Motion has a wearable for warehouse and factory work that reads barcodes and text locally and keeps the worker in voice contact, trialled with five named industrial customers in Türkiye. It is a real product with real trials; the quantified gains are the applicant's own and the advanced capabilities are planned.

Title: Gani Labs: AI That Knows Your Business, Owned by You
Subtitle: Custom AI agents built on your own documents, systems and live data, with every answer traced to its source, deployed in your environment and owned by you.
Problem Statement: Organisations run on knowledge they cannot easily use. Contracts, regulations, engineering records, reports and operational data sit in separate systems, change constantly, and must be traced back to their source, while much of the know-how lives in a few experienced people. Finding answers is slow, quality depends on who is available, and knowledge is lost when people leave. Off-the-shelf AI tools do not solve this. They do not know the organisation’s own data or rules, cannot reliably show where an answer came from, and often send sensitive information to outside providers. Building a proper system in-house takes scarce AI talent and long projects that often stall at the pilot stage, leaving organisations with AI budgets but no lasting capability.
Solution Overview: How the solution works Gani Labs builds custom AI systems on each client’s own knowledge. We start with discovery, mapping the decisions the client needs to make and the information behind them. We then ingest the client’s documents, systems and live data into a single knowledge graph that records how things relate: a clause to the law it depends on, a requirement to its design and test records, a fault to its past fixes. On top of the graph, we build AI agents for specific tasks such as contract review, compliance checks, requirements tracing and design review. The agents do the work and stop at approval points where a person decides. Every answer shows the source it came from, so users can check it before acting. The system is deployed in the client’s own cloud or on premise, connected to tools people already use such as Microsoft Teams and Outlook, and handed over as a system the client owns. Methodologies and technologies Knowledge graph and ontology modelling of each client’s domain, so the system understands its terms, records and relationships. GARUT (Graph-Inspired Agentic Retrieval with Unified Traversal), our own retrieval method, which follows links across sources and cites them in every answer. Agentic workflows orchestrated with LangGraph, with human approval gates and a full log of every agent action. A proprietary legal and regulatory knowledge base covering more than 100 jurisdictions. Model-agnostic architecture, running on the foundation models the client approves, including open-weight models hosted on site. Client data is never used to train models. Proven in production: the same engine powers Gani.AI, our own platform with close to 5,000 users. Gani is ISO 27001 certified. Partnerships and collaboration models We work with clients in three ways: Pilot: a fixed-fee pilot on one use case, with success criteria agreed up front. Custom build: a fixed-fee project that the client owns, with ongoing support. Partnership: we act as the AI development partner for companies that serve their own customers, such as consulting firms, technology providers and platforms. We are part of AWS Startups and of LIFT, the Singapore Ministry of Law’s legal technology programme run with PwC NewLaw, and we are backed by Insignia Ventures.
Solution Provider(s): Amazon Web Services (AWS Startups programme): global cloud and AI infrastructure provider, supporting us with cloud infrastructure, Amazon Bedrock and technical guidance, sector: cloud computing and AI infrastructure, Ministry of Law, Singapore (LIFT, the Legal Innovation and Future-Readiness Transformation programme): Singapore government ministry driving legal technology adoption across the legal sector, sector: government and legal services, PwC Singapore (PwC NewLaw): professional services firm and the appointed legal technology consultant for LIFT, sector: professional services and legal technology consulting, Insignia Ventures Partners: Southeast Asian venture capital firm and our institutional investor, sector: venture capital and technology investment
Implementation location(s): Indonesia (Jakarta), Singapore, Japan (Tokyo), India. Platform users in other Southeast Asian countries as well.
Implementation timeline(s): Gani.AI platform: December 2024 to present (ongoing). Gani Labs custom builds: 2026 to present (ongoing), across Singapore, India, Indonesia and Japan.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: About 3 to 4 months in total. Setup takes around 4 weeks, covering security review, environment and data access, and loading any local laws or standards. A pilot with live users then runs for about 8 to 12 weeks. The timing depends mainly on how quickly the client provides data access and completes its security review, and on how much local regulatory content needs adding for the new country.
Desired impact: Main objectives Make the knowledge organisations already hold usable, by bringing documents, systems and live data into one knowledge graph that people can query and trace. Help organisations adopt AI safely, with systems that run in their own environment, keep their data under their control, and show the source behind every answer. Close knowledge gaps, so that access to information and expertise, not company size or seniority, decides who can compete and decide well. Demonstrated impact Close to 5,000 users of our engine across Southeast Asia, Japan and India. More than 100 legal jurisdictions covered in our regulatory knowledge base, giving organisations access to legal and compliance knowledge that would otherwise require expensive specialist advice. 30 skilled jobs created in our in-house team of AI engineers and software developers. Custom systems delivered or in delivery for clients in Singapore, India and Japan, in legal services, business operations and public procurement. Expected impact Faster, better-informed decisions: less time spent searching for and tracing records, and fewer errors from outdated or missing information. Knowledge kept inside organisations when experienced staff retire or leave, which matters especially for ageing workforces in manufacturing. Wider AI adoption among organisations that cannot use off-the-shelf tools because of data security and sovereignty concerns, including the public sector and regulated industries.
Key technologies: Artificial intelligence, including large language models. The system is model-agnostic. It runs on whichever foundation models the client approves, including open-weight models hosted on site, and never uses client data to train them. AI agents. Agentic workflows are orchestrated with LangGraph, so agents can carry out multi-step tasks such as review, compliance checks and requirements tracing. Human approval gates and a full audit log cover every agent action. Knowledge graphs and ontology modelling. Each client’s domain is modelled as a graph of entities and relationships, so the system understands how records, rules and assets connect. Graph-based retrieval (GARUT). Our own retrieval method (Graph-Inspired Agentic Retrieval with Unified Traversal) follows links across sources and cites the source of every answer. It builds on retrieval-augmented generation (RAG and GraphRAG). Data ingestion and document intelligence. We process structured and unstructured data, including legacy documents, contracts, specifications, records and live system data, in multiple languages. Proprietary knowledge base. Our legal and regulatory knowledge covers more than 100 jurisdictions. Secure cloud and on-premise deployment. We build on AWS infrastructure, including Amazon Bedrock, or deploy fully within the client’s own environment. Gani is ISO 27001 certified.
Unique Characteristics: Technology: traceable answers, not just fluent ones. Our graph-based retrieval method (GARUT) links every answer to the source clause, record or regulation it came from. Generic AI tools cannot reliably do this. The knowledge graph also captures how information connects, so the system can trace a requirement to its design, or a new regulation to every contract and policy it affects. Delivery approach: a custom system built on a proven engine. Off-the-shelf tools are generic, and consultancies build from scratch. We do neither. Our engine already runs in production behind Gani.AI, used by close to 5,000 people. Clients get a system modelled on their own domain without the cost and risk of a project that starts from zero. Business model: the client owns the system. Instead of renting seats on a vendor’s cloud, clients pay fixed fees for a pilot and a build, and own the result. The system runs in their environment, works with any foundation model, and is never trained on their data. That means no lock-in to a vendor or model, and it suits government and regulated industries that cannot send data outside their walls. Built on law, the hardest test. We started with legal work because it demands precision, sources and professional language. Systems built to that standard carry the same discipline into industry, finance and government. Partnership model: we build for those who serve others. Beyond direct clients, we act as the AI development partner for companies that serve their own customers, such as procurement platforms and consulting firms. This extends our reach without building a large sales force.
Sustainable Change: One engine, many sectors. The underlying problem is the same everywhere: records that change, live in silos and must be traced. That holds for government, legal and compliance, financial services, healthcare, energy, and manufacturing and supply chains. Because we model each new domain on the same engine, every deployment makes the next one faster and cheaper. A solution proven in one sector or country can be replicated in others without rebuilding it. Knowledge that stays and compounds. When an organisation captures its records and its experts’ know-how in a knowledge graph, that knowledge outlasts any individual employee. This matters most where workforces are ageing and experienced people are retiring, as in Japanese manufacturing. Each resolved case and new document feeds back into the system, so it keeps improving after deployment. Making safe AI adoption possible for those left out. Many public bodies, regulated industries and smaller firms cannot use off-the-shelf AI because of data security and sovereignty rules. A system that runs in their own environment, uses any approved model and shows the source of every answer gives them a path to adopt AI. That helps narrow the gap between the organisations already benefiting from AI and those that are not. Scale through partners, not just direct sales. By acting as the AI development partner for platforms, consulting firms and service providers, we let them bring the same capability to their own customers. That multiplies reach across markets we could not serve directly. Stronger regulatory capacity. Our regulatory knowledge base covers more than 100 jurisdictions, and our systems map new laws to the contracts and policies they affect. This can help organisations, and the governments that regulate them, apply rules more consistently. That supports more transparent and predictable business environments.
Funding Sources: The solution has been funded through three sources: Venture capital: seed investment from Insignia Ventures Partners, a leading Southeast Asian venture capital firm, which funded development of the core engine. Customer revenue: subscriptions to our Gani.AI platform, and fixed-fee custom builds paid for directly by clients in Singapore, India and Japan. Each implementation so far has been funded by the client, not by grants. Ecosystem support: cloud and technical support through the AWS Startups programme.
