Title: ATIO Knowledge Base: AI-Assisted Discovery for Agrifood Innovation
Subtitle: FAO's global knowledge platform uses AI to structure fragmented innovation information and help agrifood businesses, policymakers and investors find relevant technologies and supporting evidence.
Problem Statement: Agrifood businesses, producer organizations, investors and public agencies need reliable information to identify technologies and innovations suited to their operating conditions. Yet this information is scattered across institutional databases, research publications, project reports and other sources, with inconsistent terminology and uneven coverage of readiness, affordability and adoption requirements. This fragmentation makes it difficult to assess which innovations merit further investigation, where they have been applied and what evidence supports their use. The challenge extends beyond primary production to food processing, storage, distribution and other activities across agrifood value chains. It is particularly consequential in low- and middle-income countries, where capacities to access, assess and adopt innovations are unequal. Farmer-led and locally developed solutions can also remain overlooked when they are poorly documented or disconnected from established knowledge networks. The resulting bottleneck is not simply a lack of technologies, but a lack of structured, discoverable and context-rich knowledge for adoption and investment decisions. Addressing it requires a scalable way to identify relevant innovations within heterogeneous source material, organize their attributes consistently and help users retrieve information against specific needs.
Solution Overview: The Agrifood Systems Technologies and Innovations Outlook Knowledge Base (ATIO KB) is FAO's global platform for discovering agrifood technologies and innovations. Hosted within the FAO Science, Technology and Innovation Portal, it combines information from multiple sources with AI-assisted enrichment and conversational discovery. It covers technological, institutional, financial, policy and social innovations across agrifood value chains, with particular attention to low- and middle-income countries. AI supports two connected functions. First, it helps transform heterogeneous source material into structured innovation records. The enrichment workflow assesses whether a source describes an innovation, extracts the innovation itself, generates or enriches descriptions and assigns metadata against ATIO taxonomies. These classifications help organize information by attributes such as innovation type, use case and adoption-related characteristics. AI-assisted quality checks support this process, while quality assurance and editorial oversight remain areas of ongoing development. Second, the ATIO Bot provides a conversational route into the knowledge base alongside filter-based search. Its technical design uses retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), combining retrieval from KB content with language-model-generated responses. Users can describe their role, challenge and information needs to explore relevant innovations. The purpose is to support discovery and further assessment using the knowledge base, rather than to establish the suitability of a technology without local evaluation. For agrifood businesses, development programmes and investors, this provides a common starting point for identifying candidate technologies and examining available evidence. Potential industrial applications include exploring innovations relevant to food processing, storage, resource efficiency and resilient supply chains. The platform supports the information-gathering stage of adoption and investment decisions; implementation outcomes depend on subsequent technical, financial and local assessment. The platform is developed through a partnership model combining FAO stewardship, external data providers and stakeholder consultation. GIZ supports ATIO through the Fund for the Promotion of Innovation in Agriculture (i4Ag), on behalf of Germany's Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ). The latest project presentation reports more than 6,000 innovations and 13 data providers. Further development includes strengthening grassroots innovation coverage and expanding discovery capabilities. ATIO KB's contribution to an industrial AI ecosystem is the use of AI to organize fragmented innovation knowledge and make it more accessible for practical technology discovery.
Solution Provider(s): Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) - lead organization and platform steward through its Office of Innovation; United Nations specialized agency in food and agriculture, Deutsche Gesellschaft fuer Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH - international cooperation organization supporting ATIO through the Fund for the Promotion of Innovation in Agriculture (i4Ag); sustainable development and agrifood innovation, Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) of Germany - federal ministry providing financial support; international development cooperation
Implementation location(s): Online deployment through the FAO Science, Technology and Innovation Portal, accessible globally and coordinated by FAO's Office of Innovation in Rome, Italy. Platform: https://sti-portal.fao.org/pages/atio-knowledge-base
Implementation timeline(s): 2024–2025: prototype development and initial launch. 2026–present: public platform operation and continued development of AI-assisted enrichment, search and user access. The GIZ-supported project runs from November 2025 to November 2027, supporting further platform development and expansion.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: An indicative 8–12 weeks to establish and run an initial, focused user pilot in a new country using the existing online platform. This assumes an identified local partner, internet-connected participants, use of existing KB content and no major software customization. Activities would include defining local information needs, preparing relevant search scenarios, onboarding users, testing AI-assisted discovery and reviewing results and feedback. Additional time would be required for new data-source integration, language adaptation or country-specific functionality. This is a planning estimate, subject to scoping with the implementing partners.
Desired impact: ATIO KB aims to make agrifood innovation knowledge easier to discover and use in technology adoption, project design and investment decisions, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Its main objectives are to: • Use AI to identify innovations in heterogeneous source material and enrich their descriptions and classifications, making fragmented information more structured and searchable. • Enable users to explore relevant technologies and supporting evidence through conversational AI and taxonomy-based search. • Broaden access to innovation knowledge, including greater visibility for farmer-led and locally developed solutions. • Strengthen knowledge sharing across data providers, development organizations, researchers, businesses and public institutions. The latest project presentation reports more than 6,000 innovations and 13 data providers. These figures demonstrate the scale of the knowledge resource and its source network. The publicly accessible platform brings this information together with AI-assisted discovery, providing a shared starting point for users investigating agrifood innovations. Expected benefits include less effort spent searching across disconnected sources, more consistent organization of innovation information and better-informed shortlisting of technologies for local assessment. For agrifood enterprises and development programmes, this can support the exploration of options relevant to processing, storage, resource efficiency and climate resilience. These downstream benefits have not yet been quantified in the evidence available for this submission. The application therefore does not attribute emissions reductions, energy savings, jobs created or completed technology adoption to the platform. A focused pilot could assess search-task completion, time needed to identify relevant records, relevance and accuracy of AI-assisted results, and documented use of findings in project or investment preparation.
Key technologies: The core technologies are generative AI, large language models (LLMs), retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), structured taxonomies and automated data integration. AI-assisted information extraction and enrichment: LLM-based workflows assess source material for relevant innovations, extract innovation information, generate or enrich descriptions and classify records against ATIO taxonomies. AI-assisted checks support the review of enriched information, with quality assurance continuing to evolve. Conversational AI and retrieval: ATIO Bot enables natural-language exploration of the knowledge base. Its documented technical design uses RAG and vector-based retrieval to combine relevant KB content with language-model-generated responses. Knowledge organization and search: Structured innovation profiles and controlled taxonomies organize heterogeneous records into searchable attributes. Filter-based search complements conversational discovery and allows users to explore records through defined categories. Data integration and platform management: Automated harvesting and Python-based processing support the integration of external sources. Drupal provides the platform's content and taxonomy management framework, with AI integration and workflow orchestration supporting enrichment processes. Together, these technologies connect source collection, AI-assisted structuring and user-facing discovery within a single agrifood innovation knowledge platform.
Unique Characteristics: ATIO KB's distinctive contribution is the combination of AI-assisted knowledge structuring, agrifood-specific taxonomies and a partnership-driven discovery platform under FAO stewardship. AI connects information preparation with user discovery. The enrichment workflow identifies innovations within heterogeneous source material, extracts relevant information and enriches descriptions and classifications. ATIO Bot then provides a conversational route into the resulting knowledge base. This connects the organization of innovation information with the practical questions of users exploring technologies for particular needs. Domain-specific knowledge organization gives this AI workflow its agrifood relevance. ATIO taxonomies organize innovations by attributes such as innovation type, use case and adoption-related characteristics. Users can explore information through both natural-language questions and structured filters, combining flexible discovery with explicit categories for further assessment. The platform also treats innovation broadly. Technological solutions are considered alongside financial, institutional, policy and social innovations across agrifood value chains. This enables users to explore both technologies and the enabling conditions that can influence their adoption. Its focus on farmer-led and locally developed innovations seeks to make less visible knowledge discoverable alongside formal research and commercial solutions. The partnership model brings together content from multiple providers within a shared discovery platform. FAO stewardship and development-cooperation support provide an institutional basis for a neutral knowledge resource serving public, research and business users. Partners contribute complementary knowledge, while AI assists with organizing heterogeneous information. The innovation lies in bringing these elements together: AI-supported information processing, domain-specific structure, inclusive coverage and collaborative delivery, applied to the practical challenge of finding relevant agrifood innovations and supporting evidence.
Sustainable Change: ATIO KB could strengthen the shared knowledge infrastructure through which agrifood technologies and innovations are discovered, assessed and considered for adoption. Its potential extends beyond individual searches to how organizations build on existing knowledge across projects, sectors and countries. First, a shared platform can reduce repeated information-gathering across disconnected initiatives. Development agencies, businesses, researchers and public institutions could use a common discovery resource to identify relevant innovations and investigate existing evidence before commissioning new work or selecting technologies. AI-assisted extraction and classification provide a mechanism for incorporating additional sources, while conversational discovery helps users navigate the growing knowledge base. Second, the platform can support cross-country learning. Innovations documented in one setting can become visible to users facing related challenges elsewhere. Their inclusion does not establish suitability for another location, but it creates a starting point for local assessment, adaptation and collaboration. This is particularly relevant where access to innovation information and assessment capacity is limited. Third, expanding grassroots coverage could broaden whose knowledge informs innovation decisions. Making farmer-led and locally developed solutions more discoverable may help development programmes, researchers and investors consider approaches that receive less attention through established research and commercial channels. Scale-up can build on the existing platform through additional data partnerships, thematic coverage and locally facilitated user pilots. Lessons from these pilots could inform improvements to classifications, AI-assisted discovery and user guidance, benefiting subsequent users across the platform. Sustained change would depend on reliable source information, effective quality assurance, continued partner participation and evidence that users apply the knowledge in real decisions. Over time, ATIO KB could become a shared resource used routinely in project preparation, technology assessment and investment screening, helping connect agrifood innovation knowledge with practical opportunities for adoption.
Funding Sources: ATIO KB has been funded through FAO's Capital Expenditure (CapEx) mechanism as part of the Science, Technology and Innovation (STI) Portal project, together with financial support from Germany's Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ), channelled through Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH under the Fund for the Promotion of Innovation in Agriculture (i4Ag).
Testimonials and Endorsements: No verified stakeholder or beneficiary quotations are included in this submission. Official information and supporting materials are provided under Media Links.

It earns its place on a live platform with a real corpus; the score is held down because nothing yet shows a user changing a decision, and the AI quality is described as work in progress.

Title: OpenFarming: Turning Everyday Orders into Supply Chain Intelligence
Subtitle: Multilingual AI turns WhatsApp and email orders into structured workflows, helping food manufacturers and distributors reduce manual work and improve inventory decisions.
Problem Statement: For many food manufacturers and distributors, demand first arrives as a WhatsApp message, voice note, email or purchase order. Employees must interpret each request, identify the correct products and quantities, check availability and enter the order into business systems. This manual bridge between customers and operations delays fulfilment and leaves demand information fragmented. In perishable supply chains, poor visibility can contribute to stockouts, excess inventory and spoilage. Smaller businesses face additional barriers: limited technical capacity, multilingual customers and workforces, and the cost of changing established processes. They need practical AI that works through existing communication channels and connects reliably to their operations.
Solution Overview: OpenFarming connects everyday customer communication to the operational systems of food manufacturers and distributors. Its commercially live Order Aggregator uses AI to convert WhatsApp messages, emails and documents into structured orders. The workflow has four steps: 1. Interpret incoming requests and extract customer, product, quantity and other order details. 2. Match customer terminology to the business’s product catalogue. 3. Support inventory validation and human review of ambiguous or incomplete requests. 4. Transfer reviewed information into operational dashboards and connected business systems. The technology combines multilingual language models, document extraction, AI-assisted product matching and workflow integrations. Human review remains part of the process, allowing staff to correct exceptions before they affect fulfilment. Paying customers include BBM Foods and Dr. Müller’s German Ice Cream in the UAE, and FJ Primeholdings in the Philippines, across order automation and AI sales use cases. The Order Aggregator and AI Sales Agent are live; demand prediction and payment reconciliation remain at MVP/pilot stage. Each implementation is developed with the customer’s operational team using its catalogues, sample transactions and existing systems. This produces a practical deployment model: begin with one workflow, measure its performance and expand when the operational value is established.
Solution Provider(s): BBM Foods — UAE food distributor and paying deployment customer in the food supply-chain sector, FJ Primeholdings Corporation — Philippines food-service and franchise operator associated with Beard Papa’s and a paying deployment customer, Dr. Müller’s German Ice Cream — UAE ice-cream manufacturer and paying AI Sales Agent customer in the food manufacturing sector, Google for Startups — technology entrepreneurship programme providing accelerator support and AI technical mentoring through its 2026 MENA programme, Techstars — global startup accelerator and investor supporting OpenFarming through its Future of Food programme.
Implementation location(s): United Arab Emirates: BBM Foods and Dr. Müller’s German Ice Cream, including the latter’s Sharjah-based manufacturing operations. Philippines: FJ Primeholdings, including its Luzon warehouse operations.
Implementation timeline(s): 2026–present: ongoing customer deployments in the United Arab Emirates and Philippines, with phased implementation of order automation, AI sales and inventory-related workflows.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: An estimated 4–6 weeks to configure, launch and evaluate an initial supervised pilot with one distributor or manufacturer. This includes workflow assessment, product catalogue preparation, integration configuration, testing with representative orders, staff onboarding and live evaluation. The timeline assumes timely access to customer data and a standard integration or agreed data-import process. Complex ERP integrations or additional localisation requirements may extend deployment.
Desired impact: Our objective is to make reliable AI useful in the daily operations of food businesses: reducing manual order handling, improving the availability of demand data and supporting better inventory decisions. OpenFarming has paying customers in the UAE and Philippines. Our November 2026 internal impact report estimates approximately 15,000 AI-assisted orders processed between 3 January and 5 November 2026. A retrospective study of 5,000 orders compared a reconstructed manual baseline with actual AI-assisted human handling, including review and corrections. It indicated a reduction from 20 minutes to 2 minutes per order, equivalent to approximately 1,500 hours of operational capacity across the sample. These are internal estimates rather than independently audited results. Aggregate order counts remain subject to log reconciliation, and time released is not presented as verified cash savings. The next impact objective is to connect better demand capture with measurable inventory outcomes. New pilots will assess processing time, correction rates and staff adoption, alongside stockouts, inventory variance and product write-offs where reliable baseline data is available. Waste reduction is an intended outcome; verified environmental savings are not yet claimed.
Key technologies: OpenFarming combines large language models and multilingual natural-language processing to interpret customer requests, extract order details and support AI-assisted sales workflows. Document processing and optical character recognition extract information from purchase orders, PDFs and images. AI-assisted SKU matching maps customer terminology, abbreviations and product descriptions to business catalogues. APIs and workflow automation connect WhatsApp, email, operational dashboards and ERP systems, supporting inventory validation and structured order processing. Human-in-the-loop review enables staff to resolve ambiguous requests and correct exceptions. Cloud infrastructure supports deployment and ongoing operation. Demand forecasting and inventory analytics are at MVP/pilot stage, extending the platform toward better replenishment decisions.
Unique Characteristics: OpenFarming makes existing business communication usable as operational data. Buyers can continue ordering through WhatsApp and email while suppliers receive structured information that supports fulfilment and inventory workflows. Its differentiation rests on three features: First, multilingual order understanding and product matching address the practical complexity of food distribution, including inconsistent product names, abbreviations and pack sizes. Second, the solution connects order capture to business operations through inventory validation, human review and ERP-connected workflows. This makes the output useful beyond the conversation itself. Third, modular deployment allows smaller businesses to start with one costly manual process. They can establish the value of order automation before adopting additional capabilities. Together, these features reduce the behavioural and technical changes required for adoption while retaining human oversight where mistakes could affect customer orders.
Sustainable Change: OpenFarming’s potential extends beyond processing individual orders. By structuring demand that previously remained inside conversations and documents, it can help smaller businesses build a usable foundation for inventory planning, procurement and coordination with suppliers. A distributor provides a practical point of entry: it connects multiple upstream producers with downstream restaurants, retailers and other buyers. Improving its order workflow can benefit these trading relationships while allowing buyers to retain familiar communication channels. The proposed replication model starts with one distributor or manufacturer in a new market, establishes baseline performance and tests a defined workflow before expanding to additional sites or businesses. Localisation focuses on product catalogues, language, integrations and staff onboarding. Industry associations and development programmes could help replicate successful deployments across groups of MSMEs. Over time, this approach could support more responsive food supply chains and fewer avoidable inventory losses, with expansion guided by measured results.
Funding Sources: OpenFarming has raised approximately USD 400,000 in investment from Techstars and Salica Investments / Spring Studios to support product development and commercial deployment. Customer revenue also supports implementation and ongoing operations, including paid engagements with BBM Foods and Dr. Müller’s German Ice Cream in the UAE, and FJ Primeholdings in the Philippines. Additional non-financial support includes technical mentoring and accelerator support through Google for Startups Accelerator: Middle East, North Africa and Türkiye.
Testimonials and Endorsements: Aniss Amrah, following a mentoring session with OpenFarming at a Google for Startups event, publicly wrote: “Openfarming has engineered a remarkably intelligent platform to replace that friction”. His post discusses the platform’s approach to fragmented agricultural supply-chain operations. [Source: Aniss Amrah’s public LinkedIn post](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/aniss-amrah_last-week-stepping-back-into-coaching-during-activity-7495476880981184512-kwCi) Google publicly selected OpenFarming for its 2026 Google for Startups Accelerator: Middle East, North Africa and Türkiye, describing the company’s work as automating distributor workflows to reduce waste and protect margins. [Source: Google Cloud’s official cohort announcement](https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/startups/meet-the-newest-cohort-of-our-mena-t-startup-accelerator) Techstars selected and invested in OpenFarming through its Future of Food Powered by Ecolab accelerator. [Source: Techstars’ official cohort announcement](https://www.techstars.com/newsroom/meet-the-startups-joining-techstars-fall-2025-accelerator-programs) These references represent mentor feedback and institutional recognition, rather than independent verification of customer outcomes.

It is the most commercially advanced entry in this batch after the Chinese manufacturers, and it loses ground on demonstration and on the missing waste outcome.

Title: Mentis & MIOS (Mentis Industrial OS): Sovereign Industrial AI Powered by Small Language Models
Subtitle: A compute-efficient, SLM-powered agentic AI operating system enabling autonomous industrial intelligence, enterprise automation and secure deployment without cloud dependence.
Problem Statement: Industrial enterprises face significant barriers to AI adoption, including high computational costs, fragmented operational data, dependence on external cloud infrastructure, limited connectivity and stringent data sovereignty requirements. Most general-purpose AI systems are not designed for the specialised, interconnected and security-sensitive nature of industrial operations. Deploying large language models for every operational task can also introduce unnecessary infrastructure costs and complexity. This creates a critical accessibility gap, particularly for MSMEs and organisations operating in resource-constrained or highly regulated environments. A more efficient, domain-specialised and locally deployable approach to industrial AI is required.
Solution Overview: Genovation's Mentis and Mentis Industrial OS (MIOS) provide an integrated, sovereign agentic AI architecture designed around specialised Small Language Models (SLMs). Rather than depending exclusively on large, general-purpose models for all tasks, Mentis uses specialised AI agents and compact language models adapted to enterprise functions. These agents support task-specific reasoning, enterprise workflows, information retrieval, operational analysis and controlled execution. MIOS extends this architecture into industrial environments by integrating operational databases, enterprise applications, industrial data sources and IoT connectivity. It provides a unified environment for industrial intelligence, KPI monitoring, natural-language querying, root-cause analysis and workflow automation. Depending on implementation requirements, the platform can additionally incorporate predictive maintenance, anomaly detection, predictive alerting and digital twin capabilities. The architecture supports private infrastructure and fully air-gapped deployment, allowing organisations to retain control over sensitive operational information while minimising dependency on external AI services. The platform is designed for modular adoption, allowing enterprises to introduce specific AI capabilities without undertaking a complete replacement of existing industrial systems.
Solution Provider(s): NVIDIA Corporation (USA) – AI and accelerated computing, Lenovo Group Limited – Enterprise computing and IT infrastructure
Implementation location(s): India, Germany, Japan
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 8–12 weeks for a defined initial implementation, subject to infrastructure availability, operational data readiness, integration requirements and customer-specific security policies.
Desired impact: The primary objective of Mentis and MIOS is to democratise industrial artificial intelligence by enabling enterprises to deploy computationally efficient, specialised and sovereign AI systems within their existing operational infrastructure. The platform aims to reduce the technological and economic barriers that prevent industrial organisations from benefiting from advanced artificial intelligence. Key objectives and anticipated impact include: 1. Making industrial AI more computationally accessible Through specialised Small Language Models and task-oriented agentic orchestration, the platform is designed to reduce reliance on computationally intensive general-purpose models for routine enterprise and industrial tasks. This approach supports more efficient AI deployment, particularly for organisations with limited AI infrastructure or restrictive data residency requirements. 2. Improving industrial productivity AI agents support automation of repetitive activities, operational reporting, information retrieval, process coordination and analytical workflows, allowing employees to focus on higher-value decision-making and operational improvement. 3. Strengthening operational intelligence MIOS connects industrial and enterprise data sources to provide a unified foundation for operational monitoring, KPI analysis, root-cause investigation and informed decision-making. 4. Improving industrial asset and resource efficiency The platform supports operational analysis and can be extended with predictive models, anomaly detection and intelligent alerting to assist organisations in identifying process inefficiencies, equipment abnormalities and emerging operational risks. 5. Enabling secure and inclusive AI adoption Private and air-gapped deployment capabilities allow security-sensitive industrial organisations to adopt AI without requiring sensitive operational data to be transmitted to externally hosted AI services. 6. Supporting sustainable industrial transformation Improved information availability, process visibility and resource utilisation can support reductions in avoidable operational waste, unnecessary equipment usage and inefficient production activities. -- Impact measurement The platform is intended to generate measurable improvements across indicators such as: - Manual processing and reporting time. - Time required to retrieve and analyse operational information. - AI workflow completion accuracy and execution time. - Computational resources required for task-specific inference. - Operational downtime and asset utilisation, where relevant advanced analytical modules are deployed. - Process inefficiencies and resource consumption.
Key technologies: Mentis and MIOS combine specialised artificial intelligence, industrial data infrastructure and governed enterprise automation. Small Language Models (SLMs): Compact, specialised language models adapted to enterprise tasks and industrial application requirements. Model specialisation and fine-tuning are used where appropriate to support efficient, context-specific intelligence. Multi-agent AI orchestration: Coordination of specialised intelligent agents capable of executing distinct tasks, interacting with enterprise systems and participating in multi-step operational workflows. Large Language Models (LLMs): Selective integration of larger models where complex reasoning or task requirements justify their use, enabling a flexible model architecture rather than exclusive dependence on SLMs. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): Contextual information retrieval from governed enterprise and operational data sources to support grounded AI responses. Industrial data integration and IoT: Connectivity with enterprise databases, ERP systems, industrial applications, equipment data and IoT information sources. Multimodal data infrastructure: Support for structured, semi-structured and unstructured data, including document, relational, time-series and other relevant enterprise information. Business intelligence and analytics: Operational dashboards, KPI visualisation, natural-language reporting and root-cause investigation. Workflow automation: AI-assisted process execution, configurable enterprise applications and human-in-the-loop approval mechanisms. Predictive analytics and anomaly detection: Optional integration of machine learning models for operational forecasting, abnormality detection and predictive alerting. Digital twin technologies: Optional development of operational digital representations linked to relevant industrial data sources and asset information. Sovereign AI infrastructure: Private deployment architectures, on-premises model execution, controlled data access and fully air-gapped operational configurations. Security and governance: Role-based permissions, workflow controls, auditability and human oversight of AI-driven operations.
Unique Characteristics: The core innovation of Mentis and MIOS lies in combining specialised Small Language Models, agentic orchestration and industrial data infrastructure within a unified enterprise operating environment. Unlike AI approaches that rely predominantly on large, general-purpose cloud-hosted models, the architecture prioritises task-specific intelligence, efficient model execution and deployment flexibility. Key differentiators include: 1. Specialised SLM-powered agents for domain-specific enterprise and industrial tasks. 2. Agentic orchestration that coordinates multiple specialised capabilities rather than relying on a single general-purpose model. 3. Private, on-premises and fully air-gapped deployment without mandatory dependence on external AI APIs. 4. Native industrial data integration, operational intelligence and governed enterprise workflow execution through MIOS. 5. A modular architecture that allows organisations to extend AI capabilities incrementally within their existing infrastructure. Together, these capabilities offer an alternative approach to industrial AI adoption, prioritising computational efficiency, sovereignty, modularity and enterprise integration.
Sustainable Change: Mentis and MIOS have the potential to contribute to a structural shift in how industrial enterprises adopt and operationalise artificial intelligence. Much of the current industrial AI ecosystem depends on expensive computing infrastructure, centralised AI services, specialised implementation expertise and fragmented technology applications. These requirements can restrict adoption among MSMEs, manufacturing enterprises in emerging economies and organisations operating under strict security or connectivity constraints. Mentis addresses these barriers through a modular, SLM-powered agentic architecture that enables industrial intelligence to be deployed within existing enterprise environments. 1. Expanding access to industrial AI By prioritising specialised, compute-efficient models and modular implementation, the solution can make advanced AI capabilities accessible to a broader range of industrial organisations. 2. Reducing dependence on centralised AI infrastructure Support for local model execution and air-gapped environments provides an alternative adoption pathway for organisations that cannot depend on externally hosted AI services. 3. Enabling industrial AI infrastructure reuse Once the underlying data and AI environment is established, additional specialised agents, workflows and operational applications can be introduced without independently rebuilding the entire technology foundation for every use case. 4. Supporting replication across sectors and geographies The architecture can be adapted to manufacturing, engineering, logistics, industrial supply chains and other data-intensive enterprise environments through configurable integrations and domain-specific AI capabilities. 5. Strengthening local technology capabilities The platform creates opportunities for local implementation partners, technical teams and industrial organisations to build, configure and operate AI-enabled applications within their existing technological ecosystems. 6. Advancing sustainable industrial modernisation Improved operational visibility, process intelligence and proactive analytical capabilities can help organisations identify inefficiencies, improve asset utilisation and support more responsible use of industrial resources. Over time, the broader impact of the solution lies in establishing an accessible technological foundation through which industrial enterprises can transition from fragmented data systems and manual operational processes toward secure, intelligent and increasingly autonomous operations. Its potential systemic contribution is the democratisation of sovereign industrial AI: enabling organisations of different sizes, sectors and geographies to implement advanced AI capabilities without becoming structurally dependent on external model providers or centralised computing environments.

Title: Zami: source-traceable market intelligence for Ethiopian industry and MSMEs
Subtitle: An AI system that reads Ethiopia's economy and its markets in English and five Ethiopian languages, from official data to public demand, and links every figure to the source it came from.
Problem Statement: Ethiopian manufacturers and MSMEs make investment, pricing and sourcing decisions without reliable, timely market information. Official statistics arrive late (Ethiopia's balance-of-payments figures reach the IMF about 18 months after the quarter) and are scattered across central-bank bulletins, ministry PDFs, regulators, exchanges and statistical reports, many of them scanned or published in Amharic, Afaan Oromoo, Tigrinya, Af-Soomaali or Qafar af. The prices that matter most to a producer — the parallel exchange rate, fuel, construction materials, commodity and food prices, advertised wages — are often not in official series at all. What buyers actually want is spread across social media and Telegram, in local languages. Large firms pay consultants to assemble this; MSMEs go without, and decisions rest on hearsay. Where AI tools exist, they rarely read Ethiopian languages and seldom show where a number came from, so their answers cannot be checked.
Solution Overview: Zami is one intelligence layer with two parts, built and operated in Ethiopia by Masha Technologies Works PLC. Zami Terminal (the economy around a producer). A market-intelligence system for Ethiopia's economy. It collects 264 official, regulatory, statistical, market, news, procurement, job and Telegram sources; preserves every original; and turns them into data: 269,516 exact statistical values in 11,159 series, 3,459,865 figures indexed from official report tables, 22 quote-checked figure datasets, and official surveys converted to data and checked word for word against the published reports (labour force, migration, demographic and health, crops, livestock). It tracks 630,655 public tenders, 378,773 job openings from 33,676 employers and over 800,000 street-price adverts, and keeps a knowledge graph of 646,824 resolved entities in which every relationship points to the sentence that states it. A Bloomberg-style terminal of more than 50 panels presents rates, exchange rates, prices, trade, energy, companies, development finance and tenders. Ask writes cited answers: a planner retrieves passages, series and table figures, a writer drafts, and a checker verifies every number against the cited evidence before the answer is shown. Zami (what buyers want). A live AI platform that collects public conversation from social, news and web sources, classifies it, and reports demand, prices and complaints from consumers, with every claim citing its source. Extraction, search and photo checks run on our own hardware (a dedicated server and 10 GPU PCs running Gemma and Qwen models). Model output stays a candidate until it is reviewed.
Solution Provider(s): Ethiopian Artificial Intelligence Institute (EAII), Startup Centre / Programme — the national AI institute of Ethiopia; Zami participates in its startup programme as an incubatee.
Implementation location(s): Ethiopia — national coverage of federal and regional sources, markets and languages; operated from Addis Ababa.

Desired impact: Objectives: 1. Give Ethiopian manufacturers and MSMEs the market information large firms buy: input costs, exchange rates, credit, demand, competitors, tenders and regulation, in one place and in their languages. 2. Make every figure checkable, so decisions rest on evidence rather than hearsay. 3. Turn Ethiopia's scattered official publications into reusable public data. What is in place today (13 October 2026) — coverage and capability, not yet user outcomes: - 269,516 exact statistical values in 11,159 series; 3,459,865 figures from official report tables - 630,655 public tenders and 378,773 job openings tracked; over 800,000 street-price adverts - 646,824 resolved entities; 92,663 extracted relationships, 36,073 reviewed - 85% of relationships correct on a random audit of 40; about 110,000 model calls a day on in-house GPUs Impact indicators we will measure in a pilot: MSMEs and business-support organisations using the terminal; time to assemble a market brief (days to minutes); tender opportunities surfaced per user; share of answers whose figures pass the checker without correction. No user outcomes have been measured yet; these are the indicators we commit to report.
Key technologies: AI/ML; natural language processing in English, Amharic, Afaan Oromoo, Tigrinya, Af-Soomaali and Qafar af; local large language models (Gemma, Qwen) and embeddings (Qwen3-Embedding) on in-house GPUs; retrieval-augmented generation with citation checking (Gemini for written answers); knowledge graph with identity resolution; OCR including a fine-tuned Amharic model; PDF table extraction; data pipelines over PostgreSQL with pgvector; Rust; web terminal.
Unique Characteristics: - Every figure is traceable. Each number points to the document or dataset it came from, and each relationship to the sentence that states it. A checker verifies every number in a written answer before it is shown. - Built for Ethiopian languages and calendars. It reads English and five Ethiopian languages, Ethiopic-script documents and scanned pages, and converts Ethiopian-calendar dates to Gregorian. - Measures what official data misses. Street inflation from adverts, the parallel exchange rate, construction material and fuel prices, and an advertised-pay index against inflation. - Low cost to run. Collection, extraction and search run on our own hardware, with no paid API; only written answers use a paid model. - Honest by design. Model output is a candidate until reviewed, and sources that block automated access are respected, never bypassed.
Sustainable Change: Most developing economies share Ethiopia's problem: official data that is late, scattered across PDFs and scans, and published in languages global AI tools do not read. Zami Terminal is a repeatable way to build a national, source-traceable economic data layer from what a country already publishes. The pipeline (collect, preserve, extract, check, cite) is language- and country-agnostic; adding a country is a source audit and language work, not a rebuild. For industry it lowers the cost of market intelligence from a consultant's fee to a query, so MSMEs can plan with the same evidence as large firms. For governments and development partners it turns their own publications into reusable data and makes procurement, labour and price trends visible as they happen. In-house models keep running costs low enough for low-income markets.

Title: ORCA-APAS: Marine Physical AI for Intelligent and Sustainable Navigation
Subtitle: An AI-powered marine navigation system integrating multi-sensor perception, intelligent decision-making, and autonomous control to enhance vessel safety, operational efficiency, and sustainability.
Problem Statement: The maritime industry faces persistent challenges, including navigation risks caused by complex and dynamic water environments, reliance on manual operations, crew shortages, and limited intelligence in conventional autopilot systems. Traditional navigation systems primarily rely on predefined routes and basic control mechanisms, offering limited environmental perception, risk assessment, and adaptive decision-making capabilities. These limitations can lead to human errors, operational inefficiencies, excessive fuel consumption, and increased safety risks. ORCA-APAS addresses these challenges by introducing AI-powered environmental perception, real-time risk identification, intelligent navigation planning, and autonomous control. It helps reduce dependence on manual operations, improve navigation safety, optimize operational efficiency, and support the maritime industry's transition toward more sustainable and intelligent operations.
Solution Overview: Solution Overview 1 How the Solution Works ORCA-APAS (Advanced Pilot Assistance System) is an independently developed Marine Physical AI solution designed for USVs, commercial ships, yachts, and government vessels. Based on ORCAUBOAT's "One Brain, Multiple Embodied Platforms" architecture, it integrates AI algorithms, a self-developed domain controller, multi-source sensors, and human-machine interfaces to enable intelligent perception, decision-making, and vessel control. The system operates through four key stages: 1) Environmental Perception: Fuses data from 4D radar, cameras, and GNSS/INS to detect vessels, obstacles, and surrounding conditions in real time. 2) Risk Assessment: Uses AI algorithms to identify navigation hazards, assess collision risks, and predict grounding risks. 3) Intelligent Decision-Making: Combines perception data, electronic charts, and navigation information to optimize routes and generate navigation decisions. 4) Navigation Control: Converts decisions into vessel control commands, supporting collision avoidance, automatic steering, dynamic positioning, remote control, and autonomous navigation. With solutions spanning L2 to L4 autonomy, ORCA-APAS enables the transition from conventional vessels to intelligent marine platforms. 2 Methodologies and Technologies Used Key technologies include: - Marine Physical AI: Integrates perception, intelligent decision-making, and physical vessel control. - Multi-Sensor Fusion: Combines radar, visible-light and infrared imaging, and GNSS/INS positioning. - AI-Based Computer Vision: Enables vessel detection, obstacle recognition, and real-time situational awareness. - Intelligent Navigation Algorithms: Supports collision avoidance, grounding prediction, and route planning. - High-Performance Computing: Uses an in-house developed domain controller and AI computing architecture for real-time processing. - Autonomous Control: Connects AI navigation decisions with vessel control systems to enable intelligent and autonomous operations. Together, these technologies extend beyond conventional autopilot capabilities, delivering integrated AI-powered navigation. 3 Partnerships and Collaboration Models ORCAUBOAT works with industry stakeholders to accelerate the deployment and commercialization of Marine Physical AI. Key collaboration models include: - Shipowners and Operators: Real-world deployment, operational validation, and system optimization. - Shipyards and Vessel Manufacturers: Integration into new-build vessels and retrofit projects. - Technology Partners: Joint development and integration of sensors, navigation equipment, and marine electronics. - Research Institutions: Collaboration on AI algorithms, autonomous navigation, and technical innovation. - Classification Societies: Product certification, safety validation, and regulatory compliance. Through in-house R&D and cross-industry collaboration, ORCAUBOAT aims to scale intelligent navigation solutions and advance safer, more efficient, and sustainable maritime operations.
Solution Provider(s): China COSCO Shipping Corporation Limited, China Resources Power Holdings Company Limited, Shell plc, Asia-Pacific Satellite Communications Co., Ltd., China Classification Society (CCS), Armona Denizcilik A.Ş., etc.
Implementation location(s): United Kingdom, France, Spain, Belgium, Iraq, Hong Kong SAR, Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia, North America, Sri Lanka, Saudi Arabia, and other markets.

Its main objectives are to: - Enhance vessel safety through AI-powered environmental perception, collision avoidance, and risk prediction. - Improve operational efficiency and reduce reliance on manual navigation. - Optimize navigation routes and energy consumption to support lower-emission maritime operations. - Accelerate the intelligent upgrade of existing vessels and the adoption of autonomous navigation technologies. Expected and Demonstrated Impact ORCA-APAS has demonstrated measurable results in real-world maritime applications: - 40% improvement in operational efficiency in a deployed commercial vessel project. - 30% reduction in fuel consumption in the same project, contributing to lower energy use and carbon emissions. - Over 2 million kilometers of cumulative unmanned navigation experience, demonstrating the system's operational maturity. - 1,000+ vessels and uncrewed surface vessels supported across multiple application scenarios. - Deployment across 16 countries and regions, supporting the global adoption of intelligent maritime technologies. By combining AI-driven navigation with real-world vessel operations, ORCA-APAS helps improve maritime safety, optimize resource utilization, and advance the transition toward a more efficient and sustainable shipping industry.
Key technologies: Artificial Intelligence (AI) & Marine Physical AI: Enables intelligent environmental perception, risk assessment, decision-making, and autonomous navigation. Multi-Sensor Fusion: Integrates 4D radar, visible-light and infrared cameras, GNSS/INS, and other sensors for comprehensive real-time situational awareness. Computer Vision & Deep Learning: Supports vessel detection, obstacle recognition, target tracking, and navigation hazard identification. Intelligent Navigation Algorithms: Enables collision avoidance, route planning, grounding prediction, and adaptive navigation decisions. Internet of Things (IoT): Connects onboard sensors, navigation equipment, controllers, and vessel systems for real-time data acquisition and communication. Edge AI & High-Performance Computing: Uses an in-house developed domain controller and AI computing architecture for real-time onboard data processing and intelligent control. Autonomous Control Systems: Integrates AI-based navigation decisions with vessel control systems to support assisted and autonomous operations.
Unique Characteristics: ORCA-APAS stands out through its Marine Physical AI architecture, full-stack in-house development, and scalable multi-vessel deployment model. Marine Physical AI: Goes beyond conventional autopilot systems by integrating environmental perception, risk assessment, intelligent decision-making, and vessel control into a unified AI-driven navigation system. One Brain, Multiple Embodied Platforms: Built on a unified AI architecture that can be adapted across USVs, commercial ships, yachts, and government vessels, enabling technology reuse and scalable deployment across different vessel types and operating environments. Full-Stack In-House Development: Combines proprietary AI algorithms, a self-developed domain controller, sensor integration, and control technologies, enabling deep hardware-software integration and continuous system optimization. Advanced Environmental Perception and Decision-Making: Integrates multi-sensor fusion and AI algorithms to identify navigation hazards, assess collision risks, predict grounding risks, and support adaptive route planning in complex marine environments. Scalable Autonomy: Supports solutions ranging from L2 assisted navigation to L4 autonomous operation, allowing flexible adaptation to different vessel requirements and levels of automation. Proven Real-World Deployment: Validated through applications across multiple vessel types and international markets, with over 2 million kilometers of unmanned navigation experience and more than 1,000 vessels supported. By combining a unified AI architecture, proprietary technologies, and proven industrial applications, ORCA-APAS offers a scalable approach to transforming conventional vessels into intelligent marine platforms and accelerating the digital and sustainable transformation of the maritime industry.
Sustainable Change: Potential for Systemic Change ORCA-APAS has the potential to drive systemic transformation in the maritime industry by making AI-powered intelligent navigation scalable, adaptable, and accessible across different vessel types and markets. Scalable Technology Adoption: Its "One Brain, Multiple Embodied Platforms" architecture enables the deployment of a unified AI navigation system across USVs, commercial ships, yachts, and government vessels, reducing development barriers and accelerating adoption. Modernization of Existing Fleets: APAS can be integrated into both new-build vessels and existing ships, providing a practical pathway for the large-scale intelligent upgrade of the global maritime fleet. Industry-Wide Safety and Efficiency Improvements: Wider adoption of AI-powered perception, risk prediction, and intelligent navigation can reduce human-related navigation risks, improve operational efficiency, and support more reliable maritime operations. International Replication and Collaboration: With deployments across multiple countries and regions, ORCAUBOAT can replicate its solutions through partnerships with shipowners, shipyards, technology providers, and local industry stakeholders, adapting the technology to different maritime environments and regulatory requirements. In the long term, ORCA-APAS aims to move the maritime industry beyond conventional manual navigation and isolated automation toward a connected, intelligent, and increasingly autonomous maritime ecosystem, supporting safer, more efficient, and sustainable global shipping.

Title: Industrial Embodied AI Solutions for Labor-Efficient, Flexible Manufacturing
Subtitle: Bowintec is co-founded by Boyuan Capital, Bosch’s market-oriented investment platform, and Galbot, with a mission to“empowering manufacture with embodied AI.” By integrating embodied AI robot, vertical models, platforms and data, Bowintec is building a deployable, scalable, and replicable full-stack innovation platform for industrial embodied AI. The company focus on key industries including automotive and auto parts, new energy, 3C electronics, semiconductors, logistics and white goods, and aims to become a global leader and standard-setter in embodied AI technology for the Industry 4.0 era.
Problem Statement: Global manufacturing faces severe labor shortages — an estimated 90 million worker gap by 2030 — while industrial robot penetration remains only about 25%. Rigid automation lines are costly to retrofit, and reliable multi-robot coordination in mixed fleets is rarely offered as a turnkey solution. Sorting, loading and material handling still depend heavily on manual labor, limiting productivity and flexibility for MSMEs and manufacturers in developing economies.
Solution Overview: BOWINtec delivers a full-stack industrial embodied AI platform integrating four layers: (1) industrial embodied AI robots (BW10, BW10-Lite, BW02) covering 10–50 kg payloads; (2) a vertical industrial model (Bolt) with multimodal perception (vision, point cloud, force-tactile); (3) an embodied AI task management platform (BEAmm-S) enabling unified mapping, single-bin-level task dispatch, zone-based control and anomaly alarms across heterogeneous robots; and (4) an industrial data collection and training platform (BRoPS) covering acquisition, labeling and model training. A closed-loop "data flywheel" — data collection 10× faster, 90% auto-verification, ~50% shorter model iteration cycles, on-site fast retraining within ~1 hour — continuously improves performance. The solution is delivered end-to-end: requirement analysis, project management, model training, standardized on-site deployment (with simulation-based pre-commissioning) and global after-sales support. BOWINtec is co-founded by Boyuan Capital (Bosch Group's market-oriented investment platform) and Galbot, combining Bosch industrial know-how, real production-line scenarios and Galbot's foundation models.

Implementation timeline(s): Ongoing since Aug 2025 (RoboFab Joint Lab with UAES); first production-line deployment Sep 2026 (UAES); Bosch Changzhou pilot commissioning Oct 2026.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Approximately 2–4 months, enabled by standardized deployment, simulation-based pre-commissioning (no on-site machine needed) and fast on-site retraining (~1 hour).
Desired impact: Objective: reduce manufacturing's dependence on manual labor and make flexible automation affordable and replicable, especially for MSMEs and developing economies. Demonstrated impact: at UAES (auto-electronics loading/unloading), 95% production success rate, +30% capacity, −50% operating cost; at Dijie Industrial (logistics sorting), 98% sorting success rate, +25% sorting efficiency, −50% labor cost; at Bosch Changzhou (warehouse in/outbound), targeting 98% success rate, +35% efficiency, −40% labor cost. Platform manages 100,000+ industrial operation segments; model iteration cycle shortened ~50%.
Key technologies: Embodied AI, industrial vertical foundation models (Bolt), multimodal perception (vision, point cloud, force-tactile), VLA models and world-model + atomic skill-tree architecture, AI agent task scheduling (BEAmm-S), industrial data collection/labeling/training platform (BRoPS) with closed-loop data flywheel, 4WD mobile platforms, dual-arm manipulation (±0.05 mm repeatability), hot-swap battery (24/7 operation), CE-certified industrial hardware.

Sustainable Change: The solution is standardized, replicable and deployable in new geographies within 2–4 months, enabling inclusive industrial transformation: it lowers barriers to flexible automation for MSMEs, addresses structural labor shortages, strengthens supply-chain resilience, and creates a transferable model of multi-robot, mixed-fleet coordination. With CE certification planned for 2027, it can scale from China to European and other high-labor-cost markets, supporting global replication and follow-on investment in industrial AI infrastructure.

Title: Dansen AI: An Operating Intelligence Layer for Industrial Enterprises
Subtitle: Connecting ERP, shop-floor data and AI agents to detect production risks, uncover root causes and coordinate accountable corrective action without replacing existing systems.
Problem Statement: Industrial enterprises, particularly manufacturers in emerging economies, face a fundamental operational intelligence gap. Although critical information exists across ERP systems, production software, procurement platforms, spreadsheets, machinery, and quality records, these systems rarely provide a unified understanding of operational conditions. Consequently, supply shortages, production delays, inventory discrepancies, quality exceptions, and process inefficiencies are frequently detected late. Staff spend significant time manually reconciling information, preparing reports, identifying root causes, and coordinating corrective actions across departments. Traditional business intelligence tools improve visibility but generally stop at reporting. Standalone AI assistants lack the operational context, system permissions, and governed workflows necessary to execute reliable industrial decisions. For small and medium-sized manufacturers, replacing existing infrastructure with expensive enterprise-wide platforms is often commercially impractical. The resulting inefficiencies can increase operational costs, delay production, create avoidable inventory and material losses, and weaken industrial competitiveness. The challenge is therefore not simply collecting more industrial data. It is converting existing fragmented data into timely, trustworthy, actionable intelligence while preserving investments in current systems.
Solution Overview: Dansen AI develops an AI-native industrial intelligence and execution platform that connects existing enterprise and operational systems into a unified environment for decision-making and governed automation. **How the solution works** 1. **Enterprise integration:** The platform connects ERP and SAP systems, production databases, inventory records, spreadsheets, and operational event streams using APIs, database integrations, and configurable connectors. Information is validated, normalized, and mapped into a consistent operational data model. 2. **Industrial operating graph:** Relationships among suppliers, orders, materials, inventory, production processes, equipment, and responsible personnel are represented in a shared operational context. This enables cross-system reasoning and traceability. 3. **AI-powered intelligence:** Specialized AI agents combine language models, operational rules, structured queries, and retrieval-based reasoning to identify exceptions, investigate root causes, evaluate possible responses, and generate recommendations. 4. **Governed execution:** Recommended interventions are presented to authorized personnel through operational command applications. Actions requiring approval follow role-based access controls, human authorization, and auditable workflows. Approved actions can be executed through supported enterprise integrations. 5. **Continuous monitoring:** Exceptions, production indicators, corrective-action ownership, and outcomes are monitored to support faster escalation and operational improvement. **Technology and deployment methodology** The platform combines enterprise data engineering, large language models, multi-agent orchestration, structured operational reasoning, API integration, event processing, and secure workflow automation. It is designed for modular deployment in customer-approved cloud, on-premises, or hybrid environments. Implementation follows discovery, data mapping, integration, configuration, pilot validation, and phased expansion. **Partnerships and practical validation** Dansen has signed enterprise engagements with Radnik Exports, an Indian garment manufacturer, and Verka (Milkfed Punjab), a dairy cooperative organization. At Radnik, an active customer-data pilot focuses on operational bulletins, production information, and inventory-related exceptions. At Verka, ongoing work focuses on connecting SAP and operational information to support procurement, production, inventory, and quality intelligence. Dansen also developed and presented an automotive supply-chain intelligence demonstrator through the NSRCEL–Maruti Suzuki startup program. Our collaboration model combines customer-provided operational expertise and data access with Dansen's reusable AI platform, engineering capabilities, and configurable industry workflows. Pilots are intended to validate measurable results before wider deployment.
Solution Provider(s): Radnik Exports Private Limited — India-based apparel and technical-textile manufacturer and exporter; enterprise customer and active pilot collaborator providing industrial workflow requirements and customer-data validation. The Punjab State Cooperative Milk Producers' Federation Limited (Milkfed Punjab / Verka) — Indian dairy cooperative federation operating across milk procurement, processing, manufacturing, and distribution; signed enterprise customer collaborating on SAP-integrated operational intelligence and industrial process digitalization.
Implementation location(s): India. 1. Delhi NCR — Radnik Exports: Active enterprise pilot using customer operational data for garment manufacturing, production planning, operational bulletin generation, and inventory intelligence. 2. Punjab — Milkfed Punjab (Verka): Signed enterprise engagement involving SAP-integrated operational intelligence for dairy procurement, manufacturing, inventory, and quality processes. Integration and implementation work is in progress; full production rollout has not yet been confirmed. The platform is currently being validated through these Indian enterprise engagements. Wider geographic deployments are planned but have not yet been implemented.
Implementation timeline(s): 2026–present (ongoing). Radnik Exports: Active customer-data pilot during 2026, with operational validation and enterprise deployment activities ongoing as of October 2026. Milkfed Punjab (Verka): Enterprise engagement and SAP integration activities undertaken during 2026; phased operational deployment remains in progress. No final completion dates or full production go-live dates are claimed at this stage.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Approximately 6–8 weeks for a focused single-site pilot in a new geography, subject to data accessibility, integration complexity, security approvals, and local operational readiness. A narrowly scoped pilot using supported ERP integrations may be technically configured and tested in approximately 3–5 weeks once customer data access and requirements are established. The additional time accommodates local discovery, infrastructure preparation, data validation, deployment approvals, and user acceptance testing. Wider multi-site implementation would follow successful pilot validation.
Desired impact: **Primary objectives** Dansen AI aims to improve industrial productivity, operational resilience, and resource efficiency by transforming fragmented enterprise data into timely intelligence and accountable action. The solution has five primary objectives: 1. Reduce the time required to identify, investigate, and resolve operational exceptions. 2. Improve manufacturing and supply-chain visibility by connecting previously isolated information systems. 3. Reduce avoidable inventory accumulation, material inefficiencies, production delays, and administrative reconciliation. 4. Enable secure, human-supervised AI decision-making within existing industrial infrastructure. 5. Make advanced operational AI more accessible to mid-market industrial enterprises through modular, reusable deployments. **Evidence and emerging impact** At Radnik Exports, operational analysis identified more than USD 100,000 in potential closed-order stock exposure within customer records. The amount represents flagged inventory exposure, not recovered financial value, and remains subject to customer confirmation. The Radnik pilot also targets a reduction in operational bulletin preparation time from approximately 60 minutes to 10–15 minutes, corresponding to a potential 75–83% improvement. This is a target awaiting operational validation, not an achieved result. At Milkfed Punjab, the proposed operational intelligence deployment is designed to improve visibility across procurement, inventory, production, and quality processes. Financial and efficiency benefits remain modelled rather than independently demonstrated. **Impact measurement** Future pilots will assess exception-detection latency, corrective-action resolution time, employee hours released from manual reporting, inventory accuracy, production delays, and material losses. Title: Rosella: AI Copilot for Industrial Risk Engineers
Subtitle: Agentic loss-control workflows that verify readiness before high-risk work begins, with source-linked evidence and enforced human approval.
Problem Statement: Industrial operations lose billions each year to unplanned downtime, equipment failure and process incidents. Many of these losses are preventable on paper: before high-risk work starts, a risk engineer must complete management-of-change reviews and permit readiness checks by gathering evidence from procedures, permits, drawings, prior incidents and audit findings, judging it, documenting it and signing off, often under production pressure. Today that judgment work is slow, hard to trace and dependent on scarce experienced engineers. Approval gates get bypassed because the bottleneck is reading speed, documentation crowds out field time, and institutional knowledge leaves when an engineer retires. The result is losses that surface only after the incident, in downtime, repair cost, insurance premiums and cost of capital.
Solution Overview: Rosella is an AI copilot for industrial risk engineers at operating companies. It works inside the workflows engineers already run, starting with management-of-change (MOC) and permit readiness. Rosella ingests the relevant record (procedures, permits, drawings, prior incidents, audit findings and site documents, including from systems such as SAP, IBM Maximo and SharePoint), assembles the evidence for a decision with every claim linked to its exact source passage, flags what is missing, stale or contradictory, and drafts the decision package for human judgment. Human approval gates are enforced in software: no high-risk work is authorized by the agent. Every action, citation, approval and override is written to an append-only audit log, so any decision can be reconstructed months later. Methodologies and technologies: large-language-model agents with retrieval over governed document stores, provenance-first evidence assembly, deterministic approval-gate enforcement and continuous evaluation of omission and hallucination rates. Partnership and collaboration model: Parakeet deploys with operating companies through 30 to 60 day implementation pilots that convert to per-site managed services, working directly with site risk engineering, operations and EHS leadership. Expansion modules cover PHA action closure, incident write-ups, audit evidence packs and cross-site intelligence.
Solution Provider(s): Frontier Specialty Chemicals — pilot customer and operating partner, specialty chemicals manufacturing, United States.
Implementation location(s): United States (industrial operating sites).
Implementation timeline(s): 2024 to present (ongoing).
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6 to 8 weeks.
Desired impact: Objectives: reduce preventable industrial losses by verifying readiness before high-risk work begins; return documentation time to field work; make every readiness decision auditable. Impact to date: Rosella and the Parakeet platform are deployed with 3 operating-company customers/pilots covering approximately 45,000 workers; a typical site contract is USD 175,000 per year. Each prevented incident avoids unplanned downtime, equipment damage and potential environmental release. Parakeet does not yet publish a quantified GHG-reduction figure; impact is tracked through readiness gaps caught before work starts and engineer hours returned to the field.
Key technologies: Large language model agents; retrieval-augmented generation over governed document stores; document and image extraction; provenance and citation systems; software-enforced approval gates; append-only audit logging; integrations with SAP, IBM Maximo and SharePoint; continuous AI evaluation (omission and hallucination testing).
Unique Characteristics: Provenance as architecture, with every claim linked to its exact source passage. Human approval gates enforced in software rather than by policy. An append-only audit log that lets any decision be reconstructed months later. A deployment model of done-for-you implementation pilots converting to per-site managed services priced on outcomes, not seats. Evaluation discipline: omission and hallucination rates measured rather than asserted.
Sustainable Change: If readiness verification becomes a standard, auditable layer before high-risk work, loss control shifts from after-the-fact investigation to continuous prevention across sites and companies. The same evidence layer improves insurability and the quality of data available to insurers and regulators, and raises the baseline for contractor and permit governance. It is replicable across sectors and geographies because it works from the documents every industrial operator already keeps, and cross-site intelligence compounds the effect: a gap caught at one site becomes a check at every site.
Funding Sources: Parakeet Financial Inc has raised approximately USD 2 million in seed investment from private venture investors. The solution is also funded through customer implementation pilots and per-site managed-services contracts with industrial operating companies.
Primary thematic focus area: Industrial AI Models and Intelligent Decision-Making
Summary: Rosella assembles evidence for management-of-change and permit readiness reviews, links every claim to its source and enforces human approval. The control design is the best part of the submission; measurement and geography are the gaps.
