Title: BYD “God’s Eye”
Subtitle: Technology for Good, Making Intelligent Mobility Accessible to All
Problem Statement: The innovation of BYD's "God's Eye" is reflected in the double breakthroughs of mode and technology: in terms of mode, the intelligent driving popularization path of "whole industry chain collaboration + inclusive pricing", through controlling the whole chain of R & D and production, sinks the intelligent driving assistant system technology to the people-friendly models, breaking the tradition of industry technology stratification; Technically, the "God's Eye" matrix lowers the threshold of use with humanized interaction, enhances user trust with active security protection, and achieves a balance between "advanced technology" and "ease of use".
Solution Overview: BYD's "God's Eye" includes three sets of technical solutions: God's Eye A, God's Eye B and God's Eye C.God's Eye Ais primarily deployed in the YANGWANG brand, God's Eye B is mainly adopted in DENZA and BYD-branded vehicles, while God’s Eye C is deployed across BYD-branded vehicle models. Among these configurations, God’s Eye C is equipped with a front-facing triple-camera perception system featuring 5R12V sensing hardware and an end-to-end control algorithm. It delivers four key technological advantages in system architecture, sensors, algorithms, and data, covering essential driving scenarios that meet users' everyday mobility needs. For highways and urban expressways, Highway Navigation On Autopilot (HNOA) enables vehicles to perform a range of driving tasks along navigation-planned routes, including entering and exiting ramps, lane keeping, cruising, autonomous lane changes, and avoiding or navigating around certain obstacles. In addition, Automated Valet Parking (AVP) provides convenient parking experiences tailored to users' actual parking habits and different scenarios. Its functions include seamless parking upon exiting the vehicle, automatic parking after the vehicle is locked, on-demand retrieval of belongings, and convenient access to the parked vehicle, effectively freeing users from cumbersome procedures such as parking and manually locking their vehicles. Memory-based Navigation On Autopilot (MNOA) is designed for frequently traveled routes, such as daily commutes between home and work. It supports functions including automatic stopping and starting at traffic lights, navigating complex intersections, autonomous overtaking, obstacle avoidance and yielding across various scenarios, and strategic lane changes based on surrounding traffic conditions. By focusing on the driving scenarios that matter most to users, BYD is committed to making the benefits of technological innovation accessible to everyone, enabling all users to enjoy safer, more comfortable, and more convenient mobility. BYD's "God's Eye" system currently maintains commercial partnerships across multiple sectors, including renowned semiconductor companies, leading LiDAR manufacturers, outstanding software and algorithm providers, as well as high-precision mapping and positioning service providers. Looking ahead, as technology continues to advance and market reach expands, BYD may establish partnerships with additional companies dedicated to the research, development, and application of Intelligent Driving Assistance technologies, working together to drive the development of the intelligent driving industry.
Implementation location(s): Global
Implementation timeline(s): BYD's "God's Eye" system was put into use in 2025.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: BYD's "God's Eye" system is expected to roll out across the European market in 2027.
Desired impact: I. Project Background Traditional driving is prone to energy waste caused by frequent acceleration, deceleration and idling. Driver fatigue accounts for 21% of traffic accidents, with an 83% fatality rate. Increasingly diverse driving conditions, urban congestion and inadequate road prediction also lead to operational errors, improper lane changes and inefficient road utilization. Meanwhile, high costs and complex configurations limit intelligent driving technologies to high-end models, hindering technology accessibility. II. Project Maturity and Application Results 2.1 Technological Maturity: Reliable Performance Across All Scenarios God's Eye enables over 1,000 km of highway and expressway driving without driver intervention. Its Automatic Emergency Braking (AEB) reliably stops vehicles at 100 km/h, while its parking success rate reaches 99%. Functions including highway and urban navigation assist, adaptive cruise control and all-terrain recognition cover diverse driving scenarios. Deployed across BYD's global vehicle lineup, the system has demonstrated reliable performance under varied road and climate conditions. 2.2 Market and Sales Performance: Sustained Global Leadership BYD sold 3,131,576 vehicles in the first three quarters of 2026, retaining its leading position in China's automotive market and the global new energy vehicle market. III. Project Impact 3.1 Economic Value: Four Key Contributions God's Eye enhances driving experiences through intelligent navigation and parking assistance; promotes technology accessibility by extending L2 driver assistance across BYD's entire vehicle lineup; supports employment through 120,000 R&D personnel and industrial value chain collaboration; and strengthens market leadership, with 3,131,576 vehicles sold in the first three quarters of 2026. 3.2 Social Responsibility: Three Key Contributions Environmental Protection: Intelligent speed control, adaptive cruise control and optimized power distribution reduce energy waste and emissions, supporting low-carbon mobility. Driving Safety: Over 1,000 km of driving without intervention, reliable braking at 100 km/h and 99% parking success enhance safety and reduce driving risks. Traffic Efficiency: Detecting road conditions up to 200 meters ahead enables optimal route planning, while intelligent parking reduces waiting time and traffic congestion. 3.3 Technological Breakthrough: Mass Production of the 4 nm Xuanji A3 Chip In May 2026, BYD launched China's first automotive-grade 4 nm intelligent driving chip, Xuanji A3. Its three-core NPU supports Transformer-based models. Three chips deliver over 2,100 TOPS of computing power, with 20% lower power consumption per unit of computing performance and 100% higher utilization. Supporting L3/L4 autonomous driving, the chip marks a major technological breakthrough. BYD also has over 3.72 million vehicles equipped with driver assistance systems, generating more than 230 million kilometers of daily driving data to support continuous algorithm optimization. 3.4 Corporate Commitment: Global Pioneer in Dual Safety Guarantees On May 28, 2026, BYD extended its intelligent parking safety guarantee to Urban Navigation Assist. For eligible accidents involving God's Eye A and B under compliant use, BYD fully compensates direct losses, including vehicle repairs, third-party property damage and personal injuries. The guarantee is free, unlimited, excluded from personal insurance claims and does not affect subsequent premiums. BYD thus became the world's only automaker offering dual safety guarantees for intelligent parking and urban navigation assist.
Key technologies: Leveraging BYD’ global manufacturing and sales network, its intelligent driving technologies can be rapidly introduced into different regional markets, extending their social benefits, including energy conservation, emissions reduction, and improved traffic efficiency, to a wider geographical scope. The business model of “cost reduction through full industrial chain integration + affordable pricing” provides a replicable model for other industry players, encouraging the automotive industry as a whole to break down pricing barriers and enabling more consumers to benefit from the safety and convenience of intelligent driving technologies. As an industry leader, BYD’s initiative also encourages more automakers to prioritize inclusive access to technology, accelerating the transformation of automotive intelligence from a premium offering for early adopters to a benefit accessible to all. Reflecting on current practices, continuous efforts are needed to further optimize technological adaptability across different application scenarios. In the next phase, priorities include expanding the coverage of intelligent driving technologies, deepening data collaboration with transportation systems, and improving system stability under complex road conditions. These efforts will extend the benefits of inclusive technology to an even broader range of specialized mobility scenarios and continuously amplify its positive social impact in terms of safety, environmental protection, and traffic efficiency.
Unique Characteristics: Business Model Innovation: Pioneering an Integrated Industrial Chain Collaboration and Affordable Pricing Approach Leveraging its independently controlled capabilities across the entire value chain, from R&D to manufacturing, BYD has pioneered an approach that integrates full industrial chain collaboration with affordable pricing. By extending Intelligent Driving Assistance Systems across its entire vehicle lineup, BYD breaks down traditional technological barriers between market segments, enabling consumers from diverse income groups to benefit from intelligent mobility at accessible prices. Technological Innovation: Comprehensive Scenario Coverage and Integrated Perception Technologies The system integrates functions such as Highway and Expressway Navigation Assistance, Urban Navigation Assistance, and Automatic Emergency Braking (AEB), covering a wide range of scenarios, including highway driving, daily commuting, and parking, while lowering the barriers to adoption for users. Meanwhile, through the integration of LiDAR and visual perception technologies, the system enables advance road condition recognition at distances of up to 200 meters, enhancing system reliability and user confidence while achieving a balance between technological sophistication and ease of use.
Sustainable Change: The popularization of BYD's "God's Eye" is reflected in its global expansion capability and the innovative leadership of the industry model: relying on BYD's global production and sales network, intelligent driving technology can be rapidly extended to different regional markets, so that social values such as environmental protection, energy saving and improving traffic efficiency can be realized in a broader scope; The "whole industry chain cost reduction + inclusive pricing" model provides a replicable model for the same industry, promotes the industry as a whole to break price barriers, and enables more consumers to enjoy the safety and convenience brought by intelligent driving technology.

Title: AI-Powered Enzymatic PET Recycling for Sustainable Manufacturing
Subtitle: AI enzyme design, automated experiments and process optimization turn waste PET bottles and polyester textiles into high-purity rPTA, advancing circularity and sustainable industrial development.
Problem Statement: Waste PET bottle flakes and polyester textile waste are difficult to return consistently to high-value material cycles. Mechanical recycling may reduce material performance and limit the range of suitable feedstocks. Chemical depolymerization often requires high temperatures, elevated pressures or catalysts, increasing energy demand and pollution-control requirements. Enzymatic recycling offers a milder depolymerization route, but industrial application remains constrained by enzyme activity, thermal stability, performance on substrates with medium to high crystallinity, and enzyme production costs. Conventional screening of naturally occurring enzymes and random mutagenesis often take years and struggle to optimize these properties simultaneously. The industry needs an integrated, scalable recycling solution that connects enzyme design, fermentation-based enzyme production, waste PET hydrolysis and recycled monomer quality control.
Solution Overview: Led by Shanghai Matwings Technology Co., Ltd., in collaboration with Shanghai Jiawu Technology Co., Ltd. and Chongqing Jiawu Technology Co., Ltd., the solution is built on high-quality data and specialized protein foundation models, with the MatwingsVenus® agent providing the user interface and a lights-out laboratory providing automated experimental validation. It integrates enzyme design, experimental validation, process optimization and industrial application to convert waste PET bottle flakes and polyester textile waste into high-purity recycled terephthalic acid (rPTA), supporting high-value resource recovery and sustainable industrial development. Matwings brings together public databases, sequences from extreme environments such as the deep sea and salt lakes, literature and real experimental feedback. Its data foundation draws on tens of billions of protein-related data records and annotations, linked to fermentation and hydrolysis process data. The proprietary MatwingsVenus® protein foundation model supports PET hydrolase discovery, sequence design, directed evolution and multi-objective screening. It jointly optimizes catalytic activity, thermal stability, performance on substrates with medium to high crystallinity, rPTA yield, expressibility and scalability. The MatwingsVenus® platform provides a closed-loop agent system linking computational design with wet-lab experimentation. It integrates more than 500 specialized protein design tools and more than 60 domain Skills refined by experts. Natural-language interaction supports knowledge retrieval, function prediction, candidate design and experimental task orchestration, while a proprietary central control system schedules the automated wet-lab platform. Candidate enzymes undergo expression, purification and activity testing. Positive results, negative results and records of technical failures are quality-controlled, traced to their sources and categorized before being fed back to expand datasets and support model post-training, evaluation and the next design cycle. This creates a computational and experimental closed loop driven by real experimental feedback. Process models draw on data from multiple fermentation and hydrolysis batches to optimize enzyme production conditions and depolymerization parameters. PET hydrolysis is carried out at atmospheric pressure and 55–65°C, followed by product recovery and purification. Process recommendations are verified through experiments or operating data before implementation. Production data are continuously fed back to support operating-condition analysis, consistent product quality and process improvement. Shanghai Matwings Technology is responsible for data, models and automated experimental systems, coordinating core enzyme R&D and iterative improvement through the closed loop. Chongqing Jiawu Technology is responsible for validating PET hydrolysis and downstream recovery processes, process scale-up and production implementation, supporting stable operation and validation in customer applications. Shanghai Jiawu Technology serves as the trading and sales entity, managing product sales, business coordination and commercial partnerships. Experimental and production data, together with feedback from customer applications, return to Matwings to support continued improvement of models, processes and products.
Solution Provider(s): Shanghai Jiawu Technology Co., Ltd., a wholly owned subsidiary of Shanghai Matwings Technology, serves as the trading and sales entity. It manages sales of rPTA and related products, business coordination and commercial partnerships, connecting product supply with downstream application needs. Chongqing Jiawu Technology Co., Ltd., a subsidiary of Shanghai Matwings Technology, focuses on biological recycling of waste polymers. It is responsible for validating PET hydrolysis and downstream recovery processes, process scale-up and production implementation, supporting stable operation and validation in customer applications.
Implementation location(s): Shanghai, China: Shanghai Matwings Technology develops the high-quality data infrastructure, protein foundation models and the MatwingsVenus® agent platform for closed-loop computational design and automated wet-lab experimentation, and conducts experimental validation. Shanghai Jiawu Technology manages trading, sales, business coordination and commercial partnerships. Changshou District, Chongqing, China: Chongqing Jiawu Technology undertakes validation of PET hydrolysis and downstream recovery processes, process scale-up, production implementation and validation in customer applications.
Implementation timeline(s): Demonstration validation, process optimization and scale-up are continuing in 2026. The project remains ongoing.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: An initial pilot at a partner facility with suitable equipment and infrastructure is preliminarily estimated to take 3–6 months, depending on feedstock characterization, equipment conditions, local approvals and partner readiness. A new installation would require a separate engineering and construction schedule.
Desired impact: The solution aims to establish a replicable technological route from waste PET and polyester textile waste to high-quality recycled monomers, improve enzyme R&D and process development efficiency, and support circular use of plastics and textile materials. The project has reported the following process and product outcomes. At atmospheric pressure and 55–65°C, PET degradation exceeds 90% within 16 hours, and rPTA purity reaches 99% or higher. Energy use in the enzyme-catalysis step is reduced by approximately 55%, and enzyme production costs by approximately 67%. AI-assisted enzyme optimization has shortened R&D from 3–5 years to 2–6 months, reduced process scale-up time by approximately 80% and improved production efficiency by approximately 5%–10%. In the performance comparison, the enzyme activity assay readout increased from 2.0 to 6.8 mM. Product formation after 72 hours of heat treatment at 65°C, used as an indicator of thermal stability, increased from 0.2 to 5.5 mM. rPTA quality testing recorded 6.3 ppm 4-carboxybenzaldehyde, 15.5 ppm p-toluic acid and an acid value of 674.5 mg KOH/g. The enzyme activity readout thus reached 3.4 times its baseline value, while the thermal-stability assay readout increased by 2,650%. The levels of 4-carboxybenzaldehyde and p-toluic acid impurities in PTA were reduced by 67% and 87%, respectively. The project has completed validation of a demonstration line for enzymatic rPTA production with an annual capacity of 400 tonnes and obtained Global Recycled Standard (GRS) certification for its pilot production line. Further capacity scale-up is ongoing to increase the value recovered from waste materials and support recycled monomer supply and regional circular value chains.
Key technologies: High-quality data governance and model training: The MatwingsVenus® Pod data foundation integrates public protein data, sequences from extreme environments, functional annotations and real experimental feedback, with more than 10 billion records. Data are managed in raw, standardized and high-confidence tiers, with cleaning and deduplication, label alignment, unit standardization, evidence traceability and version control. Training, validation and test sets are kept separate to support pre-training, function-supervised learning and post-training driven by real feedback. Protein function prediction and intelligent design: Proprietary protein foundation models combine function-supervised learning, adaptation using small datasets and active learning to support PET hydrolase discovery, sequence design, directed evolution and multi-objective screening. Candidate evaluation incorporates catalytic activity, thermal stability, substrate compatibility, expression and scale-up requirements. Research agents and automated experiments: The MatwingsVenus® platform integrates more than 500 specialized design tools and more than 60 domain Skills refined by experts. Natural-language interaction enables scientific task interpretation, tool invocation and experimental orchestration. A proprietary central control system connects automated gene synthesis, plasmid construction, culture expansion and protein purification in the lights-out laboratory, together with candidate enzyme activity testing and data feedback, forming a closed loop of design, validation and learning. Fermentation and hydrolysis process modeling: Batch process records are combined with data on temperature, pH, dissolved oxygen, feed rate and hydrolysis conversion to analyze relationships between process conditions, enzyme output, conversion and product quality. This supports operating-condition assessment and parameter optimization. Experimental measurements and model predictions are labeled separately. Model-generated process recommendations are verified through experiments or operating data before implementation.
Unique Characteristics: Integration of data and function-oriented design. A protein data foundation combining public data and proprietary sequences from extreme environments draws on annotations and continuously returned experimental results to support enzyme discovery and design around functional requirements. The dataset has been selected as a typical case of high-quality datasets by the National Data Administration of China. The models jointly optimize activity, stability, substrate compatibility, expression and performance during scale-up, connecting molecular design with industrial application requirements. Agents translate model capabilities into executable R&D workflows. MatwingsVenus® integrates specialized tools and domain Skills, using natural-language interaction to connect knowledge retrieval, candidate design and experimental orchestration. A proprietary central control system links these tasks to automated execution in the lights-out laboratory, creating an R&D system that covers computational design, wet-lab validation and data feedback. The automated experimental platform supports 24/7 operation, providing a basis for continuous design and validation. Real feedback drives continuous model improvement. Quality-controlled, traceable and categorized experimental data are used to expand datasets and support model evaluation and post-training. Positive results, negative results and records of technical failures retain their scientific or technical context. Fermentation and hydrolysis process data further calibrate process models, allowing model optimization to draw on actual production feedback and linking it to rPTA quality and process performance. Coordination across R&D, production and sales. Matwings provides data, models, agents and automated validation capabilities. Chongqing Jiawu undertakes process scale-up and production implementation, while Shanghai Jiawu manages trading, sales and business coordination. Together, they connect research capabilities, product supply and downstream demand. Data, models and platform capabilities can be reused in subsequent enzyme and process development, providing a foundation for replication and wider industrial application.
Sustainable Change: The solution could connect PET monomer recovery with circular material use by linking upstream collection and sorting, industrial enzyme production, hydrolysis and purification with downstream polymerization, spinning and packaging, increasing the value recovered from waste. Continuous experimental and process feedback can improve models and processes and reduce development effort for new feedstocks and subsequent pilots. Cooperation with local recyclers, chemical companies and research institutions could combine local waste resources with specialized AI enzyme design capabilities for staged feedstock assessment, pilot validation and scale-up. This could establish regional recycled monomer supply and improve the ability to manage feedstock variability through process parameter optimization. The platform could also support exploration of enzymatic recycling of other polymers, including nylon.
Primary thematic focus area: Industrial AI Models and Intelligent Decision-Making

Name of your organization: BEYONDDATA INFORMATION COMMUNICATION TECHNOLOGY LTD (BEYONDDATA ICT)
Title: BSF AI Hub: Industrial AI for Circular Aquaculture & Insect Protein
Subtitle: An AI-powered operating system that converts organic waste into insect protein and fish feed, monitoring water quality, predicting harvests, and connecting farmers to markets across East Africa.
Problem Statement: East Africa's aquaculture and livestock sectors face three interconnected industrial challenges: 1. Feed insecurity and cost. Commercial fish and poultry feed accounts for 60–87% of production costs for smallholder farmers. Protein inputs fishmeal and soybean meal are imported, expensive, and volatile. Kenya alone has a fish deficit of approximately 500,000 metric tonnes, bridged by imports. In the Lake Victoria Basin, 90% of farmers do not produce their own fingerlings, and the country has a 100-million fingerling annual deficit. 2. Waste and environmental degradation. Kenya generates millions of tonnes of organic waste annually. Most is landfilled or dumped, emitting methane (28× more potent than CO₂) and contaminating waterways. Meanwhile, Black Soldier Fly (BSF) larvae which can convert this waste into 37-63% protein meal and organic fertilizer are underutilised because farmers lack the technical knowledge, records, and market connections to operate profitably. 3. Fish mortality and water quality blindness. In Lake Victoria, 40% of cage farmers experienced a large-scale fish kill in the last year. Fish kills are triggered by upwelling events natural, seasonal rises of oxygen-depleted deep water occurring every May, June, September, and October. Farmers cannot detect the drop in dissolved oxygen until fish are already dying. Only 2% disinfect tools between cages; 59% dispose of dead fish into the lake. The result is catastrophic losses and food safety risks. The gap is not a lack of technology it is the absence of an integrated, industrial-grade digital infrastructure that connects waste sources, BSF production, fish farming, water quality monitoring, and market access into one traceable value chain.
Solution Overview: BSF AI Hub is an AI-powered digital operating system for the circular bioeconomy. It has two integrated modules: BSF Module manages Black Soldier Fly production from egg to harvest, tracking batches, feedstock quality, feeding, mortality, and frass output. FishOS Module manages fish farming (pond and cage) with water quality monitoring, feeding records, growth tracking, and fish marketplace. The platform is live in production at bsfaihub.beyonddataict.com. How it works 1. Farm Records. Farmers record stocking, feeding, mortality, sampling, and harvest on a mobile-first PWA that works offline. Every batch gets a unique ID for traceability. 2. Water Intelligence. IoT sensors (dissolved oxygen, temperature, pH, turbidity, ammonia) stream readings to the platform. Copernicus Sentinel-2 satellite data provides chlorophyll-a and turbidity proxies for algal bloom detection. The system compares readings against species-specific thresholds and generates real-time alerts. 3. AI Advisory. A RAG-based advisor answers farmer questions using approved fisheries and BSF knowledge plus the farmer's own records. Vision-based health checks analyze uploaded photos of larvae or fish. 4. Marketplace. Farmers list fish, larvae, and frass. Buyers post requirements. Orders flow through the platform with traceability from farm to buyer. 5. Traceability. Every product links to a batch, which links to a farm, which links to water quality history. QR-scannable Farm Passports let buyers verify provenance. They train youth in BSF farming and have partnered with over 2,000 smallholder farmers. WorldFish (CASA project) -Hydro Victoria serves as operational contractor for the Climate Resilient Aquaculture Systems for Africa project. Ethical Seafood Research -Partnership to strengthen animal welfare standards in Kenyan aquaculture. Konza Technopolies - Government AI Infrastructure Providers
Solution Provider(s): Hydro Victoria Africa - Regenerative aquaculture and circular economy social enterprise based in Busia and Kilifi, Kenya. Operates 3 hatcheries, 45 fish cages, 64 nursery ponds; produces 1.5 million fingerlings/year and 30 tonnes of table-size fish annually; trains youth in BSF farming; partnered with 2,000+ smallholder farmers; supports WorldFish's Climate Resilient Aquaculture Systems for Africa (CASA) project., Konza Technopolies - Government AI Infrastructure Providers
Implementation location(s): Kenya - Busia County (Hydro Victoria flagship farm), Kilifi County (regenerative farm), and Lake Victoria Basin counties (Kisumu, Homa Bay, Siaya). The platform is also accessible globally via bsfaihub.beyonddataict.com.
Implementation timeline(s): Current deployment: September 2026 – ongoing (production). , FishOS pilot: October 2026 – June 2027.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3– 6 Months for a new East African geography (Uganda, Tanzania) with the same physical infrastructure. Key requirements: local partner with existing farmer network (like Hydro Victoria), 3–5 IoT sensor kits, farmer onboarding workshops, and integration with local market buyers. The platform itself is geography-agnostic only the partner network and pilot farmers need to be established.
Desired impact: Enable smallholder farmers to operate profitable BSF and fish farming enterprises using digital records and AI advisory. Reduce fish mortality from water quality events through IoT and satellite early warning. Close the circular loop: waste to BSF larvae to fish feed to fish to waste. Connect farmers directly to buyers through a traceable marketplace. Provide ESOs and funders with verified impact data for reporting. The solution is designed to deliver measurable impact across environmental, economic, and social dimensions. In the pilot phase, we expect to divert over 50 tonnes of organic waste per month from landfill, building on Hydro Victoria's current processing capacity, and to produce approximately 5 tonnes of BSF larvae per month as that network scales toward 1,000 farmers. By replacing commercial fish feed with BSF larvae a substitution that matters because feed represents 60-87% of production costs we anticipate reducing feed costs for participating farmers by 20-40%. Early warning of hypoxia events, informed by research such as the King's College London pilot that detected oxygen depletion hours before fish deaths, is expected to reduce fish mortality by 15-30% and to avert at least one fish kill event per pilot farm per year. Each tonne of waste diverted from landfill avoids approximately 0.5 kg CO₂e through methane avoidance, contributing to climate mitigation. On the economic and social side, the pilot is expected to create 50 or more direct and indirect jobs through Hydro Victoria's youth training programmes and the new enterprises the platform enables, while generating at least KES 15,000 per month in additional income per participating farmer, based on current marketplace pricing for tilapia and BSF larvae. Together, these outcomes demonstrate a solution that is not only technically deployable but economically and environmentally transformative at the farm, community, and ecosystem levels.
Key technologies: Artificial Intelligence (AI): Google Gemini for chat, vision, and embeddings; RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) with pgvector for grounded advisory; computer vision for BSF health checks. Internet of Things (IoT): ESP32 microcontrollers; dissolved oxygen, temperature, pH, turbidity, ammonia sensors; solar-powered field kits. Earth Observation (EO): Copernicus Sentinel-2 for chlorophyll-a and turbidity proxies; NDWI for water body detection. Blockchain (planned): Batch-level traceability for export certification. Digital Twins (planned): Predictive modelling of fish growth and pond dynamics. Mobile PWA: Offline-first, mobile-first, works on low-end Android phones. Satellite Weather: Open-Meteo for daily forecasts per farm location.
Unique Characteristics: Full value chain, not a slice. Competitors solve one problem water quality monitoring (Constantnople), feed marketplace (Aquarech), or records (FAI). BSF AI Hub connects records to water to AI to marketplace to traceability in one platform. Circular economy by design. The platform's core logic is a loop: waste to BSF larvae to fish feed to fish to waste. No other platform closes this loop. AI that knows the farm. The RAG advisor uses the farmer's own batch records, water quality history, and approved fisheries knowledge not generic internet answers. Every answer cites its sources. Computer vision for BSF health. The platform uses Gemini plus our fine tuned model Vision to analyze larvae photos and return structured health assessments a capability no competitor offers. Copernicus satellite integration. Chlorophyll-a and turbidity from Sentinel-2 complement in-situ sensors, providing early warning of algal blooms across the lake. Traceability as a market differentiator. Farm Passports with QR codes let buyers verify the origin, water quality history, and production practices of every fish a requirement for export and institutional buyers. Partnership model. Working with Hydro Victoria Africa gives immediate access to 5,000+ smallholder farmers, 3 hatcheries, 45 cages, and existing BSF training programmes. The platform is not starting from zero it is the digital layer on top of an operational network.
Sustainable Change: BSF AI Hub is designed to become the digital infrastructure for East Africa's circular bioeconomy. The systemic change pathway: Phase 1 - Prove the model in the Lake Victoria Basin. 10 pilot farms (5 BSF, 5 fish) demonstrate reduced mortality, lower feed costs, and increased income. Data is verified and published. Phase 2 - Scale through partner networks. Hydro Victoria's 2,000+ farmers are onboarded. The platform becomes the standard digital layer for BSF and fish farming in Kenya. Expansion to Uganda and Tanzania through similar partner networks. Phase 3 - Integrate with policy and finance. The verified impact data (waste diverted, fish mortality reduced, income generated) becomes the evidence base for county and national government programmes, carbon market eligibility, and impact investment. Phase 4 - Circular economy OS. The platform connects every actor in the value chain waste suppliers, BSF farmers, fish farmers, processors, buyers, ESOs into one traceable, AI-optimised ecosystem. Waste becomes a tracked resource, not a disposal cost. Protein becomes locally produced, not imported. Fish becomes traceable, not anonymous. At scale, the platform could support: 2–18 million tonnes of organic waste recycled annually (Kenya BSF potential) USD 69-687 million annual BSF feed market value Up to 252,000 jobs created across the value chain The systemic change is a shift from linear, import-dependent, opaque food systems to circular, locally-powered, traceable ones.
Funding Sources: The platform has been developed to date with founder capital and bootstrapped resources. No external grant funding has been received. The Accelerator programme funding (if selected) would be used for: IoT sensor kits, field travel, farmer training, and pilot deployment.

Title: JAC Automotive Industrial Vision Quality Inspection System Based on CV Large Models
Subtitle: Jointly developed by JAC Group and Huawei, this solution addresses the automotive manufacturing industry's challenges of numerous inspection scenarios, frequent model changeovers, and long per-scenario development cycles of traditional small models, delivering a full-process AI quality inspection solution based on a CV foundation model. Leveraging the strong generalization capability of the CV foundation model, the solution rapidly trains high-precision scenario models from a small number of on-site images, reducing the repetitive custom development workload for new scenarios and supporting the rapid rollout and scaled application of models across multiple scenarios. To date, the solution has been partially deployed at the JAC MAEXTRO Super Factory in Hefei, China, with more than 1,600 AI inspection points covering stamping, welding, painting, general assembly, and rework, and the deployment scope will continue to expand. Meanwhile, it is being replicated to JAC Group's light truck plant and engine plant, with plans to extend it to core suppliers later if conditions allow.
Problem Statement: As new energy vehicles become increasingly electrified and intelligent, the number of electrical and electronic components inside vehicles continues to grow, and quality inspection faces challenges such as numerous inspection scenarios, rapid vehicle model changes, and long cycles for building inspection capabilities. ① Numerous inspection scenarios, with complex inspection targets and defect forms. The electrical architecture of new energy vehicles is far more complex. Taking JAC Group's MAEXTRO S800 model as an example, the number of connectors has increased from just over 100 in traditional internal-combustion models to more than 500, with over 2,000 inspection points per vehicle. Inspection targets include not only connectors but also nameplates and regulatory labels: the system must identify mis-insertion, missing insertion, and loose insertion of connectors as well as missing or damaged components, and must also check for label character errors and positional misalignment. The large number of inspection targets and the variety of defect forms place higher demands on inspection efficiency and judgment consistency. ② Frequent model changeovers and production line adjustments require inspection capabilities to be updated in sync. When a new model is introduced or a production line undergoes technical upgrades, component specifications, mounting positions, and inspection requirements may change, and existing models need to be re-adapted and re-validated. With a changeover cycle of roughly one month for new models, if the relevant inspection models cannot be adjusted in time, the launch of new processes and the production ramp-up of new models may be affected. ③ Traditional small models are customized scenario by scenario, requiring substantial development and maintenance investment. Conventional AI quality inspection typically requires images to be collected and annotated, and models to be trained and tuned separately for each scenario, making it difficult to fully reuse model capabilities across scenarios. Under the previous development model, for example, developing 150 inspection scenarios required six AI engineers working for about nine months. As vehicle models and inspection points increase, the workload of repetitive development, sample preparation, and subsequent maintenance grows accordingly, making it difficult to meet the demand for rapid multi-scenario rollout. These issues add pressure to quality management and model development, and may affect the introduction schedule of new models. Similar challenges also exist in new energy vehicle component manufacturing and other high-variety manufacturing scenarios.
Solution Overview: To address the challenges of numerous inspection scenarios, frequent model changeovers, and heavy repetitive development of small models in automotive quality inspection, this solution builds an industrial AI quality inspection system based on a CV foundation model. It first establishes an industry model reusable across automotive inspection tasks, then rapidly adapts scenario models using each workstation's on-site photos and inspection standards, eliminating the need to develop every scenario from scratch. ① A reusable automotive-industry CV foundation model. Building on Huawei's CV foundation model, JAC Group conducts continued training with the 1.3 million high-quality industrial images it has accumulated, forming the "MAEXTRO" industry CV quality-inspection foundation model. By learning the visual features of inspection objects and defects such as connectors, pipelines, bolts, adhesive applications, and nameplates, the model accumulates recognition capabilities reusable across scenarios. ② Rapid scenario-model development with few on-site photos. When a workstation is added or the vehicle model changes, developers collect and annotate on-site photos according to the new inspection objects and judgment criteria, then fine-tune the "MAEXTRO" industry model to obtain a task-specific scenario model. Because learned features are reused, a typical scenario needs only 50–100 photos, and training a new scenario model takes about one day on average. ③ A unified platform lowers development and usage barriers. Image annotation, model training, evaluation, and release are integrated into one workflow, letting factory AI developers reuse existing industry models and tools for specific workstations and reducing reliance on specialized algorithm expertise. Process and quality staff take part in defining inspection standards, reviewing samples, and validating results. ④ Closing the quality loop through production-system integration. Deployed models inspect in real time the images captured by workstation cameras or handheld terminals. When a problem is found (e.g., a wire harness connector missing or not fully inserted), the terminal prompts the worker to recheck; confirmed issues are reassembled and re-inspected until passing. Through integration completed by the line integrator, the system sends blocking logs to the factory's existing MES, and rework and re-inspection records are archived for the existing QMS to perform root-cause and early-warning analysis. False alarms and unknown-anomaly images are annotated after human review, added to the defect sample library for model retraining by JAC Group, and validated models are updated back onto the line. ⑤ Partners and collaboration model. Huawei provides the foundation model, computing resources, and the AI development platform procured by JAC Group, along with training and enablement; the line integrator handles line deployment and MES/QMS integration; JAC Group provides industry data, process knowledge, and on-site validation, leads model iteration, and owns the resulting industry model. ⑥ Responsible AI application. 1) AI assists decision-making; humans make the final judgment. AI only flags suspected defects. It is confirmed through workers' rechecks whether a defect or rework exists. 2) False alarms are confirmed by rechecks, recorded, and flow back for model improvement via the process in point ④. 3) Data governance: JAC Group has set up a dedicated data governance team; image data is used only for quality inspection, traceability, and model improvement; annotations enter the training set only after review by process and quality staff; training data, model versions, and release records are managed for traceability; future rollout to suppliers’ factories will clarify data ownership and scope of use through agreements and comply with local laws and regulations. 4) Worker privacy: inspection photography targets vehicles; quality-inspection images are not used for employee monitoring.
Solution Provider(s): Organization: Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd. Founded in 1987, Huawei is a leading global provider of information and communications technology (ICT) infrastructure and smart devices. Huawei has approximately 213,000 employees and operates in more than 170 countries and regions, serving more than 3 billion people around the world. Huawei is committed to bringing digital to every person, home and organization for a fully connected, intelligent world.
Implementation location(s): Hefei City, Anhui Province, China
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6 months
Desired impact: Focused on automotive manufacturing quality and production-line adaptability, this solution has already produced, and is expected to continue producing, the following impacts: ① Improving product quality and reducing after-sales quality risks. Since its deployment at the JAC MAEXTRO Super Factory, the solution has cumulatively detected more than 200 defect issues. Taking the wire harness insertion inspection scenario as an example, the actual defect missed-detection rate is 0.01%. For vehicle assembly quality issues, prompt on-site confirmation and timely rework help prevent defects from flowing into downstream processes and the market, reducing customer usage risks and the enterprise's after-sales repair costs. ② Accelerating production-line adaptation and supporting mass production of new models. The JAC MAEXTRO Super Factory initially adopted a scenario-by-scenario development mode using small models such as YOLO: developing 150 inspection scenarios required six AI engineers working for about nine months. Under the new solution, a typical scenario needs only 50–100 on-site photos for fine-tuning, with model accuracy reaching above 99.9%, and training a model for a new scenario takes about one day on average. Compared with traditional small-model solutions, the verification cycle after quality-inspection model changes during production-line changeovers is shortened by 70%, enabling new inspection capabilities to be put into use faster and supporting mass-production preparation and capacity ramp-up for new models. When quality-inspection verification is the critical bottleneck constraining mass production, and conditions such as orders and capacity are in place, the solution can drive earlier mass production and delivery of new models, realizing the related revenue sooner. ③ Reducing rework, after-sales repair, and related resource consumption. Timely detection and handling of manufacturing defects help reduce subsequent disassembly and reassembly, repeated rework, and damage to components, and are expected to save the labor hours and materials required for rework and lower energy consumption in the rework process. As more defects are intercepted before leaving the factory, after-sales repairs and recalls for the same types of issues will also decrease, along with the corresponding consumption of spare parts and the resource consumption and emissions in logistics activities such as the round-trip transportation of vehicles and spare parts. ④ Assisting frontline workers and promoting skill development and career transition. The solution is positioned to assist workers: AI flags suspected defects, while workers are responsible for reconfirmation and rework handling. AI-assisted defect identification helps relieve workers from item-by-item visual inspection across large numbers of inspection points, allowing them to devote more energy to reconfirmation, rework, and process issue analysis. As the CV foundation model lowers the difficulty of scenario development, JAC Group is training frontline workers and process and quality staff to take part in sample preparation, model adaptation, and effectiveness verification, and plans to provide development pathways for personnel engaged in repetitive visual inspection toward roles such as AI result reconfirmation, sample annotation, and model validation. This is expected to help employees familiar with on-site processes master AI application skills, raise the skill level of frontline positions, and broaden career development opportunities.
Key technologies: The solution primarily adopts the following two categories of technologies: ① CV vision foundation model technology. The solution uses Huawei's Pangu CV foundation model, based on a Transformer vision network architecture, as its base model. With a parameter scale of 7B, the base model is pretrained on large volumes of image and video data, learning visual features that can be reused across different tasks and enhancing generalization to new scenarios. Specifically, the Transformer correlates information from different regions of an image through self-attention mechanisms, helping the model combine local details with overall structure to identify components and their assembly states. Through targeted adaptation, the model's capabilities can be applied to tasks such as image classification, object detection, and image segmentation, which are respectively used to determine whether anomalies exist, locate targets or defects, and identify defect regions. ② Industry continued-training and scenario fine-tuning technology. Building on Huawei's Pangu CV foundation model, JAC Group conducts continued training with the high-quality industrial images it has accumulated, forming the "MAEXTRO" industry CV quality-inspection foundation model for automotive quality inspection, which strengthens the model's ability to recognize features of automotive components and production defects. After deployment, for each specific workstation, a small number of on-site photos is used to fine-tune the industry model, producing a scenario model suited to that workstation; a typical scenario requires only 50–100 on-site photos, and training a model for a new scenario takes about one day on average. By reusing the visual capabilities already learned by the base model and the industry model, the solution reduces the repetitive sample preparation and custom development work for different workstations that was required under the traditional small-model approach, lowers the difficulty of scenario-model development, and supports faster rollout of new quality-inspection scenarios.
Unique Characteristics: This solution transforms quality-inspection experience in automotive manufacturing into reusable CV quality-inspection foundation model capabilities, lowers the barrier to scenario-model development through workflow-based tooling, and explores commercial applications across the automotive industry chain. The conventional approach typically collects and annotates images separately for each scenario and trains a small model from scratch; this solution differs in two key ways: it replaces scenario-by-scenario training from scratch with an automotive-industry quality-inspection foundation model plus fine-tuning on a small number of on-site samples, and connects inspection results to production handling and model iteration, forming a closed quality loop. Its innovation and differentiation are reflected in the following four aspects: ① Building an automotive-industry CV quality-inspection foundation model and reusing inspection capabilities across scenarios. In JAC Group's previous quality-inspection solution based on small models such as YOLO (a commonly used type of lightweight object-detection model), adding a new workstation typically required collecting samples, developing, and training models separately, with a heavy workload of sample preparation and customization. This solution uses Huawei's CV foundation model as the base and conducts continued training with JAC Group's own industrial images, forming the "MAEXTRO" automotive-industry CV quality-inspection foundation model, which accumulates visual recognition capabilities for automotive components, assembly states, and defects for reuse across different processes, vehicle models, and workstations. For a new scenario, only adaptation on top of the industry model is needed, with no training from scratch: a typical scenario is fine-tuned with 50–100 on-site photos, and training a model for a new scenario takes about one day on average. ② Adopting workflow-based development to lower the barrier to building scenario models. Through a unified development platform (part of the AI development platform that JAC Group procured from Huawei), the solution organizes sample annotation, model fine-tuning, effectiveness evaluation, and model release into workflows, with no coding required for the main steps. Developers follow the workflows to reuse the industry model and adapt it to specific workstations, reducing repetitive algorithm development and debugging and enabling factories to rapidly build AI inspection capabilities across multiple workstations. ③ Turning the industry model into an asset that JAC Group can offer externally. "MAEXTRO" is the external brand of JAC Group's automotive-industry CV quality-inspection foundation model. The model was jointly developed by JAC Group and Huawei: JAC Group provided the industrial data and process knowledge required for training, and the model's intellectual property rights belong to JAC Group. By accumulating production data and quality-inspection experience into a reusable industry model, JAC Group can not only serve its own factories but also has the foundation to offer related capabilities to the industry chain. JAC Group has formulated an external commercialization plan and intends to sell the model to other automotive OEMs and component plants, helping more enterprises adapt their own quality-inspection scenarios on top of an existing industry model and reducing their investment in repetitive development. ④ Connecting production quality handling with continuous model iteration. The solution connects AI inspection to production control and quality traceability systems: suspected defects trigger worker rechecks and rework, handling records enter MES and QMS, and reviewed false alarms and anomaly samples flow back for use by JAC Group in model iteration. In this way, on-site quality management and model optimization reinforce each other, forming a closed loop.
Sustainable Change: This solution is deployed at scale at the JAC MAEXTRO Super Factory, with further expansion planned. Its systemic value lies in accumulating automotive manufacturing's visual-inspection experience into reusable industry models and development methodologies, letting factories adapt their quality-inspection scenarios on this foundation and moving AI quality inspection from repetitive scenario-by-scenario development to broader capability reuse. ① Accumulating factory practice into sustainably reusable capabilities. In daily production, the closed quality loop accumulates reviewed inspection, rework, and re-inspection records and false-alarm and anomaly samples, supporting quality traceability, issue analysis, and model iteration. As vehicle models and processes change, the accumulated industry model, scenario-adaptation methodology, and on-site handling experience guides new workstations and factories, reducing repetitive exploration. ② Replicating from one factory to different manufacturing operations. The solution is being rolled out at JAC Group's light truck plant and engine plant, validating applicability across products, processes, and inspection targets. During rollout, the industry model and development tools are reused, adapting scenario models to each factory's on-site photos, imaging conditions, and quality standards. As experience accumulates, JAC Group will gradually build AI quality-inspection capabilities spanning factories and processes. ③ Driving adoption across the supply chain. JAC Group plans to replicate the solution to one to three core upstream suppliers' factories, extending reach from one OEM to supply-chain. To enable replication across enterprises and regions, JAC Group plans three mechanisms: 1) Standardized delivery package. Industry models and scenario-model templates, photo collection and annotation specifications, judgment criteria, workflow development methodology, model release validation specifications, on-site quality handling procedures, and training materials form a standardized package reusable across enterprises. 2) Supplier enablement. Starting from common inspection scenarios, JAC Group provides adaptation and validation support; suppliers fine-tune the model with their on-site photos and, through training, gradually learn to use and maintain the system independently. For manufacturers, adapting with few on-site photos and no coding for the main steps lowers the barrier to adopting AI quality inspection without a full AI team. When upstream enterprises catch defects earlier, fewer defective components enter downstream assembly, reducing rework and material losses. ④ Lowering the barrier to industry adoption and encouraging cross-industry learning. Since the scenario-model development platform's main steps require no coding, personnel familiar with on-site processes can, after training, contribute to sample preparation, model adaptation, and effectiveness verification, helping manufacturers without full AI teams gradually build application capabilities. Inspection needs such as connectors, adhesive application, and label verification have similar scenarios in electronics and equipment manufacturing; with supplemented industry samples, model adaptation, and on-site verification, rollout to other industries can be explored.
Funding Sources: Self-funded
Primary thematic focus area: Industrial AI Models and Intelligent Decision-Making
Summary: JAC and Huawei put a 7 billion parameter vision model into quality inspection at the MAEXTRO super factory and replaced scenario-by-scenario model building with fine-tuning on a few dozen photographs. The engineering record is among the strongest here and the submission gives the Jury nothing to look at, which is where the lost points are.
Thematic focus areas (as submitted): Embodied AI, Industrial Robotics and Smart Manufacturing; Industrial AI Models and Intelligent Decision-Making

Title: Talent Bridge: AI-Powered Skills-to-Jobs Pipeline for Creative Industries
Subtitle: CreativeTech’s AI-assessed training feeds Talent Bridge’s skills-matching platform, connecting Central Asian creative-tech talent with internships and jobs in Uzbekistan and Europe.
Problem Statement: Uzbekistan’s creative and digital industries (games, animation, creative technology) are growing under a creative industires policy framework to 2030. Their growth is limited by a skills and market-access gap. Training is fragmented, graduates cannot show comparable evidence of their skills, and employers cannot easily find or trust talent from the region. The result is that young professionals go unemployed, work below their qualification level, or leave. Studios also cannot find job-ready people, and recognised pathways to international employers barely exist.
Solution Overview: The solution has two linked layers, both run by the Uzbekistan Creative Association (UzCA), an industry body representing 40+ studios. CreativeTech (training layer). This is a digital skills programme with six areas of study. AI is used across the curriculum and in performance analysis and assessment, so each learner gets measured, comparable skills data rather than only a certificate. Roughly 1,000 people have been trained, and 255 have gone on to internships. Talent Bridge (matching layer). This is a platform that turns assessed skills into profiles and matches them to employers and internships, in Uzbekistan and in Europe. Its predecessor, itskills.uz, was used by more than 5,000 people. The new version is nearly finished and adds AI-based skills mapping. Partnership model. Member studios host internships. International partners add training and market access.
Solution Provider(s): Uzbekistan Creative Association (UzCA), national games, animation and creative-technology industry association, Uzbekistan; Proxy Planet, game industry partner, South Korea; Digiage, game industry partner, Türkiye; UzCA member studios, 40+ game and animation studios hosting internships, Uzbekistan; Ministry of Digital Technologies of Uzbekistan
Implementation location(s): Uzbekistan
Implementation timeline(s): Piloted started in 2024
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6 months
Desired impact: The objective is to turn training into verified, employable skills and connect them to real jobs. Demonstrated results so far: about 1,000 people trained through CreativeTech; 255 internships secured, roughly a quarter of trainees; 5,000+ users on the predecessor platform, itskills.uz. Targets for the next phase: train 3000 people; advanced training of 500 people; 1000 internships
Key technologies: AI for learner performance analysis, assessment and curriculum design; AI-based skills mapping and employer matching in Talent Bridge; a web platform with profile and matching data.
Unique Characteristics: The solution connects the whole chain (training, assessment, matching and placement), where most programmes cover only one step. Its delivery model is also distinctive: it is run by a state-backed industry association that controls the internship supply through its member studios.
Sustainable Change: The same pipeline can be replicated across the nine countries of the Central Asia Game Alliance (CAGA), which UzCA co-founded. It would also feed the national 2030 creative-industry targets and give European employers a trusted way to recruit regional talent. Because skills data and the matching model are reusable, a new country mainly needs localisation, not a rebuild.
Funding Sources: Ministry of Digital Technologies of Uzbekistan Own funds of association and members
Primary thematic focus area: Industrial Ecosystem Enablers: Finance, Skills and Market Access
Summary: Talent Bridge pairs AI-assessed creative-industry training with a matching platform, and has placed 255 of about 1,000 trainees into internships since 2024. The delivery model is the strongest element; thin technical description and single-country scope cap the score.
Thematic focus areas (as submitted): Industrial Ecosystem Enablers: Finance, Skills and Market Access; Industrial Digital Infrastructure and Data Ecosystems

Title: YCD Farmer Guide: Voice-First AI Agritech for Rural Smallholders
Subtitle: Empowering smallholder farmers with voice-driven AI crop disease diagnosis, localized agronomic advisory, and direct market links to secure sustainable food
Problem Statement: Smallholder farmers in developing regions lose up to 40% of their crop yields annually due to delayed crop disease diagnosis and limited access to professional agronomic expertise. This challenge is further compounded by literacy barriers, language gaps, and digital illiteracy, which restrict access to standard text-based agricultural technologies. Additionally, information asymmetry and market isolation force smallholders to sell produce below fair market value. Without inclusive, real-time diagnostic tools and accessible market intelligence, smallholders struggle to maintain sustainable crop yields, secure resilient livelihoods, and ensure regional food security.
Solution Overview: How It Works & Software Features: YCD Farmer Guide is a mobile agritech platform designed for low-bandwidth and multi-lingual rural contexts. Farmers capture an image of crop symptoms or input voice queries in local languages to receive instant, voice-guided AI disease diagnoses and practical, localized agronomic treatment plans. The platform also aggregates market data to connect producers directly to local buyer links, optimizing price transparency and reducing post-harvest losses. Methodologies & Technologies Used: Computer Vision & Machine Learning: Deep learning models trained on agricultural image datasets for rapid leaf and crop pathology identification. Voice-First AI & NLP: Natural Language Processing and speech-to-speech engine supporting local voice-first interaction for low-literacy users. Mobile-First & Offline-Ready Architecture: Lightweight software framework built for low-latency operation in remote, low-connectivity agricultural zones. Partnerships & Collaboration Models: We operate a collaborative ecosystem model partnering with local agricultural cooperatives and youth development organizations for field deployment and farmer onboarding. We also engage local agricultural research experts to validate agronomic advisories and ensure local crop disease models remain accurate and actionable.
Solution Provider(s): Youths & Contemporary Development (YCD) (Non-Profit/Civil Society Sector - Lead project organization driving youth community engagement, field logistics, and rural farmer deployment), Local Agricultural Cooperatives & Farming Groups (Agricultural/Private Sector - Community-level farmer network partners facilitating field pilots and user onboarding across rural farming hubs)
Implementation location(s): South West Region(Tole) and North West Region (Bambili), Cameroon (rural agricultural farming communities and local cooperative hubs)
