Title: Trace, the ERP small Colombian businesses run by talking to ChatGPT or Claude
Subtitle: Inventory, online store and e-invoicing in one place for micro businesses that sell on Instagram and WhatsApp, with AI that records sales by voice and answers questions.
Problem Statement: Micro and small businesses are the base of Latin America's supply chains. They produce, process, distribute and resell goods, yet most still run on notebooks, phone notes and WhatsApp. ERPs are too expensive and complex for them, and electronic invoicing is now mandatory in Colombia, so many stay informal and invisible to banks, large industrial buyers and online markets. That keeps them out of formal supply chains and the digital economy.
Solution Overview: Trace puts inventory, purchases, sales, an online store and electronic invoicing in one web app that works from any phone. When something sells in the store, stock updates by itself. Payments go through Wompi, and the monthly plan already includes the invoices a small business needs. We built our own MCP server, so owners can run their business from ChatGPT or Claude. They can dictate a sale out loud, ask "what did I sell most this week?" or "what do I need to restock?", and the AI reads supplier invoices and loads inventory for them. The AI only does what the user's permissions allow, and the owner confirms before anything is saved. Records and invoices are sealed on Basis Network, our own blockchain, so the business builds a history it can prove to banks and buyers. We onboard each business hand in hand, and the plan costs about USD 20 a month.
Solution Provider(s): Wompi by Bancolombia (payment gateway, fintech), Ruta N Medellín (innovation agency of the District of Medellín, Gen N program), Cluster Negocios Digitales of the Medellín Chamber of Commerce (business cluster, Experiencia Tech 2026), Palmus Ventures (venture builder, Triage Empresarial for businesses hit by the August 2026 earthquake)
Implementation location(s): Valle del Cauca and Antioquia, Colombia (Tuluá, Medellín and nearby towns)
Implementation timeline(s): August 2026 to present
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 2 to 4 weeks. A single business can be live in one day.
Desired impact: Help micro and small businesses get organized, sell online, invoice legally and make decisions with data, using AI tools they already know. So far 12 businesses in Valle del Cauca and Antioquia run on Trace and pay for it, from phone accessory shops and jewelers that used to track everything in phone notes, to a fishing company and a trading company. Some of them already manage their business from ChatGPT or Claude through our MCP. After the August 2026 earthquake we offered 6 months free to affected businesses in Valle del Cauca through Palmus Ventures. What we expect: more formal businesses, more online sales, less time lost on paperwork and less stock wasted, and a verifiable sales history that opens the door to credit and to selling to bigger companies.
Key technologies: Generative AI through our own MCP server, so Trace works inside ChatGPT and Claude. Voice sales recording and AI that reads invoices to load inventory. Electronic invoicing integrated with Colombia's tax authority (DIAN). Blockchain (Basis Network, our own Layer 1) to seal records and invoices. Wompi payments. Mobile-first cloud web app.
Unique Characteristics: The interface is the AI the owner already uses. Instead of learning an ERP, they talk to ChatGPT or Claude, even by voice. Store, inventory and legal invoicing come in one plan at about USD 20 a month, with unlimited users. And every invoice is sealed on blockchain, which no tool for micro businesses in our market offers. We keep the AI responsible. It only acts within each user's permissions, the owner approves before anything is saved, and the data belongs to the business.
Sustainable Change: Large industrial buyers can only work with suppliers that invoice legally and keep reliable records. Trace turns informal micro businesses into suppliers that bigger companies can contract, which makes local supply chains stronger and more inclusive. Micro and small businesses are the vast majority of companies in Colombia and Latin America, and most still run on paper. Every business that joins Trace becomes formal, sells beyond its town and builds a verifiable sales history. With that history, banks and fintechs can lend to businesses they couldn't see before. The model works in any country with electronic invoicing, which is most of Latin America.
Funding Sources: Self-funded by Base Computing S.A.S. with revenue from client work and Trace subscriptions. Non-dilutive support from Ruta N Medellín (Gen N program). No equity raised.
Testimonials and Endorsements: Selected to exhibit at Experiencia Tech 2026, Cluster Negocios Digitales of the Medellín Chamber of Commerce Part of Palmus Ventures' Triage Empresarial for businesses affected by the August 2026 earthquake Our team: 1st place Gen N "Next" (Ruta N), Joven Referente 2026 (Medellín), Top 50 and USD 15K grant from Avalanche Build Games, 20+ hackathons won
Primary thematic focus area: Industrial Ecosystem Enablers: Finance, Skills and Market Access
Summary: Trace puts inventory, purchases, sales, an online store and electronic invoicing into one phone-accessible application for Colombian micro businesses, with voice entry and ChatGPT and Claude access through a company-built MCP server. Twelve businesses in two departments pay for it.
Thematic focus areas (as submitted): Industrial Ecosystem Enablers: Finance, Skills and Market Access

Title: KoAssist: The AI Project Memory for Mid-Sized Machine Builders
Subtitle: KoAssist connects to the ERP, PDM and document systems of industrial SMEs so engineers can find project knowledge, check drawings before release and reuse existing parts instead of re-designing them.
Problem Statement: Mid-sized machinery and equipment manufacturers keep their most valuable know-how in fragmented systems: ERP, PDM, file servers, e-mail and the heads of experienced engineers. As a result, engineers lose time searching for existing drawings, parts and past project decisions, re-design parts that already exist, and repeat errors that were already solved in earlier projects. With senior engineers retiring and skilled engineers scarce, this knowledge is increasingly lost. Large corporations can afford dedicated data teams and custom platforms. SMEs, the backbone of industrial value creation, cannot. Generic AI assistants do not close this gap because they do not understand technical drawings, part structures or project context, and they are not connected to the systems where engineering knowledge actually lives.
Solution Overview: KoAssist is a vertical AI platform for design engineers and project managers in machine and equipment building, developed in-house by Soneo AI GmbH (Vienna, Austria). How it works: KoAssist connects to the systems a company already uses (e.g. SharePoint, network drives, PRO.FILE PDM, ERP exports). An indexing pipeline processes PDFs, technical drawings, Excel files and documents into a secure, company-specific knowledge base. Nobody has to maintain or enter new data. The project acts as the frame around three modules: 1. Project Chat and Knowledge Search (in production with customers): engineers ask questions in natural language and get answers with source references. The chat goes beyond finding knowledge: it can perform engineering calculations, evaluate Excel and ERP data, compare variants from past projects and generate documents (PDF, Word, Excel). If no source exists, KoAssist says so instead of answering from general model knowledge. 2. Drawing Review (in beta tests with customers): before a drawing is released, KoAssist checks it for completeness, consistency and the company's own design guidelines. The result is a structured review protocol that serves as a quality management record and as clear feedback to internal and external drafters. Errors are caught at the desk instead of on the shop floor. 3. Similar-Part Search (first version, with design partners): before an engineer designs a new part, KoAssist finds existing identical or similar parts based on drawings and part data, so they can be reused instead of re-designed. This avoids duplicate part numbers and the design, tooling, procurement and inventory effort that comes with every new part. Methodologies and technologies: Retrieval-augmented generation with large language models (Anthropic Claude via Amazon Bedrock in the EU), OCR and multimodal document understanding for technical drawings, embedding-based similarity search for parts. Hosting in the EU (Germany) as standard, on-premise possible. Collaboration model: Customers start with a paid two-month test phase with a committed internal champion, followed by an annual per-user licence. Drawing Review and Similar-Part Search are developed together with industrial design partners. We work with ecosystem partners such as AI Factory Austria.
Solution Provider(s): AI Factory Austria (AI:AT), EuroHPC AI Factory providing AI compute, legal support and ecosystem access to Austrian AI companies (public research and innovation sector), NVIDIA Inception, NVIDIA's program for AI startups (technology sector)
Implementation location(s): Austria and Germany: industrial SMEs in machine and equipment building and engineering services (e.g. Graz, Tyrol, Augsburg)
Implementation timeline(s): 2025 to present (ongoing, active customer deployments)
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 4 to 8 weeks (cloud setup and data connection in 1 to 2 weeks, followed by a structured pilot)
Desired impact: Main objectives: 1. Reuse instead of re-design (Similar-Part Search): engineers find existing parts before creating new ones, reducing the number of new part numbers and duplicate designs. 2. Right first time (Drawing Review): drawing errors are caught before release, not in production or at the customer. 3. Keep knowledge in the company (Project Chat and project memory): decades of project experience stay accessible when experienced engineers retire, and can be used directly for calculations, analyses and documents. 4. Make industrial AI usable for SMEs without their own data or AI teams. Demonstrated impact: - KoAssist is in productive use with paying industrial SMEs in Austria and Germany, used by design engineering teams in their daily work. - Drawing Review is in beta tests with customers. The review protocol is already used as a quality management record and as structured feedback to external drafters. - Similar-Part Search is being developed and tested with industrial design partners on their real part data. Expected impact: - Fewer duplicate parts: every avoided new part saves design hours, a new part number and often tooling, procurement and inventory effort, and the material that comes with it. - Fewer drawing errors reaching production: less scrap, rework and delivery delays, which directly reduces material waste and energy use. - Less engineering time spent searching and recalculating, freeing scarce engineering capacity for new development. - Faster onboarding of young engineers through access to the company's accumulated project knowledge. We are measuring these effects in current customer deployments and will only publish figures once they are verified.
Key technologies: - Large language models (Anthropic Claude via Amazon Bedrock, EU region) for question answering, document generation and drawing review - Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with source-grounded answers - OCR and multimodal document understanding for technical drawings, PDFs and spreadsheets - Vector embeddings and similarity search for parts and documents - Connectors to enterprise systems (SharePoint, network drives, PRO.FILE PDM, ERP exports) - EU cloud hosting (Germany) or on-premise deployment
Unique Characteristics: - Prevention instead of search: Drawing Review and Similar-Part Search act before a part is designed or a drawing is released, where errors and duplicates are cheapest to avoid. - From answers to work: the chat does not only find knowledge, it performs calculations, evaluates data and generates documents based on the company's own project history. - Vertical instead of generic: built for engineering data (drawings, parts, project history), not for general office text. - Zero maintenance: KoAssist derives the project memory from systems that already exist (ERP, PDM, file servers). Nobody has to enter or curate data, which is where most knowledge management tools fail. - Trust by design: every answer is grounded in company sources; if there is no source, KoAssist says so instead of guessing. EU hosting or on-premise for sensitive engineering data. - SME business model: affordable per-user licence and a short paid test phase instead of long consulting projects. - Compounding advantage: every deployment improves connectors and domain understanding for the next customer.
Sustainable Change: Industrial SMEs are the backbone of manufacturing in Europe and in industrialising economies, and they all face the same problem: critical knowledge locked in fragmented systems and in the heads of a few experienced people, combined with a shortage of skilled engineers. KoAssist addresses this without requiring a data team or a large IT budget, which makes it replicable in any market with a manufacturing SME base. Follow-on effects: - Knowledge retention and transfer: young engineers gain access to decades of project experience, which accelerates skills development. - Resource efficiency: reusing existing parts and catching drawing errors early reduces material waste, scrap and rework. - Supply-chain inclusion: suppliers in global value chains can meet the documentation and quality requirements of international OEMs more easily. Scale-up path: standard connectors and a multilingual AI core allow deployment in new countries with limited adaptation. We plan to scale through integration partners, industry associations and AI Factory ecosystems, starting from our base in Austria and Germany.
Funding Sources: Revenue from paying customers (licences, paid test phases and AI implementation projects), founders' own capital, and public start-up support from the Vienna Business Agency (Wirtschaftsagentur Wien, Smart Founders programme). A pre-seed round with business angels is currently in progress.
Testimonials and Endorsements: https://omr.com/en/reviews/product/koassist
Primary thematic focus area: Industrial AI Models and Intelligent Decision-Making
Summary: KoAssist indexes a machine builder's ERP, PDM and documents so engineers can find prior parts and check drawings before release. It has paying customers and a defensible narrow scope; impact and geography are where the submission is thin.
Thematic focus areas (as submitted): Industrial AI Models and Intelligent Decision-Making; Industrial Digital Infrastructure and Data Ecosystems; AI for Green, Resilient and Sustainable Industry

Title: Global Corporate Reference: Cross-border verification of companies worldwide
Subtitle: Turns official company register records into signed digital proofs that buyers, banks, customs and AI agents can check in seconds, free, with no AI deciding any fact.
Problem Statement: A buyer, bank, customs officer or AI procurement agent dealing with a supplier abroad has to answer a basic question first: is this company real, and is it who it says it is? Every country keeps an official company register, but registers do not talk to each other. Each has its own website, language, format and status codes, and most still hand out paper or PDF certificates that are easy to fake and that no computer can check. Commercial databases charge per search, can be out of date, and are not official. Manual checks take days and often cost more than a small order is worth. Honest small firms in emerging markets and developing economies lose most: buyers trust them less, ask for more paperwork, or go elsewhere. Fake companies gain, because they hide in the confusion. As industrial supply chains and procurement move to automated systems and AI agents, the problem grows: an agent that cannot check a supplier's legal existence from an official source either excludes unknown suppliers or trusts unverified data.
Solution Overview: How it works. Global Corporate Reference (GCR), run by Global Credibility Centre, an independent think tank in London, works in four steps: Read: GCR reads a company's record only from its government's official company register, through the register's open data or an agreed connection. Check: fixed rules written in code check every field and map each register's codes to one shared set of values. If anything looks wrong, nothing is published. No AI, guessing or fuzzy matching decides any fact. Seal: GCR issues the Global Registry Pass, a W3C Verifiable Credential with a digital signature and an independent RFC 3161 date stamp. Each proof carries the hash of the register record it was made from. Changing one letter breaks the seal. Anyone checks: a person, an ERP, a customs system or an AI agent checks the proof in seconds, free, without an account, even offline. If the official record changes, the old proof is cancelled through a public status list and a new one is issued. Anyone can report a mistake, and GCR then rechecks the register. Role in an AI-enabled industrial economy. GCR is deliberately not an AI model. It is the trusted-data layer that AI systems need: machine-readable, signed facts from official sources that an AI procurement or compliance agent can check before it acts, instead of relying on scraped or generated data. This also makes it a worked example of the "trustworthy data for industry" that AIM Global promotes. Methodologies and technologies. A deterministic rule engine (Python), W3C Verifiable Credentials with Ed25519 signatures, RFC 3161 time-stamping, a Bitstring Status List for cancellations, a did:web issuer identity, and a public verify API. Proof formats follow UN/CEFACT's UN Transparency Protocol (UNTP) direction. Partnership and collaboration model. The register always stays the owner and the official source. Each register decides what GCR may read and can stop at any time; when a register issues its own digital proofs, GCR steps back for that register. GCR asks partners for introductions to registers and for funding to connect them. Funders are named publicly, get the same free service as everyone, and cannot change any proof or rule. Checking is free for everyone; GCC sells nothing on the verification surface and publishes no score, rating or ranking.
Solution Provider(s): GCR reads official open data from UK Companies House (public data API), Brazil's Receita Federal (CNPJ open data) and the Global Legal Entity Identifier Foundation (LEI golden copy, read as a second identifier), each under its published open-data terms. GCR follows the UN/CEFACT work on the UN Transparency Protocol and the Global Registry Information Directory (GRID). Discussions are open with standards and register bodies.
Implementation location(s): Technical coverage today: United Kingdom and Brazil, with LEIs read as a second identifier. The node runs in the EU; the public site is www.gcref.org
Implementation timeline(s): N/A. The system was built and tested in 2026; a public test with 100 companies follows the remaining setup steps (signing-key ceremony, legal advice).
Duration to pilot in a new geography: The technical work to connect a register that publishes open data is short. The pace is set by the register's data-use agreement and funding, not by the technology.
Desired impact: Objectives. (1) Make the basic question "is this company real?" free and quick to answer anywhere, from the official source. (2) Give honest small firms in emerging markets and developing economies a free, checkable proof of their legal existence, so buyers abroad trust them sooner. (3) Help company registers that still issue paper join the UN's emerging system of digital trade proofs now, instead of in many years. Impact. The expected impact, to be measured in a pilot: time and cost of supplier onboarding checks before and after; number of covered companies holding a proof; number of proof checks by buyers, banks and customs; and share of checked suppliers from EMDEs. GCR will report these openly.
Key technologies: W3C Verifiable Credentials (Ed25519 Data Integrity proof, plus a JWS form for UNTP alignment); IETF RFC 3161 time-stamping from two independent time-stamp authorities; W3C Bitstring Status List; did:web; ISO 6523, ISO 17442 (LEI) and ISO 3166 identifiers; a deterministic rule engine in Python (FastAPI); an open verify API and offline verification. AI: none in the fact path, by design. No AI creates, changes, signs or cancels any fact or proof. GCR's outputs are built to be consumed by AI agents and automated trade systems.
Unique Characteristics: 1) Proof, not data resale: GCR issues signed proofs from the official register instead of selling copies of records. 2) Free and identical for every company: issuance and checking are free, with no score, rating, ranking or paid placement. 3) No AI deciding facts: fixed rules in code, so every fact traces to the register record and the rule that mapped it. 4) Built for machines: any ERP, customs system or AI agent can check a proof with standard tools, offline, without an account. 5) Companies, never people: no personal data from any register is stored; a person who holds shares shows only as "Natural Person (Restricted)". 6) Registers stay in charge: the register can stop at any time, and GCR steps back once the register issues its own proofs. 7) Neutral funding model: funders are named publicly and cannot influence any proof, rule or coverage decision.
Sustainable Change: GCR is designed to make itself unnecessary register by register. Each connection gives every company in that register a free, checkable proof at once, with no action needed by the company. As registers adopt the UN Transparency Protocol, GCR helps them issue proofs under their own keys and then steps back, so the lasting change sits in the national register, not in GCR. Because the proofs follow open W3C and UN/CEFACT formats, every buyer, marketplace, bank, customs system and AI agent that learns to check one proof can check proofs from any covered country. Scale-up follows the order EMDEs and the Global South first, then G20 economies, through register associations and multilateral programmes such as UNIDO's SSTIC and AIM Global.
Funding Sources: Funded by Global Credibility Centre to date; Funding from international organisations, development banks, foundations, NGOs and governments is welcome on the same terms for all.
Primary thematic focus area: Industrial Digital Infrastructure and Data Ecosystems
Summary: The Global Corporate Reference turns official company-register records into signed, checkable proofs, starting with the United Kingdom and Brazil. The design is the most disciplined in the field; the absence of any live verification keeps it mid-table.
Thematic focus areas (as submitted): Industrial Digital Infrastructure and Data Ecosystems; Industrial Ecosystem Enablers: Finance, Skills and Market Access

Title: Flapmax Earth Intelligence
Subtitle: Sovereign AI-powered Earth intelligence for climate resilience, food security and sustainable industrial development in Africa
Problem Statement: African agricultural value chains, enterprises and public institutions face flood exposure, crop stress and climate-related disruption, while Earth observation data often remain disconnected from operational decisions. Converting imagery into useful local intelligence requires geospatial expertise, affordable computing, data governance and sustained institutional capacity. These constraints limit timely agricultural monitoring, resilient infrastructure planning and continuity of food supply and industrial activity.
Solution Overview: Flapmax Earth Intelligence transforms satellite observations into actionable intelligence for African institutions and industries. Commercial deployment is underway, with an initial focus on agriculture and food security, alongside climate and flood resilience. Additional applications include public health, environmental monitoring, and government and industrial infrastructure. The platform combines satellite imagery, weather information and local geospatial data to support agricultural monitoring, flood assessment and resilient planning. FMAX, Flapmax’s heterogeneous AI execution platform, provides the computing foundation for processing geospatial workloads across available hardware resources. The FMAX-0 roadmap extends this foundation toward shared, locally operated computing infrastructure, giving African institutions greater control over their data, processing and service delivery. Institutional engagement across Africa supports modularized deployment and technical capacity development. This work includes pathway for a proposed multicountry showcase in Egypt in 2027, with pilot scope and implementation arrangements being coordinated with participating institutions. The demonstration programme focuses on flood intelligence and agricultural monitoring using historical satellite observations. It will present georeferenced maps, changes over time and relevant exposure indicators, with observation dates and uncertainty clearly identified to support institutional review and validation. Current delivery uses ground-based computing and existing satellite data. Future integration with FLAP-0, Flapmax’s space-edge computing initiative, forms part of the longer-term roadmap. The technical foundation draws on Flapmax’s research in AI infrastructure, distributed computing and performance evaluation, including the FMAX research poster accepted at the 2024 IEEE CAS-EDS AI Compute Symposium, distributed-accelerator research published at IEEE FPL 2022, and the RISCBench poster at ACM FPGA 2026. This foundation supports a delivery approach centred on analytical accuracy, computing efficiency and practical value for agricultural and climate-resilience decisions.
Solution Provider(s): African Group on Earth Observations (AfriGEO), regional Earth observation coordination and institutional engagement; Regional Centre for Mapping of Resources for Development (RCMRD), intergovernmental geospatial and capacity-development institution hosting the AfriGEO Secretariat. These are ongoing engagement and proposed pilot-planning relationships, not signed Earth Intelligence delivery partnerships. Flapmax leads platform development.
Implementation location(s): Ongoing implementation in Ghana, Kenya, Madagascar, Nigeria, Tunisia
Implementation timeline(s): Nov 2026 - Nov 2027
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Planning estimate of 3–6 months after pilot scope, local host, data permissions and computing resources are agreed.
Desired impact: Enable African institutions and agricultural value-chain participants to use Earth observation AI for crop-condition monitoring, flood-exposure assessment and resilient planning. Initial objectives are to develop and validate an end-to-end workflow, support locally governed computing and strengthen local technical capacity. Expected benefits include faster interpretation of observations, improved identification of exposed agricultural land and assets, and more informed resource allocation and continuity planning. These outcomes have not yet been demonstrated for Earth Intelligence and are not quantified as achieved impact. Pilot evaluation will establish baselines and measure spatial accuracy against reference data, processing time, cost and resource use per area analysed, usability and decision relevance. Flood and agricultural results will be validated with institutional users.
Key technologies: Earth observation and geospatial AI; satellite-image preprocessing and change analysis; foundation-model workflows; optical and radar data workflows; heterogeneous AI execution through Flapmax FMAX; geospatial data management
Unique Characteristics: Flapmax Earth Intelligence connects satellite data processing with FMAX, allowing AI workloads to run across different processors and computing environments. Institutions can process data locally and use the same infrastructure for agricultural monitoring, flood assessment and other applications. This reduces the need to build separate systems for each use case. Future FLAP-0 integration will extend processing to space-edge systems.
Sustainable Change: The platform gives institutions a common system for running Earth observation services across departments and sectors. Expansion to another country or application reuses the processing infrastructure, with adjustments for local data, permissions and validation requirements. Training local teams to operate these services supports continuity, while planned computing infrastructure in Ghana and Nigeria could support wider regional delivery.
Funding Sources: Contracts and partnerships SoW (statement of work)
Testimonials and Endorsements: "We believe Flapmax’s expertise in sustainable AI infrastructure, heterogeneous computing, and AI-enabled data services could contribute meaningfully to these priorities." "AfriGEO welcomes continued engagement with Flapmax to identify suitable pilot opportunities, engage relevant technical and institutional stakeholders, and jointly explore potential implementation and resource-mobilization mechanisms." - Director General, Regional Center for Mapping of Resources for Development (RCMRD) Official signed LOI available.
Primary thematic focus area: Industrial Digital Infrastructure and Data Ecosystems
Summary: Flapmax Earth Intelligence turns satellite imagery, optical and radar, into crop, flood and infrastructure intelligence for African institutions, running on the company's own heterogeneous inference platform. Implementation is under way in Ghana, Kenya, Madagascar, Nigeria and Tunisia through November 2027.
Thematic focus areas (as submitted): Industrial AI Models and Intelligent Decision-Making; Industrial Digital Infrastructure and Data Ecosystems; AI for Green, Resilient and Sustainable Industry

Name of your organization: SCORE Academy / SCORE研究院 (Yongxu Management Consulting (Guangzhou) Co., Ltd. / 永续管理咨询（广州）有限公司)
Title: SCORE Academy: AI-Enabled Skills Pathway for Green & Responsible Supply Chains
Subtitle: Digital ILO SCORE skills for MSME suppliers, plus emerging AI tools for sustainability assessment, green-path planning and supply-chain ESG early warning in developing Asia.
Problem Statement: Manufacturing MSMEs in developing and middle-income economies face rising buyer and regulatory expectations on quality, productivity, clean production, occupational safety, labour practices and supply-chain due diligence. Many suppliers can pass an audit yet lack shared methods, workplace cooperation routines and continuous-improvement skills to turn requirements into daily management. Traditional in-factory coaching works, but cost and trainer capacity limit coverage across dispersed supplier networks. At the same time, factories and brand programmes need practical digital/AI support to assess sustainability gaps, plan greener improvement paths and spot ESG risks earlier, without assuming advanced digital infrastructure.
Solution Overview: How it works. SCORE Academy delivers an industrial skills pathway grounded in the International Labour Organisation (ILO) SCORE methodology (Sustaining Competitive and Responsible Enterprises): workplace cooperation, quality management, productivity and cleaner production, human resource management, and occupational safety and health. Delivery combines (1) classroom / online learning for managers and worker representatives, (2) in-factory coaching with joint management-worker improvement teams, and (3) baseline and endline assessment against SCORE Academy enterprise assessment guidance. Recently, the Academy launched online SCORE enterprise training and trainer/faculty training (WeChat mini program; web course portal at https://h5.scorechina.com) so dispersed MSME suppliers can learn a common language before or alongside on-site projects. Methodologies and technologies. Core methodology is ILO SCORE. Digital layer: modular online courses (five SCORE modules) accessible via WeChat / H5. AI layer (under development / led by the Academy): tools intended for sustainability assessment, green transformation path planning, and supply-chain ESG risk early warning. These support diagnosis and prioritisation; they do not replace workplace cooperation or factory coaching. Partnerships and collaboration models. Programmes are typically commissioned or co-designed with brand / buyer supply-chain sustainability agendas; training is delivered to supplier factories. The Academy operates as a private-sector training and consulting provider using the ILO SCORE methodology and certified SCORE expert trainers. Overseas footprint includes China and Viet Nam, with broader Southeast Asia expansion including pilots. Since 2019, supply-chain training has reached over a hundred enterprises (上百家), including suppliers of major international brands (including Apple and Amazon) in China and Viet Nam. No learner counts, completion rates, or GHG/energy KPIs are claimed for the newly launched online courses or the AI tools.
Solution Provider(s): ILO SCORE methodology and certified SCORE trainer network (international labour standards and enterprise development methodology); brand-linked supply-chain capacity-building programmes serving suppliers of major international buyers, including Apple and Amazon, in China and Viet Nam (buyer-supplier-worker improvement model; brands cited as programme context, not as formal co-owners)
Implementation location(s): China (multiple supplier sites); Viet Nam (supplier sites). Online learning via WeChat mini program and H5 for learners in those programmes. Southeast Asia expansion underway, including Indonesia pilots.
Implementation timeline(s): Offline SCORE supply-chain capacity building: ongoing since 2019. Online enterprise and trainer training: launched 2026 (WeChat mini program / H5). AI support tools: under development / progressive rollout.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Approximately 3-6 months to localise online learning access, identify a first cohort of MSME suppliers with a brand or industry partner, brief local facilitators, and run a first pilot cycle combining online modules with light-touch coaching.
Desired impact: Objectives. (1) Equip MSME industrial suppliers with a shared SCORE skills base for workplace cooperation, quality, cleaner production, HR and occupational safety and health; (2) lower the cost and raise the reach of that skills pathway through online enterprise and trainer courses; (3) use emerging AI tools to help assess sustainability gaps, plan greener improvement paths and flag supply-chain ESG risks earlier; (4) strengthen responsible and relatively lower-waste / cleaner production practices in developing Asia supply chains. No tonnes of CO2e, kWh saved, or jobs created are claimed in this submission.

Digital learning delivery: WeChat mini program and H5 web courses (https://h5.scorechina.com). Emerging AI applications for sustainability assessment, green-transformation path planning, and supply-chain ESG risk early warning (decision-support for capacity building, not factory robotics or digital twins). Standard web and mobile access suitable for MSME settings. No claim of an offline-first or low-connectivity specialised stack.
Unique Characteristics: Moves supply-chain compliance from audit-to-find-problems toward skills to fix and sustain improvements, using a proven ILO methodology. Combines online scale (enterprise and trainer tracks) with in-factory coaching so digital learning feeds real workplace teams. Integrates environment and social modules in one improvement system (cleaner production alongside OSH, HR and workplace cooperation). Adds an AI-assisted diagnosis, path-planning and ESG early-warning layer aimed at MSME suppliers, not a capital-intensive robotics retrofit. Title: AI-driven Whole-Link Intelligent Operation Platform for Source-Network-Station-User — Low-Carbon and Resilient Intelligent Scheduling Solution for Industrial and District Heating
Subtitle: Powered by industrial AI agents, digital twins and the Internet of Things (IoT), the platform enables load forecasting, simulation, autonomous decision-making and closed-loop control for heating and industrial integrated energy systems. While guaranteeing reliable energy supply, it cuts energy consumption and carbon emissions. It has been validated through large-scale operation across a heating area of over 7.8 million square metres in Shenyang, offering a replicable pathway for green industrial energy transition for developing economies.
Problem Statement: (1) Industrial and district heating in most developing countries and middle-income economies still relies heavily on empirical manual scheduling. This leads to supply-demand imbalance in pipe networks, substantial energy waste, high fossil fuel consumption and mounting carbon pressure. There is also a general shortage of AI scheduling solutions validated by large-scale real-world operation. (2) Data from thermal networks, heat exchange stations and end users are siloed. Unified sensing and intelligent decision-making capabilities are lacking, resulting in weak energy supply stability and insufficient system resilience. Common issues include overheating, inadequate heating and unplanned shutdowns. (3) Traditional energy systems lack load simulation and carbon accounting tools, making it hard to meet compliance requirements for green investment and financing as well as international carbon disclosure. This challenge becomes especially prominent amid the rapid growth of clean heating and multi-heat-source coupling scenarios. (4) Many overseas regions are constrained by limited hardware sensors. Full retrofitting entails high capital investment, and there is a shortage of AI energy scheduling solutions operable under low-cost conditions. There is also a notable gap in local technical personnel for operation and maintenance.
Solution Overview: (1) Detailed description of the solution's working principle. The platform builds a source-network-station-user full-chain closed-loop system: IoT terminals collect millions of measurement point data at high frequency, including temperature, pressure, and flow at heat sources, pipeline network heat exchange stations, and user ends; data is filtered and aggregated through the data central control platform and fed into self-developed AI agents and hydraulic digital twin models; AI completes weather-coupled load forecasting, pipeline network simulation deduction, fault prediction, and carbon emission accounting, automatically outputting optimized dispatch instructions for the entire network; these are sent to heat exchange stations, intelligent balance valves, and other execution units for automatic regulation; the GIS visualization platform enables one-screen overview, alarm handling, and operational analysis, forming a closed-loop operation of "data collection-AI analysis-decision output-automatic execution-effect feedback." The platform supports two deployment modes: a full deployment mode for economies with relatively good digital infrastructure; and a lightweight weak-data mode, which, in scenarios with insufficient sensors, relies on partial measurement points plus simulation models to still output usable optimization strategies, reducing overseas hardware retrofit costs. (2) Methods and technologies used. Industrial AI agents, time-series AI load forecasting algorithms, heating network hydraulic digital twin simulation, IoT collection, GIS spatial visualization, edge computing, big data time-series middleware; supports offline edge operation, adapting to overseas conditions with unstable networks; built-in automatic energy consumption and carbon emission accounting models. (3) Partnership and collaboration models. Domestic model: Luen Mei Smart Energy Technology (Shenyang) Co., Ltd., under Luen Mei Quantum, is responsible for platform algorithm research and development and core system delivery; equipment manufacturers provide sensors and intelligent valve hardware; local energy/heating operations teams are responsible for on-site installation, commissioning, and local operations and maintenance. International export model: Adopts a technology export + local partner joint delivery model. We export the platform, algorithms, implementation methodology, and training packages; cooperate with local energy operating companies, industrial parks, and engineering service providers to complete on-site deployment and operations and maintenance; benefit-sharing and service subscription models can be adopted to reduce local one-time capital investment and achieve sustainable operations without relying on subsidies.
Solution Provider(s): 1. Luen Mei Quantum Co., Ltd. (Luen Mei Quantum): Shanghai Stock Exchange Main Board listed company (600167.SH), a leading A-share integrated energy service provider in China with a 100% clean heating rate, serving over one million residential customers, the main developer of the self-developed platform, integrated energy service industry. 2. Domestic intelligent measurement and control equipment supplier: provides heat exchange station controllers, balancing valves, temperature and pressure sensors, and supports Luen Mei Smart Energy in integrating and promoting self-developed hardware such as electric-control integrated cabinets at heat exchange stations, industrial automation equipment manufacturing industry. 3. Local district heating operators: responsible for on-site implementation and local O&M, municipal public energy operation industry.
Implementation location(s): Shenyang City, LiaoNing Province, P. R. China
Implementation timeline(s): Since 2023
Desired impact: 1. Improve the operational resilience and supply reliability of industrial and district heating energy systems via industrial AI autonomous decision-making. 2. Reduce overall thermal energy consumption, cut fossil fuel use and greenhouse gas emissions, and facilitate green and sustainable industrial transition. 3. Deliver a lightweight, replicable solution tailored for middle-income and developing economies to bridge the energy digital divide. 4. Create local green O&M jobs and deliver standardised skills training to upgrade local industrial capacity.
Key technologies: Industrial AI agents, AI time-series load forecasting, digital twin (hydraulic simulation of thermal networks; full digital modelling of primary pipe networks in the Shenyang area completed), IoT sensing terminals, edge computing, GIS geospatial visualisation, big data time-series platform, automatic carbon and energy consumption accounting model.
Unique Characteristics: 1. Technological innovation: Self-developed industrial AI agents built specifically for heating energy scenarios, interconnecting production scheduling, equipment alarm and customer service systems. The AI agent is undergoing internal testing, advancing scheduling decision-making from perceptual intelligence to cognitive/decision intelligence. It supports lightweight low-data operation: even with incomplete sensors and unstable networks, it generates usable scheduling strategies via digital twin simulation to accommodate hardware limitations common in many developing countries. Self-developed electric-control integrated cabinets have been widely deployed at heat exchange stations, delivering a comprehensive power saving rate of 35%. This achieves vertical integration of AI algorithms and self-owned hardware actuators, delivering closed-loop AI decision and control across the full source-network-station-user chain, rather than a mere data visualisation tool. 2. Delivery model innovation: Two delivery packages are available: the full version (full sensing + automatic AI control) and the lightweight version (minimum hardware investment, prioritising energy monitoring and simulation-based decision-making). The scope can be tailored to match national fiscal conditions and infrastructure levels. 3. International cooperation innovation: Instead of exporting heavy-turnkey engineering assets, we export platform technology, methodologies and training packages. Local partners handle implementation and O&M, lowering our overseas operational burden while building local industrial capabilities and avoiding opaque "black-box" technology. 4. Sustainable business model: Subscription services and energy-saving benefit-sharing arrangements are supported. Local partners avoid large upfront capital outlay; service costs are covered by energy-saving gains, enabling a commercial closed loop independent of subsidies.
Sustainable Change: This solution is not only applicable to China's heating scenarios but can also be transferred to Central Asia, Southeast Asia, Eastern Europe, and many middle-income and developing countries with industrial centralized heating and industrial park integrated energy supply needs. Replicability conditions: Modular platform architecture, hardware not bound to specific manufacturers; built-in configurable energy consumption and carbon accounting rules, adapting to different countries' metering and environmental policies; provides standardized multilingual operation dashboards, implementation manuals, and training packages, with the carbon data governance experience accumulated from Luen Mei Quantum's seven consecutive years of proactive ESG report disclosure as the methodological foundation, facilitating localization. Spillover effects: Beyond the heating industry, the algorithm framework can be transferred to industrial steam and park-level integrated multi-energy coordination scenarios, serving manufacturing factory energy systems; helping local industries meet green trade, carbon disclosure, and green financing requirements, and supporting low-carbon transformation across the entire industrial chain. Scaling pathway: After accumulating pilot experience through demonstration projects, the solution can be replicated and promoted to similar industries and regions, with simultaneous local personnel skills training to build local energy digitalization capabilities, forming long-term sustainable transformation and narrowing the gap between regions in industrial digitalization and green transition.
Funding Sources: The project is independently invested in, independently researched, and independently designed by Luen Mei Quantum.
Primary thematic focus area: Industrial AI Models and Intelligent Decision-Making
Summary: Luen Mei Quantum operates an intelligent platform for district heating across 7.8 million square metres in Shenyang, with a hydraulic digital twin and closed-loop control. The footprint is large and the saving is real; the AI is on trial rather than in service, which is why a flagship footprint scores in the middle of the ladder.
Thematic focus areas (as submitted): AI for Green, Resilient and Sustainable Industry

Title: 基于大模型与 RAG 的合金材料研发智能体平台建设
Subtitle: 以知识增强与智能体协同，构建材料研发全流程智能辅助能力
Problem Statement: 合金新产品研发涉及材料文献、专利、标准、历史方案、试验与图表等异构资料，信息分散、格式多样且存在复杂表格和图谱，资料查找、整理和复用依赖人工。研发人员还需在性能目标、成本约束、成分边界、工艺窗口与试验约束之间反复权衡，难以快速形成可复核的候选合金方案和代表性试验方案。
Solution Overview: 围绕材料研发“资料接入—知识增强—方案生成—专家复核—结果回流”构建平台。接入文档及图片等多源异构资料，采用解析清洗、切分向量化、关键词/全文/向量混合检索与融合重排，支持来源追溯。基于统一模型、智能体与知识库底座，合金化方案推荐智能体将性能目标、成本约束、成分边界和工艺要求转为结构化任务，综合历史方案、材料数据库、研发知识和专业工具输出候选方案及依据；DoE智能体结合历史案例、RAG知识、相图计算与采样优化方法生成试验方案集。AI提供检索、建议和解释，研发人员负责专业复核、工艺判断与最终决策。
Solution Provider(s): 博威合金材料股份有限公司：铜合金领域全球龙头企业；浙江大学湖州研究院：高校院所，擅长产学研合作与科技企业孵化。
Implementation location(s): 中国-浙江省/广东省
Desired impact: 项目已完成材料研发智能体平台、合金化方案推荐与 DoE 试验方案设计智能体上线运行，形成了“资料检索—方案生成—专家复核—试验验证”的研发辅助闭环。经项目验证，知识召回准确率达到 90%以上，Recall@5 高于 90%。在业务收益方面，基于研发资料检索、方案初筛及试验设计等环节的工作量测算，可将文献、专利及历史方案的检索与整理时间缩短 50%–70%，将新材料研发方案的前期论证周期缩短约 20%–30%，通过 DoE 最小试验集与候选方案筛选，可减少 15%–25% 的低价值试验；相关方案均由研发专家复核后进入验证环节。
Key technologies: AI,LLM,RAG,Agent
Unique Characteristics: 本方案的创新不在于单点部署通用大模型，而是面向材料研发中“资料分散、知识隐性、方案论证与试验设计高度依赖经验”的实际问题，构建“数据治理—RAG 知识增强—专业智能体—专家复核—试验验证—结果回流”的闭环能力。平台将材料文献、专利、标准、历史研发方案、试验数据等异构资料转化为可检索、可追溯的研发知识；合金化方案推荐智能体和 DoE 试验方案设计智能体可综合性能、成本、成分边界、工艺窗口及试验约束，生成带依据的候选方案与代表性试验集。区别于仅提供问答或文本生成的 AI 工具，本方案保留研发专家的专业复核和最终决策权，使 AI 能力真正嵌入材料研发流程，并持续沉淀组织知识与验证结果。
Sustainable Change: 方案推动材料研发由依赖个人经验和碎片化资料的工作模式，逐步转向“知识可沉淀、过程可追溯、方案可复核、结果可复用”的组织化研发模式。短期可缩短资料检索整理、方案初筛和试验设计等前期工作时间；长期可将专家经验、历史案例与试验结果持续回流至知识库和智能体，形成随项目积累不断增强的研发能力。平台采用统一模型、知识库和智能体底座，可在合金研发场景稳定运行后，复制扩展至专利分析、技术路线研判、工艺优化、质量分析等研发及制造相关场景，为企业建设可持续演进的研发数字化基础设施。

Title: Zoris - AI-native engineering design for industrial equipment
Subtitle: Zoris turns plain-English design requirements into code-compliant (ASME), production-ready engineering drawings for custom equipment manufacturers in minutes instead of days.
Problem Statement: Custom equipment makers, fabricators and mid-sized EPC firms still hand-draft every quote and revision in legacy CAD. A single ASME pressure vessel can take an engineer days of drafting, and simple revisions take days too. These firms lose bids on speed, burn scarce senior engineers on drafting, and overbuild equipment (excess material) because there is no time to optimize.
Solution Overview: Describe -> Generate -> Refine -> Export. The engineer types the requirement in plain English; Zoris generates a dimensioned drawing with materials and automated code-compliance checks; the engineer adjusts parameters in seconds; the result exports to DXF/PDF into existing workflows. Technology: a proprietary parametric design system plus a cost-optimization layer, driven by AI. Engineers stay in control and review every output. Collaboration model: design-partner pilots with manufacturers; a live design-partner pilot with Spark Engineers (India) has saved 180+ engineering hours.
Solution Provider(s): Spark Engineers (India) - custom equipment engineering firm, design-partner pilot, industrial manufacturing; Michigan State University Momentum accelerator (2026 cohort, grant) - university accelerator; Hunter's Fund (Fall 2026 grant) - grant funder; NVIDIA Inception - technology startup program; MEDC LEAP program - state economic development program
Implementation location(s): United States and India
Implementation timeline(s): August 2026 - ongoing (platform live since August 2026; pilot with Spark Engineers in India ongoing)
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Approximately 4-6 weeks (a paid pilot, as the platform is cloud-based and needs no on-site hardware)
Desired impact: Objective: cut engineering design time for custom industrial equipment from days to minutes while keeping engineers in control and designs code-compliant. Demonstrated impact: 180+ engineering hours saved in the Spark Engineers (India) pilot; 75+ projects created. Sustainability: cost optimization reduces overbuilt designs and excess steel/material per vessel. Inclusion: faster quoting helps small and mid-sized manufacturers compete, and lets smaller fabricators in emerging markets produce compliant designs despite the shortage of experienced engineers.
Key technologies: AI (natural-language requirement understanding), a proprietary parametric design engine, automated code-compliance checking, and DXF/PDF export into existing workflows.
Unique Characteristics: Zoris is AI-native rather than a bolt-on to legacy CAD: plain-English requirements become dimensioned, code-compliant drawings in minutes. A proprietary parametric design system and cost-optimization layer reduce material use, and engineers remain in control. Delivery model: a paid pilot that converts into an annual enterprise contract, with weekly product releases.
Sustainable Change: Zoris lowers the engineering barrier for small and mid-sized fabricators and EPC firms, including in developing and middle-income economies, so they can quote faster and produce compliant designs without large senior engineering teams. Less overbuilding means less material and embodied carbon across many units. The software is cloud-based and replicable across geographies and equipment types (starting with pressure vessels), so scale-up is largely adding new design templates and code standards. Already operating in the United States and India.
Funding Sources: No equity raised to date; currently raising about $500K pre-seed. Non-dilutive grants totaling $8K: Michigan State University Momentum accelerator ($5K) and Hunter's Fund ($3K).
Primary thematic focus area: Industrial AI Models and Intelligent Decision-Making
Summary: Zoris converts written requirements into code-compliant engineering drawings for custom equipment manufacturers, with a paid pilot in India and 180 hours saved. The product is live and the demonstration is genuine; what is missing is evidence that the compliance checks are reliable and any environmental measure.

Title: Talkulate AI CPQ
Subtitle: Multi-agent AI CPQ bridging the global engineering gap. It turns simple conversations into zero-error technical configurations, democratizing complex sales for a sustainable digital economy.
Problem Statement: Across global industries - from specialized healthcare and complex logistics to advanced manufacturing and critical B2B services - the pre-sales cycle for high-stakes, multi-parameter solutions is crippled by structural friction during the scoping and configuration phase: 1. Asynchronous Friction and Time-Zone Barriers: Cross-border trade in complex solutions is constrained by geographical and time-zone fragmentation. Scoping a project - whether configuring clinical systems, multimodal supply chain networks, or industrial setups - requires multiple back-and-forth inquiries. Time-zone latency stretches standard discovery and quoting from hours into weeks, preventing emerging-market suppliers from scaling globally and delaying critical deal closures. 2. Slow Commercial Velocity Stifling Economic Growth: Protracted pre-sales negotiations and discovery cycles paralyze organizational decision-making and tie up working capital. When scoping, quoting, and validating essential logistics routes, medical diagnostic systems, or specialized services takes months of meetings, economic momentum stalls, delaying project execution and regional modernization. 3. The Domain Expert Bottleneck: Multi-variable solution design depends on scarce, high-value experts -solution architects, logistics engineers, biomedical consultants, and technical specialists. Globally, up to 60% of these experts' time is consumed by routine client intake, requirement mapping, and repetitive pricing calculations rather than high-value problem solving, clinical delivery, or R&D. 4. Systemic Exclusion of SMEs and Emerging Markets: Small and medium-sized organizations are locked out from two sides: non-expert buyers cannot translate their operational needs into technical specifications during early sales stages, while emerging-market providers lack the capital to maintain round-the-clock global pre-sales desks, cementing structural inequality in global commerce. 5. High-Stakes Errors and Systemic Waste: Manual configuration across complex variables inevitably breeds errors - incompatible clinical hardware, non-compliant logistical routing, or mismatched technical components. These failures lead to project downtime, severe financial losses, unnecessary transit emissions, and material waste. The absence of instantaneous, multi-variable, and deterministic digital pre-sales tools keeps the global digital economy fragmented, slow, and inaccessible to non-expert participants.
Solution Overview: 1. How the Solution Works Talkulate AI CPQ transforms a multi-week, asynchronous pre-sales cycle into a 5-minute real-time automated process. Phase 1 (Task-Based Intake): The client interacts with an AI agent in natural language. Instead of navigating complex SKU catalogs or technical forms, the client simply describes their business problem (e.g., "We need to set up a cold-chain logistics route for vaccines" or "We need a secure data infrastructure for a remote clinic"). Phase 2 (Dynamic Discovery): The AI autonomously conducts a structured interview, asking clarifying questions regarding budgets, regulations, and operational environments based on real-time gap analysis. Phase 3 (Deterministic Resolution & Output): Behind the scenes, the system maps the client's answers to complex business rules. It instantly generates a 100% accurate quotation, a technical specification (BOM/SOW), and a "Logic Log" - a transparent explanation of why each component or service was selected. 2. Methodologies and Technologies Used Our architecture relies on robust Multi-Agent Orchestration with Deterministic Layer to ensure zero hallucinations in high-stakes environments: 2.1 Dynamic Multi-Agent System: A swarm of specialized AI agents concurrently handles natural language discovery, regulatory compliance, engineering compatibility, and pricing calculations. 2.2. Model-Agnostic AI Framework (Zero Vendor Lock-In): Talkulate is entirely decoupled from specific LLM providers. The architecture abstracts the AI layer, allowing dynamic routing across diverse proprietary models (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google) or open-source, locally hosted alternatives (Llama, Mistral, deep-seek). This ensures clients can adapt the solution to their strict data privacy mandates, regional data sovereignty requirements, and cost targets without single-vendor dependency. 2.3 Deep Infrastructure Integration: The platform embeds directly into enterprise IT ecosystems, connecting to legacy CRMs, ERPs, and internal databases via standard APIs and modern protocols like MCP (Model Context Protocol). 2.4 Adaptive Data Layer Generation: To eliminate AI hallucinations, agents only pull verified facts from structured data. If a client already possesses mature data systems, we connect immediately; if the client lacks structured infrastructure, we deploy an automated pipeline to structure their catalogs, manuals, and business rules into a queryable data layer. 3. Partnerships and Collaboration Models 3.1 Direct B2B Sales: We sell and deploy directly to enterprise and mid-market organizations, maintaining quality control over data onboarding and measurable business outcomes. 3.2 Consulting & Digital Transformation Firms: Collaboration with management and operational consultancies that introduce Talkulate to modernise client commercial infrastructure, eliminate engineering bottlenecks, and streamline cross-border operations. 3.3 B2B Go-To-Market (GTM) & Commercialization Alliances: Partnerships with specialized B2B growth and market-access agencies, connecting demand generation directly to an automated technical quoting engine that enables producers to close complex deals internationally across time zones.
Solution Provider(s): Strategic Consulting & Commercialization Partners (Confidential / Under NDA) (Advisory and B2B growth agencies deploying pre-sales automation, Sector: Management Consulting & Sales Enablement), Mistral AI SAS (European foundation model provider for open and sovereign deployments, Sector: Artificial Intelligence), Anthropic, PBC (Frontier reasoning model provider for conversational intake, Sector: Artificial Intelligence), OpenAI, LLC (Frontier LLM provider for multi-agent task execution, Sector: Artificial Intelligence), Google LLC (Enterprise cloud infrastructure and foundation model provider, Sector: Cloud Computing & Artificial Intelligence)
Implementation location(s): United States, Vietnam, Israel, Ukraine
Implementation timeline(s): 2026 – Present (Average deployment cycle: 4 weeks per client)

Title: Nudos | AI-Powered Ocean Asset Intelligence
Subtitle: Turning images and fragmented data about ocean assets into structured intelligence for risk, operations, commerce and resilience across the ocean economy.
Problem Statement: The ocean economy operates on trillions of dollars in physical assets, yet lacks a unified intelligence infrastructure to understand their condition, risks, performance and lifecycle. Across maritime transportation, marine infrastructure, insurance, aquaculture, ports and coastal industries, critical asset information remains fragmented across photographs, inspections, reports and disconnected systems. This fragmentation creates significant inefficiencies. Organizations struggle to assess physical risks, anticipate maintenance needs, optimize asset utilization, evaluate equipment conditions and make informed investment decisions. The challenge is particularly relevant in developing economies, where specialized inspections, technical expertise and digital infrastructure can be expensive or difficult to access. While the ocean economy generates enormous amounts of visual and operational information, much of its potential value remains untapped. The fundamental problem is not simply a lack of inspections. It is the absence of accessible, standardized and actionable intelligence about the physical assets supporting the ocean economy.
Solution Overview: Nudos is building the AI-native data and intelligence layer for the ocean economy, starting with marine insurance. Our vision is to transform fragmented images, documents and information about ocean assets into structured, verifiable intelligence that organizations can use to understand physical conditions, assess risks, optimize operations and unlock new economic opportunities. The platform is designed to connect physical-asset information with real-world decisions across multiple industries. How the solution works 1. Data acquisition and integration Nudos processes existing or newly captured images of marine assets, with the architecture designed to incorporate additional authorized asset records, technical documentation and contextual information. Our web-based capture technology and integration capabilities enable information collection without requiring specialized hardware. 2. AI-powered asset understanding Multimodal artificial intelligence and computer vision extract structured observations about visible components, equipment, physical condition, deterioration and potential risk indicators. The methodology links findings to supporting evidence, distinguishes observable facts from uncertain conclusions and supports consistent evaluations. 3. Ocean asset intelligence infrastructure Information is organized into structured asset, component and condition data that can be compared, analyzed and progressively enriched. This creates the foundation for an intelligence layer capable of connecting observations across assets, portfolios, locations and time. 4. Intelligence applications The underlying data infrastructure supports a broad range of potential applications: - Ocean Risk Intelligence: Insurance underwriting, claims, asset condition assessment, risk mitigation and resilience. - Ocean Operations & Lifecycle: Maintenance planning, fleet management, equipment monitoring, asset longevity and lifecycle intelligence. - Ocean Commerce Intelligence: Identifying equipment, components, repair needs, replacement opportunities and potential services from asset information. - Ocean Market Intelligence: Understanding equipment adoption, installed components, asset characteristics and market patterns for manufacturers, distributors and other industry participants. - Ocean Resilience & Blue Economy: Supporting better asset management, preventive interventions, coastal resilience and evidence-based sustainability initiatives. These applications share a common intelligence foundation while serving different stakeholders and economic needs. 5. Decision-making and integration The infrastructure is designed to deliver actionable information through reports, dashboards, APIs and integrations with existing enterprise systems. The objective is not merely to generate assessments, but to make ocean asset intelligence usable wherever organizations make operational, commercial, financial and environmental decisions. Technology and methodology Nudos combines multimodal AI, computer vision, structured data models, domain-specific evaluation frameworks, cloud infrastructure and evidence-based decision support. Its architecture emphasizes traceability, responsible data governance, explicit uncertainty and human verification where specialized judgment is necessary. Partnership and business model Our initial commercial entry point is marine insurance, where Nudos works with insurers and marine specialists to transform vessel imagery into risk and condition intelligence. We are building a B2B infrastructure model designed to serve insurers, maritime operators, marinas, marketplaces, equipment manufacturers, distributors, financial institutions and coastal organizations through assessments, enterprise integrations, software services and data intelligence products. The long-term objective is a scalable infrastructure that connects the ocean economy through better information about its physical assets.
Solution Provider(s): Our collaboration strategy combines commercial partners, academic institutions, marine surveyors, scientific expertise and Blue Economy innovation ecosystems. Through our relationship with Universidad ORT Uruguay's innovation center and emerging international connections, including Australia's BEIP WA, we aim to strengthen technical validation, foster interdisciplinary research and expand the application of ocean asset intelligence to industrial resilience and sustainable ocean development.
Implementation location(s): Uruguay, Argentina, Colombia, Panamá, United States, Australia. Nudos operates through cloud-based infrastructure, enabling remote data collection, analysis and international deployment.
Implementation timeline(s): 2026–present. Initial development, technical validation and commercial implementation began during 2026.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Approximately 2 weeks for an initial deployment using existing marine asset assessment capabilities, depending on partner readiness, technical requirements and access to authorized data.
Desired impact: Main objective To establish an AI-native intelligence infrastructure that transforms how the ocean economy understands, manages and creates value from its physical assets. By making asset information more accessible, structured and actionable, Nudos aims to support more efficient, resilient and sustainable economic activity across maritime and coastal industries. Strategic objectives - Democratize access to advanced asset intelligence, particularly for smaller operators and organizations in emerging economies. - Improve risk assessment and decision-making across marine insurance, financing and asset operations. - Support more effective maintenance, lifecycle management and resource utilization. - Enable new economic opportunities by connecting asset condition and equipment intelligence with relevant services, manufacturers and markets. - Strengthen ocean and coastal resilience through better information, preventive interventions and evidence-based planning. - Create an interoperable intelligence foundation that supports innovation and new digital services across the ocean economy. Demonstrated progress Nudos has established its initial commercial use case in marine insurance through Sancor Seguros in Uruguay. As of October 2026, the technology had completed more than 1,200 analyses across production, development and validation activities. An initial pilot achieved an average assessment workflow time of 6.7 minutes per vessel, demonstrating the feasibility of making specialized asset evaluation significantly more accessible. Additional evaluations with North American marine industry organizations are expanding the range of workflows being tested. Expected systemic and sustainability impact At scale, the intelligence infrastructure could enable earlier identification of visible deterioration, more informed maintenance decisions, better allocation of technical resources and improved asset lifecycle planning. Potential environmental benefits include longer useful asset life, reduced unnecessary equipment replacement, better documentation of pollution-related risks and more effective coastal resilience programs. Future implementations will incorporate measurable indicators such as asset coverage, verified maintenance interventions, resource utilization, component reuse, operational efficiency and environmental outcomes. Greenhouse gas reductions and environmental benefits will be quantified only where suitable baselines and independent evidence are available.
Key technologies: Nudos combines a modular set of technologies designed to create a scalable ocean asset intelligence infrastructure. Multimodal Artificial Intelligence: Models capable of interpreting visual information and relating it to structured technical knowledge and asset context. Computer Vision: Identification and classification of visible physical components, equipment characteristics, deterioration, damage and condition indicators. AI-Powered Decision Intelligence: Domain-specific rules and evaluation methods that convert observations into consistent, evidence-backed information. Structured Asset Data Models: Organization of asset characteristics, components, observations and supporting evidence to enable comparisons and analysis. Cloud-Native Data Infrastructure: Scalable processing, storage and application services built using Google Cloud technologies. APIs and Enterprise Integration: Mechanisms for connecting asset intelligence with external platforms, operational systems and industry workflows. Longitudinal and Portfolio Analytics: The architecture supports the progressive development of condition histories, comparative asset intelligence and pattern identification across portfolios. Human-in-the-Loop Validation: Mechanisms for expert review, evidence traceability and explicit management of uncertainty. The platform is designed to incorporate additional data sources and technologies as appropriate to specific industries and applications.
Unique Characteristics: Nudos approaches a fragmented industry challenge as a data infrastructure opportunity rather than an isolated software application. 1. A unified intelligence layer for ocean assets Instead of building separate solutions for every maritime use case, Nudos is developing a common intelligence foundation that can support multiple industries, applications and business models. 2. Turning existing information into economic value The ocean economy already produces substantial amounts of photographs, documentation and operational information. Nudos aims to extract new intelligence and economic value from these existing resources, reducing the need for additional data collection whenever adequate, authorized evidence is available. 3. From physical observations to actionable intelligence The platform is designed to connect visible asset characteristics and conditions with operational decisions, commercial opportunities, risk management and lifecycle needs. 4. Evidence-based, explainable AI Observations are connected to their underlying evidence, allowing users to understand what the technology has identified and where uncertainty remains. 5. One infrastructure, multiple economic applications The same structured asset intelligence can support insurers, operators, service providers, manufacturers, marketplaces and institutional stakeholders, subject to appropriate data rights and technical validation. 6. Accessible deployment Cloud infrastructure, image-based analysis and integration capabilities reduce barriers to adopting advanced intelligence technologies, particularly for organizations without extensive digital infrastructure. 7. Industry-driven development Nudos combines specialized maritime domain knowledge with real commercial experience, beginning with marine insurance as a practical entry point to a substantially broader economic ecosystem. The central innovation is the ability to transform fragmented physical-asset information into reusable intelligence that connects previously disconnected activities across the ocean economy.
Sustainable Change: The ocean economy is composed of interconnected industries that depend on the same underlying physical assets but often operate with fragmented and incompatible information systems. Insurance companies, maritime operators, equipment manufacturers, service providers, financial institutions and public organizations frequently evaluate different aspects of the same assets without a common intelligence foundation. Nudos aims to change this by creating an AI-native data and intelligence layer that can connect physical-asset information across industries, organizations and stages of an asset's lifecycle. A new digital infrastructure for the ocean economy Just as digital infrastructure transformed financial services, logistics and commerce, a shared ocean asset intelligence layer could enable entirely new services and more informed decisions across maritime industries. Better resource allocation and asset productivity More accessible information about asset conditions, components and maintenance requirements could help organizations prioritize interventions, improve equipment utilization and extend useful asset lifecycles. New economic opportunities The infrastructure could connect manufacturers, distributors, repair services, operators and marketplaces through intelligence derived from physical assets. This creates opportunities for new services, more efficient aftermarket distribution and improved understanding of industrial equipment demand. Inclusive industrial transformation By reducing dependence on costly, fragmented data collection processes, Nudos could make advanced asset intelligence more accessible to MSMEs, smaller fleets, coastal enterprises and organizations in developing economies. Environmental resilience and circularity Better information about physical conditions and installed equipment could support preventive maintenance, component reuse, more efficient asset management and measurable environmental interventions. Partnerships with maritime operators, public institutions and development organizations could extend these capabilities into coastal resilience, aquaculture, port infrastructure and other areas of the Blue Economy. Global replication and interoperability Nudos is designed as a scalable infrastructure that can be adapted to different markets, asset classes and industrial applications through specialized data models, local expertise, enterprise integrations and appropriate governance. Over time, this could support more consistent approaches to asset information, risk evaluation and operational intelligence across borders. Long-term vision Our ambition is to make ocean asset intelligence an accessible foundation for the global ocean economy. By connecting physical assets with structured, verifiable information, Nudos seeks to enable more informed decisions, new economic opportunities, improved industrial productivity and a more resilient and sustainable ocean economy.
