Title: SocialStation® & Thinks4® — Cooperative AI for Inclusive Industry
Subtitle: A patented physical-digital platform combining cooperative AI, collaborative learning and workforce upskilling to make industrial digital transformation more inclusive, accessible and scalable.
Problem Statement: Artificial intelligence is transforming industries worldwide, yet access to its benefits remains unequal. Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), workers, educators and local communities, particularly in developing and middle-income economies, face barriers related to digital infrastructure, AI literacy, workforce skills and access to practical innovation. Most AI tools are designed primarily for individual interaction, while industrial transformation requires cooperation, shared knowledge, collective problem-solving and continuous learning. This creates a gap between access to AI technologies and the ability to adopt them effectively across organizations. Traditional training models often struggle to provide accessible, engaging and scalable learning experiences, especially for workers with different educational backgrounds and digital competencies. As a result, digital transformation risks widening inequalities between large corporations and SMEs, highly skilled professionals and vulnerable workers, and technologically advanced territories and underserved communities. The challenge is not simply to introduce more AI into industrial environments, but to ensure that people can understand, use and benefit from AI together, developing the competencies needed to participate meaningfully in the evolving digital economy.
Solution Overview: SocialStation® and Thinks4® form an integrated physical-digital ecosystem developed by IMDEA S.r.l., an Italian innovative startup, to enable Cooperative Artificial Intelligence Environments: shared spaces where people interact with AI, collaborate, develop skills and co-create knowledge. 1. How the solution works SocialStation® is a patented interactive hardware system designed to facilitate face-to-face participation and collaborative digital experiences. It integrates a digital display, camera, computing system and illuminated physical interaction buttons, creating a shared interface between people, digital resources and AI-powered applications. Thinks4® is the cooperative AI software environment that supports collaborative learning, content production and knowledge sharing. Rather than limiting AI interaction to isolated users and individual devices, the system enables groups to work around a common physical-digital interface, supporting participation, discussion and collective problem-solving. The platform can be deployed in educational institutions, vocational training centres, innovation hubs and workplace learning environments. 2. Methodologies and technologies The solution combines proprietary interactive hardware, AI-assisted content creation, collaborative learning methodologies and digital engagement tools. Its cooperative methodology is organized around four actions: Orient: identify needs, explore information and define learning objectives. Inspire: stimulate ideas, creativity and knowledge exchange. Elaborate: collaboratively develop content, solutions and learning outputs. Share: communicate results and disseminate knowledge. Thinks4® provides AI-assisted tools for creating multimedia learning materials, presentations, podcasts, videos, quizzes and other digital outputs. Interactive engagement mechanisms, gamification and learning analytics support participation and facilitate the monitoring of educational activities. The physical-digital approach is designed to encourage human interaction, rather than replacing it with automated processes. 3. Industrial applications and inclusive transformation The solution offers a foundation for workforce upskilling, AI literacy and collaborative knowledge development in industrial ecosystems. Potential applications include vocational training, employee onboarding, collaborative problem-solving, workplace knowledge transfer and digital-skills development for SMEs. In developing and middle-income economies, the model could support inclusive access to AI-enabled learning through shared installations in training centres, industrial hubs and community facilities. The objective is to make AI adoption more accessible and participatory, including for individuals who may have limited access to personal digital devices or advanced technical skills. 4. Partnerships and collaboration model IMDEA combines proprietary technology development with applied educational experimentation and an expanding international research and industrial network. Its activities include collaborations with educational institutions and engagement with academic researchers, technology companies and innovation ecosystems. IMDEA has also joined the NVIDIA Inception programme, supporting its international technology development and networking strategy. The proposed international deployment model combines local pilot projects, partnerships with vocational training providers, research institutions and industrial stakeholders, and scalable hardware-software delivery. Through licensing, equipment deployment, training services and local partnerships, the solution is designed to support adaptation to different territorial, educational and industrial needs. 5. Innovation and value proposition The distinctive feature of SocialStation® and Thinks4® is the integration of patented physical interaction technology with cooperative AI software and a structured methodology for human-centred collabora
Solution Provider(s): IMDEA S.r.l. (Italy) – Solution owner, technology developer and innovative SME specializing in patented physical-digital infrastructure and cooperative AI, NVIDIA Inception (Global) – Startup support programme providing access to technology resources and innovation ecosystem opportunities, Italian educational institutions and vocational training partners – Operational ecosystem supporting the implementation and evaluation of collaborative digital learning experiences, International academic and research network – Research dialogue and potential cooperation in human-centred AI, collaborative learning, educational technologies and AI-enabled skills development.
Implementation location(s): Italy – Naples, Campania Region. IMDEA Innovation Living Lab, based at Fabbrica Italiana dell'Innovazione, Naples, featuring six SocialStation installations. Additional educational and collaborative learning activities have been conducted with schools and educational institutions across the Campania Region, including Naples and its metropolitan area.
Implementation timeline(s): 2025–ongoing (October 2026). Implementation and applied experimentation in educational and collaborative learning environments in the Campania Region, Italy, including activities conducted through IMDEA's Innovation Living Lab and its network of educational institutions.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Estimated 3–6 months from the formalization of a local partnership, subject to hardware availability, logistics and regulatory requirements. This timeframe includes local needs assessment, adaptation of training content, hardware deployment, software configuration, facilitator onboarding and the launch of an initial pilot in a vocational training centre, SME innovation hub or industrial skills development facility.
Desired impact: The primary objective of SocialStation® and Thinks4® is to democratize access to Artificial Intelligence by transforming individual digital interaction into collaborative learning, knowledge creation and workforce development. Developed by IMDEA S.r.l., the solution aims to: 1. Expand access to AI-powered tools and digital skills, particularly for underserved communities, SMEs and workers with different educational backgrounds. 2. Strengthen workforce upskilling, reskilling and lifelong learning through cooperative AI environments. 3. Support human-centred digital transformation by integrating physical participation, AI-assisted content creation and collaborative problem-solving. 4. Enable vocational training institutions, innovation hubs and industrial ecosystems to adopt scalable and inclusive AI-enabled learning models. 5. Reduce barriers to participation in the digital economy through shared access to technology and locally adaptable training methodologies. DEMONSTRATED ACTIVITIES AND OUTPUTS During 2025–2026, IMDEA's educational and collaborative innovation activities have included: - Approximately 900 hours of training activities. - Production of 17 short films, 20 podcasts, 3 music videos and 5 masterclasses. - Implementation of 6 Scuola Viva educational initiatives. - Development of an innovation Living Lab in Naples with 6 physical-digital workstations. - Engagement with an educational network of more than 20 schools. These figures represent documented operational activities and outputs. They do not constitute independent evidence of industrial productivity improvements or quantified employment impacts. EXPECTED INDUSTRIAL AND SOCIAL IMPACT Through future industrial and vocational training pilots, the solution aims to improve access to AI skills, strengthen workforce adaptability and support cooperative knowledge transfer within SMEs. Pilot projects will be designed to measure the number of participants trained, improvements in AI and digital competencies, participation and completion rates, collaborative learning outcomes and organizational adoption. By connecting people, technology and local institutions, SocialStation® and Thinks4® seek to contribute to SDG 4 (Quality Education), SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth) and SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure). The long-term ambition is to make AI-driven industrial transformation more inclusive, measurable and accessible across different geographical and socioeconomic contexts.
Key technologies: SocialStation® and Thinks4® integrate proprietary physical-digital infrastructure, Artificial Intelligence and collaborative learning technologies into a unified human-centred ecosystem. The main technological components include: 1. PATENTED INTERACTIVE HARDWARE SocialStation® is a patented interactive physical-digital system (Italian patent application/publication reference: 202024000004284, classification G09B) integrating a 32-inch display, embedded computing unit, wide-angle camera, LED-based interface and four illuminated physical interaction buttons. Its architecture enables shared digital experiences and collaborative interaction in physical environments. 2. AI-POWERED SOFTWARE Thinks4® provides an AI-assisted cooperative environment supporting educational content generation, knowledge organization, chatbot interaction and collaborative digital production. The platform includes tools for developing videos, podcasts, presentations, e-books, quizzes and other digital learning resources. 3. COOPERATIVE INTERACTION TECHNOLOGY The system integrates physical interaction with structured collaborative workflows, enabling participants to contribute through a shared interface rather than relying exclusively on individual devices. Its four-stage methodology — Orient, Inspire, Elaborate and Share — structures cooperative learning and content development. 4. GAMIFICATION AND ANALYTICS Interactive engagement tools, cooperative activities, token-based mechanisms and digital analytics support participation and facilitate the monitoring of learning processes. 5. MODULAR PHYSICAL-DIGITAL ARCHITECTURE The combination of dedicated hardware and software enables deployment in schools, vocational training centres, workplaces, innovation hubs and other shared environments. The system is designed to support future adaptations to different languages, training contexts and sector-specific learning requirements. Together, these technologies establish a foundation for Cooperative AI Environments that combine artificial intelligence with physical presence, human interaction and collective knowledge creation.
Unique Characteristics: The core innovation of SocialStation® and Thinks4® is the transformation of Artificial Intelligence from an individual digital tool into a shared, physical-digital environment for human cooperation. The solution differentiates itself through five interconnected features. 1. FROM INDIVIDUAL AI TO COOPERATIVE AI While many AI applications are primarily designed for individual users, SocialStation® and Thinks4® enable collaborative interaction around shared technology. AI becomes a resource for collective learning, dialogue and knowledge creation. 2. PATENTED PHYSICAL-DIGITAL INTEGRATION SocialStation® combines proprietary interactive hardware with cooperative AI software, creating a distinctive interface between physical participation and digital intelligence. This approach differs from conventional individual AI applications and standard digital display systems. 3. HUMAN-CENTRED COOPERATION METHODOLOGY The four-stage framework — Orient, Inspire, Elaborate and Share — structures participation and collaborative production. The technology is designed to enhance human interaction and the role of facilitators, educators and trainers rather than replace them. 4. SHARED ACCESS AND INCLUSIVE DEPLOYMENT A single physical installation can support group activities, offering an alternative to training approaches based exclusively on individual access to personal devices and software. This model could help institutions extend access to AI-enabled learning in resource-constrained environments. 5. SCALABLE HARDWARE-SOFTWARE BUSINESS MODEL The solution supports a combination of equipment deployment, software licensing, training services and local implementation partnerships. This enables potential adaptation to educational institutions, vocational training centres, SMEs and industrial innovation hubs. Its differentiating value lies not in claiming to replace existing industrial AI systems, but in addressing a frequently overlooked challenge: the human, collaborative and organizational capabilities required for inclusive AI adoption. SocialStation® and Thinks4® propose a new interface between people and artificial intelligence, where technological innovation is designed around cooperation rather than isolation.
Sustainable Change: SocialStation® and Thinks4® have the potential to contribute to systemic change by establishing Cooperative AI Environments as shared infrastructure for inclusive digital transformation. The proposed approach moves beyond isolated technology adoption and focuses on building sustainable local capabilities through collaboration among enterprises, training institutions, research organizations and communities. 1. STRENGTHENING LOCAL AI CAPABILITIES Deploying Cooperative AI Environments in vocational training centres, SME clusters and innovation hubs could provide shared access to AI-powered learning resources. Local facilitators and trainers could develop the skills required to support continuous learning, knowledge exchange and practical AI adoption. 2. CREATING REPLICABLE COOPERATION MODELS The combination of standardized hardware, adaptable software and a structured cooperation methodology creates a foundation for replication across different territories and sectors. Local partners could adapt content, languages and training activities to specific workforce needs while maintaining a common technological framework. 3. CONNECTING EDUCATION AND INDUSTRY The model could strengthen relationships between educational institutions, vocational training providers and enterprises, facilitating knowledge transfer and the development of skills relevant to evolving industrial occupations. 4. SUPPORTING INCLUSIVE INDUSTRIAL ECOSYSTEMS Shared access to cooperative AI infrastructure could lower organizational barriers to experimentation and help smaller enterprises participate in digital transformation initiatives. This is particularly relevant in developing and middle-income economies, where limited resources and unequal access to technology may constrain AI adoption. 5. SCALING THROUGH PARTNERSHIPS IMDEA envisages international expansion through partnerships with research institutions, technology providers, local enterprises, innovation hubs and development organizations. A deployment model combining hardware installations, SaaS licensing, facilitator training and local support services could enable progressive expansion beyond individual pilot sites. 6. EVIDENCE-BASED SYSTEMIC IMPACT Future industrial pilots will seek to establish measurable evidence of learning outcomes, workforce participation, technology adoption and organizational capability development. The results could inform replication strategies and partnerships with institutions seeking to strengthen inclusive digital skills ecosystems. The long-term vision is to shift from Artificial Intelligence used by isolated individuals towards Cooperative Artificial Intelligence accessible to organizations and communities. Through this approach, digital transformation can become not only a technological process, but a collective opportunity for learning, participation and sustainable industrial development.

Title: IoT.Factora: AI copilot and live IoT inside the factory ERP
Subtitle: Live temperature, energy and machine monitoring tied to batches, work orders and cost per unit, with SMS/WhatsApp alerts and an AI copilot, for food processors and manufacturers.
Problem Statement: Food and agro-processors and manufacturers in developing and middle-income economies still check cold rooms, intake points and machines by hand and record them on paper. Temperature drift goes unseen until product spoils, energy is only known as a monthly bill, and breakdowns are found after they happen. FAO estimates that 13.2% of food produced worldwide was lost after harvest and before retail in 2021, rising to 19.9% in sub-Saharan Africa (FAO, SDG 12.3.1a). The results for plants are food loss, wasted electricity and diesel, failed audits and lost buyers. Existing monitoring tools are standalone dashboards disconnected from production records, so readings rarely change what the plant does, and many assume reliable power and connectivity.
Solution Overview: IoT.Factora is the IoT and AI module of FactoraERP, an operating system for food and agro-processing plants. Gateways and sensors (kits from hardware partners such as Teltonika and Milesight) stream temperature, energy and vibration readings over MQTT, OPC-UA, Modbus or HTTPS. Gateways buffer readings when power or the network drops and sync later, and offline sensors raise their own alert. Readings land inside FactoraERP, the system that already runs production, storage, maintenance and finance: a cold-room reading attaches to the batch in that room, an alarm opens a maintenance work order, energy is costed per unit produced, and temperature audit trails export in one click. Alerts are live by SMS, WhatsApp and email, integrated via the Africa's Talking API, and go to a named person whose acknowledgement is recorded. An AI copilot answers plain-language questions such as "which batch was in Cold Room 2 when it drifted last night?" from the plant's own records, and explains each alert in context. Methodology: deploy commodity sensors and gateways in under a day, baseline the plant for two weeks, then track excursions, response times, energy per unit and downtime. Collaboration model: hardware partners supply kits, our team handles integration, onboarding and operator training through the FactoraERP Academy, and integrators and channel partners extend reach to new countries.
Solution Provider(s): Teltonika (Lithuania; industrial IoT gateways and networking hardware), Milesight (China; IoT sensors and gateways), Africa's Talking (Kenya; SMS and messaging API used for live alerts), Purevado (Kenya; agro-processing venture in the Tamalaki group with an avocado-oil plant in Thika, first pilot candidate)
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 4–6 weeks: about one week to ship and install sensor and gateway kits and connect the plant, then a two-week baseline and the start of live monitoring.
Desired impact: Objectives: cut food loss in processing and cold storage, cut energy use per unit produced, and give processors audit-ready food-safety records so they can keep demanding buyers. Expected impact, to be measured in the first pilot and reported openly: fewer temperature excursions and faster response (time from alert to acknowledgement), kilograms of product saved, kWh and cost per unit produced, and hours of unplanned downtime avoided. We have no demonstrated customer results yet; the platform is live with a demo plant and the first pilot is being prepared at the Purevado avocado-oil plant in Thika, Kenya. Co-benefits: lower diesel and electricity use (lower emissions), and skilled operator roles through FactoraERP Academy training.
Key technologies: Industrial IoT (temperature, energy and vibration sensors; edge gateways with store-and-forward buffering; MQTT, OPC-UA, Modbus and HTTPS ingest); a cloud ERP data model that binds every reading to batches, storage bins, assets and work orders; live SMS, WhatsApp and email alerting via the Africa's Talking API with named acknowledgement; and AI: a copilot that answers questions grounded in the plant's own records and explains alerts, with anomaly detection on temperature and energy profiles and predictive maintenance from vibration as the next steps on pilot data.
Unique Characteristics: Most factory-monitoring tools stop at a dashboard. IoT.Factora lives inside the ERP, so a reading is evidence attached to the batch, the bin and the work order by design, not by an integration project. That turns monitoring into action (automatic work orders, named alerts, energy cost per unit) and audit records in one click. It's designed for real plant conditions: gateways buffer readings through power and network outages, alerts reach people by SMS and WhatsApp as well as email, and commodity partner hardware keeps deployment simple for SMEs. Delivery model: hardware partners supply kits, we integrate and train operators, and integrators and channel partners replicate the model in new countries.
Sustainable Change: Food loss in processing and storage is a sector-wide problem, not a single-plant one. Because IoT.Factora uses standard protocols and commodity hardware, the same deployment pattern can be replicated across dairies, tea and coffee factories, edible-oil processors, packhouses and cold stores in any country. Pilot results will be published, giving processors, industry associations and development programmes a measured reference for monitoring-led loss and energy reduction. Batch-level temperature evidence also helps SMEs meet buyer and regulatory requirements, opening markets for processed goods and keeping value addition and skilled jobs close to where food is grown. Over time, anonymised plant data can support sector benchmarks for energy per unit and loss rates.
Funding Sources: Self-funded by Tamalaki Business Network Ltd; no external funding to date.

Title: Awibi EHR
Subtitle: AI integrated Multimodal Electronic Health Record System
Problem Statement: Many healthcare facilities across Africa still depend on paper records, manual documentation and separate systems for managing patient information. This makes it difficult to retrieve medical histories, share information between departments and maintain consistent clinical records. Clinical information also comes in different forms, including handwritten notes, spoken consultations and printed documents. Converting these into usable digital records often requires additional time and effort from healthcare workers
Solution Overview: Awibi EHR connects records, clinical workflows and billing for smaller African healthcare facilities. It is developing speech, handwriting and other clinical intelligence tools alongside the EHR, with third-party integrations planned.
Solution Provider(s): A
Implementation location(s): Nigeria, (Kwara state in Ilorin, Osun state in Osogbo and Ede)
Implementation timeline(s): began in 2024 and still ongoing
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3–6 months
Desired impact: Our main objective is to make clinical records easier to manage and improve how healthcare facilities capture and use patient information, to show impacts to: - Reduce the manual work involved in clinical documentation. - Improve access to patient histories and medical records. - Support communication and information sharing between hospital departments. - Develop clinical AI tools that can work with speech, handwriting and medical documents. - Make selected clinical intelligence capabilities accessible to other healthcare software providers. During pilot, we measure documentation time, record retrieval, system reliability, transcription accuracy and healthcare worker feedback. Our solution will support more efficient clinical operations.
Key technologies: Our technologies ranges from AI, Fullsack software for desktop, mobile (React.js, Node.js, Electron.js, React Native) and extensive database operations (PostgreSQL). Our main intelligence technologies areas include: - Speech Recognition: Converting spoken clinical information into text. - Optical Character Recognition (OCR): Extracting text from printed and handwritten medical documents. - Natural Language Processing: Identifying and organizing relevant information from clinical text. - Structured Record Extraction: Converting medical documents and notes into organized clinical data. - Machine Learning: Developing and adapting models for clinical documentation tasks. - Clinical Decision Support: Using clinical information and defined rules to support calculations and information retrieval. - FastAPI - Application Programming Interfaces (APIs): Supporting integrations with other healthcare systems.
Unique Characteristics: we built a day to day hospital management software with the training of different multimodal clinical intelligence. we are different because we focus on how medical information is recorded in practice, including spoken consultations, handwritten notes and existing medical documents in an Offline, easy to access approach, even to the least infrastructure environments, across Africa. We are developing models that can recognize and extract information from these diverse traditional methods of health information sources, organize it into structured clinical records and allow healthcare professionals to review the results. This includes work on Nigerian clinical speech, handwriting and medical documentation. we plan to make these intelligence models available to other healthcare software providers through API integrations. Hospitals could then use selected Awibi technologies within their existing systems without having to adopt AwibiEHR itself.
Sustainable Change: AwibiEHR could help more healthcare facilities move from unstructured records and manual documentation towards organized digital clinical information and network of clinical intelligence. Beyond our own EHR, we want to develop clinical intelligence tools that other healthcare software providers can integrate into their systems. This could make speech recognition, handwriting processing and structured medical record extraction more accessible to smaller healthcare organizations. As the technology develops, we also hope to work with healthcare institutions and researchers to improve clinical AI models for African languages, documentation formats and clinical practices.

Title: Central Energy Data Repository
Subtitle: A grounded, queryable knowledge infrastructure for Europe's energy transition, and the data engine behind the Community Intelligence Platform and the Energy AI
Problem Statement: Europe's energy knowledge is fragmented, duplicated, and hard to trust. - Fragmented by design: Regulators, EU-funded projects, associations and think tanks each publish independently. Different formats, platforms and languages, with no shared index. - Costly to find and verify: Consultants, policymakers and researchers spend real hours per query re-discovering what already exists, and cannot always tell current guidance from superseded versions. - Duplicated research effort: Academia and innovators repeatedly re-run studies or feasibility checks because prior public work is not discoverable; a direct, avoidable cost to the sector. - Legal ambiguity blocks reuse: Most valuable content is copyrighted or ToS-restricted. Ad hoc scraping creates real legal exposure; nobody has systematized which sources can be used, and how.
Solution Overview: A tiered ingestion and retrieval infrastructure that turns fragmented public energy content into one coherent, cited, queryable knowledge base; the technical backbone behind the Energy AI (TEBi). - Tiered ingestion: API-first (IEA, Ember, IRENA...), RSS feeds, permitted crawling, manual curation; matched per source to its legal access terms. - Structuring & entity resolution: Structured metadata schema per document; NLP-based resolution so the same institution, regulation, or technology is recognized across sources. - Freshness & citation grounding: Content-hash change detection flags outdated content; every TEBi answer links back to a traceable source document; no answer without a citation. - Hybrid, legally-sound storage: TEB-owned content is hosted; external institutional content is indexed and linked, never redistributed; avoiding copyright exposure by design.
Solution Provider(s): TU Wien, E-Control, AI Factory Austria
Implementation location(s): Prototype with AUstria and Romania
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 1 month for each new country
Desired impact: The main objective is to develop an EU sovereign connector-management system, not just a universal scraper in the energy sector, but one where ingestion method, storage, and redistribution rights are configured per source and revisited on an ongoing basis as terms change. Also being a model that never answer without a traceable citation to a source document, including across content the platform indexes but does not host; a stricter constraint than typical RAG deployments, especially where answers can inform investment or policy decisions. Distinguishing genuinely current regulatory guidance from silently-superseded content requires content-hash monitoring plus reasoning about document relationships, not just a "last modified" timestamp, which is often missing or unreliable at the source. Thus, the same regulator, technology or regulation appears under different names, languages and formats across 30+ heterogeneous sources. Resolving this reliably, without a labeled ground-truth dataset, is an open NLP/ML problem, not a solved library import.
Key technologies: AI to vectorize and create knowledge graphs
Unique Characteristics: The digitalization of the Energy European regulation, making it language compatible with all the EU languages, queryable and reliable
Sustainable Change: This solution contributes to the EU digital sovereignty with regulation of a critical sector as Energy, and also allows to identify gaps, learnings and opportunities Amon energy regulation across the EU.
Funding Sources: Bootstrap & Angel investors
Primary thematic focus area: Industrial Digital Infrastructure and Data Ecosystems
Summary: The Central Energy Data Repository turns fragmented European energy publications into a cited, queryable knowledge base with per-source rights management. The information-governance design is careful; thin technical detail and a two-country prototype hold it to 49.

Title: BioCert: Decentralized AI-Blockchain Organic Certification Framework
Subtitle: An intelligent, tamper-proof bio-certification system combining AI anomaly detection with blockchain traceability for sustainable agri-food supply chains.
Problem Statement: Traditional organic certification frameworks suffer from centralized governance, fragmented data management, limited transparency, and vulnerability to fraud. While blockchain guarantees immutability once data is stored, it cannot verify the truthfulness of input data (the Oracle Problem). Furthermore, conventional rule-based systems fail to handle uncertainty or distinguish statistical anomalies from true non-compliance, limiting trust across agricultural supply chains.
Solution Overview: BioCert is a decentralized, multi-layered architecture designed for automated, transparent bio-certification
Implementation location(s): Hammam Sousse, Sousse, Tunisia
Implementation timeline(s): September 2025 – June 2026
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3 to 6 months
Desired impact: Enhancing Supply Chain Transparency: Establishes end-to-end auditability and trust for organic agricultural products through cryptographic proofs. Automating Certification & Fraud Prevention: Reduces certification processing time to under 0.2 seconds per decision while filtering input data fraud via AI pre-validation. Empowering Smallholder Farmers: Lowers certification overhead and provides verifiable proof of organic practices, facilitating fair market access and sustainable agriculture.
Key technologies: Artificial Intelligence (Isolation Forest, Scikit-learn, Python FastAPI ), Blockchain (Ethereum Sepolia, Solidity ERC-721 smart contracts), Decentralized Storage (IPFS via Pinata), Backend (Java Spring Boot, PostgreSQL), IoT Sensors & Web Interface (React, TypeScript).
Unique Characteristics: Pre-Blockchain AI Validation: Solves the "Oracle Problem" by evaluating data reliability and detecting anomalies using Isolation Forest before anchoring records on-chain. Hybrid On-Chain/Off-Chain Architecture: Stores sensitive, high-volume data off-chain in PostgreSQL/IPFS while recording lightweight NFT cryptographic certificates on-chain for maximum scalability and gas efficiency. Multi-Criteria Compliance Scoring: Combines weighted multi-source data (IoT, lab analyses, manual audits) with intelligent fallback rules for uncertain cases.
Sustainable Change: BioCert shifts the paradigm from static, centralized, rule-based auditing to a decentralized, data-driven trust ecosystem. By bridging AI anomaly detection with immutable blockchain ledgers, the framework can be replicated across diverse agricultural sectors (e.g., olive oil, dates, cereals) and scaled to national or international regulatory bodies, setting a new standard for sustainable digital trade and transparent agri-food supply chains in developing economies.
Funding Sources: Academic research funding from the Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research (Tunisia), supported through university laboratory resources (Miracl Laboratory and ISITCOM, University of Sousse) and computational infrastructure provided for Master's thesis research.
Testimonials and Endorsements: BioCert bridges a critical gap in agricultural traceability by combining AI-driven anomaly detection with immutable blockchain certificates. It tackles the traditional 'Oracle Problem' in food supply chains before data gets stored on-chain, proving highly effective for organic olive oil verification in Tunisia." – Research Supervisors, ISITCOM & Efrei Research Lab.
Primary thematic focus area: Industrial Digital Infrastructure and Data Ecosystems
Summary: BioCert is a research framework from Sousse that combines anomaly detection with on-chain certificates for organic produce. The idea is well placed for Mediterranean olive oil and the evidence is a paper, which is more than most concepts here and less than a deployment.

Title: ARIC: AI-Powered Mineral-to-Industry Intelligence for Africa
Subtitle: An AI-enabled industrial intelligence platform connecting Africa's natural resources with evidence-based processing, manufacturing, circular value chains and sustainable industrial investment.
Problem Statement: Africa possesses significant mineral and natural resource endowments but frequently captures only a limited share of their potential industrial value. Many resource-producing economies continue to export unprocessed or minimally processed materials while importing higher-value manufactured products. This challenge is compounded by fragmented geological, environmental, trade and industrial information; limited integration between resource identification and manufacturing planning; inadequate visibility into processing and refining opportunities; and difficulties translating resource evidence into investment-ready industrial projects. Governments, investors, manufacturers and development institutions often lack an integrated digital intelligence system capable of connecting verified resource information with industrial value chains, infrastructure requirements, environmental considerations and circular economy opportunities. These information gaps can contribute to missed industrial investment opportunities, inefficient resource utilization, limited local value addition and slower progress toward sustainable industrialization. ARIC addresses these challenges through an AI-enabled, evidence-aware resource-to-industry intelligence platform designed to support more informed industrial planning and decision-making.
Solution Overview: The African Resources Intelligence Center (ARIC) is an AI-enabled industrial intelligence platform developed as an affiliated technology initiative of Bethel Quant Trading Technologies Limited Company. ARIC is designed to connect natural resource intelligence with industrial processing, refining, manufacturing, infrastructure planning, market opportunities and circular economy pathways. How the solution works 1. Resource intelligence and data integration: ARIC integrates available geological, geospatial, satellite-derived, environmental, trade and industrial datasets from relevant sources. Its architecture supports source-specific data adapters, normalization and structured evidence management. 2. Evidence verification and governance: Information follows an evidence-aware workflow involving source identification, normalization, pending evidence, human review and verified records. This helps distinguish supported findings from unverified claims and analytical estimates. 3. AI-assisted industrial assessment: The platform supports analysis of how identified resources may relate to processing, refining, manufacturing and downstream industrial opportunities. Its objective is to connect resource availability with potential industrial development pathways rather than treating mineral identification as an isolated activity. 4. Industrial value-chain intelligence: ARIC models the resource lifecycle from identification and extraction through processing, refining, manufacturing, product markets, recovery, recycling and secondary material utilization. 5. Environmental and sustainability intelligence: The platform incorporates environmental information and is being expanded to support historical environmental assessment, resource stewardship and circular industrial development. 6. Decision-support and reporting: ARIC provides web-based intelligence interfaces, mapped evidence, structured industrial assessments and downloadable dossiers intended to support institutional research, investment screening and industrial planning. Methodologies and technologies ARIC combines geospatial data integration, satellite Earth observation, structured data processing, AI-assisted analysis, evidence provenance, human-in-the-loop verification, relational databases, web-based visualization and automated reporting. Its software architecture is designed to accommodate additional country datasets, industrial sectors and analytical modules over time. Partnership and collaboration model ARIC is developed under Bethel Quant Trading Technologies Limited Company. Its proposed collaboration model involves public institutions, geological agencies, research organizations, industrial enterprises, manufacturers, development institutions and data providers. ARIC seeks technical validation, institutional pilot partnerships, research collaboration and opportunities to demonstrate its industrial intelligence capabilities. Proposed collaborations should not be interpreted as existing formal partnerships unless independently confirmed.
Solution Provider(s): Bethel Quant Trading Technologies Limited Company — Ghanaian-founded technology company and originating development organization affiliated with ARIC; sector: artificial intelligence, software engineering, data analytics and digital technology. ARIC is currently seeking formal technical, research, industrial and institutional partnerships. No additional organizations are represented as confirmed implementation partners at this stage.
Implementation location(s): Ghana — initial geographic focus and foundation for resource and industrial intelligence development. The ARIC software platform is deployed online and accessible internationally at https://aric.betheltradingtechnologies.com. Development and technical administration are conducted remotely, including from Barbados. Broader deployment across African countries is planned. No completed on-site industrial implementation is claimed.
Implementation timeline(s): 2026–present: Software development, deployment, technical validation and progressive expansion of ARIC’s resource intelligence, evidence governance, industrial value-chain analysis and reporting capabilities. Initial geographic focus: Ghana. Institutional and industrial field pilots remain prospective and will depend on appropriate implementation partners, data access, validation arrangements and available resources.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Approximately 3–6 months for a scoped pilot in a new African geography, subject to data availability, institutional cooperation, infrastructure readiness and validation requirements. The proposed pilot would include stakeholder engagement, identification and integration of authoritative national datasets, adaptation of resource and industrial classifications, evidence validation, configuration of analytical workflows, user testing and pilot reporting. This is a planning estimate, not a previously demonstrated deployment timeline. More complex or data-restricted jurisdictions may require additional time.
Desired impact: Main objectives 1. Improve access to structured, traceable and evidence-based information about Africa’s natural resources and associated industrial opportunities. 2. Connect resource intelligence with processing, refining, manufacturing, infrastructure and market-development pathways. 3. Support more informed industrial investment screening, government planning and institutional research. 4. Promote local value addition, circular material flows, resource efficiency and sustainable industrial development. 5. Develop a scalable digital intelligence framework adaptable to multiple African countries and resource categories. Demonstrated technical progress ARIC has developed a web-based platform with resource intelligence workflows, evidence governance, industrial lifecycle modelling, administrative capabilities and downloadable industrial dossiers. The initial implementation foundation focuses on Ghana, while the broader architecture is intended for expansion across Africa. Expected impact ARIC aims to reduce information fragmentation, improve the traceability of industrial evidence, shorten the time required for preliminary industrial opportunity assessment and strengthen the identification of local processing and manufacturing opportunities. Potential longer-term outcomes include better-targeted industrial investments, stronger local value chains, resource efficiency improvements and employment opportunities. Impact measurement Future institutional pilots will seek to measure the number of verified resource records, industrial opportunities assessed, value chains mapped, decision-support reports produced, participating institutions and investment opportunities identified. Environmental outcomes may be evaluated through resource-efficiency, material recovery and relevant emissions indicators where sufficient baseline data exists. No independently verified greenhouse gas reductions, energy savings, jobs created or industrial investment outcomes are claimed at this stage.
Key technologies: ARIC integrates several complementary digital technologies: * Artificial intelligence and AI-assisted analytics: Support for resource-to-industry research, information synthesis and industrial decision-support workflows. * Geospatial information systems and Earth observation: Integration of satellite-derived and geographic information for resource and environmental intelligence. * Remote sensing: Support for optical and radar-derived observations, including relevant public Earth observation datasets. * Structured data integration and normalization: Source-specific adapters and standardized records for combining geological, environmental, industrial and trade information. * Evidence provenance and human-in-the-loop validation: Workflows designed to preserve source traceability and distinguish verified evidence from pending or unconfirmed information. * Industrial value-chain modelling: Digital representation of extraction, processing, refining, manufacturing, product markets, recovery and recycling pathways. * Cloud-based software infrastructure: Web applications, application programming interfaces, databases and background processing services. * Automated reporting and visualization: Interactive information interfaces, evidence-linked assessments and downloadable industrial intelligence dossiers. Robotics, autonomous factories and physical industrial control systems are prospective industrial development areas, not claimed as already deployed ARIC technologies.
Unique Characteristics: ARIC’s principal innovation is its integrated resource-to-industry intelligence approach. Many existing systems specialize in geological information, satellite observation, environmental monitoring, commodity trade or industrial statistics. ARIC is designed to connect these information domains into a structured industrial decision-support workflow. Key differentiating features include: 1. Resource-to-industry integration: Connects natural resource evidence with potential processing, refining, manufacturing and market opportunities. 2. Evidence-aware intelligence: Uses source provenance, structured normalization and human review to help prevent unverified information from being presented as established evidence. 3. Circular industrial lifecycle: Extends beyond extraction and production to include material recovery, recycling, secondary resources and remanufacturing. 4. Industrial opportunity orientation: Focuses on what can potentially be manufactured from available resources, what intermediate processing stages may be required and what infrastructure gaps should be investigated. 5. Continental scalability: Designed for adaptation across African countries and resource categories, subject to authoritative data access and local validation. 6. Institutional reporting: Combines digital evidence management with structured industrial assessments and downloadable dossiers intended to support planning and investment screening. 7. African-led technology development: Developed as an African-focused technology initiative seeking to strengthen domestic analytical capacity and industrial decision-making. ARIC’s distinctive contribution is the integration of these capabilities into one evidence-aware industrial intelligence framework, rather than a claim that each underlying technology is individually unprecedented.
Sustainable Change: ARIC has the potential to contribute to a structural shift in how African economies identify, assess and develop opportunities for resource-based industrialization. The platform is designed to move beyond fragmented resource information toward an integrated framework connecting evidence, industrial processing requirements, manufacturing opportunities, infrastructure needs, markets and circular material flows. Potential systemic effects include: 1. More informed industrial policy: Governments and development institutions could use evidence-linked industrial intelligence to investigate domestic processing opportunities, infrastructure priorities and potential manufacturing value chains. 2. Stronger local value addition: Better visibility into downstream industrial opportunities could help stakeholders evaluate alternatives to exporting unprocessed or minimally processed materials. 3. Improved investment preparation: Structured industrial assessments could support preliminary opportunity identification, project screening and dialogue between investors, manufacturers and public institutions. 4. Cross-country knowledge exchange: A standardized, adaptable data architecture could facilitate cooperation between African countries, subject to national data governance and institutional agreements. 5. Circular and sustainable industrial development: Integrating recovery, recycling and secondary material pathways could support more resource-efficient industrial planning. 6. Strengthened local digital capabilities: Collaboration with universities, technical institutions and industrial stakeholders could create opportunities for applied research, technical training and local participation in industrial intelligence systems. 7. Replication and scale-up: ARIC’s proposed country-adapter architecture offers a pathway for expanding from its Ghana-focused foundation into additional African countries and sectors. Over time, validated institutional pilots could establish reusable methods for connecting resource evidence with industrial opportunity assessment across the continent. The intended long-term outcome is an African-led digital intelligence infrastructure that helps institutions make better-informed decisions about transforming natural resources into sustainable industrial and economic value. These are anticipated systemic outcomes. Their realization will depend on partnerships, independent validation, investment, regulatory conditions and implementation capacity.
Funding Sources: The African Resources Intelligence Center (ARIC) has been developed through founder-led initiative, technical development efforts and resources associated with Bethel Quant Trading Technologies Limited Company. Development activities have included software engineering, AI-enabled analytical capabilities, cloud infrastructure, geospatial data integration, evidence management, industrial value-chain modelling and digital reporting systems. ARIC is currently seeking institutional partnerships, technical cooperation, innovation grants and development funding to support independent validation, geographic expansion, pilot implementation and sustainable industrial intelligence applications. No external institutional grant or investment is claimed as having been awarded specifically to ARIC.
Testimonials and Endorsements: ARIC is an emerging African-led industrial intelligence initiative. Formal independent stakeholder testimonials and institutional endorsements are not yet available for publication. The platform is being positioned for technical validation, institutional engagement and pilot collaborations with relevant industrial, research and development stakeholders. Public information about the initiative is available at: https://aric.betheltradingtechnologies.com No endorsement by the United Nations, government agencies or other institutions is implied.

Title: Hormuz Industrial Intelligence Platform
Subtitle: AI-powered market, supply-chain and risk intelligence for industrial investment and operations in complex and underserved markets.
Problem Statement: Industrial companies, investors and policymakers operating in complex and underserved markets often lack reliable, structured and current data for making investment, sourcing, market-entry and operational decisions. Critical information on companies, supply chains, infrastructure, regulations, market gaps and execution risks is fragmented across multiple sources, languages and formats. This increases due-diligence costs, slows investment decisions, creates information asymmetry and makes it harder to identify viable industrial opportunities or emerging risks.
Solution Overview: Hormuz is an AI-powered industrial and market intelligence platform that transforms fragmented public, commercial and locally sourced information into structured, decision-ready intelligence. The platform combines structured company and industry databases, market and infrastructure profiles, supply-chain mapping, risk assessment tools, market monitoring and AI-assisted research. Its methodology integrates entity resolution, taxonomy-based classification, multilingual search, source verification, structured data extraction and AI synthesis. Users can evaluate companies, sectors, industrial constraints, supply-chain risks, market gaps and investment conditions through a unified platform. AI is used to interpret and connect evidence, while critical numerical and factual data remain source-based and traceable. The platform is already operational and includes company intelligence, industrial and product-chain analysis, market monitoring, investment assessment, counterparty and transaction-risk analysis, and energy and logistics intelligence. The model can be extended to other emerging and data-fragmented markets using the same architecture and methodology.
Solution Provider(s): Hormuz Group is currently the sole operator of the solution. No formal external implementation partners are committed at this stage.
Implementation location(s): Islamic Republic of Iran — web-based implementation with nationwide market and industrial coverage.
Implementation timeline(s): 2026–present. The platform is live and under continuous implementation and expansion.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Approximately 8–12 weeks for a focused pilot, depending on local data availability, language requirements and source integration.
Desired impact: Hormuz aims to reduce information asymmetry in industrial and emerging markets by turning fragmented, multilingual and difficult-to-access information into structured, decision-ready intelligence. The solution supports industrial companies, investors, SMEs and market-entry teams in identifying viable opportunities, evaluating companies and counterparties, understanding supply-chain and infrastructure constraints, and assessing regulatory and execution risks. The expected impact is faster and better-informed industrial and investment decisions, lower preliminary research and due-diligence costs, improved visibility for local companies and industrial capabilities, and stronger market access for businesses operating in information-constrained environments. The platform is already operational in Iran. Impact measurement is being expanded around indicators such as research time saved, entities and sectors mapped, assessments completed, decision-support use cases, and adoption by business users. Audited outcome metrics are not yet available.
Key technologies: The solution combines large language models, AI-assisted evidence synthesis, structured data pipelines, knowledge graphs, entity resolution, multilingual semantic search, taxonomy-driven classification, API-based data integration and web-based intelligence dashboards. AI is used to interpret, connect and summarize evidence, while factual and numerical information is maintained with source provenance and structured verification controls. The platform also uses canonical entity matching to connect different spellings, languages and references to the same company, market, location or industrial concept.
Unique Characteristics: Hormuz is not a generic AI chatbot or a conventional market-research database. It combines structured local-market data, industrial taxonomies, multilingual entity resolution, live and periodic market signals, AI-assisted research and source traceability within a single decision-support environment. Its main differentiation is the ability to create usable intelligence in markets where reliable information is fragmented across languages, institutions, websites and unstructured sources. The platform connects company intelligence, industries, product chains, infrastructure, market conditions, investment constraints and transaction risks rather than treating each as an isolated dataset. This creates a reusable intelligence layer that can be adapted to other data-fragmented emerging markets.
Sustainable Change: The solution can contribute to systemic change by lowering the information barriers that limit investment, industrial cooperation and market access in emerging economies. A common intelligence architecture for companies, industries, supply chains, infrastructure and market risks can make fragmented industrial ecosystems more visible and easier to evaluate. This can improve access to opportunities for SMEs, reduce information asymmetry between local and international businesses, and support more evidence-based investment and industrial decisions. The underlying architecture is geography-independent. New countries can be added through local data-source mapping, taxonomy adaptation, language localization and entity resolution, allowing the model to be replicated across other information-constrained markets. At scale, Hormuz could function as a shared digital intelligence layer connecting industrial data, market participants and decision-makers across multiple emerging economies.

Title: Embodied AI Brain for Sustainable Industrial Robotics
Subtitle: An edge AI computing and operating system infrastructure that equips industrial robots with real-time perception, control, decision-making, and continuous adaptation.
Problem Statement: Industrial robots often rely on fragmented hardware, cloud-dependent AI, and fixed-program control, limiting their ability to work safely and reliably in dynamic, non-standard environments. This creates high integration costs, slow deployment, frequent manual intervention, and limited scalability across manufacturing, logistics, and specialized operations.
Solution Overview: The Embodied AI Brain is an edge-based computing and operating system solution designed to provide industrial robots with an integrated “brain” for perception, control, decision-making, and continuous adaptation. It supports humanoid robots, quadruped robots, collaborative robotic arms, wheeled robots, autonomous forklifts, and specialized equipment operating in complex industrial environments. At its core, the solution combines the Dvorak ultra-heterogeneous computing architecture with the company’s MS-OS embodied operating system and brain-inspired model framework. The architecture coordinates high-performance computing, real-time motion control, and adaptive cognitive functions at the hardware level, enabling robots to process sensor data locally and respond with low latency. The platform integrates multi-modal inputs, including cameras, 3D LiDAR, and other industrial sensors, to support environment perception, object recognition, positioning, obstacle avoidance, path planning, manipulation, and human-machine interaction. The solution is delivered through this product line: - The Transcape N Series provides modular edge-AI computing products based on mature general-purpose computing modules. It offers multiple computing configurations and compatibility with mainstream industry ecosystems for rapid deployment in humanoid robots, robotic arms, and wheeled robots. The platform follows a closed-loop methodology: sensors collect real-world operational data; on-device AI fuses and interprets this information; the control system generates real-time actions; and operational feedback supports model improvement and scenario adaptation. This approach reduces dependence on cloud connectivity, improves data security, and enables robots to operate in non-standard, changing industrial settings. The company collaborates with robot original equipment manufacturers, system integrators, and industrial end users through co-development, embedded integration, pilot testing, and batch deployment models. It works with domestic leading humanoid and quadruped robot manufacturers and has supported applications in industrial manufacturing, specialized operations, research, and commercial services. The company is also developing an overseas collaboration network through its strategic presence in Singapore, supporting cross-border partnerships and future international deployment.
Solution Provider(s): Key partners are currently subject to confidentiality agreements and are therefore not publicly disclosed. They include leading Chinese humanoid robot manufacturers, quadruped robot manufacturers, autonomous forklift OEMs, industrial system integrators, and industrial end users in manufacturing, logistics, specialized operations, research, and commercial services; Singapore-based strategic partners supporting overseas market development and cross-border deployment.
Implementation location(s): China — East China: dedicated end-user test line of an industrial forklift OEM (site name confidential).
Implementation timeline(s): Q4 2025–present: small-batch supply and system integration began in Q4 2025; dedicated end-user test-line validation and scenario iteration have continued throughout 2026.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Approximately 3–6 months, including site assessment, robot and sensor integration, system configuration, operator training, test-line validation, and initial scenario adaptation.
Desired impact: The solution’s main objective is to provide industrial robots with an affordable, deployable, and locally operated embodied-AI brain that enables real-time perception, motion control, decision-making, and continuous adaptation in dynamic, non-standard environments. It aims to reduce dependence on fixed programming, fragmented computing systems, and constant human intervention while making advanced robotics easier to integrate across manufacturing, intralogistics, and specialized industrial operations. In the autonomous-forklift use case, the solution has demonstrated the following results during prototype and dedicated test-line validation: - 30% improvement in point-to-point material-handling efficiency compared with conventional manual forklift operation. - 92% recognition and grasping success rate for irregular goods in the end-user test-line environment. - ±10 mm to ±30 mm operational positioning accuracy, supporting autonomous work around non-standard racks and varied cargo placement. - Reduced interruptions and fewer manual interventions when handling dynamic obstacles and temporary changes in storage locations. Expected broader impacts include higher industrial productivity, safer human-machine collaboration, reduced rework and operational downtime, and more efficient use of equipment and materials. The solution is also designed to support lower-energy, edge-based operation by processing data locally; however, GHG-emission reductions and energy savings have not yet been independently quantified and will be measured in future scaled deployments.
Key technologies: - Embodied AI: Brain-inspired AI models for perception, decision-making, adaptive learning, and robot memory. - Edge AI computing: Dvorak ultra-heterogeneous computing architecture for low-latency, on-device processing and real-time robot control. - Multi-modal sensor fusion: Integration of 3D LiDAR, high-definition cameras, and other industrial sensors for environment perception, object recognition, positioning, and obstacle avoidance. - Real-time motion control and planning: Dynamic path planning, manipulation control, autonomous loading and unloading, and response to changing work conditions. - Embodied operating system: MS-OS provides software coordination between sensing, AI inference, decision-making, and control functions. - Continuous learning and feedback loops: Operational data supports scenario adaptation and iterative improvement of AI models.
Unique Characteristics: The solution is distinctive because it provides a full-stack, edge-based embodied-AI foundation rather than a single robot component or cloud-only AI application. Its Dvorak ultra-heterogeneous computing architecture coordinates high-performance computing, real-time control, and adaptive cognitive functions at the hardware level, enabling the “brain,” “cerebellum,” and “cortex” functions required for responsive robot operation. Key differentiators include: - Hardware-to-software integration: Dedicated embodied-AI computing products are combined with the MS-OS operating system and brain-inspired models, connecting sensing, inference, decision-making, motion control, memory, and continuous adaptation in one platform. - Local, low-latency intelligence: Multi-modal sensor data can be processed at the edge, allowing robots to respond in real time in environments where cloud connectivity, latency, privacy, or operational resilience are concerns. - Adaptation to non-standard industrial scenarios: Rather than relying only on fixed maps, standardized pallets, or pre-programmed workflows, the solution is designed for changing conditions such as irregular goods, varied rack configurations, temporary location changes, and dynamic obstacles. - Deployment model: The Transcape N Series supports rapid integration with mainstream computing and robot ecosystems. - Cognitive extension through Si-Cortex: The Si-Cortex unit is designed to enhance contextual memory and adaptive capability, helping robots improve performance as they encounter repeated operational scenarios. - Co-development delivery model: The company works with robot OEMs, system integrators, and industrial users through embedded integration, joint scenario development, test-line validation, and iterative deployment. This helps translate a general platform into validated solutions for specific industrial workflows.
Sustainable Change: The solution can support systemic change by making embodied AI a reusable industrial capability rather than a bespoke, one-off robotics project. Its modular computing products, operating system, and sensor-to-control software stack can be adapted across robot types and industrial workflows, reducing the time and technical effort required to deploy intelligent automation in new factories, warehouses, and specialized work sites. As deployments expand, it can create a repeatable model for collaboration among robot OEMs, system integrators, industrial users, and research partners. Localized edge processing also makes the solution relevant in locations where cloud access is unreliable, data must remain on site, or low-latency response is essential. This can broaden participation in industrial AI beyond large, highly digitized enterprises. Potential follow-on effects include improved productivity and reliability in material handling and manufacturing operations; safer human-machine collaboration; increased demand for local system-integration, maintenance, and AI-operations skills; and a stronger ecosystem of robot developers and industrial solution providers. The Transcape N Series can support rapid replication using mainstream ecosystems. With site-specific validation, standardized integration packages, and partnerships in new markets, the solution can be scaled from pilot installations to multi-site deployments across manufacturing, intralogistics, and specialized industrial sectors.

Title: Industrial Embodied Intelligence Full-stack Execution Solution for Flexible Manufacturing
Subtitle: A full-stack embodied AI system integrating self-developed electric grippers, dexterous hands, tactile-vision sensing and data platform. It delivers low-cost, network-light robotic manipulation for factories in developing and middle-income economies, enabling rapid deployment on existing production lines.
Problem Statement: Many manufacturers in developing and middle-income economies face high automation costs, complex integration, limited network infrastructure, and lack of flexible robotic end tools. Traditional pneumatic grippers are energy-intensive and unable to handle diverse, fragile workpieces. This solution addresses these pain points with low-power, adaptable, offline-capable embodied execution hardware and software.
Solution Overview: This solution is a full-stack embodied AI manipulation system built on Jodell’s self-developed electric grippers, dexterous robotic hands, tactile sensors and vision perception modules. It adopts edge-side lightweight AI inference, which supports offline operation without stable high-speed internet. The system integrates adaptive grasping algorithms, force-tactile closed-loop control and one-click rapid configuration, so it can be retrofitted onto existing industrial robots for sorting, assembly, handling and inspection tasks. We combine mechatronics design, tactile-vision fusion perception and lightweight embodied learning methodologies. Our collaboration model is open: we work with local system integrators, robot manufacturers and industrial SMEs in target economies to deliver on-site testing, customization and after-sales support, lowering the technical threshold for local factories.
Solution Provider(s): No fixed dedicated key partners for this project yet. We adopt open collaboration mode and intend to cooperate with regional robot integrators, local manufacturing associations and industrial SMEs in target economies for pilot deployment and scaling.
Implementation location(s): China (Suzhou, Jiangsu)
Implementation timeline(s): 2020 – Ongoing (domestic commercial deployment)
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3–4 months, including local integration testing, on-site commissioning and operator training
Desired impact: The core objective is to deliver affordable, network-light embodied AI robotic manipulation tools for manufacturing SMEs in developing and middle-income economies, lowering the threshold of flexible automation for factories with limited infrastructure. Demonstrated & expected impact: Compared with traditional pneumatic grippers, our electric end-effectors cut energy consumption by over 60%. The one-click deployment reduces production changeover time by 40%. It helps local factories stabilize output, reduce workpiece damage rate, and cultivate local robotic operation technicians, supporting inclusive industrial growth.
Key technologies: Embodied AI, lightweight edge AI inference, tactile-vision fusion perception, force-tactile closed-loop control, dexterous robotic manipulation, mechatronics of electric end-effectors, rapid visual programming for industrial robots.
Unique Characteristics: Different from expensive, cloud-dependent automation solutions, our system supports offline edge computing and does not require stable high-speed internet. It adopts plug-and-play electric grippers and dexterous hands, which can be retrofitted onto existing robot hardware without full production line replacement. We provide simplified operation training and localized technical support, tailored for resource-limited SMEs in emerging economies. The energy-saving design also brings continuous operating cost advantages.
Sustainable Change: This solution can drive systemic change by building a replicable low-cost automation model for manufacturing MSMEs across developing economies. Once validated in pilot sites, the offline, retrofittable embodied AI manipulation system can be quickly replicated across different industries and countries in Asia and the Pacific. It helps form local technical service teams, nurtures regional talent pools for robotic operation and maintenance, and shifts the local industry mindset: automation is no longer exclusive to large factories with abundant capital and stable internet. The follow-on effect will be inclusive industrial upgrading, wider adoption of energy-saving robotic equipment, and stronger resilience of regional manufacturing supply chains. We plan to share deployment cases and simplified operation guidelines with local industrial associations to accelerate scaling.
Funding Sources: Funded by company self-raised capital and internal R&D investment.
Primary thematic focus area: Embodied AI, Industrial Robotics and Smart Manufacturing
Summary: Suzhou Jodell Robotics makes grippers, hands and force-tactile control that retrofit onto existing industrial robots. The hardware line is coherent and the retrofit angle is commercially sensible; the evidence is a website, one trade story and figures with no method behind them.

Solution Overview: Futurelab Studios combines hands-on workshops for leadership teams with Forward AI deployment, where our engineers sit inside client teams to build and run AI workflows on real tasks such as sales reporting, rural distribution planning and field-force support. We also build voice agents for low-literacy, low-connectivity users; SachivG, built with Piramal Foundation, is used by about 800 public-sector functionaries. Methods: embedded delivery, reusable playbooks, workflow-level adoption tracking. Technologies: large language models, voice AI, workflow automation. Collaboration model: we work inside client teams and train their people to run the workflows. Clients include Coca-Cola, PepsiCo, Syngenta and Xiaomi.
Solution Provider(s): OpenAI (Select Partner, AI platform), Anthropic (Claude Partner Network, AI platform), Piramal Foundation (philanthropy and public-sector development, SachivG)
Implementation location(s): India
Implementation timeline(s): July 2024 to present
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6 to 8 weeks
Desired impact: Objective: help industrial and consumer-goods organisations, including MSME-linked supply chains, move from buying AI tools to using them daily, by building skills and embedding AI into real workflows. Demonstrated reach: 70+ organisations served since July 2024, about 500 leaders trained, and SachivG voice agent used by about 800 public-sector functionaries with Piramal Foundation. Key technologies: Large language models (OpenAI and Claude), voice AI agents for low-literacy and low-connectivity users, workflow automation and data integration with existing business systems.
Unique Characteristics: We deliver adoption, not just software. Our engineers work inside client teams (Forward AI deployment) and pair this with hands-on leader training. Voice-first design serves users that typical industrial AI ignores. Playbooks are reusable across clients, sectors and languages. Built in India for developing-economy conditions by a founder with 12 years in rural FMCG distribution.
