Title: AI-Powered Biomass Energy for Sustainable Industry
Subtitle: Turning agricultural residues into industrial heat and steam, with AI optimising biomass sourcing, fuel quality and energy efficiency to reduce fossil fuel use and emissions.
Problem Statement: Industries requiring process heat and steam face high energy costs, dependence on fossil fuels and pressure to reduce emissions. Meanwhile, agricultural residues are often underused or openly burned, wasting potential fuel and contributing to air pollution. Industrial adoption of biomass is constrained by seasonal availability, fragmented supply chains, variable moisture and fuel quality, and inefficient operation. The solution addresses these challenges through AI-supported biomass supply planning, fuel assessment and process optimisation, helping industries access reliable, efficient and sustainably sourced energy.
Solution Overview: AI-Powered Biomass Energy for Sustainable Industry Our proposed solution converts locally available agricultural residues and sustainably sourced biomass into heat and steam for industrial processes, reducing reliance on fossil fuels. AI supports feedstock assessment, supply planning and operational optimisation by analysing biomass availability, moisture content, energy demand and system performance. This helps industries improve combustion efficiency, manage fuel variability and monitor energy use and emissions. By connecting agricultural waste streams with industrial energy needs, the solution aims to lower energy costs, reduce greenhouse gas emissions and open-field burning, and create income opportunities for farmers and local biomass suppliers.AI-Powered Biomass Energy for Sustainable Industry Our proposed solution converts locally available agricultural residues and sustainably sourced biomass into heat and steam for industrial processes, reducing reliance on fossil fuels. AI supports feedstock assessment, supply planning and operational optimisation by analysing biomass availability, moisture content, energy demand and system performance. This helps industries improve combustion efficiency, manage fuel variability and monitor energy use and emissions. By connecting agricultural waste streams with industrial energy needs, the solution aims to lower energy costs, reduce greenhouse gas emissions and open-field burning, and create income opportunities for farmers and local biomass suppliers.
Solution Provider(s): Packages Group, Bulleh Shah Packaging, Ittehad Chemicals, StarchPack
Implementation location(s): Pakistan
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 8 months
Desired impact: The solution aims to replace part of industrial fossil fuel consumption with sustainably sourced agricultural residues for process heat and steam. AI will support reliable biomass sourcing, improve fuel selection and optimise energy performance. Expected impacts include lower fossil fuel use and associated greenhouse gas emissions, reduced energy costs, productive use of residues otherwise openly burned, and income and employment opportunities in biomass collection, processing and supply. Performance will be measured through fossil fuel displaced, useful heat delivered, biomass consumed, energy cost per unit of production, net emissions avoided and jobs created. Quantified targets will be established through site-specific baseline assessments and pilot validation, accounting for transport emissions and sustainable residue availability.
Key technologies: The proposed solution combines AI and machine learning, satellite-based biomass assessment, geographic information systems (GIS), and sensor-based industrial monitoring. Satellite and crop data will help estimate residue availability and seasonality, while AI will support procurement planning, supply forecasting and matching biomass characteristics with industrial heat demand. Sensors will monitor parameters such as fuel moisture, temperature, fuel consumption and steam output. These data will inform operational recommendations for biomass boilers and provide a digital dashboard for tracking efficiency, costs and emissions.
Unique Characteristics: The innovation lies in connecting agricultural residue supply with industrial energy operations through one AI-supported decision platform. The solution links spatial estimates of biomass availability with procurement, fuel quality and industrial heat demand, helping operators manage seasonal shortages and variable feedstock quality. Its distinctive approach combines local sourcing, traceable supply chains and continuous performance monitoring. Sustainability screening will account for competing uses of residues and the need to retain sufficient material for soil health. By linking farmers, biomass suppliers and industrial users, the solution aims to make biomass energy more reliable and commercially attractive while enabling measurable environmental and livelihood benefits.
Sustainable Change: The solution could support a sustained shift towards circular industrial energy systems by establishing reliable links between agricultural residue suppliers and industrial heat users. Predictable demand for sustainably sourced biomass can encourage investment in local collection, storage and processing businesses, creating rural income opportunities and reducing incentives for open-field burning. The digital platform can be replicated across industrial facilities and agricultural regions, adapting biomass supply forecasts and operational recommendations to local conditions. As adoption grows, shared supply networks could serve industrial clusters, improve logistics and reduce procurement costs. Verified pilot results, standardised fuel-quality requirements and transparent performance monitoring could strengthen confidence among industries, suppliers and financiers, supporting wider investment. Sustainability screening would guide expansion within available residue supplies while protecting soil health and existing agricultural uses.

Title: Smart Off-Grid Clean Cooling: AI-Powered Sustainable Refrigeration
Subtitle: AI-driven, solar-powered refrigeration combining digital twins, predictive energy management and innovative thermal storage to deliver reliable, affordable and decarbonized cooling.
Problem Statement: Industrial refrigeration faces two interconnected challenges: limited access to reliable and affordable cooling in energy-constrained regions, and the high energy consumption and carbon footprint of conventional refrigeration systems. In emerging markets, unreliable electricity infrastructure and dependence on diesel generators restrict access to refrigeration, particularly across agricultural and food supply chains, contributing to post-harvest losses and economic inefficiencies. In developed markets, industrial cooling remains energy-intensive, creating significant operating costs and decarbonization challenges. Conventional solar refrigeration solutions often rely on expensive electrochemical batteries and lack intelligent coordination between variable solar generation, thermal demand and energy storage. There is a critical need for scalable, cost-effective refrigeration technologies that combine renewable energy, innovative storage and AI-driven optimization to deliver reliable cooling independently of grid constraints while accelerating industrial decarbonization.
Solution Overview: BMTA&C Energy has developed Smart Off-Grid Clean Cooling, an innovative AI-powered refrigeration technology designed to deliver reliable, energy-efficient and low-carbon cooling for industrial and agri-food applications, both in off-grid environments and in hybrid configurations. The solution combines four complementary technological components: 1. Solar-powered refrigeration architecture: An integrated refrigeration system powered by photovoltaic energy, incorporating an innovative solar-tracking approach to maximize renewable energy generation and reduce dependence on conventional electricity sources. 2. Innovative thermal energy storage: A proprietary cooling and thermal storage architecture that stores energy in thermal rather than exclusively electrochemical form. This enables refrigeration continuity during periods of limited solar availability while significantly reducing reliance on conventional batteries. 3. AI-powered predictive energy management: A digital-twin-based intelligent control system that integrates real-time sensor inputs, climatic and weather data, photovoltaic generation forecasts, thermal storage conditions and refrigeration demand. Predictive models anticipate operating conditions and optimize energy allocation, cooling production, storage charging and discharging, and system operation to maintain refrigeration performance with minimum energy consumption. 4. Intelligent monitoring and predictive maintenance: The digital architecture is designed to support continuous performance monitoring, early detection of operating anomalies and predictive maintenance capabilities, improving equipment reliability and reducing potential downtime. Unlike conventional refrigeration systems, the solution coordinates renewable energy generation, thermal storage and cooling demand through an integrated predictive control approach, rather than treating these components independently. Technology development and industrial validation: Smart Off-Grid Clean Cooling builds on over five years of prior deep-tech R&D in innovative refrigeration technologies, during which BMTA&C Energy developed an earlier patented cooling concept that reached TRL 5. Building on this technological foundation, the company has successfully progressed its new Smart Off-Grid Clean Cooling solution from small-scale development to a validated industrial-scale pilot unit, now being prepared for field testing with OCP Group's Al Moutmir initiative in Morocco. In parallel, BMTA&C Energy is in discussions regarding a potential pilot deployment within the Rungis International Market ecosystem in France. Partnership and deployment model: BMTA&C Energy works with industrial and agricultural partners to validate the technology under real operating conditions, assess performance and prepare commercial deployment. Its business development strategy combines direct industrial collaborations with distribution partnerships to accelerate adoption across different markets. The solution addresses two complementary opportunities: expanding access to reliable refrigeration in underserved regions and decarbonizing cooling infrastructure in established industrial markets.
Solution Provider(s): OCP Group – Al Moutmir Initiative (Morocco): Agricultural innovation and sustainable farming initiative supporting the deployment and validation of BMTA&C Energy's new refrigeration technology in Morocco; Rungis International Market Ecosystem (France): One of the world's largest fresh-produce wholesale markets, involved in an industrial refrigeration pilot collaboration; ThrivAgric (Nigeria): Agritech company supporting smallholder farmers and agricultural value chains, collaborating with BMTA&C Energy on refrigeration technology deployment and validation in Nigeria; Mohammed VI Polytechnic University (UM6P) – EMINES School of Industrial Management (Morocco): Engineering, research and innovation ecosystem supporting BMTA&C Energy through incubation, technical development and prototyping.
Implementation location(s): Morocco – Benguerir: Full-scale prototype development, integration and testing at the EMINES Start-up Lab within the Mohammed VI Polytechnic University (UM6P) ecosystem. Morocco – Benslimane: Planned field deployment within the Al Moutmir/OCP Group agricultural ecosystem.
Implementation timeline(s): September 2026 – May 2027: Deployment, operation and field validation of the industrial pilot with OCP Group’s Al Moutmir initiative in Morocco.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Approximately 3–6 months, depending on site readiness, local integration requirements, equipment availability and logistics. The modular architecture is designed to facilitate adaptation to different climatic conditions, refrigeration needs and energy infrastructures.
Desired impact: BMTA&C Energy aims to transform refrigeration by making clean, reliable and affordable cooling accessible regardless of grid availability, while reducing the energy consumption, operating costs and carbon footprint of conventional refrigeration infrastructure. The solution pursues four main objectives: 1. Accelerate decarbonization: Replace or reduce dependence on fossil-fuel-based electricity and diesel generators through solar-powered refrigeration, innovative thermal energy storage and AI-driven energy optimization, significantly reducing CO₂ emissions. 2. Improve energy efficiency: Leverage digital twins, predictive AI control and real-time operating data to optimize refrigeration production, solar energy utilization and thermal storage management, minimizing energy losses and improving overall system efficiency. 3. Reduce costs and improve affordability: Reduce dependence on electrochemical batteries by up to 88% through innovative thermal storage and intelligent energy management, addressing one of the major cost barriers to off-grid refrigeration. 4. Expand access to reliable cooling: Enable continuous refrigeration in underserved regions, reducing post-harvest losses, strengthening agricultural value chains and supporting economic opportunities for farmers and distributors. Expected impact and international deployment perspectives: Morocco – OCP Group / Al Moutmir: An industrial pilot is being implemented from September 2026 to May 2027, supported by a signed commercial agreement and a Letter of Intent (LOI) for six additional units. The pilot will generate field data on energy performance, operating costs, reliability and environmental impact, with significant opportunities for nationwide scale-up through the Al Moutmir agricultural ecosystem. Nigeria – ThrivAgric: A signed LOI for the potential deployment of 50 refrigeration units, representing approximately €1.5 million in potential revenue. This collaboration aims to expand decentralized cold-chain access for agricultural producers and distributors. Nigeria – Village Farms: Ongoing discussions regarding a potential deployment of 400–1,000 refrigeration units over five years, supporting the development of decentralized agricultural cold-chain infrastructure in southeastern Nigeria. France – Rungis International Market: Advanced discussions regarding a paid pilot deployment within one of the world's largest fresh-produce wholesale markets, targeting energy-efficient and low-carbon refrigeration in an established food distribution ecosystem. These partnerships and deployment opportunities demonstrate strong market interest across Africa and Europe, with potential for significant reductions in refrigeration-related emissions, energy costs and food losses. Through its AI-powered energy management and scalable cooling architecture, BMTA&C Energy aims to accelerate the adoption of affordable, intelligent and decarbonized refrigeration worldwide.
Key technologies: Smart Off-Grid Clean Cooling integrates advanced refrigeration engineering, solar photovoltaic energy, innovative thermal energy storage and artificial intelligence within a unified intelligent energy-management architecture. 1. Artificial Intelligence and Predictive Control: AI-based predictive models anticipate refrigeration demand, solar energy availability and system operating conditions to optimize energy allocation, equipment operation and thermal storage utilization. 2. Digital Twin Technology: A dynamic digital representation of the refrigeration and energy-storage system combines physics-based modelling with real-time operational data, enabling performance prediction, scenario evaluation and intelligent control decisions. 3. IoT and Real-Time Monitoring: Integrated sensors continuously monitor key operating parameters, including temperatures, energy generation, thermal storage conditions and refrigeration system performance. These inputs feed the digital twin and intelligent control algorithms. 4. Weather and Climate Data Integration: Climatic conditions and weather forecasts are incorporated into predictive control strategies to anticipate solar energy availability and refrigeration requirements. 5. Innovative Thermal Energy Storage: An integrated thermal storage system stores energy as cooling capacity, reducing reliance on conventional electrochemical batteries and enabling refrigeration continuity during periods of limited solar generation. 6. Solar Photovoltaics and Intelligent Energy Integration: Solar energy generation is coordinated with refrigeration production and thermal storage through predictive energy management to maximize renewable energy utilization and optimize overall system performance. Together, these technologies create an intelligent refrigeration system capable of coordinating renewable energy generation, thermal storage and cooling demand through AI-driven predictive decision-making.
Unique Characteristics: BMTA&C Energy introduces a new approach to sustainable refrigeration by combining innovative thermal energy storage with AI-powered predictive energy management in an integrated, off-grid-capable architecture. Its innovation lies in the intelligent coordination of renewable energy generation, cooling production, thermal storage and refrigeration demand to overcome the technical and economic limitations of conventional cooling systems. 1. Innovative thermal storage architecture: The solution integrates thermal energy storage directly into the refrigeration system, enabling cooling autonomy during periods without solar generation while substantially reducing dependence on expensive electrochemical batteries. 2. AI-driven predictive energy optimization: Unlike conventional refrigeration controllers relying primarily on fixed thresholds and reactive operation, the solution integrates digital-twin-based predictive models, real-time sensor data and climatic forecasts to anticipate operating conditions and proactively optimize energy management. 3. Integrated off-grid refrigeration system: Rather than independently managing solar generation, refrigeration and storage, the technology coordinates these components within a unified architecture to improve energy efficiency, reliability and cost-effectiveness. 4. Dual-market opportunity: The same technological platform addresses two major challenges: expanding access to reliable refrigeration in underserved and off-grid regions, and accelerating the decarbonization of cooling infrastructure in established markets. 5. Reduced battery dependence and improved affordability: By combining thermal storage with intelligent energy management, the solution reduces the need for electrochemical batteries, addressing one of the main cost and sustainability barriers to solar-powered refrigeration. 6. Rapid development and industrial validation: Building on the team's previous experience in innovative refrigeration technologies, including five years of R&D on an earlier patented concept that reached TRL 5, BMTA&C Energy has advanced its new Smart Off-Grid Clean Cooling solution from small-scale development to a validated industrial-scale pilot unit. The technology is being prepared for field testing with OCP Group's Al Moutmir initiative in Morocco, with additional pilot opportunities under discussion internationally. This combination of intelligent energy management, innovative thermal storage and industrial adaptability positions Smart Off-Grid Clean Cooling as a scalable AI-powered solution for expanding cooling access and accelerating decarbonization.
Sustainable Change: Smart Off-Grid Clean Cooling has the potential to transform how refrigeration infrastructure is powered, managed and deployed across industrial and agricultural value chains, addressing two major global challenges: the lack of access to reliable cooling in underserved regions and the high energy consumption and carbon footprint of conventional refrigeration systems. 1. Expanding access to cooling beyond grid limitations: By enabling reliable solar-powered refrigeration with reduced dependence on electrochemical batteries, the solution can support the development of decentralized cold chains in regions with limited or unreliable electricity access. This can help reduce post-harvest losses, improve food preservation, strengthen agricultural supply chains and expand market opportunities for farmers and distributors. 2. Accelerating refrigeration decarbonization: In established markets, the technology offers an alternative to conventional energy-intensive refrigeration systems. By combining renewable energy, thermal storage and AI-driven optimization, it can support the transition toward lower-carbon cooling infrastructure while reducing long-term operating costs. 3. Demonstrating the potential of AI for sustainable industrial operations: The integration of digital twins, predictive control and real-time data demonstrates how artificial intelligence can optimize physical energy systems, moving beyond conventional monitoring toward proactive operational decision-making. This approach could also be adapted to other energy-intensive thermal applications. 4. Enabling scalable and replicable deployment: The modular architecture is designed to accommodate different climatic conditions, refrigeration requirements and energy infrastructures. Through partnerships with industrial users, agricultural organizations and distribution networks, the solution can be replicated across multiple sectors and geographies, accelerating the adoption of sustainable cooling technologies. 5. Strengthening resilient and sustainable value chains: More reliable and affordable refrigeration can improve food quality, reduce waste, support agricultural productivity and strengthen the resilience of food distribution systems. In emerging markets, this can also contribute to local economic development and new business opportunities around decentralized cold-chain services. 6. Building an ecosystem for clean cooling innovation: Through industrial collaborations, technology integration and knowledge sharing, BMTA&C Energy aims to foster wider adoption of AI-enabled clean cooling solutions and encourage cooperation between research institutions, industrial partners and local market actors. By combining technological innovation with a scalable deployment model, BMTA&C Energy seeks to contribute to a broader transition toward intelligent, decentralized and low-carbon refrigeration infrastructure, making sustainable cooling more accessible and economically viable across global markets.
Funding Sources: BMTA&C Energy has been primarily funded through non-dilutive financing, including innovation grants and R&D support from the Fund for Innovation in Development (FID, France), Bpifrance (France), and the Mohammed VI Polytechnic University (UM6P, Morocco). To date, the company has secured nearly €500,000 in non-dilutive funding to support its technological development, prototyping and validation activities. The current Smart Off-Grid Clean Cooling solution is also supported by commercial funding through a paid industrial pilot contract with Al Moutmir initiative in Morocco, contributing to its field deployment and performance validation. This combination of institutional innovation support and commercial pilot revenue demonstrates the company's ability to mobilize non-dilutive financing and growing market demand for its technology.

Title: ITIKA AI: Every Business Call Answered, in Africa's Own Languages
Subtitle: AI voice agents and a cloud call center that let African businesses answer every call in Luganda, Swahili or English, with AI and human staff working together, and no phone hardware.
Problem Statement: In Africa, most customers reach businesses by phone calls. Banks, hospitals, hotels, insurers, manufacturers, distributors and online shops all depend on these calls for sales, bookings, orders and support. Small and medium businesses can rarely staff phones all day. Calls go unanswered when staff are busy or the business is closed, and each missed call can mean a lost sale, a missed appointment or a customer who goes to a competitor. Existing call-center and voice-AI tools are built for wealthy markets. They are expensive, they need phone hardware or technical staff, and they mostly speak English. They do not understand callers who speak Luganda, Swahili or other local languages, or who mix languages in one sentence, which is normal in Uganda and East Africa. As a result, local businesses lose revenue, and customers who don't speak English well, or who can't read and write, get worse service.
Solution Overview: **How it works** ITIKA AI is a cloud call center with AI voice agents for African businesses. A business keeps its normal local phone number. When a customer calls, ITIKA routes the call according to the business's rules: - Human first: the call rings the business's staff in a web browser console (no desk phones needed). If nobody answers within a set time, the AI agent answers so the call is never lost. - AI first: the AI agent answers straight away, handles common requests, and transfers to a person when needed. - After hours: the AI answers outside business hours. The AI agent speaks English, Swahili and Luganda (the caller chooses on a keypad menu, and the choice is remembered for later calls). It answers questions from the business's own documents (FAQs, price lists, policies), takes messages, and uses the business's systems through secure tools (for example, checking an account or a booking). When a person is needed, it does a warm transfer: it briefs the staff member out loud and on screen before connecting the caller, so the customer doesn't have to repeat themselves. ITIKA can also make outbound calls for businesses, such as payment reminders, order confirmations and appointment reminders. After every call, ITIKA records it, transcribes each speaker in the original language with an English translation, and produces a summary, next steps, the caller's intent, sentiment and the business outcome. Managers see reports on how their phones are answered: calls answered, missed calls, time to answer, and transfers. **Methodologies and technologies** - Real-time voice AI on Google Gemini (speech-to-speech for English and Swahili; a speech-to-text, language model and text-to-speech pipeline for Luganda). - Real-time media and call infrastructure on LiveKit, connected to the public phone network through Africa's Talking (SIP), on a local Ugandan number. - Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) over each business's documents. - A multi-tenant cloud platform (Python/FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Google Cloud Run) where one AI agent serves many businesses, each with its own instructions, voice, languages, knowledge and tools. - Durable background workflows for transcription, analysis and scheduled outbound calls. - We build iteratively and test on real phone calls, starting in Kampala seeking pilots in banking, hospitality, tourism, health, insurance and e-commerce. **Partnerships and collaboration model** ITIKA works with infrastructure providers (Africa's Talking for telephony, LiveKit for real-time voice, Google Cloud for AI and hosting). We are also working towards a collaboration with Sunbird AI, a Ugandan language-AI lab. We built an open-source connector (Apache-2.0) that adds Sunbird's Ugandan-language speech models to LiveKit, the widely used voice-AI framework, and we are benchmarking those models on real phone calls. With businesses, we work as a pilot partner: we configure the agent for their workflows, run it alongside their staff, and improve it together.
Solution Provider(s): Africa's Talking — pan-African communications platform (voice, SMS and phone numbers across Africa); telecommunications sector; ITIKA's telephony provider, Google Cloud — Google's cloud and AI platform (Gemini models, Cloud Run, Cloud SQL); technology/cloud sector; ITIKA's AI and hosting provider, LiveKit — open-source real-time voice and video infrastructure used by voice-AI developers worldwide; technology sector; ITIKA's real-time voice and agent infrastructure, Sunbird AI — Ugandan non-profit AI lab building speech and language models for Ugandan languages; AI research sector; collaboration in progress (open-source integration and joint testing on real calls)
Implementation location(s): Kampala, Uganda
Implementation timeline(s): October 2026 – ongoing (building and live testing on real phone calls in Uganda).
Duration to pilot in a new geography: About 3–6 weeks. The platform runs in the cloud, and businesses need no hardware. A new country needs a local phone number from a telecom partner (Africa's Talking operates in several African countries), the local language set up and tested, and the first business configured. Adding a new local language that current AI models handle poorly can take longer.
Desired impact: **Main objectives** 1. Help African businesses, especially MSMEs, answer every customer call, so they stop losing sales, bookings and orders to missed calls. 2. Give customers service in their own language (Luganda, Swahili, English and, later, more African languages), including people who don't speak English well or can't read and write. They only need a basic phone call, not a smartphone or internet. 3. Give African businesses enterprise-grade customer-service technology at a price they can afford, with no hardware or technical staff. **Demonstrated so far** - A working platform built and running end to end on a live Ugandan number: inbound and outbound calls, AI agent in three languages, human and AI routing, warm transfers to staff, call recordings, transcripts and summaries, and reports. - During testing, ITIKA handled 57 calls, 47 of them answered by the AI. - An open-source connector that brings Sunbird AI's Ugandan-language speech models to the LiveKit voice-AI framework, with a published latency benchmark. **Expected impact (next 12 months)** - Pilots with six businesses in Uganda (bank, hotel, tourism, hospital, insurance and e-commerce), then paying customers across East Africa. - For each business: fewer missed calls, faster answers, more appointments and orders confirmed, and staff freed from repetitive calls to handle complex customers. - Jobs: ITIKA plans to hire local engineers, customer-success staff and native-speaker language reviewers as it grows. Human agents stay central to the model, because the AI hands complex calls to them. - No on-premise phone hardware is needed, which avoids buying, powering and replacing equipment. The founder is a refugee living in Uganda. He built ITIKA to create economic opportunity locally and to show that world-class AI products can be built in Africa, for Africa.
Key technologies: - Artificial intelligence: large language models and real-time speech-to-speech AI (Google Gemini), speech recognition and speech synthesis for African languages (including evaluation of Sunbird AI's Ugandan-language models), retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) over business documents, and AI analysis after each call (summaries, intent, sentiment, outcomes, lead scoring). - Voice and telecom: real-time media (LiveKit, WebRTC), SIP trunking to the public phone network (Africa's Talking), keypad (DTMF) language menus, and warm call transfer to staff in a browser. - Cloud: a multi-tenant platform on Google Cloud (Cloud Run, Cloud SQL/PostgreSQL, Cloud Storage), durable workflows (Inngest) for transcription and scheduled outbound calls, and secure API integration with business systems. - Open source: an Apache-2.0 LiveKit plugin for Sunbird AI's speech models.
Unique Characteristics: - Built for African languages and how people really speak: Luganda, Swahili and English on the same phone line, for callers who switch languages mid-sentence. Prompts include local details, such as how Luganda expresses large money amounts, so that amounts are understood correctly. Most global voice-AI products only work well in English. - Humans and AI work together: each business chooses human-first, AI-first or after-hours AI. When the AI transfers a call, it briefs the staff member out loud before connecting the caller, so the customer never has to repeat themselves. AI supports staff instead of replacing them. - Works with any phone: customers reach ITIKA with a normal call from any basic mobile phone. They need no app, smartphone or data. This includes rural and low-literacy customers. - No hardware, low cost: a business keeps its local number, and staff answer from a web browser. One shared AI platform serves many businesses, which keeps the cost per business low. - Insight from every call: recordings, transcripts in the original language with English translation, summaries and service reports turn phone calls, which most African businesses never measure, into data they can act on. - Open contribution to the ecosystem: we open-sourced a connector that makes Ugandan-language speech models from a local lab (Sunbird AI) usable in a global voice-AI framework. This links African language research with real business use.
Sustainable Change: - Replication across Africa: the platform is multi-tenant and cloud-based. A new business can be set up in days, and a new country in weeks, with a local number and language. After Uganda, East Africa is the next step (Kenya, Tanzania, Rwanda), followed by other African markets and then global markets. - Local languages: every real call in Luganda, Swahili and other languages shows where speech models fail on phone audio and mixed-language speech. By testing with African language labs such as Sunbird AI and sharing results, ITIKA can help make African-language voice AI fast and accurate enough for everyday use. This benefits the whole ecosystem, not only ITIKA. - MSME competitiveness: when small businesses can answer every call, follow up on leads and confirm orders, they can compete with larger companies and serve customers they currently lose. This contributes to local economic growth and formal jobs. - Data-driven service: call analytics give businesses, and in aggregate whole sectors, a clear picture of customer demand and service quality. This can improve how banks, hospitals and public services serve people. - Inclusion: voice in local languages over a basic phone call reaches people that text, apps and English-only services leave out. A refugee-founded company building this in Kampala also shows that displaced people can create technology businesses and jobs where they live.
Funding Sources: ITIKA AI has been entirely self-funded (bootstrapped) by the founder from personal savings. ITIKA has not yet received any grants, investment or loans. We are now seeking funding and partners to run paid pilots with businesses in Uganda and expand across East Africa.
Testimonials and Endorsements: Not yet available. ITIKA is preparing its first pilots with businesses in Kampala, and we will gather testimonials from them.
Primary thematic focus area: Industrial Ecosystem Enablers: Finance, Skills and Market Access
Summary: ITIKA AI is a cloud call centre with voice agents for African businesses, routing each call to staff first and to the model if nobody answers. It runs on a live Ugandan number in three languages and has handled 57 calls, 47 of them by the agent.
Thematic focus areas (as submitted): Industrial AI Models and Intelligent Decision-Making; Industrial Ecosystem Enablers: Finance, Skills and Market Access; Industrial Digital Infrastructure and Data Ecosystems

Title: Mindus Mobile Green AI Box: turnkey industrial AI, offline, at 240 watts
Subtitle: A 1.2 kg offline AI unit running six specialised models under a patented green application architecture — turnkey analysis for industry where there is no cloud, no bandwidth and no staff.
Problem Statement: Industrial AI today assumes four things most of the industrialising world does not have: reliable broadband, a cloud account with a foreign provider, a power budget measured in kilowatts, and skilled labour to run it. Where those are missing - coastal regions, ports, recycling sites, remote plants across Africa, the Pacific and the Arab States - AI is simply absent, and decisions are taken on estimates. Our field partner Plastic Odyssey documented the cost of that: pre-mission estimates of 0.5–2 tonnes of plastic against 5.3 tonnes actually collected. Logistics, labour and recycling capacity were all planned on the wrong number. The labour problem is the one least talked about. Every AI offering on the market ships a model and leaves the integration, the data pipeline, the operations and the maintenance to the customer. That presumes data scientists, ML engineers and IT staff on site - exactly the people a port authority, a recycling operator or an NGO field team does not have and cannot hire. The model may be free; the labour to turn it into a working job is not, and it is not available locally. So the technology stays in the capital, or in the vendor’s cloud, and the operator keeps counting by hand. Where connectivity does exist, cloud AI carries two further problems. Every image and sensor reading leaves the country, which is unacceptable for industrial, environmental and public data under growing data-sovereignty rules. And the energy and network cost of shipping raw data to a data centre and back is paid on every single inference, so the carbon footprint of “doing AI” grows with use. The result is an AI divide: the industries and territories that most need intelligent decision-making are the ones structurally excluded from it - by bandwidth, by energy, by labour - and the solutions on offer make the climate problem worse while they do it.
Solution Overview: The Mindus Mobile Green AI Box is a turnkey AI solution: a desktop unit of about 15 × 15 cm and 1.2 kg that arrives with the customer’s complete workflow already built, not with a model waiting for a job. How it works. The Box is built on the NVIDIA DGX Spark platform with 128 GB of unified memory shared between processor and graphics. That memory is what allows six specialised models to stay resident at once, alongside a full application server and the imagery pipeline. It runs entirely offline from its own built-in Wi-Fi access point; a whole team works off the Box with no internet at all. Its power adapter is physically unable to deliver more than 240 W, and typical AI load is 60–90 W. The Box never reaches out on its own: data has nowhere to go and never leaves the room. Methodology. Each step of a workflow is performed by its own small model, purpose-sized for that one task, orchestrated under Mindus’s patented green application architecture (EP 3455718 B1, US 11,249,735 B2, FR 3051268 B1): applications run on the server and stream a lightweight compressed view to any browser or phone; a model is loaded only when an application needs it. The first workflow, built for Plastic Odyssey, turns drone imagery of a shoreline into a cleanup and recycling plan in seven steps: survey, orthomosaic, detection, segmentation, classification against a reference database, learning from operator corrections, and narrative reporting - every step after the flight running on board. Partnership model. The partnership with Plastic Odyssey is formalised in a signed Memorandum of Understanding: Mindus builds and delivers the Box; the operating partner owns the method and the field operation (Plastic Odyssey flies the drones and runs the cleanups).Reference databases built for a domain are community assets: Mindus builds and distributes them but does not own, licence or sell them. Delivery follows a three-tier model: a first Box in a new domain carries the non-recurring engineering; replicated Boxes in an existing domain are productised units; both come with a fixed monthly support contract and no data monetisation.
Solution Provider(s): Plastic Odyssey (France) — NGO and social enterprise fighting plastic pollution through a global expedition vessel, onboard laboratory and low-tech recycling solutions; sector: environment / circular economy. Mindus is Plastic Odyssey’s official AI and technology partner under a signed Memorandum of Understanding, and Plastic Odyssey is the first deployment partner for the Box.
Implementation location(s): N/A — first field deployment in preparation with Plastic Odyssey; platform developed and operated in Monaco.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Replicating an existing workflow (e.g. shoreline plastic analysis) in a new country: 2–3 months, covering shipment, local reference-database extension and operator training. A new industrial domain (e.g. recycling feedstock classification, equipment inspection): 6–9 months, covering model selection and training, workflow build and field validation. No local infrastructure, connectivity contract or data-centre capacity is required at either stage.
Desired impact: Objectives. (1) Give industrial and environmental operators in low-connectivity, low-energy regions the same quality of AI-driven decision-making available in a data centre, with no cloud, no bandwidth and no data leaving the site. (2) Make green AI a property of the architecture rather than a reporting line: a hard power ceiling, small specialised models, no network transit. (3) Replace planning-by-estimate with planning-by-measurement in the first domain, marine plastic recovery and recycling. Impact, demonstrated and expected. Energy: the Box runs six models and a full application server for a whole team inside 240 W peak (60–90 W typical), against 0.5–5 kW for a rack-mounted private AI appliance; it can be operated from a vehicle or a solar array. Emissions: the patented application architecture measures up to 80% lower CO₂ per application than a conventional split-architecture equivalent, before counting the avoided network transit and data-centre load. Decision quality: in the first domain, replacing the 0.5–2 t estimate with a measured 5.3 t changes crew size, vessel time and recycling throughput for every mission. Sovereignty: zero data egress by construction. Labour: each Box is operated by the partner’s own local team after training, not by Mindus staff; the skills stay in the territory.
Key technologies: Edge AI on NVIDIA DGX Spark (Grace Blackwell, 128 GB coherent unified memory), hard-capped at 240 W. Computer-vision pipeline of small specialised models: object detection (YOLO family), segmentation (SAM2), retrieval-augmented classification (DINOv2 embeddings with a FAISS vector index against a domain reference database), and photogrammetry/orthomosaic generation (OpenDroneMap). A quantised large language model (Llama 3.3 70B, Q4) running on board for narrative report generation. Container orchestration (Docker Compose, FastAPI) under the Mindus green application server, whose patented architecture streams a compressed binary view of each application to any browser or phone over the Box’s own Wi-Fi. Continuous learning from operator corrections feeds the reference database. No internet, no cloud dependency, no telemetry.
Unique Characteristics: Everyone else ships a model. Mindus ships the workflow. Off-grid and edge AI products hold one small model at a time; the Box keeps six specialised models resident together with a full application server, so the customer receives their complete job — from raw imagery to a signed report — working on day one. Green by architecture, not by setting. The power ceiling is fixed by the adapter and cannot rise; the application architecture that keeps CO₂ per application low is patented in Europe, the United States and France; there is no infrastructure layer to decarbonise because the Box is the infrastructure. Sovereign by construction. The Box never reaches out. This is not a policy or a configuration; there is no path for data to leave. Business model. Fixed-price hardware and workflow, a fixed monthly support contract, no revenue share, no equity, no data monetisation. The domain reference databases the Box builds are community assets, distributed but not owned by Mindus — the opposite of the data-capture model of cloud AI. Heritage. Mindus has run mission-critical software in production since 1989 for banks, insurers and manufacturers; the Box is that engineering discipline applied to a 240 W budget, built by Monaco’s first certified B Corporation.
Sustainable Change: Replication by domain. The Box is domain-agnostic; only the models and workflow change. The first domain is shoreline plastic analysis; the natural second step is on-site classification of recovered plastic as recycling feedstock, where Plastic Odyssey already operates low-tech recycling solutions — turning survey data into an industrial input. Further domains in preparation include telemedicine in Nigeria; equipment inspection, quality control and agricultural analysis follow the same pattern. Each new domain lowers the cost of the next. Replication by geography. Once a domain workflow exists, a replicated Box ships as a productised unit in weeks, with no local infrastructure. A country can stand up sovereign industrial AI capacity without a data centre, a connectivity contract or a foreign cloud account. Data commons. Every deployment extends a shared, openly distributed reference database for its domain. The plastics database alone, built across Plastic Odyssey’s route of the world’s most polluted coastal cities, becomes a public asset for recyclers, regulators and researchers. Standard-setting. A hard power ceiling and zero data egress are measurable, auditable properties. They offer regulators and procurement bodies a concrete definition of “green” and “sovereign” AI that can be written into tenders and standards — which is where systemic change in industrial AI will actually be decided.
Funding Sources: Self-funded to date. Mindus SARL has financed the Box entirely from its own revenue as a software house in production since 1989, with no external investors, no venture capital and no grant to date. The first Box is priced to recover the platform built with it; subsequent Boxes in a domain are productised units with a fixed monthly support contract. Mindus is seeking grant funding or time-limited project finance for the first field deployments, not equity or perpetual revenue-share structures.
Testimonials and Endorsements: Signed Memorandum of Understanding between Mindus SARL and Plastic Odyssey, naming Mindus as Plastic Odyssey’s official AI and technology partner for the analysis of shoreline drone surveys at marine World Heritage sites.
Primary thematic focus area: Industrial Digital Infrastructure and Data Ecosystems
Summary: Mindus packages a complete offline AI workflow into a 1.2 kilogram, 240 watt unit built on DGX Spark. The engineering is the strongest element; with no field site and no product demonstration, application and geography remain at the floor.
Thematic focus areas (as submitted): AI for Green, Resilient and Sustainable Industry; Industrial Digital Infrastructure and Data Ecosystems; Industrial AI Models and Intelligent Decision-Making

Title: ARU EVA – AI-Powered Smart Energy & Building Management Platform
Subtitle: An intelligent IoT platform that combines occupancy sensing, automated energy control, and real-time analytics to reduce electricity waste, operational costs, and carbon emissions in buildings.
Problem Statement: Hotels, commercial buildings, offices, and residential properties waste significant amounts of electricity due to inefficient HVAC systems, unnecessary lighting, and equipment operating in unoccupied spaces. Traditional building management systems are often expensive, complex to install, and difficult to retrofit into existing buildings. Many facilities also lack accurate occupancy information, real-time energy monitoring, and actionable insights to optimize consumption. This results in higher operational costs, unnecessary carbon emissions, and inefficient use of energy resources, particularly in emerging markets where affordable and scalable smart building solutions are needed.
Solution Overview: ARU EVA is an intelligent, scalable energy and building management platform developed by ARU Group for Manufacturing & Contracting. It combines locally developed IoT hardware, smart occupancy sensors, automation controllers, and an AI-assisted software platform to optimize energy consumption across hotels, commercial buildings, offices, and residential properties. **How the Solution Works** ARU EVA uses advanced presence sensors to detect human occupancy, including stationary occupants, helping prevent unnecessary energy consumption without compromising comfort or safety. Smart Room Control Units (RCUs) automate lighting, air conditioning, and connected electrical equipment based on occupancy, operating schedules, and configurable energy-saving rules. The EVA platform provides centralized monitoring, real-time energy consumption data, automated alerts, operational analytics, and sustainability reporting. Its AI Advisor is designed to identify inefficient consumption patterns and recommend energy optimization strategies. The system supports local, cloud, and hybrid deployment, allowing essential building automation to operate even during internet interruptions. **Technologies and Methodologies** - IoT-enabled control units and occupancy sensors. - presence detection technology. - AI-assisted energy optimization and predictive analytics. - Smart HVAC and lighting automation. - Energy monitoring through smart meters and Modbus communication. - Cloud and edge computing architecture. - Real-time dashboards and carbon emissions estimation. - Retrofit-friendly hardware for existing buildings. **Partnership and Collaboration Model** ARU Group works with hotels, property owners, facility management companies, system integrators, and technology partners through pilot projects, hardware deployment, platform subscriptions, and scalable commercial implementations. The solution is designed for deployment across multiple properties and markets, supporting energy efficiency, digital transformation, and measurable sustainability improvements.
Solution Provider(s): ARU Group for Manufacturing & Contracting (Egypt) – Solution developer and technology provider specializing in IoT hardware manufacturing, intelligent building automation, energy management systems, and AI-assisted sustainability solutions. ARU Group leads product development, hardware integration, software engineering, pilot implementation, and commercialization.
Implementation location(s): Egypt – Successfully deployed across 6 real-world sites, including 2 hotels and 4 additional facilities. Hardware and software testing have been completed, with the solution validated in operational environments.
Implementation timeline(s): 2026 – Present. Completed product testing and validation, followed by deployment across 6 sites, including 2 hotels. Operational implementation and market expansion are ongoing.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Approximately 2–4 weeks for a small-scale pilot, subject to site readiness, hardware availability, and local installation requirements. The solution has completed testing and has been deployed across 6 operational sites, supporting replication in new markets.
Desired impact: ARU EVA aims to reduce energy waste, operating costs, and greenhouse gas emissions in hotels, commercial buildings, and industrial facilities through intelligent IoT automation, real-time monitoring, and AI-assisted energy management. The solution optimizes HVAC, lighting, and connected electrical equipment using advanced occupancy detection and automated control, while maintaining occupant comfort and operational safety. **Demonstrated Progress:** - Completed hardware, firmware, and software testing. - Deployed across 6 real-world sites in Egypt, including 2 hotels. - Demonstrated the technical feasibility of integrating occupancy sensing, automated controls, and centralized monitoring in operational environments. **Expected Impact:** - Reduced electricity consumption and operating expenses. - Lower CO₂ emissions through avoided electricity consumption. - Improved building energy efficiency and operational visibility. - Reduced barriers to adopting intelligent energy management through affordable, locally developed technology. - Increased opportunities for local electronics manufacturing, technical employment, and digital skills development. Energy savings are monitored in kWh, while avoided CO₂ emissions can be calculated using applicable grid emission factors. Quantified reductions will be reported against verified site-specific consumption baselines as monitoring data becomes available. The long-term objective is to scale ARU EVA across thousands of rooms and facilities, enabling measurable environmental and economic impact.
Key technologies: ARU EVA integrates the following technologies: 1. **Internet of Things (IoT):** Locally developed smart controllers, connected sensors, and embedded firmware for real-time building automation. 2. Advanced human presence detection, including stationary occupants, enabling intelligent occupancy-based energy management. 3. **AI-Assisted Analytics and Decision Support:** Analysis of energy consumption, occupancy patterns, and equipment operating data to support optimization recommendations and automated control strategies. 4. **Smart HVAC and Lighting Automation:** Configurable control logic for air conditioning, lighting, and electrical loads, including equipment scheduling and runtime balancing. 5. **Energy Monitoring and Industrial Communication:** Integration with digital electricity meters using Modbus RS485 for monitoring energy consumption and supporting sustainability calculations. 6. **Edge and Cloud Computing:** Local, cloud, and hybrid system architectures that support continued local control during internet outages. 7. **Embedded Systems and Wireless Connectivity:** ESP32-based controllers, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE), and Ethernet connectivity. 8. **Data Analytics and Digital Dashboards:** Centralized monitoring, operational alerts, energy performance visualization, and estimated carbon emissions reporting.
Unique Characteristics: ARU EVA differentiates itself from conventional Building Management Systems (BMS) through the integration of locally developed IoT hardware, advanced occupancy detection, intelligent automation, and scalable energy management software. **Key Innovations:** 1. **Locally Developed End-to-End Technology:** ARU develops its own electronic control units, embedded firmware, and software platform, reducing dependence on expensive proprietary building automation ecosystems. 2. **Advanced Human Presence Detection:** Unlike traditional motion sensors, 24 GHz mmWave radar can detect stationary occupants, enabling more accurate occupancy-based energy control while reducing the risk of incorrectly switching off systems in occupied rooms. 3. **Retrofit-Friendly Architecture:** The solution can be integrated into existing buildings, reducing the need for extensive infrastructure replacement and enabling wider adoption. 4. **Unified Multi-Sector Platform:** A single adaptable platform serves hotels, homes, offices, and other facilities, with configurable controllers, occupancy rules, and operational dashboards. 5. **Offline-Resilient Operation:** Local automation continues without an active internet connection, while cloud and hybrid architectures enable centralized supervision and remote management. 6. **Integrated Energy and Sustainability Intelligence:** Automated controls, smart-meter integration, energy analytics, and AI-assisted recommendations combine operational efficiency with environmental performance monitoring. 7. **Accessible Deployment Model:** Modular hardware and scalable software services are designed to reduce adoption barriers for SMEs and organizations seeking affordable smart energy solutions. ARU EVA has progressed beyond laboratory validation, with completed system testing and deployment across 6 real-world sites in Egypt, including 2 hotels.
Sustainable Change: ARU EVA has the potential to accelerate the transition toward intelligent, energy-efficient, and low-carbon buildings and industrial facilities, particularly in emerging markets where conventional automation systems can be prohibitively expensive. **Scalable Energy Efficiency:** By combining affordable IoT hardware with intelligent automation, ARU EVA can enable hotels, SMEs, commercial buildings, and industrial operators to adopt energy-saving technologies without completely replacing existing infrastructure. **Replication Across Markets:** The modular architecture supports deployment across different building types, from individual rooms and small facilities to multi-building portfolios. Its local, cloud, and hybrid operating models make it adaptable to varying infrastructure and connectivity conditions. **Strengthening Local Manufacturing:** Developing electronic controllers, firmware, and software locally can support domestic manufacturing, technical job creation, and knowledge transfer, helping establish a more competitive regional industrial technology ecosystem. **Digital and Green Transformation:** Wider adoption can improve energy productivity, reduce avoidable electricity demand, and support decarbonization through data-driven building operations. **Technology Partnerships:** Collaboration with property developers, hotel operators, facility management providers, system integrators, universities, and industrial stakeholders can accelerate deployment, localization, and skills development. Following completed testing and implementation across 6 sites in Egypt, ARU aims to expand nationally and into regional and international markets through scalable deployment and technology partnerships. The long-term vision is to make intelligent energy management accessible to thousands of facilities, contributing to SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy), SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure), and SDG 13 (Climate Action).
Funding Sources: ARU EVA has been primarily self-funded through ARU Group for Manufacturing & Contracting's internal resources and investment in research and development, electronic hardware design, embedded firmware, software development, system testing, and initial deployments. The company has completed product testing and deployed the solution across six real-world sites in Egypt, including two hotels. ARU Group is currently exploring strategic partnerships, investment opportunities, and innovation funding programs to expand local manufacturing capacity, strengthen product development, and accelerate regional and international market expansion.
Testimonials and Endorsements: ARU EVA has been deployed across six real-world sites in Egypt, including two hotels, providing practical operational experience and opportunities for direct feedback from end users and facility operators. The deployments have supported the validation and refinement of the solution's hardware, software, occupancy sensing, and building automation capabilities. Formal customer testimonials, case studies, and reference letters may be provided upon availability and subject to customer authorization.
Primary thematic focus area: AI for Green, Resilient and Sustainable Industry
Summary: ARU EVA combines occupancy sensors, room controllers and a monitoring platform to cut electricity waste in Egyptian hotels and commercial buildings, with six sites reported including two hotels. The engineering is real and the AI claim is thin.
Thematic focus areas (as submitted): AI for Green, Resilient and Sustainable Industry; Industrial AI Models and Intelligent Decision-Making; Industrial Digital Infrastructure and Data Ecosystems

Title: ARIM - Adaptive Agricultural Risk Intelligence Model
Subtitle: An adaptive agricultural intelligence model that creates living virtual representations of farms, connecting AI, computer vision, IoT and operational data to understand conditions, predict risks and simulate production decisions.
Problem Statement: Agricultural operations are interconnected systems, but the information required to manage them is fragmented across physical inspections, paper records, disconnected sensors, cameras and individual management tools. Farmers and agricultural businesses often discover problems after they have already affected production, resulting in avoidable mortality, crop losses, inefficient resource use and reduced profitability. A temperature change in a poultry house, for example, cannot be understood independently of bird distribution, ventilation, stocking density, water availability and the building's physical characteristics. Similarly, a change in crop conditions may be influenced by soil moisture, weather, irrigation, pests and previous management decisions. Most existing agricultural monitoring solutions address individual variables or provide isolated alerts without developing a comprehensive understanding of the agricultural operation in which those events occur. This creates a fundamental intelligence gap: agricultural stakeholders can collect data about their operations but often lack the ability to connect that data, understand relationships between conditions, anticipate their consequences and evaluate interventions before implementing them. The problem is particularly significant in developing agricultural economies, where many farms operate with limited connectivity, inconsistent record-keeping, constrained technical resources and little access to continuous specialist support. ARIM addresses this gap by developing an adaptive intelligence model capable of representing agricultural operations, interpreting their changing conditions and supporting evidence-based management decisions.
Solution Overview: ARIM (Adaptive Agricultural Risk Intelligence Model) is an agricultural intelligence architecture developed to create a continuously updated virtual representation of real agricultural operations. It combines artificial intelligence, computer vision, Internet of Things (IoT), spatial modelling, operational records and predictive analytics to understand how agricultural environments function and how their conditions change over time. Rather than treating a farm as a collection of disconnected monitoring points, ARIM models it as an interconnected system of buildings, production units, equipment, environmental conditions, resources, biological populations and operational activities. 1. Virtual representation of agricultural operations ARIM establishes a digital representation of the physical farm, including its buildings, production houses, storage facilities, equipment and operational zones. Individual units can be independently identified, modelled and represented in three dimensions. Each unit can have its own operational profile, including dimensions, capacity, equipment, environmental parameters, sensor locations and production activities. This creates a spatial understanding of the farm, allowing users to examine individual buildings, understand their operating conditions and relate events to their actual physical locations. 2. Continuous environmental and operational observation - The model integrates information from different sources, including: - CCTV and IP cameras for visual observation of agricultural activities. - Computer vision for identifying relevant activities, patterns and potential abnormal conditions. - IoT sensors for temperature, humidity, water levels, environmental conditions and other measurable parameters. - Operational records covering stocking, feeding, production, mortality, maintenance and resource consumption. - Historical observations and external information, including weather data where available. These sources provide complementary information about what is happening within each agricultural unit. 3. AI-powered analysis and risk intelligence ARIM processes incoming observations and connects them with the spatial and operational context of the farm. Its intelligence layer is designed to identify abnormal conditions, detect emerging risks, analyse patterns over time and assess relationships between different operational variables. For example, in poultry production, the model can combine environmental readings, bird distribution and visual observations to investigate potential heat stress, cold stress, overcrowding, water interruptions or other production risks. The objective is to move beyond identifying individual events towards understanding their possible causes, consequences and relationships with other farm conditions. 4. Predictive analysis and scenario simulation ARIM is designed to support forward-looking agricultural management. Using accumulated operational data, environmental observations and historical patterns, the model can estimate potential risks and help evaluate alternative management decisions. Through the virtual farm, users can explore scenarios such as changes in stocking density, ventilation, feeding schedules, water availability, equipment configuration and environmental management. This creates an opportunity to assess the potential implications of a decision within the model before applying it to the physical operation. Predictive accuracy and simulation capabilities will be progressively validated against real operational outcomes. 5. Decision support and operational feedback ARIM translates identified conditions and potential risks into information that farmers and farm managers can use. The system is designed to provide alerts, visual representations, reports and recommendations, with the ability to associate observations with specific buildings, units and operational activities. Key technologies: ARIM uses the following technologies to collect, process and interpret information from agricultural operations: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning: Analyses farm data, identifies patterns, detects possible problems and estimates future risks. Computer Vision: Processes camera footage to observe livestock, crops, equipment and activities, identifying changes or conditions that may require attention. Sensors and Connected Devices: Collect measurements such as temperature, humidity, water levels and equipment status from farms and production facilities. 3D Modelling: Creates digital models of farms, buildings, equipment and production areas, showing their dimensions, positions and relationships. Data Analysis and Simulation: Examines production history and current conditions to estimate risks and compare possible management decisions. Edge Computing: Processes selected data on devices or computers located at the farm, reducing the need to send all information to remote servers. Cloud Infrastructure: Stores and processes information, manages AI models and allows authorised users to access farm records across different locations. Offline Data Management: Stores information locally when internet access is unavailable and synchronises it when connectivity returns. Event and Record Management: Keeps dated records of observations, detected problems, alerts, actions taken and subsequent results.
Unique Characteristics: ARIM's innovation is that it connects the physical layout of an agricultural operation with the information collected from it. Instead of treating cameras, sensors, buildings and production records as separate things, it brings them together to understand how the entire operation is functioning. 1. A digital model of the actual farm ARIM can create a digital representation of a farm, including its buildings, production units, equipment and operating areas. Each area can be identified and monitored separately, allowing information to be linked to the exact location where a condition or problem occurs. 2. Understanding problems using multiple sources ARIM combines information from cameras, sensors and farm records to investigate problems. For example, high temperatures in a poultry house can be examined alongside humidity, ventilation, bird movement and water availability. This provides more information for determining what may be causing the problem. 3. Identifying risks before losses occur Beyond showing current conditions, ARIM is being developed to identify patterns that may indicate an emerging problem. Its planned simulation capabilities will allow farmers to examine how changes in stocking, ventilation, feeding or water supply could affect production. 4. Connecting infrastructure with production Buildings, equipment, environmental conditions, livestock, crops and operational activities are represented in relation to one another. This helps explain how a problem with one part of a farm can affect other parts of the operation. 5. Learning from actions and results ARIM records identified problems, actions taken and what happens afterwards. For example, if a farmer changes ventilation after a heat warning, subsequent temperature readings and production records can help assess whether the intervention worked. 6. Working within African infrastructure conditions The system is designed to accommodate unreliable internet, limited connectivity and different levels of available equipment. Local data processing, temporary storage and synchronization when connectivity returns can help maintain monitoring even when internet access is interrupted. 7. Applying the same approach to different agricultural activities Poultry is the starting point, but the same approach can be adapted to livestock farms, crop fields, irrigation systems, storage facilities and processing operations. Each application would have its own measurements, operating conditions and risk models.
Sustainable Change: ARIM aims to change how agricultural operations are managed by connecting information from farms, agricultural businesses and the institutions that support them. Today, information about production, equipment, resources, costs and risks is often kept in separate records or is not collected at all. This makes it difficult to identify problems early, plan production and make informed decisions. At farm level ARIM creates digital models of farms, buildings, equipment and production units. Cameras, sensors and farm records help monitor conditions, identify problems and track changes in production, costs and resource use. Across agricultural businesses Hatcheries, feed suppliers, cooperatives and processors can use farm information to understand customer needs, monitor production, plan deliveries and identify farms that need support. Research and government planning With appropriate permission and protection of personal information, aggregated data can help researchers and public agencies understand production trends, common agricultural problems, infrastructure needs and climate risks. Expansion across Africa ARIM will initially be developed and tested in Uganda, beginning with poultry production. Its underlying technology can later be adapted to crop farming, livestock, storage and processing facilities, then introduced in other African countries. Long-term ambition The goal is to make agricultural operations easier to understand and manage, while giving farmers, businesses, researchers and institutions better information about what is happening, what is going wrong and what needs to change. This can support more reliable food production, stronger agricultural businesses and better use of resources.

Title: Pareto OS: Corporate AI Brain and Governed Agents for Supply Chains
Subtitle: A modular AI operating layer connecting enterprise knowledge, data and workflows to help teams make better decisions and execute supply-chain processes with human oversight.
Problem Statement: Industrial and distribution businesses often operate across disconnected ERP systems, spreadsheets, documents and messaging channels. Employees spend substantial time finding information, reconciling records and coordinating approvals. Fragmented knowledge and weak visibility delay procurement and replenishment, increase rework and make it difficult to deploy AI safely beyond isolated experiments. Organizations in developing economies also face shortages of specialist AI skills and limited capacity to maintain custom solutions.
Solution Overview: Pareto combines a corporate AI brain, governed AI agents and implementation services to turn business processes into connected AI-enabled workflows. The corporate brain organizes authorized enterprise documents and data so employees and agents can retrieve relevant knowledge in context. Agents use that knowledge and approved tools to support analysis, recommendations and execution, with human review for consequential decisions. The architecture integrates with existing business systems rather than requiring their replacement. Delivery starts with process mapping, data and access assessment, selection of a measurable use case, and a baseline. A multidisciplinary team builds and tests the workflow, integrates required systems, validates outputs with business owners, and expands only after operational acceptance. Governance includes access control, traceability, monitoring, evaluation and defined human escalation. Deployment design reflects each client’s infrastructure and security requirements. Applications include procurement and supply-chain analysis, commercial decision support, financial reconciliation and enterprise knowledge access. Pareto’s work with Grupo Profarma and Grupo ABC provides relevant Brazilian enterprise experience; individual use cases are at different stages and are not presented as a single uniform rollout. Collaboration combines Pareto AI specialists, client process owners and IT teams, plus practical training that enables business professionals to participate in building and improving workflows.
Solution Provider(s): Pareto (Brazilian AI consulting and implementation company; solution developer and delivery lead), Grupo Profarma (Brazilian pharmaceutical distribution and retail group; enterprise client and implementation context), Grupo ABC (Brazilian food retail group; enterprise client and implementation context). Client references are not a claim of co-sponsorship or endorsement of this submission.
Implementation location(s): Brazil. Enterprise implementation contexts include Grupo Profarma, headquartered in Rio de Janeiro, and Grupo ABC, operating in Minas Gerais. Specific deployment sites and scope vary by use case.
Implementation timeline(s): Enterprise AI implementation and ongoing development during 2026; work continues. Individual project start dates and rollout periods vary and can be clarified during evaluation.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Preliminary planning estimate: 8–12 weeks for a tightly scoped pilot after agreement on scope, data availability, access, local requirements and client team availability. Integration complexity and procurement can extend this period; this is not a delivery commitment.
Desired impact: The objectives are to improve operational productivity and decision quality, reduce repetitive coordination and reconciliation work, strengthen data visibility and traceability, and build internal AI capability. In distribution and retail, better demand, procurement and exception handling can also support more efficient use of inventory and reduce avoidable waste. Pareto has enterprise implementation experience in Brazil, including the Grupo Profarma Aura program and Grupo ABC workflows. This submission does not claim an independently verified aggregate savings, emissions reduction or job-creation figure. For each pilot, impact should be measured against a baseline using cycle time, staff hours per process, error/rework rate, service level, inventory-related indicators and adoption. Environmental benefits are expected potential outcomes where the selected workflow influences resource use, not measured GHG savings claimed here.
Key technologies: Large language models and retrieval-augmented generation for enterprise knowledge access; AI agents with controlled tool use and workflow orchestration; machine learning and analytical models where prediction or anomaly detection is appropriate; APIs and connectors to enterprise systems; structured data stores and document retrieval; access controls, audit logs, evaluation and observability. The solution does not depend on robotics, blockchain or new physical equipment.
Unique Characteristics: The distinguishing feature is the combination of a reusable corporate knowledge and orchestration layer with client-specific business processes, governance and skills transfer. It goes beyond a standalone chatbot by connecting knowledge to approved actions in existing systems. Pareto pairs technical implementation with business-process redesign and practical training for domain professionals. Modular delivery allows an organization to begin with one measurable workflow and expand through shared infrastructure, while preserving client control over its data and project intellectual property according to contract.
Sustainable Change: The approach can help organizations move from isolated AI experiments to an enduring capability to improve multiple processes. Reusable integration, governance and knowledge components reduce repeated setup effort across departments. Training business professionals helps retain capability locally instead of making every improvement dependent on scarce external specialists. Adaptation through local implementation partners and client teams can support replication in other developing and middle-income economies, with localization of language, regulation, data access and operating practices. Wider impact depends on successful pilots, measured outcomes and sustainable operating capacity, rather than assuming that technology alone produces transformation.
Funding Sources: Commercial enterprise implementations. Funding amounts and project-level arrangements are not disclosed in this submission.
Testimonials and Endorsements: No stakeholder quotation or formal endorsement is included in this submission. Client references describe implementation context and do not imply endorsement.
