Title: VeriChain: Turning Product Movements into Industrial Market Intelligence
Subtitle: An AI-powered product-intelligence network connecting businesses and institutions to improve market visibility, detect supply-chain risks, protect consumers and support faster recalls
Problem Statement: Once products leave factories, information about their movement, distribution and safety becomes fragmented across businesses and institutions. Manufacturers struggle to understand downstream markets and detect unusual product movements. Distributors and retailers operate with disconnected records, while public institutions often lack timely, reliable evidence to investigate counterfeit, diverted or unsafe goods. When a product safety incident occurs, identifying affected batches and coordinating recalls can become slow and difficult. The core challenge is the absence of interoperable, connected product evidence. This affects industrial competitiveness, consumer safety and the ability of organizations to respond collectively to supply-chain risks
Solution Overview: VeriChain is an AI-powered network that connects product identities, supply-chain movements and operational evidence across manufacturers, distributors, retailers and authorized public institutions. How it works: 1. Identify: Products or batches receive unique digital identities that connect them to their manufacturing and distribution records. 2. Connect: Authorized supply-chain participants record movements, custody changes and verification events, directly or through integrations with existing systems. 3. Analyze: Our proprietary AMANDA Intelligence Core combines specialized AI models, deterministic detection and connected operational context to identify distribution patterns, emerging demand and suspicious activity. 4. Act: Manufacturers gain market intelligence, while authorized institutions can investigate product risks, identify affected products and coordinate evidence-based responses, including targeted recalls. Technologies: Digital serialization, standards-aligned data exchange, APIs, specialized AI and machine learning, operational ontology, offline synchronization and governed workflows. Collaboration model: Manufacturers fund the network through per-unit payments and bring their existing distribution partners. Authorized downstream participants and public institutions can access relevant network capabilities without routine access fees, subject to permissions and data-sharing arrangements.
Solution Provider(s): No formal external implementation partnerships have been concluded yet. but Consumer Council of Zimbabwe (CCZ)— Consumer advocacy and protection. An initial meeting was held, and CCZ requested a second meeting, :Prospective FMCG manufacturers (Zimbabwe) — Two manufacturers are in commercial discussions, including one that has completed an on-site productionline assessment. Their names remain confidential. These are exploratory engagements and prospective collaborators not signed partnerships.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Estimated 3weeks--2months, depending on manufacturer onboarding, system integration, data-sharing arrangements and local requirements
Desired impact: VeriChain’s objective is to create safer, more transparent and better-connected product markets by making reliable supply-chain evidence accessible to the organizations responsible for producing, distributing and protecting goods. Expected impact includes: • Safer products and markets: Help identify suspicious product movements, possible counterfeiting, diversion and other risks earlier, allowing authorized teams to investigate before problems spread. • Faster, more targeted recalls: Help manufacturers and public institutions identify affected products, batches and distribution channels, improving the speed and precision of safety responses. • Stronger public institutions: Provide authorized consumer-protection and regulatory bodies with relevant evidence and intelligence without routine network-access fees, supporting better oversight and collaboration. • Interoperability: Connect information held by manufacturers, distributors, retailers and institutions, reducing fragmentation and improving coordinated responses. • More resilient industries: Support informed distribution decisions, emerging-market visibility and earlier identification of supply-chain disruptions. Impact measurement: The first pilot will track connected product units, participating organizations, suspicious events investigated, time required to trace affected products, recall response times and the completeness of shared evidence. These are expected benefits. Quantified real-world improvements will be established through live pilot evaluation.
Key technologies: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning: Proprietary AMANDA Intelligence Core combines deterministic detection and specialized models to analyze temporal, spatial, network and behavioral patterns, supporting anomaly detection and market intelligence. Digital Product Serialization: Unique identities link individual products and batches to recorded movements and verification events. Industrial Data Integration: APIs and standards-aligned event records connect information across participating manufacturing, distribution and retail systems. Operational Ontology: A digital representation of products, organizations, locations, movements and relationships provides context for AI analysis and investigations. Edge Computing and Offline Synchronization: Supports evidence capture in low-connectivity environments and later synchronization. Governed Digital Workflows: Access controls, evidence provenance, auditability and human oversight support secure and accountable decisions. The platform is undergoing further technical and operational validation ahead of live deployment.
Unique Characteristics: VeriChain combines product intelligence, supply-chain interoperability and institutional collaboration within one network. Its key innovations include: • Network-based intelligence: Instead of relying on isolated verification records, VeriChain connects authorized product events across multiple organizations to create a more complete operational picture. • Proprietary AMANDA technology: Specialized AI and deterministic methods analyze connected evidence to identify unusual movements, market patterns and potential risks. • Public-interest access: Authorized public institutions can use relevant evidence and response capabilities without routine network-access fees. • Manufacturer-led expansion: Manufacturers fund the network and bring their existing distribution partners, reducing barriers to downstream participation. • Adaptability: Low-connectivity support and integration with existing systems make the approach suitable for businesses with different levels of digital infrastructure. This allows the same connected evidence to support commercial intelligence, consumer protection and coordinated industrial responses
Sustainable Change: VeriChain aims to help African product markets move from isolated organizational records toward interoperable, intelligence-driven supply chains. As more manufacturers connect their existing distribution networks, authorized participants can contribute product and movement evidence that becomes useful across organizational boundaries. This could strengthen regional industrial ecosystems in several ways: helping manufacturers understand cross-border distribution, enabling smaller businesses to participate in shared digital infrastructure, and improving cooperation between businesses and public institutions. For consumer protection, a wider network could make it easier to identify suspicious product movements, trace affected batches and coordinate recalls across distribution channels and jurisdictions. The model is designed for replication across FMCG, pharmaceutical and agricultural supply chains, with potential expansion through African trade corridors. The long-term opportunity is not simply to digitize individual supply chains, but to establish shared intelligence infrastructure that supports safer markets, stronger institutions and more competitive industries. The first live pilot will test this approach and establish the evidence needed for responsible expansion.
Funding Sources: VeriChain has been entirely bootstrapped through our own limited resources, time and determination. I’m Nitiance Murimira, a 21-year-old self-taught systems architect from rural Hwedza, Zimbabwe, with O Level as my highest formal qualification. Over the past 11 months, I’ve been building VeriChain despite having very limited resources, sometimes relying on just one hour of capped public Wi-Fi a day to continue development. What started as an idea has grown into a working MVP, with manufacturer interest and early engagement with consumer-protection institutions. We haven’t had the financial resources or infrastructure that many technology startups begin with, but we’ve continued building and improving the system. We are now seeking the funding and partnerships needed to move from technical development into our first live industrial deployment

Title: tita AI- Enabled Automatic Timetable Generator
Subtitle: An AI-enabled academic scheduling platform that generates conflict free lecture and examination timetables, reduces administrative workload, and connects students, lecturers and institutions.
Problem Statement: Many tertiary institutions across Africa still rely on manual, paper based timetable scheduling, which is time consuming, labour intensive and prone to human errors. This often results in overlapping lectures, double booked venues, lecturer scheduling conflicts and omitted courses, disrupting academic activities and reducing institutional efficiency. Frequent timetable changes and poor communication also leave students and lecturers without timely access to accurate academic information. Additionally, repeated timetable printing increases operational costs and paper waste. These challenges highlight the need for an affordable, automated and accessible scheduling solution that improves academic coordination, reduces administrative workload and supports efficient teaching and learning across African tertiary institutions.
Solution Overview: TITA is an AI-enabled automatic timetable generation and academic management platform designed to eliminate scheduling conflicts, reduce administrative workload and improve academic efficiency across African tertiary institutions. How the Solution Works TITA enables institutions to upload or enter academic data, including courses, lecturer allocations, student groups, available venues and academic calendars, through a centralised administration dashboard. The system automatically generates lecture and examination timetables while detecting and preventing scheduling conflicts involving lecturers, students and venues. Institutional administrators can review, modify and approve timetables before publication. Students access their schedules, academic calendars, assignments and announcements through the tita student app, while lecturers use the lecti app to manage teaching schedules, communicate updates and coordinate academic activities. Methodologies and Technologies Used TITA combines automated scheduling algorithms, conflict detection, institutional data management and mobile technology to provide an integrated academic management solution. Our technology considers lecturer availability, course allocations, student groups and venue capacity to generate optimised academic schedules. The platform accommodates different institutional structures, enabling universities, polytechnics and colleges to configure the system according to their academic requirements. Through centralised administration, real-time notifications and mobile accessibility, TITA reduces manual scheduling, minimises paper based processes and improves access to accurate academic information. Partnerships and Collaboration Models TITA operates a Business-to-Business (B2B) subscription model, partnering directly with tertiary institutions to deploy its technology. Institutions receive onboarding, staff training, technical support and ongoing platform improvements. We also collaborate with education technology providers, including Adapt IT in South Africa, to support technology integration, institutional pilots and expansion into new African markets. Our development approach incorporates feedback from institutional administrators, lecturers and students to ensure the platform addresses real academic challenges.
Solution Provider(s): Adapt IT Education (Pty) Ltd, South Africa – An education technology company providing student management and administrative software solutions to tertiary institutions. Sector: Education Technology (EdTech), Software Development and Higher Education Management.
Implementation location(s): Nigeria, Liberia, The Gambia, South Africa
Implementation timeline(s): 2024-Present
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 1-3 weeks
Desired impact: TITA's primary objective is to transform academic scheduling across African tertiary institutions through AI-enabled automation, improving operational efficiency, reducing administrative costs and expanding access to reliable academic information. Our solution aims to: Eliminate scheduling conflicts:Automatically generate lecture and examination timetables, preventing lecturer, student and venue clashes. Improve operational efficiency: Reduce the time, effort and manpower required for manual timetable preparation. Promote environmental sustainability: Reduce dependence on printed timetables, lowering paper consumption, printing costs and associated environmental impact Improve educational accessibility:Provide students and lecturers with real-time schedules, announcements and academic updates through the tita and lecti apps. Accelerate digital transformation: Help tertiary institutions replace manual academic processes with affordable digital systems. Demonstrated Impact:TITA currently serves over 70,000 students across five paying tertiary institutions, with deployments in Nigeria, Liberia, The Gambia and South Africa. Expected Impact: Within 12 months, TITA aims to expand to 150 tertiary institutions, improving academic coordination and reducing paper-based administrative processes across Africa. We will measure impact through timetable conflicts prevented, administrative hours saved, reductions in paper printing, institutional adoption, user engagement and operational cost savings. Where reliable baseline data are available, we will also estimate associated carbon emissions avoided. Our solution directly supports SDG 4 (Quality Education), SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure) and SDG 13 (Climate Action)** by combining accessible digital education infrastructure with more resource-efficient academic administration.

Intelligent Scheduling Algorithms: Detect and prevent timetable clashes, double-booked venues and overlapping academic activities. Cloud-Based Technology: Supports centralised academic data management, system accessibility and deployment across multiple institutions. Mobile Applications: The tita student app and lecti lecturer app provide digital timetables, academic announcements and schedule updates. Web-Based Administration Platform:Enables institutions to manage academic records, configure scheduling requirements, generate timetables and approve publication. Data Analytics: Provides institutional insights to support academic planning, resource allocation and operational decision-making. Together, these technologies reduce manual processes, improve institutional efficiency and enable scalable digital academic management across African tertiary institutions.
Unique Characteristics: TITA stands out by combining AI-enabled automatic timetable generation, mobile accessibility, academic management and revenue-generating opportunities in one integrated platform designed for tertiary institutions. Our key innovations and competitive advantages include: AI-Enabled Timetable Generation: Automatically creates conflict-free lecture and examination timetables, eliminating lecturer, student and venue clashes while reducing administrative workload. Integrated Digital Ecosystem: Connects institutions, students and lecturers through a centralised administration platform, the tita student app and lecti lecturer app, providing real-time schedules, announcements and academic updates. Mobile-First, User-Friendly Design: Offers an intuitive interface designed to meet the digital habits and expectations of Gen Z and Millennial users, making academic information accessible directly from their smartphones. Innovative Revenue Model:Combines affordable annual institutional subscriptions with in-app advertising opportunities, creating multiple revenue streams and supporting long-term financial sustainability. Scalable and Adaptable Technology: Accommodates different institutional structures and academic systems, with the capacity to support over one million students as the platform expands. Strategic Partnership Model: Collaborates with established education technology providers, including Adapt IT in South Africa, to support system integration, institutional adoption and expansion into new African markets. Environmental Benefits: Digital timetable distribution reduces dependence on paper-based scheduling, repeated printing and associated resource consumption. Our uniqueness lies in combining intelligent scheduling, integrated academic applications, an engaging mobile experience, affordable pricing and strategic distribution partnerships within one scalable solution.
Sustainable Change: TITA has the potential to drive lasting transformation in African tertiary education by making automated academic scheduling an accessible, affordable and widely adopted institutional standard. Title: ShambaBoy: Offline Farm Evidence and Human-Reviewed AI
Subtitle: Offline field records and constrained AI help Kenyan farm teams coordinate work, review evidence and respond to weather risks, with people retaining decision authority.
Problem Statement: Farm operations are the upstream execution layer of agrifood supply chains, yet managers often coordinate dispersed workers through paper and messaging. When connectivity drops, records of what was assigned, observed and approved become difficult to reconcile. Weather-sensitive tasks can be delayed or poorly timed, while workers lose a usable history of their approved experience. AI cannot responsibly resolve these gaps from incomplete or untraceable data. The practical challenge is to capture field evidence under intermittent connectivity, preserve who reviewed it, and make relevant information usable for human decisions. ShambaBoy addresses this operational information gap for Kenyan farm teams. Resource savings and climate benefits remain hypotheses to be evaluated in intended-user trials.
Solution Overview: ShambaBoy connects assigned farm work to offline field records and supervisor review. A worker records task evidence such as photos, notes, time and relevant location context in a mobile app. Local SQLite storage preserves the workflow when internet access is interrupted; records synchronize when connectivity returns. A supervisor reviews the evidence and approves or queries the task. Approved work can contribute to a portable worker history. The AI layer uses permission-scoped farm records to summarize activity and help identify missing evidence. Its weather specialist explains server-generated forecast-risk assessments for rainfall, wind and heat, and can propose a permitted follow-up or rescheduling action. Deterministic permission checks and human approval constrain operational changes; AI does not make employment decisions or prescribe agronomic treatments. The product uses React Native/Expo and TypeScript, a web dashboard, a Node.js backend and PostgreSQL, with Google Gemini/Vertex AI and specialist agents. Current evidence is a working product and controlled technical testing. Intended-user AI field validation is pending. The proposed collaboration is a consent-based Kenyan farm evaluation, with farm teams helping define useful records, an agronomy/climate advisor reviewing weather-related assumptions, and a research or implementation partner helping assess reliability, usefulness and privacy. These are sought collaborations, not confirmed partnerships.
Solution Provider(s): SHAMBABOY LTD — Kenyan agritech software developer and applicant. No formal deployment or research partner is claimed for this submission; farm, climate-advisory and evaluation collaborations are being sought.
Implementation location(s): N/A — no completed intended-user AI implementation is claimed. Development and controlled technical testing are based in Kenya.
Implementation timeline(s): N/A — intended-user AI pilot pending; product development began in 2024.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Estimated 8–12 weeks after securing a suitable local partner, participant permissions and a small pilot budget. This includes workflow/language adaptation, onboarding, a 4–6 week supervised trial and review. Timing depends on connectivity, data-protection requirements and local support.
Desired impact: The objective is to make daily agrifood work traceable and usable for human decisions even when internet access is unreliable. We seek to reduce missing records, make supervisor review more timely, help teams understand weather-related task risks, and give workers access to approved work histories. For an initial evaluation, we propose 1–2 farm teams and approximately 10–20 voluntary users, subject to partner agreement. Measures would include evidence completion, synchronization success after connectivity interruptions, review turnaround, repeat use, AI-summary accuracy and the rate of unsupported or unsafe suggestions. We would collect baseline and endline user feedback and record consent, access and deletion issues. These are proposed study measures and targets for recruitment, not achieved traction. We have no verified quantified emissions reductions, energy savings, yield gains or jobs created to report. Public app availability and the Google Play 100+ install bracket establish distribution only; they do not establish active use or impact.
Key technologies: Offline mobile data capture and SQLite synchronization; React Native/Expo and TypeScript; a web operations dashboard; Node.js/Express APIs and PostgreSQL; photo/notes/time and relevant location evidence; role-based access and supervisor approvals. The AI layer uses Google Gemini/Vertex AI and specialist agents for permission-scoped record retrieval, summarization and weather-risk explanation. Weather-risk categorization and permission enforcement are handled by backend rules. We do not claim a proprietary trained foundation model, industrial robotics, IoT sensors, blockchain or digital twins.
Unique Characteristics: ShambaBoy combines three workflows that are often disconnected: assigning field work, collecting evidence during connectivity interruptions, and preserving the supervisor decision alongside the record. The same approved record can support farm coordination and a worker’s history of experience. Its AI is anchored to the operational record and constrained tools, rather than treating a generated answer as proof that work happened. A weather explanation can be traced to the backend risk assessment; consequential actions retain human review. This makes the approach relevant to small agrifood operators that cannot assume reliable connectivity or dedicated technical staff. The distinguishing proposition is practical accountability across the complete task-to-evidence-to-approval workflow. Comparative performance and willingness to adopt still require field evaluation.
Sustainable Change: If validated, a consistent task–evidence–approval record could become a reusable coordination layer across farms, cooperatives and agrifood service providers. Buyers and support programmes could request specific operational evidence with permission, while workers could carry approved experience between engagements. These pathways could reduce repeated data collection and improve accountability without requiring every organization to build its own field-record system. Expansion would start with repeatable onboarding and locally agreed evidence standards, then test replication in another Kenyan setting before moving to other markets. Climate and certification claims would require independent validation and additional domain partnerships; the current product is not a carbon-credit verification service. Sustained change depends on adoption, data portability, worker agency and a viable service model. We would assess whether benefits reach workers as well as managers, and avoid making access to employment or finance depend solely on AI-generated assessments.
Primary thematic focus area: Industrial Digital Infrastructure and Data Ecosystems
Summary: ShambaBoy records farm tasks offline and keeps supervisor approval beside the evidence, with AI summarising permissioned records. The design is well matched to the setting; without a field pilot it remains a prototype with a working app.

Title: AgriCare AI: An Drone based Platform for Sustainable and Resilient Agriculture
Subtitle: An integrated agricultural intelligence platform combining drone-based field scanning, edge AI, IoT-enabled monitoring, and multilingual voice assistance to help farmers improve productivity, conserve resources, and reduce agricultural losses.
Problem Statement: Smallholder farmers face interconnected challenges, including crop diseases, inefficient irrigation, unpredictable weather, limited access to agricultural expertise, post-harvest losses, and inadequate market information. These challenges are intensified by fragmented agricultural data, unreliable connectivity in rural areas, and language barriers that prevent farmers from accessing timely, actionable advice. Conventional digital farming solutions often address individual problems rather than providing an integrated decision-support system. AgriCare AI addresses this gap by combining field-level intelligence, resource optimization, crop health wassessment, and market information in an accessible platform designed for smallholder farming contexts.
Solution Overview: AgriCare AI is an AI-powered, multimodal smart farming platform integrating seven features: AI crop recommendation, crop disease detection, smart irrigation, multilingual voice assistance, post-harvest intelligence, AI market intelligence, and a peer-to-peer farmer marketplace. How the solution works:Drone-based field scanning captures aerial crop imagery for monitoring field conditions and identifying potential crop stress. The distributed, node-based Edge AI architecture includes an ESP32-CAM-based sensing node, a LoRa communication node, an Edge AI processing node for local analysis, and a drone intelligence node. These components collect, transmit, and process agricultural data to support crop monitoring and informed farming decisions. The platform also provides irrigation guidance, crop-health insights, post-harvest recommendations, market information, and accessible farmer assistance. Methodologies and technologies: The solution combines AI/ML, computer vision, drone technology, IoT sensors, embedded systems, Edge AI, ESP32-CAM, LoRa communication, and lightweight models such as MobileNetV2 for crop-image analysis. Multilingual conversational AI and Twilio-based IVR support voice-based access where integrated. Cloud services can support centralized analytics and synchronization when connectivity is available. Partnerships and collaboration:Collaboration with agricultural universities, agronomists, agricultural extension services, farmer-producer organizations, and technology providers can support field validation, localized recommendations, farmer training, and deployment. Partnerships with agricultural buyers can help strengthen market access. These are proposed collaboration opportunities, not confirmed partnerships.
Solution Provider(s): T. John Institute of Technology — Academic institution associated with the development team; sector: Higher Education and Technology. No additional formal external implementation partners confirmed.
Implementation timeline(s): NA
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Approximately 3–6 months, depending on local crop requirements, hardware integration, data availability, connectivity, language adaptation, and access to agricultural partners. Deployment would include site assessment, system configuration, field testing, farmer onboarding, and performance evaluation.
Desired impact: AgriCare AI aims to improve agricultural productivity, resource efficiency, and climate resilience by providing smallholder farmers with accessible AI-powered decision support. Its objectives include early crop-disease detection, optimized irrigation, reduced post-harvest losses, improved market access, and accessible multilingual agricultural guidance. The platform combines drone-based field monitoring, distributed Edge AI nodes, and IoT sensors to support timely, data-driven farming decisions, including in areas with limited internet connectivity. Expected impact:Reduced unnecessary water consumption, fewer avoidable crop and post-harvest losses, improved access to agricultural expertise, and more efficient farming operations. Potential environmental benefits include reduced resource wastage and lower emissions associated with inefficient agricultural practices. Impact will be measured through water consumption, crop-disease detection accuracy, crop-loss rates, farmer adoption, and changes in production and market outcomes. As the solution is at the prototype stage, quantified field impacts have not yet been independently established. Numerical targets will be defined following baseline assessment and pilot testing.
Key technologies: AgriCare AI uses Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, computer vision, drone-based field scanning, distributed node-based Edge AI, IoT sensors, ESP32-CAM, LoRa communication, and lightweight neural networks such as MobileNetV2 for crop-image analysis. Additional technologies include embedded systems, multilingual conversational AI, Twilio-based Interactive Voice Response (IVR), agricultural data analytics, and cloud integration for data synchronization and centralized analysis. Together, these technologies support field monitoring, localized data processing, crop-health assessment, irrigation decision support, and accessible farmer services.
Unique Characteristics: AgriCare AI differentiates itself through the integration of drone-based field scanning and a distributed, node-based Edge AI architecture. Specialized sensing, communication, drone-monitoring, and processing nodes enable agricultural data collection and localized AI analysis, reducing dependence on continuous internet connectivity. Unlike solutions focused on a single farming challenge, AgriCare AI integrates crop recommendation, disease detection, smart irrigation, multilingual voice assistance, post-harvest intelligence, market intelligence, and a peer-to-peer farmer marketplace. Its modular architecture supports adaptation to different crops, languages, and farming environments. The combination of edge computing, connected hardware, and farmer-facing AI services aims to make precision agriculture more accessible to smallholder farmers.
Sustainable Change: AgriCare AI could help extend AI-enabled agriculture to smallholder farmers, particularly in rural communities with limited connectivity and access to agricultural expertise. Its modular node-based architecture can be replicated across regions by adapting hardware configurations, crop datasets, languages, and agricultural recommendations to local needs. Collaboration with agricultural universities, extension services, farmer-producer organizations, and technology providers could support field validation, farmer training, and wider adoption. Integration with agricultural buyers and marketplaces could further strengthen supply-chain connections and market access. If pilot studies demonstrate measurable benefits, the platform could contribute to more efficient water use, reduced agricultural losses, improved digital inclusion, and more resilient food-production systems. Long-term scaling would depend on affordability, reliable hardware, local partnerships, data privacy, and demonstrated benefits across different farming conditions.

Title: Global Credibility Registry: AI-Powered Trade & Trust Pass for Emerging SMEs
Subtitle: Automated AI infrastructure delivering verifiable digital trust passes (GRP) to seamlessly connect developing-economy SMEs with global supply chains.
Problem Statement: SMEs and solopreneurs in developing and middle-income economies face an exorbitant "Trust Deficit" when attempting to enter global industrial supply chains. Traditional cross-border due diligence and compliance checks (KYB) are prohibitively expensive ($1,000s per vendor), slow, and heavily reliant on manual review. As a result, millions of capable emerging-market suppliers are locked out of international trade corridors, while global buyers struggle to verify supplier legitimacy across fragmented, multi-lingual government registries.
Solution Overview: 1. How the Solution Works: Global Credibility Registry (GCR) functions as a lightweight, zero-manual-overhead AI data pipeline that transforms fragmented government registry data into standardized, verifiable international trust passes. The system operates via a 5-step automated workflow: 1)Input: The emerging-market SME inputs its company registration number and basic entity details. 2)Deterministic Query: GCR automatically queries official, primary government registries (e.g., Brazil Open CNPJ, China SAMR, UK Companies House) via Open Data APIs in real time. 3)AI Schema Mapping & Translation: A lightweight multi-lingual AI agent normalizes heterogeneous data schemas, cleans corporate text, and translates registration fields without hallucination (every data point remains 1-click linked to its official primary source). 4) Self-Verification: A company representative verifies control via cryptographic proof, claiming their official entity profile. 5) Pass Issuance: GCR generates a Global Registry Pass (GRP), delivering an embedded dynamic web badge, a verifiable PDF evidence pack with QR code validation, and a public validation portal page. 2. Methodologies and Technologies Used 1) Deterministic Fact-Mapping: Replaces subjective credit scoring with rigid, verifiable mapping against primary government sources. 2) Zero-Hallucination AI Architecture: Utilizes lightweight, domain-specific AI agents for Schema mapping, field alignment, and multi-lingual translation while maintaining absolute source-data fidelity. 3) Archival & Verification Infrastructure: Integrates legal deposit archival identifiers (ISBN/DOI) and cryptographic hash verification to ensure data immutability and compliance authority. 4) API-First Design: Enables seamless B2B integration with e-commerce platforms, trade portals, and supply chain management software. 3. Partnerships and Collaboration Models 1) Government & Open Data Registries: Direct API integration and collaboration with national corporate registrars and open data initiatives across developing and G20 economies. 2) International Trade & B2B Platforms: Partnering with cross-border e-commerce platforms, trade incubators, and industrial associations to offer batch KYB verification for onboarded suppliers. 3) UN & Development Agencies: Collaborating with multilateral organizations (such as UNIDO and Global Digital Compact working groups) to provide subsidized trust passes to micro-manufacturers and SMEs in emerging trade corridors (e.g., BRICS+, AfCFTA).
Solution Provider(s): United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO) (Multilateral UN agency promoting inclusive and sustainable industrial development across developing economies; Sector: Multilateral/Public Sector Governance), BRICS+ & AfCFTA Business Councils (Regional trade alignment and business incubation bodies facilitating cross-border industrial trade corridors across emerging markets; Sector: International Trade & Business Development), UK Companies House & International Open Data Registrars (National corporate registries providing real-time official Open Data API feeds for entity verification; Sector: Public Sector / Government Data Registries), Global Trade & Cross-Border B2B E-Commerce Platforms (Digital trade networks, industrial supply chain platforms, and SME incubators integrating batch KYB verification for onboarded suppliers; Sector: Technology / Cross-Border E-Commerce & Supply Chain Logistics).
Implementation location(s): Active Registry Node: United Kingdom (London headquarters / UK Companies House API Integration). Target Cross-Border Trade Corridors (Deployment Focus): Middle-Income and Developing Economies across BRICS+ and AfCFTA corridors (e.g., cross-border B2B manufacturing and supplier trade flows connecting Asia, Africa, and Latin America with G20/European buyer networks).
Implementation timeline(s): Initiation & Core Architectural Framing: September 2026 - Present
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 1 to 2 Weeks for API Adapter Deployment (1 Month Full SME Pilot Execution)
Desired impact: Main Objectives - Eliminate the "Trust Deficit" for MSMEs: Provide micro, small, and medium enterprises in developing and middle-income economies with an accessible, deterministic corporate verification pass to enter international industrial supply chains. - Automate Cross-Border Compliance: Replace costly, slow manual KYB and due diligence processes with zero-hallucination AI schema mapping linked directly to official government Open Data APIs. - Advance GDC Objective 2: Operationalize UN Global Digital Compact goals by fostering digital inclusion, open data standards, and transparent trade architecture for emerging-market exporters. Expected & Target Impact (Quantified) - 95% Reduction in Onboarding Cost: Lowers vendor verification costs for emerging-market SMEs from traditional agency rates ($1,000–$3,000 per check) down to $149/year, saving small suppliers millions collectively in export overhead. - Verification Speed Accelerating from Weeks to Minutes: Reduces cross-border vendor due diligence turnaround time from 14–21 business days to under 5 minutes. - 10,000+ MSMEs Onboarded in Target Pilot Phase: Enables over 10,000 industrial suppliers across China, BRICS+, and AfCFTA corridors to achieve verifiable digital trade identities within the first 12 months of pilot scaling. - Unlocking $50M+ in Cross-Border Digital Trade: Facilitates direct market access and international procurement eligibility for previously overlooked suppliers, driving sustainable economic growth and job retention in export manufacturing hubs.
Key technologies: Key Technologies Used - Deterministic AI & Multi-Lingual NLP Agents - Domain-specific, zero-hallucination Language Models (LLMs) calibrated strictly for cross-lingual schema mapping, entity resolution, and structured data extraction. The AI parses multi-lingual registry fields (e.g., Chinese, Portuguese, English) into standardized international KYB formats while maintaining 1-click source traceability to eliminate hallucination risk. - API-First Open Data Integrators - Automated REST and GraphQL integration pipelines that dynamically connect GCR with official government Open Data portals (such as UK Companies House, Brazil Open CNPJ, and China SAMR framework registries) for real-time entity validation. - Cryptographic Proof & Archival Identifiers - Cryptographic verification hashes combined with international legal deposit archival structures (ISBN/DOI) to create tamper-proof, time-stamped dynamic web badges and PDF evidence packages for verified corporate entities. - Cloud-Native Web Architecture - A lightweight, microservices-based SaaS infrastructure hosting real-time verification portals, dynamic SVG badge rendering, and automated document generation for instant B2B supply chain compliance checks.
Unique Characteristics: Key Differentiating Features - Deterministic AI vs. Generative Hallucination - Unlike standard LLM deployments that generate plausible text, GCR operates a deterministic, zero-hallucination data architecture. Every field in a Global Registry Pass (GRP) maps 1:1 to official primary government registries (e.g., SAMR, UK Companies House, Open CNPJ) with 1-click source traceability. - Radical Cost Compression for Emerging Markets - Traditional international KYB and corporate verification agencies charge $1,000–$3,000 per manual check with multi-week lead times. GCR’s automated 5-step pipeline compresses vendor verification cost to $149/year while delivering instant results, making formal international trade identity affordable for MSMEs in developing countries. - Universal "Passport-Style" Verifiable Identity - GCR standardizes heterogeneous legal formats across different national jurisdictions into a single, internationally recognized format. It provides multi-channel verification assets: a dynamic web badge, a downloadable PDF evidence pack with QR validation, and a public portal listing. - Archival Authority & Legal Deposit Standard
Sustainable Change: Potential for Systemic Change & Sustained Impact - Institutionalizing a Universal Trust Standard for Emerging-Market SMEs - By replacing opaque, expensive, third-party due diligence with an open, deterministic AI data pipeline, GCR fundamentally shifts how global supply chains verify vendor identity. Much like SSL certificates standardized web security, the Global Registry Pass (GRP) establishes a low-cost, universally accessible trust baseline that integrates seamlessly into corporate procurement, global e-commerce, and trade finance platforms. - Democratizing Export Market Access & Closing the Compliance Gap - Small and medium enterprises in developing and middle-income economies are disproportionately penalized by high compliance barriers and multi-thousand-dollar manual KYB costs. Lowering entity verification expenses to an accessible tier permanently lowers the barrier to international trade. This empowers solopreneurs and industrial suppliers across China, BRICS+, and AfCFTA corridors to participate in global supply chains without facing prohibitive regulatory overhead. - Replication via Modular Open Data Adapters - GCR’s architecture is natively designed for frictionless global scale-up. Because the solution relies on lightweight AI schema mapping paired with government Open Data APIs, expanding GCR to a new country or legal registry requires only a localized API adapter rather than localized physical infrastructure. This modular design allows multilateral organizations, national trade promotion agencies, and industry councils to replicate and deploy GCR across new jurisdictions in 2–4 weeks. - Catalyzing Transparent Trade Data Infrastructure - As a verifiable, zero-hallucination data registry, GCR incentivizes national government registrars and trade ministries to upgrade and open their public corporate data infrastructure. By demonstrating the economic return of transparent API access—specifically enhanced export competitiveness for local SMEs—GCR drives long-term policy shifts toward interoperable, open government data ecosystems.
Funding Sources: Openness to Institutional & Strategic Funding: While currently self-funded through pre-pilot deployment, GCR is actively open to co-funding, technical assistance grants, and strategic implementation partnerships with international development agencies, national governments, trade promotion bodies, and multilateral organizations. Such funding would accelerate: - Localized API adapter integrations for high-priority export hubs in developing and middle-income economies. - Subsidized or zero-cost Global Registry Pass (GRP) issuance for micro and small enterprises (MSMEs) to maximize market inclusion.
Testimonials and Endorsements: N/A – Pre-Pilot Phase As GCR is currently in its pre-pilot architectural stage (launched late September 2026), formal beneficiary quotes and external testimonials are not yet available. Initial stakeholder feedback and pilot beneficiary testimonials will be formally gathered and published following the live pilot demonstration and showcase at the AIM Global Action Forum in Vienna (November 25–26, 2026).

Summary: The Global Credibility Registry issues verifiable trust passes built from official company records, starting with a UK node and corridors into middle-income markets. The concept and the deterministic design are sound; it remains a pre-pilot proposition with no verified user.

Title: Exportplug: AI-Powered Digital Trade for African Exporters
Subtitle: Exportplug helps African agricultural SMEs simplify export processes, access global buyers and navigate international trade through digital tools and AI-enabled assistance.
Problem Statement: Agricultural exporters and small businesses across Nigeria and other developing economies face fragmented export processes, complex documentation, limited access to reliable international buyers, and difficulty understanding trade requirements. These barriers increase transaction costs, delay shipments, limit competitiveness and prevent many SMEs from participating in global value chains. Many businesses also lack affordable digital tools and specialised trade knowledge. Exportplug addresses these challenges by bringing export discovery, buyer connections, trade information and digital export workflows into one platform, with AI-enabled support designed to make international trade more accessible and efficient.
Solution Overview: Exportplug is a digital trade platform connecting Nigerian non-oil exporters with international buyers and providing tools to simplify export operations. The platform supports product listings, exporter storefronts, buyer enquiries and requests for quotations, while helping businesses organise the information required for export transactions. Its AI-enabled trade assistant is intended to help exporters understand trade procedures, identify relevant documentation requirements and navigate common export questions. AI-assisted document preparation and HS code classification can further reduce manual work where these capabilities are available and validated. The platform focuses on agricultural and other non-oil products, including cocoa, cashew, sesame, spices and related commodities. Its digital-first model can reduce information barriers for SMEs that cannot afford extensive in-house export expertise. The solution combines software, trade knowledge and connections across the export ecosystem. Potential collaboration areas include exporter associations, logistics providers, inspection and certification bodies, financial institutions and international trade-support organisations. Specific implementation partnerships will be identified and developed according to each market's requirements.
Implementation location(s): Nigeria — digital platform serving Nigerian non-oil exporters and connecting them with international buyers.
Implementation timeline(s): 24 months
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Approximately 3–6 months, subject to local trade regulations, buyer and exporter onboarding, integration requirements and pilot-partner availability.
Desired impact: Exportplug's primary objective is to make international trade more accessible and efficient for Nigerian agricultural exporters and SMEs through digital infrastructure and AI-enabled trade support. The solution aims to reduce the time and effort required to discover buyers, understand export requirements, prepare trade documentation and coordinate export transactions. By bringing these activities into a single digital environment, Exportplug seeks to reduce information gaps, improve operational efficiency and help more small businesses participate in international value chains. Key technologies: Exportplug uses a web-based digital marketplace and structured data systems to organise exporter profiles, product listings, buyer enquiries and trade-related information. Its AI-enabled development roadmap includes a trade assistant for export-related questions, support for export documentation workflows and HS code classification to help users identify relevant product classification requirements. The technology approach combines digital marketplace infrastructure, data processing and AI-assisted information retrieval and generation. Where AI outputs relate to regulatory or customs requirements, users should be able to review and verify the results against authoritative sources. The solution is designed to evolve through integrations with relevant trade, logistics and compliance services as these become available.
Unique Characteristics: Exportplug combines exporter discovery, international buyer access, requests for quotations and export workflow support in one digital platform focused on non-oil trade. Unlike a general marketplace, it is designed around the practical requirements of exporters who need to identify buyers, understand trade procedures and organise transaction documentation. Its AI-enabled direction adds a layer of accessible trade assistance to these workflows, with the potential to guide less experienced exporters through complex processes and reduce dependence on fragmented information sources. The business model combines transaction-based revenue with subscription options, supporting continued access to digital trade tools. The solution's distinctive opportunity is to make export capabilities more accessible to smaller businesses that lack dedicated trade and compliance teams.
Sustainable Change: Exportplug has the potential to contribute to systemic change by helping shift export participation from fragmented, relationship-dependent processes towards more accessible and data-driven digital trade workflows. By equipping SMEs with buyer-discovery tools, structured trade information and AI-enabled assistance, the platform can help reduce barriers that disproportionately affect businesses with limited resources and export expertise. Title: Governed AI for Smarter, Sustainable Construction
Subtitle: Turn fragmented construction data into trusted cost, productivity and sustainability insights in minutes, without specialist BI skills or hallucinated metrics
Problem Statement: Construction and infrastructure organisations operate across disconnected project management, ERP, scheduling, estimating, procurement, accounting and spreadsheet systems. Their data is available, but reliable answers are not. Reporting requires both technical business intelligence expertise and specialists who understand construction calculations. Outsourcing a custom dashboard can cost A$60,000 to A$80,000 and take four to six weeks across data extraction, mapping, metric definition and visualisation. This creates a significant barrier for smaller organisations and teams with limited analytical capacity. Decision-makers receive outdated information, struggle to compare project performance and cannot consistently connect cost, productivity, material consumption and environmental outcomes. Generic AI tools do not resolve the underlying problem. Without governed definitions, they can produce inconsistent calculations and unreliable answers from raw data.
Solution Overview: Konstruq consolidates construction data and models it through a governed semantic layer, enabling users to create dashboards and ask questions in plain language. The solution operates through five steps: 1. Connect: Ingest data from project management, ERP, scheduling, procurement and other systems. A live Procore integration is already available. 2. Map: Align inconsistent source structures and terminology with governed construction datasets. Standardise: Apply prebuilt calculations, KPIs and metric definitions across cost, schedule, productivity, materials and other project functions. 3. Analyse: Use AI to select and interpret approved metrics rather than independently inventing calculations over raw tables. 4. Visualise: Deliver reusable dashboards and traceable answers that construction professionals can use without SQL, Python or BI expertise. The working platform includes 635+ governed construction metrics, 33 semantic datasets and 80+ prebuilt dashboards. We are extending this foundation to building-emissions tracking and comparisons of human labour, machinery and robotics productivity. Our collaboration model brings together project owners, engineering teams and domain specialists. Users provide source data and reporting requirements; specialists validate calculations; Konstruq implements the governed model and reporting interface. New pilots would establish agreed baselines and measure reporting efficiency, data quality and relevant operational outcomes.

Konstruq currently works with enterprise beta participants, prospective design partners and individual strategic advisors. Requested a reporting use case comparing labour, machinery and robotics productivity and cost. This is a use-case engagement, not a confirmed formal partnership. eLab: Building-emissions tracking engagement. Confirm its full legal name, organisational profile, location and permission to reference it. Do not list VINCI, Atlassian, ByteDance or Procore as partners solely because of advisor experience, previous employment, product use or an integration.

The pilot would cover requirements, source-data assessment, integration, metric validation, dashboards and user testing. Complex integrations, security approvals or local emissions-factor requirements may extend this timeframe.
Desired impact: Konstruq’s main objective is to make trusted industrial analytics accessible to construction professionals without requiring specialist BI skills. The solution aims to: Reduce reporting lead times from weeks to minutes for supported, configured workflows. Lower dependence on repeated bespoke dashboard development. Standardise project calculations across disconnected systems. Improve visibility into cost, productivity, procurement and material performance. Enable traceable sustainability and emissions reporting. Help smaller organisations access analytical capabilities traditionally requiring specialist teams. No verified GHG reductions, energy savings or customer cost savings are claimed yet. Pilots would measure reporting hours, reporting cost, metric accuracy and adoption. Environmental applications would use agreed boundaries, verified emission factors and documented baselines before claiming reductions.
Key technologies: - Governed semantic modelling: Standardises construction calculations, relationships, KPIs and metric definitions. - AI and natural-language interfaces: Translate questions into governed analytical requests and explain results. - Data integration and transformation: Consolidate information from enterprise platforms and spreadsheets. - APIs and authentication: Support authorised connections, including the live Procore integration. - Cloud-based data infrastructure: Supports data processing, analytical datasets and application delivery. - Dashboarding and visualisation: Turn approved metrics into reusable reports and comparative insights. Konstruq analyses machinery and robotics performance data; it does not manufacture robots or directly control industrial equipment.
Unique Characteristics: Konstruq’s advantage is not another connector or chatbot. It is the construction knowledge encoded between source data and the answer. Traditional BI tools require customers to define calculations and build models themselves. Platform-specific analytics primarily serve their own ecosystems. Generic AI tools can generate calculations from raw data without consistent construction definitions. Konstruq combines multi-system data consolidation, prebuilt domain calculations, governed datasets, dashboards and constrained AI in one product. Construction professionals can visualise information without specialist BI expertise, while AI reasons over approved metrics rather than inventing them. Our commercial model supports both project-based adoption and portfolio subscriptions. Customers can begin with one defined use case, then reuse the same governed foundation across projects. The approach also creates a foundation for sustainability reporting and future predictive analytics.

Once calculations and source mappings are validated, they can be reused across projects and adapted across organisations and countries. This reduces repeated modelling work and makes performance comparisons more consistent. The wider opportunity is to make domain expertise usable without requiring every construction professional to become a data analyst. Smaller firms and resource-constrained agencies could gain better visibility using systems they already operate. With local industry and research partners, the same foundation could connect cost, productivity, material use and emissions. This would support more transparent procurement and investment decisions. Title: Travessia: a voice-first app for informal cross-border traders in Africa
Subtitle: Traders speak what they want to carry and get the rules, a checklist and a QR Trade Passport in plain language, built for people who cannot use compliance documents.
Problem Statement: Trade rules were written for formal businesses, not for small traders. Requirements are fragmented across agencies and countries, documents are built for formal operators, and fees and queues are unexpected. Many traders depend on intermediaries and risk informal payments. The trader loses time, money, goods and trust in the formal system, and governments lose visibility over a large share of the trade crossing their borders.
Solution Overview: Travessia is voice-first trade facilitation infrastructure. A trader says what she wants to carry, for example “30 pieces of clothing from Angola to Zambia”. AI identifies the product, route and purpose, then explains the rules in plain language. The app prepares a personalised checklist, shown and read aloud, and flags gaps and inconsistencies. It issues a Trade Passport, a QR credential an officer can scan to see a prepared operation. It supports but never replaces the competent authority. The first corridor is Lobito (Angola, DRC, Zambia), and an interactive prototype has been built. It is listed on the UN Digital Cooperation Portal as a Global Digital Compact contribution.
Solution Provider(s): No formal partners yet. The pilot is designed with border authorities, trader associations and corridor operators on the Lobito Corridor, and institutional partners are being sought.
Implementation location(s): N/A.
Implementation timeline(s): About 6 to 9 months once the core is built: core regulatory engine and voice assistant in the first 3 months, then trader testing on real routes in months 4 to 6, and authority integration after that. (Ajusta este intervalo, é uma estimativa tua.)
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6 to 9 months
Desired impact: The objective is to make cross-border trade easier, safer and more transparent for small-scale traders, and to give governments structured, anonymised data on trade that is invisible today. Expected impact: traders know which documents to bring and what to expect, officers receive prepared operations, and governments and development institutions gain evidence on products, routes, peak periods and bottlenecks. As the solution is at prototype stage and pre-revenue, impact is projected and will be measured in the pilot (time saved, costs avoided, operations prepared).
Key technologies: Voice interface and speech understanding, AI for product, route and purpose identification, a regulatory engine that turns multi-country rules into personalised instructions, QR-based verifiable credentials (Trade Passport), and a privacy-preserving analytics layer.
Unique Characteristics: Four layers rarely meet in one product: a voice interface that removes the digital-literacy barrier, regulatory intelligence for each product and crossing, a digital credential officers can verify, and trade data infrastructure. Most digital trade tools assume a literate user. Travessia assumes the opposite. It is free for traders and paid by institutions.
Sustainable Change: Travessia can scale corridor by corridor (Lobito, then Beira, then West African Lusophone links), adding languages as it grows, from Portuguese, French and English to Lingala, Bemba, Kikongo and others. Anonymised, aggregated data on small-scale trade can inform policy, customs authorities and development finance, supporting formalisation and the inclusive trade agenda of the AfCFTA. It contributes directly to the Global Digital Compact objective of expanding inclusion in the digital economy.
Funding Sources: No external funding to date. The solution has been developed and self-funded through ILOG Consultancy. A pre-seed round is being sought to build the MVP and run the Lobito pilot.
Primary thematic focus area: Industrial Ecosystem Enablers: Finance, Skills and Market Access
Summary: Travessia lets informal cross-border traders speak what they carry and receive the rules, a checklist and a QR passport in plain language. The design is well judged for its users; with no pilot and no authority engagement, it remains a prototype.
Thematic focus areas (as submitted): Industrial AI Models and Intelligent Decision-Making; Industrial Digital Infrastructure and Data Ecosystems; Industrial Ecosystem Enablers: Finance, Skills and Market Access

Title: Auditable AI Evidence Passport for Sustainable Agroindustrial Supply Chains
Subtitle: Hybrid evidence intelligence and versioned decision rules for transparent, traceable environmental due diligence in Brazilian Amazon coffee and cocoa value chains.
Problem Statement: Coffee and cocoa exporters, processors and their small suppliers need to reconcile company registries, rural property identifiers, geospatial deforestation information and transaction documents to assess supply-chain risks. Sources are fragmented, often updated at different times and may contain gaps or conflicting claims. Manual due diligence is hard to reproduce consistently. Generic generative AI can generate fluent but unsupported compliance conclusions. VerdeSaber aims to convert heterogeneous records into source-linked evidence, explicitly distinguish risk from missing information, and support defensible human and policy-based decisions without misrepresenting uncertainty.
Solution Overview: VerdeSaber is developing an auditable evidence-and-decision architecture for agroindustrial supplier screening. A planned pre-check uses a company identifier (CNPJ), rural land registry information (CAR), product and harvest period; expanded diligence is designed to connect transaction documents, property polygons and supplier/lot identifiers. A structured evidence record preserves its provenance, date of the underlying fact, collection time, scope and verification status. Versioned deterministic rules are intended to produce a reasoned classification and next diligence action, with a human review path when information is incomplete. Technical foundation already developed or specified includes data-source ingestion routines, connectors to Brazilian public environmental and business records, an append-only evidence model and a Python bridge related to the EU Deforestation Regulation information system. The bridge has approximately 137 automated tests; this is connector-level testing, not proof of AI model accuracy or commercial deployment. The planned AI research layer will extract data from heterogeneous documents with exact source references, link entities across business and geospatial records, reconcile conflicting or outdated evidence and calibrate confidence. AI will propose and support evidence; a separate, versioned rule engine will make reproducible classifications. Low-confidence cases will abstain and go to human review. Current maturity: experimental proof of concept (approximately TRL 3), not an integrated production-ready AI solution. The initial intended validation context is coffee and cocoa supply chains in Rondônia, Brazil. Formal partners for this specific solution will be named only after documented commitment.
Solution Provider(s): No external partner is formally committed to implementing this specific submission at present. VERDESABER LTDA leads the development. Potential technical cooperation with research institutions and value-chain organizations will be confirmed through written agreements before any joint pilot.
Implementation location(s): N/A — no completed agroindustrial field deployment is claimed. The technical proof of concept has been developed in Porto Velho, Rondônia, Brazil.
Implementation timeline(s): N/A — integrated AI pilot deployment has not yet been completed. Core architecture and connector development took place in 2025–2026.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Estimated 18–24 months to develop and independently validate the integrated AI layer in a first relevant-environment pilot; after that, a new-geography pilot may need approximately 3–6 additional months for local source mapping, data governance and partner onboarding. These are planning estimates, not achieved milestones.
Desired impact: The primary objective is to develop an auditable, human-supervised AI-assisted due diligence workflow for agroindustrial supply chains. Intended outcomes include more reproducible supplier decisions, transparent identification of missing records, better access to documentary verification for MSMEs, and support for sustainable sourcing. Measured technical progress to date includes approximately 137 automated tests of one Python regulatory-information-system connector, not an end-to-end model validation or proof of environmental impact. No verified reduction in emissions, deforestation, processing time or compliance risk is claimed yet. For future field evaluation, VerdeSaber proposes to benchmark the workflow against manual diligence and generic AI across real, consented cases; record evidence traceability, error rates and cases correctly withheld for human review; and test a target of at least 50% reduction in diligence effort. This target is aspirational and will not be reported as achieved without controlled measurements. Climate and conservation benefits would be assessed through defensible indicators, not inferred from software use alone.
Key technologies: Current foundation: Python services and API connectors; ingestion and normalization of public data; Brazilian company identifiers (CNPJ) and rural land registry (CAR) linkages; remote-sensing datasets where legally available (e.g., INPE PRODES/DETER); geospatial evidence processing; append-only, time-stamped provenance records; version-controlled policies and deterministic risk rules; automated connector tests. Research under development: AI-assisted document parsing and grounded extraction; entity resolution; temporal conflict analysis; confidence calibration and abstention; human-review escalation. The submission does not claim a deployed predictive model, live EU regulatory integration, blockchain, IoT or measured AI accuracy.
Unique Characteristics: The distinguishing architecture separates probabilistic interpretation from the authority to issue a compliance classification: AI is designed to prepare and support cited evidence, while a deterministic, versioned rules engine reaches an auditable status or escalates the case. Individual evidence items retain source references, timestamps and context; disagreements, stale records and absence of information are treated explicitly instead of being silently converted into green-light decisions. The design supports selective review and explainable next actions, with traceable changes when rules or source facts change. The business approach targets modular reuse of data connectors and policy configurations for smaller agroindustrial operators rather than bespoke systems per buyer. These innovations remain under active validation.
Sustainable Change: A reproducible evidence protocol can lower the cost of trustworthy industrial sourcing checks while helping smaller suppliers demonstrate what is known, what is missing and what must be corrected. If validated, the architecture could be replicated from Rondônia coffee and cocoa to other Brazilian Amazon value chains and subsequently to other countries by replacing jurisdiction-specific data connectors and policy rules, with local legal review. Shared definitions of evidence and public-source provenance could enable interoperable buyer–supplier due diligence, reduce duplicate document requests and improve traceability of green claims. At present these are intended systemic effects, not measured deployment results. Adaptation would require lawful access to local data, secure handling of sensitive information, human oversight and country-specific validation.
Funding Sources: Development of this specific proof of concept has primarily used VerdeSaber's own engineering and operating resources. Separately, VerdeSaber is a beneficiary of FAPERO/Finep Tecnova III funding for the distinct Verde Turismo sustainable-tourism technology project; that funding is not presented as a grant for this AI evidence-passport solution. Further R&D support and industrial pilots remain contingent on future decisions and agreements.
Testimonials and Endorsements: N/A for this specific solution: the integrated AI component is still at proof-of-concept stage, and no verified beneficiary testimonial or impact endorsement from an agroindustrial pilot is claimed. Organizational service attestations exist but do not establish validation of this product.
Primary thematic focus area: AI for Green, Resilient and Sustainable Industry
Summary: VerdeSaber is building an auditable evidence passport for Brazilian coffee and cocoa supply chains, with versioned rules deciding the compliance status. The architecture is well judged; as a proof of concept with no field use, it scores on design.
