Title: Phygitalytics: AI-Powered Industrial Sustainability Intelligence
Subtitle: Turning fragmented ESG and industrial sustainability data into auditable intelligence for carbon management, resource efficiency, regulatory readiness and responsible decision-making.
Problem Statement: Industrial enterprises, particularly MSMEs in developing and middle-income economies, face growing pressure to measure, report and improve their environmental and sustainability performance. However, critical data on greenhouse gas emissions, energy consumption, water usage, waste, supply chains and governance remains fragmented across PDF reports, spreadsheets, operational systems and regulatory disclosures. Existing sustainability solutions can be expensive, technically complex and difficult to adapt to local regulatory frameworks. Smaller enterprises often lack dedicated sustainability specialists, advanced analytics capabilities and affordable digital infrastructure. Consequently, organizations struggle with data quality, inconsistent reporting, limited benchmarking, regulatory readiness and the ability to translate historical sustainability data into actionable operational decisions. Phygitalytics addresses this gap by making AI-powered sustainability data extraction, analytics, anomaly detection and decision support accessible, explainable and auditable. The objective is to help enterprises move beyond compliance-oriented reporting toward measurable resource efficiency, environmental accountability and evidence-based industrial sustainability transformation.
Solution Overview: Phygitalytics ESG Intelligence Platform is an AI-powered, BRSR-native sustainability intelligence solution designed to transform fragmented environmental, social and governance information into structured, validated and actionable intelligence. How the solution works 1. Data ingestion and extraction: The platform processes sustainability reports, BRSR disclosures, PDFs and structured datasets using AI-assisted extraction workflows, converting fragmented information into standardized sustainability metrics. 2. Data validation and harmonization: Extracted information is validated, normalized and mapped to sustainability indicators and reporting frameworks, including BRSR, GRI, SASB and CSRD-related requirements. 3. Sustainability intelligence: The platform provides analytics covering Scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions, energy consumption, water management, waste, employee well-being, governance and reporting quality. 4. Natural-language analytics: Users can ask sustainability questions in natural language. A controlled text-to-SQL workflow translates validated requests into database queries and presents results through visualizations and contextual analysis. 5. Anomaly detection and benchmarking: Analytical workflows identify potential reporting inconsistencies, unusual trends, missing disclosures and opportunities for comparative performance assessment. 6. Decision support: Scenario analysis, risk indicators and recommendation workflows help organizations explore potential sustainability improvements and prioritize areas requiring further investigation. 7. Responsible AI and governance: The architecture incorporates controlled data access, validation, observability, evaluation and audit-oriented workflows. AI-generated insights support human decisions rather than replacing accountable professionals. Methodologies and technologies The solution combines generative AI, retrieval and context-management techniques, natural-language-to-SQL, statistical analytics, structured databases, data-quality validation, visualization and modular AI orchestration. It is designed for cloud and on-premises deployment, allowing adaptation to organizational data sovereignty, privacy and infrastructure requirements. AI-driven optimization is needed to continuously balance energy efficiency, operational reliability and production demand.

The solution combines industrial operational data with physics-based and data-driven models to analyze equipment performance, predict system behavior and identify more energy-efficient operating strategies. It works together with energy management and industrial automation systems to provide actionable optimization recommendations and support continuous performance improvement. The approach combines industrial AI, process domain knowledge, energy management and automation technologies, and can be adapted to different equipment configurations and operating conditions. Deployment is typically carried out in collaboration with customers and qualified engineering partners, combining Rockwell Automation’s technology capabilities with customer process knowledge and local engineering expertise.

Title: Noveum.ai: reliability infrastructure for industrial AI agents
Subtitle: Test, trace and improve AI assistants and workflow agents before release, with reproducible evidence and human review. Built and delivered by Noveum’s in-house team.
Problem Statement: Industrial firms adopting AI assistants face a practical trust problem: a plausible answer can hide a failed tool call, a wrong workflow outcome or a regression after a model change. Smaller firms often lack a repeatable evaluation process and specialist staff. We propose adapting Noveum’s existing evaluation platform to industrial knowledge assistants and operational workflows, starting with low-risk decision support rather than autonomous equipment control.
Solution Overview: Noveum connects instrumented agent traces, saved test datasets, configured evaluators, scenario testing and engineer-reviewed recommendations. For an industrial pilot, the business owner defines the task, approved knowledge and expected result; Noveum’s own team integrates the selected agent, captures permitted evidence, builds representative cases and compares baseline and candidate behavior. Deterministic checks verify observable tool/state outcomes; rubric-based checks and human review assess response quality. The customer approves changes and release decisions. A proposed six-to-eight-week pilot would cover one knowledge assistant or workflow, deployment/data boundaries, baseline measurement, failure review and exportable cases. Noveum would own implementation through its in-house AI and voice agents vertical. We seek an industrial SME or ecosystem host as a pilot counterpart; no UN, government or manufacturing partner is claimed. Existing commercial evaluation evidence comes from conversational and voice systems; industrial deployments remain a proposed extension.
Solution Provider(s): No formal industrial pilot partners appointed. Noveum.ai / MagicAPI Inc. is the solution owner and in-house technical delivery organization.
Implementation location(s): N/A for industrial implementation. The existing general-purpose platform has commercial conversational/voice evaluation experience, including a published MyOperator case in India.
Implementation timeline(s): N/A for industrial implementation. Noveum’s AI evaluation platform work dates from 2025; an existing client evaluation report is dated 3 November 2025.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Estimated 6-8 weeks after a pilot host, representative agent, approved data and access/security arrangements are ready. This is a proposed schedule, not an existing commitment.
Desired impact: The objective is to help industrial organizations adopt AI with checkable quality and operating controls. A pilot would measure task completion, grounded-answer quality, failed tool actions, regression frequency, review effort and evaluation cost. Noveum has published commercial evaluation evidence, but we do not claim measured manufacturing productivity, energy savings, emissions reductions or jobs created. Industrial impact would be established with a pilot baseline and jointly agreed metrics. Start with one workflow and report both improvements and remaining failures.
Key technologies: Python and TypeScript instrumentation; trace/span capture; dataset and evaluation APIs; deterministic and model-based scoring; configurable chat and voice scenario testing; evidence-linked recommendations; cloud or scoped private deployment. Model-based evaluations require approved model endpoints and a defined data-processing boundary. SOC 2 Type II is in progress; no completed certification or blanket industrial safety compliance is claimed.
Unique Characteristics: The differentiation is the engineering workflow after a failure is detected: connect a business outcome to the exact agent/tool evidence, compare candidate changes on repeatable cases, inspect regressions and retain the engineer’s approval. Noveum’s own team can build integrations and agent workflows as well as evaluate them. Industrial partners would receive a scoped implementation and reusable evidence, rather than an unverified promise that one quality score certifies safety. Deployment and support are sized to the host’s resources.
Sustainable Change: Reusable evaluation cases and reviewer practices can make AI adoption more accessible to smaller industrial firms that cannot build a full reliability team. An initial host can establish a repeatable method for approving sources, testing local-language journeys and comparing releases. With permission, generic templates and lessons could be adapted across firms and countries while keeping each company’s data and IP boundaries separate. The intended result is sustained capacity to inspect and improve agents; broader impact remains to be measured.
Funding Sources: The existing software has been developed as Noveum’s commercial product, supported by company resources and customer engagements. No dedicated funding for the proposed industrial adaptation, UN financing or committed pilot budget is claimed.
Testimonials and Endorsements: Published Noveum customer case: MyOperator, conversational and voice-agent evaluation. https://noveum.ai/en/case-studies/myoperator . This is evidence from a commercial evaluation engagement, not an industrial deployment or independent certification. No UN or government endorsement is claimed.

The product is real and the industrial application is proposed, which on this ladder places it in the middle: the discipline of the submission is not the same thing as evidence of industrial use.

Title: Bean Origin: AI-Powered Traceability and Sustainable Coffee Supply Chains
Subtitle: Bean Origin uses digital traceability, sustainability data and AI-powered insights to connect coffee farmers, cooperatives and buyers, improving supply-chain transparency, responsible production and access to global markets.
Problem Statement: Smallholder coffee farmers and cooperatives face fragmented record-keeping, limited farm-to-market traceability, inconsistent sustainability data, and difficulties demonstrating compliance with evolving environmental and due diligence requirements. These challenges reduce transparency, increase verification costs, and limit access to international markets. Buyers and other value-chain stakeholders also lack reliable, connected information on coffee origin, quality, production practices, and sustainability. Coffee Pulse addresses these gaps through Bean Origin, a digital platform that connects farm-level and supply-chain data, strengthens traceability, and is developing AI-powered capabilities to support sustainability assessment, compliance workflows, and better market decisions.
Solution Overview: Bean Origin, developed by Coffee Pulse Uganda Ltd, is a digital platform improving traceability, sustainability data management and market access in agricultural value chains, starting with coffee. It connects farmers, cooperatives and supply-chain stakeholders through structured digital records covering producer identity, farms, harvests, batches, lots, quality and sustainability information. Digital lot records and QR-enabled access improve visibility and information sharing from origin to market. The platform uses digital traceability, sustainability data collection and is developing AI-powered capabilities to analyse information, identify missing documentation, flag potential compliance issues and support market intelligence. Blockchain-based verification is also being explored to strengthen the integrity of selected supply-chain records. AI workflows will retain human oversight, and the platform supports rather than replaces formal certification or regulatory authorities. Coffee Pulse collaborates with farmers, cooperatives, exporters, international buyers, technology partners and agricultural institutions through onboarding, pilot projects, data validation and training. Accepted into in5 Tech Dubai, Coffee Pulse is expanding its network while developing solutions for more transparent, sustainable and market-ready agricultural supply chains.
Solution Provider(s): Ndugu Coffee – Coffee production, sourcing and supply chain; Great Lakes Coffee Roastery – Coffee roasting, processing and value addition; in5 Tech Dubai – Technology incubation and startup support; Hub71 – Abu Dhabi technology startup ecosystem; Coffee Pulse’s participating coffee cooperatives in Uganda – Agricultural production and smallholder farmer organisations.
Implementation location(s): Uganda/ Kampala, Dubai/ UAE
Implementation timeline(s): Uganda – Kampala and participating coffee cooperatives’ sites across Uganda.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3–6 months, depending on local partner onboarding, data availability, regulatory requirements, and integration needs.
Desired impact: Bean Origin aims to improve agricultural supply-chain transparency, sustainability, and market access through digital traceability and AI-powered decision support. Its objectives are to connect farm-level data with supply-chain records, strengthen sustainability and due diligence documentation, reduce manual verification processes, and help farmers, cooperatives, and buyers make better-informed decisions. The solution is currently being tested and expanded in Uganda, engaging over 500 farmers across three coffee cooperatives. Its digital platform supports producer identification, farm and harvest records, batch and lot traceability, and access to origin information. Coffee Pulse is developing AI capabilities to identify missing documentation, support compliance workflows, and provide market intelligence. Expected impacts include improved traceability, reduced information gaps, more efficient documentation, stronger readiness for environmental and buyer requirements, and improved access to international markets for smallholder farmers and coffee businesses. Over time, the solution aims to support more sustainable production and responsible sourcing by making relevant supply-chain information easier to record, access, and verify. Quantified reductions in greenhouse-gas emissions, energy use, or jobs created have not yet been established. Future pilots will measure adoption, traceability coverage, documentation efficiency, and market-access outcomes to assess the solution’s impact.
Key technologies: Bean Origin uses digital traceability and data management technologies to connect coffee farm records, harvests, batches, lots, quality information and sustainability data across the supply chain. Artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities are under development to support market intelligence, identify missing documentation, and assist with compliance workflows and decision-making. Blockchain technology is being explored to strengthen the integrity and verifiability of selected supply-chain records. QR-code technology enables stakeholders to access digital lot and origin information, improving transparency from farm to market. The platform combines structured data collection, digital records and traceability workflows to support sustainability monitoring, due diligence and market access. AI-assisted workflows will retain human oversight, while the platform supports rather than replaces formal certification and regulatory verification.
Unique Characteristics: Bean Origin is distinctive in combining farm-to-market digital traceability, sustainability data, QR-enabled lot information and developing AI-powered decision support within one platform. Rather than treating traceability, compliance documentation and market intelligence as separate services, it connects these functions to help farmers, cooperatives and buyers access more reliable, actionable supply-chain information. Its approach begins with smallholder coffee farmers and cooperatives, helping digitise fragmented records and link producer, farm, harvest, batch and lot information to international buyer requirements. AI capabilities under development aim to identify documentation gaps, support due-diligence workflows and improve market decisions, while blockchain-based verification is being explored to strengthen the integrity of selected records. The business model combines digital infrastructure with agricultural commerce, creating opportunities for transaction-based revenue and premium data and intelligence services. Its collaborative delivery approach involves farmers, cooperatives, coffee businesses and technology ecosystem partners. With over 500 farmers across three cooperatives engaged in Uganda, Bean Origin is developing a practical, scalable model that can expand beyond coffee to other agricultural commodities across Africa.
Sustainable Change: Bean Origin has the potential to transform agricultural value chains by replacing fragmented, paper-based records with connected digital infrastructure that improves traceability, sustainability monitoring and access to market information. By starting with coffee farmers and cooperatives in Uganda, the solution can demonstrate how digital tools help smallholder producers participate more effectively in international markets and respond to evolving environmental and due diligence requirements. Its model can be replicated across coffee-producing regions and adapted to other agricultural commodities, including cocoa and other export crops. As more farmers, cooperatives, exporters and buyers participate, shared digital records could improve supply-chain coordination, reduce information gaps, strengthen responsible sourcing and make origin and production information more accessible. Future AI capabilities could further scale this impact by helping identify documentation gaps, support compliance workflows and deliver actionable insights to stakeholders with limited access to specialised expertise. Partnerships with agricultural institutions, governments, technology providers and international buyers could accelerate adoption and encourage interoperable data practices. Over time, Bean Origin aims to contribute to more transparent, inclusive and sustainable agricultural trade, helping producers capture greater market opportunities while supporting evidence-based sustainability and due diligence practices across African commodity value chains.

Title: Real-World Tactile Data for Industrial Embodied AI
Subtitle: A PaXini–BYD initiative transforming real-world automotive assembly expertise into multimodal tactile datasets to advance industrial robot learning, intelligent manufacturing, and scalable Physical AI.
Problem Statement: Despite advances in industrial automation, complex manufacturing tasks remain heavily dependent on skilled human workers. Three interconnected challenges hinder the broader adoption of Embodied AI: 1. The Tactile Intelligence Gap: Conventional vision-based robots struggle with contact-rich operations requiring precise tactile perception, adaptive force control, and real-time responses to material variations. 2. The Real-World Industrial Data Gap: Skilled workers' tactile expertise remains largely unstructured, while the scarcity of high-quality multimodal industrial datasets limits robot learning, generalization, and deployment. 3. The Geographic Data and Digital Equity Gap: Industrial AI datasets risk underrepresenting manufacturing conditions, local expertise, and operational practices in developing and underserved regions, for instance, in most parts of Africa. Limited digital infrastructure and access to AI technologies may further widen this divide. Addressing these challenges is essential to developing scalable, geographically representative, and inclusive industrial AI systems that can benefit manufacturers across different economies.
Solution Overview: PaXini × BYD: Building Real-World Data Infrastructure for Industrial Embodied AI PaXini and BYD are transforming human tactile expertise and physical interactions into high-quality multimodal datasets for robotic learning and scalable automotive automation. 1. Technical Solution: From Human Expertise to Machine Intelligence The solution integrates PaXini's proprietary data collection hardware, tactile sensing, AI models, and robotics in real automotive production. - Proprietary multimodal data collection: PaXini's self-developed hardware captures synchronized vision, tactile, force/torque, proprioceptive, and motion trajectory data. - Industrial expertise digitization: By capturing skilled workers' physical interactions during contact-rich assembly operations, the solution transforms tacit manufacturing expertise into structured, reusable datasets for robotic learning. - Embodied AI model training: The collected industrial datasets are used to train embodied AI models, enabling robots to learn complex manipulation skills grounded in real-world physical interactions. - Robotic task validation: Models are evaluated through robotic tasks, connecting real-world data collection, model development, and performance assessment. 2. Real-World Implementation: Automotive Assembly at BYD The initiative is being implemented in BYD's real-world automotive manufacturing environment, where frequent model changes, complex assembly procedures, and stringent quality requirements create significant challenges for traditional automation. PaXini has validated its proprietary multimodal industrial data collection system in BYD's manufacturing operations. The collected data are already being used for embodied AI model training and robotic task validation. PaXini and BYD are also advancing industrial data collection, governance, and application, while exploring the broader integration of tactile perception technologies into automotive production processes. The long-term objective is a replicable approach across production lines and facilities. 3. Partnership Model: Industry-Driven Co-Development The partnership follows a demand-driven, collaborative development model: - BYD provides real-world production scenarios, defines operational requirements, and contributes industrial process expertise. - PaXini provides tactile sensing technologies (self-developed hardware equipment and solutions), multimodal data collection capabilities, embodied AI methodologies, and robotic system expertise. - Joint development focuses on translating industrial knowledge into reusable datasets, validating technical approaches, and developing scalable solutions for future deployment. - Both parties also plan to jointly advance relevant national industrial training initiatives for humanoid robotics and embodied intelligence, further connecting industrial applications with technology development and workforce capabilities. 4. Scalability and Sustainable Industrial Development The initiative aims to establish a replicable framework for collecting, governing, and utilizing real-world industrial embodied data. Starting with automotive assembly, this framework has the potential to be adapted across production lines, manufacturing facilities, and other contact-intensive industries. By expanding access to high-quality industrial AI training data, the solution seeks to strengthen industrial innovation and resilience. In future deployments—including underserved manufacturing regions in Africa and elsewhere—locally grounded data collection could better represent diverse equipment, production conditions, and workforce expertise, supporting context-relevant models and local AI capacity-building.
Solution Provider(s): BYD Company Limited (Automotive Manufacturing & New Energy Vehicles): A global automotive manufacturer providing real-world industrial production scenarios, manufacturing expertise, and operational requirements for embodied AI development and validation. PaXini AI (Embodied AI & Industrial Robotics): A physical intelligence technology company providing proprietary tactile sensing technologies, multimodal embodied data collection hardware, AI model training capabilities, and robotic systems for industrial applications.
Implementation location(s): Currently implemented at BYD's manufacturing facilities in Shenzhen, China. The solution is planned to expand across BYD's nationwide production network within one year, followed by its global manufacturing network within three years.
Implementation timeline(s): Ongoing program started in September 2026.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Three years or sooner.
Desired impact: Main Objectives The initiative aims to establish scalable industrial embodied AI data infrastructure by transforming skilled workers' tactile expertise and physical interactions into high-quality multimodal training datasets. It seeks to improve robotic adaptability and industrial resilience; longer term, it also aims to broaden representation of diverse manufacturing environments in AI training data. Demonstrated Impact - Successfully validated PaXini's proprietary multimodal data collection system in BYD's real-world automotive manufacturing environment. - Initiated embodied AI model training and robotic task validation using industrial datasets integrating vision, tactile sensing, force/torque, proprioception, and motion trajectories. - Established a strategic industry–technology partnership to advance industrial data governance, robotic learning, and practical applications of embodied AI. Expected Impact - Industrial productivity: Improve robotic manipulation capabilities in contact-intensive assembly processes, reducing reliance on repetitive manual operations. - Resource efficiency: Support more precise assembly and adaptive process control, with the potential to reduce material waste and production errors. - Inclusive technology access: Develop replicable data collection and training methodologies that can be adapted to the needs and connectivity constraints of underserved manufacturing regions, enabling more representative datasets, technology transfer, and local capacity-building. - Workforce development: Transform skilled workers' operational knowledge into reusable digital resources and assets, supporting industrial AI skills development and human–robot collaboration.
Key technologies: - Embodied AI and Industrial Robotics: Robot learning and task validation for complex, contact-rich automotive assembly operations. - Proprietary Multimodal Data Collection Hardware: PaXini's self-developed equipment for collecting synchronized, high-quality industrial embodied data. - Multidimensional Tactile and Force Sensing: Advanced tactile sensors and force/torque sensing technologies capturing physical contact, force feedback, and manipulation dynamics. - Real-World Industrial Data Collection: Integrated acquisition of vision, tactile, force/torque, proprioceptive states, and motion trajectory data from real manufacturing environments. - AI Model Training and Robotic Learning: Multimodal embodied AI model training and robotic task validation using real-world industrial datasets.
Unique Characteristics: - Tactile-Driven Physical AI: Integrates multidimensional tactile sensing and force/torque feedback, enabling AI systems to learn physical interactions beyond conventional vision-based approaches. - Proprietary Multimodal Data Infrastructure: Leverages PaXini's self-developed hardware to capture high-quality, synchronized vision, tactile, force/torque, proprioception, and motion trajectory data in real manufacturing environments. - Closed-Loop Robot Learning: Establishes a data-to-model-to-robot validation framework, transforming skilled workers' tacit knowledge into reusable datasets for embodied AI training and industrial task validation. - Industry-Driven Co-Development: Combines BYD's real production scenarios and manufacturing expertise with PaXini's sensing, data, and AI capabilities, ensuring innovation addresses actual industrial challenges. - Scalable and Replicable Architecture: Transferable data collection and robotic learning methods can be adapted to diverse industrial environments, potentially incorporating underrepresented local manufacturing practices into future training datasets.
Sustainable Change: - Scalable Industrial Deployment: Establish a replicable framework for multimodal data collection, model training, and robotic validation, with potential expansion across BYD's global manufacturing network and other industries. - Inclusive Data and Digital Equity: Future deployment in developing and underserved regions, including parts of Africa, could incorporate local industrial conditions, equipment, and workforce knowledge into training datasets, reducing geographic underrepresentation and supporting local AI capacity-building. - Sustainable and Human-Centered Manufacturing: More precise, adaptive robotic operations could reduce defects and material waste, while supporting safer human–robot collaboration, skills development, and higher-value work. - Global Knowledge Sharing and Systemic Impact: Encourage interoperable industrial data practices and international technology cooperation, broadening access to Physical AI and its long-term benefits for economic opportunity and human well-being.

Title: AMICUS-AI: Predictive Energy Management for Sustainable Industry
Subtitle: An AI-powered IoT energy management system that predicts energy demand, optimises solar–grid power selection and improves renewable-energy utilisation, reliability and efficiency in industrial facilities.
Problem Statement: Existing hybrid solar–grid energy management technologies provide automatic power-source switching, battery monitoring and basic energy management. However, many conventional systems rely on fixed voltage thresholds, predefined switching rules and reactive control mechanisms. Although these technologies help maintain electricity supply, they have limited capacity to predict future energy demand, anticipate solar generation fluctuations, analyse consumption patterns or make adaptive, data-driven energy-management decisions. In industrial facilities, SMEs, manufacturing workshops and technical institutions, this limitation can result in suboptimal solar energy utilisation, unnecessary dependence on grid electricity, inefficient battery utilisation, increased operating costs and vulnerability to power interruptions. Advanced intelligent energy management solutions are often expensive, complex to customise and difficult for smaller enterprises to maintain using locally available technical expertise. The key gap is the limited integration of affordable IoT monitoring, predictive artificial intelligence and automated hybrid energy management in a locally adaptable solution for developing economies. AMICUS-AI seeks to address this gap by advancing an existing ESP32-based automatic solar–grid changeover prototype into an AI-enhanced predictive energy management system. By combining real-time electrical monitoring, machine-learning-based forecasting and intelligent source-selection support, the solution aims to move beyond reactive threshold-based switching towards predictive, efficient and adaptive energy management. It will provide a modular and affordable approach that can be adapted to the energy needs of SMEs, industrial facilities and technical institutions, supporting renewable-energy utilisation, operational efficiency and sustainable industrial development.
Solution Overview: AMICUS-AI is an AI-powered predictive energy management solution designed to transform conventional hybrid solar–grid systems from reactive, threshold-based switching into intelligent, data-driven energy management. It builds on an existing ESP32-based automatic solar–grid changeover prototype developed through engineering innovation at Rift Valley National Polytechnic (RVNP), Kenya. How the solution works The system integrates solar photovoltaic generation, battery storage, grid electricity and industrial loads through an intelligent monitoring and control architecture. An ESP32 microcontroller interfaces with electrical sensors to continuously collect data on solar voltage and current, battery voltage, grid voltage and electricity consumption. The collected data are transmitted to a digital monitoring platform for real-time monitoring, storage and analysis. The existing automatic changeover mechanism selects between solar and grid power according to predefined electrical operating conditions and battery thresholds, prioritising solar energy whenever suitable and switching to grid supply when solar or battery conditions are inadequate. The proposed AI enhancement will introduce predictive intelligence into this process. Machine-learning models will analyse historical and real-time operating data to forecast solar energy availability, electricity demand and battery operating conditions. These predictions will support more informed decisions on energy-source selection and utilisation, helping industrial facilities minimise avoidable grid consumption, improve battery management and maintain reliable electricity supply. The system will retain conventional electrical protection, interlocking and safety controls independent of AI predictions to ensure safe switching and equipment protection. Methodologies and technologies Development will follow an iterative engineering and applied research methodology involving: 1. Hardware integration: ESP32 microcontroller, ACS712 current sensor, ZMPT101B AC voltage sensor, battery voltage monitoring circuits and automatic relay or contactor-based changeover. 2. IoT monitoring: Continuous acquisition and transmission of solar, battery, grid and load data. 3. Data analytics: Collection, cleaning, processing and analysis of energy-performance datasets. 4. AI model development: Python and Scikit-learn will be used to develop and evaluate machine-learning models, initially considering Random Forest for solar availability and electricity-demand forecasting. 5. Model validation: Evaluation of prediction accuracy using actual operational data before integration into the energy management process. 6. System integration and testing: Integration of predictive outputs with the existing monitoring and control architecture, followed by controlled testing and industrial pilot evaluation. The main technologies include Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), Internet of Things (IoT), embedded systems, electrical sensors, renewable-energy systems, cloud-based data management and digital monitoring dashboards. Partnerships and collaboration model Rift Valley National Polytechnic (RVNP) will provide institutional coordination, electrical and electronic engineering expertise, technical facilities, innovation support and a platform for prototype development and testing. The project will seek strategic technical collaboration with Kenya Power and Lighting Company PLC to support grid integration, power-system expertise and technical validation; Geothermal Development Company to explore renewable-energy integration and energy optimisation opportunities; and Menengai-based industries as potential industrial demonstration and pilot sites. Further collaboration will be pursued with renewable-energy companies, solar technology providers, AI specialists and IoT developers to support system development, data analytics, deployment, maintenance and commercialisation. Title: CashAid: Accessible AI-Assisted Financial Tools
Subtitle: An early Ghanaian prototype combining accessible navigation, financial information and camera-based banknote identification to support independent participation in the digital economy.
Problem Statement: Inaccessible financial interfaces can limit independent economic participation by persons with disabilities, especially visually impaired users. Identifying banknotes, finding nearby ATMs with precise directions and accessing relevant financial information are practical barriers. CashAid addresses these everyday access needs. Its industrial relevance is indirect: inclusive financial access may help people participate as workers, consumers or entrepreneurs. It is not a manufacturing or industrial automation system.
Solution Overview: CashAid is an early web prototype built with Base44 no-code tools and existing AI/data services. It combines accessible navigation, ATM-location/accessibility functions, jurisdiction-relevant current/daily financial information, currency conversion and a camera-based AI Money Identifier. We do not claim to own an AI model, operate payments or have bank integrations. About 67 respondents reached through Ghana Blind Union WhatsApp and 21 through BHP Telegram provided qualitative feedback, including requests for simple navigation and precise ATM directions. These are community feedback channels, not formal partnerships or measured adoption. We seek technical and accessibility partners for structured testing and reliability improvements.
Solution Provider(s): No formal implementation partners confirmed. Community feedback was collected through Ghana Blind Union WhatsApp and BHP Telegram channels; this does not imply institutional endorsement.
Implementation location(s): N/A — early prototype developed in Accra, Ghana; no formal industrial implementation.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Not yet established. Pilot timing requires technical reliability checks, accessibility testing, local data validation and an agreed partner; no deployment timeline is promised.
Desired impact: The objective is to make everyday financial information and navigation more independently usable by persons with disabilities. The evidence so far is qualitative feedback from about 88 community respondents; it is not evidence of sustained usage or quantified economic impact. Future testing should measure successful banknote-identification tasks, reliable financial-information access and navigation usability. No job creation, emissions reduction, industrial productivity gains or financial savings are claimed.
Key technologies: Base44 no-code web application development; integration of existing AI/data services for financial information and camera-based banknote identification; location/navigation functionality and currency conversion. Title: CalmCar–Tripy ConnectOne Robotaxi for Sustainable Shared Mobility
Subtitle: A phased China–UK–Türkiye collaboration combining L4 autonomous driving, cost-efficient computing and local mobility expertise to advance scalable shared mobility.
Problem Statement: Deploying autonomous shared-mobility services across borders requires more than supplying vehicles. High system costs, differences in local road conditions, testing requirements and operating permits can delay adoption. Technology providers and mobility operators must coordinate vehicle integration, safety validation, localisation and ongoing technical support. Successful deployment also depends on effective fleet management, remote operations, customer service and a commercially viable local service model. The CalmCar–Tripy project addresses these challenges through a phased deployment approach designed to support the introduction of L4 Robotaxi services in overseas markets.
Solution Overview: CalmCar plans to supply ConnectOne vehicles based on the SAIC MAXUS MIFA 7 platform, together with automotive computing hardware, autonomous-driving technology and lifecycle technical support. The July 2026 public disclosure identifies hardware from NVIDIA and Horizon Robotics; the final deployment configuration remains subject to technical confirmation. ConnectOne combines L4 driving capabilities with a dual-computing architecture that incorporates redundancy. Its end-to-end driving system is designed to support operation in complex road scenarios. The delivery model brings together vehicle and software integration, local adaptation, testing and ongoing technical support. The proposed solution also incorporates multi-sensor fusion, high-definition mapping, AI-based decision-making and a multi-layered safety architecture. Under the cooperation agreement, CalmCar is responsible for the vehicle-based Robotaxi product, the autonomous-driving technology solution and lifecycle technical support. Tripy's planned responsibilities include technical adaptation and localisation in Türkiye; road-test planning and operational management; fleet-management infrastructure; remote-operations systems, call-centre systems and fleet-control systems; Robotaxi fleet leasing and mobility-service models for corporate customers; and commercial development with public institutions, private-sector organisations and international partners. Tripy also plans to develop operations in selected markets outside Türkiye. These activities form part of the agreed project scope, with commercial operations planned for a later phase. The planned sequence is demonstration and investor presentations in China, licensing and testing in the United Kingdom, followed by closed-site testing and public-road operations in Türkiye. Tripy has established a company in the UK and is pursuing the necessary permits. Public disclosures indicate that preparations and permit applications for Robotaxi operations in London are ongoing. In Türkiye, road testing and commercial preparations remain subject to applicable regulations and the necessary permits. Progression between stages will depend on project readiness and local regulatory approvals.

Its project role includes technical adaptation and localisation, road-test operations, fleet-management and remote-operations systems, and commercial market development. CalmCar is the submitting organisation and technology provider. Developed in collaboration with a local mobility operator, the project combines fleet leasing with mobility services, enabling more efficient vehicle utilisation and reducing reliance on private car ownership. This approach supports the development of local autonomous-mobility operations while providing a scalable pathway for electric shared transport. Cost efficiency is a key advantage of the solution. Title: TUDOK – Evidence Integrity and Human Oversight for Industrial AI
Subtitle: An experimental, model-agnostic AI output evaluation method supporting evidence traceability, uncertainty assessment and human review in industrial decision-making.
Problem Statement: Artificial intelligence is increasingly used to support industrial decision-making, including manufacturing, quality management, maintenance, infrastructure operations and resource planning. However, AI-generated recommendations can appear coherent, technically plausible and persuasive while containing unsupported claims, inconsistent reasoning, misleading framing or insufficiently communicated uncertainty. This creates a significant challenge for organizations seeking to use AI responsibly. Traditional evaluation approaches may focus on factual accuracy, model performance or regulatory requirements without consistently examining the relationship between claims, available evidence, uncertainty and the need for human intervention. In industrial environments, overreliance on insufficiently verified AI outputs can contribute to operational errors, resource inefficiency, inappropriate risk assessments and reduced accountability. These challenges are particularly relevant to organizations with limited access to independent AI evaluation expertise. The central problem addressed by TUDOK is how to identify and document potential weaknesses in AI-generated decision-support outputs before they influence consequential human or operational decisions. There is a need for transparent, reproducible and model-agnostic evaluation methods that support evidence integrity, meaningful human oversight and risk-aware escalation without replacing expert judgment.
Solution Overview: TUDOK is an experimental, model-agnostic AI-output evaluation methodology developed within the GRM808 Ethical Intelligence research framework. It aims to improve evidence integrity, transparency and human oversight in industrial AI-assisted decision-making. How it works TUDOK introduces a structured evaluation layer between AI-generated recommendations and consequential decisions. It assesses outputs using four dimensions: - C – Coherence: Logical and conceptual clarity. - K – Consistency: Contradictions and internal inconsistencies. - I – Contextual Truth-Alignment: Alignment with available evidence, context and uncertainty. - D – Distortion Pressure: Misleading framing, unsupported confidence and omissions. The proposed workflow identifies claims, evaluates evidence and uncertainty, records potential weaknesses and flags outputs requiring expert verification or human review. Methodologies and technologies The approach combines structured evaluation rubrics, claim-level evidence mapping, uncertainty assessment, machine-readable assessment records and human-in-the-loop principles. Internal exploratory tests have been documented. AI-assisted automation and industrial integration remain development objectives. Partnerships and collaboration GRM808–TRUST seeks universities, AI researchers, industrial technology developers and manufacturing partners for independent validation, cross-model benchmarking and controlled industrial pilot studies. Partners may contribute evaluation protocols, technical expertise, industrial use cases and independent assessment. Development status TUDOK is in the research and pre-validation phase. Industrial performance improvements and independent scientific validation have not yet been demonstrated. Positive, negative and inconclusive test results are equally valuable. TUDOK is not an objective truth detector or regulatory certification system. Research references https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21320434 https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20382213 https://github.com/grm808-cos/tudok-operator
Solution Provider(s): GRM808–TRUST is the submitting research and intellectual property management initiative. No external implementation partners are formally committed at this stage. We are seeking universities, independent AI researchers, industrial technology developers and manufacturing organizations for joint prototyping, benchmarking and independent validation.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Estimated 6–12 months for a controlled research and technical pilot, subject to partner availability, access to suitable test cases, prototype development, data protection requirements and independent evaluation. This is a preliminary planning estimate, not a confirmed deployment schedule.
Desired impact: The primary objective of TUDOK is to improve the reliability, transparency and human oversight of AI-assisted industrial decision-making through structured evaluation of evidence integrity, consistency, uncertainty and misleading framing. The solution aims to identify potentially unreliable AI-generated recommendations before they influence operational decisions, supporting safer adoption of AI in manufacturing, infrastructure management and industrial services. A preliminary 20-prompt, single-model, single-evaluator demonstration has documented the application of the methodology. This is not independent scientific validation or proof of industrial impact. Expected benefits include improved auditability, earlier identification of unsupported claims, more effective human review and reduced reliance on misleading AI outputs. Future pilots will measure evaluation reliability, agreement between independent evaluators, detection performance and practical decision-support value. No verified reductions in emissions, energy consumption or operational costs are claimed at this stage.
Key technologies: TUDOK combines AI-output analysis, structured evaluation methodologies and human-in-the-loop governance. Its current methodological components include: - Large Language Models (LLMs) as evaluation subjects and sources of test outputs. - Model-agnostic C/K/I/D scoring for coherence, consistency, contextual truth-alignment and distortion pressure. - Claim-level analysis, evidence mapping and uncertainty assessment. - Machine-readable JSON reporting schemas, structured datasets and evaluation templates. - Documented evaluation protocols, diagnostic flags and human-review procedures. Future development may incorporate AI-assisted claim extraction, automated evaluation workflows, API integration and industrial decision-support interfaces. The current public implementation primarily consists of research protocols, assessment schemas and preliminary demonstration materials. It is not yet a production-ready industrial AI platform.
Unique Characteristics: TUDOK proposes a distinctive evaluation approach focused on the integrity of AI-generated information before it influences consequential decisions. Rather than assessing only factual accuracy, linguistic quality or model performance, it combines four dimensions: coherence, consistency, contextual truth-alignment and distortion pressure. A key research hypothesis is that apparently persuasive AI outputs may still contain weaknesses in evidence handling, uncertainty communication or misleading framing. The methodology is model-agnostic and designed for structured evaluation without access to proprietary model weights or internal architecture. Its proposed value lies in combining evidence assessment, explicit uncertainty reporting, auditable evaluation records and human escalation within one review-oriented workflow. Publicly available research protocols and evaluation templates support independent examination and reproducibility. The claimed differentiation remains a research hypothesis requiring comparative benchmarking against existing AI evaluation approaches.
Sustainable Change: TUDOK has the potential to support a broader transition from AI adoption based primarily on functionality and performance toward AI-assisted decision-making that also requires evidence integrity, transparency and accountable human oversight. If independently validated, its model-agnostic methodology could be adapted across manufacturing, industrial services, infrastructure management and public-interest decision-support systems. Its proposed modular approach may enable organizations, including SMEs, to introduce structured AI-output review procedures without replacing their existing AI models or operational infrastructure. Open research materials could support replication, comparative testing, academic cooperation and the development of shared evaluation practices. Longer-term opportunities include integration into industrial AI assurance workflows, professional training and cross-border technology cooperation. Systemic impact will depend on independent validation, demonstrated operational value, practical integration feasibility and responsible adoption by participating organizations.
Funding Sources: TUDOK has been developed through founder-led research and development within the GRM808–TRUST research portfolio. No externally funded industrial implementation or confirmed deployment financing is reported at this stage. We are seeking research institutions, industrial partners and potential funding partners to support independent validation, prototype development and controlled pilot studies.
Testimonials and Endorsements: No formal institutional endorsements or independently verified beneficiary testimonials are available at this stage. The TUDOK methodology has been shared for professional discussion and scientific review. However, research interest, correspondence and feedback are not presented as institutional endorsement or proof of successful implementation. Independent evaluation and documented stakeholder feedback are objectives of the proposed validation partnerships.
Primary thematic focus area: Industrial Digital Infrastructure and Data Ecosystems

Title: Continuous Industrial AI Governance, Lifecycle Tracking & ROI Optimization
Subtitle: Automating global compliance mapping, asset inventorying, and spend telemetry to ensure resource-efficient, accountable, and sustainable industrial AI deployment.
Problem Statement: Global industrial enterprises are rapidly scaling Artificial Intelligence across core operations like quality inspection, predictive maintenance, workforce management, and supply-chain logistics. However, they face two critical operational blind spots that they cannot objectively solve with current manual methods: The Compliance Deficit & Non-Tariff Market Barriers: Navigating overlapping international regulations such as the fully active EU AI Act and Gulf Corridor mandates is impossible using manual consulting. This forms a severe barrier that locks small and mid-sized enterprises (SMEs) out of higher-value cross-border supply chains. The Resource & Capital Blind Spot: Executive teams lack a centralized, accurate inventory of the AI tools running across their footprint. They cannot monitor true system compute costs, track token consumption, or detect unmanaged software. Scarce capital is drained into unmonitored AI systems that yield zero measured economic return on investment (ROI).
Solution Overview: AM8 is a web-based SaaS platform that unifies multi-jurisdiction regulatory compliance verification with autonomous AI investment governance. Instead of deploying invasive network scanners, AM8 operates via a secure, non-invasive platform architecture built on a continuous three-stage workflow: 1. Unified Guided Declaration: The organization registers an AI system via a standardized compliance questionnaire. This single intake records what the system does, who it affects, where it is deployed, and where its outputs are used, driving both the compliance and financial tracking engines. 2. Title: AviX: Intelligent Robotics for Resilient Poultry Production
Subtitle: A solar-powered robotic and AI-assisted platform for environmental monitoring, farm records and intelligent decision support in commercial poultry production.
Problem Statement: Poultry producers lose birds, feed and revenue when heat stress and ammonia buildup go undetected or are detected too late. Birds exposed to harmful environmental conditions can experience increased mortality, poorer growth and reduced feed efficiency, meaning more of the farmer’s feed investment is lost without achieving the expected production output. These risks may also vary across different areas of a poultry house, making periodic manual observation insufficient for timely intervention. Farmers need earlier, location-specific visibility into environmental stress so they can act before conditions significantly affect bird survival, feed utilization and overall production performance.
Solution Overview: AviX is an intelligent poultry monitoring and decision-support system designed to help farmers detect and respond to heat and ammonia stress before these conditions contribute to bird mortality, poor feed utilization and production losses. An autonomous robotic unit travels along an overhead track inside the poultry house, carrying environmental sensors that collect temperature, humidity and ammonia readings across different zones. This allows AviX to identify not only that a harmful condition exists, but also the specific location where intervention is needed. The software connects these readings with digital farm records and poultry-management SOPs to provide location-specific alerts and recommended actions. Farmers can also record daily farm activities through a voice-enabled interface currently being developed for English, Nigerian Pidgin and Yoruba. The AI layer is in Early R&D and is being developed to retrieve relevant historical farm records, combine previous events with current sensor conditions, and support increasingly contextual recommendations. Data generated through future pilots and continued usage will support development of predictive models for earlier risk detection. AviX combines robotics, IoT environmental sensing, embedded systems, solar-supported power, farm-management software, multilingual NLP, historical-data retrieval and AI-assisted decision support. AviX has received early-stage support from FEMBOL Group and has held exploratory discussions with Taro Agric and MAED Agrolinks regarding future validation and testing. These relationships are not yet formal pilot partnerships.
Solution Provider(s): No formal implementation partners at present. AviX has received early-stage grant and business-registration support from FEMOL Group and has held exploratory validation discussions with Taro Agric and MAED Agrolinks regarding potential future testing and collaboration.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3–4 months total for a full pilot cycle (48 hours on-site installation). We require 6–8 weeks to finalize our commercial MVP build, coordinate with a local farm partner, and ship the compact robot unit (the overhead track uses standard conduit pipe sourced locally). Physical installation and calibration in a 100m barn take just 2 days between flock batches, followed by a 6-to-7-week pilot across one full broiler grow-out cycle to validate mortality and feed-saving results.
Desired impact: AviX’s primary objective is to reduce preventable bird mortality, feed losses and production losses caused by heat and ammonia stress that is detected too late. AviX aims to give poultry farmers continuous, location-specific environmental intelligence so they can identify harmful conditions earlier and intervene before flock performance deteriorates. The expected impact is lower mortality, improved feed conversion and feed efficiency, faster response to environmental risks, and improved production performance. During full broiler-cycle pilots, we will establish farm baselines and measure mortality rate, feed consumed relative to weight gain, frequency and duration of heat/ammonia events, detection-to-intervention time, and production outcomes. AviX’s historical record system will preserve sensor readings, farm activities, interventions and outcomes across production cycles, enabling farmers to compare current performance with previous cycles and enabling AviX to improve future recommendations. Subject to successful validation, our three-year target is approximately 75–100 commercial poultry farms and 250–400 monitored pens. These are scaling targets; quantified mortality and feed-efficiency improvements will be established through field validation rather than claimed in advance.
Key technologies: Robotics and embedded systems: an overhead track-based mobile robotic platform and embedded control architecture. IoT/environmental sensing: sensors for location-specific monitoring of temperature, humidity and ammonia. Solar energy: solar-supported power and docking architecture for resilient operation. Farm software and digital records: dashboards, alerts and longitudinal environmental and production records. Artificial intelligence and NLP: Early-R&D multilingual natural-language processing for English, Nigerian Pidgin and Yoruba voice-based recordkeeping, retrieval of relevant farm history and contextual decision support. Future predictive analytics: models trained on consented pilot and operational data to identify environmental patterns and support earlier risk warnings once sufficient representative data have been collected.
Unique Characteristics: AviX differentiates itself by combining mobile robotics, spatial environmental sensing, historical farm intelligence and AI-assisted decision support in one poultry-production platform. Rather than relying only on fixed monitoring points, the track-based robot is designed to collect environmental readings across multiple zones and associate detected risks with their specific location. AviX goes beyond monitoring by connecting sensor readings with longitudinal farm records and SOP-aligned recommendations. Its voice interface, initially being developed for English, Nigerian Pidgin and Yoruba, is intended to make digital recordkeeping more accessible to farm workers who may find conventional data entry cumbersome. The accumulated farm history creates a growing operational memory, allowing current conditions to be considered alongside previous events, actions and outcomes. Solar-supported operation and lightweight routine monitoring also make the architecture relevant to settings with constrained power infrastructure. Together, these features position AviX as a physical-and-digital intelligence platform rather than simply an IoT sensor, farm-management application or standalone AI assistant.
Sustainable Change: AviX has the potential to shift poultry management from periodic observation and reactive intervention toward continuous, location-aware and increasingly data-driven decision-making. As adoption grows, each production cycle can contribute structured environmental, operational and outcome data, creating a longitudinal evidence base that helps individual farms understand recurring risks while supporting the development of more reliable decision-support and predictive models. The model is designed for replication: standardized robotic hardware and track installation can be paired with a shared software platform, while language, SOPs and recommendations can be localized for different production environments. Following validation in Nigeria, AviX intends to expand through poultry-industry, research, fabrication and distribution partnerships into additional African markets and, later, other poultry-producing regions. At scale, this approach could broaden access to precision-poultry technologies, strengthen operational resilience and create a growing evidence base for better poultry-production decisions in markets where advanced automation has historically been less accessible.

Recently, AviX was selected among the Top 10 finalists in a FEMBOL Group innovation programme and awarded a ₦200,000 grant together with CAC registration support. The grant was awarded only recently and has not yet been disbursed, so it has not funded our development to date.
