Title: AI Quality Assistant: Intelligent Manufacturing Quality and Defect Prevention
Subtitle: An AI-powered manufacturing quality solution that analyzes defects, scrap, and rework, identifies production risks, and provides actionable recommendations to support faster decisions and continuous improvement.
Problem Statement: Manufacturing facilities often struggle to detect quality problems early, identify recurring defects, and analyze scrap and rework data quickly. Delayed analysis can increase production costs, waste materials, and allow quality issues to continue across shifts and production lines. Many teams lack accessible tools to turn production data into timely, actionable decisions.
Solution Overview: AI Quality Assistant is a digital solution designed to support manufacturing quality management through data analysis, risk identification, and actionable recommendations. It uses production data, including total output, defects, scrap, rework, production lines, shifts, and main defect categories, to calculate quality indicators and identify potential problem areas. The prototype applies quality management principles and continuous improvement methodologies to help users monitor defect rates, compare performance across periods, prioritize high-risk production lines or shifts, and investigate recurring quality issues. Its analytical approach supports structured problem-solving and can be extended to methodologies such as 5M/6M root cause analysis, 8D, PFMEA, and statistical process control. The solution is designed to transform routine production records into accessible indicators, risk alerts, and recommendations that help quality and production teams make more timely, evidence-based decisions. Its intended benefits include earlier identification of quality deviations, improved visibility of scrap and rework, and more systematic follow-up of corrective actions. These benefits require further validation in real manufacturing environments. AI Quality Assistant is currently an independently developed prototype. The proposed collaboration model includes working with manufacturers, quality engineers, production teams, industrial technology providers, and academic institutions to validate the methodology, test the solution using real or anonymized production data, improve its analytical capabilities, and measure its impact through pilot projects. Future development may include more advanced AI-assisted diagnostics, predictive quality analytics, and integration with existing manufacturing data systems.
Solution Provider(s): No formal partners at this stage. AI Quality Assistant is an independently developed prototype. Potential future partners include manufacturing companies and industrial plants (manufacturing sector), quality management and continuous improvement professionals (industrial quality sector), and universities or research institutions (education and applied research sectors). These are prospective collaborators, not confirmed partnerships.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3–6 months, subject to access to a manufacturing partner, availability of production data, and successful pilot preparation and validation.
Desired impact: The main objective of AI Quality Assistant is to help manufacturing companies improve product quality, identify production risks earlier, and make more informed decisions using production data. The prototype analyzes output, defects, scrap, rework, production lines, shifts, and main defect categories to calculate quality indicators, highlight potential problem areas, compare performance across periods, and provide actionable recommendations. The expected impact includes reducing defect rates, material waste, and rework; improving production efficiency; supporting more systematic corrective actions; and strengthening data-driven quality management, particularly for small and medium-sized manufacturers. Potential impact will be measured through indicators such as defect rate, scrap rate, rework rate, and the time required to identify and investigate quality problems. Where baseline data is available, pilot testing will compare these indicators before and after implementation. Material waste reductions may also be used to estimate potential environmental benefits. AI Quality Assistant is currently an independently developed prototype and has not yet been validated in a manufacturing plant. Therefore, no verified reductions in defects, waste, costs, greenhouse gas emissions, or job creation can be reported at this stage. These impacts will be assessed through future pilot projects with manufacturing partners.
Key technologies: AI Quality Assistant uses data analytics, automated quality indicators, rule-based risk assessment, and AI-assisted diagnostic logic to support manufacturing quality management. The prototype processes production data, including output, defects, scrap, rework, production lines, shifts, and defect categories, to identify trends, compare performance across periods, highlight potential risks, and generate actionable recommendations. The solution applies digital quality management principles and continuous improvement methodologies. Its analytical framework can support structured root cause investigation and may be extended to methodologies such as 5M/6M analysis, 8D, PFMEA, and statistical process control. The prototype is designed to work with structured production records and is intended to make quality analysis more accessible to manufacturing teams. Advanced machine learning, predictive analytics, IoT integration, and connections to manufacturing execution systems (MES) are potential future enhancements and are not claimed as fully implemented capabilities.
Unique Characteristics: AI Quality Assistant differentiates itself by bringing manufacturing quality indicators, risk identification, period-to-period comparisons, and actionable recommendations together in one accessible digital prototype. Instead of requiring quality teams to interpret multiple reports separately, it organizes production data on defects, scrap, rework, lines, and shifts to help identify priority problems and support faster, evidence-based decisions. Its distinctive approach combines practical quality management principles with automated data analysis and structured diagnostic logic. The solution is designed to be adaptable to different manufacturing processes and accessible to small and medium-sized manufacturers that may have limited resources for advanced industrial analytics. Another differentiating feature is its modular development approach. The prototype can be tested using existing production records, with the potential to expand through collaboration with manufacturers, quality specialists, and research institutions. Future development could incorporate validated predictive analytics and integrations with existing factory systems. AI Quality Assistant is currently an independently developed prototype, not a commercially deployed product. Its innovation and practical value will be further evaluated through pilot projects, using measurable indicators such as defect rates, scrap, rework, and the time required to identify quality problems.
Sustainable Change: AI Quality Assistant has the potential to promote a broader shift toward data-driven quality management in manufacturing, particularly among small and medium-sized enterprises that may lack access to advanced industrial analytics tools. By making production quality indicators, risk identification, and structured recommendations more accessible, the solution could help organizations move from reactive defect correction toward earlier detection, systematic problem-solving, and continuous improvement. If validated through pilot projects, the approach could be replicated across different production lines, shifts, facilities, and manufacturing sectors by adapting its indicators and diagnostic rules to local processes and data requirements. Wider adoption could encourage more consistent quality monitoring, better use of production data, reduced material waste, and stronger collaboration between production teams and quality professionals. The solution could also support knowledge sharing by providing a repeatable framework for evaluating defects, scrap, rework, and corrective actions. Future collaboration with manufacturers, universities, and industrial technology partners could help establish common evaluation methods and improve its adaptability across countries and industrial contexts. Long-term systemic impact will depend on successful real-world validation, usability, data quality, and sustainable implementation. As an independently developed prototype, AI Quality Assistant has not yet demonstrated these broader effects; they are intended outcomes to be assessed through future pilots and scale-up activities.
Funding Sources: Self-funded through independent development, using personal time and available resources. No external funding, grants, or implementation-specific financing have been received to date.
Testimonials and Endorsements: N/A. No formal testimonials or endorsements are available at this stage. AI Quality Assistant is an independently developed prototype that has not yet been validated through industrial pilot projects.
Primary thematic focus area: Industrial AI Models and Intelligent Decision-Making
Summary: AI Quality Assistant turns output, defect and rework data into quality indicators, risk flags and recommendations for small manufacturers. The scope is right; without a plant or a measured result it remains a prototype.
Thematic focus areas (as submitted): Industrial AI Models and Intelligent Decision-Making; Embodied AI, Industrial Robotics and Smart Manufacturing; AI for Green, Resilient and Sustainable Industry

Title: Co-Trainer: AI reinforcement for vocational and workforce skills
Subtitle: A trainer-led AI prototype helping vocational learners revisit approved instructions, ask questions and obtain human help after formal training.
Problem Statement: Vocational and technical training does not end when learners leave the classroom. Many learners struggle to recall procedures, apply newly acquired skills independently, or obtain timely clarification when trainers are unavailable. Printed guides and static learning materials cannot respond to individual questions, while general-purpose AI tools may provide answers that conflict with approved training procedures. Co-Trainer addresses this gap by providing AI-assisted instructional reinforcement grounded in materials supplied and approved by human trainers. It aims to make technical knowledge more accessible, strengthen learning continuity and support workforce skills development, particularly in training environments where individual follow-up support is limited.
Solution Overview: Sirilio Co-Trainer is an AI-powered instructional reinforcement platform designed to extend the support of human trainers beyond formal training sessions. Trainers provide approved instructional materials, which Co-Trainer processes into structured, step-by-step guidance. Learners can revisit procedures, request simpler explanations, ask questions and receive contextual assistance grounded in the original training content. The platform incorporates source verification, guided learning workflows, progress tracking and contextual help-request records accessible through a separate helper dashboard. Shared-guide questions are answered with verified source quotations; unresolved questions can be referred to the human trainer. Its existing prototype uses a Python/Flask backend, PostgreSQL, browser-based interfaces and large language model integration. Co-Trainer follows a human-trainer-first approach: AI reinforces approved instruction rather than independently defining what learners should be taught. Sirilio intends to pilot the solution with a Nigerian vocational or technical training provider, initially supporting a small cohort of trainers and learners. The pilot will evaluate usability, instructional recall, response accuracy and opportunities for wider deployment. The longer-term vision is to make personalised instructional reinforcement more accessible to vocational training institutions, workforce development programmes and employers across Africa.
Solution Provider(s): No formal institutional or implementation partners have been confirmed at this stage. Sirilio is seeking a Nigerian vocational or technical training institution for its first controlled pilot.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Approximately 8–12 weeks, subject to securing a local training partner, adapting approved instructional materials, completing technical readiness checks and onboarding trainers and learners. The first controlled pilot is provisionally targeted for January 2027 in Nigeria.
Desired impact: Our objective is to extend human trainers' support beyond classroom instruction and help learners recall and apply approved vocational and technical guidance. Co-Trainer aims to improve access to instructional clarification, encourage independent learning and help trainers identify learners requiring additional human support. The first controlled pilot is provisionally targeted for January 2027, subject to securing a Nigerian vocational training partner and completing technical readiness checks. The proposed pilot will involve approximately 2–3 trainers and 15–25 learners. Evaluation will examine learner engagement, instructional recall, response relevance, usability, trainer feedback and opportunities for wider adoption. These are intended outcomes that will be evaluated during the pilot, not benefits already demonstrated.
Key technologies: Co-Trainer is built using a Python/Flask backend, JavaScript/HTML/CSS browser interfaces and PostgreSQL for structured instructional content, learner interactions and progress records. The platform incorporates large language model integration for contextual explanations and assistance constrained by trainer-approved learning materials. Shared-guide Q&A displays verified source quotations. Document-processing capabilities support PDF and DOCX content extraction, alongside pasted text and TXT/MD intake. Source verification helps maintain alignment between AI responses and the original training material. Additional capabilities include structured learning workflows, learner progress tracking and prototype speech-recognition functionality. English is currently supported; wider localisation remains a development priority.
Unique Characteristics: Co-Trainer's innovation lies in transforming trainer-approved instructional content into an interactive, personalised learning support experience without replacing the human trainer. Unlike general-purpose AI assistants that generate responses from broad knowledge, Co-Trainer is designed to reinforce the specific procedures and materials learners have actually been taught. Its differentiating features include source-grounded explanations, reusable instructional guides, step-by-step learning support, learner progress tracking and contextual help-request records available to a human helper through a separate dashboard. These records support human follow-up rather than constituting an automated trainer notification and response service. This approach combines the scalability of AI with the contextual knowledge and oversight of human trainers. For vocational training providers and employers, Co-Trainer offers a potential way to extend instructional support beyond scheduled sessions without requiring trainers to be continuously available. Its initial focus on African vocational and workforce development environments creates opportunities for future localisation, multilingual support and deployment across different technical skills programmes.
Sustainable Change: Co-Trainer has the potential to change how vocational and workforce training institutions provide ongoing instructional support. By transforming approved training materials into interactive AI-assisted learning resources, institutions could provide more consistent follow-up guidance across multiple learner cohorts, while allowing human trainers to focus on practical instruction and complex learner needs. For smaller vocational training providers and employers, this approach could improve access to personalised learning support without requiring proportional increases in trainer availability. Following validation through an initial Nigerian pilot, Sirilio intends to explore partnerships with vocational institutions, workforce development organisations and employers to assess opportunities for wider adoption. Longer-term development priorities include multilingual support, accessibility improvements and adaptation to different technical training environments. Title: Akro TerraSense: AI-Powered Agricultural Intelligence for Sustainable Farming
Subtitle: An integrated AI-enabled platform combining satellite intelligence, climate monitoring and digital farm management to improve agricultural productivity, strengthen resilience and support sustainable land use.
Problem Statement: Agriculture across Africa faces persistent challenges that undermine productivity, climate resilience and sustainable growth. Farmers frequently lack access to reliable, location-specific information on soil conditions, crop suitability, environmental risks and changing weather patterns. Many continue to make critical production decisions using fragmented information, traditional practices and limited access to digital advisory services. At the same time, agricultural businesses, development organisations and public institutions face difficulties accessing integrated, reliable data on farmland, agricultural activities and environmental conditions. This limits their ability to monitor production, anticipate climate-related disruptions, allocate resources effectively and develop evidence-based agricultural policies. Existing agricultural technologies often address these challenges separately, requiring users to rely on multiple disconnected systems for farm management, land information, environmental monitoring and agricultural intelligence. This fragmentation creates inefficiencies, increases operational costs and limits the practical use of data in agricultural decision-making. These challenges are particularly significant for smallholder farmers, who are disproportionately exposed to climate variability, limited technical support and resource constraints. There is therefore a need for an accessible, integrated agricultural intelligence solution that transforms complex environmental, geospatial and farm-level data into practical insights, enabling farmers and agricultural stakeholders to make better-informed decisions, reduce avoidable losses and transition towards more sustainable and resilient agricultural practices.
Solution Overview: Akro TerraSense is an AI-enabled agricultural intelligence platform developed by AkroSystems to address the fragmentation of agricultural information and improve decision-making across agricultural production systems. The solution integrates geospatial intelligence, satellite-derived environmental data, digital farm records and analytical capabilities into a single platform that supports farmers, agribusinesses and agricultural institutions. How the solution works Akro TerraSense operates through five interconnected modules: Farm Intelligence: Consolidates agricultural and environmental information to provide farm-level insights that support crop planning, assessment of growing conditions and informed production decisions. Farm Manager: Provides digital tools for registering farms, managing plots, recording agricultural activities, tracking resources and organising production information. This supports operational efficiency and improved farm management. Disaster Alert: Uses satellite-derived and environmental monitoring information to identify potential agricultural hazards, particularly fire-related risks, and support early awareness of threats to farms and agricultural assets. Land Register: Enables the digital organisation and management of agricultural land information, including location-based records that improve visibility and support land-use planning. National Agricultural Atlas: Provides an interactive geospatial interface for exploring agricultural information across geographical areas, supporting regional analysis, resource planning and institutional decision-making. The platform combines Geographic Information Systems (GIS), satellite-derived observations, environmental datasets, structured agricultural records and AI-enabled analytical approaches. Its modular architecture allows agricultural and geospatial information to be organised, visualised and interpreted through accessible digital interfaces. TerraSense's development approach focuses on integrating fragmented datasets, improving the accessibility of agricultural intelligence and progressively strengthening analytical capabilities through field validation and user feedback. Further development priorities include location-specific crop recommendations, expanded climate-risk intelligence and the integration of additional agricultural datasets. TerraSense supports the digital transformation of agricultural production by enabling more informed resource allocation, improved farm planning, environmental risk awareness and responsible land management. It is designed to strengthen the information infrastructure available to agricultural enterprises, farmers and institutions, contributing to more efficient and climate-resilient agricultural value chains. AkroSystems is pursuing a collaborative implementation model involving agricultural enterprises, research institutions, technical specialists and potential data partners. The company is engaging AJA Climate Solutions regarding pilot validation in agricultural environments, with the objective of assessing practical functionality, gathering user feedback and refining the platform. Future institutional engagement will focus on agricultural research, meteorological information, technical validation and access to relevant datasets, subject to appropriate partnership and data-sharing arrangements. Akro TerraSense is currently at Technology Readiness Level 6 (TRL6), with a functional and demonstrable application. Its next phase focuses on structured field validation, technical refinement and evidence generation to support wider adoption and commercial readiness.
Solution Provider(s): Akro TerraSense is currently independently developed by AkroSystems and has no formal external partners at this stage. We are actively exploring strategic collaborations with agricultural research institutions, climate technology organisations, agribusinesses and relevant government agencies to support pilot implementation, technical validation, data integration and future market adoption.
Implementation location(s): N/A – Akro TerraSense is currently at the MVP/pilot-ready stage and has not yet been implemented in an external operational environment.
Implementation timeline(s): N/A – External pilot implementation has not yet commenced.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Approximately 3–4 months, subject to local data availability, stakeholder engagement and pilot-site readiness. This period would cover initial needs assessment, adaptation of relevant agricultural and environmental datasets, platform configuration, user onboarding and training, followed by initial field testing and performance monitoring. The existing functional platform provides a foundation for deployment without requiring development from scratch.
Desired impact: Akro TerraSense aims to accelerate the digital transformation of African agriculture by making reliable, location-specific agricultural intelligence accessible to farmers, agribusinesses and institutions. Its primary objective is to improve agricultural decision-making, resource efficiency, climate resilience and sustainable land management through an integrated AI-enabled platform. The solution has five principal objectives: 1. Improve agricultural productivity: Equip farmers with farm-level environmental intelligence and digital management tools to support better crop planning, resource allocation and production decisions. 2. Strengthen climate resilience: Improve access to environmental monitoring and agricultural hazard information, enabling earlier identification of potential threats and more informed risk management. 3. Promote efficient resource utilisation: Support the tracking and management of agricultural inputs, activities and resources to reduce operational inefficiencies and encourage more sustainable farming practices. 4. Advance agricultural digitalisation: Replace fragmented and largely manual agricultural recordkeeping with integrated digital systems that improve information accessibility, transparency and operational planning. 5. Support evidence-based agricultural development: Provide agribusinesses, researchers and public institutions with geospatial agricultural information to strengthen planning, investment decisions and agricultural development initiatives. Akro TerraSense is expected to contribute to improved farm management, reduced information gaps, better agricultural risk awareness, more efficient resource utilisation and greater access to digital agricultural services. At the institutional level, the platform could strengthen agricultural data availability, support more targeted interventions and improve the ability of stakeholders to identify agricultural opportunities and vulnerabilities. Over time, these improvements could contribute to higher agricultural productivity, reduced avoidable losses, improved livelihoods and more climate-resilient agricultural value chains. As the solution progresses into field validation, AkroSystems intends to assess its performance through measurable indicators, including: - Number of farmers and agricultural enterprises onboarded. - Number of farms and agricultural plots digitally registered. - Changes in the time required for farm recordkeeping and management. - User adoption and frequency of platform utilisation. - Number of environmental risks identified and communicated. - Changes in agricultural input utilisation and operational efficiency. - User-reported improvements in decision-making. - Changes in crop productivity and avoidable losses, where reliable baseline and follow-up data are available. Akro TerraSense is currently at the MVP/pilot-ready stage (TRL6). Consequently, verified impact figures relating to increased yields, greenhouse gas emissions reductions, resource savings or jobs created are not yet available. These outcomes will be assessed through structured pilot implementation and subsequent monitoring. The immediate objective is to establish a credible evidence base demonstrating the platform's technical performance, usability and potential agricultural value before scaling.

Artificial Intelligence and Data Analytics: AI-enabled analytical approaches support the interpretation of agricultural and environmental information, with ongoing development focused on strengthening location-specific recommendations and predictive decision support. 2. Geographic Information Systems (GIS): Geospatial technologies enable the mapping, visualisation and spatial analysis of farms, agricultural land and environmental conditions. These capabilities underpin the Land Register, Farm Intelligence and National Agricultural Atlas modules. 3. Satellite and Remote Sensing Data: Satellite-derived environmental information supports the monitoring of agricultural landscapes and relevant environmental risks, including fire-related hazards. This provides an additional information source for agricultural planning and risk awareness. 4. Cloud-Based Digital Infrastructure: The platform uses a modular digital architecture to support the integration, management and presentation of agricultural information through accessible web-based interfaces. 5. Agricultural Data Management: Structured digital records enable the registration of farms, organisation of agricultural plots, tracking of farm activities and management of relevant production information. 6. Environmental Monitoring and Geospatial Visualisation: The combination of environmental datasets and interactive mapping tools supports the identification, interpretation and communication of location-specific agricultural conditions.
Unique Characteristics: Akro TerraSense's principal innovation lies in its integrated approach to agricultural intelligence. Rather than addressing farm management, environmental monitoring, land information and agricultural mapping as separate functions, the platform brings these capabilities together within a unified digital environment. 1. Five interconnected agricultural intelligence modules: TerraSense combines Farm Intelligence, Farm Manager, Disaster Alert, Land Register and National Agricultural Atlas. This enables the platform to address both day-to-day farm management needs and broader agricultural information requirements through a common digital solution. 2. Integration of geospatial and operational agricultural data: The platform connects location-based agricultural information with digital farm records, enabling users to consider agricultural activities in relation to their geographical and environmental context. This creates opportunities for more informed farm planning, land management and resource allocation. 3. Agricultural intelligence across multiple decision-making levels: TerraSense is designed to serve individual farmers, agribusinesses and institutions. While farmers can use the platform to organise operations and access relevant information, agricultural organisations and institutions can use aggregated and appropriately governed data to support broader planning and analysis. 4. Environmental risk intelligence integrated with farm management: The Disaster Alert module introduces environmental hazard awareness into the agricultural management environment, allowing users to consider potential risks alongside operational farm information. 5. Modular and adaptable architecture: The platform's modular structure enables individual capabilities to be refined and expanded without requiring the entire solution to be redesigned. This supports progressive integration of new agricultural datasets, analytical models and services. 6. Designed around African agricultural information needs: TerraSense is being developed with the realities of African agricultural systems in mind, including fragmented information, limited access to location-specific intelligence, climate-related vulnerabilities and the need for practical digital tools. 7. Potential for collaborative deployment: The platform is intended to support different deployment arrangements, including direct access by agricultural enterprises and collaboration with research institutions, development organisations and agricultural service providers.
Sustainable Change: 1. Transition towards data-driven agricultural systems: By making digital farm records, geospatial intelligence and environmental information more accessible, TerraSense could support a gradual shift from fragmented, reactive decision-making towards more informed and proactive agricultural management. As adoption increases, farmers and agricultural enterprises could develop stronger capabilities to use data in planning, monitoring and resource allocation. 2. Strengthening agricultural information infrastructure: Through its National Agricultural Atlas and Land Register modules, TerraSense could contribute to improved organisation and accessibility of agricultural information. Subject to appropriate data governance, privacy safeguards and institutional collaboration, aggregated information could support agricultural research, investment planning, development programming and evidence-based public policy. 3. Building more climate-resilient agricultural value chains: By integrating environmental monitoring and agricultural risk intelligence into farm management processes, TerraSense could strengthen the capacity of agricultural stakeholders to identify vulnerabilities, anticipate certain environmental threats and respond more effectively. At scale, these capabilities could support greater resilience across agricultural production systems and associated value chains. 4. Replication across agricultural contexts: TerraSense's modular architecture creates opportunities to adapt the platform to different crops, farming systems, geographical areas and institutional requirements. Following successful pilot validation in Ghana, the solution could be progressively adapted for deployment in other African markets through partnerships with agricultural organisations, research institutions and local technology stakeholders. 5. Supporting an inclusive agricultural innovation ecosystem: TerraSense could create opportunities for collaboration among farmers, agribusinesses, agricultural researchers, technology developers, climate service providers and public institutions. Such collaboration could support the development of locally relevant agricultural datasets, improved digital services and new approaches to delivering agricultural intelligence. 6. Long-term sustainability and scale: The intended commercial model is based on providing digital agricultural intelligence and management services to different categories of users and institutional customers. Potential subscription-based and institutional service arrangements could support the platform's continued development and maintenance, subject to commercial validation. The wider systemic opportunity is to make agricultural intelligence a more accessible and routinely used component of agricultural production, business management and institutional planning.
Funding Sources: Akro TerraSense has been developed through internal resources and investment by AkroSystems. Development to date has focused on building the core platform and its five interconnected modules. The solution has not yet received external grant funding or institutional investment specifically for its implementation. AkroSystems is exploring funding and strategic partnership opportunities to support field validation, product refinement and future commercial deployment.
Testimonials and Endorsements: Akro TerraSense is currently at the MVP/pilot-ready stage. Formal beneficiary testimonials and independent institutional endorsements are not yet available. AkroSystems intends to collect structured user feedback, testimonials and evidence of performance during its planned field validation activities.

Title: IndustryForward AI: From Readiness to Transformation
Subtitle: Edit An AI-enabled industrial transformation solution leveraging globally proven readiness frameworks to accelerate AI adoption, operational excellence, sustainability, and industrial competitiveness.
Problem Statement: Industrial enterprises, particularly micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) in developing economies, face persistent barriers to adopting artificial intelligence (AI), Industry 4.0 technologies, and sustainable manufacturing practices. These include limited technological and organizational readiness, skills shortages, fragmented industrial data, constrained access to finance, and difficulties translating modernization ambitions into actionable investment decisions. Although internationally established industrial assessment frameworks, such as those developed by the International Centre for Industrial Transformation (INCIT), have been successfully deployed across several countries, including Saudi Arabia, significant gaps remain in their accessibility, coordinated application, and translation into practical transformation programmes, particularly among resource-constrained manufacturers. Industrial modernization initiatives frequently address operational excellence, digitalization, AI readiness, and environmental sustainability independently. This fragmented approach limits synergies, complicates investment prioritization, and prevents enterprises from developing integrated transformation roadmaps with measurable economic and environmental outcomes. At the ecosystem level, policymakers, industry associations, and development institutions often lack consolidated, standardized, and internationally benchmarked industrial intelligence to identify structural weaknesses, prioritize interventions, mobilize resources, and monitor industrial transformation progress. IndustryForward AI addresses the critical gap between industrial readiness and actual transformation. It aims to make internationally proven assessment methodologies and AI-enabled decision intelligence more accessible, connecting enterprise diagnostics with investment prioritization, capacity development, technology adoption, and measurable performance improvements. By linking enterprise-level transformation with ecosystem-level intelligence, the solution seeks to accelerate inclusive, competitive, resilient, and sustainable industrial development, initially in Lebanon and subsequently across other developing economies.
Solution Overview: IndustryForward AI: From Readiness to Transformation is a proposed AI-enabled industrial transformation model helping manufacturers, especially MSMEs, turn assessments into investments and measurable improvements. Its initial implementation is envisaged in Lebanon, with potential for international replication. HOW THE SOLUTION WORKS 1. Assess industrial readiness. Participating factories undergo assessments using four frameworks from the International Centre for Industrial Transformation (INCIT): the Smart Industry Readiness Index (SIRI) for Industry 4.0; the Consumer Sustainability Industry Readiness Index (COSIRI) for sustainability; the Artificial Intelligence Maturity Readiness Index (AIMRI) for AI readiness; and the Operational Excellence Readiness Index (OPERI) for productivity and operational capabilities. Their use requires INCIT authorization and qualified assessors. 2. Generate industrial intelligence. Assessment findings would be consolidated, benchmarked and analyzed to identify capability gaps, interdependencies and improvement opportunities. Subject to INCIT agreement, the programme would explore its CivicHorizon industrial intelligence platform and existing AI-supported capabilities. Proposed additional analytics could rank interventions by impact, feasibility, cost and sustainability. Experts would validate recommendations. 3. Translate findings into action. Each manufacturer would receive a sequenced transformation roadmap covering relevant priorities such as production efficiency, quality, digital connectivity, responsible AI use cases, resource efficiency, workforce skills and financing requirements. Business cases and milestones would guide investment. 4. Support execution and measure results. The programme would connect participating firms with technical assistance, training, technology providers and potential financiers. Baselines and follow-up indicators—such as productivity, downtime, AI uptake, energy intensity and implementation progress—would track results. With safeguards, aggregated findings could inform industrial policy. METHODOLOGIES, TECHNOLOGY AND EVIDENCE The approach combines standardized INCIT diagnostics, international benchmarking, AI-assisted decision support, expert validation, implementation planning and results monitoring. It would apply confidentiality, data governance and responsible AI safeguards. It does not claim ownership of INCIT frameworks or existing platforms. The proposed model draws on proven components: Saudi Arabia adopted SIRI through its National Industrial Development and Logistics Program; SIRI has been used by manufacturers in Singapore and Indonesia; an AIMRI industrial assessment was conducted in Türkiye; and COSIRI has been applied in Azerbaijan. These cases demonstrate the use of underlying frameworks—not deployment of IndustryForward AI or of all four indices together. The integrated Lebanese model remains untested. PARTNERSHIPS AND COLLABORATION Transformeus SARL proposes to coordinate programme design, enterprise support, transformation planning and performance monitoring. The Lebanese Private Sector Network (LPSN) would be invited to mobilize cross-sector private-sector engagement; the Association of Lebanese Industrialists (ALI) to engage factories and validate sector priorities; and Lebanon's Ministry of Industry to explore policy alignment and use of aggregated insights. INCIT would be approached as prospective methodology and technology partner for authorized assessments, assessor development, benchmarking and possible CivicHorizon access. All partnerships remain prospective. Starting with a Lebanese pilot, IndustryForward AI seeks to establish a replicable public–private pathway from industrial diagnosis to responsible technology adoption, investment and measurable industrial transformation.
Solution Provider(s): Transformeus SAL (Lebanon) – Management consultancy specializing in industrial transformation, AI adoption, digitalization, operational excellence, sustainability, MSME development, and capacity building; proposed programme coordinator and technical implementation lead, Lebanese Private Sector Network (LPSN) – Cross-sector private-sector network promoting economic development, investment, innovation, competitiveness, and job creation; prospective strategic partner for private-sector mobilization and ecosystem coordination, Association of Lebanese Industrialists (ALI) – National industrial association representing Lebanese manufacturing enterprises and promoting industrial competitiveness, modernization, innovation, and policy advocacy; prospective industrial sector and enterprise engagement partner, Ministry of Industry, Republic of Lebanon – Government institution responsible for industrial policy, manufacturing sector development, modernization, and competitiveness; prospective national institutional and policy alignment partner, International Centre for Industrial Transformation (INCIT), Singapore – International nonprofit organization developing globally recognized industrial readiness frameworks, benchmarking methodologies, and industrial intelligence solutions, including SIRI, COSIRI, AIMRI, OPERI, and CivicHorizon; prospective international technical and technology partner.
Implementation location(s): The underlying INCIT industrial transformation methodologies have been applied internationally, including in Saudi Arabia (national SIRI adoption programme), Singapore and Indonesia (SIRI industrial assessments), Türkiye (SIRI, COSIRI and AIMRI assessments, including Viessmann), Azerbaijan (COSIRI industrial assessment), and Egypt (SIRI assessment and capacity-building activities). INCIT also reports international governmental engagement with its CivicHorizon industrial intelligence platform. IndustryForward AI's proposed integrated deployment across the Arab States, beginning in Lebanon, has not yet commenced.
Implementation timeline(s): The underlying INCIT industrial transformation methodologies have a documented international implementation history spanning 2017–2026: 2017–2019, Singapore: SIRI was launched in November 2017 and subsequently deployed through government-supported industrial assessments, with over 200 official assessments completed by 2019. 2020–2022, Global: International SIRI rollout began in October 2020 through collaboration with the World Economic Forum and Singapore Economic Development Board. The 2022 global study covered approximately 600 manufacturing enterprises across 30 countries. 2022 onward, Saudi Arabia: A national SIRI adoption initiative was established through the INCIT–NIDLP partnership announced on 24 June 2022. 2021–2022, Philippines: An ADB-supported SIRI pilot in 2021 was followed by a national adoption agreement in October 2022. 2024, Indonesia and Egypt: Documented SIRI application at PT Akebono Brake Astra Indonesia and assessor training and guided assessment activities in Egypt. May 2025, Türkiye: AIMRI industrial assessment completed at Viessmann on 26–27 May 2025, producing a prioritized AI transformation roadmap. By June 2025, Azerbaijan: COSIRI applied at Crispa Snacks, with the case study published on 25 June 2025. INCIT's 2025 Global SIRI Report additionally documents manufacturing insights from thousands of companies across more than 60 countries. These implementation periods relate to established INCIT methodologies. IndustryForward AI proposes to leverage this international experience for an integrated deployment across the Arab States. Its own regional implementation has not yet commenced.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: IndustryForward AI is designed as a continuous industrial transformation initiative, with an initial 24-month implementation cycle in a new geography, structured around multiple cohorts of manufacturing enterprises, particularly MSMEs. The proposed implementation model comprises: - **Months 1–3 — Mobilization and setup:** Establish institutional partnerships, secure technology access, qualify assessors, select priority industrial sectors, and recruit the first cohort. - **Months 4–6 — First cohort deployment:** Conduct integrated industrial readiness assessments, AI-supported benchmarking, and develop customized transformation roadmaps. - **Months 7–12 — Implementation and expansion:** Support the first cohort's transformation activities while onboarding and assessing subsequent cohorts. Facilitate technology adoption, skills development, and investment planning. - **Months 13–18 — Scaling and continuous improvement:** Expand beneficiary coverage, strengthen sector-level industrial intelligence, and monitor enterprise transformation outcomes. - **Months 19–24 — Consolidation and institutionalization:** Evaluate results across cohorts, document measurable industrial improvements, develop policy recommendations, and establish mechanisms for continued implementation and geographic expansion. The initiative follows a rolling-cohort model, allowing assessment, technical assistance, capacity building, and performance monitoring to operate simultaneously across different groups of beneficiaries. While the initial programme cycle spans 24 months, the first cohort could begin assessments within approximately 3–6 months, subject to partnership agreements and operational readiness. The long-term objective is to establish a sustainable, nationally anchored industrial transformation mechanism that continues beyond the initial implementation period and can be replicated across the Arab States.

Unique Characteristics: IndustryForward AI's innovation lies in turning established industrial readiness technologies into a coordinated, AI-enabled pathway from assessment to investment, implementation and measurable impact. Its distinctive contribution is the proposed delivery model—not ownership of INCIT's assessment frameworks or existing digital platforms. 1. Integrated industrial transformation. The initiative proposes to deploy four complementary methodologies developed by the International Centre for Industrial Transformation (INCIT): SIRI (Industry 4.0 readiness), COSIRI (sustainability), AIMRI (AI maturity) and OPERI (operational excellence). Applied selectively according to enterprise needs, these frameworks would provide a multidimensional view of manufacturers' capability gaps and priorities. INCIT already offers cross-index integration through CivicHorizon; IndustryForward AI would seek authorized access rather than claim to have invented it. 2. AI-supported decisions that lead to action. Assessment results would inform benchmarking, scenario analysis and intervention prioritization, potentially using CivicHorizon's existing industrial intelligence capabilities. Technical experts would validate recommendations and translate them into sequenced roadmaps, investment cases, capacity-building plans and achievable operational improvements. Proposed additional AI functions would be developed or validated before deployment. 3. Public–private implementation partnership. The proposed model brings together Transformeus as programme coordinator; the Lebanese Private Sector Network (LPSN) for private-sector mobilization; the Association of Lebanese Industrialists (ALI) for manufacturer engagement; Lebanon's Ministry of Industry for potential policy alignment; and INCIT as prospective technology and methodology partner. These partnerships are not yet formalized. The model connects industry demand, international expertise, enterprise support and policy intelligence rather than treating transformation as an isolated consultancy exercise. 4. Affordable, multi-cohort delivery. A 24-month rolling programme would organize manufacturers—particularly MSMEs—into successive cohorts. Standardized processes, shared training, sector-focused interventions and repeatable monitoring would aim to reduce delivery costs and make advanced assessment and transformation support accessible to smaller factories. 5. Finance-linked implementation. Roadmaps would be converted into prioritized business cases and, where feasible, connected to technology providers, lenders and development programmes. Cost-sharing or blended-finance mechanisms could be explored with partners; no dedicated financing facility is currently secured. 6. Two levels of measurable value. At factory level, indicators could include AI adoption, productivity, downtime, energy intensity, workforce skills and investment mobilized. At ecosystem level, consent-based, anonymized aggregate data could inform sector benchmarking and industrial development priorities. Baselines and follow-up assessments would distinguish actual results from projected benefits. The initiative builds on documented international INCIT experience, including SIRI adoption in Saudi Arabia and enterprise assessments in other countries. These precedents validate elements of the technology and methodology, not prior implementation of IndustryForward AI itself. The differentiation is therefore a replicable, locally anchored mechanism that connects industrial intelligence with practical transformation, financing opportunities and evidence-based public–private coordination—initially in Lebanon, with potential expansion across the Arab States.
Sustainable Change: IndustryForward AI aims to generate systemic change by establishing a continuous, evidence-based industrial transformation mechanism that extends beyond individual factory assessments or time-limited technical assistance. The proposed 24-month, multi-cohort programme would begin in Lebanon and create a model for replication across the Arab States. 1. Institutionalize industrial transformation. Through prospective collaboration among Transformeus, the Lebanese Private Sector Network (LPSN), the Association of Lebanese Industrialists (ALI), Lebanon's Ministry of Industry and the International Centre for Industrial Transformation (INCIT), the initiative would connect industry needs, national policy, technical expertise and implementation support. Partnerships and access to INCIT technology remain subject to agreement. 2. Inform policy and investment. With appropriate consent, confidentiality safeguards and anonymization, aggregated results from SIRI, COSIRI, AIMRI and OPERI assessments could reveal common gaps in productivity, digital readiness, AI capabilities and sustainability. These insights could help institutions target training, incentives, technology support and investment toward the most pressing industrial priorities. 3. Create demonstration and supply-chain effects. Successive cohorts would produce practical transformation cases, allowing manufacturers to learn from peers and adopt proven approaches. Improvements within participating factories could stimulate demand for local technology providers, engineering services, workforce training and supplier upgrading, extending benefits beyond direct beneficiaries. 4. Build enduring local capabilities. Training assessors, advisors and enterprise personnel would strengthen domestic expertise in Industry 4.0, operational excellence, responsible AI and resource efficiency. Over time, qualified local providers and industry institutions could continue supporting new cohorts without depending entirely on externally funded projects. 5. Link readiness to financing and delivery. Translating assessments into prioritized business cases could create a pipeline of bankable modernization projects. Engagement with financial institutions and development partners may enable tailored financing, shared technical assistance and co-investment mechanisms. No dedicated financing facility has yet been secured. 6. Enable scalable regional replication. Standardized INCIT methodologies and potential access to CivicHorizon provide a basis for consistent assessment and benchmarking, while local partners would adapt sector selection, delivery, financing and governance to each market. Documented applications of INCIT frameworks in Saudi Arabia and other countries support the feasibility of international adaptation; they do not constitute prior deployment of IndustryForward AI itself. The long-term objective is to shift industrial support from isolated diagnostics toward recurring assessment, implementation and results measurement. Sustained impact would be evaluated through technology adoption, productivity, workforce capabilities, resource efficiency, investment mobilization and the number of enterprises supported beyond the initial cohorts. By reinforcing enterprise competitiveness and institutional decision-making together, IndustryForward AI could contribute to SDGs 8, 9 and 17.
Funding Sources: IndustryForward AI builds on internationally established INCIT methodologies previously deployed through different funding arrangements, including government-supported assessments, multilateral development assistance, and subsidized industrial transformation programmes. Documented precedents include Singapore's government-funded SIRI assessments, Asian Development Bank (ADB) support for SIRI adoption in the Philippines, and Brazil's publicly subsidized industrial digital transformation programme. The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), potentially supported by European Union funding, is identified as a priority prospective financing partner. The EBRD has an established track record in Lebanon through its Advice for Small Businesses, Innovation, and Resource Efficiency and Circularity programmes, combining technical assistance, enterprise advisory services, and investment grants. Additional financing partnerships could be explored with UNIDO, other international development organizations, and bilateral donors supporting industrial competitiveness, digital transformation, responsible AI adoption, and sustainability. The proposed financing structure would cover industrial readiness assessments, access to digital intelligence tools, assessor certification, capacity building, enterprise transformation roadmaps, implementation support, and impact monitoring. Name of your organization: Fundación para el Fomento Integral y Desarrollo (FUNDafid)
Title: AgroIA FUNDafid: Multimodal AI for Sustainable Rural Production
Subtitle: AI-powered agricultural decision support through WhatsApp, combining images, video, production data and sensors to improve timely decisions and reduce preventable losses.
Problem Statement: Small rural producers often face production problems without timely access to affordable and specialized technical assistance. Disease, contamination, environmental imbalance, poor production practices, or delayed decisions can cause avoidable production losses and reduce household income. The problem is intensified in rural areas where agricultural specialists are scarce, distances are significant, connectivity can be limited, and producers may rely on informal or delayed advice. AgroIA addresses the gap between the moment a production problem appears and the moment a producer can obtain structured technical guidance. The initial application focuses on small oyster mushroom producers in Nariño, Colombia, where production depends on careful management of environmental conditions, substrate, contamination risks, and production practices.
Solution Overview: AgroIA FUNDafid is a multimodal artificial intelligence decision-support system designed to provide first-line agricultural technical assistance through WhatsApp. A producer can submit photographs, videos, text descriptions, production history, and relevant environmental information. When available, the system can also incorporate measurements such as temperature, relative humidity, pH, electrical conductivity, CO2, light, and moisture. The AI layer analyzes the available evidence together with a crop-specific agricultural knowledge base and structured diagnostic protocols. The system does not treat an uncertain AI interpretation as a definitive diagnosis. Instead, it identifies observable signs, proposes possible causes and differential diagnoses, indicates confidence, identifies missing information, recommends immediate actions, identifies actions to avoid, and determines whether human technical review is required. High-risk, uncertain, contaminated, systemic, or insufficiently documented cases can be escalated to an agricultural specialist. The system records structured cases and, after human validation, can use outcomes as learning data for future improvement. AI-generated outputs are not automatically treated as validated truth. The prototype uses a modular software architecture with a backend API, structured data models, multimodal AI services, a crop-specific knowledge base, case management, and a planned WhatsApp Cloud API integration. The initial implementation model is based on collaboration among FUNDafid, agricultural specialists, technology developers, producer organizations, research institutions, and potential public-sector or development partners.
Solution Provider(s): o formal external partner has been confirmed specifically for AgroIA FUNDafid at this stage. FUNDafid is developing the solution and plans to establish partnerships with agricultural research institutions, universities, AI technology specialists, producer organizations, municipalities, and agricultural extension programs for field validation, technical verification, data governance, and scale-up.
Implementation location(s): N/A – AgroIA is currently at the prototype stage and has not yet been deployed in a sustained field implementation. The prototype has been developed and tested in a local development environment in Colombia.
Implementation timeline(s): N/A – field implementation has not yet started. Prototype development and testing have been conducted during 2026.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Approximately 3 months, depending on local partner availability, producer recruitment, connectivity, technical validation, data governance requirements, and adaptation of the agricultural knowledge base.
Desired impact: The main objective of AgroIA FUNDafid is to make timely and structured agricultural decision support more accessible to small rural producers through an AI-enabled digital service. The solution aims to help producers identify production problems earlier, improve decision-making, avoid inappropriate interventions, document production cases, and obtain human technical support when AI evidence is insufficient. The initial planned field validation will target approximately 50 small rural producers in La Florida and El Tambo, Nariño, Colombia, focusing on oyster mushroom production over a 12-month period. The planned validation will document approximately 100–150 production cases and evaluate diagnostic agreement with agricultural specialists, appropriate human escalation, response time, follow-up, producer usefulness, and production outcomes. At the current prototype stage, AgroIA does not claim demonstrated reductions in production losses, increased income, or quantified environmental impacts. These impacts will be measured during controlled field validation. In the longer term, the solution aims to reduce preventable production losses, improve resource efficiency, strengthen productive resilience, and contribute to more stable economic opportunities for small rural producers.
Key technologies: AgroIA FUNDafid combines: Multimodal generative artificial intelligence for analysis of text, images and planned video inputs. Computer vision for agricultural image interpretation. Structured agricultural knowledge bases and diagnostic protocols. Rule-based safety and uncertainty management. Human-in-the-loop validation and escalation. Cloud-based backend services and APIs. PostgreSQL-compatible structured data storage. Secure multimedia storage. WhatsApp Cloud API for producer communication. Optional environmental sensor data integration. Structured case and outcome databases for validated learning data. The technology architecture is modular so that additional crops, sensors, languages, and deployment channels can be incorporated without redesigning the entire system.
Unique Characteristics: AgroIA is designed as more than a generic agricultural chatbot. It combines multimodal AI, crop-specific knowledge, structured diagnostic protocols, uncertainty management, human oversight, and longitudinal case information. Its main differentiating feature is the explicit management of uncertainty. The system is designed to recognize when available evidence is insufficient rather than presenting an uncertain AI interpretation as a definitive diagnosis. The solution can request additional photographs, videos, environmental measurements, production history, or other information before generating a recommendation. It can also escalate complex or high-risk cases to human specialists. The WhatsApp delivery model reduces the need for producers to learn a new specialized platform. This approach is particularly relevant for rural and low-resource environments where digital access, technical skills, and specialist availability can be limited. The solution also creates a structured pathway for validated production cases and outcomes to become learning data, supporting future adaptation to local crops and production conditions.
Sustainable Change: AgroIA could contribute to systemic change by extending the reach of agricultural technical assistance rather than attempting to replace agricultural specialists. The system can provide first-line triage and structured information before a human specialist intervenes. This could allow limited technical capacity to serve more producers and prioritize cases requiring expert attention. The architecture is designed for replication across agricultural value chains. After validation with oyster mushroom production, the same framework could be adapted to other crops by modifying the agricultural knowledge base, diagnostic protocols, datasets, and validation procedures. The solution could also be integrated into producer associations, cooperatives, municipalities, agricultural extension programs, NGOs, development projects, and public-sector productive-development initiatives. At scale, AgroIA could create a digital layer connecting rural producers, agricultural specialists, institutions, and validated production data. This could improve the timeliness of technical assistance while generating evidence for more targeted agricultural interventions. The long-term objective is to create an adaptable and responsible AI infrastructure for inclusive rural productive development, with human oversight, local validation, data protection, and measurable impact. 25. Funding Sources: AgroIA FUNDafid has been developed primarily through FUNDafid's own organizational resources and in-kind contributions, including staff time, technical formulation, agricultural knowledge development, prototype design, software development, testing, and project management. The current prototype has not received a dedicated external grant or investment specifically for AgroIA. FUNDafid is currently seeking external funding and strategic partnerships to conduct controlled field validation with rural producers, strengthen the multimodal AI infrastructure, integrate WhatsApp and sensor data, conduct independent technical evaluation, and prepare the solution for broader deployment.

Title: Biosphere OS: AI Water Digital Twin for Sustainable Agroindustry
Subtitle: An AI-enabled platform that anticipates orchard water stress and creates a traceable record to support climate resilience and more sustainable agricultural supply chains.
Problem Statement: Avocado producers in Mexico face increasing water stress, climate variability and growing demands from buyers for credible environmental information. Many small and medium-sized producers lack accessible digital tools that connect field conditions, irrigation records and crop needs to support timely decisions. Data may be incomplete or scattered across farms, making it difficult to anticipate water stress, assess irrigation practices and provide consistent, verifiable evidence about water use. Biosphere OS addresses this gap by helping producers turn field and climate data into practical irrigation decision support and a structured record of water-related practices.
Solution Overview: Biosphere OS is developing an AI-enabled digital twin for agricultural production systems, initially focused on avocado orchards in Uruapan, Michoacán, Mexico. The platform is designed to bring together orchard-level information—including soil moisture, irrigation events, weather and evapotranspiration data, and crop growth stage—into a shared view of field conditions. Predictive models are intended to identify emerging water-stress risks and support localized irrigation decisions. Recommendations will be reviewed with producers and local technical advisors, so they can be assessed against field conditions and adjusted to the needs of each site. A water traceability layer will organize relevant observations and records and use cryptographic methods to make subsequent changes detectable. This can support transparency and review; it does not, by itself, certify the accuracy of source data or replace independent verification. The proposed delivery model combines a digital platform with a phased field pilot: establish a baseline, configure available data and minimum viable telemetry, validate the workflow with participating producers, and evaluate adoption and water-related indicators before considering replication. Biosphere OS will seek collaboration with producer organizations and local technical, research and implementation partners. Specific pilot partners remain to be confirmed.
Solution Provider(s): Biosphere OS (solution developer); pilot producer organizations, local agricultural technical advisors and research or implementation partners are being identified and are not yet confirmed
Implementation location(s): N/A — the solution has not yet been implemented. Proposed initial pilot location: Uruapan, Michoacán, Mexico.
Implementation timeline(s): N/A — no implementation period has been completed. The proposed pilot schedule will be agreed with participating producers and partners.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Approximately 3–6 months for site onboarding, data-readiness assessment, local configuration and pilot preparation, subject to producer participation, data availability and access to field measurements.
Desired impact: The main objective is to help avocado producers make better-informed irrigation decisions by combining field observations, soil-moisture and irrigation data, weather and evapotranspiration information, and crop-stage context in one decision-support workflow. The proposed pilot will assess whether the platform can improve the timeliness and consistency of irrigation decisions, strengthen producers’ ability to monitor water-related practices, and create a more structured record for supply-chain engagement. Impact will be measured against a baseline agreed with participating producers. Potential indicators include water applied per hectare where reliable measurement is available, irrigation frequency, soil-moisture trends, completeness of field records, producer adoption and user-reported decision usefulness. No water savings or emissions reductions are claimed in advance; these will be reported only if supported by comparable measurements.
Key technologies: The proposed solution combines predictive machine learning with agricultural data integration and a digital representation of orchard conditions. Depending on site readiness, inputs may include soil-moisture sensors, irrigation records, weather and evapotranspiration data, and crop-stage observations. The platform is designed to use these inputs to identify potential water-stress conditions and support localized irrigation decisions. A cryptographic recordkeeping layer can make changes to submitted records detectable and support traceability. Data availability, sensor configuration and model performance will be assessed and validated during the pilot.
Unique Characteristics: Biosphere OS combines decision support and water traceability in a single workflow tailored to small and medium-sized agricultural producers. Its proposed “Water Passport” organizes water-related field records alongside the context needed to interpret them, such as location, time and source. Predictive analysis is intended to help producers act on emerging water-stress risks, while the traceability layer can make later changes to records detectable. This approach moves beyond displaying sensor readings: it aims to connect field data with producer decisions and supply-chain communication. The resulting records may help buyers and other stakeholders review water-related practices, subject to data quality and appropriate verification. The platform is designed for phased adoption, beginning with a pilot and adapting to local data availability and production practices.
Sustainable Change: If validated, Biosphere OS could help make practical digital decision support and structured water records more accessible to small and medium-sized producers. More consistent information could support learning within producer groups, improve conversations between producers and buyers, and inform future water-management practices across agricultural supply chains. The approach is designed to be adapted to other regions and crops by recalibrating models, data inputs and workflows with local producers and technical partners. A phased replication model—starting with a measured pilot, documenting performance and limitations, and then adapting the solution to new sites—could support wider adoption while preserving local relevance. Any broader claims about water savings, market access or producer income would depend on evidence from implementation.
Funding Sources: Biosphere OS is currently at the pilot-development stage and has not yet completed a prior implementation of this solution. Development to date has been supported by No previous implementation-specific funding is available to report. No funding from previous deployments is reported.
Testimonials and Endorsements: No formal stakeholder testimonials or endorsements are available at this stage. Biosphere OS is preparing to validate the solution with participating producers and will seek permission to publish attributable feedback during or after the pilot.
Primary thematic focus area: AI for Green, Resilient and Sustainable Industry
Summary: Biosphere OS proposes a water digital twin for avocado orchards in Michoacan, with a traceable Water Passport for buyers. The concept is well aimed; with no implementation and no funding, it cannot be assessed beyond design.
