Title: OlaBrain: AI-Powered Circular Battery Intelligence and Smart Energy Management
Subtitle: An AI and IoT-powered platform transforming suitable retired electric motorbike batteries into intelligent, second-life energy storage systems for businesses and decentralised renewable energy applications.
Problem Statement: The growing adoption of electric mobility is creating an increasing need for effective battery lifecycle management. However, many batteries that reach the end of their first use in electric vehicles may still retain useful capacity and can serve other energy applications. In developing economies such as Rwanda, the limited availability of affordable battery health assessment, monitoring and intelligent energy management systems makes it difficult to identify, assess and safely reuse these batteries. At the same time, small businesses, households and decentralised energy systems face challenges accessing reliable and affordable electricity storage, while renewable energy installations require better monitoring and management. OLAMOVE addresses this challenge through an integrated circular energy solution combining AI, IoT and modular battery storage. The solution aims to extend battery useful life, improve energy storage performance, reduce battery waste and make renewable energy storage more accessible.
Solution Overview: OlaBrain is OLAMOVE's developing AI and IoT-powered battery intelligence platform, integrated with OlaEnergy, our modular solar and backup energy storage initiative. The solution connects battery assessment, second-life battery repurposing and intelligent energy management into one system. It works through five main stages. Battery data collection and assessment: Battery Management Systems (BMS), sensors and monitoring devices collect information on battery voltage, current, temperature, charging cycles, capacity and operating conditions. This data supports the assessment of battery condition and remaining useful capacity. AI-powered battery intelligence: OlaBrain is being developed to analyse battery performance data, identify degradation patterns, estimate battery state of health, support remaining useful life prediction and identify potential maintenance requirements. Intelligent battery repurposing: Based on battery condition and suitability assessments, batteries with sufficient remaining capacity can be considered for second-life applications, including modular solar and backup energy storage. Batteries that do not meet safety and performance requirements are excluded from reuse. Smart energy management: Through OlaEnergy, suitable repurposed battery modules are integrated into energy storage systems. The intended intelligent monitoring capabilities include tracking charging and discharging, energy consumption, system performance and operating conditions. Performance monitoring and lifecycle management: OlaBrain is intended to provide a centralised digital platform for monitoring battery performance, supporting maintenance decisions, tracking battery utilisation and generating operational and environmental performance reports. Methodologies and technologies The solution combines battery diagnostics, data analytics, machine learning, IoT connectivity, Battery Management Systems, modular energy storage and solar energy integration. AI models will be developed and validated using real battery operating data, with a focus on battery health prediction, degradation analysis and intelligent energy management. Partnership and collaboration model OLAMOVE leads product development, battery assessment, system integration, testing and market deployment. The company seeks collaboration with battery manufacturers, renewable energy developers, technology providers, research institutions and industrial partners to strengthen AI development, hardware integration, validation and market expansion. The OlaEnergy pilot has received financial support from RES4Africa Foundation through the RAISEAfrica 2026 programme, providing an important foundation for prototype development, testing and market validation. The solution is being developed through practical testing and customer-oriented validation in Rwanda, with the ambition of adapting it to other African markets.
Solution Provider(s): RES4Africa Foundation (Renewable Energy Solutions for Africa) is a key development partner supporting OLAMOVE's OlaEnergy pilot project through financing awarded under the RAISEAfrica 2026 programme (Renewables Accelerators for Innovative Startups and Entrepreneurs in Africa). RES4Africa Foundation works in the renewable energy sector, promoting sustainable energy solutions, innovation and investment across Africa. YOOS Group Ltd is an existing supply-chain partner supporting OLAMOVE's electric mobility operations, contributing to the company's wider battery and clean mobility ecosystem. **OLAMOVE Ltd** is the lead developer and implementing organisation, responsible for solution development, battery assessment, system integration, testing and deployment.
Implementation location(s): Rwanda, particularly Kigali and Nyamata in Bugesera District, where OLAMOVE conducts its electric mobility operations and develops and tests its modular battery repurposing and energy storage initiative.
Implementation timeline(s): 2026 to present. Development and validation activities for OlaEnergy and the associated battery intelligence capabilities are ongoing.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Approximately 3–6 months, depending on local technical requirements, battery availability, regulatory conditions, infrastructure readiness and partnerships. Deployment would include an initial assessment, system integration, installation, testing and performance validation.
Desired impact: The main objective of OlaBrain and OlaEnergy is to improve battery lifecycle management and expand access to reliable, affordable and sustainable energy storage through AI-powered intelligence and circular battery reuse. The solution has five main objectives. 1. Extend battery useful life: Identify suitable retired electric motorbike batteries and assess their remaining capacity for safe second-life applications, reducing premature disposal and improving resource efficiency. 2. Improve industrial intelligence: Use AI and data analytics to support battery health assessment, degradation prediction, predictive maintenance and better operational decisions. 3. Expand access to clean energy: Transform suitable second-life batteries into modular solar and backup energy storage systems for households, small businesses and decentralised energy applications. 4. Improve energy resilience: Support more reliable electricity access through intelligent battery monitoring, energy storage management and integration with renewable energy systems. 5. Promote circular industrial development: Demonstrate how locally available battery resources can be repurposed into productive energy assets, creating opportunities for technical skills development, employment and local value addition. Expected and emerging impact: OLAMOVE has already assembled more than 150 electric motorbikes and served over 1,000 customers through its wider electric mobility operations. This provides an existing operational environment and potential source of battery performance data for developing and validating the solution. Through OlaEnergy, we are developing and testing modular energy storage systems using suitable repurposed electric motorbike batteries. Our expected impact includes: - Extending the productive use of suitable retired batteries through second-life applications. - Improving battery assessment and maintenance decisions through AI-supported analytics. - Reducing demand for newly manufactured batteries in applications where second-life batteries are technically suitable. - Increasing access to affordable backup and renewable energy storage for small businesses and households. - Supporting local technical employment and skills development in battery technology, electronics, AI and renewable energy. We are also targeting approximately 70–80% usable remaining capacity as an initial assessment benchmark for selecting suitable batteries for second-life applications, subject to battery chemistry, safety testing and application requirements. This is a development target, not yet a verified project-wide result. As implementation progresses, we will measure battery reuse rates, usable storage capacity, energy delivered, system reliability, battery lifecycle extension and avoided emissions against appropriate baselines.
Key technologies: The solution combines the following technologies. - Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning: Battery state-of-health estimation, degradation analysis, predictive maintenance and intelligent energy management. - Internet of Things (IoT): Connected sensors and monitoring devices for collecting real-time battery and energy system performance data. - Battery Management Systems (BMS): Monitoring battery voltage, current, temperature, charging and discharging conditions, and protection parameters. - Data Analytics: Processing battery performance and operational data to support technical and business decisions. - Cloud-based Digital Platforms: Centralised data management, remote monitoring, reporting and battery lifecycle tracking. - Solar Photovoltaic Technology: Integration of renewable energy generation with modular battery storage systems. - Modular Energy Storage Technology: Integration of suitable second-life battery modules into scalable backup and renewable energy storage solutions. These technologies will work together through OlaBrain, providing the digital intelligence layer for OlaEnergy's physical energy storage systems.
Unique Characteristics: OlaBrain and OlaEnergy bring together two areas that are often addressed separately: electric mobility battery lifecycle management and decentralised renewable energy storage. The solution's main innovation is its use of AI and IoT to support the transition of suitable electric motorbike batteries from their first-life mobility applications into productive second-life energy storage applications. Its distinguishing features include: 1. AI-supported battery second-life assessment: Rather than treating all retired batteries as waste, the solution uses battery performance data and intelligent assessment to identify batteries that may remain suitable for other applications. 2. Integration of digital intelligence and physical infrastructure: OlaBrain is designed to connect battery monitoring, predictive analytics and operational decision-making with OlaEnergy's modular solar and backup storage systems. 3. Circular and locally adaptable business model: OLAMOVE combines its existing electric mobility operations with battery repurposing and energy storage, creating opportunities to recover additional value from battery assets within the local economy. 4. Modular and scalable deployment: The energy storage systems are designed to accommodate suitable battery modules and serve different energy requirements, including households, small businesses and decentralised energy systems. 5. Practical development in an emerging market: The solution is being developed and tested in Rwanda, where access to affordable energy storage, local technical capacity and sustainable battery management are important development priorities. By combining AI, battery technology, renewable energy and circular economy principles, OLAMOVE aims to develop a replicable model for more sustainable industrial and energy systems across African markets.
Sustainable Change: OlaBrain and OlaEnergy have the potential to contribute to a wider transformation in how electric vehicle batteries are managed, reused and integrated into energy systems across developing economies. Beyond individual battery storage installations, the solution aims to establish a more connected circular battery ecosystem in which battery manufacturers, electric mobility operators, energy developers, businesses and technical service providers can participate. Its potential contribution to systemic change includes: 1. Advancing circular industrial value chains** By creating a structured approach to battery assessment, repurposing and second-life deployment, the solution can help establish local battery reuse and maintenance value chains. This can reduce underutilisation of valuable resources and create additional economic opportunities. 2. Supporting renewable energy expansion** Repurposed batteries can provide additional storage options for solar energy systems, small businesses and decentralised electricity networks. This can contribute to improved energy resilience and more productive use of renewable energy. 3. Promoting AI adoption among African MSMEs** OlaBrain demonstrates how AI can address practical industrial challenges beyond conventional software applications. Its approach can encourage other local businesses to adopt data-driven systems for asset management, predictive maintenance and operational efficiency. 4. Building local technical capacity** The solution can create opportunities for training and employment in battery diagnostics, electrical engineering, renewable energy systems, IoT and AI-supported operations, while encouraging collaboration between businesses, universities and technology providers. 5. Enabling replication across African markets** The modular design and digital intelligence platform can potentially be adapted to other African countries with growing electric mobility markets, increasing battery availability and demand for affordable energy storage. In the longer term, OLAMOVE aims to develop OlaBrain into a scalable battery intelligence platform that can support multiple battery types, mobility operators and energy storage applications. Our ambition is to demonstrate that developing economies can move beyond importing and consuming clean technologies towards developing, adapting and deploying intelligent circular industrial solutions that create local economic value and contribute to global sustainability objectives.
Primary thematic focus area: AI for Green, Resilient and Sustainable Industry
Summary: OlaBrain assesses retired motorbike batteries for state of health, grades them for second-life use and manages them as modular solar and backup storage in Rwanda. Development and validation are under way at Kigali and Nyamata, with financing from the RES4Africa programme.
Thematic focus areas (as submitted): Industrial AI Models and Intelligent Decision-Making; Industrial Digital Infrastructure and Data Ecosystems; AI for Green, Resilient and Sustainable Industry

Title: Green Europe Youth Lab: AI for a Sustainable Future
Subtitle: Empowering young people to use AI, digital technologies and collaborative learning to develop innovative solutions for environmental challenges and build a more sustainable Europe.
Problem Statement: Young people often lack practical opportunities to apply digital technologies and artificial intelligence to real-world environmental challenges. Education does not always sufficiently connect digital skills, sustainability, and active civic participation. As a result, students may struggle to turn their knowledge into concrete solutions for issues such as pollution, biodiversity loss, and unsustainable resource use. There is a need for inclusive, hands-on learning experiences that empower students to collaborate, think critically, and develop innovative solutions for a greener Europe.
Solution Overview: 1. How the solution works 1. How the solution works Green Europe Youth Lab: AI for a Sustainable Future empowers secondary school students to use AI and digital technologies to address environmental challenges such as pollution, waste, water quality, biodiversity loss, and unsustainable tourism. Students work in teams to investigate local issues, collect and analyse data, develop technology-supported solutions, test their ideas, and present recommendations to schools and communities. Activities may include drone imagery, AI-based image recognition, digital mapping, and multimedia awareness campaigns. 2. Methodologies and technologies used The solution combines project-based, inquiry-based, STEM, and experiential learning with design thinking and teamwork. Students develop critical thinking, problem-solving, digital literacy, and responsible AI skills. Technologies include AI-assisted image recognition, machine learning, drones, geographic information systems (GIS), environmental sensors, data visualisation, and digital collaboration tools. Students learn to evaluate AI outputs critically, protect personal data, and validate findings using reliable evidence. 3. Partnerships and collaboration models The initiative connects schools, students, environmental organisations, local authorities, universities, technology providers, and European education networks. Teachers coordinate activities, students lead investigations, environmental experts provide guidance, and public institutions support community-based projects. Universities and technology partners contribute technical expertise, while international networks enable cross-border collaboration and knowledge exchange. Partnerships are developed through workshops, fieldwork, mentoring, digital exchanges, pilot projects, and public presentations. The model is adaptable to different schools and communities, promoting digital innovation, environmental responsibility, and active European citizenship.
Solution Provider(s): Ekonomska škola Šibenik – Public secondary vocational school specialising in economics, commerce and administration, with expertise in digital education, student projects and international cooperation; Education and Vocational Training Sector, Croatia, Udruga EMEDEA – Non-governmental organisation and sustainable development cluster based on Murter, working in environmental sustainability, youth engagement, STEM education and inclusive development; Civil Society, Environment and Education Sectors, Europe Direct Adriatic Croatia – European Commission information centre managed by EMEDEA, promoting EU awareness, citizen participation and European cooperation in Šibenik-Knin County; European Information and Civic Engagement Sector, UNESCO Associated Schools Network (ASPnet) – International educational network promoting sustainability, global citizenship, peace and intercultural understanding; International Education and Sustainable Development Sector, European Parliament Ambassador School Programme (EPAS) – European Parliament educational programme promoting European citizenship, democratic participation and youth engagement; European Education and Civic Participation Sector.
Implementation location(s): Ekonomska škola Šibenik, Šibenik, Croatia
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3–6 months
Desired impact: Main objectives Green Europe Youth Lab: AI for a Sustainable Future aims to empower secondary school students to apply artificial intelligence and digital technologies to real-world environmental challenges. The solution connects quality education, digital innovation, and environmental sustainability through practical, project-based learning. Its main objectives are to develop students' AI and digital competencies, strengthen environmental awareness and critical thinking, encourage responsible technology use, and support young people in designing evidence-based solutions to pollution, waste management, biodiversity loss, and other local sustainability challenges. The initiative also aims to strengthen cooperation between schools, environmental organisations, public institutions, and European education networks. Expected impact The solution is designed to generate educational, environmental, and community benefits. Expected outcomes include improved AI literacy, stronger STEM skills, increased youth participation in sustainability initiatives, and practical proposals for addressing local environmental issues. Impact will be measured through indicators such as: Number of participating schools, teachers, and students. Number of environmental investigations and student-led projects completed. Number of AI-supported prototypes, digital tools, or practical recommendations developed. Improvement in students' digital, AI, and environmental competencies, measured through pre- and post-activity assessments. Number of partnerships established and environmental awareness activities delivered. Where measurable, quantities of waste identified or collected, areas surveyed, and environmental improvements supported by student projects. The initiative's longer-term ambition is to establish a scalable educational model that can be adopted by schools in different European communities and adapted to local environmental priorities. As the solution is currently being developed as a concept, quantified environmental outcomes have not yet been established. Baseline measurements and pilot results will be used to set realistic targets and assess its effectiveness. The project will avoid claiming reductions in greenhouse gas emissions or other environmental benefits unless these can be measured and verified.
Key technologies: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and machine learning for environmental data analysis, image recognition, and pattern detection; drones and aerial imagery for observing local environmental conditions; Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and digital mapping for visualising environmental challenges; environmental sensors and Internet of Things (IoT) technologies for monitoring selected environmental indicators; spreadsheets and data visualisation tools for analysing and presenting findings; and digital collaboration and multimedia tools for student teamwork, knowledge sharing, and environmental awareness campaigns. Technologies are selected according to project needs, available resources, and students' competencies.
Unique Characteristics: Green Europe Youth Lab: AI for a Sustainable Future combines artificial intelligence, digital technologies, environmental education, and youth participation in a practical, interdisciplinary learning model. Its distinctive feature is the transformation of students from technology users into young innovators who investigate real environmental challenges and develop evidence-based solutions for their communities. Unlike traditional environmental education, the solution integrates AI-assisted image recognition, drones, digital mapping, and data analysis with hands-on fieldwork and project-based learning. Students connect digital skills with sustainability challenges such as pollution, waste management, biodiversity loss, and responsible resource use. The solution also stands out through its collaborative model, connecting schools, environmental organisations, public institutions, technology experts, and European education networks. Its flexible, low-cost approach allows schools to start with accessible digital tools and gradually introduce more advanced technologies. The model is designed to be adaptable and replicable across different schools and regions. Through shared learning resources, student collaboration, and cross-border knowledge exchange, successful practices can be transferred to other communities. Its innovation lies not only in the technologies used, but also in combining digital competence development, environmental responsibility, and active European citizenship in a scalable educational approach.
Sustainable Change: Green Europe Youth Lab: AI for a Sustainable Future has the potential to transform how schools integrate artificial intelligence, digital innovation, and environmental sustainability into education. By combining practical learning with real-world environmental challenges, the solution can help embed digital and AI competencies, critical thinking, and environmental responsibility into regular teaching practices. Its modular approach allows other schools to replicate activities using locally available resources, adapting projects to challenges such as pollution, waste management, water quality, biodiversity loss, and sustainable tourism. Shared teaching materials, digital resources, and cross-border cooperation can support knowledge transfer and enable schools to build a wider European network of young environmental innovators. Partnerships with environmental organisations, public institutions, universities, and technology providers could strengthen the model, provide expert mentoring, and help translate student proposals into community initiatives. Over time, successful pilot projects could inform local sustainability activities and encourage greater youth participation in environmental decision-making. The solution could scale through teacher training, open educational resources, Erasmus+ cooperation, and partnerships with European education networks. Its long-term systemic impact would be a stronger connection between education, responsible AI adoption, environmental action, and civic participation, helping prepare a generation of digitally competent and environmentally responsible citizens. These outcomes would be assessed through measurable indicators, pilot results, and evidence of adoption by additional schools and communities.
Funding Sources: N/A – The solution is currently at the concept stage and has not yet received dedicated funding. Potential future funding sources include Erasmus+, EU environmental and digital innovation programmes, national education grants, local and regional authorities, and private-sector sponsorships.
Testimonials and Endorsements: Although Green Europe Youth Lab: AI for a Sustainable Future is currently at the concept stage, the proposing school has experience in digital education, AI, and technology-supported student projects. Ekonomska škola Šibenik – Dron Liga and “Young People Take Off Towards a European Future”: The school received support from the Croatian Ministry of Science, Education and Youth for activities developing students' digital and technological skills through drone-based learning. Source: https://ss-ekonomska-si.skole.hr/skola_buducnosti/ European Parliament Ambassador School Programme (EPAS): The school has demonstrated sustained student engagement in European citizenship, collaborative projects, and active participation, achieving fifth place among Croatian EPAS schools in 2026. Source: https://ess-epas.com.hr/ These documented experiences provide a foundation for developing and piloting the proposed solution. No direct testimonials specifically endorsing Green Europe Youth Lab are available at this stage.

Title: Espact Digital Buddy
Subtitle: An AI-powered Skills-to-Jobs platform connecting African youth and women to personalized digital learning, career guidance, mentorship, and verified employment and entrepreneurship opportunities.
Problem Statement: Many African youth and women face a significant gap between acquiring digital skills and accessing meaningful economic opportunities. Limited career guidance, mentorship, employer networks, reliable internet access, and relevant job opportunities prevent many from translating their skills into employment, entrepreneurship, and sustainable income. Existing training programmes often lack personalized learning pathways and structured support to help learners transition from education to earning.
Solution Overview: ESPACT Digital Buddy is an AI-powered Skills-to-Jobs platform designed to bridge the gap between digital skills acquisition and meaningful economic opportunities for African youth and women. Building on ESPACT’s experience in digital skills training and employability support, the platform connects learning, career development, mentorship, and access to employment, internships, freelance work, and entrepreneurship opportunities in one integrated ecosystem. The solution uses AI to recommend personalized learning pathways based on users’ skills, interests, progress, and labour-market demand. Learners access digital learning resources, including videos, quizzes, practical tasks, role-play exercises, and skills assessments. AI-powered career guidance helps users identify suitable career paths, understand skill gaps, and prepare for opportunities. Human mentors, tutors, and supervisors complement AI support by providing practical guidance, feedback, and accountability. The platform incorporates cybersecurity education, certification, and a digital identity code following registration and verification. It is designed to connect learners with verified employers and relevant economic opportunities, helping them translate learning into income and career progression. Methodologies and technologies: The solution combines AI-assisted personalization, competency-based learning, practical assessments, human mentorship, digital identity and verification processes, and skills-to-opportunity matching. Its development approach incorporates user feedback, including insights from women and young people, to improve accessibility, relevance, safety, and usability. Partnerships and collaboration: ESPACT leads the initiative and intends to collaborate with technology developers, educational institutions, trainers, mentors, employers, recruiters, youth and women's organizations, and public-sector stakeholders. These partners can contribute to platform development, learning content, mentorship, user recruitment, job and internship opportunities, and impact measurement. The model is designed to support collaboration across sectors and countries, beginning with Nigeria and Kenya and expanding to other African markets.
Solution Provider(s): Dipgrom Limited — planned technology development partner for web and mobile platform development, subject to formal engagement and confirmation. Potential collaboration partners include educational institutions, employers, recruitment platforms, digital learning providers, youth-serving organizations, women's economic empowerment organizations, and public-sector institutions. These are prospective partner categories rather than confirmed project partners.
Implementation location(s): Nigeria; Lagos and Abuja
Implementation timeline(s): June 2026- June 2027
Duration to pilot in a new geography: August 2027- July 2028
Desired impact: The primary objective of ESPACT Digital Buddy is to improve the transition from digital learning to sustainable livelihoods for African youth and women by integrating personalized skills development, career guidance, mentorship, and access to economic opportunities. Specific objectives include: - Expanding access to relevant, practical, and affordable digital skills education. - Improving employability through personalized learning pathways, career guidance, and skills assessments. - Connecting learners with verified employment, internships, freelance work, and entrepreneurship opportunities. - Increasing women's participation in the digital economy through inclusive, flexible, and safety-conscious learning and career support. - Strengthening collaboration between learners, educators, mentors, employers, and technology providers. - Using feedback and platform data to continuously improve learning outcomes and opportunity matching. Demonstrated progress: ESPACT's wider digital skills and employability initiatives have reached more than 52,000 young people and women. ESPACT reports that over 65% have progressed into employment, entrepreneurship, internships, consultancy, freelance work, or other income-generating opportunities. These figures reflect ESPACT's broader programmes and should not be attributed exclusively to Espact Digital Buddy. Early validation: Espact Digital Buddy has an initial pilot database of 205 users, with more than 89% positive feedback reported. Expected impact: The platform aims to support an initial rollout in Nigeria , reach 10,000 or more users in its first 12 months after launch, and contribute to a longer-term ambition of reaching five million young people by 2030. Expected outcomes include improved digital competencies, stronger career readiness, increased access to employment and entrepreneurship, and more sustainable income opportunities. These are targets, not yet demonstrated platform-wide results. The solution contributes to SDG 4 (Quality Education), SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), and SDG 1 (No Poverty), with gender inclusion supporting SDG 5 (Gender Equality). The solution was recognized by UNITAR as top 25 digital solution promoting livelihoods and employment in Africa, selected by UNICEF AI Accelerator Programme and African Impact Initiative in Toronto.
Key technologies: Artificial Intelligence (AI): Personalized learning recommendations, career guidance, skills-gap identification, and matching between user profiles and relevant economic opportunities. Digital learning technologies: Online learning resources, interactive videos, quizzes, role-play exercises, practical assignments, and competency-based assessments. Digital identity and verification: Registration and verification processes that support user identification and more trustworthy interactions within the platform. Data analytics and feedback systems: Monitoring learner progress, assessing engagement, gathering user feedback, and improving the relevance of learning recommendations and opportunity matching. Web and mobile technologies: Planned digital delivery through web and mobile platforms to broaden access across different devices and user contexts. Cybersecurity and digital safety education: Learning resources designed to improve users' awareness of online risks, privacy, fraud, discrimination, and safer participation in digital work. The platform is being developed, and the final technical architecture and implementation of individual features will depend on the development phase and available resources.
Unique Characteristics: ESPACT Digital Buddy differentiates itself by addressing the often-overlooked transition between acquiring digital skills and earning an income. Rather than operating solely as an online learning platform or job board, it is designed to integrate learning, career development, mentorship, and economic opportunity within one ecosystem. Its principal innovations include: - Learning-to-earning integration: Connecting practical learning and competency assessments with employment, internships, freelance work, and entrepreneurship opportunities. - AI-powered personalization: Adapting learning pathways and career recommendations to individual skills, interests, progress, and labour-market needs. - Human and AI support: Combining AI-enabled guidance with human mentors, tutors, and supervisors to provide more practical and accountable support. - Feedback-driven improvement: Using learner feedback and engagement patterns to refine recommendations and improve the relevance of learning pathways. - Women-centred and inclusive design: Addressing barriers such as limited internet access, shared devices, financial constraints, caregiving responsibilities, and low confidence through flexible and accessible delivery approaches. - Trust and digital safety: Incorporating user verification, cybersecurity education, and awareness of online fraud, privacy risks, and discrimination. - Scalable partnership model: Connecting training providers, employers, mentors, technology developers, and community organizations to strengthen the pathway from education to economic participation. The combination of AI-enabled personalization, human support, inclusion-focused design, and access to economic opportunities positions Digital Buddy as a practical approach to improving the conversion of digital skills into sustainable livelihoods.
Sustainable Change: ESPACT Digital Buddy has the potential to shift digital skills development from a training-centred model towards an integrated, outcomes-oriented approach in which learning is directly connected to employment, entrepreneurship, and income generation. At the individual level, the platform can help young people and women identify career pathways, build market-relevant competencies, access mentorship, and pursue suitable economic opportunities. At the institutional level, it can strengthen collaboration between educators, employers, civil society organizations, technology providers, and public-sector stakeholders. As the platform grows, aggregated and responsibly managed data on skills gaps, learner progress, employer demand, and opportunity outcomes could help training providers and partners improve programme design and make skills development more responsive to labour-market needs. The model is designed for replication across African countries through localized learning resources, regional employer networks, and partnerships with local institutions. Beginning with Nigeria and Kenya, the approach could be adapted to different languages, economic contexts, and labour markets before expanding further across Africa and into other regions. Potential longer-term effects include improved youth employability, stronger women's economic participation, increased digital entrepreneurship, more inclusive access to decent work, and reduced mismatch between training investments and labour-market demand. By supporting more people to move from learning into earning, the platform could contribute to inclusive economic growth and progress towards SDGs 4, 5, 8, and 1. Realizing this potential will require sustainable financing, reliable technology infrastructure, strong employer participation, responsible AI governance, user protection, and rigorous measurement of employment and income outcomes.
Funding Sources: ESPACT Digital Buddy has emerged from ESPACT's wider digital skills, technology, and employability work. The initiative has benefited from the experience, networks, and programme knowledge developed through ESPACT's existing activities. Espact Digital Buddy has also received early validation through a pilot user base and feedback. The platform is currently being developed, and additional funding is required to complete development, strengthen the technology infrastructure, support pilot implementation, expand user acquisition, and establish employer and institutional partnerships. The intended funding model includes prospective grants, innovation and accelerator programmes, corporate social responsibility partnerships, development-sector funding, and strategic partnerships. Potential future revenue streams may include paid learning services, employer partnerships, and other sustainable service models.

Title: Circular Intelligence: AI for Smarter Waste Recovery
Subtitle: An AI-enabled solution in development to improve waste classification, collection planning, recycling, and resource recovery for a more circular and sustainable industrial future.
Problem Statement: Waste management and recycling operations face challenges including inadequate waste data, inconsistent source segregation, inefficient collection planning, and limited connections between waste generators and recycling markets. These challenges can increase operational costs, reduce material recovery, and leave valuable recyclable and organic resources underutilised. Many small waste operators and businesses also lack affordable digital tools to support data-driven decisions. In Nigeria, there is an opportunity to apply accessible AI and digital technologies to improve waste visibility, resource recovery, and circular-economy operations. Circular Intelligence aims to address these challenges through an AI-enabled approach currently in early development.
Solution Overview: Circular Intelligence is an early-stage solution being developed by Sustainable Africa Solutions Ltd to support smarter waste management and resource recovery in Nigeria. The concept combines digital data collection, existing AI tools, and operational dashboards to help waste generators and operators make better-informed decisions. Potential functions include AI-assisted waste classification, recording and estimating recyclable and organic material volumes, supporting collection planning, and tracking recovered resources. The solution is intended to help markets, businesses, communities, waste operators, and recycling enterprises improve operational visibility and identify opportunities to convert waste into useful materials. The initiative aligns with the principles of the circular economy by promoting resource efficiency, reuse, recycling, and responsible waste management. It also aims to create inclusive green-economy opportunities for young people, women, and persons with disabilities. SAS Ltd is currently at the early-development stage and uses existing AI tools in some operations. The integrated platform and its proposed capabilities have not yet been fully developed or validated. The next phase will focus on defining a minimum viable product, identifying technical and implementation partners, and conducting a pilot to assess feasibility, usability, waste recovery performance, and potential environmental and socioeconomic benefits.
Solution Provider(s): Sustainable Africa Solutions Ltd (SAS Ltd) — Lead organisation; an early-stage Nigerian sustainability enterprise focused on waste management, recycling, resource recovery, and circular-economy solutions. Technical AI development partners, waste collection operators, recycling businesses, and pilot-site organisations are potential partners to be identified and engaged as the solution develops. No formal external implementation partners have yet been confirmed for this specific solution.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3 month
Desired impact: The main objective of Circular Intelligence is to explore how accessible AI and digital technologies can improve waste classification, collection planning, material recovery, and circular-economy operations in Nigeria. The solution aims to help waste generators, collection operators, and recycling businesses make better-informed decisions, reduce avoidable waste, improve resource efficiency, and identify opportunities to convert recyclable and organic materials into valuable resources. It also seeks to create inclusive green-economy opportunities for young people, women, and persons with disabilities. As the solution is still in early development, quantified environmental and socioeconomic impacts have not yet been demonstrated. During pilot implementation, we intend to establish baseline measurements and track the volume of waste collected and recovered, recycling rates, collection efficiency, participating businesses, jobs and livelihoods supported, and estimated greenhouse-gas emissions avoided using an appropriate methodology.
Key technologies: The current approach uses existing AI tools in some operations, alongside digital tools for information processing and planning. The proposed Circular Intelligence solution is expected to explore AI-assisted waste classification, data analytics for estimating waste volumes, and digital dashboards for monitoring collection and resource recovery. AI-based forecasting and image recognition may be considered during development, subject to technical feasibility, data availability, and testing. The solution is not currently presented as an integrated AI platform, and technologies such as IoT sensors, robotics, blockchain, and digital twins have not been confirmed as part of the current system. Technology selection will be guided by affordability, reliability, accessibility, and suitability for Nigerian waste-management operations.
Unique Characteristics: Circular Intelligence aims to make AI-assisted waste management more accessible to waste operators, small businesses, markets, and recycling enterprises in Nigeria. Its distinctive approach is to connect waste data, collection planning, and resource recovery within a practical circular-economy model. Rather than focusing only on waste disposal, the solution seeks to improve visibility into available materials and support decisions that enable reuse, recycling, and recovery of value from waste. It will explore affordable, adaptable digital tools suited to resource-constrained settings, with potential to support small and medium-sized enterprises. The solution is currently in early development. Its differentiating features will be refined through technical development, engagement with prospective users, and pilot testing rather than assumed to be proven capabilities.
Sustainable Change: Circular Intelligence could contribute to systemic change by helping shift waste management in Nigeria from predominantly disposal-oriented practices towards data-informed resource recovery and circular-economy operations. Title: THUMBI: Teach by Hand, Delegate by Voice
Subtitle: A low-cost dual-arm robot small workshops can teach by demonstration in minutes and command by voice - no programmers, no cloud - built from open-source arms at a fraction of a cobot's cost.
Problem Statement: Small and medium workshops in developing and middle-income economies are largely locked out of industrial automation: industrial cobots and vision-guided cells cost more than an SME can justify, demand specialist programmers the workshop does not have, and depend on cloud connectivity that is unreliable or unavailable. The result is that routine handling, kitting, light assembly and sorting stay manual, data-driven quality control does not reach these firms, and workers have no path to upskill into roles that sit alongside automation.
Solution Overview: THUMBI is a dual-arm industrial robot purpose-built to be teachable and deployable where resources, skills and connectivity are constrained. Hardware: two self-assembled open-source SO-100/SO-101 robotic arms with RGB/RGB-D cameras and soft grippers, delivering a working cobot-class platform at a tiny fraction of a conventional industrial cobot's cost. Learning: an operator teaches a task by hand using leader-follower demonstrations; the robot learns the skill through imitation learning (ACT, diffusion policy) and a small on-device vision-language-action model (SmolVLA). Interface: the same robot is then commanded by spoken instruction - a small on-device model maps a spoken command to a learned skill, so a workshop operator with no programming background and no cloud account can deploy and re-deploy the robot. The same platform retrains by demonstration for new tasks: kitting and light assembly, waste sorting (BEEAH Future Pioneers entry), and assistive tasks. Perception, inference and control all run locally on-device, so the robot works offline and keeps data on-site. Safety: low operating speed, soft grippers, force and software limits, and an e-stop. Partnerships and collaboration: THUMBI is currently a solo-founder project with no formal commercial partners; the founder maintains research exchanges with robot-learning groups at TU Delft, University of Edinburgh, Idiap and Stanford that inform the learning stack. No customer pilots have been executed - the solution is at working-prototype maturity and has been externally evaluated through competition entries rather than commercial deployments. the
Solution Provider(s): No formal partners at this stage. THUMBI is developed by a solo founder (Ribotech, Ras Al Khaimah, UAE). The learning stack and vision research inform the project through research exchanges with groups at TU Delft, University of Edinburgh, Idiap and Stanford; none of these are formal project partners.at i
Implementation location(s): N/A - THUMBI is at working-prototype maturity and has not yet been deployed in a customer site.
Implementation timeline(s): N/A - not yet implemented.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Approximately 3-6 months to deploy and pilot in a new location, covering on-site assembly/integration of the dual-arm platform, collection of a small set of leader-follower demonstrations for the target tasks, on-device training of the imitation-learning policy and on-device voice-to-skill mapping, and acceptance testing with the host workshop's operators. No cloud provisioning, no external model hosting and no specialist programming staff are required.
Desired impact: Main objective: put deployable industrial automation within the reach of small and medium workshops in developing and middle-income economies - at a tiny fraction of a conventional cobot's cost, without requiring programmers, cloud accounts or reliable internet. Expected impact (directional, not customer-validated; THUMBI is at working-prototype maturity with no deployed customer sites): (a) economic - an SME that can afford the platform can automate repetitive handling/kitting/light-assembly tasks that currently demand fully manual labour, freeing labour for higher-value work; (b) skills - the teach-by-demonstration plus voice-command interface turns experienced workshop operators into 'robot teachers,' upskilling the existing workforce rather than displacing it, and the low-cost open-source hardware lowers the barrier to entry for technical talent in constrained regions; (c) environmental - a waste-sorting application (BEEAH Future Pioneers entry) enables hands-off sorting that increases material recovery and reduces landfill/missorted waste; (d) data and sovereignty - perception, inference and control run locally on-device, so operational data never leaves the workshop and the robot works in locations where cloud connectivity is weak or prohibited. The solution aligns with SDG 8 (decent work and productivity via upskilling rather than displacement), SDG 9 (industrial innovation and infrastructure via affordable, open-source automation) and SDG 12 (responsible consumption and production via waste sorting and more efficient resource use), and supports Global Digital Compact Objective 2 by expanding SME inclusion in the digital economy.duct
Key technologies: Robotics and hardware: two self-assembled open-source SO-100/SO-101 dual-arm platforms with RGB/RGB-D cameras and soft grippers. Learning stack: imitation learning via behaviour cloning (Action Chunking with Transformers, ACT), diffusion policy and a small on-device vision-language-action model (SmolVLA). Interaction: leader-follower (teach-by-demonstration) data collection for training, and an on-device speech-to-skill mapping that lets an operator command a learned skill by voice. Perception and control: on-device RGB/RGB-D vision for state estimation, local inference and local control loops - no cloud compute. Safety: low operating speed, soft grippers, force and software limits, and an e-stop.te.
Unique Characteristics: What makes THUMBI distinctive is the combination of who it is for, how it is taught and where it runs. (1) Accessibility of use: a workshop operator teaches a task by guiding the robot's arms by hand (leader-follower demonstration) in minutes and then commands the robot by speaking - there are no programmers, no cloud accounts and no model-serving infrastructure to manage. (2) Accessibility of cost: the hardware is built from open-source SO-100/SO-101 arms that a team can self-assemble, delivering cobot-class dual-arm capability at a tiny fraction of a conventional industrial cobot's cost. (3) Edge-only operation: all perception, inference and control run locally on-device, so the robot operates where cloud connectivity is weak, unreliable or prohibited, and operational data never leaves the workshop. (4) Task flexibility through retraining by demonstration: the same platform can be retrained by hand for kitting/light assembly, waste sorting (BEEAH Future Pioneers entry) or assistive tasks without a new codebase. (5) Delivery model: an open, low-cost stack built around established imitation-learning methods (ACT, diffusion policy) and a small vision-language-action model (SmolVLA), combined with safety through low speed, soft grippers, force/software limits and an e-stop - a defensible, safe platform aimed at the smallest workshops rather than flagship factory floors.arou
Sustainable Change: THUMBI's potential for systemic change comes from changing the economics and the skills dynamics of industrial automation, not just shipping another robot. Because the platform is open-source, low-cost and self-assemblable, it can be replicated across developing and middle-income economies by local technical talent without depending on an import chain of expensive proprietary cobots - a step toward localising advanced-manufacturing capability where it is most needed. Because it is taught by demonstration and commanded by voice, it creates a new skill pathway: experienced workshop operators become 'robot teachers,' and the same workflow is reusable in technical and vocational education, accelerating the supply of robotics-capable workers. Because every stack - perception, inference, control - runs on-device, it offers a template for industrial AI that respects data sovereignty and operates where cloud infrastructure is weak, a model that can be adapted to other constrained-sector use cases (food processing, light textiles, recycling, assistive manufacturing). Follow-on effects of a successful pilot include: replication of the hardware by local assemblers, curriculum and training modules around teach-by-demonstration, and the emergence of a low-cost robotics applications ecosystem for SMEs. At current prototype maturity, none of these are realised; the pathway depends on reaching a pilot and demonstrating reliability in a real workshop. (Notably, the project has been externally evaluated through the IEEE Global Robot Championship Malta Robot Arm AI ChynChallenge (NeurIPS 2026), where a policy was submitted in October 2026, providing credible third-party validation of the learning stack even though no commercial pilot has been executed.) pa

Title: Therm IA
Subtitle: ThermIA is an AI driven project designed to estimate industrial waste heat losses and identify more efficient heat recovery solutions. By analyzing thermal energy losses and suggesting optimized recovery pathways, ThermIA aims to improve industrial energy efficiency, reduce energy waste, and support energy transition and decarbonization goals.
Problem Statement: Industries lose significant amounts of thermal energy through inefficient processes and unrecovered waste heat, increasing energy consumption, operating costs, and CO₂ emissions. However, identifying where heat is being lost and determining the most efficient recovery pathway can be complex. ThermIA addresses this challenge by using AI to estimate industrial heat losses and identify optimized heat recovery opportunities, helping industries improve energy efficiency, reduce waste, and accelerate decarbonization.
Solution Overview: How the solution works ThermIA is an AI supported solution designed to help industries identify thermal energy losses and determine promising heat recovery opportunities, it uses industrial data, such as temperatures, energy consumption, operating conditions, and available process information, to estimate waste heat and identify where recovery could be most effective. The system then evaluates potential recovery pathways based on energy efficiency, technical feasibility, and expected environmental benefits. The goal is to help industries make data-informed decisions, reduce energy waste, lower operating costs, and decrease CO₂ emissions. ⁠Methodologies and technologies used ThermIA combines artificial intelligence, data analysis, thermal energy assessment, and industrial energy-efficiency principles. Potential technologies include machine-learning models for estimating heat losses, thermal energy balances to understand industrial processes, and optimization methods to compare recovery scenarios. Where suitable, sensor data and industrial monitoring systems could improve the accuracy of estimates. The proposed solution would be validated through industrial case studies and comparisons with measured or calculated energy performance. Partnerships and collaboration models ThermIA could be developed through collaboration between industrial companies, universities, energy engineers, AI specialists, and research centers. Industrial partners would provide process data and help identify real operational needs, while academic and technical partners would support model development, testing, and validation. Pilot projects with selected factories could demonstrate feasibility and measure potential energy and emissions savings. Future partnerships with energy-efficiency organizations and public institutions could support wider adoption across Moroccan industries.
Solution Provider(s): We won the gold prize in Rally AI futere lab 2026, it is a programe by the moroccan Ministry of Digital Transition and Administrative Reform to support smart energy solutions and other AI supported solutions.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: We estimate that deploying and piloting ThermIA in a new industrial location would require approximately 3–6 months
Desired impact: main objectives: ThermIA aims to help industries identify and quantify thermal energy losses, optimize waste heat recovery pathways, improve energy efficiency, and reduce operating costs and greenhouse gas emissions. By combining AI driven analysis with industrial energy assessments, the solution seeks to support more informed decisions about recovering and reusing otherwise wasted thermal energy. Expected impact: ThermIA is expected to reduce avoidable energy waste, lower industrial energy demand, and contribute to decarbonization. Its impact will be assessed during pilot projects by measuring recoverable heat, energy savings (kWh), associated CO₂ emissions avoided (tonnes of CO₂ equivalent), and potential cost reductions. It may also support the development of green engineering and AI-related skills and create future opportunities in energy-efficiency services. As ThermIA is still at the development stage, these impacts have not yet been demonstrated, and quantified targets will be established after collecting baseline data from a pilot industrial facility.
Key technologies: ThermIA primarily relies on Artificial Intelligence (AI) and machine learning to estimate industrial thermal energy losses, analyze process data, and identify promising heat recovery opportunities. It combines thermal energy modeling and data analytics to assess heat flows, compare recovery scenarios, and evaluate potential energy savings and emissions reductions. Where available, IoT sensors and industrial monitoring systems could provide real-time data on temperatures, energy consumption, and operating conditions to improve the accuracy of the analysis. In future development, a digital twin could be integrated to simulate industrial processes and compare different heat recovery strategies before implementation. These technologies would support data-driven decisions, improve industrial energy efficiency, and contribute to decarbonization. The solution is currently at the development stage, and the integration of these technologies will depend on data availability and pilot requirements.
Unique Characteristics: ThermIA’s distinctive feature is its focus on using AI not only to estimate industrial heat losses but also to identify and compare potential heat recovery pathways tailored to each facility’s operating conditions. Rather than relying solely on general energy audits, the proposed solution aims to transform available industrial data into actionable recommendations that help decision-makers prioritize technically feasible and economically attractive recovery options. Its modular approach could allow adaptation to different industrial sectors and facility sizes. ThermIA also aims to connect engineering expertise with AI-driven analysis through collaboration between industrial companies, researchers, and technology specialists. Future development could include simulation tools to assess recovery scenarios before implementation. The project is currently at the development stage, and its accuracy, cost effectiveness, and advantages over existing energy assessment methods will need to be validated through pilot testing.
Sustainable Change: ThermIA could contribute to systemic change by making industrial energy efficiency and waste heat recovery more accessible, measurable, and data-driven. By helping industries identify opportunities to recover energy that would otherwise be lost, the solution could encourage a shift from energy-intensive practices toward more efficient and lower-carbon industrial operations. Its modular design could enable replication across different factories and industrial sectors in Morocco, with potential expansion to other countries facing similar energy challenges. Partnerships with universities, research centers, industrial operators, and energy-efficiency organizations could support knowledge sharing, technical validation, and wider adoption. Over time, aggregated pilot results could help demonstrate the economic and environmental value of industrial heat recovery, encourage investment in cleaner technologies, and inform broader industrial decarbonization strategies.

Title: SymbIA: AI-Enabled Industrial Traceability and Data Integrity
Subtitle: A digital framework for traceable industrial circularity, integrating primary observations and data verification to strengthen environmental monitoring, material traceability and sustainability reporting.
Problem Statement: Industrial circularity and environmental performance are difficult to verify when data on waste flows, material recovery and industrial processes are fragmented, manually reported or lack reliable traceability. This limits transparency, weakens the evidence available for sustainability reporting, and makes it harder for manufacturers, recyclers and regulators to assess resource efficiency and environmental outcomes. Small and medium-sized enterprises often lack affordable digital infrastructure to collect, connect and verify this information across operational processes and value chains.
Solution Overview: SymbIA is a proposed digital framework for strengthening industrial traceability, environmental monitoring and the integrity of sustainability data. Its architecture combines Primary Integrity Observation (PIO), which is intended to capture evidence from industrial operations through appropriate data sources such as sensors, cameras, operational records and field observations, with an Integrity Verification System (IVS), designed to check data consistency, preserve traceability and support auditable reporting. The framework is intended to connect observations, operational records and material-flow information into structured, traceable evidence that can support waste management, material recovery, circularity metrics and environmental performance monitoring. Depending on the pilot use case, the architecture could integrate IoT devices, cloud-based data management, digital evidence logs and analytical tools. AI-assisted anomaly detection, data classification and decision support could be explored as development components, subject to technical validation. The proposed methodology consists of defining an industrial use case, mapping its data flows and verification requirements, designing a minimum technological core, and validating it through a pilot with an industrial or recycling operator. Potential collaboration models include technology developers, manufacturers, recyclers, environmental service providers and research or implementation partners. SymbIA is currently at the design and methodological validation stage; the proposed capabilities have not yet been demonstrated through a deployed prototype.
Solution Provider(s): Solution lead: SymbIA project founder and initiator, responsible for the conceptual architecture, industrial use-case definition, traceability methodology and pilot design. Technology development partners, industrial operators, recycling companies and environmental service providers are potential collaborators to be identified and confirmed. No formal implementation partners are currently confirmed.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Approximately 4–6 months from project kick-off, subject to funding, confirmation of an industrial pilot partner, data access and completion of the minimum technological core. This period includes use-case definition, system development, integration, testing and initial pilot validation.
Desired impact: SymbIA aims to improve the traceability, verification and reliability of industrial environmental data, particularly in circular economy and waste recovery processes. Its main objectives are to connect primary operational observations with structured records, strengthen data integrity, and support more transparent monitoring of material flows and environmental performance. Expected impacts include improved traceability of recovered materials, more reliable sustainability reporting, earlier identification of data inconsistencies, and better-informed industrial decisions. In the longer term, the framework could help industrial operators and recyclers identify resource-efficiency opportunities and improve the monitoring of waste recovery and environmental outcomes. As SymbIA is currently at the concept stage, no operational impact has yet been measured or independently validated. Quantitative indicators for a future pilot could include the percentage of material flows with traceable evidence, completeness of operational records, time required to prepare reports, number of data inconsistencies detected, and the accuracy of recorded recovery volumes. Baselines and targets would be established with the pilot partner.
Key technologies: SymbIA's proposed architecture combines the following technology components: - IoT and digital data acquisition: potential integration of sensors, cameras, operational records and field observations to capture primary evidence from industrial processes. - Data integration and cloud infrastructure: structured collection and organization of operational, material-flow and environmental information. - Data integrity and verification mechanisms: the proposed Primary Integrity Observation (PIO) and Integrity Verification System (IVS) components are intended to support traceability, consistency checks and auditable evidence records. - AI-assisted analytics (planned): potential use of machine learning for anomaly detection, data classification and decision support, subject to development and validation. - Digital reporting and monitoring: indicators and structured reports to support circularity monitoring and environmental performance assessment. These are proposed technology components rather than a description of an existing deployed system. The final technology stack and any AI models will be selected and validated during development of the minimum technological core.
Unique Characteristics: SymbIA's proposed differentiator is its focus on the integrity and traceability of industrial environmental data, rather than data collection alone. Its PIO–IVS architecture is designed to link primary observations with verification procedures and structured records, creating a clearer evidence trail for material flows, waste recovery and environmental reporting. The framework is intended to be modular and adaptable to different industrial and recycling contexts, with a minimum technological core that can be tailored to a specific use case before scaling. This approach could help organizations improve the consistency and auditability of sustainability information and identify gaps between reported activities and recorded evidence. Unlike a fully developed commercial platform, SymbIA is currently a concept-stage initiative. Its novelty, technical feasibility, performance and cost-effectiveness must be demonstrated through prototype development and a real-world pilot. No proprietary AI model or validated performance advantage is claimed at this stage.
Sustainable Change: SymbIA could contribute to systemic change by providing a modular and replicable framework for improving the traceability, verification and reliability of industrial environmental data. By linking primary observations with structured records and verification procedures, the approach could help establish more consistent evidence practices for material flows, waste recovery and sustainability reporting. Initially validated in one industrial use case, the framework could be adapted to other sectors, including recycling, plastics recovery, used tyres and other circular economy value chains. Over time, replication could support greater interoperability between industrial operators, recyclers and environmental service providers, helping organizations compare performance and identify opportunities for resource efficiency. Its longer-term systemic potential lies in making reliable environmental evidence more accessible to small and medium-sized enterprises, supporting better-informed decisions and strengthening accountability across industrial value chains. Reusable technical components, common data structures and documented verification methods could facilitate adoption in different regions. This potential remains prospective. SymbIA has not yet been piloted, and replication, adoption, measurable environmental benefits and long-term sustainability will depend on successful prototype development, validation with industrial partners, and evidence of technical and economic feasibility.
Funding Sources: SymbIA has been developed to date through founder-led conceptual work and the preparation of its methodological and technical architecture. No external funding has been secured for the development or implementation of the solution. The project is currently seeking funding and strategic partnerships to develop its minimum technological core and validate it through an industrial pilot.
Testimonials and Endorsements: N/A — SymbIA is currently at the concept stage and has not yet been validated through an operational pilot. No formal testimonials or third-party recommendations are currently available.

Summary: SymbIA proposes an observation and verification framework for industrial circularity data. The conceptual split is sensible; with no build, no partner and only a social page, it cannot be assessed as a solution.

Title: Ghost Data Still Exists: Autonomous AI Agent for Data Deletion Audit
Subtitle: Autonomous AI agent that audits industrial ecosystems to detect, track, and ensure the effective exclusion of sensitive data residue.
Problem Statement: As industries integrate AI, cloud, and big data ecosystems, improper data retention—known as Ghost Data—becomes a critical risk. Even after formal data deletion requests, remnants lurk in processing pipelines, caches, log files, and AI model training sets. This failure exposes industrial companies to severe risks of privacy breaches (non-compliance with LGPD/GDPR), intellectual property leaks, cybersecurity risks, and a loss of regulatory trust in the global market.
Solution Overview: How the Solution Works: Ghost Data Still Exists acts as a continuous autonomous auditor. It scans storage layers, data pipelines, and real-time processing logs to track the data lifecycle. When a deletion is executed, the agent validates whether the digital footprint has been entirely removed, generating compliance reports and auditable digital certificates of elimination. Methodologies and Technologies Used: Autonomous AI agent-based development (agent orchestration architectures and LLMs), real-time data pipeline analysis, integration via RESTful APIs, log parsing techniques, and cryptographic data integrity verification. Partnership and Collaboration Models: B2B/Enterprise model integrable into industrial infrastructures and cloud ecosystems. Strategic partnerships with innovation ecosystems and incubators (such as MeuLab-Tech), global technological development programmes (UNDP / FTL), and cloud service and data governance providers.
Solution Provider(s): MeuLab-Tech (Startup / Software and AI Solutions Development Lab), UNDP Angola - Frontier Tech Leaders Programme (International Organisation / Technology and Innovation Leadership Programme).
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 2 to 3 months (estimated time for API integration, mapping of industrial partner data pipelines, and auditor agent testing and validation phase).
Desired impact: Up to 80% reduction in manual data privacy and compliance auditing time. Proactive elimination of regulatory fine risks due to improper data retention. Significant increase in investor and partner confidence by ensuring large-scale industrial data protection.
Key technologies: Artificial Intelligence (Autonomous AI Agents, LLM Orchestration and Prompt Engineering), Microservices Architecture (Python / Node.js), Database and Log Management (PostgreSQL, Vector Databases), Cloud APIs and Cryptographic Auditing Tools.
Unique Characteristics: Unlike traditional data governance tools that merely check static database tables, Ghost Data Still Exists employs autonomous AI agents capable of reasoning and dynamically inspecting the entire data lifecycle—including temporary files, unstructured logs, and AI training pipelines. Additionally, it introduces a continuous, automated validation model ("Audit-as-a-Service"), enabling industries in emerging and global markets to achieve high compliance standards with low implementation complexity.
Sustainable Change: The solution contributes to the consolidation of a global culture of ethical and transparent AI. By solving the Ghost Data challenge, the tool paves the way for industries of all sizes to adopt advanced digital ecosystems and AI models without the fear of regulatory infringements or data leaks. In the long term, the architecture can be replicated and standardised as an essential governance module for any industrial digital infrastructure, promoting a safer, more resilient, and auditable global data ecosystem.
Funding Sources: Self-financing and Bootstrap (Own Development / MeuLab-Tech Startup), supported by the innovation and technical skills development ecosystem in Artificial Intelligence and Data Science acceleration programmes/hackathons (such as the technological training programmes driven by UNDP Angola's Frontier Tech Leaders initiative).
Testimonials and Endorsements: The 'Ghost Data Still Exists' approach addresses a critical and often overlooked gap in AI and data engineering ecosystems: the auditable certainty of sensitive data residue elimination. Presenting solutions of such technical maturity demonstrates the immense potential of tech talent in emerging markets to solve global compliance challenges. — Evaluation Team/AI Engineering Mentors in the HackerRank Orchestrate Challenge (October 2026).
Primary thematic focus area: Industrial AI Models and Intelligent Decision-Making
