Title: Airmesh AI
Subtitle: AI-powered multi-zone climate control for healthier indoor environments and more energy-efficient cooling in schools and buildings.
Problem Statement: Buildings are commonly cooled and ventilated using centralized or limited sensing that assumes relatively uniform indoor conditions. In practice, temperature, CO₂, particulate matter and humidity can differ significantly across zones. This can leave some occupants in poor conditions while energy is simultaneously spent conditioning areas that do not require the same response. In hot climates, where cooling represents a major share of building electricity demand, more intelligent and localized control can contribute to energy efficiency and climate resilience.
Solution Overview: .AirMesh AI is an AI-powered, multi-zone indoor climate management system designed to make ventilation and cooling more responsive, predictive and energy-aware. Distributed environmental sensor nodes monitor CO₂, PM2.5, temperature and humidity across different areas of an indoor space. Instead of assuming that conditions are identical throughout a room, AirMesh identifies local differences between zones. Sensor data is analysed by a predictive machine-learning system that evaluates recent environmental trends and identifies developing deterioration approximately 15 minutes ahead. The AI provides a recommended response to a local master controller. The controller remains responsible for validating the recommendation using predefined safety and fallback rules before activating or adjusting ventilation. Sensors then continue monitoring conditions to determine whether the intervention improved the environment. The overall operating concept is: Sense → Predict → Validate → Act → Verify A cloud-connected AirMesh dashboard allows users to view zone conditions, environmental trends, system status and AI recommendations from a single interface. AirMesh currently includes the multi-zone system architecture, sensor-network simulation, machine-learning model, cloud backend, dashboard and 3D device concept. The ML prototype was developed and evaluated using real university lecture-hall environmental data containing CO₂, PM2.5, temperature and humidity measurements. Prototype evaluation demonstrated the ability to identify near-term environmental deterioration, achieving 62.1% deterioration recall at an approximately 15-minute prediction horizon. AirMesh is designed as a retrofit-oriented solution that can complement existing ventilation and cooling infrastructure rather than requiring complete HVAC replacement. The initial use case is classrooms, with potential adaptation to universities, offices, healthcare facilities and other multi-zone buildings. Collaboration model: AirMesh seeks pilot collaboration with schools and universities; technical collaboration with HVAC, facility-management and building-automation companies; and research partnerships for independent energy and indoor-environment validation.
Solution Provider(s): No formal external implementation partners are currently confirmed. AirMesh AI is presently being developed by the founding team, with future collaboration planned with schools and universities for pilot deployment, HVAC and facility-management companies for building integration, and academic or climate-energy researchers for independent validation.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Approximately 3–6 months, depending on pilot-site access, hardware procurement, local integration requirements, approvals, and coordination with the building or facility partner.
Desired impact: The main objective of AirMesh AI is to make indoor climate control more predictive, localized and energy-aware by combining multi-zone environmental sensing with machine-learning-based decision support. The solution is designed to: Detect developing deterioration in CO₂, PM2.5, temperature and humidity across different indoor zones. Predict near-term environmental deterioration before conditions worsen. Enable a Master ESP32 controller to validate AI recommendations and activate ventilation only when required. Reduce unnecessary whole-room ventilation and cooling by supporting more targeted responses. Improve indoor environmental conditions for occupants while creating a pathway toward lower building energy demand. Provide a scalable retrofit architecture that can later be adapted from classrooms to offices, universities and other multi-zone buildings. At the current prototype stage, demonstrated impact is primarily technical. The ML system operates at an approximately 15-minute prediction horizon and achieved 62.1% deterioration recall in prototype evaluation using real university lecture-hall environmental data. The system architecture, sensor-network simulation, cloud API and monitoring dashboard have also been developed. AirMesh has not yet completed a physical building pilot, so we do not currently claim quantified energy savings, GHG-emission reductions or health outcomes. The next validation step is to measure, in a real pilot, changes in ventilation/cooling runtime, electricity consumption, indoor environmental conditions and associated CO₂-equivalent emissions compared with conventional operation.
Key technologies: AirMesh AI combines: Artificial Intelligence / Machine Learning – predictive analysis of environmental trends and near-term deterioration. Internet of Things (IoT) – distributed environmental sensing across multiple indoor zones. Environmental sensing technology – measurement of CO₂, PM2.5, temperature and humidity. Embedded control systems – a local master controller validates AI recommendations and manages physical response. Cloud computing and backend software – supports AI processing, monitoring and data exchange. Digital dashboard – visualizes multi-zone conditions, environmental trends, system status and AI recommendations. Automated climate-control logic – supports targeted ventilation based on sensor conditions and predictive analysis. Closed-loop verification – sensor readings after intervention are used to determine whether conditions improved. Together, these technologies create an adaptive: Sense → Predict → Validate → Act → Verify indoor climate-management process.
Unique Characteristics: AirMesh AI is distinctive because it integrates multi-zone sensing, predictive AI, local control validation and closed-loop verification within a retrofit-oriented building climate system. Its key differentiators include: Multi-zone intelligence: Rather than relying on a single measurement point, AirMesh monitors conditions across multiple areas of the same room or building space. Predictive rather than purely reactive operation: Machine learning analyses recent environmental trends to identify developing deterioration before conditions significantly worsen. Human-controlled safety architecture: AI recommendations are validated by a local controller using predefined safety and fallback logic before any physical response occurs. Targeted ventilation: Responses can be based on conditions where intervention is required rather than assuming all areas need the same treatment. Closed-loop verification: The system continues monitoring after intervention to determine whether the response improved environmental conditions. Retrofit-oriented approach: AirMesh is intended to add intelligence to existing cooling and ventilation infrastructure rather than requiring complete replacement. Modular scalability: The sensing architecture can be expanded according to building size and zoning requirements. Unified dashboard: Operators can view environmental conditions, AI recommendations and system status through one interface. The broader innovation is the transition from passive monitoring and uniform climate control toward predictive, localized and energy-aware building management.
Sustainable Change: AirMesh AI could contribute to broader change by helping shift indoor climate management from uniform, reactive operation toward distributed, predictive and energy-aware control. The architecture is modular, allowing the same basic approach to be replicated across different building types. A classroom may require only a small number of sensing zones, while universities, offices, healthcare facilities and commercial buildings could deploy larger networks using the same operating model. Its retrofit-first design is important for scalability. Instead of requiring building owners to replace complete HVAC systems, AirMesh is intended to function as an additional intelligence and sensing layer alongside existing infrastructure. This can lower barriers to adoption and create opportunities for deployment through existing HVAC contractors, facility-management companies and building-automation providers. If physical pilots validate its energy and environmental benefits, AirMesh could help building operators move away from fixed schedules and single-point sensing toward data-driven, localized climate management. The technology is also designed using widely accessible sensing, AI and cloud technologies, allowing adaptation to different climates, building types and regional requirements. AirMesh therefore has the potential to scale through replication, retrofit deployment, research cooperation and industry partnerships, moving from classrooms into broader commercial and institutional building infrastructure.
Funding Sources: AirMesh AI has been self-funded by the founding team to date. Development costs for prototyping, software development, cloud services, simulation, dashboard development, 3D design and project presentation have been covered directly by the founders. The solution has not yet received external grant funding, investment capital, commercial revenue or paid pilot funding. Future funding is expected to come through a combination of pilot partnerships, climate and innovation grants, strategic industry collaboration, and eventually revenue from hardware deployment, integration and recurring software/support services.
Testimonials and Endorsements: No formal beneficiary testimonials have been collected yet, as AirMesh AI is currently at the prototype stage and has not undergone a physical classroom pilot. However, the project received external recognition through its selection as a research poster at the Abu Dhabi Climate Solutions Summit 2026, hosted by Khalifa University, where the AirMesh AI concept and technical approach were presented. The Summit brought together researchers, industry representatives, policymakers, investors and young innovators, and more than 100 innovative research posters were accepted as part of the program. Title: BEL AVENIR Community Intelligence AI
Subtitle: An AI-powered data and decision-support platform helping communities, local organisations and development actors turn community information into actionable insights for resilient and inclusive local development.
Problem Statement: Conflict-affected and displaced communities in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo face fragmented information, limited access to reliable local data and weak mechanisms for translating community needs into timely decisions. Local organisations, development actors and institutions often collect information through disconnected surveys, interviews and reports, making it difficult to identify trends, prioritise needs, allocate resources and design resilient services. Limited digital infrastructure and connectivity further constrain access to data-driven decision-making. The solution addresses this information and decision-making gap through an accessible AI-powered platform adapted to low-resource and conflict-affected environments.
Solution Overview: BEL AVENIR Community Intelligence AI is a proposed AI-powered digital platform designed to collect, structure, analyse and transform community-level information into actionable insights for local development and resilient decision-making. The platform would enable trained community partners and organisations to collect structured information through mobile-friendly forms, surveys and community consultations, including information on socioeconomic needs, access to services, livelihoods, environmental concerns, displacement-related challenges and local priorities. Data would be securely aggregated and processed through an AI-assisted analytical layer. AI models would help identify recurring needs, emerging trends, geographic patterns and priority areas, while natural language processing could analyse qualitative responses in French and, where technically feasible, Swahili and other locally relevant languages. The platform would generate dashboards, summaries, alerts and decision-support reports for authorised users. The solution would be designed with privacy, data minimisation, informed participation, human oversight and conflict sensitivity as core principles. It would use cloud and/or lightweight local digital infrastructure, secure databases, APIs, AI/NLP models, analytics dashboards and mobile data-collection tools. Offline-capable data collection would be considered for areas with limited connectivity. The initial development model would involve BEL AVENIR working with technology developers, universities, civil-society organisations, community representatives and development partners. The solution would be tested through a controlled pilot before adaptation and replication in other African contexts.
Solution Provider(s): BEL AVENIR-CONGO (BEL AV) - Civil society organisation based in the Democratic Republic of the Congo working with children, vulnerable and conflict-affected communities, education, environmental protection, peacebuilding and social cohesion; University of Lubumbashi, Faculty of Legal, Political and Administrative Sciences - academic partner for research, legal and ethical analysis and capacity development; future technology and data partners - AI development, data infrastructure, cybersecurity and technical implementation.
Implementation location(s): GOMA, LUBUMBASHI
Implementation timeline(s): N/A - implementation has not yet started.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Approximately 6 - 9 months, including local needs assessment, stakeholder engagement, technical adaptation, data governance preparation, user training, testing and pilot deployment.
Desired impact: The main objective is to strengthen data-driven and inclusive decision-making by enabling local organisations, development actors and relevant institutions to transform fragmented community information into reliable, timely and actionable insights. The expected impact includes improved identification and prioritisation of community needs, faster analysis of field information, more efficient allocation of limited resources, stronger participation of vulnerable communities in decision-making and improved coordination among local actors. As an initial pilot objective, the solution could aim to reduce the time required to consolidate and analyse community information by at least 50%, while establishing a structured digital evidence base that can support local planning and programme design. Additional indicators would include the number of communities and users reached, datasets processed, reports generated, community priorities identified and decisions or interventions informed by the platform. These figures are proposed pilot targets rather than demonstrated results and would be validated during implementation.
Key technologies: The proposed solution would use: Artificial Intelligence and machine learning; Natural Language Processing (NLP); AI-assisted data classification and summarisation; Mobile and web-based data collection; Secure cloud and/or lightweight digital databases; Data analytics and interactive dashboards; Geographic information and mapping technologies; Application Programming Interfaces (APIs); Role-based access controls and data-security mechanisms; Offline-capable digital data collection for low-connectivity environments. The technology architecture would be designed to remain modular and adaptable to locally available infrastructure.
Unique Characteristics: The solution combines AI-powered analysis with community-generated data and local knowledge, focusing on contexts where reliable information infrastructure is limited. Its distinctive features would include a low-resource and potentially offline-capable approach, multilingual and locally adaptable data processing, human oversight of AI-generated outputs, privacy- and conflict-sensitive data governance, and a community-centred data collection model. Rather than replacing community organisations or decision-makers, the platform would augment their capacity to analyse information and make evidence-based decisions. Its modular architecture would also allow adaptation to different sectors, communities and African country contexts.
Sustainable Change: The solution could contribute to systemic change by strengthening the digital information infrastructure available to organisations and institutions working in underserved and conflict-affected environments. Once validated, the platform could be replicated across different communities and countries by adapting its data models, languages, indicators and local partnerships without rebuilding the entire system. Open standards and interoperable architecture could facilitate collaboration with universities, civil-society organisations, development actors and technology providers. Over time, the solution could support stronger local digital and AI skills, improve the quality of community-level evidence used in planning, reduce duplication in data collection and enable smaller organisations and local actors to participate more effectively in data-driven development. Its long-term potential would be to establish a scalable African model for responsible AI-assisted community intelligence that supports more inclusive, resilient and evidence-based local development.
Funding Sources: The solution has not yet received dedicated funding and has not been previously implemented. It is currently at the Idea/Concept stage. Initial concept development has been supported through the existing organisational capacity, volunteer contributions and in-kind resources of BEL AVENIR-CONGO (BEL AV). Future funding would be sought through innovation grants, responsible AI and digital transformation programmes, development partners, impact-oriented funding and strategic technology partnerships.
Testimonials and Endorsements: No specific testimonials or endorsements are available for the proposed AI solution at this stage, as the solution has not yet been implemented. BEL AVENIR-CONGO has, however, an established record of community engagement, human rights advocacy, peacebuilding and work with vulnerable and conflict-affected communities in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Relevant organisational references can be provided upon request.

Name of your organization: Map Before Machine AI Developing Services
Title: Map Before Machine™: Pre-AI Gateway for Sustainable Industry
Subtitle: A pre-AI software gateway cutting data-center carbon waste, ensuring resilient human-in-the-loop audit trails, and providing inclusive, neuro-accessible AI governance for global industry.
Problem Statement: Every major AI platform opens to a blank text box, which creates three critical problems for industrial adoption: 1) Massive Energy Waste (The Sustainability Problem): Because users face a blank screen, they rely on vague, trial-and-error typing. This back-and-forth guessing wastes expensive AI computing power and directly increases data-center carbon emissions. 2) Loss of Human Oversight (The Resilience Problem): When AI provides an instant answer, human operators stop reasoning for themselves. In high-stakes industries like healthcare or defense, this "automation bias" causes workers to blindly trust the machine and miss dangerous errors. 3) Excluding Diverse Workers (The Inclusion Problem): Current AI tools demand strong writing skills, usually in English. This creates a massive barrier that leaves out visual learners, neurodiverse thinkers, and non-English speaking global workforces.
Solution Overview: How the Solution Works Map Before Machine™ acts as a mandatory checkpoint before a user can type a prompt into an AI tool. Instead of starting with a blank screen, users must complete a simple 3-stage sequence (Attempt → Map → Refine): Attempt & Map: Before the AI opens, the user visually sketches their idea and writes a clear directional claim (e.g., "[Concept A] affects [Concept B] because [Reason]"). This creates a verifiable, timestamped record proving human reasoning happened first. Refine (The Gate Unlocks): The user then writes one highly specific question identifying exactly what they need help with. Only then does the AI unlock to refine the user's original idea. The Industrial Value: By forcing the user to define the problem upfront, this process completely stops the wasteful, back-and-forth guessing that burns massive amounts of AI computing power. It also ensures that human operators in critical sectors maintain strict oversight, preventing dangerous automation bias. Methodologies and Technologies Used The solution is powered by the peer-reviewed Somagraphic Learning™ framework. 1) Inclusive UI Methodology: We use an original visual-cognitive structure called Shape-Emotion Grammar™. Instead of relying on heavy text or English fluency, it uses simple shapes and visual cues so that neurodiverse thinkers and global workers can easily map their thoughts. 2) Tri-Modal Deployment Technology: To ensure it scales across both advanced and developing nations, the technology deploys in three ways:API Gateways: Natively integrated into enterprise AI software as a pre-chatbot screen. 3) LMS Plugins: Directly embedded into platforms like Canvas and Moodle with zero IT overhaul. Analog E-Copies: Pen-and-paper formats requiring zero software, perfect for highly secure infrastructure or under-resourced environments. 4) Partnerships and Collaboration Models We operate as a B2B consultancy under a UAE licensing model, offering system integration, enterprise advisory, and institutional pilots globally. 5) Industry Pilots: We secure pilot agreements to test the guardrail in high-stakes environments, including a signed pilot agreement with a U.S. defense consulting firm to run our 60-participant IRB-ready protocol. 6) Research Collaborations: We partner globally to build policy-neutral standards, including active research contributions to the Oxford AIEOU Human Flourishing Lab and collaborations with the World Affairs Council through the Global Classroom Educator Fellowship 7) Ecosystem Integration: We are actively seeking partnerships with enterprise SaaS providers and AI systems integrators to embed this gateway directly into high-compliance sectors like FinTech, LegalTech, and Healthcare.
Solution Provider(s): Oxford AIEOU Human Flourishing Lab (Collaborative research partner, Academic and AI Ethics sector), U.S.-Based Defense Consulting Firm (Signed pilot agreement partner for 60-participant IRB protocol, Defense and Enterprise Compliance sector), Culture Vitale and MENA Speakers (Global practitioner platforms for enterprise delivery, Corporate L&D and Workforce Training sector), Gumroad (Pre-AI Thinking Cards, e-copies)
Implementation location(s): Currently being piloted in the United States, and I have an active E-trader business license in the United Arab Emirates. (expanding in UAE too)
Implementation timeline(s): Pilot launches Nov 30, 2026
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Estimated Time to Pilot: Immediate (1 to 4 weeks for deployment); 1 to 4 months for full empirical benchmarking. Justification: Because Map Before Machine™ utilizes a tri-modal deployment strategy, it completely bypasses traditional IT procurement delays and hardware installation bottlenecks. The time to pilot in a new geography scales according to the region's digital infrastructure: Tier 1 (Immediate / Under 1 Week): In under-resourced or highly secure geographies, the protocol deploys immediately as an analog-first, pen-and-paper toolkit requiring zero electricity, zero software, and zero IT approval. Tier 2 (1 to 4 Weeks): For digitally connected enterprise environments, lightweight browser extensions and LMS-ready plugins (for platforms like Canvas or Moodle) can be integrated in under 30 days, requiring zero backend stack rebuilds. Tier 3 (1 to 4 Months for Full Validation): To capture region-specific data, our fully developed 60-participant IRB-ready pilot protocol can be executed in 1 to 4 months to establish empirical benchmarks on carbon abatement and token optimization for that specific geography.
Desired impact: Main Objectives of the Solution Map Before Machine™ provides the missing pre-AI infrastructure needed to safely and sustainably scale AI across global industries. It achieves three clear goals: 1) Cut AI Carbon & Compute Waste: Stop the endless guessing games caused by blank prompts. By forcing users to define their problem first, we eliminate wasted AI processing power and lower data-center emissions. 2) Ensure Human-in-the-Loop Safety: Prevent "automation bias" in high-stakes sectors like defense and healthcare. Our protocol creates a timestamped record proving human operators thought through the problem before the AI acted. 3) Provide Neuro-Inclusive Global Access: Remove text-heavy English language barriers. Our Shape-Emotion Grammar™ uses simple visual cues, ensuring equitable AI access for neurodiverse thinkers and global workers. Demonstrated and Expected Impact Instead of relying on expensive hardware cooling, our solution cuts industrial AI waste at the behavioral source: 1) Reduced GHG Emissions (Expected): Unmanaged AI demand could emit 24–44 million metric tons of CO2e annually in the U.S. by 2030. By enforcing targeted queries, we project a 35–50% drop in wasted AI tokens, potentially avoiding >500 MtCO2e/year globally with zero hardware costs. 2) Increased Industrial Safety (Expected): In critical infrastructure, forcing users to map their intent first increases the rate at which human operators catch AI errors, preventing dangerous system failures. 3) Proven Behavioral Change (Demonstrated): Initial testing shows users ask significantly more specific, targeted questions when forced to use our visual mapping step before opening the AI. 4) Commercial & Pilot Readiness (Demonstrated): The framework has passed three independent peer reviews in 32 days. We have also secured a signed agreement with a U.S. defense consulting firm to run our 60-person pilot protocol in high-stakes environments.
Key technologies: 1) Pre-AI Software Gate A digital checkpoint built directly into AI systems. It locks the blank prompt box, forcing users to map out their thoughts before the AI is allowed to run. 2) Visual AI Scanners We only use AI after the human does the thinking. Our system scans the user's completed visual map (shapes and text) and translates it into a highly specific instruction for the AI to follow. 3) Live Tracking & Secure Audit Logs Dashboards measure exact energy and computing power saved in real time. The system also creates a permanent, timestamped record of the user's original idea, satisfying strict safety and legal rules for high-risk industries. 4) Easy Platform Plugins & Offline Tools The software easily plugs right into standard learning platforms like Canvas and Moodle. For off-grid areas or highly secure facilities, it also works as a simple pen-and-paper toolkit that requires zero electricity or software.
Unique Characteristics: 1) Acting Before the AI Starts (The Core Innovation) Most safety tools check the AI's answer after it is generated. We govern the human's thinking before the AI even turns on. This prevents workers from blindly trusting the machine and stops wasted computing power at the source. 2) Visual, Language-Free Access Standard AI tools demand strong English writing skills. Instead, we use Shape-Emotion Grammar™ - a visual system using simple shapes and arrows. This removes language barriers so neurodiverse thinkers and non-English speaking global workers can easily direct the AI. 3) Instant Deployment Everywhere Enterprise software usually takes months to approve and install. Our tool deploys instantly in three formats: as software built into the AI screen, as plugins for learning platforms, or as offline pen-and-paper cards. It works perfectly in both high-tech offices and remote, off-grid areas. 4) Slashing AI Emissions Without New Hardware To cut AI energy use, the industry buys expensive cooling hardware. We cut emissions behaviorally. By making users map their thoughts first, we stop the endless trial-and-error typing that wastes massive amounts of data-center energy. This achieves green sustainability without spending millions on new infrastructure.
Sustainable Change: 1) Creating a New Global Safety Rule Beyond being just a tool, this framework is designed to become a universal standard for AI safety. We are building a blueprint for the Center for Pre-AI Cognitive Governance, which will help governments and high-risk industries adopt this pre-AI checkpoint as a mandatory compliance rule worldwide. 2) Permanent Carbon Reductions As AI grows, the energy used by data centers is skyrocketing. By permanently changing how workers interact with AI (forcing them to ask highly specific questions rather than guessing), this solution can systematically cut millions of tons of carbon emissions across all industries, without requiring new hardware. 3) Redefining AI Education Worldwide Current global guidelines (like those from UNESCO) teach people how to use AI after it is turned on. This solution shifts the global standard to "Pre-AI Literacy". By using simple visual shapes instead of heavy text, this systemic change guarantees that non-English speakers, visual learners, and marginalized groups can safely direct AI tools. 4) Instant Global Replication Because the solution works offline on paper, as a simple learning plugin, or as built-in software, it can be copied and scaled instantly anywhere in the world. It is designed to work perfectly whether it is used in a high-tech corporate office or an under-resourced community, ensuring true digital equality.
Funding Sources: 1) Self-Funded by the Founder The solution was built entirely from scratch by the solo founder without any outside grants, institutional backing, or investor funding. 2) Commercial Revenue & Licensing The framework currently funds itself through active business revenue. Operating under a UAE business license, we generate income by selling B2B enterprise licenses and running paid pilot programs for high-compliance sectors, such as our recent agreement with a U.S. defense consulting firm. 3) Global Training & Partnerships Additional funding comes from delivering paid enterprise consulting and workforce training through global practitioner platforms, including Culture Vitale and MENA Speakers.

Title: DME Industrial Copilot — Accessible Agentic AI for Industrial Operations
Subtitle: A proposed AI assistant for industrial SMEs: source-backed equipment guidance and draft maintenance work orders, with human review.
Problem Statement: Industrial SMEs often keep equipment manuals, operating procedures and maintenance records in separate files and spreadsheets. During equipment problems, staff can struggle to find relevant guidance quickly, particularly when experienced colleagues are unavailable. Cost and integration complexity can limit access to industrial software. DME proposes a focused knowledge and maintenance assistant to address these barriers; these needs have not yet been validated through a customer pilot.
Solution Overview: The proposed workflow is: equipment issue -> retrieve relevant approved documentation -> ask clarifying questions -> suggest checks with source citations -> draft a maintenance work order -> human review and approval. It would use Python, document processing, retrieval-augmented generation, a language model and a simple web interface. Planned safeguards include document access controls, audit logs and explicit acknowledgement when evidence is insufficient. It would not control machinery or replace qualified maintenance judgment. Arabic and English interaction is a development goal requiring testing. An initial demonstration would use public or permission-cleared documents over an estimated four to six weeks, followed by evaluation of retrieval, citations, unsupported answers and work-order usefulness. DME seeks an industrial SME or maintenance organization to co-define a narrow use case and evaluate a future prototype. No completed prototype, deployment, customer, measured impact or confirmed partnership is claimed.
Solution Provider(s): None confirmed. Seeking an industrial SME or maintenance organization as a future design and evaluation partner.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Not yet pilot-ready. An initial document-based demonstration is estimated at 4–6 weeks; a subsequent pilot schedule would be agreed after securing a partner, authorized data and safety requirements.
Desired impact: The objectives are to make approved technical knowledge easier for industrial SMEs to access, support consistent maintenance documentation, and help workers prepare evidence-backed maintenance tasks. Intended benefits include shorter information-search time and more consistent work-order preparation. Better-informed maintenance may support equipment longevity and resource efficiency, contributing to SDGs 8, 9 and 12. No operational, financial or environmental impact has been demonstrated. A future evaluation would compare task completion time, answer and citation correctness, unsupported-answer frequency and reviewer-rated work-order usefulness against a baseline. Downtime, energy, waste and emissions benefits would require separate pilot measurement; no numerical savings are claimed.
Key technologies: Proposed technologies: Python; parsing and indexing of permission-cleared manuals and procedures; text embeddings and a searchable document store; retrieval-augmented generation with a language model; structured workflow orchestration; and a web interface. Planned supporting controls include user access permissions, source citations, audit logging and human approval. Arabic/English interaction would be tested during development. These are planned components, not claims of a completed implementation.
Unique Characteristics: The proposed differentiation is a narrow, evidence-backed workflow connecting industrial knowledge retrieval to a reviewable maintenance work-order draft. Responses would identify their supporting sources and flag missing evidence. The design aims to reduce adoption barriers for smaller industrial teams through a simple interface and gradual onboarding of existing documents. Human approval is central, and machinery control is outside the initial scope. Arabic/English access is a planned goal. These features are design intentions requiring prototype validation, not proven advantages over existing products.
Sustainable Change: If validated, the approach could help smaller industrial firms preserve operational knowledge and make it more accessible to staff. A reusable document-onboarding and evaluation process could support adaptation to additional equipment types, sites and languages. Local industrial partners could guide terminology and review safety requirements. Replication would depend on document rights, data quality, domain review, security and affordable operating costs. The initial priority is to establish reliable performance on one narrow workflow before seeking wider adoption. No scale-up or systemic impact is currently claimed.

Title: AI-Enabled Institutional Energy Intelligence for Sustainable African Institutions
Subtitle: An AI-driven energy intelligence model integrating forecasting, anomaly detection, and decision support to improve energy efficiency, resilience, and sustainability across African institutions.
Problem Statement: Many African institutions operate within unreliable and inefficient energy environments characterized by frequent power interruptions, fragmented energy infrastructure, limited monitoring capabilities, and inadequate access to reliable energy consumption data. These challenges increase operational costs, undermine institutional productivity, complicate renewable energy integration, and constrain evidence-based energy management. Although investments in electricity infrastructure and renewable energy systems are increasing, many institutions lack the analytical capabilities required to forecast energy demand, detect abnormal consumption patterns, and optimize available energy resources. Existing energy management solutions often depend on reliable data, stable infrastructure, and operating conditions that may not reflect the realities of resource-constrained African institutions. The central challenge is therefore not only inadequate energy infrastructure but also the absence of adaptable, data-driven intelligence to manage existing and emerging energy systems effectively. The proposed solution addresses this gap by developing and validating an AI-enabled Institutional Energy Intelligence Model that supports predictive analysis, anomaly detection, and informed energy management decisions under varying operational conditions.
Solution Overview: The proposed AI-Enabled Institutional Energy Intelligence solution is a collaborative research initiative designed to develop, test, and validate an adaptable artificial intelligence model for improving energy management in African institutions. The solution integrates energy data collection, machine learning, anomaly detection, and decision-support methodologies to support more efficient, reliable, and sustainable energy operations. The proposed implementation follows five interconnected stages: 1. Energy Data Foundations: Establish institutional energy baselines through available electricity consumption records, energy infrastructure assessments, and, where feasible, IoT-enabled monitoring. Data quality, missing measurements, and governance requirements will be systematically addressed. 2. AI-Based Energy Forecasting: Develop and evaluate machine learning models capable of predicting energy demand and consumption patterns under varying operational conditions, including incomplete data and intermittent electricity supply. 3. Anomaly Detection and Diagnostics: Develop analytical methods to identify unusual consumption patterns, operational inefficiencies, and potential energy system abnormalities. 4. Intelligent Decision Support: Integrate forecasting and diagnostic outputs into a proposed decision-support framework to assist institutional managers in energy planning, resource allocation, and renewable energy integration where applicable. 5. Validation and Replication: Evaluate model performance and practical applicability across participating institutions, documenting adaptation requirements and opportunities for wider adoption. The initiative is structured around a three-country African research consortium: * Abdulkadir Kure University, Nigeria: Lead institution responsible for research coordination, institutional energy baseline development, and living-laboratory activities. * Council for Scientific and Industrial Research – Institute for Scientific and Technological Information (CSIR-INSTI), Ghana: Contributes expertise in artificial intelligence, machine learning, data analytics, and model development. * Botswana University of Agriculture and Natural Resources (BUAN), Botswana: Supports contextual adaptation, comparative validation, and assessment of replication opportunities. The research adopts a collaborative model combining institutional experimentation, interdisciplinary expertise, shared validation, and knowledge transfer. Expected outputs include a validated research model, forecasting and anomaly detection methodologies, a decision-support framework, and guidance for adaptation to other African institutions. Title: INSURED FUTURE: Human-AI Skills and Accountable SME Workflows
Subtitle: A proposed method for SME teams to preserve source meaning, approval boundaries and evidence of completion when using AI to prepare and hand over operational information.
Problem Statement: AI-assisted drafting and summarisation can create a process risk when an SME team works from a revised instruction: an output may use a superseded version, change a condition, imply permission that was not granted, or report completion before the assigned action has occurred. A fluent document or a source link alone does not establish an adequate handover. Smaller teams may also have limited resources for specialist review and correction. This proposal addresses a bounded information task and the practical skills needed to control it; it does not assert measured prevalence or quantified losses across industry.
Solution Overview: INSURED FUTURE proposes a task-based Human-AI workflow combining source/version control, explicit decision authority, review of dependent outputs and an evidence-based account of completion. For a first SME use case, a team would prepare a non-safety-critical internal briefing and two dependent summaries after a source instruction changes. The workflow identifies the owner and current basis, prepares AI-assisted outputs, checks decisive conditions, obtains the necessary approval, applies authorised corrections to affected materials and records the actual handover outcome. The proposed method keeps claim standing separate from process state: a source assertion, observation or constructed assumption is not the same thing as a proposal, approval, performed action or verified receiving result. A small controlled document set and a simple maintained register can support the first exercise. Existing language-model tools can assist retrieval, comparison and drafting under human supervision; no proprietary model or integrated software product is claimed. An implementation would be co-designed with an SME or industrial support organisation and a domain reviewer. Local language, accessibility, source access, responsibilities and acceptance criteria would be agreed before a trial. RRC-AI would contribute the research framework, workflow design and practical Human-AI review. External partners and the local receiving environment remain to be established. The published working paper supplies the conceptual basis and proposed acceptance checks: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24040969.
Solution Provider(s): research, Human-AI workflow design and practical review. No external institutional or industrial partner is currently confirmed. An SME or industrial support organisation and an appropriate domain reviewer are sought for a bounded feasibility exercise.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: A validated deployment-to-pilot estimate is not yet available at the Idea/Concept stage. The first step would be partner-led scoping of one information task, followed by a bounded document-based feasibility exercise. A schedule would be agreed after the source set, language, access conditions, domain review, responsibilities and resources are confirmed; no fixed deployment commitment is made.
Desired impact: The main objectives are to help SME teams preserve decisive source conditions in AI-assisted work, maintain the scope of approval, correct affected outputs consistently and report actual completion accurately. The proposed first exercise compares a competent ordinary workflow with an AI-assisted workflow using the same task, source access and support. Acceptance checks would cover current-source use; preservation of actor, scope, time, permission and uncertainty; correction across the briefing and both summaries; evidence of the assigned handover; and accurate treatment of missing or failed checks. Total effort would include preparation, review, false alarms, correction, recovery and maintenance. Error counts would be reported with the evaluated denominator. These are intended outcomes and an evaluation plan. No industrial deployment results, productivity gains, jobs created, energy savings or emissions reductions have been measured. Development of human capability would require a separate assessment and would not be inferred solely from the quality of a joint human-AI artifact.
Key technologies: Proposed use of existing generative-AI language-model tools for source comparison, drafting and translation; controlled documents, versioned records and a simple task/decision register for traceability; and human review against agreed acceptance criteria. The first feasibility exercise can be organised with ordinary document and spreadsheet tools. Specific models, interfaces and any software integration would be selected and recorded for the actual task. RRC-AI does not present a newly trained model or an existing industrial software deployment.
Unique Characteristics: The proposed distinctive contribution is the way practical Human-AI skills are joined to accountable delivery in one work episode. It separates the evidential standing of a claim from the state of an action, preserves permission and scope across transformations, and checks the receiving result against the task actually agreed. Review should correct affected outputs while preserving already adequate work and avoiding unnecessary approval repetition or paperwork. The approach also makes the total burden of control visible. These are proposed design features; novelty, added value and performance require comparison with existing methods and tools rather than being assumed.
Sustainable Change: If a bounded exercise shows practical value, the method could be adapted to other information workflows and local languages through reusable task templates, acceptance checks, examples and operator training. Industrial support organisations could help SMEs identify suitable processes and obtain domain review. Replication would preserve local responsibility, lawful source use and appropriate access rather than impose one universal workflow. For developing and middle-income economies, adaptation would begin with a partner-identified need and realistic infrastructure, language and resource conditions. Initial work using controlled documents and a simple register could reduce dependence on bespoke software. Wider adoption, financing and integration would require evidence of benefit, local capacity and an agreed partnership model. These are prospective pathways, not demonstrated scale-up effects.

Summary: INSURED FUTURE proposes a task-based workflow for SME teams using language models, with source control, named decision authority, review of dependent outputs and an evidence record of completion. Two working papers are published with DOIs; no pilot has run.

Title: NURTURE-Africa: Physics-Informed AI for Climate-Resilient Farming
Subtitle: A resource-aware digital twin that helps smallholder farms manage water, nutrients and energy under climate and data constraints.
Problem Statement: Smallholder farmers in water- and nutrient-constrained regions must make linked decisions about irrigation, fertilisation and energy use with incomplete data, uncertain weather and limited advisory capacity. Existing tools often address these resources separately. More complex AI can also become costly or unreliable when local observations are sparse. The challenge is to provide decision support that improves resource use without creating new environmental, financial or operational burdens.
Solution Overview: NURTURE-Africa combines field measurements, water-nutrient-energy accounting, mechanistic models and uncertainty-aware decision support in a digital-twin framework. The system compares three levels of advice, from simple practice-based guidance to calibrated models and, where the available data justify it, physics-informed constrained learning and dynamic state estimation. Physical and operational limits such as available water, pump capacity, nutrient safety and energy access are treated as constraints rather than left for an unconstrained AI model to infer. The system is designed for low-connectivity agricultural settings. Field records, sensor observations and contextual data can be collected through an offline-first data layer and synchronised when connectivity is available. If the data are insufficient for a reliable recommendation, the system can fall back to a simpler validated method or withhold the recommendation. The proposed delivery model combines AI and digital-twin development with African agricultural research, farmer organisations, local advisory actors and socioeconomic evaluation. The aim is not to maximise model complexity, but to determine when additional AI produces a measurable improvement in farm decisions and when a simpler approach is more appropriate.
Solution Provider(s): • Higher Institute of Technological Studies of Sfax (ISET Sfax), Tunisia – Applied research and higher education partner contributing water-nutrient-energy science, irrigation and nutrient-management methods, and the scientific design of a candidate North African field-validation setting. • Association of Women in Agriculture in Kenya (AWAK), Kenya – Women-led agricultural and community network supporting farmer engagement, gender and inclusion, local needs assessment and a candidate replication and adoption pathway in eastern Kenya. The final scientific host and field site remain subject to confirmation. • Smart Agro Hub S.A., Greece – Agri-innovation ecosystem partner supporting links with advisory services and public authorities, replication pathways, exploitation and wider Africa-Europe knowledge exchange.
Implementation location(s): Do not select MVP/Pilot-ready yet. The integrated NURTURE solution has not completed field validation.
Implementation timeline(s): N/A – the integrated solution has not yet been deployed. Candidate field-validation settings are being developed in Tunisia and Kenya, subject to site access, scientific capacity and local approvals.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: N/A – field implementation has not yet started.
Desired impact: The main objective is to help smallholder farmers and advisers make safer and more resource-efficient decisions across water, nutrients and energy while maintaining acceptable crop and livelihood outcomes. NURTURE-Africa will test whether integrated resource management and progressively more sophisticated decision-support methods improve farm decisions compared with current practice and simpler advice. It will also determine when additional AI does not justify its monitoring, computing or delivery cost. Field impact has not yet been demonstrated, so no universal percentage reduction in water, energy or fertiliser use is claimed. The planned evaluation will measure water use in m³/ha, pumping energy in kWh/m³, nutrient inputs and balances, crop output, farm gross margin, physical-constraint violations, predictive calibration, decision regret, usability and adoption. Site-specific improvement targets will be fixed only after baseline measurements and statistical design are completed.
Key technologies: Physics-informed and constrained machine learning; ensemble-based state estimation; mechanistic water, nutrient and energy models; digital twins; decision-support systems; IoT and field sensing; remote sensing where locally useful; offline-first data collection; interoperable data interfaces; uncertainty quantification and human-in-the-loop recommendations.
Unique Characteristics: NURTURE-Africa does not assume that the most complex AI model is automatically the best solution. It compares simple advice, calibrated modelling and advanced physics-informed AI on the same decision problems and includes the cost of data collection, monitoring, computation and delivery in that comparison. AI recommendations are constrained by physical and operational limits. When observations are incomplete or a model cannot estimate a state reliably, the system can revert to a simpler method instead of producing a false sense of precision. The approach is also designed around local agricultural knowledge, low-connectivity operation and farmer usability. Technical performance, affordability and the ability to act on a recommendation are evaluated together rather than treated as separate outcomes.
Sustainable Change: The broader value of NURTURE-Africa is not limited to a single farm or pilot site. The project is designed to produce reusable measurement protocols, interoperable data structures, transparent model-comparison methods and practical rules for deciding which level of digital support is appropriate under different resource and data conditions. These outputs can be used by agricultural advisers, research organisations, public authorities and local technology providers to design services that match local capacity instead of importing a fixed high-cost technology stack. By identifying both where advanced AI adds value and where simpler methods are sufficient, the approach can reduce unnecessary technology costs and make digital agricultural decision support more accessible. Replication would still require local calibration, farm data, institutional participation and environmental safeguards rather than assuming that one model transfers unchanged between regions.
Funding Sources: NURTURE-Africa itself has not yet received implementation funding and has not completed field deployment. Its technical foundation builds on Negentra’s previous publicly funded R&D in digital twins, real-time data processing and decision-support software, including a TÜBİTAK 1507 R&D project. The current NURTURE-Africa configuration is being developed as a new research and innovation initiative, with field validation and implementation funding still to be secured.
Testimonials and Endorsements: No public beneficiary testimonials are available yet because field implementation has not started. Prospective research, agricultural and community partners have contributed technical feedback and expressions of interest during solution development, but we do not present these as beneficiary endorsements or evidence of completed deployment.

Title: Factory OS: Physics-Aware AI for Sustainable Food Manufacturing
Subtitle: An emerging industrial intelligence platform combining digital twins, process-aware AI and production analytics to improve resource efficiency, quality and decision-making in food-processing MSMEs.
Problem Statement: Small and medium-sized food-processing enterprises face persistent operational inefficiencies due to fragmented production data, variable raw-material characteristics, limited equipment monitoring and dependence on manual decision-making. These challenges are particularly significant in batch-based operations such as dehydration, freeze-drying and other preservation processes, where processing time, energy consumption, product yield and quality depend on interacting material and equipment conditions. Many smaller manufacturers lack affordable systems that connect shop-floor operations with production planning, quality management and resource accounting. Conventional enterprise software may record transactions without adequately representing the physical behaviour of manufacturing processes. Factory OS addresses this gap by developing an accessible, physics-aware industrial intelligence platform that can help food-processing MSMEs make informed production decisions, identify inefficiencies and systematically improve operational performance.
Solution Overview: Factory OS is a proposed industrial intelligence platform being developed by Devalsari Naturals Pvt. Ltd. for small and medium-sized food manufacturers. It aims to connect production planning, actual equipment behaviour, resource use and product quality within an accessible, modular digital system. The initial use case is batch-based food dehydration, where variation in raw-material moisture, load size, environmental conditions and processing settings makes yield, production time and energy requirements difficult to predict. The architecture comprises three connected layers: 1. Factory Twin — A structured operational model of production equipment, batches, material inputs, process parameters, capacity, quality checkpoints and resource consumption. The initial version will use operator-entered production records, supplemented by available equipment and sensor measurements. 2. Factory Guru — A proposed physics-aware decision-support engine combining material and energy balances, equipment constraints, historical observations, statistical forecasting and, when adequate data are available, validated machine-learning models. Its intended functions include estimating batch duration and usable yield, forecasting resource requirements, identifying deviations and supporting equipment scheduling. Recommendations will remain subject to operator approval. 3. Factory OS — The production-management layer intended to coordinate work orders, batch documentation, SOP checkpoints, machine allocation, inventory movements, quality records and operating-cost analysis. Development will proceed through structured batch-data collection, prototype software development, calibration against measured production results, prediction-error assessment and controlled pilot testing. Evaluation will focus on energy consumption per kilogram of acceptable finished product, yield, batch-time accuracy, quality consistency and operator usability. Devalsari Naturals has relevant food-processing infrastructure and applied process experience that could support initial testing. However, the integrated Factory OS software is at design/pre-MVP stage and has not yet demonstrated independently verified productivity or emissions reductions. External collaboration is proposed with appropriately authorised researchers, equipment specialists and independent MSME processors. Participation, data access, intellectual-property rights and deployment responsibilities would be governed by written agreements. The objective is to develop affordable, evidence-based manufacturing intelligence adaptable to resource-constrained industrial environments.
Solution Provider(s): Devalsari Naturals Private Limited (India) — applicant, proposed solution developer and initial industrial validation organisation; active in postharvest processing, bioactive ingredients and food-processing technology. Title: CleanLoop AI: Turning Industrial Waste into Clean Resources
Subtitle: AI-powered cleantech that transforms industrial waste into valuable resources, optimises material recovery, and helps businesses reduce environmental impact through circular innovation.
Problem Statement: Industrial businesses face growing pressure to reduce waste, lower operating costs, and use resources more efficiently. Yet fragmented waste data, limited material traceability, and difficulty identifying reuse and recycling opportunities can leave valuable resources underutilised or sent to landfill. For small and medium-sized enterprises, limited technical capacity and access to affordable recovery technologies can make circular practices difficult to implement. Potential users of industrial by-products may also struggle to identify reliable suppliers and assess material suitability. CleanLoop AI addresses the disconnect between industrial waste generation and resource recovery. The proposed solution would help businesses identify recoverable materials, match waste streams with potential reuse opportunities, and make better-informed decisions about waste reduction and circular production.
Solution Overview: Solution Overview CleanLoop AI is MDIHUB’s proposed AI-powered cleantech platform that helps industrial businesses identify, recover, and commercialise resources currently treated as waste. It would connect waste generators with recyclers, manufacturers, technology providers, and entrepreneurs who can reuse materials or convert them into valuable products. The solution centres on industrial symbiosis: enabling one business’s by-products to become another business’s inputs. How the solution works 1. Waste-stream assessment and data collection Participating businesses record the type, quantity, composition, location, and availability of their waste or by-products. Initial assessments would combine site audits, laboratory results where necessary, and existing production records. Connected sensors could subsequently automate selected measurements. 2. AI-assisted material classification The platform would analyse submitted information to categorise materials and flag potential recovery pathways. Computer vision could assist with image-based identification, while technical specialists would verify uncertain classifications and safety-sensitive recommendations. 3. Resource matching and opportunity identification A recommendation engine would match available materials with potential buyers, recyclers, processors, and research partners. Matches would consider material specifications, volumes, location, transport costs, processing requirements, and applicable regulations. 4. Recovery and product-development pilots Selected opportunities would undergo technical and commercial feasibility assessments. MDIHUB and its partners would support prototyping and trials—for example, converting suitable recovered materials into manufacturing inputs or testing recycled feedstock for additive manufacturing. Battery-related opportunities would require specialist testing, handling, and compliance review. 5. Transaction support and impact monitoring The platform would support partner introductions, material specifications, and recovery tracking. Dashboards would monitor material quantities, costs, revenue, and estimated environmental outcomes against documented baselines. ### Methodologies and technologies used - Material-flow analysis to map resource inputs, outputs, and losses. - Circular design and techno-economic assessment to evaluate practical, commercially viable recovery options. - Machine learning and recommendation algorithms to identify patterns and rank potential material matches. - Computer vision and optional IoT sensors to improve material identification and operational data collection. - Geospatial analysis to assess proximity and transport implications. - Lifecycle assessment methods to compare environmental outcomes, with assumptions and data limitations clearly stated. - Human-in-the-loop verification to ensure AI recommendations undergo appropriate technical review. Partnerships and collaboration models Proposed collaborations is going to include: - Industrial businesses supplying waste-stream data and hosting pilots. - Recyclers and processors validating recovery routes and delivering treatment services. - Universities, TVET colleges, and laboratories supporting testing, research, prototyping, and skills development. - Technology providers supporting platform development, sensors, and secure data infrastructure. - Government, municipalities, and development-finance partners supporting ecosystem coordination and appropriate funding mechanisms. - Startups and community enterprises developing services and products around validated recovery opportunities. Collaboration would begin through defined pilot agreements covering responsibilities, data ownership, intellectual property, safety, costs, and performance indicators. Successful pilots could progress into service contracts, material-supply agreements, or jointly commercialised products.

Its proposed combination of data-driven matching, technical validation, and enterprise support would aim to establish lasting resource-exchange relationships beyond individual pilot projects. These relationships could encourage investment in recovery capacity and greater use of secondary materials. - New enterprise opportunities: Validated recovery pathways could support businesses in material collection, testing, repair, processing, and product manufacturing. MDIHUB’s incubation model would help translate technical opportunities into viable enterprises. - Better industrial decision-making: Consistent material records and documented pilot results could help participating businesses incorporate resource efficiency into procurement, production planning, and investment decisions. - Skills and knowledge transfer: Training and collaboration with technical institutions could build local capability in AI applications, material assessment, and circular product development, reducing dependence on external expertise over time. ### Replication and scale-up The solution could expand through a repeatable implementation model: assess local waste streams, recruit committed partners, validate recovery pathways, and establish commercially viable exchanges. Shared data templates, assessment procedures, and training resources would support adaptation across industrial clusters, provinces, and potentially other countries. Evidence from successful pilots could also inform industry guidance and discussions on secondary-material quality, traceability, and regulatory barriers. Sustained impact would depend on reliable material quality and supply, customer demand, viable transport and processing costs, appropriate compliance, and a business model that supports continued operation beyond grant funding. Scaling would therefore prioritise proven exchanges rather than platform registrations alone.
