Title: INDUSTRIA ONE
Subtitle: From Connected Industrial Data to Intelligent, Inclusive and Sustainable Manufacturing
Problem Statement: Manufacturers in developing and middle-income economies often possess production machinery, programmable logic controllers, sensors, energy meters and enterprise applications that generate valuable operational data. Yet the information remains dispersed across equipment vendors, incompatible protocols, isolated dashboards and disconnected databases. Without meaningful asset context, trustworthy historical records and reusable interfaces, plant engineers cannot reliably link machine status, production output, energy consumption, downtime and quality losses. Advanced analytics and industrial artificial intelligence become expensive to introduce, difficult to validate and hard to reproduce across facilities. The resulting gap is not merely a shortage of algorithms. It is an industrial interoperability and capability gap: many micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) cannot justify costly equipment replacement, long integration projects, continual cloud dependencies or specialist AI staffing. At the same time, energy and resource performance cannot be improved or verified consistently without accurate production-normalised baselines. INDUSTRIA ONE is conceived to address this sequence of barriers by starting with working industrial data infrastructure and developing specific industrial AI applications only where reliable data, measurable use cases and human engineering oversight exist.
Solution Overview: INDUSTRIA ONE is a proposed industrial intelligence solution built on the operating industrial connectivity, Unified Namespace (UNS), data management and application capabilities documented for MACHHUB, an industrial data platform developed by Intellogic Technology. MACHHUB is the underlying technology foundation; INDUSTRIA ONE is the proposed solution identity and use-case layer for sustainable manufacturing. Any commercial use of the underlying platform, branding, intellectual property or deployment rights must be authorised and documented by the relevant rights-holder. The confirmed present-state capability for the INDUSTRIA ONE concept is its operational UNS-based platform. Public MACHHUB materials describe industrial connectivity through OPC UA, Modbus, Serial, Mitsubishi MELSEC, Omron FINS, Panasonic MEWTOCOL, Siemens SIMATIC S7 and Beckhoff ADS/TwinCAT; built-in MQTT messaging; event-driven tag subscriptions; an industrial historian; structured collections; dashboards; permissions; automation; and on-premises application hosting. These are descriptions from the vendor website and require version-specific demonstration for this application. MACHHUB also advertises an AI Assistant in beta, which must not be represented as a validated industrial anomaly-detection, prediction or optimisation model. INDUSTRIA ONE’s proposed industrial AI modules—including production-aware energy anomaly detection, operational diagnostics and optimisation recommendations—remain in development. Accordingly, the strongest currently supportable entry is Emerging Innovations, not Deployable Solutions. The proposal does not claim that the AI has been validated in an industrial pilot or that factory-level energy or emissions savings have already occurred. Its comparative strength is that the industrial data foundation and related application ecosystem are not merely conceptual.
Solution Provider(s): Machinery & Engineering Industries Federation (MEIF), Malaysia — National industry federation representing machinery, engineering and advanced manufacturing industries, advocating industrial transformation, productivity enhancement, technology adoption and global competitiveness; Sectors: Machinery and Equipment Manufacturing, Engineering, Advanced Manufacturing, Industrial Automation, Industrial Digitalisation and Sustainable Manufacturing; Proposed Partnership Role: Industry ecosystem engagement, manufacturing MSME outreach, identification of potential pilot sites, industrial validation, technology adoption and scaling of Unified Namespace (UNS) and emerging Industrial AI applications.
Implementation location(s): Malaysia/Selangor
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6 moths
Desired impact: INDUSTRIA ONE aims to accelerate inclusive, intelligent and sustainable industrial transformation by making industrial digital infrastructure and emerging AI technologies more accessible, affordable and scalable, particularly for manufacturing micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) in developing and middle-income economies. The solution's primary objective is to bridge the industrial digital and AI divide by establishing a unified, interoperable and AI-ready manufacturing ecosystem through Unified Namespace (UNS) technology. By connecting existing machinery, industrial sensors, production systems and enterprise applications, INDUSTRIA ONE enables manufacturers to consolidate fragmented operational data into a structured, contextualised and reusable industrial information environment. This reduces integration complexity, improves operational visibility and establishes the foundation for progressive industrial AI adoption without requiring extensive replacement of existing manufacturing equipment. Building upon its operational UNS platform, INDUSTRIA ONE seeks to develop AI-powered applications for energy efficiency, predictive maintenance, production optimisation and intelligent engineering decision-making. These capabilities are intended to help manufacturers identify operational inefficiencies, reduce avoidable energy consumption, minimise equipment downtime and improve production performance. The solution also promotes responsible, human-centred AI adoption by ensuring that industrial intelligence supports professional engineering judgement, operational safety and accountable decision-making. **The expected industrial impact encompasses five interconnected dimensions: improved productivity, greater resource and energy efficiency, reduced environmental impact, enhanced MSME competitiveness, and strengthened local engineering capabilities.** Through improved data integration and future AI-enabled analytics, manufacturers are expected to gain better visibility of equipment utilisation, production losses and energy consumption. This can support evidence-based operational improvements, lower manufacturing costs and more efficient use of existing industrial assets. Environmental impact will be assessed through measurable indicators, including electricity consumption per unit of acceptable production (kWh/unit), energy savings (kWh), material waste reduction, equipment efficiency and associated greenhouse gas emissions (tCO₂e). Economic and operational impacts will be evaluated through equipment availability, unplanned downtime, overall equipment effectiveness (OEE), production throughput, integration costs and potential productivity improvements. These indicators will be measured against documented baselines during industrial pilot implementation. INDUSTRIA ONE will also support inclusive economic development by providing a scalable pathway for MSMEs to adopt advanced industrial technologies while strengthening local participation in digital value creation. Its proposed capability-building and technology-transfer activities will develop practical competencies in industrial connectivity, UNS architecture, data engineering, automation, AI applications and sustainable manufacturing. Social and workforce outcomes will be assessed through the number of enterprises supported, engineers and technicians trained, practical competencies achieved and skilled employment opportunities supported or created. At its present development stage, the UNS platform is operational, while industrial AI applications remain under development. Accordingly, the benefits described above represent expected outcomes to be validated through controlled industrial pilots rather than already demonstrated factory-level results. Quantified achievements in energy savings, greenhouse gas reductions, productivity improvements and employment creation will be reported only when supported by verified measurements.
Key technologies: INDUSTRIA ONE integrates Unified Namespace (UNS), Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), industrial communication technologies, real-time data infrastructure, edge computing and emerging Artificial Intelligence (AI) capabilities to enable intelligent, interoperable and sustainable manufacturing. 1. Unified Namespace (UNS) Technology: At the core of INDUSTRIA ONE is a working Unified Namespace platform, built upon the MACHHUB technology foundation. UNS establishes a common, structured and contextualised industrial data environment, enabling seamless information exchange among machines, production systems, enterprise applications and future AI services. This architecture reduces data fragmentation, simplifies industrial integration and provides a scalable foundation for intelligent manufacturing. 2. Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) and Connectivity: INDUSTRIA ONE connects industrial machines, programmable logic controllers (PLCs), sensors and production equipment through supported industrial communication protocols, including MQTT, OPC UA and Modbus. These technologies facilitate industrial data acquisition, equipment monitoring and interoperability between operational technology (OT) and information technology (IT) systems. 3. Real-Time Industrial Data Infrastructure: The solution incorporates MQTT-based publish-subscribe messaging, industrial data contextualisation, historical data storage, dashboards and application integration. These capabilities enable manufacturers to collect, organise, analyse and reuse operational information across production processes, supporting real-time visibility and data-driven engineering decisions. 4. Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning: INDUSTRIA ONE is developing AI-powered industrial intelligence applications for anomaly detection, predictive maintenance, energy consumption analysis and production optimisation. These capabilities aim to transform industrial data into actionable insights, improving equipment reliability, resource efficiency and manufacturing productivity. AI functionality remains under development and will undergo technical validation before industrial pilot deployment. 5. Edge Computing and Industrial Application Hosting: The underlying platform supports on-premises deployment and industrial application hosting, providing a foundation for flexible industrial computing environments. These capabilities can support local data processing, operational data control and integration with existing manufacturing infrastructure. 6. Industrial Interoperability and Sustainability Analytics: By integrating heterogeneous industrial systems through standardised data structures, INDUSTRIA ONE supports engineering performance monitoring and the development of sustainability applications covering energy efficiency, equipment utilisation and resource productivity. INDUSTRIA ONE's technological innovation lies in combining an operational UNS-based industrial digital infrastructure with emerging AI capabilities, providing an accessible and scalable pathway for manufacturing MSMEs to progress towards intelligent, productive and environmentally sustainable operations.
Unique Characteristics: INDUSTRIA ONE introduces an innovative, inclusive and scalable approach to industrial AI adoption by transforming fragmented manufacturing data into a unified digital foundation for intelligent and sustainable manufacturing. Its distinctive value lies in combining an operational Unified Namespace (UNS) platform, emerging industrial AI capabilities, engineering-led implementation and an accessible technology adoption model for manufacturing MSMEs. 1. Unified Industrial Data Architecture: Unlike conventional industrial digitalisation solutions that rely on isolated systems and complex point-to-point integrations, INDUSTRIA ONE utilises a working UNS architecture built upon MACHHUB technology. It establishes a common, contextualised industrial information environment, enabling interoperability across machines, sensors, production systems and enterprise applications. This provides a reusable data foundation for multiple industrial applications rather than requiring separate infrastructure for every use case. 2. AI-Ready Infrastructure with Progressive Intelligence: INDUSTRIA ONE addresses a fundamental barrier to industrial AI adoption: the lack of accessible, structured and reliable operational data. Its modular architecture enables manufacturers to begin with industrial connectivity and progressively introduce AI applications for predictive maintenance, energy efficiency, anomaly detection and production optimisation. These AI capabilities are currently under development, supported by an operational industrial data platform. 3. Affordable, Retrofit-Oriented Industrial Transformation: Instead of requiring manufacturers to replace existing equipment or undertake extensive technological upgrades, INDUSTRIA ONE prioritises integration with available industrial assets through supported communication interfaces. This approach has the potential to reduce adoption complexity and capital requirements, making intelligent manufacturing more accessible to MSMEs in developing and middle-income economies. 4. Engineering-Led, Human-Centred Intelligence: INDUSTRIA ONE positions AI as an enabler of professional engineering decision-making rather than a replacement for human expertise. Its intended approach combines industrial data, intelligent analytics, engineering verification and measurable operational improvement, promoting responsible and trustworthy technology adoption. 5. Ecosystem-Based Delivery and Capability Building: The proposed collaboration model connects technology providers, manufacturers, industry federations, universities and engineering professionals. It emphasises industrial validation, applied research, local technical capability development, technology transfer and replication across different manufacturing environments. 6. Sustainability-Driven and Replicable Innovation: INDUSTRIA ONE connects industrial digitalisation with measurable sustainability objectives, including energy efficiency, resource productivity, reduced production losses and improved manufacturing competitiveness. Standardised UNS data structures and reusable integration approaches provide a foundation for adapting the solution across industrial sectors and geographical markets. INDUSTRIA ONE's defining innovation is its ability to bridge the gap between industrial connectivity and artificial intelligence, creating a practical pathway from fragmented industrial data towards inclusive, intelligent and sustainable industrial transformation.
Sustainable Change: INDUSTRIA ONE has the potential to accelerate systemic industrial transformation by establishing an accessible, interoperable and scalable digital foundation that enables manufacturers, particularly MSMEs in developing and middle-income economies, to progressively participate in the industrial AI revolution. Its long-term impact extends beyond individual factory digitalisation towards transforming industrial ecosystems, strengthening technological independence and advancing inclusive, sustainable industrial development. 1. Transforming Industrial Digital Infrastructure: Through its operational Unified Namespace (UNS) architecture, INDUSTRIA ONE introduces a reusable industrial data foundation that can connect heterogeneous equipment, production systems and enterprise applications. By reducing fragmented data environments and dependence on complex point-to-point integrations, the solution can support a more interoperable industrial ecosystem and facilitate future digital innovation. 2. Democratising Industrial AI Adoption: INDUSTRIA ONE enables manufacturers to begin with existing industrial infrastructure and progressively adopt AI applications for energy efficiency, predictive maintenance and production optimisation. This phased approach can reduce technological and financial barriers, potentially narrowing the industrial AI divide between large enterprises and MSMEs. 3. Creating Replicable Industrial Transformation Models: Standardised UNS data structures, modular integration approaches and reusable implementation methodologies create opportunities for replication across manufacturing sectors, industrial clusters and national economies. Successful pilot validation could establish a transferable industrial digitalisation framework suitable for wider deployment across ASEAN and other developing regions. 4. Strengthening Local Innovation and Engineering Capabilities: Through collaboration among industry federations, universities, engineering institutions, technology providers and manufacturers, INDUSTRIA ONE can support technology transfer, applied research, professional development and the creation of skilled technical opportunities. This ecosystem approach strengthens local capacity to develop, deploy and sustain industrial technologies. 5. Accelerating Sustainable Industrial Development: By enabling integrated industrial data monitoring and developing AI-driven performance optimisation capabilities, INDUSTRIA ONE can support broader improvements in energy efficiency, resource productivity, operational resilience and environmental performance. These improvements could contribute to long-term industrial competitiveness while advancing SDGs 9, 12 and 8. Ultimately, INDUSTRIA ONE seeks to create a multiplier effect: transforming individual factories into connected industrial enterprises, connected enterprises into intelligent manufacturing ecosystems, and these ecosystems into foundations for inclusive, resilient and sustainable industrial growth.

Title: IKABENE.tech — AI-Powered Industrial Evidence & Traceability
Subtitle: An AI-enabled evidence platform connecting industrial product traceability, Digital Product Passports, emissions data and compliance workflows to support transparent, sustainable manufacturing.
Problem Statement: Manufacturers, particularly small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), face growing challenges in demonstrating product origin, supply-chain traceability, environmental performance and regulatory compliance. Critical evidence is often fragmented across spreadsheets, supplier documents, production records and disconnected systems. This creates administrative burdens, inconsistent reporting, limited audit readiness and difficulties accessing international markets. As sustainability and product transparency requirements evolve, many businesses lack affordable, integrated digital infrastructure to collect, organise and substantiate the information required by customers, regulators and supply-chain partners. IKABENE.tech addresses this challenge by developing AI-enabled evidence infrastructure that connects industrial data, product traceability, Digital Product Passports and environmental measurement, reporting and verification (MRV) workflows within a structured, human-supervised system.
Solution Overview: IKABENE.tech is an AI-enabled industrial evidence infrastructure solution designed to help businesses organise, trace and substantiate product, operational and sustainability information. How the solution works The proposed architecture comprises an Evidence AI Engine and Evidence OS, supporting three interconnected application areas: 1. Digital Product Passports (DPP): Structuring product identity, origin, materials, supplier documentation and lifecycle evidence to improve traceability and transparency. 2. Environmental MRV: Organising activity data, emissions factors and calculation records to support Scope 1, 2 and 3 greenhouse gas accounting and sustainability reporting. 3. Compliance and evidence management: Linking source documents, requirements, controls and verification records to support internal reviews and external assessments. Methodologies and technologies The solution combines AI-assisted document interpretation, structured data capture, evidence classification, traceability records and configurable compliance workflows. Its intended methodology prioritises source attribution, data quality, version control, human oversight and verifiable records. Emissions calculations are designed around activity data, applicable emissions factors and documented calculation methodologies, with human review of assumptions and outputs. The platform follows an evidence-first approach: information should be supported by identifiable records rather than unsupported AI-generated assertions. Collaboration model IKABENE.tech is developing a business-to-business SaaS model for manufacturers, suppliers and industrial SMEs. Its commercial approach includes product-level onboarding, subscription services and proposed pilot engagements. Collaboration opportunities include industrial manufacturers, sustainability specialists, technology integration providers and standards-related organisations, subject to formal agreements and project-specific validation. The solution is intended to support scalable industrial digitalisation, particularly for SMEs seeking stronger supply-chain transparency, sustainability evidence and international market readiness.
Solution Provider(s): IKABENE GROUP is the lead organisation developing IKABENE.tech, an AI-enabled industrial evidence and sustainability technology solution. The initiative is pursuing collaboration with manufacturers, technology integration providers and sustainability specialists to support pilot validation and deployment. Title: Jafife Food Value Engine AI for Sustainable Food Industry
Subtitle: AI-driven food intelligence can help businesses retain quality, reduce preventable losses, streamline processes and extract more value from perishable items.
Problem Statement: Preservation, storage, inventory, logistics, and sales choices are typically based on fragmented or outdated information, leading to a major loss of economic and environmental value for the food industry. Worldwide, FAO estimates that 13.3% of food was lost between harvest and retail in 2023. Food loss and waste together contribute an estimated 8-10% of global greenhouse gas emissions, according to UNEP. These issues are especially acute for agri-food SMEs and cooperatives in emerging economies, where access to sophisticated monitoring, preservation technology, predictive analytics, and market data is limited. Jafife's expertise in sustainable food preservation in Morocco shows that product deterioration is only part of the issue. Businesses also lose value when they do not have timely information about shelf life, proper preservation procedures, availability of stock, logistics, and market demand. Existing methods often treat these concerns independently. Fragmentation means that companies cannot act correctly before food deteriorates and loses its quality or commercial value. Jafife seeks to bridge this industrial decision-making gap, decrease avoidable food losses, enhance resource efficiency, and strengthen the economic resilience of food value chains.
Solution Overview: Jafife Food Value Engine is an AI-powered food value platform aimed at helping food growers, processors, and industrial food organizations maintain, optimize, and capture more value from perishable items. The system combines three complementing capabilities: food preservation, food intelligence, and food valorization. Data integration: The platform aggregates product and batch information, quality indicators, inventory, storage conditions, logistics, preservation choices, and market demand from existing business systems, structured data exchanges, and, where accessible, IoT monitoring. Predictive intelligence: The Food Value Engine uses data analytics, predictive models, and decision-support logic to evaluate product deterioration risks, remaining shelf life, and options to retain commercial value. Recommendations for operation: The system is to recommend when and how to conserve, store, move, prioritize, process, or sell products prior to quality and economic value dropping. Business optimization: A SaaS interface allows operators to see recommendations, monitor product condition, and analyze operational and commercial results. Technology & methodology The system integrates industrial data, IoT-enabled monitoring, machine learning, food-preservation knowledge, and human-supervised decision intelligence. Deployment and Partnership Model Jafife works on a B2B basis with food growers, cooperatives, processors, distributors, and industrial partners. The deployment starts with an assessment of the business needs, data integration, setup, user training, and operational validation. Jafife’s broader Moroccan food ecosystem encompasses over 1,000 growers, 65 food businesses, and more than 100 stores across four cities. These relationships provide access to industry information and potential deployment partners; they are not claimed as active users of the new AI engine. We have found a first pilot customer for the Food Value Engine. The engine is moving toward real-world validation and commercial deployment, with a paid launch expected in March 2027. The final aim is to render sophisticated food-value information available and economically viable for industrial SMEs in emerging economies.
Solution Provider(s): Bekra Technology (Morocco, sustainable food processing, preservation, and renewable-energy technologies; historical operational and technical foundation from which Jafife emerged). Jafife has also identified its first prospective Food Value Engine pilot customer in Morocco (agrifood sector); the organization's name and formal participation status remain subject to confirmation and disclosure authorization. Additional implementation partnerships will be established as pilot deployment progresses.
Implementation location(s): Morocco , fez
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 12–16 weeks for an initial single-site pilot, depending on technical readiness, partner confirmation, data availability and local implementation requirements. The deployment will be done in four phases: Weeks 1-2: Site evaluation, operational baseline and data access setups. Weeks 3-6: Data integration, AI configuration and monitoring set-up. Weeks 7-12: Operational testing, personnel training and refinement of recommendations. Weeks 13-16, as needed: Extended validation, impact assessment and preparation for commercial rollout. The goal is to show technical viability, user uptake, measurable food loss reduction and economic value capture before scaling up to more industrial sites.
Desired impact: Jafife’s mission is to accelerate the sustainable transformation of industry by enabling food companies to make smarter, more resource efficient, and economically viable choices across the entire perishable food supply chain. Primary Objectives Predict the risks of deterioration and prescribe prompt steps in the areas of preservation, storage, logistics, and commercialization to reduce avoidable food losses. Enhance industrial productivity and operational efficiency by improving inventory visibility, product prioritization, and resource allocation. Empower businesses to safeguard salable products and align available inventory with market demand to improve the recovery of economic value. Increase access to AI-driven decision support for agrifood SMEs and cooperatives in developing economies. Anticipated and Quantifiable Impact , recommends for the first pilot to measure: Avoided food losses, in kg and as a share of equivalent product throughput. Better preservation and marketing decisions resulting in greater net economic value. Operators implement AI recommendations. Inventory deterioration and changes in inventory management efficiency. Estimated net greenhouse gas emissions avoided using relevant product-specific parameters and including additional operational emissions. Indicative pilot evaluation targets are a 25% relative reduction of avoidable food losses compared to a baseline, depending on the product categories and operating conditions.
Key technologies: Jafife Food Value Engine uses proven digital technologies and knowledge in the food area to help predictive industrial decision-making. Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning: Predictive models and decision support tools to assess risks of product deterioration, remaining shelf life, preservation choices, and economic potential. Industrial Data Integration: Structured data ingestion and planned API-based connectivity to bring together product, inventory, quality, storage, logistics, and demand information from existing business systems. Internet of Things (IoT): Connectivity for temperature and humidity monitoring where possible to supplement operational data and provide greater visibility of storage conditions. Food Preservation Decision Intelligence. Domain-specific knowledge about food quality and preservation methods employed to provide suggestions according to product attributes and operational conditions. Cloud-Based SaaS Platform: A digital interface to give product intelligence, prioritized recommendations, operational monitoring, and performance metrics. Marketplace and demand intelligence planned capabilities to connect product availability and quality to prospective commercial demand, allowing for better allocation and value recovery. The technology architecture is modular, enabling implementation starting with existing operational records and evolving to linked monitoring and other integrations. The AI model’s performance and operational effectiveness are yet to be validated with pilot users.
Unique Characteristics: Jafife is a global approach to food value optimization, which links preservation, industrial intelligence, and commercial prospects in a unified decision support platform. 1. Monitoring to actionable decisions Usually, the inventory and IoT monitoring systems will share information about stock or environmental conditions. Jafife is designed to translate information around food quality, storage, inventory, logistics, and demand into recommendations around what to do next. 2. Economic value saving, not only waste reduction The food worth engine is not only about detecting or addressing food waste but also about intervening before products lose quality or commercial worth. This links sustainability targets to the profitability of industry. 3. Three interwoven layers of value Jafife integrates food preservation, food intelligence, and food valorization so that operational and commercial decisions can be seen simultaneously and not separated in different systems. 4. From real-life food industry experience The solution is based on 5 years of expertise in sustainable food preservation and processing in Morocco on the basis of real issues in the agrifood value chains. 5. Deployment model accessible The suggested modular SaaS architecture permits connection with existing corporate data, thus considerably lowering the need for a total infrastructure replacement. 6. Title: Agentic Discovery for Sustainable Industry
Subtitle: An AI-powered multi-agent research platform accelerating the discovery and evaluation of affordable, sustainable thermal energy storage materials for industrial applications.
Problem Statement: Industrial decarbonization requires affordable and reliable technologies capable of reducing fossil fuel consumption and supporting the integration of renewable energy. Thermal energy storage is a promising solution, yet identifying suitable materials remains technically complex, costly, and time-consuming. Researchers and industrial companies must evaluate numerous materials based on thermal capacity, temperature stability, conductivity, cost, availability, safety, and environmental impact. Relevant information is fragmented across scientific publications, materials databases, and technical reports. These challenges are particularly significant for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in developing economies, where access to specialized research infrastructure, advanced computational resources, and materials expertise can be limited. The central challenge is to make scientific material selection faster, more transparent, and more accessible, enabling industrial companies to identify promising thermal storage technologies without undertaking prohibitively expensive initial research.
Solution Overview: GreenMat AI is a proposed AI-powered scientific discovery platform designed to accelerate the identification, evaluation, and preliminary optimization of materials for industrial thermal energy storage. The platform would operate as a coordinated research laboratory composed of specialized AI agents. Instead of conducting isolated searches or generating static recommendations, these agents would collaborate throughout an iterative scientific discovery process. 1. Scientific knowledge acquisition A literature research agent would retrieve and organize relevant information from scientific publications and materials databases, including Materials Project, NIST JARVIS, and other appropriate sources. The system would extract material properties, experimental conditions, supporting references, and available uncertainty estimates. 2. Hypothesis generation A scientific reasoning agent would identify promising material families and formulate testable hypotheses based on industrial requirements, such as operating temperature, thermal performance, material availability, and cost constraints. 3. Computational experimentation An experimental agent would evaluate candidate materials through numerical simulations, sensitivity analyses, and reproducible computational tests. Initial experiments would focus on simplified thermal storage performance models, with more advanced modeling introduced as validated data become available. 4. Multi-objective evaluation A decision-support agent would compare candidates against technical, economic, and environmental criteria, explicitly identifying trade-offs and uncertainties. 5. Iterative scientific learning Experimental findings would be shared among the agents. Results that contradict initial hypotheses would trigger revised rankings, additional investigation, or alternative experiments. 6. Human validation and transparency Researchers would retain control over consequential decisions. Each recommendation would include supporting evidence, assumptions, limitations, and references.
Solution Provider(s): No formal institutional or industrial partners have been confirmed at this stage. GreenMat AI is currently proposed as an independent innovation concept. Potential collaboration targets include university materials science laboratories, industrial SMEs, research institutions specializing in energy storage, and organizations supporting sustainable industrial development. Materials Project and NIST JARVIS are identified as potential scientific data resources, not as confirmed project partners.
Implementation location(s): The solution has not yet been implemented.
Implementation timeline(s): No implementation period has been completed.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: An initial digital pilot could be developed within approximately 6–9 months, subject to securing appropriate technical resources, scientific data, and an industrial or academic partner. The proposed pilot would involve four phases: Months 1–2: Data collection, scientific requirements definition, and architecture development. Months 3–4: Development of the multi-agent workflow and initial computational experiments. Months 5–6: Benchmarking, technical validation, and evaluation against conventional material screening approaches. Months 7–9: Adaptation to a partner's industrial requirements, pilot evaluation, and preparation for further validation. Physical materials testing and industrial deployment would require additional validation and could extend beyond this timeframe.
Desired impact: GreenMat AI aims to accelerate scientific material selection and improve access to advanced research capabilities for sustainable industrial applications. Objective 1 — Accelerate research and development Reduce the time required to identify and evaluate promising thermal energy storage materials by automating literature review, property extraction, hypothesis generation, and preliminary computational analysis. Objective 2 — Improve industrial energy efficiency Support the identification of materials that could enable more affordable and effective thermal energy storage systems, helping industrial companies integrate renewable energy and reduce fossil fuel dependence. Objective 3 — Democratize scientific capabilities Make advanced materials screening methodologies more accessible to SMEs and research organizations with limited computational infrastructure and specialized scientific expertise. Objective 4 — Strengthen evidence-based industrial decisions Provide transparent, reproducible comparisons that integrate technical performance, economic considerations, environmental criteria, and uncertainty. Proposed impact measurement During the initial pilot, performance would be evaluated through: Time required to screen and compare candidate materials against a conventional research workflow. Number of candidate materials assessed within a fixed computational budget. Proportion of recommendations supported by traceable scientific evidence. Technical performance and estimated cost of shortlisted materials. Potential energy savings and greenhouse gas emissions reductions, calculated only when sufficient application-specific operating data become available. An initial experimental objective would be to evaluate at least 50 candidate materials and establish whether the automated workflow can reduce preliminary screening time by 25% or more relative to a defined manual baseline. These figures are proposed evaluation targets, not demonstrated results. Current impact status The project is at the concept stage. No verified energy savings, greenhouse gas reductions, job creation figures, or research acceleration results are currently available.
Key technologies: GreenMat AI proposes to integrate several complementary technologies: Multi-agent artificial intelligence Specialized AI agents would collaborate on scientific literature analysis, hypothesis generation, experiment planning, computational execution, and interpretation of results. Large language models (LLMs) Language models would support scientific information extraction, structured reasoning, and communication between specialized research agents. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) A retrieval system would connect AI-generated analyses to scientific publications and structured materials databases, improving traceability and reducing unsupported conclusions. Scientific data infrastructure Materials Project, NIST JARVIS, and relevant scientific literature would provide potential sources of materials properties and computational research data. Computational simulation Python-based scientific computing tools would support reproducible numerical experiments, simplified thermal performance modeling, and sensitivity analyses. Multi-objective optimization Candidate materials would be evaluated against multiple constraints, including thermal properties, cost, environmental impact, safety, and material availability. Agent orchestration An orchestration framework such as Omnigent could coordinate agent responsibilities, exchange structured results, and manage iterative research workflows. All technologies described above form part of the proposed architecture and should not be interpreted as already deployed or validated.
Unique Characteristics: GreenMat AI combines agentic scientific discovery with a specific industrial sustainability application. Its proposed differentiation is based on five characteristics. 1. From information retrieval to experimental discovery Unlike conventional AI research assistants that primarily retrieve and summarize information, GreenMat AI would connect scientific knowledge acquisition with hypothesis generation, computational testing, and iterative decision-making. 2. Adaptive multi-agent collaboration Specialized agents would exchange structured evidence and update their research strategy based on experimental findings. Unexpected results could trigger new hypotheses rather than simply being incorporated into a static report. 3. Integrated technical, economic, and environmental assessment The platform would evaluate materials not only according to scientific performance but also their suitability for practical industrial use, affordability, availability, and potential sustainability benefits. 4. Transparent and reproducible reasoning Scientific recommendations would be accompanied by references, underlying assumptions, experiment records, and uncertainty indicators. This approach aims to improve the reliability and auditability of AI-assisted scientific decisions. 5. Accessibility for industrial SMEs The proposed platform would seek to reduce the technical barriers associated with early-stage materials research. Its modular architecture could eventually support lower-cost research workflows adapted to the resources and requirements of industrial companies in emerging economies. The innovative contribution is therefore not the invention of an individual AI technique, but the integration of complementary scientific AI capabilities into an accessible and evidence-driven industrial discovery workflow.
Sustainable Change: GreenMat AI has the potential to contribute to a broader transformation in how industrial innovation is conducted, particularly in regions where advanced research infrastructure is not widely accessible. Accelerating sustainable industrial innovation By automating parts of the scientific discovery process, the platform could shorten the early stages of materials research and help industrial organizations identify promising energy storage technologies more efficiently. Reducing barriers to scientific participation The development of reusable research workflows could allow universities, smaller laboratories, and SMEs to conduct preliminary materials evaluations without requiring the same level of infrastructure as major research institutions. Supporting technology adaptation across regions A modular system could be adapted to different industrial sectors, operating temperatures, locally available materials, and geographic constraints. This could encourage the development of industrial solutions better suited to local economic and environmental conditions. Building collaborative innovation ecosystems The platform could support knowledge exchange between universities, industrial companies, technology developers, and public institutions. Subject to intellectual property and data licensing requirements, selected methodological components could be made openly available to encourage reproducibility, research cooperation, and further innovation. Enabling expansion beyond thermal energy storage Although the initial concept focuses on thermal storage materials, the underlying multi-agent scientific discovery architecture could eventually be adapted to other industrial sustainability challenges, including alternative construction materials, low-carbon manufacturing, resource efficiency, and industrial waste valorization. Long-term vision The objective is to develop a reusable scientific decision-support infrastructure that makes industrial research more efficient, accessible, and responsive to sustainability challenges. If validated through reproducible experiments and real-world partnerships, this approach could help strengthen industrial innovation capabilities and accelerate the development of sustainable technologies across emerging economies.
Primary thematic focus area: AI for Green, Resilient and Sustainable Industry
Summary: GreenMat AI proposes a multi-agent platform to screen thermal energy storage materials for industry. The scientific question is well posed; with no build, no partner and no result, it remains a proposal.

Title: Cane Service Cluster: SMS-Powered AI Coordination for Smallholder Sugar
Subtitle: A USSD/SMS platform that organises smallholder sugarcane farmers into coordinated clusters satellite/drone crop calendars, shared mechanisation and transport, and instant payment.
Problem Statement: Kenya's 200,000+ sugarcane smallholders farm 1–5 acre plots on informal timelines, and the entire value chain suffers from this fragmentation. Mills cannot see which fields will be mature, when, or in what tonnage so they crush below capacity at some times and immature cane at others. Cane is frequently cut at the wrong maturity (losing sucrose value) and then waits 24–72+ hours in the field for unpredictable harvesting gangs and transporters, further eroding sugar content. Farmers pay high, unreliable per-service costs for tractors and trucks, then wait weeks or months for payment with opaque, unverifiable deductions eroding trust and reinvestment. Meanwhile, digital tools that could help assume smartphones, apps and data bundles that most smallholders do not have. The result: lost farmer income, underutilised mills, weak trust across the industry, and an agricultural system producing less value per hectare and per unit of land, water and fuel than it should.
Solution Overview: How it works. Cane Service Cluster (CSC) organises 10–20 neighbouring farmers (≈50–100 hectares) into a service cluster an operational unit, not a new contractual intermediary; each farmer keeps their existing mill contract. Registration happens by USSD or through a trained local field agent, capturing identity, M-Pesa number, field location/size, variety, crop class and planting history. Field boundaries are GPS-mapped and refined with imagery. The platform then generates a shared digital cane calendar: planting, fertiliser, weeding and harvest windows per block, delivered to farmers as plain-language Kiswahili SMS, and to the mill as an aggregated supply-forecast dashboard showing expected mature tonnage weeks to months ahead. When a block is harvest-ready, mechanisation, harvesting crews and transport are booked and routed across the cluster (one tractor route serving ~15 adjacent farms), with weighbridge queue slotting so cut cane reaches the mill within hours. On delivery, weighbridge weight and quality data automatically calculate the farmer's payment under mill terms, itemise every deduction (transport, services, inputs) on an SMS receipt, and trigger instant M-Pesa settlement. Farmers can also book services, track deliveries and raise disputes via USSD. Methodologies and technologies. Free Sentinel-2 satellite NDVI time-series track crop vigour at regional scale; field agents capture drone imagery processed through MAPSTER (Oak Ridge National Laboratory's edge geospatial platform), whose small-metadata architecture transmits plot-level readiness signals over low-bandwidth rural networks, with containerised AI detection flagging stress and maturity indicators on imagery. Satellite/drone estimates are treated as advisory and validated by field agents and mill cane-quality sampling before any cutting decision a calibration protocol that turns free data into decision-grade local intelligence. Scheduling and routing algorithms sequence services across the cluster; M-Pesa integration with deduction logic and an auditable ledger handles settlement; role-based dashboards serve mills, providers, agents and regulators. Everything the farmer touches runs on USSD/SMS no smartphone, app or data bundle required. Partnerships and collaboration models. The pilot is anchored by a tripartite structure: the pilot mill (Chemilil Sugar Factory) provides weighbridge and quality data and adopts the forecast dashboard; the Kenya Sugar Board convenes, endorses and helps align policy and data standards; and mobile network/mobile-money partners (Safaricom-class) provide USSD, SMS and M-Pesa integration. Service providers (tractor, harvest, transport operators) join a marketplace with rating and assured payment. Development partners co-fund cluster onboarding and demonstration. Field agents prioritising local women and youth are recruited, trained and paid as the human validation and support layer. The platform is contract-neutral: it supports both mill-contracted and farmer-contracted transport, so adoption requires no legal or structural reform, and the same playbook replicates across mills and sugar zones later extending to other smallholder value chains.
Solution Provider(s): Kenya Sugar Board, Chemilil Sugar Factory
Implementation location(s): Kenya
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 24 months
Desired impact: Main objectives. Cane Service Cluster (CSC) is an AI-assisted, USSD/SMS-accessible coordination platform for smallholder sugarcane industries, with three objectives: (1) give every actor farmer, mill, service provider a shared, predictive crop calendar that ends blind decision-making in planting, harvesting and logistics; (2) cut the post-harvest sucrose loss from uncoordinated cut-to-crush delays; and (3) deliver transparent, instant digital payment that builds trust across the value chain. The core innovation is decision-making infrastructure that runs on the phones farmers already own no smartphone, app or data bundle required. Expected impact (24-month pilot, 5 clusters, ~75–100 farmers, 250–500 ha): operational targets include cut-to-crush time cut from 24–72+ hours to ≤12 hours; ≥80% of farmers paid within 24 hours of weighbridge delivery (vs weeks today), with 100% itemised deduction transparency; ≥80% of cane harvested within optimal maturity windows (protecting sucrose premium and mill recovery). Climate and efficiency impact: reduced diesel burn from shared tractor/truck routing (fewer empty trips), and avoided land-pressure from yield uplift the model is designed to show, against a matched comparison group, that the same sugar output can come from less land, water and fertiliser per tonne. Employment: 10–15 rural field-agent jobs (prioritising women and youth) plus youth-run service micro-enterprises. At maturity (100+ clusters across East African sugar belts), the same coordination layer extends to tea, dairy and horticulture smallholder systems.
Key technologies: AI/ML crop analytics: growth-stage and maturity estimation models combining Sentinel-2 satellite NDVI time series with agent-captured drone orthomosaics; containerised AI detection (via MAPSTER edge architecture, Oak Ridge National Laboratory) flags crop stress, gaps and readiness signals directly on imagery all calibrated against mill cane-quality sampling, so AI recommendations are validated before any cutting decision. Low-bandwidth edge data infrastructure: MAPSTER's edge-client/server design transmits only small metadata packages for instant discovery over weak rural networks, syncing full imagery as connectivity allows making plot-level intelligence viable where cloud pipelines fail. Mobile decision interface: USSD menus and SMS engine (bidirectional, Kiswahili, queued for offline delivery) the AI calendar's outputs delivered to feature phones. Scheduling and optimisation engine: service routing and sequencing for mechanisation, harvest crews and transport, with weighbridge queue slotting. Digital payments: Payment integration with automated deduction logic, SMS receipts and an auditable reconciliation ledger. Dashboards: web-based supply-forecast dashboards for mills and aggregated, anonymised analytics for industry bodies.
Unique Characteristics: AI on a feature phone: the full loop AI-informed planting/harvest calendar, service booking, transport dispatch, AI-verified payment runs on USSD/SMS. Smartphone-first agritech excludes precisely the farmers who lose most to poor coordination; we inverted the assumption. Fused intelligence: satellite (wide-area, free) + drone edge analytics (plot-level, cloud-independent) + mill quality data (ground truth) a three-layer validation stack that treats AI as advisory until locally proven, building trust rather than hype. Contract-neutral design: works within existing mill–farmer contracts and both transport contracting models, so deployment requires no legal or structural reform a deployment-speed advantage most platforms lack. Business model aligned to trust: farmers pay per service (shared cluster costs), the mill pays a subscription for the forecast dashboard it most values, providers pay a booking fee for assured demand every party pays for the benefit it receives, with itemised transparency as the product's core. Delivery approach: locally recruited field agents (women and youth prioritised) as the human-AI interface registering, validating AI outputs and resolving disputes, which is what makes the system resilient in low-literacy settings.
Sustainable Change: CSC's deeper contribution is proving that coordination infrastructure is the missing layer of inclusive industrialisation for smallholder-based value chains. Immediate follow-on effects within sugar: mills gain the forward supply visibility needed to plan crushing capacity and investment; transparent payment records create the credit histories that unlock input finance and crop insurance for farmers who are currently unbankable; and reliable cluster demand professionalises service providers. Replication is structural, not aspirational: the USSD backbone, cluster playbook and contracting templates are crop-agnostic, so the same system extends to tea, dairy, horticulture and cereals across East Africa's millions of smallholders each new value chain adding data that improves the AI models for all. At policy level, aggregated, anonymised cluster data gives bodies like the Kenya Sugar Board their first credible, real-time view of the sector, enabling evidence-based regulation on pricing, maturity standards and climate adaptation. Because the model is paid for by the value it creates (mill subscriptions, service fees) rather than perpetual grants, it is designed to sustain and scale itself turning scattered one-acre farmers into organised, data-rich industrial suppliers, and giving the world's smallholder industries a deployable template for AI that works where the infrastructure is thin.
Testimonials and Endorsements: Kenya Sugar Board
Primary thematic focus area: Industrial AI Models and Intelligent Decision-Making
Summary: INNO-NEAT proposes satellite and drone data, an edge scheduling engine and SMS messaging to coordinate smallholder cane deliveries to Kenyan mills. The concept is specific and the channel is right; there is no deployment and no evidence.

Title: Farview: Industrial Execution-Intelligence Platform
Subtitle: AI-powered execution-intelligence layer that connects schedules, engineering, procurement, and field teams to predict readiness, prevent delays, and enable accountable recovery on complex capital projects.
Problem Statement: Complex capital projects in utilities, shipbuilding, and industrial construction suffer from fragmented execution data. Schedules (P6/MS Project), materials/ERP transactions (SAP/EAM), and site execution happen in silos. Teams cannot answer three critical questions: Can this work-package proceed now? What evidence confirms readiness? What downstream milestones are exposed if a blocker persists? The result is idle time, avoidable rework, unreliable milestone forecasts, and delayed energization/delivery. Farview addresses this by operating at the cross-functional dependency and readiness layer.
Solution Overview: Farview is an industrial execution-intelligence platform for complex capital projects. It overlays existing ERP/project-control systems (P6, MS Project, SAP/EAM) rather than replacing them. How it works: Farview connects schedules, engineering documents, procurement data, supplier information, site/field execution records, and commissioning dependencies into a unified model. It models work-package prerequisites, evaluates readiness using evidence and provenance, propagates blocker impacts across downstream milestones, and supports what-if scenario analysis. The platform provides role-specific views (PM, site engineer, procurement, commissioning lead) and tracks accountable recovery actions. Methodologies and technologies: Current prototype demonstrates role-based project/portfolio views, prerequisite readiness checks, constraint ranking, delay propagation, what-if scenarios, evidence recency/confidence scoring, and tracked recovery actions. Current demos use sample/seeded scenarios. AI-powered document/email ingestion, natural-language copilots, learning recommendations, and production-grade P6/SAP connectors are roadmap items. Partnership model: Farview operates as a deployable SaaS overlay. Early engagement includes Mahatransco (empanelled vendor), Cochin Shipyard (pilot proposal submitted), and active utility/shipbuilding customer outreach in India.
Solution Provider(s): Mahatransco (empanelled vendor); Cochin Shipyard (pilot proposal submitted); utility and shipbuilding customer outreach partners.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3-6 months for deployment and pilot launch
Desired impact: Main objectives: - Enable cross-functional readiness assessment: answer whether a work package can proceed based on integrated schedule, engineering, procurement, and site evidence. - Propagate blocker impacts downstream so teams see the full chain of exposure before delays compound. - Reduce idle time and avoidable rework through earlier detection of constraint violations. - Improve milestone forecast reliability by replacing optimistic assumptions with evidence-based readiness scores. - Assign accountable recovery actions with traceable provenance. Expected and demonstrated impact (qualitative at prototype stage): - Earlier blocker detection prevents downstream cascade failures in complex projects. - Improved milestone forecast reliability through evidence-based readiness and constraint ranking. - Reduced idle time on site by surfacing true prerequisites before dispatching crews. - Better use of scarce industrial resources (engineers, equipment, materials) by preventing premature mobilization. - More reliable energization and project delivery timelines through proactive dependency management. Note: As an early-stage startup, Farview has not yet deployed field-wide metrics. Impact statements reflect the demonstrated capabilities of the functioning prototype and the expected outcomes in pilot deployments in utilities and shipbuilding.
Key technologies: Core technologies: - Cross-functional dependency modeling and constraint-based readiness evaluation - Evidence/provenance tracking with recency and confidence scoring - Scenario analysis and what-if simulation engine - Role-based project/portfolio visualization dashboards - API-based integration layer for existing systems (P6, MS Project, ERP/EAM) Current state: Functioning prototype demonstrates role-based views, prerequisite readiness checks, constraint ranking, delay propagation, and tracked recovery actions using sample/seeded scenarios. Roadmap items (not yet deployed): AI-powered document and email ingestion, natural-language copilots, learning-based recommendations, production-grade P6 and SAP connectors.
Unique Characteristics: Farview operates at the cross-functional dependency and readiness layer—between schedule tools (P6/MS Project), transaction systems (SAP/ERP/EAM), and site execution. P6 manages "what the plan says"; SAP manages "what the system records"; Farview answers "can the work proceed now, what evidence confirms readiness, and what downstream commitments are at risk." Key differentiators: - Cross-functional dependency graph that links schedules, engineering deliverables, procurement status, supplier readiness, and site/field execution data into a unified readiness model. - Evidence-based readiness scoring: teams can see the actual evidence supporting each prerequisite, with recency and confidence indicators. - Constraint ranking and delay propagation: blocker impacts automatically surface downstream exposure so teams can prioritize based on actual cascade risk. - Scenario analysis (what-if) for planning recovery paths without disrupting live project data. - Role-specific views: project managers see portfolio-level readiness; site engineers see task-level prerequisites; procurement sees supplier dependency chains. - Accountable recovery actions with tracked provenance and follow-through. - Overlay architecture: works alongside existing P6/MS Project/SAP systems without replacing them—lower adoption friction than full platform replacements.
Sustainable Change: Farview addresses a systemic gap in industrial project execution: the disconnect between planning (schedules), transaction recording (ERP), and field execution readiness. By operating at this cross-functional layer, the solution can: - Shift industry practice from reactive delay management to proactive readiness assessment across complex capital projects. - Create a reusable dependency-readiness knowledge graph that can be transferred across organizations and geographies, particularly benefiting developing and middle-income markets where execution risk is highest. - Enable better utilization of scarce industrial resources (skilled engineers, specialized equipment, materials) by preventing premature mobilization and reducing idle time. - Improve reliability of grid infrastructure and industrial facility delivery timelines, which has direct sustainability implications through reduced waste and more efficient energization. - Support technology transfer and capacity building: the platform's role-based views and evidence-provenance model can strengthen project management capabilities in MSMEs and public-sector organizations. Replication potential: The solution is designed for rapid deployment in new geographies (estimated 3-6 months). Priority markets are India and other developing economies where complex capital projects in utilities, shipbuilding, and industrial construction face the greatest execution risk. The overlay architecture allows adoption without displacing incumbent systems.

The concept is well specified and the file contains no evidence from a real project, so the score is that of a prototype rather than a platform.

Title: EmpowerAI: Bridging the Digital Divide for Vulnerable Communities in Sierra Leone.
Subtitle: Empowering youth and women in Western Area Rural, Sierra Leone with AI-driven digital skills, vocational micro-learning, and smart marketplace access for inclusive economic resilience.
Problem Statement: In the Western Area Rural District of Sierra Leone, disadvantaged youth and women face a severe crisis of economic exclusion, survival vulnerability, and systemic neglect. The solution directly addresses the following critical and life-threatening challenges: • In Sierra Leone, a devastating epidemic of substance abuse, specifically Kush and Tramadol, is claiming the lives of youth daily especially the Western Area Rural District. This crisis is fueled by extreme unemployment, pervasive hopelessness, and a total lack of productive economic opportunities or vocational pipelines, driving vulnerable youth toward addiction as a coping mechanism. • Women in this district lack access to formal financial resources, technical skills, and stable income channels. They are heavily dependent on low-yield, informal micro-trading, leaving them unable to break the cycle of poverty or shelter their families from severe financial shocks. • The Digital and Industrial Skills Divide: A Modern economic opportunities require baseline digital literacy and vocational skills, yet local communities lack accessible training infrastructure. High data costs and systemic educational gaps prevent youth and women from participating in the emerging digital economy. • Small-scale female traders and youth-led micro-enterprises are completely cut off from broader regional marketplaces due to a lack of digital storefronts, supply chain literacy, and fair pricing mechanisms.
Solution Overview: Project EmpowerAI is an offline-capable digital gateway deployed via community hubs to combat youth unemployment, substance abuse, and women's economic exclusion. The platform functions through three streamlined phases: • VOICE ASSESSMENT: Users engage via an automated, voice-driven interface that assesses their baseline skills in local dialects, eliminating literacy barriers. • TARGETED UPSKILLING: The AI maps personalized, micro-learning paths in high-demand digital skills and sustainable vocational trades, offering direct alternatives to idleness and drug abuse. • MARKET INTEGRATION: The platform automatically builds digital storefronts and translates product logs, linking women-led cooperatives and skilled youth directly to regional and international B2B buyers. METHODOLOGIES AND TECHNOLOGIES USED • Edge-Cached AI: Compressed Large Language Models (LLMs) deployed on local micro-servers to allow full platform functionality without internet data costs. • Localized NLP: Natural Language Processing models optimized for Krio speech-to-text navigation. • Predictive Matching Engine: Algorithms that analyze regional market trends to secure optimized pricing and automated logistics routing for local micro-entrepreneurs. PARTNERSHIPS AND COLLABORATION MODELS: • Grassroots Execution: Managed by Help Life for Needy Charity Foundation alongside local tribal authorities and youth councils for trusted community mobilization. • Vocational Alignment: Alliances with local TVET institutions to ensure certified, industry-standard skill curricula. • Fintech & Logistics Integration: Collaborations with mobile money operators (Orange/Africell) and regional freight providers to secure instant payments and reliable distribution networks.

Title: GreenScan by Green Balm | AI Mapping for Mine-Site Restoration
Subtitle: GreenScan uses AI to analyse aerial images of degraded mine sites, flag visible signs of erosion and vegetation loss, and help restoration teams prioritise field assessments.
Problem Statement: At sites like Venard Mine in Zimbabwe, open pits, mine shafts, exposed soil and vegetation loss make it difficult to assess land degradation safely and systematically. Restoration teams need a practical way to use aerial imagery to identify visible signs of degradation, prioritise areas for field verification and establish a baseline for tracking recovery.
Solution Overview: GreenScan is Green Balm’s web-based tool for assessing degraded mine sites and planning restoration. The current prototype lets users upload aerial photographs for AI-assisted analysis. It flags visible indicators such as exposed soil, sparse vegetation and possible erosion channels. Users review these findings alongside available site boundaries and observations to identify priority areas for field verification and document baseline conditions. The methodology combines AI image analysis, site mapping and human review. During the proposed pilot at Venard Mine near Mutorashanga, Zimbabwe, we plan to compare AI findings with field observations to assess which indicators the tool identifies reliably. Repeat imagery from comparable viewpoints would help track changes in vegetation cover and exposed soil over time. On-site specialists would verify hazards, assess potential contamination and determine whether areas are suitable for restoration. The proposed collaboration model brings together mine operators and landholders for site access and records, environmental and GIS specialists for field verification and mapping, and local community members for site knowledge and input on restoration priorities. Green Balm would coordinate the pilot and use partner feedback to improve the assessment workflow and reporting.
Solution Provider(s): Green Balm (solution developer and proposed pilot coordinator, environmental technology and mine-site restoration). External pilot partnerships are yet to be formalised.
Implementation location(s): GreenScan has a live web MVP. Field implementation at Venard Mine still being proposed.
Implementation timeline(s): N/a
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Approximately 3 months from confirmation of a local partner and site access to launch a small-scale pilot. This includes adapting GreenScan to local site conditions, collecting baseline aerial imagery and conducting initial field verification.
Desired impact: GreenScan’s objective is to help mine operators and restoration teams assess degraded land, prioritise field inspections and establish a baseline for monitoring recovery. It uses AI-assisted analysis of aerial imagery to flag visible indicators such as exposed soil, sparse vegetation and possible erosion channels. The live MVP demonstrates image upload and AI-assisted analysis. At the proposed Venard Mine pilot in Zimbabwe, we aim to assess a 100 m × 100 m plot (1 hectare). We will compare AI-flagged areas with field observations, record the proportion of findings confirmed on site and measure the time needed to complete an initial assessment. Repeat imagery will help track changes in vegetation cover and exposed soil as rehabilitation progresses. Field performance and restoration outcomes are yet to be measured.
Key technologies: GreenScan combines AI image analysis, aerial imagery and digital mapping in a web-based platform. Its AI analyses uploaded aerial photographs to flag visible signs of land degradation, including exposed soil, sparse vegetation and possible erosion channels. The mapping interface lets users review findings alongside site boundaries and identify areas for field verification. The proposed pilot will use repeat aerial imagery to monitor changes in vegetation cover and exposed soil over time.
Unique Characteristics: GreenScan brings aerial image upload, AI-assisted analysis and site mapping into one web-based workflow built for mine rehabilitation. It turns aerial photographs into a preliminary assessment by flagging visible signs of degradation, such as exposed soil, sparse vegetation and possible erosion channels. Restoration teams can use these findings to decide where to inspect first and establish a baseline for tracking recovery. The proposed Venard Mine pilot will test this approach by comparing AI findings with field observations from environmental specialists and using local knowledge to inform restoration priorities. Repeat imagery will help teams track changes in vegetation cover and exposed soil over time.
Sustainable Change: GreenScan could help mine operators and restoration teams make site assessment and recovery monitoring a routine part of mine rehabilitation. A consistent workflow for reviewing aerial imagery, verifying findings in the field and comparing images over time could help teams direct rehabilitation resources to priority areas and document changes in land cover. The proposed Venard Mine pilot will test this workflow and document which AI findings are reliable enough to guide field inspections. If validated, the approach could be adapted to other mining regions through partnerships with local environmental specialists and mine operators. Over time, using comparable assessment records across sites could help teams share lessons about which restoration practices work under different conditions.

Title: AI-Powered Transport Corridor Intelligence Platform for Sustainable Mobility and Smart Infrastructure in Africa
Subtitle: Leveraging AI, Real-Time Traffic Sensing, and Integrated Mobility Data to Optimise Transport Networks, Improve Public Transport Planning, and Enable Sustainable, Data-Driven Urban Development Across Africa.
Problem Statement: Across Africa, urbanisation, population growth, and increasing demand for mobility are placing significant pressure on existing transport infrastructure and public transport systems. Many cities continue to experience severe traffic congestion, inefficient transport network planning, fragmented public transport services, and limited visibility into real-time traffic conditions and passenger mobility patterns. These challenges undermine economic productivity, increase transportation costs, contribute to greenhouse gas emissions, and restrict access to reliable, affordable, and sustainable mobility. A fundamental challenge is the lack of accurate, integrated, and continuously updated transport data required to support intelligent mobility planning and infrastructure investment. Public transport networks, particularly informal and semi-formal transport services such as minibus taxis, frequently operate without comprehensive digital route maps, reliable movement records, or systematic demand measurements. Consequently, transport authorities, urban planners, infrastructure developers, and mobility operators often rely on incomplete, outdated, or fragmented information when making critical operational and investment decisions. Furthermore, traditional traffic monitoring and transport planning approaches are often expensive, infrastructure-intensive, and poorly suited to the rapidly evolving mobility patterns of African cities. Existing systems frequently lack the capabilities to integrate diverse sources of vehicle movement, traffic activity, public transport connectivity, and transport demand information into a unified intelligence framework. The limited adoption of Artificial Intelligence, machine learning, and intelligent transport data analytics further constrains the ability of cities to anticipate mobility demand, identify emerging congestion patterns, optimise transport corridor utilisation, and plan infrastructure investments proactively. This creates a significant gap between the growing complexity of urban transport systems and the analytical capabilities available to manage them effectively. These challenges also have broader implications for sustainable industrial development. Inefficient transport corridors disrupt the movement of workers, goods, and services, increase logistics costs, reduce business productivity, and contribute to unnecessary fuel consumption and environmental degradation. Without reliable transport intelligence, governments and industry stakeholders face difficulties prioritising infrastructure investments, improving connectivity between economic centres, and measuring the effectiveness of sustainable mobility interventions. There is therefore an urgent need for a scalable, affordable, and AI-enabled transport corridor intelligence solution capable of continuously collecting traffic activity data, monitoring vehicle movements, digitally mapping public transport networks, integrating fragmented mobility datasets, and generating actionable insights for transport planning and infrastructure management. Addressing this challenge requires transitioning from fragmented, reactive transport monitoring towards integrated, data-driven, and predictive mobility intelligence that enables African cities to improve transport efficiency, strengthen public transport accessibility, support economic productivity, and advance environmentally sustainable urban and industrial development. VelozTech seeks to address this gap by developing an integrated transport corridor intelligence platform that combines vehicle tracking, traffic sensing, public transport network mapping, and mobility data analytics, with AI-powered forecasting and decision-support capabilities as a proposed enhancement.
Solution Overview: VelozTech's AI-Powered Transport Corridor Intelligence Platform integrates IoT, GPS vehicle tracking, traffic sensing, cloud computing, and geospatial analytics to improve mobility planning and sustainable transport infrastructure across Africa. The platform collects real-time vehicle movement data, maps public transport networks, and analyses traffic patterns. Proposed AI and machine learning capabilities will forecast transport demand, identify congestion hotspots, and support infrastructure planning. Technologies include GPS tracking, spatial analytics, predictive modelling, cloud data pipelines, and interactive dashboards. VelozTech seeks partnerships with government transport authorities, public transport operators, universities, telecommunications providers, and industrial stakeholders for data sharing, research, pilot deployments, and scaling. The solution aims to improve transport efficiency, economic connectivity, and sustainable urban development.
