Title: Asset Intel Africa: AI-Enabled Industrial Asset Decision Intelligence
Subtitle: Turning equipment, maintenance and operational data into reliability, economic and lifecycle decisions for mining, construction and asset-intensive industries.
Problem Statement: Asset-intensive industries generate substantial equipment, maintenance and operational data, yet this information is often fragmented across spreadsheets, maintenance systems, operational reports and financial systems. As a result, managers may know that equipment failed or accumulated downtime without understanding which failures create the greatest operational and economic exposure, which assets require priority intervention, or when continued repair becomes less economical than overhaul or replacement. This challenge is particularly important in emerging industrial markets, where organisations may operate expensive equipment fleets while having uneven levels of digital maturity and limited access to advanced asset analytics. Asset Intel addresses the gap between collecting industrial data and making economically informed asset decisions.
Solution Overview: Asset Intel Africa is developing a modular industrial asset decision-intelligence platform. Its working MVP, Downtime IQ, captures and analyses asset, downtime, maintenance and reliability information across multiple sites. The platform calculates measures including availability, utilisation, MTBF, MTTR, downtime duration, repeat failures and FMEA/RPN-based risk information, and connects these operational indicators with economic-impact analysis. The broader architecture includes: Downtime IQ — operational reliability, downtime and maintenance intelligence. Strata Intel — mining-specific fleet, site, production and resource intelligence. Lifecycle Engine — lifecycle cost, total cost of ownership, overhaul/replacement and capital-planning intelligence. The current platform combines structured industrial data, statistical reliability methods, criticality analysis, economic modelling and explainable decision logic. An AI-assisted layer is being integrated to support natural-language interaction, pattern interpretation and explainable management recommendations; these AI functions are not yet claimed as production-validated. Asset Intel is designed to complement rather than replace ERP/EAM/CMMS systems and can progressively integrate data from platforms such as SAP and IBM Maximo. The preferred collaboration model is structured pilot deployment with industrial operators, equipment owners, OEMs and technology partners using real operational data, followed by enterprise integration and expansion across additional sites or fleets.
Solution Provider(s): N/A — Asset Intel Africa currently has no formal implementation partners. The company is actively seeking design partners and pilot collaborators among mining operators, construction and infrastructure companies, heavy-equipment owners, OEMs and industrial technology/EAM integration partners.
Implementation location(s): N/A — the solution has not yet completed a live customer deployment. The working MVP has been developed and validated using realistic industrial and heavy-equipment operating datasets and workflows.
Implementation timeline(s): N/A — commercial pilot deployment is the next implementation milestone.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Approximately 4–8 weeks, depending on customer data readiness and integration requirements. A pilot can begin with structured spreadsheet or exported operational/maintenance data, reducing dependency on complex system integration during initial validation. More advanced ERP/EAM/CMMS integrations can follow after the initial pilot.
Desired impact: The primary objective of Asset Intel Africa is to help industrial organisations extract greater economic and operational value from existing physical assets by improving the quality and speed of asset-related decisions. The solution is intended to: identify avoidable and recurring downtime; improve maintenance and reliability prioritisation; increase equipment availability and productive utilisation; quantify the economic consequences of asset underperformance; support better overhaul, replacement and capital decisions; extend useful asset life where economically justified; reduce unnecessary maintenance, premature replacement and inefficient use of industrial resources. Asset Intel Africa has not yet completed a live customer deployment and therefore does not claim quantified customer impact from the software today. Pilot deployments will measure impact through indicators including reduction in unplanned downtime, improvement in availability and utilisation, MTTR and repeat-failure reduction, maintenance-cost avoidance, production recovered, asset-life extension and economic value recovered. Where customers provide suitable energy, fuel and emissions data, the platform can also quantify the resource and environmental implications of improved equipment utilisation and lifecycle decisions.
Key technologies: Asset Intel Africa currently combines: Cloud-based industrial data architecture for structured equipment, maintenance, reliability and operational information. Relational asset and multi-site data models supporting equipment histories, incidents, preventive maintenance and FMEA workflows. Statistical reliability analytics, including MTBF, MTTR, availability, utilisation, repeat-failure and failure-pattern analysis. FMEA and risk-priority methodologies for structured failure and criticality assessment. Economic modelling connecting equipment downtime and performance with cost, production and financial exposure. Explainable decision logic designed to show why an asset or failure receives management priority. AI-assisted analytics and natural-language decision support are under active integration, intended to interpret patterns, support industrial queries and generate explainable recommendations from authorised asset data. These AI capabilities are not yet represented as production-validated predictive maintenance. Future development includes deeper failure-distribution modelling, lifecycle forecasting, cross-fleet benchmarking and responsible AI-supported asset recommendations.
Unique Characteristics: Asset Intel Africa differs from conventional maintenance-management and asset-management systems by focusing on decision intelligence rather than record-keeping alone. Most CMMS/EAM systems are designed primarily to capture work orders, maintenance histories, inspections and asset records. Asset Intel is designed to sit above or alongside these systems and answer a different set of questions: What asset problem matters most? What is its operational consequence? What is its economic impact? What action should management prioritise? The platform connects: Asset event → Reliability impact → Operational criticality → Economic consequence → Decision priority. Its modular architecture also separates immediate reliability decisions from mining operational intelligence and long-term lifecycle/capital decisions through Downtime IQ, Strata Intel and Lifecycle Engine. A further differentiator is accessibility across different levels of industrial digital maturity. Organisations can begin with structured spreadsheets or exported data and progressively move toward deeper enterprise integration. The platform is being designed around the operating realities of African asset-intensive industries while remaining scalable to other industrial markets.
Sustainable Change: Asset Intel Africa has the potential to broaden access to sophisticated industrial asset intelligence beyond large organisations with extensive specialist teams and enterprise analytics infrastructure. The architecture can be replicated across mines, construction projects, industrial sites, infrastructure operators and equipment fleets because the underlying questions—asset reliability, downtime, utilisation, cost, lifecycle and capital allocation—are common across asset-intensive industries. At scale, the platform could create a structured industrial data layer that enables: cross-site and cross-fleet performance comparisons; anonymised asset-performance benchmarks; earlier identification of recurring equipment problems; better utilisation of existing industrial capital; more evidence-based equipment replacement and lifecycle decisions; integration of operational, financial and sustainability considerations into asset management. The solution can also support industrial digitalisation in environments where sophisticated data infrastructure is not yet widespread by allowing organisations to begin with relatively simple data sources and progressively increase analytical maturity. Over time, accumulated and appropriately governed industrial data could support sector-specific benchmarks and AI models adapted to African operating conditions, creating locally relevant industrial intelligence rather than relying exclusively on models developed from other operating environments. This creates a pathway from individual equipment optimisation to broader improvements in industrial productivity, resource efficiency and capital effectiveness across emerging economies.

The company is currently seeking strategic pilot partners, non-dilutive funding, accelerator support and aligned investment to support product validation, enterprise integrations, further AI development and market expansion.

Title: AgroSmarty: AI-Enabled Optimization of Agricultural Input Supply Chains and Use
Subtitle: An AI-enabled decision-support platform connecting agricultural input supply-chain optimization with responsible fertilizer and pesticide use planning to improve resource efficiency and sustainable agricultural production.
Problem Statement: Agricultural input supply chains often operate with fragmented information and limited coordination between actual agricultural needs and commercial decisions. Procurement, imports, inventory, sales, and distribution are frequently driven by historical sales patterns rather than reliable regional and seasonal demand intelligence. At the same time, agriculture faces a dual challenge: protecting crop production from pests and diseases while preventing inappropriate and excessive use of agricultural inputs. The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) estimates that up to 40% of global crop production is lost annually due to plant pests and diseases. Meanwhile, pesticide use is subject to increasingly important regulatory requirements, including restrictions on approved uses and maximum residue limits in food products. Insufficient integration of crop requirements, cultivation stages, soil conditions, climate factors, and pest and disease risks can result in both inadequate crop protection and unnecessary or inappropriate fertilizer and pesticide use. This can contribute to crop losses, inefficient resource allocation, excess inventory, supply shortages, environmental degradation, and food-safety risks. These interconnected challenges create financial exposure for agricultural input businesses while limiting the sector’s ability to improve agricultural productivity, optimize input consumption, comply with relevant safety requirements, and support sustainable food production.
Solution Overview: AgroSmarty is an early-stage AI-enabled decision-support concept designed to optimize agricultural input supply chains and support the responsible use of fertilizers and pesticides. Its distinctive approach connects farm-level agricultural requirements with regional market intelligence and enterprise supply-chain decisions, linking actual agricultural needs to input consumption and commercial resource allocation. 1. How the solution works AgroSmarty is envisioned as an integrated platform with three interconnected layers: A. Dans les communautés rurales les plus reculer .Les jeunes et les femmes rencontrent des difficultés d'accès aux financements, aux équipements modernes et aux opportunités entrepreneuriales. Nous consistant à mettre en place un dispositif agricole innovant permettant aux bénéficiaires de développer des activités de production, de transformation et de commercialisation. Elle prévoit notamment l'utilisation de serres intelligentes, de systèmes d'irrigation économes en eau, de capteurs et d'outils numériques pour améliorer le suivi des cultures. Sa particularité est de combiner des technologies accessibles, notamment les serres intelligentes, les capteurs connectés, l'irrigation automatisée et l'analyse des données agricoles par l'IA, afin d'améliorer les rendements, d'optimiser la gestion de l'eau et d'anticiper les risques liés aux cultures. Le projet se distingue également par son modèle économique inclusif, fondé sur la formation, la production agricole, la transformation locale et la commercialisation. Il prévoit de créer des opportunités d'emploi et de favoriser l'émergence de petites entreprises agricoles portées par les jeunes et les femmes.
